title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
abstract: Objectives: Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and Methods: We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations. Results: Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. Identified challenges i…

title: Detection and luminosity-dependent evolution of the high-energy hump in the Be/X-ray pulsar 1A 1118-61
abstract: Accreting X-ray pulsars exhibit strong luminosity-dependent changes in their broad-band spectra. At high luminosities, their spectra are usually described by a power-law continuum with a high-energy cutoff, whereas low-luminosity observations have revealed a two-hump spectral morphology. We aim to trace the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar and to constrain the luminosity range over which the high-energy hump becomes resolved as a separate spectral feature. We combine dense and monitoring with three νstar observations of the 2026 outburst to trace the spectral evolution from łum to a low-luminosity plateau at ≃(1--3) łum in the 4--35 keV band. For each νstar and ART-XC observation, we compare single- and two-component spectral models to determine where an additional high-energy component is required. We also use the two-component model to trace the flux evolution of both components. As the source faded, a smooth single-component continuum no longer adequately described the spectrum, and a two-component model became statistically preferred. At low luminosities, the spectrum developed two resolved broad humps, peaking near ∼10 keV and ∼30--40 keV. title: E-learning readiness and ICT usage among public primary schools in Athi River Sub-County
abstract: It is noteworthy to gauge the level of knowledge, understanding and usage of ICTs in public primary schools by assessing the e-learning readiness of public primary schools in Athi River Sub-County in particular. This paper therefore sought to establish whether e-learning readiness in primary schools is part and parcel of its development initiatives, given the thriving industrial activities in this area. The County, therefore, provides an appropriate setting for comparison of e-learning readiness between rural and urban schools. It was concluded that schools in Athi River Sub-County are not ready to roll out LCP presently, since their e-learning readiness is low given that teachers are currently inadequately trained and the schools have insufficient basic ICT infrastructure and equipment, such as internet connectivity, computer laboratories and Laptops/Tablets/Computers.
venue: African Journal of Early Childhood Education

title: Multicenter cohort retrospective clinical study assessing the impact of complete pathological tumor response on survival rates in patients with locally advanced gastric and esophagogastric junction cancer: long-term results (report 4)
abstract: Background . Advancements in neoadjuvant/perioperative therapy regimens have resulted in improved treatment outcomes and significant increases in complete pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced gastric and esophagogastric junction cancer. The aim of the study was to analyze long-term treatment outcomes in patients who achieved pathological complete tumor response following neoadjuvant therapy. Material and Methods . Data from 195 patients with histologically confirmed gastric or esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma (cT2–4N0–3M0), who achieved pathological complete response (pCR, ypT0N0M0) after neoadjuvant therapy and radical surgery, were retrospectively analyzed. Results . With a median follow-up duration of 39 months, the overall 3-year and disease-free survival rates for the entire group of patients were 90.9 ± 2.2 % and 89.1 ± 2.5 %, respectively. Regional lymph node status, both before the start and after completion of neoadjuvant therapy (cN and ycN), was the only statistically significant prognostic factor (p < 0.05) in both univariate and multivariate analyses. None of the parameters characterizing the treatment options, including adjuvant chemotherapy, had a significant effect. Conclusion . Patients with locally advanced gastric cancer who achieved pCR demonstrated favorable long-term treatment outcomes. No survival advantage from adjuvant ch…
venue_publisher: Tomsk National Research Medical Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences

title: Testing cosmological structure formation in a unified dark matter-energy model with a fast transition
abstract: Unified dark matter-energy (UDM) models, a class of models in which dark matter and dark energy exist as a single cosmological fluid, are an alternative approach to Λ cold dark matter (ΛCDM). In this work we focus on a model with a fast transition between dark matter-like and dark energy-like behaviour. The epoch and rapidity of the transition are the key features to enable the formation of structure in this model. We studied its viability using cosmic microwave background and weak lensing data with nested sampling inference methods. We found that the preferred region of the parameter space is the one with early and fast transition models, where the model's ΛCDM limit also lies. Our study confirms that this UDM model is able to form cosmological structure compatible with the data used.

title: Development and optimization of parameter recommendation model for automotive resistance spot welding
Carbon quota adequacy analysis and regulation strategy for coordinated electricity–carbon scheduling
abstract: High renewable penetration and the carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goals subject power‐system operation scheduling to the dual pressure of maintaining power and energy balance while ensuring carbon quota adequacy. Random renewable fluctuations propagate to source‐side carbon emissions through thermal‐power adjustments, making deterministic annual quota decomposition unsuitable for risk control in coordinated electricity–carbon plans. This study proposes a carbon quota adequacy analysis method and dynamic regulation strategy. First, a carbon‐emission deviation uncertainty model expresses source‐side deviations as a linear function of renewable disturbances. Linear random-vector mapping and finite-lag covariance propagation yield the first and second central moments of cumulative deviations and a component quota adequacy index. Second, an intertemporal inventory state equation exploits the long settlement cycle of carbon quotas to convert static component constraints into mutual-aid constraints across time windows while conserving the total quota. Third, a distributionally robust coordinated electricity–carbon scheduling model represents adequacy risk by a chance constraint over a carbon-emission deviation ambiguity set. A generation-order table endogenously determines chronological marginal-unit emission factors, enabling a second-order cone reformulation. Case studies reve…

title: Evaluation of Pantoea anthophila Y-7 as A Causative Agent of Brown Spot in Polygonum cuspidatum Isolated from Henan, China
abstract: Polygonum cuspidatum is a medicinally important plant; however, it is susceptible to microbial diseases that adversely affect its growth and productivity. In this study, 22 bacterial strains were isolated from diseased tissues of P. cuspidatum in Nanyang City, Henan Province, China. In vitro and in vivo pathogenicity assays were conducted, and among the 22 bacterial strains tested, only strain Y-7 was able to induce brown spot symptoms on the leaves of P. cuspidatum. Strain Y-7 was successfully re-isolated from diseased leaves following inoculation, thereby fulfilling Koch's postulates and confirming it as the causal agent of leaf brown spot in P. cuspidatum. Strain Y-7 was identified as Pantoea anthophila based on morphological, physiological, biochemical, and genome analysis. These findings provide valuable insights into the characteristics of this pathogen and may support the development of effective disease management strategies.

title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions…
venue: ECOBIZTECH: Journal of Economics, Business, and Technology

title: Artificial intelligence, the labor market, and energy consumption: What do major agencies in Latin America say?
abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has attracted significant attention in recent years; however, there are still few studies that rigorously examine its impacts on the labor market and, consequently, on the economy (Roose, 2023; Babina et al., 2022; The Adecco Group Institute, 2024). In this context, it is recognized that AI is transforming both employment dynamics and energy consumption on a global scale. This work aims to preliminarily understand the current state of AI in Latin America and review the state of the art on the matter, with special interest in identifying some relevant conclusions from three multilateral agencies. Recent studies, like the one by Jung and Katz (2026), claim that a 1% increase in AI spending is associated with a 0.036% growth in GDP, an effect that mainly materializes through improvements in the productivity of skilled labor.
venue: Denarius. Revista de economía y adminstración

title: Legal governance of blue carbon credits in China’s voluntary carbon market
abstract: Introduction Blue carbon credits are increasingly advocated as a way to finance the conservation and restoration of coastal ecosystems; however, the development of carbon markets does not necessarily guarantee credible climate mitigation. This article examines the legal governance of blue carbon credits in China's national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction market. Methods Combining doctrinal legal analysis, institutional comparison, and qualitative risk assessment, the study operationalizes a six-part framework covering additionality, quantification accuracy, permanence, leakage control, prevention of double counting, and independent validation, verification, and transparency. This analysis reviews China's CCER regulatory framework and the Ecological and Environmental Code, along with the methodologies for mangrove afforestation, coastal salt marsh restoration, and seagrass bed restoration. Results It finds that existing rules establish basic safeguards for project eligibility, carbon accounting, third-party verification, and centralized registration; however, they do not fully address the interaction between pre-existing conservation obligations and additionality, baseline uncertainty, long-term reversal liability, cross-mechanism information coordination, and ecological accountability. These gaps show that neither formal compliance with regulatory requirements nor p…

title: Measuring the perceptions of transfer of sports-based skills to the job market and their policy implications
abstract: Introduction Academic research has found that participation in sport can have physiological, psychological, and social benefits. The objective of this paper is to investigate the socio-professional advantages that can be gained through participation in competitive sport and the policies that could be resulting from them. Methods This research was based on a questionnaire distributed to 659 individuals from 56 countries with the aim of identifying whether they perceived that their participation in competitive sport has instilled in them job transferable soft skills such as leadership, time management, teamwork, decision-making, and ability to work under pressure. Results The results showed that most of the participants have highlighted that sport has provided them several soft skills that were very beneficial in their professional career. Discussion These positive outcomes can lead to the elaboration of policies that can raise the awareness on the societal benefits of competitive sport, develop the subject of physical education and sports in schools and universities curricula and strengthen a country's national power.
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Industrialization in middle Africa: do renewable energy, finance, trade, electricity access, environmental taxation, and FDI matter?
abstract: Background This study examines the effects of renewable energy consumption (REC), financial development (FD), trade openness (TO), access to electricity (AE), environmental tax (ETX), and foreign direct investment (FDI) on industrialization. Methods Drawing on a panel dataset of eight Middle African countries covering the period from 2000 to 2021, the analysis employs panel FMOLS, DOLS, and RLS estimators, complemented by pairwise Granger causality tests to assess both the robustness and causal direction of the relationships. Findings The findings reveal that REC exerts a positive and statistically significant influence on industrialization across all estimation techniques, a result further reinforced by Granger causality evidence indicating a bidirectional relationship between REC and industrialization. Likewise, FD emerges as one of the most influential drivers of industrialization, displaying positive effects that remain significant at the 1% level across all models, together with unidirectional Granger causality running from FD to industrialization. Similarly, TO also has a positive and statistically significant effect on industrialization, while the Granger causality confirms a unidirectional causal relationship from TO to industrialization. Furthermore, AE exerts a positive and significant influence on industrialization under every method, accompanied by bidirectional cau…

title: Service-access factors add predictive information for lifetime HIV testing among United States adults: a survey-weighted explainable machine-learning study
abstract: Background HIV testing is a central entry point to prevention and care, yet uptake remains uneven across population groups. Although many demographic and behavioral correlates are known, the incremental predictive contribution of service-access opportunities and the geographic transportability of prediction models remain unclear. Methods We analyzed 2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 245,683 adults aged 18–64 years with known lifetime HIV testing status. Twenty-nine predictors were organized using Andersen’s Behavioral Model into predisposing, enabling/service-access, and need/health-behavior domains. Survey-weighted penalized logistic regression, extreme gradient boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine models were evaluated in a held-out test set using discrimination, calibration, and state-stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. We compared models with sequentially added domains and with all domain combinations, validated the model in held-out states, explained predictions with Shapley additive explanations, assessed performance by subgroup and without protected attributes, and examined a hypothetical capacity-constrained outreach scenario. Results Weighted lifetime HIV testing prevalence was 45.6%. Extreme gradient boosting achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.740 (95% confidence interval 0.730–0.749)…

title: Uncovering themes in user reviews of a smart urban mobility application with BERTopic: a data-driven framework for service improvement
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify the thematic structure of long-form user feedback on a smart urban mobility application in Istanbul by analyzing user reviews and to translate these themes into actionable insights for service improvement. Design/methodology/approach A total of 10,000 user reviews of the Istanbulkart – Dijital Hesabim application, posted on the Google Play Store between June 2019 and April 2025, were analyzed using BERTopic, which combines transformer-based contextual embeddings with density-based clustering and a class-based TF-IDF representation. The topics were then consolidated into themes and interpreted qualitatively. Findings The model extracted 40 topics, consolidated into six themes: transportation card integration issues, technical performance and application stability, payment systems and financial transactions, authentication and security, identity verification and account recovery, and general satisfaction and criticism. Transportation card integration problems formed the largest topic (13.21% of the 5,406 classified reviews), indicating that the transition between physical and digital systems remains the most salient difficulty in these reviews. Research limitations/implications The corpus, in which dissatisfied users are over-represented, comprises long-form Android reviews of a single application, so the findings describe what these users repo…

title: RADIOGRAFÍA DE CINCO EXPERIENCIAS IBEROAMERICANAS EN APRENDIZAJE-SERVICIO UNIVERSITARIO: CLAVES Y DESAFÍOS PARA SU INSTITUCIONALIZACIÓN
abstract: The article analyzes the processes of institutionalization of University Service-Learning (USL) in five Ibero-American universities located in Spanish state, Chile, and Ecuador. The aim is to identify how USL is understood, organized, and implemented, as well as to examine its main challenges and the factors that facilitate sustainable institutionalization. A qualitative approach with a phenomenological orientation was adopted, using a questionnaire to characterize the programs (institutional, educational, and community frameworks), followed by a focus group with institutional leaders to explore the key factors and challenges involved in the institutionalization of USL. The findings show that the institutionalization of USL promotes the consolidation of partnerships with community organizations, the systematization and evaluation of experiences, and the improvement of teaching practices, while also fostering meaningful learning and transformative experiences among students. The main challenges identified include the need to restructure relationships with community partners, the risk of trivializing the model by prioritizing service over learning, and the existence of academic barriers related to time constraints, funding, and the lack of institutional recognition. In addition, transformations were observed in the professional and relational perspectives of both faculty and stud…

title: The Constitutional Position of Indonesia’s Public Prosecution Service: Normative Analysis, Doctrinal Implications, and Legal Reform
abstract: This study analyzes the constitutional position, role, and function of the Public Prosecution Service of the Republic of Indonesia within Indonesia’s constitutional structure, drawing on constitutional law doctrine, statutory evolution, comparative jurisprudence, and Constitutional Court decisions up to 2023. Although the Prosecution Service exercises the principle of dominus litis within the boundaries of the Criminal Procedure Code, its institutional placement has provoked an unresolved doctrinal debate between executive subordination, functional-judicial autonomy, and hybrid constitutional models. Using normative legal research with statute, conceptual, and comparative approaches (examining the Netherlands, France, the United States, and the United Kingdom), this study evaluates the statutory tension in Law No. 11 of 2021 amending Law No. 16 of 2004, which classifies the Prosecution Service as a government institution while mandating independent prosecutorial power without altering the President’s unilateral removal authority. The findings reveal that while Law No. 11 of 2021 and Constitutional Court Decisions No. 28/PUU-V/2007, No. 16/PUU-XVI/2018, and No. 70/PUU-XX/2022 reinforce functional autonomy and ex-ante party neutrality, structural vulnerability persists. The study concludes that reconceptualizing the Prosecution Service as an independent executive body anchored in…

title: When participation is not inclusion: the service-participation paradox in mental health
abstract: Purpose This conceptual paper aims to examine why increased participation in mental health services does not necessarily produce social inclusion and develops a framework for distinguishing participation that expands a person’s social world from participation that remains contained within services. Design/methodology/approach As a conceptual paper, it develops a theoretical distinction and framework by drawing on selected literature on mental health recovery, social inclusion, community integration and occupational engagement. Findings The paper introduces the service-participation paradox, whereby services can successfully increase participation while leaving a person’s wider social world largely unchanged. It distinguishes service-contained from inclusion-oriented participation, proposes a two-dimensional matrix crossing participation intensity with social-world expansion and offers a sustainability heuristic for examining what remains beyond the service’s direct organisation and mediation, alongside meaning, choice and agency as person-centred criteria for interpreting both dimensions. Practical implications Services are encouraged to evaluate participation not only by attendance but by whether it is meaningful, chosen and expands access to relationships, roles and settings beyond the service system. Originality/value The paper offers a novel conceptual framing of the relati…

title: Increasing Elementary School Students’ Interest And Engagement In Learning Through An Educational Media-Based Community Service Program At Sehati Private Elementary School In Kota Pari Village
abstract: Purpose: This community service activity aimed to increase elementary school students’ learning interest and engagement through the use of interactive educational media at Sehati Private Elementary School, Kota Pari Village, Pantai Cermin District, Serdang Bedagai Regency. The activity addressed the limited use of interactive media in learning. Method: The activity employed Participatory Action Research (PAR), involving needs identification, planning, media development, implementation, evaluation, and reflection. The media included pop-up books, flashcards, educational puppets, and an educational snakes-and-ladders game. Media feasibility was assessed by three validators, while student responses were evaluated before and after implementation. Practical Applications: The results showed an average media feasibility score of 90.69%, categorized as highly feasible. Student responses in the Strongly Agree category increased from 46.25% to 68.75%, while Disagree decreased from 5.00% to 0.00%. Conclusion: The use of educational media increased students’ enthusiasm and participation while providing teachers with sustainable alternatives for creating interactive, engaging, and meaningful learning.

title: The Impact of Work Discipline on Work Productivity Among Employees Of The 3 Ilir Service Unit at Perumda Tirta Musi Palembang
abstract: Purpose: This community service program aimed to examine the impact of work discipline on employee productivity at the 3 Ilir Service Unit of Perumda Tirta Musi Palembang. Method: A qualitative approach was employed using semi-structured interviews with three purposively selected informants: the Assistant Manager of Customer Service and Meter Reading, the Meter Reading Supervisor, and a Meter Reading Field Officer. Practical Applications: The findings indicate that strengthening work discipline through consistent supervision, adherence to standard operating procedures, performance evaluation, and continuous training can improve employee productivity, operational efficiency, service quality, and customer satisfaction. Conclusion: Work discipline positively influences employee productivity. Employees consistently demonstrated attendance, compliance with organizational regulations and work standards, vigilance, and ethical behavior, enabling tasks to be completed accurately, efficiently, and on time. Overall, fostering a strong culture of work discipline supports higher productivity and enhances the quality of public services in public sector organizations.

title: Analysis of Wear-Resistant Coating Technologies for Extending the Service Life of Ventilation Mill Components
abstract: Within Thermal Power Plants, the components of the ventilation mill operate under complex conditions. Despite the operation conditions of high temperatures, these components are exposed to a high level of wear due to dust and sand particles flowing through the system. This paper aims to analyse the enhancement of the wear resistance of the ventilation mill. Within this research, a CFD analysis was performed as a comprehensive tool to determine the critical zones in the system. Considering the working conditions, it is emphasized that these components are characterized by high velocity particle flows, sand concentrations reaching up to 40%, and the presence of other abrasive mineral particles. Within this research, the application of various wear-resistant coatings is analyzed through detailed experimental testing to confirm the validity of each solution and establish an optimal proposition. Applying the various deposition techniques was considered, including manual metal arc welding, high-velocity oxygen fuel (HVOF) spraying, and plasma welding, utilizing filler materials with diverse chemical compositions. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Energy- Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), the structure and distribution of chemical elements of the coatings were determined. Determination of hardness distribution across a cross-section of samples is important in selecting t…

title: Corrigendum: The impact of teleworking and work flexibility on service work efficiency
Impact of E-Logistics Service Quality on Customer Satisfaction and Loyalty in Sri Lanka
abstract: The increase in online purchases has significantly increased the need for e-logistics services. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the impact of e-logistics service quality on customer satisfaction and loyalty. However, it was discovered that there has not been much research on the quality of e-logistics services in Sri Lanka. The present study aims to fill this gap in the literature. In order to conduct this research Order Accuracy (OA), Timeliness (T), Order Discrepancy Handling (ODH), and Information Quality (IQ) have been taken as the variables of the e-logistics service quality. A structured questionnaire was employed to collect data from 304 Sri Lankan individuals who make online purchases. The results were analyzed using the SPSS Statistical Software. While timeliness was found to have no direct impact on customer loyalty, information quality, order discrepancy handling, and order accuracy were discovered to have a significant positive relationship with customer loyalty. According to the mediation analysis using the Sobel test, customer satisfaction partially mediates the nexus between order accuracy and customer loyalty, information quality and customer loyalty, and order discrepancy handling and customer loyalty while customer satisfaction fully mediates the relationship between timeliness and customer loyalty. Moreover, the finding of the research r…

title: Earlier first viral load testing and differentiated service delivery enrolment after revised antiretroviral therapy guidelines in four South African districts
abstract: Background: In April 2023, South Africa revised antiretroviral therapy (ART) guidelines, moving the first viral load (VL) from 6 months to 3 months post-initiation. Clients with VL < 50 copies/mL became eligible for differentiated service delivery (DSD) at their 4-month review. Objectives: We assessed early implementation of this strategy in four South African districts. Method: We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of TIER.Net data from 664 523 people initiating ART between 2017 and 2023 in Johannesburg, Sedibeng, Capricorn, and Mopani. Primary analyses compared 2022 and January–April 2023 (pre-implementation) with May – December 2023 (early implementation). Outcomes included VL timing, coverage, suppression (< 50 copies/mL and < 200 copies/mL), and DSD enrolment timing and coverage among those with VL < 50 copies/mL. Follow-up was defined as 6 months from recommended first VL timing. Trends from 2017 to 2023 were described. Results: Among 91 723 ART initiators pre-implementation and 39 084 early implementation, the proportion without a recorded VL declined from 41.1% to 33.5%, and median time to first VL decreased from 175 to 105 days. VL testing within 3 months increased from 13.5% to 51.8%. Among those with VL results, suppression remained stable (64.5% vs 64.6% for VL < 50 copies/mL; 85.5% vs 84.9% for VL < 200 copies/mL). DSD enrolment within 6 months of VL < …
venue: Southern African Journal of HIV Medicine

title: Continuance intention to use logistics AI customer service robots: a stimulus-organism-response perspective and dual risk moderation
abstract: Purpose Against the deep integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into logistics services, this study aims to explore the formation mechanism of users' continuance intention to use logistics AI customer service robots (LOG-AI-CSRs). It clarifies how the four stimulus factors influence dual-dimensional trust, and such trust subsequently fosters users' continuance intention. The moderating roles of perceived AI hallucination and privacy concerns are also examined. Design/methodology/approach Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework and theory of mind perception, this study constructs a theoretical model with dual trust and value-in-use as mediators, and perceived AI hallucination and privacy concerns as moderators. Data were collected via Questionnaire Star with 384 valid samples, and hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) and Bootstrap analysis. Findings Perceived responsiveness, perceived interactivity, perceived agency and perceived experience positively promote cognitive trust and affective trust. Cognitive trust and affective trust enhance continuance intention to use and exert significant serial mediation effects through value-in-use. Perceived AI hallucination negatively moderates the impacts of cognitive trust on value-in-use and continuance intention to use, and privacy concerns negatively moderate the effects of affective trust…

title: Comparing Traditional and Alternative Genetic Counseling Service Delivery Models in Multidisciplinary Breast Cancer Clinics: A Survey of Patient Experience and Understanding after Genetic Testing
Service Excellence in Urban Village Government: Realizing Excellent, Responsive, and Human-Centered Public Services
abstract: Purpose: This community service program aimed to improve the competencies of village government officials in Pondokgede District in delivering excellent, responsive, and human-centered public services. Method: The training involved 48 village government officials in Pondokgede District and employed interactive learning methods, including presentations, discussions, question-and-answer sessions, and role-playing activities to strengthen participants’ understanding and practical skills in service excellence. Practical Applications: Participants gained practical knowledge in effective communication, complaint handling, and citizen-oriented service delivery, enabling them to respond more professionally to public needs and service challenges in the Pondokgede District context. Conclusion: The program was successfully implemented with high participant engagement and enthusiasm. The training enhanced participants’ understanding of service excellence principles and their application in public service delivery. The competencies acquired are expected to improve the quality, responsiveness, and professionalism of public services in Pondokgede District, ultimately contributing to greater public satisfaction and better local government performance.

title: How AI-powered chatbot empathy drives online repurchase intention: the mediating role of service trust
abstract: AI chatbots are performing an increasing amount of emotional labor for online retailers. However, it is still unclear if the engineered empathetic nature of these AI chatbots can lead to increased repeat purchasing behavior and how they do so. This paper uses the stimulus-organism-response model to conceptualize AI chatbot emotional support as a stimulus, service trust as an organismic state (or internal experience), and repurchase intentions online as a response to those stimuli. Additionally, we examine the role that digital anxiety may play as a boundary condition. Using survey data from 447 Iraqi consumers who have purchased items online, we used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLSSEM) to analyze our results. The results show that AI chatbot emotional support was significantly related to service trust, which in turn was significantly related to repurchase intentions. Furthermore, trust completely mediated the positive relationship between the two variables, such that all of the effects of chatbot emotional support on repurchase intentions were carried by trust. Contrary to expectations, digital anxiety did not moderate the relationship between chatbot emotional support and trust or conditionally affect the mediation of trust; thus, the process of generating trust occurs at similar rates regardless of level of digital anxiety. Overall, the findings sugges…
venue: Denarius. Revista de economía y adminstración

title: When digital-only and physical-only service experiences become infeasible: a phygital feasibility restoration framework for hybrid ecosystems
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain when digital-only and physical-only service experiences become infeasible for customers and how phygital service design restores journey feasibility in hybrid ecosystems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a conceptual approach and draws on affordance theory and service-dominant logic to develop a 4A taxonomy of single-modality infeasibility and a phygital feasibility restoration framework, which is supported by ten propositions and four vignettes. Findings Single-modality infeasibility arises when access, ability, acceptability or appropriateness conditions fail. Phygital design restores feasibility through substitution, augmentation, scaffolding and safeguarding, which, in turn, improves experience feasibility, continuity and ecosystem resilience. Originality/value This study reframes phygital service experience as a feasibility restoration problem rather than an integration problem, shifting the design and policy test from nominal availability to feasible participation. The framework treats the human side of service as a design resource that technology, including artificial intelligence, should augment rather than displace, thereby advancing theory, service design, inclusion, wellbeing and policy in hybrid ecosystems.

title: How phygital service modality shapes consumer responses: personalization, emotion and the paradoxical role of anthropomorphism
abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine how AI-enabled phygital service modalities (text-based chatbots and image-based augmented reality [AR]) influence consumer responses. Drawing on media richness theory and cue utilization theory, it proposes perceived personalization (cognitive) and positive emotion (affective) as the core mechanisms underlying modality effects and examines the moderating role of anthropomorphism across two product categories. Design/methodology/approach Two quantitative experimental studies were conducted with US consumers, examining chatbot and AR modalities in surroundings product (furniture; Study 1) and body-centric product (fashion; Study 2) contexts. Findings Phygital service modalities differentially influence consumer responses through distinct cognitive and affective mechanisms. AR generates stronger personalization effects in surroundings product contexts where spatial visualization demands are high, while positive emotion mediates responses consistently across both product categories. Counterintuitively, anthropomorphism negatively moderates the personalization mechanism for surroundings products but not for body-centric products. Practical implications AR is most effective as a primary modality for surroundings products requiring spatial visualization. Because perceived anthropomorphism diminishes personalization effectiveness, firms are recomme…

title: Drivers and barriers to sustainable service switching: evidence from search engines
abstract: Purpose The rapid expansion of digital services, accelerated by artificial intelligence, is intensifying the environmental footprint of widely used services such as search engines. While environmentally sustainable alternatives exist, their adoption remains minimal. This study aims to investigate what drives users to switch from conventional services to sustainable options, using search engines as the research context. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave online survey of German internet users captures both switching intention and behavior over a two-month period. The study builds on the push-pull-mooring model, integrating established with novel, sustainability-specific predictors. Findings The pull factor, consisting of alternative attractiveness, subjective norm and perceived usefulness, strongly drives switching intention, while the mooring factor, comprising switching costs, inertia and low consciousness for sustainable consumption, significantly lowers switching intention. Moreover, the mooring factor not only directly reduces switching intention but also mitigates the influence of the pull factor on switching intention and weakens the relationship between switching intention and switching behavior. In contrast, the push factor has no significant effect on switching intention. Originality/value This study extends the PPM model to sustainable service contexts, offering r…

title: LA ENSEÑANZA DE LAS LENGUAS Y LAS CULTURAS MINORITARIAS COMO INSTRUMENTO PARA LA INTEGRACIÓN: UN PROYECTO DE APRENDIZAJE-SERVICIO UNIVERSITARIO
abstract: This article presents a Service-Learning (SL) experience developed as part of a Bachelor's Degree Final Project in Social Education. The project aimed to analyse the potential of teaching Basque as a tool to promote the sociolinguistic integration of migrant adolescents living in a residential care home. From this perspective, learning the language of the host community constitutes a key element in fostering community participation and facilitating social inclusion, even when the language is a minority language. A qualitative study with an ethnographic approach was conducted involving ten male adolescents, aged between 15 and 17 years, from different national backgrounds and living in a residential care home. Data were analysed through content analysis based on the student's field diary and the evaluation instruments designed throughout the intervention. The findings indicate that the experience promoted participants' engagement with the Basque language and culture, broadened their opportunities for social integration, and contributed to the development of the student's professional and methodological competences. The study concludes that Service-Learning represents a valuable pedagogical approach for promoting sociolinguistic inclusion and social equity in culturally diverse contexts.

title: A Study on the Mutual Construction Mechanism Between Emotional Labor and Professional Identity of English Pre-service Teachers in the Context of Foreign Language Teaching Competitions
abstract: This study explores the ecological characteristics of English pre-service teachers’ emotional labor in high-stakes foreign language teaching competitions and its reshaping effect on professional identity. Drawing on educational ecology and Hochschild’s (1983) theory of emotional labor, the research tracked five pre-service teachers (S01-05) participating in a provincial-level teaching competition. Data were collected through a customized Competition-Grounded Emotional Labor Scale (24 items, six dimensions), semi-structured interviews, and non-participant observation. Quantitative profiles revealed a clear divergence: S04 relied heavily on deep acting and cognitive reappraisal and attained the highest professional efficacy (M = 4.50), whereas S03 exhibited high surface acting, emotional dissonance, and exhaustion (M = 4.25 each) with low efficacy (M = 3.25). Qualitative analysis showed that the competition’s high-pressure ecology compelled frequent surface acting to meet evaluative criteria, yet deep acting and cognitive reappraisal enabled some participants to transform emotional consumption into a sense of professional efficacy. The study proposes an ecological model, and demonstrates that emotional labor is not merely a psychological adaptation strategy but a key mediating variable in pre-service teachers’ identity transition from “student”…

title: Digital art engagement and emotional processing: examining empathy and need for affect in the link between visual narrative engagement and mood regulation
abstract: Introduction As digital visual narratives become increasingly embedded in everyday life, understanding their psychological consequences has become an important research concern. Although previous studies have linked narrative engagement to emotional experiences, the mechanisms and boundary conditions underlying these associations remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on Narrative Transportation Theory and Need for Affect Theory, this study examines the relationship between self-reported visual narrative engagement tendencies and perceived mood regulation, focusing on the mediating role of dispositional empathic concern and the moderating role of need for affect. Methods Data were collected from 556 university students in China using a two-wave time-lagged design. A moderated mediation model was proposed and tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The findings revealed that self-reported visual narrative engagement tendencies were positively associated with dispositional empathic concern, which, in turn, was positively associated with perceived mood regulation. Furthermore, need for affect positively moderated the relationships between visual narrative engagement tendencies and both dispositional empathic concern and perceived mood regulation. Discussion These findings highlight the potential mediating role of dispositional empathic…

title: Promoting or inhibiting: the impact of environmental regulation on enterprises' digital transformation
abstract: Purpose The impact of stringent environmental regulations on corporate investment and financing decisions is increasingly prominent. The implementation of China's new Environmental Protection Law (the new EPL) in 2015 represents a significant increase in environmental regulatory intensity in developing countries. Heavy-polluting enterprises must strike a balance between the dual transformation tasks of green transformation and digital transformation. Design/methodology/approach Based on the new EPL, we construct a quasi-natural experiment to explore the impact of environmental regulation on enterprises' digital transformation. Findings Our findings reveal that the new EPL significantly inhibits corporate digital transformation. Mechanism analysis indicates that, on the one hand, the new EPL crowds out firms' operational resources and weakens their financial support conditions for digitalization; on the other hand, it exacerbates business risks and dampens firms' willingness to undertake digital activities. These two channels jointly impede corporate digital transformation. Furthermore, additional analyses show that the inhibitory effect of the new EPL on digital transformation is more pronounced among smaller firms, in more competitive industries or in regions with lower levels of marketization. Practical implications The research results of this paper provide empirical evidenc…

title: Physical activity plays a direct role in the regulation of vitamin D metabolism and status
abstract: To date, efforts to address vitamin D insufficiency have focused primarily on increasing dietary vitamin D intake, particularly using supplements. In this perspectives article, we review recent evidence demonstrating that physical activity exerts direct positive effects on vitamin D metabolism, and we propose that interventions designed to increase physical activity may be a complementary strategy to improve individual and population vitamin D status. Recent evidence from carefully conducted randomised controlled trials indicates that physical activity has causal effects on vitamin D metabolism in humans. A single bout of exercise causes an acute increase in the concentration of circulating 25(OH)D and 1,25(OH) 2 D 3 in the hours after each bout. Furthermore, in the longer term, regular exercise (without weight loss) ameliorates the normal seasonal decline in serum 25(OH)D during winter and completely prevents the decline in 1, 25(OH) 2 D 3 . Thus, recent evidence demonstrates that physical activity affects vitamin D metabolism and status over both hours and months, including increased concentrations of biologically active 1, 25(OH) 2 D 3 . These findings have important implications for individuals, researchers and policymakers. Physical activity interventions and policies could be used as an adjunct to target population vitamin D insufficiency and, furthermore, some of the ben…

Ti Coating Regulation of MEMS Device Overload Resistance: Preparation, Characterization, and Application
abstract: This study proposes a method to enhance the overload resistance of silicon-based MEMS devices in high-impact environments using Ti metal coatings. Compared to Al, Ni, and Cu, Ti forms Ti–O–Si covalent bonds with single-crystal silicon, integrating excellent interfacial bonding and plastic energy dissipation. A 1 μm-thick Ti coating was deposited by magnetron sputtering, with low-temperature plasma surface activation improving the coating-substrate interface. Mechanical tests show surface activation enhances adhesion by 31.43% without significantly changing the coating’s intrinsic elastic modulus and hardness. A silicon-based MEMS electrothermal actuator has been used as a test case, impact tests demonstrate the Ti-coated device’s maximum undamaged impact amplitude increased from 18000 g to 21600 g (20.00% improvement). This study confirms Ti coatings effectively enhance MEMS structural reliability under high overload via the synergistic effects of interface strengthening and plastic energy dissipation.

title: Seeing through hypoxia: an oxygen-independent fluorescent reporter reveals ferritin regulation and mitochondrial remodeling in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Abstract GFP-like fluorescent proteins, including GFP, mCherry, and their derivatives, have transformed in vivo biology but require molecular oxygen for chromophore maturation, potentially decoupling fluorescence from protein abundance under hypoxia. Here, we developed CeFbFP, a Caenorhabditis elegans-optimized flavin-binding fluorescent protein (FbFP) that matures independently of oxygen, and benchmarked it against mCherry using matched reporters driven by the ferritin gene ftn-1 promoter. Both reporters detected ftn-1 induction at 0.5% O2, but CeFbFP produced a larger, more reproducible fold induction and remained robust at 0.2% O2. Following hypoxia, 2 h of reoxygenation at 21% O2 increased mCherry fluorescence 4.5-fold despite declining mCherry protein abundance, demonstrating that oxygen-dependent maturation can drive fluorescence and reporter abundance in opposite directions; by contrast, CeFbFP fluorescence and protein abundance remained concordant. Using CeFbFP, we found that pathogenic bacteria and hydrogen sulfide regulate ftn-1 differentially during hypoxia and that ftn-1, unlike the related ferritin gene ftn-2, is required for hypoxic survival. Mitochondrially targeted CeFbFP revealed reduced mitochondrial area and perimeter and increased network fragmentation in animals maintained chronically at 0.5% O2, without the reoxygenation that GFP-like reporters require—its…

title: Strengthening Food Safety Regulation and Hotel Compliance in Rwanda: Evidence from Kigali Paramount Hotel
abstract: Food safety in hotels is an important public health concern, yet little evidence exists on how strengthened food safety regulation is reflected in daily hotel practice in Rwanda. This study assessed the level of food safety compliance at Kigali Paramount Hotel, a newly opened four-star training hotel in Kigali, across four dimensions: hygiene and sanitation, regulatory framework, staff training, and inspection and monitoring. It also examined how these dimensions relate to one another and how guests perceive the hotel’s food safety practices. A convergent mixed-methods case study design was used. Structured questionnaires were completed by all 34 frontline kitchen and food and beverage employees and by 57 hotel guests, and semi-structured interviews were held with three key informants.

title: Community of inquiry presences, GenAI use, and metacognitive regulation in GenAI-mediated L2 learning: evidence from SEM and fsQCA
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has made language practice readily accessible. Yet access alone tells us little about how learners engage with the technology and regulate their learning. Drawing on the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework, this study examined the relationships among perceived social presence (SP), cognitive presence (CP), teaching presence (TP), GenAI use for second language (L2) learning (GLU), L2 speaking self-efficacy (LSS), student engagement (SE), and metacognitive regulation tendency (MRT). Survey data from 1,160 Chinese university students across seven universities were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). SEM revealed strong interrelationships among the three CoI presences and a positive association between their shared dimension and GLU. Within the hypothesized model, GLU was indirectly associated with MRT through LSS ( β = 0.108) and SE ( β = 0.477). However, these indirect associations were sensitive to alternative model specifications, particularly the pathway involving student engagement. fsQCA identified the joint presence of SP, CP, and TP as a configuration associated with high GLU (consistency = 0.943; coverage = 0.853). High MRT was associated with two configurations, GLU combined with SE and LSS combined with SE, both highlighting engagement as a …

title: The Emerging Crosstalk Between Nrf2 and the cGAS–STING Pathways: A Novel Axis in Neuroinflammation and Immune Regulation
Islamic Spiritual Education and Self-Regulation among Pesantren Students: Reframing Ruqyah Syar’iyyah as a Pedagogical Framework
abstract: This study examines how meanings associated with Ruqyah Syar’iyyah are understood in an Islamic boarding-school setting, translated into educational practices, and related by participants to students’ self-regulation. An interpretive qualitative case study was conducted at Al Ashriyah Sesela Islamic Junior High School in West Lombok Regency, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. The primary dataset comprised five interview transcripts from three students (SNT-01–SNT-03), one teacher/dormitory supervisor (GR-01), and one school/foundation administrator (PMD-01). Observations were conducted on the interview days (August 20 to September 5, 2026), and member checking was conducted separately on October 2, 2026, with SNT-01, SNT-02, SNT-03, and GR-01. The transcripts were analyzed through manual descriptive coding, independent second coding (Cohen’s κ = 0.42), source triangulation, an audit trail, cross-case comparison, thematic grouping, and interpretive synthesis. Four themes emerged: spiritual-pedagogical reframing of Ruqyah Syar’iyyah; internalization through habituation, modeling, mentoring, and reflection; reported emerging self-regulation practices in learning, emotions, and conduct; and the social and residential educational ecology that may support or constrain these practices. The proposed Pedagogical Internalization Framework is a context-specific interpretation of participants’…

title: Electrochemically responsive coordination polymer nanoplatform for localized gardiquimod delivery in osteoarthritis via regulation of the MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway
abstract: In this study, a multifunctional Cu-based coordination polymer nanoplatform ( 1-DASA-ATPMS@CP1@Gardiquimod ) was developed for Gardiquimod delivery. Structural characterization confirmed successful fabrication, favorable physicochemical properties, and efficient drug loading. In vitro electrochemical studies demonstrated rapid, potential-dependent Gardiquimod desorption from the electrode-immobilized material, indicating electroresponsiveness under in vitro conditions. The nanoplatform showed good biocompatibility and attenuated interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β);-induced inflammatory injury in chondrocytes by reducing inflammatory mediators and cartilage-degrading enzymes. In vivo , intra-articular administration of the nanoplatform, without electrical stimulation, alleviated cartilage degeneration and osteophyte formation in a destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM)-induced OA rat model. These effects were associated with inhibition of the mitogen-activated protein kinase/nuclear factor-κB (MAPK/NF-κB) pathway through reduced c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p65 phosphorylation. Overall, the results demonstrate the in vitro electroresponsive property of the platform and support the therapeutic potential of the loaded formulation for OA, while in vivo electrically triggered release requires further investigation.

title: Soybean Root and Biomass Production Response to Farming Practices and Liquid Organic Manures
abstract: Background: Comparative evaluation of natural, organic and integrated farming practices with respect to dry matter production and root biomass is essential to determine their relative efficacy in promoting sustainable crop productivity and resource-use efficiency, especially in the context of declining soil health and the need for environmentally sound agricultural practices in soybean. Hence, the current study was carried out to find out the effect of farming practices and foliar application of liquid organic manures on root characteristics and biomass production in soybean. Methods: The present investigation was carried out at Main Agricultural Research Station, University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad with vertisols under irrigated conditions. The experiment was executed in a strip design with three replications and three farming practices in main plot and five types of liquid organic manures as foliar sprays at crop critical stages in sub plot. The influence of farming practices and liquid organic manures on root studies and dry matter production of soybean (variety: Dsb 34) was studied and carried out during kharif, 2022-23 and 2023-24. Result: The pooled data of two years concluded that, organic farming recorded significantly higher root physiology parameters viz., number of nodules plant-1 (36.87), dry weight of nodules (48.16 mg), root length (1067 cm), root volume …

title: A Novel Dual Interleaved Boost Converter Topology for Improved Efficiency and Dynamic Response
abstract: This study proposes a Dual-Interleaved Boost Converter (DIBC) as an improvement over the conventional In-terleaved Boost Converter (IBC) to enhance voltage conversion capability and performance characteristics. The DIBC is built using a two-level interleaved boost converter configuration arranged in a cascade. The per-formance of both topologies is evaluated using PSIM simulation with an input voltage of 18 V and a switching frequency of 20 kHz. The IBC is operated at a 50% duty cycle, while the DIBC uses a 70% duty cycle. The simu-lation results show that the IBC produces a steady-state output voltage of 36.00 V, while the DIBC reaches 199.97 V. Ripple analysis shows that the DIBC has an absolute output voltage of 1.030 V and a ripple current of 0.069 A, higher than the IBC's 0.241 V and 0.005 A, respectively. However, after normalizing to their respec-tive output values, the DIBC produces a ripple voltage of 0.517% and a ripple current of 0.51%, compared to 0.669% and 0.69% for the IBC. In terms of power, the IBC produces an input power of 44.00 W and an output power of 37.08 W with an efficiency of 84.27%, while the DIBC produces an input power of 2798.10 W and an output power of 2640.66 W with an efficiency of 94.37%. Transient response analysis shows that the DIBC reaches steady state in approximately 0.87 s, faster than the IBC which requires approximately 1.84 s under th…

title: Dose–response relationship between weekly physical activity volume and depressive symptoms among Chinese adults: a cross-sectional analysis of a national sports and society survey
abstract: Background Identifying modifiable protective factors for depression remains a public health priority. This cross-sectional study examined the shape of the dose–response relationship between weekly physical activity (PA) volume and depressive symptoms among Chinese adults. Methods This cross-sectional analysis used the 2024 National Sports and Society Survey and included 11,379 adults with complete data on PA volume and depressive symptoms (complete-case sample, n = 10,096). PA volume was measured with an IPAQ-type instrument and expressed as MET-min/week; depressive symptoms with the CES-D-10 (score ≥ 10). Logistic regression used stepwise adjustment, with restricted cubic splines and survey-weighted sensitivity analyses. Results The weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 25.2%. Restricted cubic splines showed a broadly inverse, non-linear association ( p = 0.001), with the lowest odds near 4,000 MET-min/week. Each 1-SD increase in log-transformed PA volume was associated with an adjusted odds ratio (aOR) of 0.87 (95% CI 0.83–0.91), and the highest quartile had 29% lower odds than the lowest (aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.63–0.80). The association was directionally consistent across subgroups, but attenuated toward the null under the raw survey weights and sensitive to weight trimming. Conclusion Higher weekly PA volume was associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms in a no…

title: Evaluation and prediction of self-healing performance of ultra-high-performance concrete based on the entropy weight method and response surface methodology
abstract: Abstract To enhance the autogenous self-healing capacity of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) from the perspective of mix proportion design, this study systematically investigates the effects of ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS), silica fume (SF), and steel fibers on the self-healing behavior of UHPC under water immersion conditions based on the response surface methodology. Multiple quantitative evaluation indicators were adopted and combined with the entropy weight method to construct a comprehensive scoring system, thereby realizing the objective evaluation of self-healing performance for different mix proportions. Then, regression models capable of predicting compressive strength, flexural strength, and the comprehensive score of self-healing performance were established. The results indicate that the self-healing of UHPC exhibits significant time dependence. The self-healing products are mainly composed of carbonate deposits and secondary hydration products. Increasing the contents of steel fibers and SF can effectively enhance the compressive and flexural strengths of UHPC. Elevating the GGBS dosage is more conducive to improving the self-healing performance, and there exists a significant positive synergistic effect between GGBS and steel fibers. The established models demonstrate good fit and reliable predictive ability. This study provides support for th…

title: Inhibition of soluble epoxide hydrolase alleviates silver nanoparticle-induced pulmonary inflammatory response in a mouse model of metabolic syndrome
abstract: Introduction Nanosized particles pose health risks following inhalation exposure. Epidemiological studies indicate that individuals with metabolic diseases are more susceptible to particulate air pollution, leading to increased inflammation and lung injury. Previously, we found that silver nano particles (AgNPs)‐exposed metabolic syndrome (MetS) mice had elevated lung inflammation and altered inflammatory lipid mediators, linked to increased levels of soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH). sEH degrades anti‐inflammatory epoxyeicosatrienoic acids (EETs), so inhibiting it may improve EET bioavailability and help resolve pulmonary inflammation. 1‐Trifluoromethoxyphenyl‐3‐(1‐propionylpiperidin‐4‐yl) urea (TPPU), a potent sEH inhibitor, has shown efficacy in preclinical models of various chronic inflammatory diseases. Our current study hypothesizes that inhibiting sEH with TPPU can alleviate inflammation induced by AgNPs in susceptible mouse model of MetS. Methods To test this hypothesis, C57BL/6J male mice were fed either a healthy diet or a high‐fat Western diet for 14 weeks. Subsets of mice were treated with TPPU (10 mg/L) via drinking water for 1 week prior to AgNP exposure to inhibit sEH activity. After 1 week of treatment, mice were exposed to 50 µg/mouse AgNP via oropharyngeal aspiration. Endpoints of pulmonary inflammation and toxicity were evaluated 24 h following AgNP exposure. …

title: Deposition of Inconel 718 and Stellite 6 Coatings on Steel by Directed Energy Deposition and Evaluation of Cavitation Response under Ultrasonic Testing
abstract: Two coatings deposited on steel by directed energy deposition (DED) were exposed to ultrasonic cavitation under a single laboratory protocol. The Inconel 718 coating was deposited on an InssTek MX-Mini system using a laser power of 230 W, a travel speed of 550 mm/min, a 0.15 mm layer height, a 0.30 mm step-over and a powder feed rate of 1.0 g/min; a second series was deposited by the same process route from Stellite 6, a cobalt-based Co-Cr-W-C hardfacing alloy. Both series used the same plain-carbon steel substrate and the same cylindrical specimen geometry. Cylindrical specimens were exposed in distilled water on a piezoceramic vibratory apparatus at a frequency of 20 ± 0.03 kHz, a vibration amplitude of 50 µm and a water temperature of 22 ± 1 °C, for a total attack time of 165 min. For the Stellite 6 series, cumulative mass loss was recorded gravimetrically at eight intermediate intervals and described by with A = 0.12, B = 3.873 × 10⁻³ and an endpoint cumulative mass loss of 9.35 mg. The Inconel 718 series was characterized after exposure by optical observation, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). The eroded Inconel 718 surface showed a radial, flow-like morphology together with localized pits and shallow grooves, without macroscopic coating detachment in the examined fields. A representative EDS acquisition yielded 41.5 wt% Ni,…

title: P14.10.B CDKN2A homozygous deletion defines a distinct treatment response pattern and therapeutic vulnerability in IDH-mutant astrocytoma
abstract: Abstract Background CDKN2A homozygous deletion (HoD) is associated with poor prognosis in IDH-mutant astrocytomas, but its treatment implications remain incompletely understood. Material and Methods We applied machine learning-based contouring of serial peri-cavity MRI FLAIR volumes from post-resection, pre-radiotherapy baseline through early post-treatment intervals, alongside MR spectroscopy. Underlying biology was investigated using transcriptomic analyses of TCGA IDH-mutant gliomas and single-cell RNA sequencing. Functional validation was performed in CDKN2A knock-in models of CDKN2A-null IDH-mutant glioma cell lines. In parallel, in silico screening of cell cycle-targeting compounds, prioritised by neural network-based predictions of blood-brain barrier permeability and clinical feasibility, was followed by in vitro evaluation. Results CDKN2A HoD tumours demonstrated an initial reduction in FLAIR, whereas non-deleted tumours showed gradual reduction or stability. MR spectroscopy suggested elevated 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) levels in CDKN2A HoD tumours, consistent with altered metabolism. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of cell cycle dysregulation, neuronal stemness programs, and increased IDH1 expression, supported by single-cell RNA sequencing and a morphology grade-matched cohort, indicating effects independent of histological grade. Case Report: Complete histopathological response in a patient with pleural mesothelioma
abstract: Introduction We present a patient with pleural mesothelioma (PM), epithelioid subtype, who achieved a complete histopathological response following second-line treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) pembrolizumab in combination with lenvatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets multiple anti-angiogenic pathways. Case Following first-line chemotherapy, disease progression was observed, and the patient started second-line treatment with pembrolizumab and lenvatinib. After the fourth cycle, a near-complete radiologic response was achieved. The near-complete response persisted until the 22 nd cycle, when the patient unfortunately died. The patient had an overall survival of 16.8 months from the start of second-line treatment and 27.9 months from initial diagnosis. Autopsy revealed that the cause of death was a myocardial infarction, possibly related to the treatment, although the definitive cause could not be established. Furthermore, the autopsy did not identify viable mesothelioma cells in any of the examined tissues, demonstrating a complete histopathological response. Discussion This is the first reported complete histopathological response in PM achieved without prior surgical intervention. Complete responses in PM remain exceptionally rare, with only two previously reported, both following surgical resection and treatment with ICIs. Together, these cases …

title: Synchronous Thermochromic and Heat-Response-Enhanced Anisotropic Conductive Janus Film Functionalized by Upconverting Luminescence for Multi-Scenario Applications
abstract: Abstract Developing stimulus-responsive multifunctional materials for multi-scenarios is meaningful. Herein, synchronous thermochromic and heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus films (STHACJFs) are first designed and fabricated by respectively utilizing Janus-nanofiber and composite-nanofiber as microscopic building units to form the down-layer heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus-nanofibers array membranes (HACJAMs) and up-layer thermochromic composite-nanofibers array membranes (TCAMs) of Janus films via electrospinning. Thermochromic transition temperatures of TCAMs are innovatively designed to match with response temperatures of HACJAMs, thereby enabling synchronous thermochromism and conductive anisotropy enhancement under single-temperature stimulation. The Janus-nanofiber with two micro-partitions endows HACJAMs with high conductive anisotropy and strong luminescence. An innovative strategy combining the phase transition-enhanced conductivity of W-doped VO2 with the intrinsic conductivity of polyaniline (PANI) is proposed to enhance the conductive anisotropy degree upon heating, and response temperatures of HACJAMs are regulated by adjusting W atomic percentages to tune the phase transition temperatures of W-doped VO2. Upon heating to 60, 55, and 45 °C, W-doped VO2 and PANI synergistically enhance the conductivity along the length direction o…

Resilient supply and demand networks: analysis and stress-testing framework
abstract: Abstract Supply and demand networks (SDNs) are systems of relationships that provide for the allocation of physical goods around the world. These networks are susceptible to shocks that can then propagate through the whole system. Understanding systemic risk and resilience is required to better build and support functional SDNs. In this paper, we demonstrate a new methodology for assessing SDN risk and resilience through implementing stress testing of interconnected networks. We first construct a multilayer multigraph of entities and relationships from a variety of incomplete sources and then infer relationships to construct the SDN. Then we perform forward stress testing by propagating different threat scenarios, including topological risk and resilience modeling. We also implement reverse stress testing where the goal is to evaluate a set of threat scenarios that most likely results in systemic collapse below a risk and resilience tolerance threshold. Agent-based modeling is used as a mathematical foundation for performing both forward and reverse stress testing. Our methodology is demonstrated in a case study focusing on a global copper SDN, outlining its construction, and a scenario analysis for a mine shutdown and resulting spike in copper prices.

From farm to fine dining: trust is the backbone of luxury food supply chains
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how trust is built, maintained and challenged along the understudied luxury food supply chain, which is characterised by more personal transactions and higher quality stakes than conventional agri-food sectors. Design/methodology/approach Using the French Riviera caviar market as the focal empirical setting, the authors conducted 21 semi-structured narrative interviews with chefs (n = 11), distributors (n = 5), and producers (n = 5) selected through purposive and snowball sampling. The authors analysed the interviews using structuring qualitative content analysis, combining main categories derived from a theory-informed interview guide with inductively developed subcategories. Findings Trust in luxury food supply chains emerges as a relational and symbolic construct, shaped by cultural capital, artisanal values and sustained interpersonal engagement. Participants relied primarily on repeated interaction, personal credibility and proactive transparency, rather than on the transactional, system-based trust models typical of conventional food sectors. Trust expectations vary systematically across supply chain roles, while luxury value is symbolically co-created through shared narratives of rarity, craftsmanship, authenticity and heritage. Trust is also particularly fragile: operational failures can simultaneously undermine relational confiden…

title: From NIMBY versus YIMBY to place-attachments and place-logics: understanding residents’ views of place-making in South Africa and Sweden
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the paper is to further the empirical and theoretical understanding of the role of residents and their leaders in local place-making projects. Design/methodology/approach The paper compares reflections on two cases that explore the role of residents and their leaders in various place-making projects from Sweden and South Africa. Findings This study shows that residents’ attitudes towards place-making are more varied and complex than portrayed in the NIMBY-YIMBY dichotomy, and that local leaders play an important role in representing residents on place-making projects. The attitudes and actions of local leaders can vary over time, falling into four broad categories of “allies”, “opponents”, “entrepreneurs” and “guerillas”. However, the self-understanding of leaders as acting in the interests of their place is consistent across these multiple engagements, and there is an enduring and specific vision for development that informs the views and actions of leaders in both cases. This study suggests that local resident and their leaders’ motivations can be strong due to place-attachment and that reasoning is guided by local logics. Originality/value Empirically, the paper adds the perspective of residents and their leaders on the politics of place-making, suggesting that they are often the more consistent in their understanding and vision, whereas external actor…

title: Management consultants – monsters or benign change agents? The case of the NSW transport asset holding entity
abstract: Purpose This study critically examines the role of private consultants in public-sector financial governance under New Public Management (NPM) and New Public Financial Management (NPFM). Focusing on the New South Wales Transport Asset Holding Entity (TAHE), the research investigates how consultancy expertise and accounting technologies were mobilised in the case study to construct a quasi-market entity that advanced short-term fiscal objectives while obscuring long-term financial realities and the public interest. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in political economy and public-interest accounting traditions, the study employs a multi-method, qualitative case study design. Informed by the theoretical lenses of consultocracy and consultology, the analysis triangulates legally vetted and publicly contested documents, including Auditor-General reports, parliamentary inquiries, financial disclosures and investigative journalism, to trace institutional decision-making and intra-firm knowledge practices. Findings The analysis demonstrates that consultants acted as powerful political-institutional actors. They shaped the structural and financial design of TAHE to classify capital funding as equity rather than as an expenditure. Crucially, distinct consultancy teams within a single Big Four firm produced contradictory asset valuations. Internal firm dynamics helped contain these co…

title: Virtual reality booking systems: drivers and ESG outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how technological, organizational and environmental factors influence the integration of 360° virtual reality-enhanced booking systems (VRBS) and examines the subsequent impact on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance in the hospitality industry. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the technology–organization–environment (TOE) framework and stakeholder theory, quantitative data were collected from 588 four-star, five-star, and Chinese gold and platinum diamond hotels and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Relative advantage, digital infrastructure and competitive pressure significantly drive VRBS integration, whereas cybersecurity concerns and organizational agility are nonsignificant antecedents. VRBS integration enables hotels to use resources more responsibly, while enhancing stakeholder trust and transparency, thereby improving ESG performance. Hotels prioritize visible advantages, competitive dynamics and peer behavior over internal capabilities when deciding on integration. Practical implications Hotel managers can adopt VRBS without substantial restructuring because organizational agility and cybersecurity concerns pose minimal barriers. Given the influence of competitive pressure, late-adopting hotels should implement VRBS proactively to remain competitive and meet evol…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Empowering Health Cadres for Integrated Management of Non-Communicable Diseases in PLHIV Communities: A Participatory Action Research Approach in Yogyakarta, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, are an important health concern among People Living with HIV (PLHIV), particularly as they age. In Indonesia, HIV and NCD services are still delivered separately. Community health cadres may help bridge this gap. Objectives: To empower NCD health cadres within an older PLHIV peer-support group to improve NCD awareness, access to care, and links with health services. Methods: We used a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach with four stages (planning, action, observation, and reflection) in Kelompok Dukungan Sebaya (KDS) Surya Senja, Yogyakarta. In the planning stage, we conducted Focus Group Discussions (FGD) with 26 members and analysed the data using narrative inquiry and thematic analysis. Together with members and health workers, we then formed and trained NCD cadres in a one-day training modelled on the Posbindu PTM (community-based NCD post), followed by routine NCD check-ups at monthly meetings. We reflected on the program using a SWOT analysis. Results: Most participants were aged >50 years (84.62%), and 73.08% reported a history of NCDs. Three themes emerged: low health literacy of NCDs, self-discrimination when accessing healthcare, and low medication adherence. In response, cadres were trained and began routine early-detection check-ups within the communi…
