title: Bidirectional energy-flow modulation for passive visual admittance control using vision–force measurement fusion
abstract: Abstract Precision and compliance are essential to high-contact robotic tasks, while contact oscillations can be vital to both the end effector as well as the operation object. Passivity-based energy regulation of robot manipulators is a promising way to maintain decent operation behavior. However, current passive admittance methods in Cartesian-space depend on accurate pose reconstruction, making them difficult to apply directly to vision-guided high-precision alignment tasks. Furthermore, conventional passivity-based control usually requires large damping or strong energy constraints, leading to conservative control behavior. To address these limitations, a three-layer dynamic model consisting of nominal, offset and measured states is constructed, and a bidirectional energy-flow modulation mechanism is introduced to adaptively regulate energy exchange according to the real-time status. Moreover, a PID-based energy compensation, an adaptive virtual damping and an energy tank mechanism are integrated to constrain energy injection, dissipation, and release, thereby ensuring closed-loop passivity preservation while maintaining dynamic performances. Bolt alignment experiments are conducted under different initial positions, tilt-angle deviations and strong-contact conditions. At initial position 1, compared with shear thickening fluid visual admittance method, the proposed method …

title: An AI-based framework for assessing physical fitness, energy metabolism, and biomechanical efficiency in sprinting and hurdle events
From resistance to integration: the dynamic evolution and enhancement of college English learner engagement in the digital textbook context — a narrative tracking study
abstract: The widespread adoption of digital textbooks offers unprecedented opportunities for longitudinal inquiry into learner engagement in university English education. This study employed a narrative inquiry paradigm to track 20 undergraduates’ engagement across one semester (six units, 16 weeks) using the Finance English Integrated Course digital textbook. Data included three waves of semi-structured narrative interviews ( N = 60), 16-week learning logs and weekly questionnaires, plus platform behavioral logs from Unipus AI. Four-dimensional engagement (behavioral, cognitive, affective, interactive) was analyzed. Key findings: (1) Students’ experiential trajectories followed a three-phase pattern—Resistance (U1–U2), Adaptation (U3–U4), and Integration (U5–U6); “pleasant routine” dominated (42.5%), but “challenging efforts” and “aesthetic peak” combined only 32.5%, revealing a “convenience-induced superficial engagement” paradox. (2) Four-dimensional engagement showed “asynchronous evolution”: affective engagement improved earliest (around U3), cognitive engagement latest (around U5), behavioral engagement was most variable, and interactive engagement was most agentic—challenging the unitary engagement assumption in prior literature. (3) Three conceptual propositions were inductively derived—the Three-Phase Digital Textbook Adaptation Engagement Model, the Asynchronous Four-Dimension…

title: Energy security risks and banking stability: the moderating roles of renewable energy and governance effectiveness
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether energy security risk (ESR) is associated with country-level banking stability and whether this relationship varies with renewable energy development and governance effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a panel of 64 countries from 2010 to 2021. Two-way fixed effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors provide the baseline estimates, while two-step system GMM is used as a supplementary dynamic check. Additional analyses consider the World Uncertainty Index, alternative banking indicators, net energy-trade position, nonlinearities and lagged moderators. Findings Higher ESR is associated with lower banking Z-scores, higher nonperforming loan ratios and lower net interest margins. The association remains after controlling for broader country-level uncertainty. It is stronger in net energy-importing economies and at higher ESR levels, but weaker where renewable energy penetration and governance effectiveness are greater. Lagged-moderator estimates provide strong support for the renewable energy interaction and more qualified evidence for governance effectiveness. Research limitations/implications The country-level design supports macroprudential inference but cannot identify heterogeneous responses across individual banks. The estimates are associational and do not establish causal effects. Practical implications…

title: Adoption of sustainable construction techniques for energy-efficient buildings among construction professionals in Ghana
abstract: Purpose The construction industry in Ghana and the Global South faces increasing energy costs, vulnerability to climate change and limited adoption of sustainable construction techniques. This study aims to investigate the adoption of sustainable construction methods for energy-efficient buildings in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted to administer questionnaires to 193 construction professionals, purposively selected for participation in this study. Both descriptive and inferential statistical tools, namely, mean score, standard deviation, frequencies and percentages, Pearson correlation and factor analysis were used to identify various types of sustainable construction techniques, their drivers and benefits, as well as to determine the clusters associated with them. Findings This study identified two main components underpinning construction techniques in Ghana: integrated energy-efficient practices and energy design strategies. It also revealed that the adoption of sustainable construction techniques is strongly associated with the identified drivers and benefits, while no significant association exists between the level of education and the adoption of these techniques for energy-efficient buildings. Practical implications This study underscores the necessity for targeted training, a skilled workforce and development of policies that enco…

title: CO2 Hydrogenation over Cu/UiO-66: Correlation of Structural Evolution with Methanol and Ethanol Formation from a Multi-Technique Approach
abstract: Abstract Cu-exchanged linker-defective UiO-66 metal–organic framework (MOF) catalysts were studied under carbon dioxide (CO2) hydrogenation conditions at 200–250 °C, 7–13 bar, and a 3/1 H2/CO2 molar ratio. These catalysts generate carbon monoxide (CO), methanol (MeOH), and ethanol (EtOH) under CO2 hydrogenation conditions. Extensive isotopic labeling, in situ, and post catalysis studies revealed that MeOH is a product of CO2 reduction, whereas EtOH is not. Instead, EtOH originates from acetate moieties present in the MOF, mainly from ion exchange with Cu(II)-acetate, which are reduced and protonated to form EtOH. Conversely, the use of Cu(II)-nitrate avoids EtOH formation, but the resulting catalyst is much less active in terms of CO2 conversion and MeOH production rate (rMeOH) at 200 °C and 13 bar (0.63 molMeOH·molCu–1·h–1) compared to its acetate-derived analogue (2.1 molMeOH·molCu–1·h–1), probably due to differences in the Cu speciation. Besides the removal of acetate moieties, we find that under reaction conditions, Cu/UiO-66 catalysts lose a substantial fraction of linker molecules without compromising their crystallinity and porosity. We observe an increase of XCO2 and rMeOH over a period of 72 h on stream, which we correlate to (1) a gradual reduction of Cu(II) generating interfacial Cu(I) sites linked to both metallic Cu(0) sites as well as the Zr6 cluster, (2) an incre…

title: Transforming coal and gas infrastructure into cleaner energy assets: techno-economic and emissions analysis for Indonesia’s 2060 net-zero emissions goal
Risk-aware adaptive hierarchical diffusion for communication fault diagnosis and joint communication-edge computing resource scheduling in cyber-physical power systems
abstract: Dynamic power communication networks must jointly allocate routes, transmission bandwidth, edge-computing cycles, traffic admission, and service priorities while preserving the latency and reliability requirements of protection and control services. Existing deterministic optimizers and single-pass reinforcement-learning policies have difficulty representing multiple high-quality allocations and maintaining instantaneous feasibility when traffic, topology, and electrical operating conditions change simultaneously. This paper proposes a risk-aware adaptive hierarchical diffusion policy for joint communication and computing resource scheduling. The scheduling problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process over a four-level architecture comprising core routing, edge computation, access bandwidth, and service control. A coarse-to-fine conditional reverse process generates the four action groups sequentially, while service-risk and constraint gradients guide each intermediate sample. A state-complexity controller adjusts the denoising depth online, and a risk-weighted projection maps the terminal sample to the state-dependent feasible set. The method is evaluated on an 18-node communication network coupled with a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution system under four traffic classes and disturbance-driven workloads. Across 30 random seeds, the proposed policy achieves t…

title: Joint waveform learning in fiber wireless fronthaul integration toward intelligent decision making in electrical automation
abstract: Electrical distribution networks rely on communication links to carry measurements and control commands, yet the final stretch of these links usually mixes optical fiber with radio. Analog transport over fiber keeps remote units simple and cheap, but it also lets every distortion travel with the signal, and distorted signals lead to wrong switching decisions in the grid. Existing predistortion methods chase waveform fidelity alone, so a clean-looking link may still mislead the decision. We therefore place the optical and radio segments inside one trainable loop and learn the correction waveform from the prevailing distortion and the cost of wrong decisions. On measured fronthaul data, the error vector magnitude falls from 3.95 per cent to 2.14 per cent and decision accuracy rises from 0.931 to 0.967, while the expected cost of misjudgement is more than halved and the waveform gains hold across all tested distortion regimes.

title: Systematization of Approaches to Transferring Integration and Calibration Procedures for Electro-Optical Systems from Prototype Development to Serial Production
abstract: Electro-optical and laser systems reach their specified performance only after assembly, alignment, and calibration, and the knowledge behind these operations accumulates in the prototype laboratory long before serial production begins. Drawings and specifications travel to the factory with the product, while the integration know-how stays with developers and integrators, leading to rework, unit failures, long test and calibration cycles, and a lasting dependence of production on the development team. This review systematizes approaches to transferring integration and calibration procedures from prototype development to serial production. An integrative review of recent research on optical packaging, alignment automation, production ramp-up, tacit knowledge transfer, work instructions, design for assembly, and multistage inspection supported a classification built on four criteria: the lifecycle stage at which transfer begins, the carrier of integration knowledge, the division of labor, and the control strategy during calibration. The analysis yields five classes, namely documentation handover, expert accompaniment, procedure codification, design anticipation, and equipment embedding, together with a mechanism that decouples mechanical assembly from integration. Firsthand integration practice illustrates the codification and design anticipation classes, as well as the decouplin…

title: Optimising Lean Mass and Performance: A Sports Nutrition Framework for Protein Intake in Track and Field Athletes During Energy Balance and Restriction
abstract: Track and field athletes across sprinting, jumping, throwing, endurance, and race walking disciplines require strategic protein nutrition to support training adaptation, manipulate body composition, and optimise power-to-weight or strength-to-weight ratios. This review synthesises current evidence to establish practical protein recommendations that exceed general population guidelines (0.8–1.0 g·kg⁻¹·day⁻¹) while addressing the unique demands of weight-stable and energy-restricted athletic phases. For athletes maintaining body weight or aiming for lean mass gain, daily protein intakes of approximately 1.6 g·kg⁻¹·day⁻¹, distributed as 0.3–0.4 g·kg⁻¹ per meal across 3–4 feedings, optimally stimulate muscle protein synthesis; when using whole foods rather than isolated proteins, slightly higher per-meal doses (0.4–0.5 g·kg⁻¹) are recommended. During voluntary energy restriction for high-quality weight loss defined as fat mass reduction with preservation or gain of lean mass daily protein requirements increase to 1.6–2.4 g·kg⁻¹·day⁻¹, with per-meal targets of 0.4–0.5 g·kg⁻¹. This elevated intake counteracts the energy-conservation-induced suppression of muscle protein synthesis, particularly when combined with resistance exercise. Mechanistic evidence shows that higher protein availability during energy deficit restores postprandial anabolic responses and mitigates lean mass loss w…

title: Association between internet non-use and mortality risk among older adults: the explanatory contribution of social integration
abstract: Purpose Digital exclusion has emerged as an important dimension of social exclusion among older adults and has been associated with adverse health outcomes. However, its association with all-cause mortality and the potential role of social integration remain unclear. This study examined whether recent internet non-use was associated with all-cause mortality and explored the potential contribution of social integration. Design/methodology/approach Data were obtained from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), including 47,989 community-dwelling adults aged 50 years and older from 18 countries. Internet non-use was defined as no internet use during the previous seven days. Country-stratified Cox proportional hazards models examined the association between internet non-use and mortality, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, depressive symptoms, and physical health. Mediation analyses evaluated the potential contribution of social integration. Findings Internet non-use was independently associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics, depressive symptoms, and physical health. This association remained after accounting for social integration, although it was partially attenuated. Social integration explained part of the observed association, suggesting that it may represent a potential expl…

title: ANFIS-Based Energy Optimization Simulation of Portable Solar Greenhouse System for Oil Palm Pre-Nursery for Oil Palm Pre-Nursery
abstract: Portable greenhouses in off-grid agricultural regions often face inefficient energy utilization and rigid con-trol strategies that fail to adapt to dynamic environmental fluctuations. This study develops an adaptive ener-gy management strategy for a portable solar-powered greenhouse using an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The framework integrates real-time sensing of soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and bat-tery voltage to optimize irrigation and ventilation scheduling. System performance was validated through sim-ulations using localized solar irradiance data from the Photovoltaic Geographical Information System (PVGIS) database for Ketapang, Indonesia. The simulated system, comprising a 100 Wp photovoltaic (PV) pan-el and a 12 V 40 Ah lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) battery, powers irrigation pumps, fans, and lighting. Simulation results demonstrate that the PV system generates a daily average of 450 Wh, consistently exceeding the 307.2 Wh demand while maintaining the battery State of Charge (SoC) within safe thresholds. The ANFIS model, trained on 500 samples, achieved a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 10.68 seconds and a Mean Ab-solute Error (MAE) of 6.97 seconds. Compared with previous agricultural control approaches that reported RMSE values exceeding 15 seconds, the proposed ANFIS model achieved a lower RMSE of 10.68 seconds, in-dicating improved p…

title: Beyond additive integration in physical education teacher education: a PE-anchored framework for disciplinary coordination
abstract: Interdisciplinary STEM and STEAM education raises a question of pedagogical accountability: when knowledge from several disciplines enters a learning task, what shows that the contributions have become educationally consequential? Physical education teacher education (PETE) makes this question visible because STEAM resources can assist movement analysis and design while also diverting attention from movement learning. This conceptual article develops a PE-anchored account of disciplinary coordination through a purposive theoretical synthesis of 21 academic works. We propose bounded professional knowledge coordination as a way to examine how teachers frame a disciplinary problem, selectively mobilize and check external knowledge, and return the resulting explanations or designs to embodied practice. Disciplinary anchoring identifies the educational purpose without granting PE authority over the validity of other disciplines’ claims. Six proposed readiness capacities and three quality lenses translate the account into questions for curriculum and assessment. The contribution to interdisciplinary STEM/STEAM education is a provisional basis for distinguishing the presence of multiple disciplines from coordination whose consequences can be examined. Neither this account nor its downstream specifications has been empirically validated. The proposed analytical contribution is a tracea…

title: Synergistic PAM/XG Network Enables Suspension-Stable and Long-Range Collimated Abrasive Slurry Jet for Hard-Rock Drilling
abstract: Abstract Abrasive water jet (AWJ) technology is critical for unconventional natural gas extraction and hard-rock drilling. However, conventional water-based carriers suffer from rapid particle settling and severe kinetic energy attenuation, whereas single-polymer carrier fluids fail to simultaneously satisfy particle suspension, pumpability, and long-standoff jet collimation. To overcome the trade-off between suspension stability and fluid mobility, this study proposes a rigid-flexible binary polymer carrier blending polyacrylamide (PAM) and xanthan gum (XG) at an optimal mass ratio of 1:9 (1.6 wt % total concentration). Rheological and jetting characterizations demonstrate that the synergistic PAM/XG network sustains ceramsite particles for 2723 s while reducing efflux time by 14.75% compared to pure XG. Under high-pressure jetting, the fluid exhibits pronounced shear-thinning (viscosity dropping to 21 mPa·s) and achieves an 87.4% thixotropic structural recovery, generating viscoelastic hoop stresses that reduce jet expansion width by 58.3% at a 25 cm standoff distance. Consequently, at an extended standoff distance of 120 mm, the composite carrier achieves an erosion depth of 39.5 mm and a removal volume of 8.3 cm3, which represent increases of 42.1 and 260.9% over AWJ, respectively, while decreasing kinetic energy attenuation constants kH and kV by 48.3 and 49.4%. ​Integrating implementation science in psychedelic-assisted therapy research: translational research methods and design considerations
abstract: Abstract Rationale Psychedelic-assisted therapy has demonstrated efficacy in several conditions—particularly major depression and posttraumatic stress disorder—but limited implementation research may risk compromising the translation of these interventions into real-world clinical practice. Objectives Here, we identify frameworks and methods from implementation science that could be incorporated into upcoming phase 2–4 clinical trials of psychedelic-assisted therapy to inform the translation of ​ these interventions into real-world practice. Results Hybrid Type 1 trials could fill the present implementation research gap in PAT by simultaneously evaluating clinical efficacy or effectiveness, while collecting implementation data. Informed by implementation frameworks and principles, we propose two distinct prototype Hybrid Type 1 trials—a traditional two-arm effectiveness trial and a factorial optimization trial—to facilitate data collection and analyses that could inform future clinical and early implementation research. Conclusions The present co​mmunication offers a starting point for clinical researchers to identify accessible concepts, ​frameworks, and methods that could be incorporated in upcoming effectiveness and implementation research of psych​edelic-assisted therapy. The proposed research designs integrate effectiveness- and implementation approaches to support the sys…

title: Temporal dependence and variable persistence in daily fluctuations of the peso/dollar exchange rate: Mexico, 2004–2026
abstract: This study analyzes the temporal dependence of daily Mexican peso/U.S. dollar exchange-rate fluctuations over 2004–2026 using the Hurst exponent, detrended fluctuation analysis (dfa), and the semiparametric gph estimator. The sample is divided into subperiods associated with different economic and financial episodes and is complemented by a rolling-window analysis. The results reveal substantial temporal heterogeneity: Hurst, dfa, and gph estimates vary across subperiods and, in some cases, provide divergent signals. In the recursive analysis, the signal compatible with persistence remains in a majority of windows when window lengths of 181, 252, and 365 observations are considered, although mean H declines as the window length increases. The Ht – Ht (t + 1) representation also shows a concentration of estimates around central H levels of approximately H = 0.53–0.55, depending on the window length. These findings are consistent with time-varying dependence and changes in the intensity of the estimated temporal structure. The evidence does not by itself establish long memory for the entire sample, causal relationships between economic episodes and persistence, or a formal rejection of the efficient market hypothesis. The phase-space analysis is therefore interpreted as an exploratory representation of the recursive dynamics of the estimator.

title: Low-density parity-check coding for indoor LiFi: impairment-driven code design, current evidence, and open problems
abstract: Abstract Light fidelity (LiFi) operates over an intensity-modulated direct-detection channel whose impairments differ structurally from those of radio links: signals must be real and non-negative, noise is partly signal-dependent, the transmitter doubles as a luminaire and is, therefore, constrained in the run-length statistics of its output, and channel gain depends strongly on receiver position and orientation. Forward error correction for LiFi has, nonetheless, largely been inherited from radio standards rather than designed against these impairments. This review organizes the field around an impairment-to-code-property mapping: for each distinct optical impairment we identify the LDPC design lever, we find that protograph constructions have been optimized directly against optical channel statistics in several works, whereas quasi-cyclic constructions – the family with the most mature hardware support and the most direct girth control at short block length – remain almost wholly unevaluated over optical wireless channels, with a single recent exception in free-space optics. We further find that carrierless amplitude and phase modulation, despite being motivated by severe bandwidth limitation, has no published LDPC-coded evaluation. We close with open problems ordered by the same impairment map, of which quasi-cyclic construction under LiFi short-block frame constraints and c…

title: Design and Implementation of an Integrated Rainwater Harvesting System in the Hargosari Village Rest Area
abstract: Purpose: The aim of this activity is to design and implement a rainwater harvesting system that is effective, efficient, and appropriate to local conditions, as well as to increase community capacity in independent and sustainable water management. Method: Implementation methods include:survey and analysis of water needs and potential rainfall, planning the design of an integrated rainwater harvesting system participatory system development. Practical Applications: After the Rainwater Harvesting system was completed, the Rest Area now has an alternative water source derived from rainwater utilization. This condition indirectly has the potential to improve the image of the tourist area and support the economic activities of the community around the location. Conclusion: The Rainwater Harvesting system also has a positive impact on improving the quality of public facilities. The availability of water reserves ensures the operation of toilets and sanitation facilities, thereby enhancing the comfort of rest area visitors.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATION DEVELOPMENT: FROM TRIAL-AND-ERROR TO PREDICTIVE AND AUTONOMOUS FORMULATION DESIGN
abstract: Pharmaceutical formulation development has long relied on sequential experimentation in which formulation scientists select active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), excipients, compositions, and process parameters, manufacture prototypes, characterize critical quality attributes (CQAs), and iteratively modify unsuccessful formulations. While this approach remains valuable, it can become less efficient when formulation spaces expand and relationships among material attributes, process parameters, and product performance become nonlinear. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning, Bayesian optimization, natural language processing, and related computational approaches are enabling a transition toward predictive formulation development. These methods can bring together formulation composition, API descriptors, excipient characteristics, process variables, and analytical outcomes to predict CQAs such as dissolution, particle size, viscosity, stability, drug release, encapsulation efficiency, and manufacturability. Recent work has demonstrated ML-assisted excipient selection, prediction of tablet drug-release profiles, AI-assisted liquid formulation development, and Bayesian optimization for formulation experimentation. A promising next step is inverse formulation design, in which the desired product profile is specified first and algorithms identify candid…

title: The Effect of Virtual Try-On Technologies on Purchase Intention in Fashion Retailing: The Mediating Role of Perceived Product Fit
abstract: The rapid development of online fashion stores has added more challenges to the reality that consumers cannot physically analyse something like a piece of fashionable dress and buy it, especially in a size that fits. One of the biggest factors that prevents purchase intention and causes dissatisfaction and high turnover among consumers is the uncertainty related to the fittings. In turn, fashion retailers have been steadily developing virtual try-on (VTO) technologies as a new tool for assessing online products. However, the empirical findings on the usefulness of virtual try-on technologies in influencing purchase intention remain mixed, which justifies the need for a more focused conceptual framework. This concept paper examines the influence of virtual try-on technologies on purchase intention in online fashion retailing and how perceived product fit mediates this effect. The paper presents a summary of the potential theoretical and empirical sources on the subject and argues that virtual try-on technologies do not directly impact purchase intention; instead, they have an indirect impact, as they enhance consumers' confidence in the garment fit. The perceived product fit concept is theorised as being an important thinking process which minimises the uncertainty of the fit and maximises the confidence in making the decision. The article introduces a well-organised conceptual …

title: Modeling forest age and NPP and developing site index tables for the Manas River Basin, Xinjiang
abstract: Introduction The dynamic variation of net primary productivity (NPP) with forest age is crucial for evaluating forest productivity and potential carbon input. In arid regions, this process is likely modulated by water availability and site heterogeneity, although the present study focuses on characterizing the age -NPP relationship rather than directly attributing it to a specific hydrological driver. Using the Manas River Basin in Xinjiang as a case study, this research aimed to characterize the age -NPP relationships and site quality patterns of dominant tree species under arid conditions and their implications for global ecosystems of similar types. Methods This research established a forest age-NPP relationship model for four dominant tree species ( Spruce , Poplar , Elaeagnus angustifolia , and Populus euphratica ) and one mixed stand type ( Mixed wood ), and developed a site index table. Based on multi-period forest resource survey data, we systematically compared the fitting performance of five models (SEM, SDP, L, M, and Γ) and employed the guide curve method to fit tree height growth processes for compiling the site index table. Results (1) Among the five candidate models, SEM and Γ functions showed the best performance in describing the NPP -forest age relationship in arid regions, although their predictive skill varied among tree species and the mixed stand type. Dif…

title: Implementing multisensory interactions in extended reality for education: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Immersive Extended Reality (XR) technologies have increasingly been used in education, but most systems continue to engage learners primarily through visual and auditory channels. The integration of additional sensory modalities remains uneven, and evidence concerning their educational contribution is fragmented. This scoping review synthesised empirical research on multisensory XR in education, focusing on study characteristics, outcome measurement, reported user-experience and learning-performance outcomes, and technical and experimental limitations. We searched the ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus for studies published between 1 January 2016 and 9 April 2025. Following eligibility screening and forward and backward snowballing, 46 studies were subsequently included. Most included studies focused on virtual reality (VR), with Visual + Haptic and Visual + Audio + Haptic being the most common modality combinations. Haptic devices and physical objects were frequently used. Studies were concentrated in STEM, SHAPE, and medical and nursing education and typically used small to moderate samples. User experience was assessed primarily through questionnaires, whereas learning performance was evaluated mainly through knowledge tests and observable task-performance indicators. Favourable findings were frequently reported for presence, immersion, and engagement, whe…

title: P07.01.A Near-real-time virtual histology for intraoperative neuro-oncology using multiphoton microscopy in 100 neurosurgical specimens
abstract: Abstract Background Intraoperative neuro-oncology requires rapid tissue assessment while preserving diagnostically relevant morphology. Frozen sections remain the current standard but require processing time, personnel, and tissue handling that may affect specimen quality. Multiphoton microscopy (MPM) enables optical sectioning of intact tissue and generates H&E-like images after a brief staining step that typically takes less than one minute. In contrast to stain-free Raman imaging, MPM provides approximately 1 µm-resolution, cm-scale imaging without the need for excessive sample squashing. We therefore evaluated whether MPM can address routine intraoperative neuropathology questions across a heterogeneous neurosurgical cohort. Material and Methods In a prospective study, 100 intraoperative specimens from cranial, spinal, and pituitary procedures were examined using MPM. Fresh tissue samples were briefly stained and imaged without physical sectioning in an intraoperative setting to generate virtual H&E-like views. Two board-certified neuropathologists without prior experience with MPM independently reviewed the images in repeated blinded reading sessions. Final diagnoses based on routine formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded histology served as the reference standard. Reviewers were provided with limited clinical information including patient age, sex, lesion location, and suspecte…

OS09.5.A Virtual Cell Transplantation in Spatial Transcriptomics Models Tissue Context-Dependent Cell Phenotypes Across Brain States and Glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Cell states and phenotypic heterogeneity in glioblastoma are predominantly regulated by dynamic local cell-cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment. If the impact of these microenvironmental interactions can be learned, large parts of the cellular molecular programs become predictable. Here, we established GATMovin, a deep-learning framework designed to decode the local dependencies of tumor niches and predict cellular transcriptional changes ,enabling in silico simulation of cell movement and invasion across tissue contexts.We integrated multiple internal and external single-cell spatially resolved datasets across diseases (n = 12) and species (n = 2) (total 273 datasets), including Xenium human glioblastoma samples (n = 9, 5,001 genes). GATMovin uses a staged architecture: a bridge encoder maps panel expression, cell-type identity, and Nicheformer alignment features into a shared latent space; same-type nearest neighbors provide soft anchors; and donor-conditioned graph attention predicts residual latent shifts after in silico perturbations such as virtual transplantation or movement across niches, while preserving lineage cell identity. Results are explorable at gat-movin.com for interactive querying. In glioblastoma (9 Xenium samples, 5,001 genes, n = 221,847 cells), virtual relocation of T cells from tumor periphery to core produced directional shifts t…

title: Long-term effects of different straw return proportions on soil salinity-alkalinity properties, rice roots, and yield in a saline sodic paddy field
abstract: Soil salinization threatens food security and sustainable agriculture, and straw return is increasingly recognized as an effective measure to improve saline soils. However, the long-term effects of different straw return rates on soil properties, rice root traits, and yield in saline-sodic paddy fields remain unclear. We conducted a 7-year field experiment in saline-sodic rice fields to assess the effects of straw return rates (0, 2.8, 4.2, 5.6, and 7.0 t ha -1 ) on soil physicochemical properties, root morphology, root physiological activity, root ion accumulation, and rice yield. Straw return significantly reduced soil bulk density, pH, exchangeable sodium (ENa + ), and exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP), while increasing soil porosity and cation exchange capacity (CEC); however, soil properties did not differ significantly between 5.6 and 7.0 t ha -1 . High return rates (5.6 and 7.0 t ha -1 ) inhibited root growth at the mid-tillering stage in early years, but this inhibition weakened over time and eventually turned into a promoting effect. Straw return promoted root growth during middle and late growth stages, increasing rice yield by 15.60%–29.11% (four-year average). Rice yield was also significantly affected by straw return year (Y). Compared with 2017, yields in 2019, 2021, and 2023 increased by 35.02%, 41.12%, and 42.30%, respectively. Regression models showed maximu…

title: Adjunctive effects of single-plant-derived supplementation on dynamic maximal strength in adult men undertaking resistance training: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Background: Whether single-plant-derived supplements provide benefits beyond resistance training alone remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified their effects on dynamic maximal strength in adult men undertaking resistance training and examined related outcomes and potential effect modifiers. Methods This PRISMA 2020–compliant review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261468034). The search covered PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through July 1, 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials evaluated an orally administered preparation derived from a single identifiable plant species for at least 4 weeks, with resistance training identical or matched between groups, and reported a dynamic repetition-maximum strength outcome. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Pooled effects were estimated using random-effects models and expressed as Hedges' g or mean differences with 95% CIs. Results Sixteen trials involving 564 adult men contributed 17 independent comparisons. Supplementation favored upper-body ( g = 0.32, 95% CI 0.06–0.58; I 2 = 53%) and lower-body (g = 0.44, 95% CI 0.20–0.67; I 2 = 39%) dynamic maximal strength. A favorable effect was also observed for upper-body muscular endurance ( g = 0.64, 95% CI 0.22–1.06; I 2 …

title: Identification of key pathways and functional modules associated with multiple abiotic and biotic stress conditions in barley
abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) is frequently exposed to diverse abiotic and biotic stresses that threaten its productivity and quality. This study aimed to identify key pathways, gene modules, and hub genes associated with multiple stress conditions in barley using a weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). A total of 515 RNA-Seq samples representing 14 different stress types were integrated and analyzed to construct a comprehensive co-expression network. Eleven distinct gene modules were identified, five of which showed significant correlations with abiotic and/or biotic stresses. Functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction (PPI) analyses revealed that these modules are primarily involved in energy metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, carbon metabolism, and protein processing—pathways critical for stress adaptation. The black and pink modules were associated with metabolic regulation and structural stability under abiotic stress, whereas the blue and green modules were linked to protein turnover and pathogen response during biotic stress. The red module highlighted the downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation under both stress types, indicating energy conservation mechanisms. Collectively, these findings provide novel insights into the coordinated transcriptional networks that regulate stress resilience in barley and identify potential molecular targets …

title: From Enforced Rivalry to Resistant Kinship: Female Solidarity, Domestic Sovereignty, and the Reconfiguration of Patriarchal Power in Khaled Hosseini’s A Thousand Splendid Suns
abstract: Khaled Hosseini's A Thousand Splendid Suns (2007) examines the relationship between patriarchal domination, female subjectivity and collective resistance through the changing relationship between Mariam and Laila, two women compelled to inhabit the same marriage and domestic environment. Although existing scholarship has explored sisterhood, gendered violence and women's resistance in the novel, the relationship between enforced rivalry and the redistribution of authority within the household requires more precise attention. This article argues that Hosseini represents female solidarity not merely as emotional companionship but as a gradual challenge to the domestic arrangements through which patriarchal power maintains women's separation and dependence. Employing theoretically informed close reading, the study examines Rasheed's manipulation of marital hierarchy, Mariam and Laila's initial antagonism, the formation of trust through caregiving and shared vulnerability, and the political consequences of their collective resistance. Drawing upon feminist theories of patriarchal bargaining, relational agency, coercive control and the gendered production of space, the article proposes counter-domestic sovereignty as a bounded interpretive concept describing women's capacity to reorganize relationships, obligations and decisions within a household formally controlled by male authori…
venue: Journal of Social Sciences, Humanities and Innovation

title: A new piece of the Butia archeri complex (Arecaceae)
abstract: Background and aims – Butia archeri is a species complex from the Brazilian Central Plateau that comprises unresolved species. One of these populations, with collection records from the 1950s, has recently been documented on YouTube, prompting field surveys. Material and methods – Following standard methodology, the pinnae and flowers were analysed by using LM (free-hand transverse sections) and SEM. At this point we compared the morphoanatomy of the new species, Butia cerussa sp. nov., with that of B. archeri and the other recognized species of the complex. We made an identification key and an updated distribution map of the complex. Key results – Butia cerussa sp. nov. can be differentiated from B. archeri by a series of striking characters. Among these, congested light purple flowers stand out, as do pistillate and staminate flowers of distinct sizes. The white pulverulent aspect of the rachis and rachillae of the inflorescence is also a noticeable and unprecedented characteristic for the genus. Anatomically, there are also distinctive differences between B. cerussa sp. nov. and B. archeri , notably the absence of raphides and the fact that the accessory bundles do not surround the fibrous ring completely in the new species. Conclusion – Endemic to the Cerrado sensu stricto, its type population is located near charcoal-burning and mining activities, highlighting the urgency …

title: Effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation on medical students’ learning outcomes
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) holds broad application prospects in medical education; however, systematic empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness in facilitating case discussions and virtual patient consultation remains scarce. This study recruited undergraduate medical students and conducted experiments to examine the pedagogical effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation. Methods A total of 207 medical undergraduates participated in this study. Using the self-developed intelligent experimental platform, medical students engaged in AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation. Experiment 1 employed a single-factor, three-level between-subjects design to compare the effects of AI-assisted case discussion, peer case discussion, and a lecture-only control condition on medical students’ knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and interaction quality. Experiment 2 utilized a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design to examine the effects of virtual patient consultation and the sequencing of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation on medical students’ knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and consultation process quality. The control group participants were the same individuals across both experiments. Results Results indicated that the AI-assisted case discussion group achieved significantly hi…

title: Stand density and pruning shape leaf pressure-volume traits and their coordination with functional traits in a poplar plantation
abstract: Stand density and pruning are silvicultural measures used to modify canopy structure and resource distribution in plantations. However, their effects on within-growing-season and canopy-position variation in leaf pressure-volume (PV) traits, their coordination with functional traits, and the scale dependence of these relationships remain unclear. To address these questions, we investigated Populus tomentosa plantations in northern China subjected to two stand densities and three pruning intensities, using leaf samples collected monthly from top and bottom canopy positions from May to October 2024. The results showed that leaf PV traits varied markedly by month and canopy position. Canopy differences emerged mainly from August to October, with bottom canopy leaves generally showing more negative osmotic potentials than top canopy leaves. Leaf osmotic potential at full turgor ( Ψ sat ) and water potential at the turgor loss point ( Ψ tlp ) generally reached their most negative values from June to August and became less negative thereafter, whereas bulk modulus of elasticity (ϵ) showed a corresponding mid-season increase, and leaf capacitance ( C leaf ) remained relatively stable across months. Lower stand density and heavier pruning were generally associated with more negative osmotic potentials. PV traits showed significant, trait-specific associations with leaf morphology and g…

title: Evolution and expression of mitochondrial pyruvate carrier genes in upland cotton under salt and drought stresses
abstract: Background The mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) transports cytosolic pyruvate across the inner mitochondrial membrane, linking glycolysis to the tricarboxylic acid cycle and to respiratory energy supply. MPC genes have been characterized in a few model plants, yet nothing is known about this family in upland cotton, whose productivity is strongly limited by drought and salinity. Methods Here we present a genome-wide identification of the MPC family in upland cotton, combining sequence analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, synteny and duplication-mode assignment, promoter analysis, transcriptome profiling and RT-qPCR. Results We identified 11 GhMPC genes in upland cotton, distributed across both the A and D subgenomes. The 11 genes formed two clades that differed in intron number, and their promoters carried matches in motifs associated with abiotic stresses. Transcriptome profiling revealed time-dependent responses to salt and osmotic stress that culminated around 12 h, and co-expression network analysis placed GhMPC-9 at a hub position under both stresses, with GhMPC-8 additionally prominent in the drought module. RT-qPCR confirmed significant induction of both genes in leaves under salt and drought, with the most consistent responses at 12 h. Conclusion This work provides the first systematic overview of the MPC family in cotton and lays a foundation for further function…

title: A data-driven multidimensional framework for physiological emotion characterisation in immersive virtual reality
abstract: Abstract Objective. Current affective computing relies on supervised models constrained by predefined frameworks such as the valence–arousal circumplex, precluding discovery of intrinsic physiological structures and obscuring inter-individual variability in emotional response. This study investigates the physiological organization of emotional states through an unsupervised, data-driven framework applied to multimodal physiological recordings acquired in virtual reality (VR). Approach. Thirty-eight healthy participants underwent a 35 min VR protocol inducing seven emotions—Relaxation, Happiness, Sadness, Fear, Disgust, Empathy, and Frustration—via custom immersive scenarios. Simultaneous recordings of electroencephalographic, electrocardiographic, blood volume pulse, galvanic skin response, and respiration signals were acquired; 74 features were extracted and reduced to 36 via correlation-based selection. Principal component analysis (PCA) identified latent physiological dimensions, and K -means clustering was applied within each emotion to characterise inter-individual variability. Main results. PCA revealed four physiologically interpretable dimensions, collectively explaining 40.1% of total variance, capturing distinct autonomic, cardiovascular, and neural signatures of emotional responding. Subjective arousal was broadly reflected in one component, but no dimension mapped o…

title: ESAP-SAM: a power-grid facility segmentation model integrating multiscale adaptation and boundary refinement
abstract: Segmenting power-grid facilities in high-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle imagery is challenging because transmission lines are extremely elongated, backgrounds are complex, and general-purpose foundation models may lose high-frequency details or overfit small domain-specific datasets. We propose ESAP-SAM, an automatic segmentation framework built on the Segment Anything Model (SAM). ESAP-SAM freezes the SAM image backbone and introduces an Efficient Multiscale (EMS) Adapter, a Hybrid Prompt (HP) encoder, and a Boundary-Refinement Attention (BRA) module. The EMS Adapter preserves multiscale and direction-dependent features, while the HP encoder generates image-derived dense prompts for automatic inference. The BRA module uses edge cues to refine decoded features and improve contour continuity and localization. On the Transmission Towers and Power Lines (TTPLA) dataset, ESAP-SAM achieved 91.02% precision, 85.88% recall, and 88.37% F1. It also achieved 82.43% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 81.56% average path length similarity (APLS). For the Power Line Dataset (PLD), the listed values were 90.64% precision, 84.86% recall, 87.65% F1, 84.34% mIoU, and 81.98% APLS. ESAP-SAM ranked first on all five metrics in both comparison tables. The results show that parameter-efficient adaptation, automatic prompt generation, and boundary refinement can jointly improve overlap accurac…

title: A multi-period temporal consensus framework for mapping future suitable habitats of nine Camellia oilseed species in China
abstract: Oilseed Camellia species are important perennial woody oil resources in China, but their long production cycles and contrasting ecological requirements increase their vulnerability to climate driven changes in habitat suitability. Identifying areas with persistent climatic suitability is therefore critical for long term cultivation, introduction, and germplasm conservation. In this study, we used ensemble species distribution models to assess the current and future climatic suitability of nine oilseed Camellia species in China under SSP2-4.5 and applied a multi-period temporal consensus framework to identify habitats remaining suitable across 2041–2060, 2061–2080, and 2081–2100. We also quantified species-specific environmental controls and shifts in suitability centroids. The nine species showed marked climatic niche differentiation, with annual mean temperature, temperature seasonality, mean diurnal range, precipitation during dry or cold periods, and annual precipitation emerging as major constraints. Current suitable habitats were concentrated mainly in subtropical China, whereas temporally stable suitable areas were consistently smaller and differed substantially among species. Camellia drupifera , Camellia oleifera , and Camellia semiserrata retained relatively large stable areas, while Camellia saluenensis showed the lowest climatic persistence. Future suitability also s…

Apparent Power as a Unifying Metric for Frontal Polymerization
abstract: Abstract In self-sustained transformations such as frontal polymerization, the balance between power generated and power transfer governs propagation dynamics. Herein, we demonstrate the use of an experimentally practical apparent power expression to characterize frontal polymerization. We validated our expression by frontally polymerizing 1,5-cyclooctadiene, dicyclopentadiene, and 5-ethylidene-2-norbornene at various initiator loadings, finding a strong correlation between apparent power and reaction propagation. Raising a system’s apparent power drove a progressive transition in the observed front regime, from quenched through unstable to uniform. We further demonstrated that modulating apparent power influences backbone isomerization and polymer morphology. To further validate our expression, we used heat sinks to vary the reaction power, linking distinct front regimes with apparent power values. Geometric normalization extended this framework to literature examples and frontal radical polymerization, allowing for meaningful comparisons across variable reaction systems and mechanisms. This analytical tool offers a more holistic comparison of monomers and reaction mechanisms that otherwise differ in their thermodynamics and kinetics.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Peer Growth Group Intervention to Enhance Psychological Resilience in Early Career Nurses: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Early career nurses face significant occupational pressures and risks, making psychological resilience critical for effective management of workplace stress. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a theory-driven resilience-building intervention for early career nurses. Method: This study adopted a two-arm, 1:1 pilot randomized controlled trial design to evaluate the effectiveness of a bi-weekly, eight-session resilience intervention for early career nurses. Outcome was measured by the Nurse Resilience Scale, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and general self-efficacy scale. Results: Twenty-seven nurses were randomly assigned to an intervention group ( n = 13) or a wait-list control group ( n = 14). The intervention significantly improved overall nurse resilience ( p = .016), and no significant between-group differences were found in self-efficacy (overall p = .98). Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that a structured, theory-driven intervention can effectively enhance resilience among early career nurses, which highlights the intervention's practical utility in fostering adaptive coping mechanisms.
venue: The Journal of Continuing Education in Nursing

title: Concentration-Induced BiVO4/V2O5 Phase Separation Enables Porous Thick-Film Photoanodes for Solar Water Oxidation
abstract: Abstract Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting is a promising approach for sustainable hydrogen production by directly converting solar energy into chemical fuels. In this work, thick (∼40 μm) BiVO4 photoanodes containing an intrinsic BiVO4/V2O5 heterojunction were fabricated by spin coating through controlled adjustment of precursor concentration. Increasing the precursor concentration promoted the in situ formation of a BiVO4/V2O5 thick-film with a porous architecture, delivering a photocurrent density of 1.5 mA cm–2 at 1.2 V vs Ag/AgCl (or 0.13 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs RHE)—approximately 100 times that of the dilute S0.03M precursor reference. Structural, optical, and electronic characterization indicates that the enhancement arises from the combined effects of increased light harvesting, a V2O5-rich near-surface region, heterojunction-modified electronic states, and improved electrolyte accessibility throughout the porous film. UV–Vis spectroscopy, ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS), reflection electron energy-loss spectroscopy (REELS), and Mott–Schottky probe different regions of the electronic structure, with surface-sensitive measurements reflecting near-surface states and UV–vis measurements capturing bulk optical transitions. Selective removal of V2O5 preserved the porous BiVO4 framework but reduced the photocurrent by a factor of approximately 2.5, confirmi…

title: EP09.17 Radiotherapy Peer Review in Neuro-Oncology: A Survey of United Kingdom Professionals
abstract: Abstract Introduction Radiotherapy peer review is a key component of quality assurance in neuro-oncology, given the anatomical complexity and proximity to critical structures. However, variation in practice and implementation is not well characterised within or between European health systems. We evaluated current peer review practice across neuro-oncology services in the United Kingdom (UK). Methods A national online survey was developed by the Peer Review Working Group convened by the Tessa Jowell Academy (a networking and learning platform for neuro-oncology professionals). The survey was distributed between October and December 2025. Questions addressed peer review structure, scope, multidisciplinary involvement, use of artificial intelligence (AI), and perceived impact. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics at both institutional and practitioner levels. Results Seventy-two clinicians from 38 hospitals responded, representing 29 of 30 UK neuro-oncology networks and one centre in the Republic of Ireland. Most respondents were oncologists (83%), and 47% had over 10 years’ experience. Structure: Peer review was widely implemented, with 79% (30/38) of hospitals reviewing all cases and 76% (29/38) holding weekly meetings. However, 38% (27/72) of respondents reported insufficient protected time, and 5% (2/38) reported no routine peer review. Scope and practice: Most cen…

title: Exclusion before displacement and the reorganization of waste access in Makassar’s waste-to-energy transition
abstract: Makassar’s waste-to-energy (WtE) transition is promoted as a technological response to urban waste and clean-energy challenges, yet its social consequences remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates how planned WtE development restructures power relations, access to waste resources, and livelihood security among waste-dependent communities around the Tamangapa disposal site. A qualitative case study combined in-depth interviews with eight key informants, an informal small-group discussion, participant observation, and document analysis, supported by a descriptive survey of 98 purposively selected respondents. Findings indicate that planned WtE arrangements position municipal waste increasingly as industrial feedstock alongside existing informal material-recovery practices. This creates an anticipatory mechanism of material exclusion through reduced or uncertain access to recoverable waste and procedural exclusion through unequal access to project information and environmental-risk knowledge. Survey findings show substantial livelihood vulnerability, limited understanding of WtE technology, high perceived ecological risk, and strong support for community monitoring and protection mechanisms. Conceptually, the study shows that exclusion can emerge through the reorganization of practical access before formal displacement occurs, revealing an anticipatory form of envir…

title: Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer for Vehicle-to-Grid Services: Converter Control, Power Quality and Grid-Interface Behaviour
abstract: Bidirectional wireless power transfer lets parked electric vehicles provide vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services without a plug, but its converter control and grid-interface behaviour have rarely been studied together. This paper presents a simulation-based study of a 7.7-kW, 85-kHz double-sided inductor-capacitor-capacitor (LCC) wireless charger connected to a 230-V, 50-Hz single-phase grid through an LCL-filtered active front end. A fundamental and multi-harmonic model of the wireless link is derived and cross-checked against 240 switching-level MATLAB/Simulink operating points (mean power error 0.26%, maximum 3.5%). Single-, dual- and zero-voltage-switching (ZVS)-constrained triple-phase-shift (SPS, DPS, TPS) modulation are synthesised by optimisation and embedded in a cascaded controller with a second-order-generalised-integrator-phase-locked loop (SOGI-PLL), DC-link power feed-forward, proportional-resonant current control and IEEE Std 1547-2018 frequency-watt and volt-var functions. With SPS, the grid-to-battery efficiency at 1.54 kW is 69.8% (charging) and 59.7% (V2G); DPS and TPS raise it above 90% and reach 91.8%–92.2% at rated power, TPS avoiding hard switching at every simulated point, with partial ZVS at some edges. The charger reverses its ±7.7-kW range within 22 ms at the grid, keeps the current total demand distortion (TDD) below 0.8% with a distorted grid voltage, fol…

title: Socio-economic and geographic determinants of solar photovoltaic adoption in post-conflict Somalia: evidence of energy leapfrogging from a nationally representative survey
abstract: Background In fragile and post-conflict settings such as Somalia, decentralized solar photovoltaic (PV) systems may extend electricity access where centralized grids remain limited. Nationally representative evidence on household solar adoption remains scarce. This study examines socio-economic, infrastructural, and geographic factors associated with household solar PV adoption using Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory and the Energy Ladder Hypothesis. DOI frames technology diffusion across households, while the Energy Ladder perspective helps interpret energy choices in relation to resources and access. Methods Data were drawn from the nationally representative Somali Integrated Household Budget Survey (SIHBS) 2022. The household was the unit of analysis. Household-head records were retained, the solar outcome and 13 candidate predictors were harmonized from survey variables, and complete-case analysis without imputation yielded N = 6,883 households. Solar adoption was coded as binary. Bivariate associations were assessed using Pearson chi-square tests and one-way ANOVA, followed by variance inflation factor and tolerance diagnostics. Four specifications—logit, probit, complementary log-log (cloglog), and penalized logistic/Lasso—were fitted and compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. The cloglog model provided the best fit; results are reported as exponentia…

title: Statistical Energy Budget of the Solar Wind with Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter. I. Unbalanced Total Energy Radial Evolution
abstract: Abstract The magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) description of the solar wind has long been regarded as one of the most successful frameworks for investigating solar wind heating and acceleration. Under a set of simplifying assumptions, it provides a reduced large-scale description that is widely used to study the energetic role of electromagnetic fluctuations in the solar wind energy budget. In practice, applying simplification to MHD can result in the loss of some physics compared to an exact set of equations. However, an observational energy budget can help us to verify whether any energetic information has been lost in the process of simplification. To do so, we directly test the validity of the large-scale nonlinear ideal MHD energy budget with solar wind observations from the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and the Solar Orbiter (SO). After verifying the reliability of the measurements through comparison with previous studies of similar solar wind properties, we test the conservation of the total energy predicted by the MHD theory. We find that the average total energy increases with radial distance by 49% (±9%) between 14 and 203 solar radii. The increase in kinetic energy is not sufficiently compensated by the decrease of the thermal and electromagnetic contributions. We investigate the major sources of observational uncertainty and find that they cannot account for the observed energy…

title: Beyond Halal Certification: Capacity Gaps and the Global Competitiveness of Indonesian MSMEs in Accessing International Markets
abstract: Aim: This article examines the distance between holding a halal certificate and actually being ready to operate in foreign markets among Indonesian micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It also pinpoints structural obstacles and proposes ways to build firm capabilities. Worldwide Muslim consumer expenditure is forecast to grow from roughly US$2.4 trillion in 2023 to US$3.4 trillion in 2028, but MSMEs, which generate about 60.5% of GDP and provide 97% of jobs, account for only around 15.7% of national exports. Method: We carried out a systematic literature review following PRISMA 2020 reporting rules. Five databases returned 1,248 records; 987 remained for screening once duplicates were removed, 249 full texts were appraised, and 10 studies were synthesised thematically. Results: Certification appears to be a precondition for being accepted in the market, not an advantage in its own right, and the compulsory phase for micro and small enterprises, effective 18 October 2026, makes it a minimum standard. The heaviest constraints are production capacity, access to finance, the cost of traceability, and coordination among institutions. Among 212 Indonesian halal SMEs, backing from Islamic financial institutions and government influenced performance solely via internal capabilities. Firm-level proof that certification raises the exports of Indonesian halal MSMEs is still rare.…
venue: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies

title: Moderate-Intensity Interval Training Is Sufficient to Increase Muscle Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity and Exercise Tolerance in Young Untrained Men
abstract: Introduction: There is considerable evidence that physical activity can stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in muscles, enhance maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, improve physical fitness, and help maintain overall health in humans. On the other hand, there is growing evidence that excessive training load may have a detrimental effect on mitochondria and glucose homeostasis. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) would be sufficient to increase muscle mitochondrial oxidative capacity and exercise tolerance in untrained healthy people. Methods: Eleven young, healthy, untrained males took part in this study. They performed a 7-week endurance training program (MIIT) on a cycle ergometer, composed of 4 sessions per week, each lasting 40 min. Before and after the MIIT training program, a pulmonary maximal oxygen consumption (V̇O 2max ) as well as lactate threshold (LT) were determined and a muscle biopsy from the m. vastus lateralis was taken to evaluate the level of muscle proteins related to energy metabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis, and to measure the muscle's maximal mitochondrial respiration rate. Results: The training resulted in an increase of skeletal muscle homogenate V̇O 2max (by ~50%, P =0.001), due to increased mitochondrial mass and the enrichment of mitochondria with the individual respiratory chain complexes. The M…

title: Strengthening Community Capacity through Waste Sorting Education and Composting Technology
abstract: Purpose: This community engagement aimed to strengthen household waste management capacity in Sukalaksana, Curug District, Serang City, by improving community knowledge and practical skills in waste sorting and organic waste processing. Method: A participatory approach was implemented through socialization, demonstrations, hands-on practices, and mentoring. The activities introduced two appropriate technologies, namely Compost Biopores and Composters. Participants practiced preparing organic waste, installing biopore containers, applying EM4, assembling composters, and applying decomposition solutions. Practical Applications: The program provided communities with practical knowledge and applicable technologies for processing organic household waste at its source. The activities also encouraged community participation and supported the development of environmentally responsible waste management practices. Conclusion: The program strengthened community engagement and practical capacity in organic waste processing. Compost Biopores and Composters offer simple, replicable alternatives for household-scale waste management and can support sustainable community-based waste reduction.

title: Constitutional capacity and political selection: the feasible set of political rules
Empowering Rural Aquaculture Security: A Participatory CCTV Optimization and Capacity Building Strategy in BUMDes Marga Jaya, East Lampung
abstract: Purpose: Rural Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) operating aquaculture units often face severe financial vulnerabilities and loss of Village Native Income (PADes) due to recurring night-time fish poaching and asset theft. This study evaluates and optimizes the existing CCTV infrastructure at BUMDes Marga Jaya, East Lampung, through a participatory community empowerment framework. Method: Executed under a 40-day Thematic Community Service (KKN-T) program by ITS NU Lampung, this project combined descriptive qualitative case study methods with a 4-stage community engagement strategy involving socialization, participatory technical auditing, hands-on training for four primary BUMDes operators/guards, and SOP formalization. Practical Applications: The program successfully upgraded network configurations, eliminated blind spots, conducted mobile app training, established bi-weekly maintenance SOPs, and integrated off-grid UPS/solar planning approved through village development deliberations. Conclusion: Combining optimized real-time CCTV technology with intensive community capacity building achieved zero theft incidents, enhanced internal labor discipline, and established a scalable model demonstrating how higher education partnerships bridge the digital divide for rural enterprise sustainability.

title: The interactive effect of intellectual capital and knowledge-centric culture on organisational performance: the sequential roles of knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability
abstract: Purpose Guided by the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how intellectual capital – comprising human, structural and relational capital – contributes to organisational performance through organisational knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability as serial mediators. In addition, the study examined the moderating role of a knowledge-centric culture. Design/methodology/approach The data were collected from employees at high-tech companies in China. Hypotheses were tested using Mplus (v.8.6). Findings The results indicate that human, structural and relational capital positively enhance organisational knowledge absorption capacity, thereby promoting innovation capability and improving organisational performance. The findings further support a serial mediation process whereby intellectual capital influences organisational performance through knowledge absorption and innovation capability. Moreover, a knowledge-centric culture strengthens the relationship between intellectual capital and knowledge absorption capacity, thereby amplifying the indirect effects on organisational performance. Originality/value This study offers an integrated explanation of how intellectual capital drives organisational performance through organisational knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability. Identifying knowledge-centric culture as a key boundary condition moves …

title: Insights into the Physiological and Molecular Mechanism in Root Formation of Semi-lignified Branches Cuttings of Aquilaria sinensis
abstract: Aquilaria sinensis, a key agarwood source, faces population decline from overharvesting, necessitating urgent development of efficient breeding methods for conservation and economic purpose. Cutting propagation is viable, but A. sinensis’ difficult-to-root characteristic limits efficiency. Therefore, we systematically evaluated the effects of growth regulator concentration, substrate, and trimming techniques on the rooting of semi woody cuttings through orthogonal experiments combined with physiological trait detection and transcriptome analysis. The optimal treatment involved treating flat trimmed cuttings with 200 ppm ABT-6 and inserting them into a loess:peat soil (1:2) substrate. This combination achieved a maximum rooting rate of 71.25%. The rooting of cuttings involves three stages: induction (0-30 days), expression (30-40 days), and extension (40-60 days). During root induction, ABT treatment increased endogenous IAA, ZR, and GA3 levels while suppressing ABA, establishing a hormone balance beneficial for adventitious root initiation. Besides, it also changed the activities of key enzymes (POD, IAAO, and PPO) and content of nutrients, but the changing trends were different. The transcriptome analysis showed that 93 DEGs identified in phytohormone signal transduction pathway. Our results significantly improve the rooting efficiency of A. sinensis cuttings and provide an in…

title: Temperature-Regulated Dispersion and Filter Cake Formation Mechanism of Organo-Montmorillonite in Oil-Based Drilling Fluids
abstract: Abstract Maintaining stable rheological properties and effective fluid loss performance under high-temperature conditions remains a critical challenge for oil-based drilling fluids (OBDFs). Organo-montmorillonite (OMt) is widely used as a multifunctional additive in OBDFs; however, the effects of quaternary ammonium salt molecular structure and high temperature on OMt dispersion, filter cake formation, and fluid loss control mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, OMt modified with quaternary ammonium salts featuring different alkyl chain lengths and chain numbers was dispersed in white oil to investigate how modifier structure and thermal treatment influence fluid loss through changes in OMt dispersion and filter cake formation. The results demonstrate that alkyl chain structure governs the dispersion, exfoliation, and network-forming capability of OMt in the oil phase. Compared with single-chain modified OMt systems, double-chain DC18-Mt exhibits stronger exfoliation and network-forming ability, promoting the formation of a three-dimensional network structure and enhancing viscosity, yield point, and viscoelastic properties. Moreover, DC18-Mt forms a continuous and compact filter cake, whereas C18-Mt and C22-Mt generate loose and porous filter cakes, resulting in inferior fluid loss control capability. Mechanistic analysis reveals that high temperature regulates fluid loss …

title: Stereo- and Enantioselective Living Coordination Chain Transfer Cyclopolymerization of 2-Methyl-1,5-Hexadiene: A Kinetic Ratchet Mechanism for the Polymerizability of α,ω-Dienes over α-Olefins
abstract: Abstract Stereo- and enantioselective living coordination cyclopolymerization of 2-methyl-1,5-hexadiene (2-MHD) using a set of cyclopentadienyl, amidinate (CPAM) group 4 metal pre-initiators, in combination with a borate co-initiator, has been reported to produce different stereochemical microstructures of poly(methylene-1,3-(1-methyl)cyclopentane) (PMMCP). Living chain transfer cyclopolymerization of 2-MHD has also been achieved in the presence of excess equivalents of ZnEt2 to provide low molar mass, end-group-functionalized PMMCP of narrow dispersity upon a reactive quench with iodine. Successful use of 2-MHD as a monomer and prior observation of selective polymerizability of 1,5-hexadiene over 1-hexene using the sterically encumbered homochiral pre-initiator (SC, SZr)-4 are rationalized by a kinetic ratchet mechanism accessible to α,ω-nonconjugated dienes but not α-olefins. These results serve to extend the mechanistic picture of coordination cyclopolymerization of α,ω-nonconjugated dienes and provide a foundation for the design of "next-generation" polyolefins.

title: A novel mechanism of Mogroside V in Parkinson’s disease: inhibition of neuroinflammation via the COX-2/IL-17A pathway
abstract: Background Neuroinflammation is a major factor in Parkinson’s disease (PD). This study examined the neuroprotective effects and mechanisms of Mogroside V (MV), known for its anti-inflammatory properties, on PD. Methods In vivo PD mouse models were developed with striatal injections of rotenone (Rot) or α-synuclein preformed fibrils (α-Syn PFF), while the PD monkey model used PFF. 10 mg/kg MV was administered orally to mice before PD induction. Mice’s motor function, dopaminergic damage, α-Syn pathology, and inflammation were assessed. In vitro , 100 μmol/L MV was tested on SH-SY5Y cells treated with Rot or α-Syn with cell viability, reactive oxygen species release (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), adenosine triphosphate (ATP) assays. MV’s targets and pathways were identified by network pharmacology and RNA transcriptome analysis, validated and confirmed by cellular thermal shift assay, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation. Changes of target protein expression were confirmed in PD patients’ plasma with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and PD monkeys’ substantia nigra with Western blot analysis. Results MV markedly improved motor abilities of Rot- and α-Syn-induced PD mice, including increasing 13.53 mm/s and 17.20 mm/s of average movement speed in the open field ( P < 0.01, P < 0.001), prolonging 98.40 s and 53.40 s of the latency to fall from the…

title: Mechanism for Utilizing Academic Supervision Findings in Setting Priorities and Evaluating Follow-Up Actions for Instructional Improvement in Madrasah
abstract: Academic supervision supports instructional quality through observation, feedback, guidance, and evaluation. However, its findings are not always systematically used to determine improvement priorities and follow-up actions. This study examines how supervision findings guide instructional improvement in madrasah. A Systematic Literature Review guided by PRISMA 2020 principles searched Scopus and Google Scholar for publications from 2016 to 2026. Of 62 identified sources, 59 were accessible and screened, and 22 met the inclusion criteria. Articles addressing academic or instructional supervision, teacher development, supervision findings, feedback, coaching, follow-up, or instructional improvement were included; irrelevant, duplicate, inaccessible, and bibliographically unverifiable sources were excluded. Data were extracted using a literature matrix and analyzed thematically to identify patterns in supervision practices, interpretation, priority setting, follow-up, and evaluation. The analysis produced six stages: collection, interpretation and diagnosis, priority setting, follow-up planning, implementation of improvement actions, and evaluation and reflection. The model’s conceptual contribution is to position priority setting as an explicit decision-making stage, align follow-up with diagnosed teacher needs, and use evaluation to guide subsequent improvement. The model offers…
