title: Maternal and Child Health and Well-Being: A Lifecourse and Systems-Based Perspective on Integrated Care and Health Equity
abstract: Introduction: Maternal and child health remains a global public health priority amid persistent inequities in access to healthcare, preventable morbidity, and intergenerational health outcomes. Fragmented services frequently disrupt continuity of care across pregnancy, childbirth, the postpartum period, and early childhood. This study aimed to develop a conceptual framework integrating lifecourse and systems-based perspectives to strengthen integrated maternal and child healthcare and advance health equity. Methods: An integrative literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed empirical and conceptual studies retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science. Eligible publications in English addressed maternal and child health, integrated care, health equity, and related determinants. Following systematic screening and eligibility assessment, 78 studies were included in the thematic synthesis and conceptual framework development. Results: The synthesis identified interconnected biological, social, economic, community, and health-system determinants shaping maternal and child health across the lifecourse. Integrated care connecting antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal, and pediatric services emerged as a critical pathway for strengthening continuity, early risk identification, and coordinated care. Primary healthcare integration, community-based interventions, and multisectora…
venue: International Journal of Health and Social Sciences

title: The pre-activation ecotone: a conceptual framework for unscheduled care and the emerging role of mobile integrated healthcare
abstract: Purpose To define the “pre-activation ecotone” as a conceptual framework for unscheduled care, representing the interval between recognition of a health need and formal health system entry, and to examine its implications for care delivery design, patient decision-making, and system integration. Design/methodology/approach A targeted narrative synthesis of literature spanning ecology, emergency medicine, health services research, and public health. Sources were identified through targeted database searches (PubMed, Scopus), gray literature review, and reference chaining, with emphasis on studies and models addressing unscheduled care access, system design, and cross-sector coordination. Because the manuscript is intended as a conceptual framework rather than a formal review of all available evidence, studies were not systematically appraised or graded. Findings In the United States, current approaches to unscheduled care prioritize expansion of episodic access points, with limited attention to the pre-engagement setting where patient-driven decisions under uncertainty often lead to emergency system activation. Evidence from emergency medical services and health services research identifies this interval as functionally distinct yet structurally underdeveloped. Mobile integrated healthcare is emerging within this space, demonstrating feasibility in addressing unmet care needs an…

title: Church Attendance Management System Based on Edge AI and MobileNetV2
abstract: Purpose: Manual attendance recording in religious institutions is inefficient and limits demographic analytics. This paper presents an edge-based face recognition system deploying MobileNetV2 on Raspberry Pi 5 for automated church attendance tracking with complete local biometric processing. Method: The system integrates with a web-based platform for demographic management and synod-compliant reporting. An 8-week field evaluation at GKI Karawaci involved 412 active congregants (drawn from a total registry of 1,247) across 32 services. The system achieved 96.8% recognition accuracy, 247 ms end-to-end latency (~4 FPS), and 8.2 W power consumption. Practical Applications: Compared to manual methods, the system eliminated per-service recording time, reduced data entry errors by 93.6%, decreased monthly administrative effort by 67.4%, and improved demographic data accuracy from 64.3% to 98.7%. Local processing ensures privacy without cloud dependency. Conclusion: This work validates deployed face recognition as a cost-effective, ethically grounded solution for improving operational efficiency in religious and resource-constrained community settings.

title: Stakeholder digital readiness for AI-driven dengue surveillance and reporting system
abstract: Background As the public health sector moves towards digital health transformation, artificial intelligence offers opportunities to improve disease surveillance, early disease detection and strengthen reporting systems. However, the adoption of these technologies depends on stakeholder knowledge, readiness, and practices. Therefore, this study assesses stakeholders’ awareness, preventative practices, digital access, and readiness for dengue surveillance in Kingston, Jamaica. Methods The study employed a cross-sectional quantitative mixed-mode survey. The questionnaire comprised of multiple choice and open-ended questions with 397 participants and 391 eligible data registrations. Participants were recruited through online channels and in-person paper-based questionnaires administered at healthcare facilities across Kingston. Quantitative data was analyzed descriptively on SPSS Version 30 with Pearson Chi-square tests and a p -value of ≤ 0.05, while qualitative components were thematically analyzed. Findings Results reveal that 72.1% of the participants reported having high readiness, 10.2% reported moderate digital readiness and 17.6% reported low readiness. 96.4% of the study participants expressed willingness to adopt AI-driven digital health tools. Yet only 31.1% of the participants who answered the question indicated high confidence, while 50.4% of the study respondents indi…

title: Explaining citizen complaints against the police: organizational, environmental and system factors
abstract: Purpose The study aims to examine variation in citizen complaints against police departments, with particular attention to how organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems shape complaint volume. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 129 large U.S. municipal police departments, this study employs stepwise negative binomial regression to assess the impact of organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems on complaint volume. Findings Organizational characteristics – particularly department size and educational requirements – emerge as significant predictors of complaint volume, with larger agencies generating more complaints and those requiring education beyond high school generating fewer. In contrast, community-level variables such as crime rates, unemployment and racial composition show limited explanatory power. Importantly, features of citizen complaint systems play a meaningful role. Departments that allow third-party complaints and avoid penalties for false reporting exhibit different complaint patterns, suggesting that system accessibility influences complaint levels. Moreover, the relationship between in-service training and complaints varies depending on complaint system openness, indicating that training effectiveness may depend on broader accountability structures. Practical imp…

title: On the Nature of the Be Star/White Dwarf System Nova FQ Circinus
abstract: Abstract The classical nova FQ Cir has recently been shown to have a Be star donor, and has been identified as a high mass cataclysmic variable (HMCV), with an orbital period of ∼2.04 days (twice the 1.02 day periodogram peak). Using the extensive OGLE optical archive, together with existing observations from ASAS-SN, we instead find significant modulation between ∼50 and 60 days and propose that the orbital period is likely closer to ∼62 days. We interpret the low-amplitude 1.02 day modulation as a nonradial pulsation of the Be star. We also reassess the HMCV classification based on properties of known Be star-white dwarf systems.

title: Indian Farm Distress Early Warning System – Phase 1
abstract: Agricultural distress in India can arise from the combined effects of rainfall variability, changes in crop production, fluctuations in agricultural market prices and difficulties associated with agricultural credit. Although information relating to these factors is available through different public institutions, the data are maintained in separate systems and may differ in format, coverage and frequency of update. This Phase I paper proposes the design and development of an Indian Farm Distress Early Warning System that will integrate four categories of public data: rainfall information from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), crop production and yield information from the Ministry of Agriculture, market-price information from AGMARKNET, and agricultural credit information from NABARD. The proposed workflow will prepare and combine the selected indicators, calculate a District Distress Score for the districts included in the study, apply K-Means clustering (with four clusters) for risk grouping, and use a Random Forest model to forecast next-season risk. Outputs are planned to be presented through a Streamlit web dashboard and a Power BI analytical report. This paper focuses on the problem context, objectives, related work, proposed data sources, system design and evaluation plan. It does not report implementation results or predictive-performance values; these will be…

title: An L1 two-scale finite element method for a multi-term time-fractional subdiffusion problem
GMR-EfficientUNet: an improved network integrating gated bottleneck convolution and multi-scale attention residual fusion for high-precision breast ultrasound mass segmentation
abstract: Abstract Breast ultrasound (BUS) is widely used in breast imaging because it is non-ionizing and well suited to dense breast tissue. However, speckle noise, blurry mass boundaries, and large variations in lesion scale remain challenging for automated segmentation. This paper presents GMR-EfficientUNet, an EfficientNet-B2/U-Net-based encoder-decoder framework that adapts a Gated Bottleneck Convolution (GBC) module and a Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention (MSCA) module from prior work and combines them with a Residual Adaptive Fusion (RAF) module for breast ultrasound mass segmentation. Within the proposed integration, GBC is applied to refine the initially fused encoder-decoder representation, MSCA performs multi-scale contextual modeling on the refined features, and RAF learns pixel-level fusion weights between the enhanced representation and the original DoubleConv feature. On the BUSI dataset, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 82.07%, MIoU of 73.73%, recall of 83.49%, and precision of 83.62%. On the BUET dataset, it achieved a Dice coefficient of 81.70% and MIoU of 72.57%; among the evaluated models, it obtained the highest Dice, MIoU, and recall, while TransUNet achieved a higher precision. The ablation results demonstrated the effectiveness of RAF in improving segmentation performance. Additional experiments showed improved boundary localization, competitive perform…
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals that gut microbiota modulates the association between dietary imbalance and gastrointestinal symptoms in children with functional dyspepsia
abstract: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a prevalent pediatric gastrointestinal disorder. Although dietary factors and gut microbiota dysbiosis are implicated in its pathogenesis, the interplay among diet, microbiota, and FD remains poorly understood. Methods This case–control study enrolled 34 children with FD and 40 healthy controls. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Fecal microbiota was profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics was employed to detect fecal metabolites. Clinical symptoms were evaluated using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) and the Functional Gastrointestinal Disorder Symptom Screening Questionnaire (FGIDQ). Results We identified 16 differentially abundant bacterial species and 476 differential metabolites (458 downregulated, 18 upregulated). Folate intake was significantly lower in the FD group ( p = 0.0038). Three major dietary patterns were identified: pattern 1 (high-fat, high-protein dietary pattern), pattern 2 (traditional staple food dietary pattern), and pattern 3 (diverse mixed diet dietary pattern). The standardized scores for patterns 2 and 3 were significantly lower in the FD group than in the control group. Correlation analysis revealed that the abundance of g__Monoglobus was positively correlated with intakes of valine, protein, and zinc; g__Intestinibacter abundance showed …

title: Applying Ecosystemic Autopsy to Juvenile Delinquency: A Multi-Level Case Analysis of Adolescent Development
abstract: Juvenile delinquency is a complex developmental and social concern shaped by the interaction of behavioural, emotional, academic, familial, social, and environmental factors. Although ecological perspectives recognize these influences, an integrated examination of how risk and protective factors interact across developmental stages remains important for understanding individual pathways to delinquency. This paper applies the Ecosystemic Autopsy (EcoA) framework, grounded in Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, to develop a contextualized understanding of juvenile delinquency through a retrospective qualitative single-case analysis. The case involved an 18-year-old male, assigned the pseudonym “Daniel,” selected because the available documentation covered multiple developmental and ecological domains. Data were drawn from one consolidated case review report containing psychoeducational assessments, developmental history, educational records, behavioural observations, and previous intervention records. The researcher organized the documented information into five a priori ecological categories: microsystem, mesosystem, exosystem, macrosystem, and chronosystem. The report documented difficulties in working memory, processing speed, reading comprehension, and written expression, alongside behavioural and emotional challenges. It also recorded practical and vocational strengt…

title: Multi-scale predictive control of boiler furnace temperature field based on MPC-Seq2seq
abstract: Introduction Boiler furnace temperature fields are significantly affected by strong nonlinearity and large time lags. Conventional methods exhibit limited capability in capturing spatiotemporal features and suffer from optimization delays, which restricts the efficient operation of boiler units. Methods To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-scale prediction method that combines a Lightweight Temporal Convolutional network with a Sequence-to-Sequence architecture. Wavelet packet decomposition is used to extract temperature sub-sequences, an encoding network is constructed, and a spatiotemporal dual attention mechanism is integrated to achieve accurate prediction of the furnace temperature field. In addition, a predictive control technique based on adaptive-reference-point multi-objective differential evolution is applied for combustion regulation. This technique takes multi-step prediction data as input, enhances collaborative optimization by introducing an adaptive update mechanism, and incorporates dual constraints on thermal efficiency and emissions to obtain the optimal control results. Results A 300 MW coal-fired utility boiler is selected as the research object for experimental validation. In furnace temperature prediction, the root mean square error of the proposed model is 1.53 °C, and the mean absolute percentage error under full load is 1.15%, both of whic…

title: Weekend effect on in-hospital mortality and healthcare utilization: a multi-method validation with time series analysis, Cox regression, and random forest in a Chinese tertiary hospital
abstract: Background Patients admitted on weekends may face elevated mortality risk, a phenomenon termed the “weekend effect.” While extensively studied in Western healthcare systems, evidence from Chinese tertiary hospitals remains limited, and most studies rely on single-method regression. This study had three distinct aims: (i) to estimate the association between weekend admission and in-hospital mortality; (ii) to characterize weekly temporal patterns in mortality; and (iii) to explore the variable importance of a broad set of patient-level and operational variables. Time series analysis, Cox proportional hazards modeling, and random forest were used to address these three aims, respectively. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 379,804 patients admitted to a tertiary general hospital in Shenzhen, China, from 2015 to 2023. Patients were categorized into weekday ( n = 304,693) and weekend/holiday ( n = 75,111) admission groups. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, defined as all-cause death during the index admission; patients were followed from admission to discharge, and those discharged alive were censored at discharge. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, treatment delay, nosocomial infection, and hospitalization cost. A multi-method strategy was used: (1) seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and seasonal autoregressive integrated moving aver…

title: Clinical outcomes associated with early airway management strategies in open and closed laryngeal trauma: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Selection of an initial airway strategy in laryngeal trauma depends on injury severity and respiratory status. This study aimed to examine associations between initial airway strategy and acute airway-related complications in adults with laryngeal trauma. Methods This two-center retrospective cohort included adults with open or closed laryngeal trauma treated from May 2020 to May 2025. The primary outcome was any acute airway-related complication during the index admission. Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for pretreatment severity, age, trauma type, admission delay, airway narrowing, and dyspnea. The analysis was restricted to Schaefer–Fuhrman grades I–III because all grade IV patients underwent initial tracheostomy. Strategy conversion and tube-removal outcomes were summarized descriptively. Results Among 206 patients, acute complications occurred in 28/76 (36.8%), 23/48 (47.9%), and 11/82 (13.4%) patients initially managed with observation, orotracheal intubation, and tracheostomy, respectively (omnibus P < 0.001). The principal model included 156 complete cases and 50 events. Compared with initial tracheostomy, observation [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 9.65; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.99–36.66] and intubation (aOR, 11.21; 95% CI, 3.61–40.76) were associated with higher odds of complications (both P < 0.001). Airway narrowing (aOR, 2.26; 95% C…

title: Resistance to mall expansion: still not buying the destination argument
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyse stakeholders’ reactions to expansion arguments for an out-of-town shopping mall in a contested planning process. The proposed expansion occurs against a backdrop of growing competition from e-commerce and increasing pressure on physical retail formats. This study seeks to explain how these arguments function as a means of making expansion appear feasible and desirable for place development, and whether they remain persuasive despite critique and uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This study is based on a document analysis of 144 formal stakeholder considerations submitted in response to the expansion vision of a Swedish shopping mall, examining how stakeholders engage with and contest expansion arguments. Findings This study identifies a destination argument that legitimises mall expansion through claims of uniqueness, experiencification and an expanded hinterland. Stakeholders frequently contest these claims, not because they lack information, but because they hold competing views on retail place development and its consequences. The findings show how destination arguments can remain influential despite substantial scepticism and critique. Practical implications The findings suggest greater scrutiny of destination arguments used to justify mall expansion. Claims of uniqueness, wider catchment areas and spillover benefits sh…
venue: Journal of Place Management and Development

title: Mango Production Processes and Marketing Strategies in Bangladesh
abstract: In essence the marketing of mango is contingent on the linkage between production possibilities, product status and environment in which the decision is made. The study investigated the relationship between mango cultivation, harvesting, processing, the environment and regulatory framework and marketing strategies in the context of Canada’s production environment in Chapainawabganj, Bangladesh. Judgement sampling was used to get responses from professionals and business participants that are associated with the mango value chain in a quantitative survey. A total of 210 questionnaires were analysed from 260 questionnaires received. The responses were measured on a 5-point Likert scale, and examined using the partial least squares structural equation modelling in the software SmartPLS with 5000 bootstrap resamples. The composite reliabilities were between 0.782 and 0.862, while the AVEs were between 0.550 and 0.719. The strongest positive relationships were seen between harvesting (β = 0.380, p < 0.001), the environmental and regulatory context (β = 0.202, p = 0.017) and processing (β = 0.192, p = 0.037). The association between cultivation was positive but not statistically significant (β = 0.100, p = 0.219). The model had an explained variance of 40.6% and a reported Q² of 0.258 and standardised root mean square residual of 0.077 for marketing strategies. The results suggest an…

title: Utopia of Ideas - A Nozickian Utopian Defense of the Right to Moderate Digital Content
abstract: Abstract In this paper I present two presumptive considerations in favor of extensive content moderation rights for digital platforms. I first develop a defense of this system as implementing a close realization of Robert Nozick’s conception of a utopian society. I argue that granting digital platforms such rights approximates Nozick’s picture of utopia on normatively relevant metrics. Second, I present a presumptive, partly Nozickian, humility-based case against the regulation of content moderation. Surprisingly, the Nozickian framework will turn out to be in principle compatible with some powerful regulatory tools, and thus does not entail a thoroughgoing cyberlibertarianism without additional assumptions, which I briefly discuss in closing.

title: From exposure to imprint: CEO formative experiences and the architecture of accounting and financial decisions
abstract: Purpose This review explains how chief executive officers' formative experiences become organizationally consequential and why apparently similar exposures are associated with different accounting, financing, risk and stakeholder decisions. Design/methodology/approach Following the Search-Appraisal-Analysis-Synthesis (SAAS) workflow, the study maps 105 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2011 and 2026 using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer and conducts a structured content synthesis of 102 studies whose focal construct is an executive formative experience. Findings The literature converges around upper-echelons and imprinting perspectives but does not support a uniform “adversity produces conservatism” account. The synthesis distinguishes four adversity-related imprint families – threat vigilance and loss avoidance; uncertainty habituation, resilience or self-efficacy; scarcity orientation; and prosocial reorientation – while treating institutional socialization as conceptually distinct. Persistent imprints become observable only when later situations activate them and when executive discretion permits expression. Accounting and financing architecture provides particularly discriminating tests of these mechanisms. Originality/value The review moves beyond exposure–outcome associations by separating exposure formation, imprint content, activation, expression and observed …

title: ASSESSMENT OF RIGHT VENTRICULAR SYSTOLIC FUNCTION USING 2D AND 3D ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY IN PATIENTS WITH DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY
abstract: Background: Impaired Right Ventricular (RV) systolic function in patients with Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) carries substantial prognostic significance and predicts cardiovascular death and hospitalization. Therefore, this study is intended to assess RV systolic function in patients with DCM using 2-Dimensional (2D) and 3-Dimensional (3D) Echocardiography. Aim: To correlate the 2D and 3D echocardiographic modalities for a better calibration for assessment of RV systolic function in patient with dilated cardiomyopathy Methods and Results: This hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted at KLE’S Dr. Prabhakar Kore Hospital and Medical Research Centre, Belagavi, from March 2020 to February 2021. Thirty-five patients who were hospitalized, non-hospitalized or out-patients diagnosed with DCM with or without signs of heart failure were included. This study compared various parameters assessed by 2D and 3D Echo modalities for evaluating RV size, RV volumes and RV ejection fraction (RVEF) in patients with DCM. Results: Male predominance (68.57%) has been observed in the study. The commonest (31.43%) ECG/EKG finding noted was complete or incomplete Left bundle branch block (LBBB). Severe LV systolic dilation assessed by LV internal systolic dimension (LVISd) by 2D//M-mode echo (LVISd) was noted in most of these patients (68.57%), which strongly indicates Severe LV sy…

title: Financial Literacy for Islamic Boarding School Students: Building a Fundamental Understanding of Money Management
abstract: Purpose: This community service program aimed to improve the financial literacy of students (santri) at Pesantren Muhammadiyah Cabang Tanjung Duren by enhancing their understanding of personal financial management, financial planning, income and expense management, and the importance of saving as a foundation for developing financial independence. Method: The program was conducted through a collaboration between the Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Trisakti, and Pesantren Muhammadiyah Cabang Tanjung Duren. The training employed an educational approach consisting of lectures, interactive discussions, and practical explanations on basic financial literacy concepts. The activities focused on introducing fundamental principles of responsible financial management and encouraging participants to apply these concepts in their daily lives. Practical Applications: The program provides practical knowledge that enables santri to manage their personal finances more effectively by planning expenditures, controlling financial resources, and cultivating saving habits. The knowledge gained can also serve as a foundation for managing small-scale entrepreneurial activities and promoting responsible financial behavior, thereby supporting the development of financial independence within the pesantren community. Conclusion: The financial literacy training successfully enhanced partici…

title: Improving MSME Financial Governance Through SIAPIK And BukuWarung Education During Industrial Visit
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to improve MSME financial governance by educating participants on digital recording applications (SIAPIK and BukuWarung), addressing the prevalent issue of manual and unstructured financial management in MSMEs. Method: This community service employed an educational approach via an industrial visit to PT. Bakpia Juwara Satoe. Methods included field observation, interactive material delivery, application demonstrations, and participatory evaluation. Practical Applications: The initiative provides MSMEs with accessible digital tools for real-time transaction recording and automated financial reporting, enhancing operational efficiency, business decision-making, and access to formal financing. Conclusion: The activity successfully enhanced participants' digital accounting literacy. Integrating industrial visits with practical application training effectively equips MSMEs to adopt systematic, accurate, and accountable financial management practices.

title: Methodology for Financial Evaluation of Investment Projects for the Production of Dual-Use Products
The broad reach of financial socialisation in the home
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether cognitive ability, gender, socioeconomic status (SES), interest in finance and country context condition the association between parental financial socialisation and young adults' objective financial knowledge and subjective financial knowledge (financial confidence). By examining both outcomes together, the study addresses a gap concerning the boundary conditions of family financial socialisation. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 353 university students across Australia, New Zealand and New Caledonia, objective financial knowledge was measured using a ten-item test and financial confidence using subjective financial knowledge. Parental financial socialisation was measured with the Parent Financial Socialisation Scale (PFSS). Ordinary least squares regressions and PROCESS Model 1 moderation tests incorporated fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy, cognitive reflection, gender, SES, financial-information engagement and country controls. Common-method-bias diagnostics were also conducted. Findings Parental financial socialisation was positively associated with both objective financial knowledge and financial confidence. Fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy and cognitive reflection were associated with objective financial knowledge, whereas only cognitive reflection among the cognitive measures was associated with financia…

title: Financial Management Extension And Training For MSMEs In Saparua District, Central Maluku Regency
abstract: Purpose: To improve the financial literacy and management skills of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Saparua District, focusing on transaction recording, cash flow management, and separating business from household finances. Method: Conducted on August 13–15, 2026, involving 30 MSME participants. Activities included socialization, instructional sessions, practical exercises, and smartphone-based training using the “Buku Kas” application, evaluated descriptively. Practical Applications: Participants demonstrated increased awareness and skills in recording transactions, monitoring cash flows, and managing capital. The “Buku Kas” application provided a simple digital tool for systematic financial management. Conclusion: The program strengthened foundational financial management knowledge and provided practical digital tools for sustainable MSME management. Continued mentoring is recommended to ensure independent application use.

title: Unveiling the impact of ESG and financial stress on European banks' profitability
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance influences bank profitability and how this relationship is shaped by financial stress conditions in the European banking sector. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on panel data from 30 European banks across 13 countries over the period 2012–2021. The study employs Panel Estimated Generalized Least Squares, System Generalized Method of Moments, and quantile regression techniques to assess linear, nonlinear, and heterogeneous effects. Findings The results show that ESG performance positively affects bank profitability, while financial stress significantly reduces it and weakens ESG benefits. The relationship is nonlinear, with ESG effects strengthening beyond certain thresholds, while social factors enhance performance, environmental effects remain limited, and governance improves resilience but exhibits diminishing returns at higher levels. Practical implications Banks should strategically calibrate ESG investments, particularly governance, to balance costs and benefits, especially under financial stress. Policymakers should promote incentive-based frameworks that support ESG adoption without imposing excessive short-term burdens. Originality/value This study contributes by integrating financial stress into the ESG–financial performance nexus, highlighting nonlinear dynamics a…

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in construction finance: transforming cost estimation, risk management and financial performance
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming construction finance by improving cost estimation, cash flow forecasting, financial risk assessment, procurement and decision support. However, research remains fragmented across AI subfields and financial functions, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how AI creates financial value within construction organisations. This study aims to synthesise contemporary literature and develop an integrated conceptual framework of AI-enabled construction finance. Design/methodology/approach A structured integrative literature review was conducted using a transparent search and screening protocol. Forty-six peer-reviewed studies published between January 2021 and June 2026 were systematically identified, screened and coded using Gioia’s hierarchical coding methodology to examine AI subfields, construction finance applications, organisational benefits, implementation challenges and emerging research directions. Findings Machine learning (ML) and optimisation dominate existing research because of their widespread application to cost estimation, cash flow forecasting, financial risk assessment and resource optimisation. Computer vision, natural language processing, robotics and automated planning remain comparatively underexplored but demonstrate growing potential to enhance project controls, contract administration and operational eff…
venue: Journal of Financial Management of Property and Construction

title: Sharia Digital Economic Empowerment Through Financial Education And QRIS Implementation In Rural MSMEs
abstract: Purpose: This study critically analyzes Sharia digital economic empowerment for rural MSMEs, addressing the gap where QRIS infrastructure expansion precedes community cognitive readiness. Method: Using a descriptive qualitative approach based on Participatory Action Research, the study focuses on Rita Chips MSME as a purposive single case. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and financial documentation across three sequential intervention stages: Sharia financial literacy education, bookkeeping assistance, and QRIS facilitation. Practical Applications: The results show that partners initially relying on unrecorded cash transactions overcame cognitive and administrative resistance through the principle of trustworthiness and clear net profit calculation, enabling smooth QRIS adoption with only infrastructural barriers remaining. Conclusion: QRIS is effective as a downstream, rather than upstream, instrument in a validated, replicable village-based Sharia digital empowerment model.

title: Electromagnetic Field Prediction and Transmission Characteristic Parameters Calculation of Hybrid Plasmonic Waveguides with Physics-Augmented Deep Learning
EU skilled circular migration and financial risk
abstract: Purpose This study examines which institutional and labor market conditions are associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility between EU country pairs and how these conditions relate to human capital allocation risk. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses an annual panel of undirected EU27 country pairs from 2004 to 2020, restricted to pair-years in which both countries were EU members. The outcome is a weighted corridor-level index combining reciprocal balance and skilled flow volume. It captures balanced reciprocal skilled mobility, not repeated movement by the same individuals. Country-pair fixed effects, year effects, lagged predictors, mediation, moderated mediation and alternative outcome checks are applied. Findings Destination skill shortages are positively associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility. Qualification recognition has no statistically significant direct association with the outcome, but the recognition-to-employment-absorption pathway is positive. This indirect pathway weakens as overqualification risk rises. Research limitations/implications Aggregate pair-year flows cannot identify return or repeated movement by the same workers. The design therefore supports corridor-level inference about balanced reciprocal mobility rather than individual circular migration. The models also identify an upstream human capital allocation channel rat…

title: Pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy versus open donor right hepatectomy in living donor liver transplantation: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis
Effect of physical, psychological and demographic factors of construction craft workers on hazard recognition performance and safety risk perception
abstract: Purpose Despite advances in safety protocols, the construction industry still experiences high occupational injury rates, partly due to limitations in craft workers’ hazard recognition performance (HRP) and safety risk perception (SRP). However, prior research has largely examined antecedents of safety cognition in isolation, with limited attention to the combined effects of physical, psychological and demographic factors, including sleep quality, job stress, fatigue, education, experience and age. This study aims to examine the combined associations of physical (fatigue, sleep quality), psychological (job stress) and demographic (age, education, experience) factors to provide a more systemic understanding of safety cognition. Specifically, safety risk perception is operationalized through the Discrepancy in Safety Risk Perception Index, which measures the alignment or discrepancy between workers’ subjective risk assessments and an established expert-referenced benchmark. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional quantitative design was used, integrating structured surveys with image-based hazard identification tasks. Data were collected from 96 construction craft workers across 11 construction projects in Iran using validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized direct and mediated pathways, with fatigue position…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: DESIGN CENTRADO NO USUÁRIO NA ERA DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA: UMA ANÁLISE DAS INTERFACES CONVERSACIONAIS SOB A ÓTICA DE DONALD NORMAN
abstract: A ascensão de sistemas baseados em Inteligência Artificial (IA) Generativa e Grandes Modelos de Linguagem (Large Language Models – LLMs) transformou o paradigma da Interação Humano-Computador, substituindo interfaces gráficas determinísticas por diálogos probabilísticos em linguagem natural. Embora ofereçam alta capacidade de automação, essas interfaces frequentemente operam como "caixas-pretas", dificultando a compreensão dos limites do sistema e induzindo à confiança excessiva (overtrust) diante de erros ou alucinações. Diante desse cenário, este artigo tem como objetivo analisar como os princípios de Design Centrado no Usuário (DCU) de Donald Norman podem ser aplicados às interfaces de IA generativa para aprimorar a compreensão, calibrar a confiança e apoiar a tomada de decisão dos usuários. Metodologicamente, realizou-se uma pesquisa qualitativa, de natureza aplicada e caráter exploratório-descritivo, fundamentada em revisão bibliográfica e em um estudo de caso avaliativo da interface conversacional do ChatGPT, confrontando os preceitos de Norman com as diretrizes contemporâneas de Interação Humano-IA. Os resultados demonstram que o minimalismo da "caixa de texto em branco" amplia o Abismo da Execução pela ausência de significantes sobre as capacidades do modelo, enquanto a falta de indicadores visuais de incerteza aprofunda o Abismo da Avaliação. Conclui-se que a adaptação…

title: Design, synthesis, and antileishmanial activity of novel analogs of the orally active antileishmanial lead tetrahydro-pyrroloquinazoline alkaloid natural product peganine for visceral leishmaniasis
abstract: Abstract Leishmaniasis is a neglected tropical disease affecting millions of people worldwide with an estimated 1 million new cases occurring annually. The current treatments against leishmaniasis suffer from drug resistance, toxicity, and inconvenient routes of administration prompting an urgent need for the development of new oral, and safe drugs. We have previously identified an orally active antileishmanial lead natural product, peganine that significantly reduced parasitic burden following oral administration to hamsters, albeit at a relatively high dose. We have rationally designed and synthesized novel analogs of peganine and evaluated their antileishmanial activity against the species of leishmania responsible for visceral leishmaniasis, Leishmania donovani . The analogs were rapidly synthesized in 1–2 steps in good to excellent yields and exhibited promising parasite growth inhibition (up to 70%) in axenic and intracellular amastigote macrophage models at 10 µM and 20 µM. Many of the molecules showed little to no toxicity to the mammalian HEK cells, supporting the potential for selectivity against L. donovani . Based on ≥ 50% growth inhibition of intracellular amastigotes at 10 and 20 µM and parallel host cell compatibility, we identified several promising hit analogs (14, 15, 16, 25, 26, 28, and 40). While vehicle-related toxicity at higher thresholds limited full dos…

title: Knowledge-conditioned multimodal generation and communication-guided selection for agricultural product packaging design
Is assessment design encouraging AI offloading?
abstract: Generative AI has ended the assumption that unsupervised student work reflects a student’s own unaided thinking, forcing a return to first principles in assessment. This article uses The University of Sydney’s two-lane approach, which separates secure assessment of learning from open assessment for and as learning, to frame a practical account of putting AI into students’ hands. Drawing on ‘Dr MattTabolism’, an AI biochemistry tutor I built and deployed, and on a computational study of how students actually used it, I show a consistent gap between how such tools are designed and how they are used. Students largely sought answers rather than sustained dialogue, satisfaction did not correlate with improved learning outcomes, and usage concentrated around deadlines. How educators contextualised AI use affected learning more than how the tool behaved. I argue that this offloading is partly a product of over-assessment, and that formative, lower-stakes work remains essential precisely because it is where students can afford the desirable difficulties that learning requires. Reducing assessment load is a validity measure, not a soft option. I close with practical starting points for educators, framed around the pedagogical roles AI can play and the risks each carries, and the educator’s role as designer.

title: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
abstract: Abstract Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced el…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: The Symbolic Translation of Chinese Ink Art and Its Application in Contemporary Poster Design
abstract: Chinese ink art is an important expression of traditional Chinese aesthetics. Its brushwork, tonal variation, textures, and use of empty space not only form a distinctive visual language but also convey artistic conception, vitality, and ideas of spatial organization. Translating this language into design signs suited to contemporary visual communication remains an important question in adapting traditional art to present-day contexts. Drawing on semiotics, this study uses a literature review and case analysis to examine the formal characteristics and cultural meanings of ink-art signs. Through three poster examples, it discusses graphic extraction and reconstruction, integration with layout, and typographic reconstruction. The analysis suggests that the contemporary use of ink art involves more than reproducing traditional imagery. Rather, it requires selecting visual features, interpreting their cultural associations, and reorganizing them through contemporary design methods. These approaches offer a way to connect traditional aesthetic sensibilities with the communicative demands of contemporary posters.
venue: World Journal of Education and Humanities

title: Briefing: The problem with Jane Jacobs
abstract: The writing of Jane Jacobs has had an enormous breadth of influence on city planning and architecture over six decades. In this paper, I argue that Jacobs’ work has been so influential because her vision of the city was subsumed into a mood of radical economic liberalism – centred on mid-century New York – that readily translates, across political divisions, into hegemonic forms of market development today. This was a mood that opposed New Deal and Fair Deal principles, and that was spearheaded by key figures including the classical liberalist economist Ludwig von Mises, his protégé Friedrich August von Hayek, and the radical Objectivist philosopher Ayn Rand. Jacobs’ city of ‘individual plans’ and ‘spontaneous order’ – conceived in opposition to Keynesian plans of collective sovereignty and central planning – was part of a demolition job on modernism’s social mission (and American social democracy), achieved through tropes of vitality associated with individualist capitalism. The paper discusses the economic origins of Jacobs’ writing but is equally interested in the movements that have mobilised her work. Many of those, while putatively critical of orthodox market-development, are entirely consonant with it.

title: A cube complex for virtual Artin groups
Entre la lentitud y el mercado: fricciones en la producción de ciudad pequeña en Colombia
abstract: This article seeks to understand the role of membership in the Cittaslow network in the reconfiguration of territorial production in Pijao and Marulanda, two small Colombian towns that have historically been marginalized. It analyzes, from an ethnographic perspective, the frictions that emerge between aspirations for insertion into global tourist circuits and localized economic practices. It shows that the declaration of “slow town” functions as a symbolic catalyst that activates material transformations and struggles to define what ways of life, what organization and use of space, and what expressions of tradition are legitimate in the present and future of the territory. The tensions surrounding tourism as a “magic solution,” plural economies, and neo-rural projects reveal that Cittaslow does not operate as an external alternative to capitalism, but rather as a field where territorial commodification and practices of reciprocity coexist ambivalently, actively participating in the material and symbolic production of these territories where the rural and the urban converge.

title: Digital-Based Service Quality at the Integrated Police Service Center of the Central Sulawesi Regional Police (A Study of the Issuance of Police Clearance Certificates)
abstract: This study examines the quality of digital-based services for issuing Police Clearance Certificates (Surat Keterangan Catatan Kepolisian/ SKCK) at the Integrated Police Service Center (SPKT) of the Central Sulawesi Regional Police. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. The study was conducted at the SPKT over a three-month period and involved five informants: the Head of SPKT, an SPKT officer, a digital-service operator, and two members of the public who had used the service. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that service quality remains suboptimal. Of the five SERVQUAL dimensions, tangibles, reliability, and responsiveness have not been fully achieved, while assurance and empathy are relatively satisfactory. Physical facilities and digital devices are available, but unstable internet connectivity, difficulties in using the application, and continued reliance on face-to-face counters constrain access. Although procedures are clear, registration, account verification, and document-upload problems prevent users from experiencing consistent service outcomes. Officers are willing to assist, but response speed is constrained during periods of high demand and when problems originate in the central system. By contra…

title: MEDIATING EFFECT OF JOB SATISFACTION ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SERVICE INNOVATIONS AND EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE IN DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS IN MUBI, ADAMAWA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study delves into the intricate relationships between service innovation, job satisfaction, and employee performance within Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Mubi, Adamawa state, Nigeria. The banking landscape has undergone profound transformations in recent years, compelling institutions to embrace innovation while simultaneously maintaining employee well-being and performance. The study adopted a survey research design and through meticulous analysis of survey data collected from banking employees using multiple linear regression, this research uncovers interrelated patterns about innovation effects. The result shows that job satisfaction emerges as a partial mediator in the relationship between service innovation and employee performance. This partial mediation suggests dual pathways of influence innovation directly enhances performance through improved tools and processes, while simultaneously boosting satisfaction that further drives performance gains. The mediating role varies across innovation dimensions, adding another layer of complexity to our understanding of workplace dynamics in the banking sector. The DMBs should treat employee satisfaction not as a by-product but as a core strategic lever because this can further be enhanced and institutionalised through regular staff feedback mechanisms, recognition programs, and well-being initiatives.

title: Factors influencing Elementary-Pre-Service Teacher’s Dispositions Toward Mathematics: An Exploration of Perceptions and Origins
abstract: The purpose of this convergent parallel mixed-methods study was to examine dispositions toward mathematics held by elementary pre-service teachers (EPSTs) and to identify factors contributing to their mathematical aversion. Drawing on a productive disposition framework, we analyzed five constructs: self-confidence, perceived value, enjoyment, motivation, and past experiences. Three hundred eighteen EPSTs enrolled in a mathematics methods course participated in the study. Quantitative analyses included descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from 177 participants who reported mathematical aversion were analyzed using two-cycle inductive coding procedures. Quantitative results indicated no statistically significant differences in disposition constructs by gender, though a significant difference emerged for perceived value across programs of study. Approximately 56% of EPSTs reported aversion toward mathematics, with origins traced predominantly to elementary and middle school years. Qualitative findings revealed that negative teacher experiences constituted the most frequently cited reason for aversion (25%), followed by low self-confidence (16%) and perceived difficulty (14%). These findings highlight the need for teacher preparation programs to address affective dimensions of mathematical learning and to help EP…

title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
abstract: Abstract The auditory brainstem implant (ABI) targeting the cochlear nucleus (CN) can restore hearing in patients ineligible for cochlear implants. However, conventional ABI using surface electrode array yields highly variable outcomes, from poor to moderate, due to limited spatial resolution and restricted tonotopic access. Here, we developed a penetrating ABI based on a high-density, ultra-flexible implantable neural electrode array (uFINE). In normal-hearing rats, uFINE mapped frequency tuning from 0.5 to 32 kHz in CN and the inferior colliculus (IC). Selective CN stimulation via uFINE evoked IC responses closely matching acoustic tonotopy, with IC tuning widths comparable to tone-evoked responses, and these remained stable for over 136 days, with minimal gliosis observed. Daily sequential CN–IC microstimulation progressively shifted the location of the CN-evoked IC response peak toward the targeted IC stimulation site, consistent with use-dependent plasticity. Together, these findings demonstrate that uFINE enables high-resolution, tonotopically precise, and long-term stable CN stimulation across a broad frequency range with minimal tissue disruption, highlighting its potential to enhance ABI-mediated hearing restoration.

title: Unlocking giant nonlinear optical response and near-theoretical crystallinity in bio-derived cobalt–methylcellulose films: eco-friendly biopolymer composites with tailored optoelectronic properties
Implementation of the Affordable Food Movement Policy in Support of Inflation Control in Palangka Raya City, Central Kalimantan Province
abstract: Volatile food prices and heavy dependence on supplies from outside the region pose structural challenges to inflation control in Palangka Raya City. The city government runs the Affordable Food Movement (Gerakan Pangan Murah, GPM) as a direct market intervention, yet its effect on the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) remains limited. This descriptive qualitative case study analyzes why GPM has not controlled regional inflation optimally and formulates strategies to improve its implementation, using the Van Meter and Van Horn (1975) model. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with nine informant groups, observation, and document review, and verified through source and technique triangulation. Five inhibiting factors emerged: (1) a spatial mismatch between GPM sites and the BPS sample markets used for the CPI; (2) import dependence above 80% for volatile food across a vast, sparsely populated area; (3) the absence of a dedicated mayoral regulation and uncertain municipal funding; (4) limited human resources and the suspension of the mobile GPM fleet in 2026; and (5) short coordination lead times and uneven neighborhood-level socialization. Five strategies are proposed: aligning sites with sample markets, upstream inter-regional business-to-business cooperation, a mayoral regulation with earmarked budget, reactivating the mobile fleet with a task force, and a seven-d…

title: Technology Integration Among Alternative Learning System Teachers in Bukidnon, Philippines: A Phenomenological Study
abstract: Technology integration is increasingly used in instruction; however, limited attention has been given to how Alternative Learning System (ALS) teachers experience its use in everyday teaching contexts. This study explored the lived experiences of ALS teachers integrating technology in Bukidnon, Philippines, during School Year 2026–2027, focusing on their motivations, challenges, responses, and recommendations. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed. Fifteen ALS teachers with direct experience integrating technology were purposively selected as information-rich participants. Data were gathered through semi-structured, in-depth interviews, audio-recorded with informed consent and transcribed. The transcripts were analyzed thematically. The researcher repeatedly read the transcripts, identified significant statements, assigned initial codes, clustered related codes into categories, and compared patterns across participants to develop overarching themes. Four themes emerged: Adapting Instruction to Learners’ Needs Through Technology; Experiencing Challenges in Technology-Supported Instruction; Integrating Technology Through Flexible Teaching Practices; and Strengthening Technology-Supported Learning in ALS. Participants described integrating technology to engage learners, clarify concepts, address varied learning needs, provide flexible access to materials, and support …

title: Protection of Live-in Partners in India: Judicial Discretion, Social Morality, and Conflict with Marital Rights
abstract: In India, where the majority still views marriage not just as an indispensable social institution but as a sacrament, any perceived threat to it is likely to be met with hostility, and the live-in relationship is no exception. As the number of people opting to live in rather than marry rises, so do the legal dilemmas associated with such cohabitation. In the absence of formal legislation, live-in partners are left at the mercy of the judiciary for the protection of their rights. Against the backdrop of growing intolerance and violence against live-in couples, especially when one or both partners are married, the core research problem is whether a person’s statutory right to enjoy the company of their spouse, the spouse’s lifestyle choice resulting in a civil wrong, or social morality ought to weigh against granting live-in partners protection against threats to their lives. The paper examines the lack of uniformity in the exercise of writ jurisdiction by the courts in such matters. Through a doctrinal analysis of case law and statutes, it presents key counter-arguments that courts ought to take into consideration while adjudicating such matters, such as the unwarranted application of the qualification of a relationship in the nature of marriage, the need to uphold constitutional morality, and the availability of civil remedies to the aggrieved spouse. The findings highlight tha…

title: The Role of Sustainability Management and Safety Culture in the Sustainable Performance of Companies
abstract: Pressure on companies to implement sustainability principles is increasing as organizational performance is no longer judged solely on financial aspects, but also on environmental, social, and human safety aspects. This study aims to analyze the role of sustainability management and safety culture in supporting sustainable performance and understand the relationship between the two within an organization. The study used a qualitative approach with a literature review method and an interpretive paradigm. Data were obtained from journal articles, academic books, proceedings, research reports, and relevant documents selected purposively based on relevance, credibility, and currency. The analysis was conducted through identification, selection, grouping, interpretation, and synthesis of findings into the themes of sustainability management, safety culture, the integration of sustainability and occupational safety, and organizational performance. The study results show that sustainability management serves as a strategic framework that integrates economic, environmental, and social aspects into organizational strategy and operations. Meanwhile, safety culture supports sustainable performance through worker protection, accident reduction, increased operational continuity, and strengthened organizational communication and learning. These two concepts are complementary, with sustainabi…

title: Optimization of an Agrobacterium-Mediated CRISPR/Cas9 Delivery System Targeting the GS3 Gene in JP-5 Oryza sativa
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa) is an important food crop for more than half of the world’s population. The two main cultivated rice species are Oryza sativa and Oryza glaberrima. Among the Oryza sativa species, JP-5 is a japonica rice variety that is cold tolerant and has short generation time along with other beneficial agronomic characteristics. However, this variety has short grain size, and it is known that the food supply and market value of rice is highly influenced by its grain size and, larger grain size is favored by the consumer. Therefore, the present study is aimed at optimizing the procedure for increasing grain size of rice using CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) Cas-9 technology. This technique can be used to efficiently mutate the GS3 (Grain Size 3) gene which is a major QTL (quantitative trait locus) that negatively regulates the grain size in rice. This study has established an optimized and reproducible workflow from rice seed sterilization to callus induction, callus infection with bacteria, selection and then regeneration of the rice plants. For sterilization, 20% Clorox and 75% ethanol have shown best effects, for callus induction, 2mg/L 2,4-D (2,4 dichloro-phenoxy acetic acid) concentration was best showing callus induction rate of 89.17 ± 3.00%, and 35mg/L hygromycin was optimized for selection of transformants. Among the hormonal c…

title: Autogestión territorial, turismo comunitario y resistencia urbana en el área de interés ambiental Monteleón de la periferia norte de Manizales, Colombia
abstract: The article analyzes how young people from the northern outskirts of Manizales (Colombia), through community tourism initiatives, are shaping practices of territorial self-management and urban resistance in the face of spatial injustice and socio-spatial segregation. Based on a qualitative study with a socio-geohistorical approach and urban ethnography, it examines the territorial transformations of the Monteleón environmental area of interest and the neighboring neighborhoods of the Ciudadela del Norte commune, where stigma, infrastructure deficits, and inequalities in access to the city have historically been concentrated. The article argues that community-based tourism, as promoted by the Tour de la Cinco collective, is a model for the social management and production of space, neighborhood destigmatization, expansion of the right to the city, and generation of local economic opportunities. It argues that these forms of territorial self-management allow us to imagine and test alternative futures for working-class urban peripheries, challenging the neoliberal logic that has guided the city's development in recent decades.

title: Algorithmic Mediation: Redefining Neutrality in Digital Copyright Disputes
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital platforms and generative artificial intelligence (AI) has outpaced traditional copyright litigation, which remains slow, costly, and constrained by territorial jurisdiction. Scholarly debate has concentrated largely on substantive questions such as AI authorship and the legality of training data, while the procedural architecture for resolving complex, high-volume copyright disputes has received comparatively little attention. This paper examines algorithmic mediation as an emerging stage in the evolution of Online Dispute Resolution (ODR). Using doctrinal and comparative methods, it evaluates three established models of technology-enabled intellectual property (IP) dispute resolution: the WIPO Arbitration and Mediation Center, ICANN’s Uniform Domain Name Dispute Resolution Policy (UDRP), and platform-based enforcement systems, including YouTube’s Content ID and statutory notice-and-takedown procedures. It also examines the Indian legal framework, including the Mediation Act, 2023, and recent regulatory developments in the European Union. The analysis shows that existing systems achieve speed and scale, but often at the cost of transparency, contestability, and balance between rights holders and users. Building on these findings, the paper proposes a hybrid AI-assisted mediation model in which algorithmic decision-support tools analyse similarity …

title: An Enhanced Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection System for IoT Networks Using Feature Engineering and Data Preprocessing
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created new opportunities for smart and connected applications, but it has also increased the number of potential security vulnerabilities. IoT networks generate large volumes of heterogeneous traffic, making the detection of malicious activities a challenging task. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) based on machine learning can identify abnormal network behaviour and provide an effective security mechanism for IoT environments. However, the performance of a machine learning model strongly depends on the quality of the input data, preprocessing techniques, feature representation, and class distribution. This research focuses on developing a machine learning-based IoT intrusion detection system with particular emphasis on data preprocessing and feature generation. The proposed framework includes data cleaning, handling of missing values, encoding of categorical attributes, feature reduction, and feature generation before applying a machine learning classifier. The ToN-IoT dataset is considered for evaluating the proposed approach because it contains normal and malicious IoT network traffic representing different attack categories. Random Forest is considered as the primary classification algorithm because of its ability to handle high-dimensional data, nonlinear relationships, and multiple classes while maintaining rela…

title: Risk reduction at Kumbh Mela through public health, WASH and crowd management
Bleeding Without Remedy: Menstrual Leave and the Male Architecture of Indian Law
abstract: Menstruation remains a source of stigma at work, and India still has neither a central statute nor a Union policy on menstrual leave. This article approaches the question of menstrual leave from a feminist perspective and makes three arguments. The first is diagnostic: legislative silence is often put down to the arithmetic of private members’ business, but it also reflects a legal order whose default worker and default idea of neutrality are male, the sense in which “law is male”. The second is doctrinal: read together, the Supreme Court’s January 2026 judgment on menstrual health, the Karnataka High Court’s April 2026 decision on menstrual leave, and Articles 42 and 39(e) of the Constitution give the claim to menstrual leave firmer ground than the dignity and health argument usually made under Article 21. The third is practical: the objection that leave will be priced into women’s hiring is serious, the Supreme Court has voiced it, and any defensible scheme has to be designed with it in view, as an entitlement the employee claims, with universal coverage and with a cost that does not fall on the individual hire.

title: EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF DEMOGRAPHIC PROFILE ON THE USAGE OF UPI APPS IN SHIVAMOGGA DISTRICT
abstract: In present scenario UPI payments are playing a pivotal role in digital world because of its user friendly, convenience and secure transactions. There are so many demographic and other factor influence the adoption and usage of UPI apps. This research paper focuses to evaluate the impact of Demographic profile of respondents such as qualification. Occupation and age on the usage of UPI Apps. The Primary and secondary data has been used to gather the information. The primary data are collected through structure questionnaire from 120 respondents using the Stratified Sampling technique. The study is conducted in Shivamogga District. The statistical tools such as Mediation analysis and Moderation Analysis were applied in order to find out the direct, indirect and conditional relationship among the variables. The mode of payment and frequency of usage are mediator and moderator for the study. The findings reveal that Educational Qualification and Occupation do not exert a statistically significant direct effect on UPI usage. However, both exhibit a robust indirect influence, significantly mediated by the individual’s Preferred Mode of Payment and Frequency of Usage (e.g., Bootstrap CI for Education via Mode of Pay: 0.0369 to 0.1518). Furthermore, the relationship between Age and UPI usage is found to be significantly moderated by the Preferred Mode of Payment (Interaction Term p=0.0…

title: THE POSITION AND POWERS OF INDEPENDENT STATE INSTITUTIONS IN INDONESIA’S CONSTITUTIONAL SYSTEM AFTER THE AMENDMENTS TO THE 1945 CONSTITUTION
abstract: The 1999–2002 amendments to the 1945 Constitution gave rise to independent state institutions that sit uneasily within the classical separation of powers, raising questions about their position, the scope of their powers, and their accountability. This study uses normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, drawing on the Constitution, the statutes establishing these institutions, and Constitutional Court Decisions No. 36/PUU-XV/2017 and No. 70/PUU-XVII/2019. The findings show that these institutions do not share a single status. Some, such as the General Elections Commission and the Judicial Commission, are grounded in the Constitution, while others, such as the Corruption Eradication Commission, the Business Competition Supervisory Commission, the National Human Rights Commission, and the Ombudsman, were established by statute and can therefore be altered through ordinary legislation. Independence functions as a safeguard for performing duties, not as an exemption from law, and accountability may take legal, administrative, financial, and public forms. Oversight is necessary but must remain proportional and must not take over an institution’s core functions. The study recommends that statutes clarify each institution’s position, powers, jurisdictional boundaries, and reporting mechanisms

title: A Critical Study on Legal Implications of the POCSO Act, 2012 on Consensual Minor Relationships in India
abstract: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) protects children against the infringement of their rights. However, its definition of a child, which includes everyone below the age of eighteen, results in many issues. Since consent is irrelevant below that age under section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and the POCSO Act’s definition of a child, even consensual relationships between adolescents are being criminalized. Surveys such as the NFHS-5 show that 39% of women aged 25 to 49 had their first sexual encounter before the age of 18, and significant numbers of pre-marital relationships exist among adolescents in India. Yet only a minuscule number of cases arising from relationships between minors end in conviction, which indicates that non-exploitative cases are putting pressure on the judicial system. Although the legislation does not discriminate on the basis of gender, male adolescents have been disproportionately punished under it. This encourages the stereotyping of males as violent individuals. On the other hand, young females are denied autonomy to be sexually active, being perceived as incapable of giving consent and only as victims. Often, the legislation is misused by parents to control voluntary relationships between adolescents, to discourage relationships across caste lines and to settle unrelated family and property disputes. In s…

title: Talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership: Associations with perceived retention conditions in an Indonesian regional government agency
abstract: Employee retention is a concern for public agencies whose work requires specialized technical competence, and the Regional Financial and Asset Agency (BKAD) of North Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, has experienced a decline in headcount retention that is concentrated among employees on government work agreements (PPPK). This study examines how perceived talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership are associated with perceived retention conditions among current employees. A cross-sectional survey was administered to all 116 eligible staff, comprising civil servants and PPPK employees, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression complemented by confidence intervals, robust standard errors, and dominance analysis. The results show that employees who rate each of the three practices more favorably also report more favorable retention conditions, and that the three practices jointly account for a substantial share of the variation in these conditions. However, the practices cannot be ranked with confidence, and the association for talent management is the least robust. Because only employees who stayed were surveyed, the outcome overlaps conceptually with two predictors, and all data come from a single source, the findings describe associations and do not explain why employees left. The study suggests that career development, knowledge shar…

title: A Systemic Functional Analysis of Modality and Power Relations in Bilingual Corporate Sustainability Discourse
abstract: This study investigates modality as a linguistic resource for constructing reality and negotiating power relations in bilingual sustainability reports produced by SET50-listed companies in Thailand. Drawing on Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL), particularly Halliday and Matthiessen’s interpersonal metafunction framework and Humphrey, Droga, and Feez’s modality analysis model, the study employs a mixed-methods approach integrating Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to examine English and Thai versions of Chairman and CEO messages in 2024 annual reports. Using maximum variation purposive sampling, three companies from different industrial sectors were selected: Thai Oil, Krungthai Bank, and CP ALL. The findings reveal systematic cross-linguistic differences in modality use. English texts predominantly employ higher modality through nominalization, modal adverbials, and modal nouns, projecting institutional certainty, strategic commitment, and organizational credibility aligned with international investor expectations. In contrast, Thai texts rely more heavily on medium and lower modality, particularly through modal verbs such as cha (จะ) and samat (สามารถ), reflecting relational communication strategies, linguistic hedging, and cultural preferences for interpersonal flexibility. Across all sectors, both languages largely avoid coercive high-modality modal verbs, suggesting a s…

title: Anticoagulation and antiplatelet management during ECPR in adults: an international survey of current practices
Effective Machine Learning Methods Used for Stock Price Forecasting: A Performance Evaluation
abstract: A crucial component of financial decision-making and investment planning is stock price forecasting, but it is a complicated problem because of the non-linear and unstable dynamics of the market. In this paper, the researcher outlines a functioning stock market forecasting model which aims at enhancing the degree of forecasting precision founded on the past data of the S and P500 index. The approach involves the use of systematic data gathering and a thorough preprocessing procedure, such as the management of missing data, feature scaling with standardization and chronologically dividing the dataset into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Machine learning (ML) models called Random Forest (RF) and Linear Regression (LR) are used to analyze current market trends and forecast future prices. The key error measures (R2, MSE, RMSE and MAE) are used to evaluate the performance of each model, which guarantees an accurate evaluation of forecasting reliability. The results of the experiments prove that both models provide very accurate predictions, though LR has slightly better error performance, and RF has high levels of generalization. The comparative analysis also demonstrates that proposed models are superior to the current models, such as ANN and SVM. Overall, the work offers an informative, evidence-based prediction model, which is resistant, stable, and can be used in supporti…

title: Research on the calculation method of flexural bearing capacity of wet joints of prefabricated concrete bridge beams based on the strut and tie model
abstract: Abstract Wet joints in prefabricated concrete bridge beams constitute typical disturbed regions (D-regions), where geometric change, reinforcement discontinuity, and material heterogeneity invalidate conventional beam theory. This study proposes a two-level analytical framework for UHPC wet joints: the strut-and-tie model (STM) is first used to represent the internal force-transfer mechanism of the joint region, and a sectional equilibrium analysis is then employed to convert the governing tie-strut state into positive-section flexural capacity. To adapt STM to UHPC wet joints, an effective UHPC participation area is defined from the average crack spacing, and a UHPC-oriented effective compressive-strength coefficient is introduced for the concrete strut. For keyed interfaces, an interface tensile-strength reduction coefficient is further proposed to represent the combined influence of interfacial weakening, mechanical interlocking, and local stress concentration. Four-point bending tests were conducted on specimens with rectangular, rhombus, and Chinese “干”-shaped keyways while keeping joint width, lap form, reinforcement arrangement, material class, and loading scheme unchanged. The proposed method reproduced the test and literature database with a mean error of 11% and a standard deviation of 0.13.
