Longitudinal coupling of automated telephone-based cognitive change and brain atrophy across the Alzheimer’s disease risk continuum
abstract: Abstract Background Repeated monitoring of people at risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) to detect progressive neurobiological change can place substantial demands on clinical resources, highlighting the need for scalable, low-burden approaches. We therefore examined whether changes in speech-based cognitive measures derived from verbal responses in telephone-based assessments were coupled with long-term brain atrophy trajectories spanning normal aging to mild cognitive impairment. Methods In the German PROSPECT-AD study, 198 participants completed phonebot-guided verbal learning (VLT) and semantic verbal fluency (SVF) tasks at home at least twice. We automatically extracted several fine-grained features from recordings and aggregated them into cognitive-task latent factors and speech-based cognitive (SB-C) scores. Individual change rates of these speech-based cognitive measures were estimated using latent growth curve models and associated with regional gray matter atrophy trajectories in a subsample with longitudinal MRI available ( n = 108), using linear mixed-effects models. We also compared the association with atrophy of speech-based and paper-based cognitive measures using predefined comparison-specific non-inferiority margins. title: EXPERIMENTAL INVESTIGATION OF THE EFFECT OF DIFFERENT RECTIFIER TOPOLOGIES ON OUTPUT VOLTAGE AND TOTAL HARMONIC DISTORTION IN SYNCHRONOUS ALTERNATOR EXCITATION
abstract: In this study, the effects of supplying the field (excitation) winding of a synchronous alternator through single-phase half-wave, single-phase full-wave, three-phase half-wave (3-pulse), and three-phase full-wave (6-pulse) rectifier circuits on the no-load stator output voltage and total harmonic distortion were experimentally investigated. The test machine was a synchronous alternator with the following nameplate specifications: 220/380 V (Δ/Y), 2.9/1.7 A (Δ/Y), 1.1 kVA, power factor cos φ = 0.8, rated speed 3000 rpm, 2p = 2 poles, 50 Hz. The measured field winding resistance was R = 197.2 Ω and inductance L = 1743.3 mH, yielding a time constant τ = L/R ≈ 8.84 ms. Measurements were performed on the stator phase-to-neutral voltages using a True RMS power analyser with an accuracy class of ±1% ±1 digit and a harmonic measurement range up to the 40th order. Under excitation currents ranging from 100 mA to 300 mA, the stator phase voltage total harmonic distortion remained nearly constant at approximately 7.1%–8.4% across all rectifier topologies. This finding indicates that the high inductance of the field winding attenuates the supply voltage ripple, acting as a natural low-pass filter and producing a smooth direct current in the field circuit. title: Technology Integration in Basic Education: Teachers’ Experiences, Emotions, and Coping Strategies
abstract: Technology integration has become an expectation in basic education, yet teachers work with uneven access to devices, internet connectivity, technical assistance, and professional development. Existing studies have examined technology use, technostress, or coping mostly within single subject areas, small groups, or pandemic-related contexts, and few have explored teachers’ experiences, emotions, and coping strategies together across elementary, junior high school, and senior high school levels within one school setting. This study explored the experiences, emotional responses, coping strategies, and recommendations of public school teachers in the Department of Education Division of Valencia City, Bukidnon, during School Year 2026–2027. A qualitative descriptive-phenomenological design was used. Nineteen teachers (two elementary, nine junior high school, and eight senior high school) from two public schools were purposively selected. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, audio recordings, and field notes, with member checking after transcription, and were analyzed through six-phase thematic analysis. Code accumulation showed that the last four interviews produced no new codes. Five themes emerged: technology integration as an engaging but context-dependent practice, emotional ambivalence amid technical uncertainty, adaptive professional growth, resilient and co…

abstract: The inclusion of students with visual impairments is a challenge, as the school community needs to go beyond simply having them present in the classroom and ensure access, retention, participation, and quality learning.This requires overcoming physical, communication, and attitudinal barriers through structural and pedagogical adaptations. One of the greatest challenges lies in the teaching of Geometry, a naturally visual field that demands instructional methods that do not rely exclusively on graphical resources. In this context, students with visual impairments face difficulties involving similar figures, since classroom experiences are predominantly visual, highlighting the need for a learning model grounded in inclusive teaching methodologies and pedagogical resources. Thus, the guiding research question emerges: how can the integration of Van Hiele theory, the Fedathi Sequence, and instructional resources, from the perspective of Universal Design, promote the development of geometric thinking in students with visual impairments?The objective is to demonstrate that the interconnection between Van Hiele theory, the Fedathi Sequence, and resources based on the perspective of Universal Design for Learning is of fundamental importance for the development of geometric thinking in students with visual impairments. Investigation of the Relationships Among Smartphone Addiction, Recreational Activity Participation, and Leisure Satisfaction with Structural Equation Modeling: A Study on High School Students
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the relationships among high school students' smartphone addiction, recreational activity participation, and leisure satisfaction, to determine whether these variables differ by gender and grade level, and to test the mediating role of recreational activity participation in the relationship between smartphone addiction and leisure satisfaction. The sample of the study, which was conducted with a quantitative research approach in a correlational survey model, consists of 351 high school in Türkiye. Data were collected through the Smartphone Addiction Scale, the Recreation Activity Participation Frequency Scale, and the Leisure Satisfaction Scale. Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, correlation analysis, and structural equation modeling were used in the analysis of the data. The results showed that smartphone addiction negatively predicted leisure satisfaction, whereas recreational activity participation positively and significantly predicted leisure satisfaction. Smartphone addiction was found to be higher in female students and recreational activity participation higher in male students. Strain-driven and electric-field-tunable self-morphotropic phase boundary in nitride perovskite
abstract: Abstract Ultrahigh piezoelectricity has long been associated with chemically complex morphotropic phase boundaries (MPBs). However, integrating conventional lead-based oxide perovskites onto Si platforms remains challenging, owing to compositional complexity, chemical incompatibility, and thermal-budget constraints. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify a strain-driven self-morphotropic phase boundary (SMPB) in lanthanum tungsten nitride (LaWN 3 , LWN). Biaxial strain ( η ) induces a sequential symmetry progression and enables polarization rotation and ultrahigh piezoelectric responses. We further demonstrate that this SMPB is dynamically tunable by an electric field, yielding ultrahigh piezoelectric stress ( e ij ) and strain ( d ij ) coefficients that exceed those of conventional nitride piezoelectrics (e.g., AlN, AlScN, GaScN) by orders of magnitude. Our results establish a deterministic pathway to ultrahigh piezoelectricity in nitride perovskites, offering a compelling materials platform for adaptive electromechanical devices in next-generation telecommunications and integrated microelectronics.

Developing a Flipped Learning Environment Based on an E-Projects Strategy and Its Impact on Developing Infographic Production Skills
abstract: The study aimed to develop a flipped learning (FL) environment using an e-projects strategy and investigate its impact on developing infographic production skills among students in the Graphic Design and Digital Media Diploma at the University of Hail (UOH). The research adopted a quasi-experimental design and involved 48 students divided into two groups. The first group (24 students) used a standard FL environment, and the second group (24 students) used an FL environment based on an e-projects strategy. The results showed statistically significant differences between the mean scores of the two groups on the post-application of the achievement test, observation card, and final product evaluation card related to infographic production skills (η² = .89, .76, and .65, respectively), indicating large effect sizes. The study recommended using FL environments based on the e-projects strategy for teaching the Graphic Design and Digital Media Diploma courses at UOH, as this approach would contribute to developing students’ cognitive and practical skills and enable them to apply acquired knowledge in practical projects.

title: Articulação entre Teoria Histórico-Cultural e o software Geogebra no ensino-aprendizagem de Matemática: uma revisão de literatura
abstract: This article addresses contemporary discussions on the use of digital technologies in Mathematics Education, highlighting the importance of the articulation between Historical-Cultural Theory and the GeoGebra software as a mediating instrument for learning. The study is part of the research line Digital Technologies in Science and Mathematics Teaching of the Graduate Program in Science and Mathematics Education. The objective of the study was to describe how the scientific literature has discussed this articulation. This is a bibliographic research study with a qualitative approach, basic nature, and exploratory purpose, developed through a survey of academic productions available in the CAPES Theses and Dissertations Database and Google Scholar between 2016 and 2025. The methodological procedures included the search for combined descriptors, the application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, and content analysis of the selected studies. The results showed that the literature identifies GeoGebra as a mediating cultural tool capable of enhancing the formation of mathematical concepts and the development of theoretical thinking when integrated into intentionally organized pedagogical practices. The analyzed studies indicate a predominance of approaches focused on teacher mediation, investigative activities, and the collective construction of meanings. The review also revealed g…

title: Learning Action Cell Implementation Among DepEd Schools in the Philippines: A Scoping Review
abstract: Learning Action Cell (LAC) is a school-based professional development strategy institutionalized by the Philippine Department of Education (DepEd) to enhance teacher competence and promote collaborative learning among educators. This study aimed to map the existing evidence on the implementation of LAC in DepEd schools through a scoping review. Methods: A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Literature was searched through ERIC, ProQuest, Philippine E-Journals, Google Scholar, and supplementary sources. Records published between 2016 and 2026, corresponding to the implementation period following DepEd Order No. 35, s. 2016, were identified and screened using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria in Rayyan. Results: Fifteen (15) studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the review. Findings indicate that LAC is an effective strategy for enhancing teacher collaboration, professional expertise, reflective practice, and pedagogical competence. However, challenges such as insufficient time, heavy teacher workload, limited resources, inconsistent administrative support, and contextual variations were identified as barriers to effective implementation. Although substantial evidence highlights the potential of LAC to promote teacher development, evi…

title: Trends and Impacts of Flipped Learning in Mathematics Education: A Systematic Review over the Past Decade
abstract: The aim of this study is to systematically review research on mathematics education utilizing the flipped learning (FL) model in Türkiye over the past decade. The research employed the document analysis method. The Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, ERIC, ULAKBİM TR Index, YÖK National Thesis Center, and DergiPark databases were systematically examined. A total of 68 studies (26 articles, 9 doctoral dissertations, and 33 master's theses) were identified. Data were analyzed using thematic content analysis. The findings revealed that studies focusing on the FL model in mathematics education in Türkiye have increased significantly, particularly since 2016. Most studies employed mixed-method designs, used small sample sizes, and involved short-term interventions, with secondary school and university students as participants. Common data collection tools included achievement/skill tests, scales, interviews, and observations. FL implementations were frequently supported by student-centered approaches and online platforms. Results suggest that most studies on the FL model in mathematics education primarily focus on students' academic achievement and perceptions of the model. Additionally, several studies have explored its effects on attitudes, knowledge retention, conceptual understanding, motivation, self-regulation, classroom participation, and problem-solving skills. However, further co…

title: Learning Motivation and Study Discipline as Predictors of Students’ Perceived Understanding of Aqidah Akhlak: A Correlational Study
abstract: Aim: This study investigated the individual and joint associations of learning motivation and study discipline with Grade 8 students’ self-reported understanding of Aqidah Akhlak in an Indonesian Islamic junior secondary school. Method: A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional correlational design was employed. The population comprised 95 students at MTs Al-Islam Jamsaren Surakarta, of whom 54 participated through non-probability sampling. Data were obtained using separate questionnaires measuring learning motivation, study discipline and perceived understanding, and analysed by multiple linear regression following diagnostic tests for residual normality, linearity, multicollinearity and heteroscedasticity. Results: Learning motivation was positively associated with perceived understanding after adjustment for study discipline (B = 0.975; ? = .683; p = .001). The coefficient for study discipline was positive but not statistically significant (B = 0.200; ? = .143; p = .458). The overall regression model was significant, F(2, 51) = 50.086, p < .001, R² = .663. Novelty/Implication: In this sample, motivation—but not study discipline—showed a statistically significant unique association with students’ perceived understanding. Because all three variables were measured by self-report and the predictors showed substantial collinearity, the findings do not establish causal eff…

title: Evaluating Student Perceptions of Flexible Learning through the Lens of the Community of Inquiry Framework
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the transition of educational systems to flexible learning, presenting unique challenges for STEM education. This study investigated experiences and perceptions of 396 college students enrolled in science courses at a Philippine university located in a remote place, utilizing the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework and the concept of self-regulation. Employing a convergent mixed-methods research design, the study collected data through online surveys across two semesters. Thematic analysis revealed that the primary benefits of flexible learning included improved time management, development of independent learning abilities, and enhanced media application skills. Conversely, internet connectivity posed the greatest challenge, followed by difficulties in module understanding and managing time. The primary suggestion to enhance flexible learning was the use of video recordings, followed by increased teacher-student interaction, enhanced module content, and maximum utilization of social media platforms. The findings also highlight the importance of cognitive, social, and teaching presences in remote science education. The study concludes that strategically integrating online and offline components can maximize the advantages of flexible learning while addressing the limitations of face-to-face instruction.

title: Self-Awareness Beragama sebagai Praktik Metakognitif: Analisis Refleksi Ibadah dalam Problem-Based Learning pada Pembelajaran PAI di SMAN 1 Losari
abstract: Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) selama ini cenderung berorientasi pada aspek kognitif, sehingga refleksi ibadah sebagai praktik metakognitif belum berkembang secara optimal untuk membangun kesadaran beragama siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk: (1) mengidentifikasi bentuk refleksi ibadah dalam pembelajaran PAI berbasis Problem-Based Learning (PBL); (2) menganalisis proses refleksi ibadah melalui tahapan PBL; (3) mendeskripsikan peran desain masalah dan aktivitas pembelajaran dalam menumbuhkan self-awareness beragama; serta (4) mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat munculnya refleksi ibadah sebagai praktik metakognitif. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kasus di SMAN 1 Losari. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara mendalam dengan satu guru PAI dan dua siswa kelas XI, observasi pembelajaran, serta dokumentasi berupa jurnal refleksi siswa. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) refleksi ibadah muncul dalam bentuk kesadaran terhadap kualitas ibadah, evaluasi dan monitoring konsistensi, serta strategi perbaikan personal; (2) proses refleksi berkembang secara bertahap melalui tahapan memahami masalah kontekstual, merencanakan solusi, serta memonitor dan mengevaluasi pelaksanaan ibadah; (3) desain masalah autentik, aktivitas dialogis melalui diskusi dan presentasi, serta jurnal refleksi dan umpan balik guru berperan penting dalam m…

title: Explainable Machine Learning Algorithms for State-of-Health Estimation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction address related but distinct aspects of lithium-ion battery degradation. This study evaluates separate XGBoost regressors for SOH estimation and RUL prediction using four NASA Ames lithium-ion cells with complete capacity-fade trajectories. The reference capacity is defined as the median capacity of the first five discharges, while end of life (EOL) is defined as the first subsequent cycle at which capacity falls to or below 80% of this reference. At a fixed observation point of 600~s, the prediction features comprise electrical, thermal, cycle-related, initial-reference, and preceding electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements. Full-discharge capacity and future EOL information are used only to construct retrospective target labels and are excluded from the corresponding predictors. A leave-one-cell-out evaluation yields 351 evaluated cycles. XGBoost achieves pooled SOH and RUL mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 1.157 percentage points and 17.948 cycles, respectively, while ridge regression achieves 1.195 percentage points and 17.611 cycles. The held-out B0006 cell exhibits a substantially higher XGBoost RUL MAE of 34.886 cycles, highlighting the limitations of cross-cell prognostic transfer despite low pooled SOH error. title: MACHINE LEARNING AND TEST ANXIETY: A CASE FOR RESTRAINED, TRANSPARENT AND STUDENT-GOVERNED USE
abstract: Test anxiety is a well-documented barrier to student performance, and machine learning (ML) is increasingly proposed as a way to predict, detect and respond to it. This position paper argues that, in the current state of evidence and regulation, ML should be used for test anxiety with restraint. Five problems are identified: weak and noisy ground-truth labels; evaluation practices, such as student-level data leakage and the absence of simple baselines, that overstate accuracy; unequal performance and base rates across groups; reliance on emotion inference from biometric signals that is scientifically contested and, in education institutions, prohibited in the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act with narrow exceptions; and the power asymmetries of assessment settings, where students cannot readily refuse and labels persist. The paper proposes a six-principle framework (support not sanction, student governance, simple models first, prospective and subgroup-aware validation, human in the loop, and no biometric emotion inference during assessment), and applies it to common proposals in a decision table. It addresses four objections and sets out a research agenda that includes trials of whether acting on predictions improves student outcomes, fairness analysis, and studies in low-resource contexts such as Nigerian schools.

A Support Vector Machine-Based Model for Detecting Malicious Social Media Posts
abstract: The proliferation of social media platforms has led to a significant increase in the spread of malicious content, including fake news, hate speech, malware-laden links, and other offensive material capable of inflicting real harm on users and on society at large. This study proposes a Support Vector Machine (SVM) based model for the binary detection of malicious posts, in which a post is treated as malicious if it carries fake (deceptive) news content and as non-malicious if it carries real news. The publicly available Kaggle Fake News detection dataset, comprising 4,009 news articles (2,137 fake and 1,872 real) described by their URL, headline and body text, was used. Each text attribute was converted to a numeric code, and the data were partitioned into 3,207 training and 802 test samples using a random 80:20 split (random seed 10). A Scikit-learn SVC classifier with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel and default hyperparameters was trained in Python 3.7.4. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 88.9% (error rate 11.1%), with a macro-averaged precision of 0.889, recall of 0.890 and F1-score of 0.889; for the malicious class, precision was 0.914 and recall 0.873. These results describe performance on this dataset and split only. The study discusses the limitations of the adopted feature representation and recommends larger, multi-platform datasets in fut…

title: Dia da brincadeira Matemática: aprendizagens de licenciandos em pedagogia em uma ação extensionista na Educação Infantil
abstract: The presence of mathematics in Early Childhood Education and the way future pedagogues are prepared to mediate it constitute the theme of this work. This is a qualitative study, with a narrative approach, developed from a curricularized extension activity called Mathematical Play Day, carried out in the course Special Topics in Education II, of the Pedagogy program at the Faculty of Education of Itapipoca, a campus of the State University of Ceará. The objective was to understand what learning about the teaching of mathematics in Early Childhood Education is constructed by undergraduates as they experience a formative cycle of planning, execution, and reflection, in the context of the curricularization of extension. The activity brought together 40 undergraduates, organized into eight teams with defined internal roles, responsible for developing mathematical activities linked to the numerical, spatial, measurement, and data fields, applied to around 80 children from the Infantil IV and V classes of an Early Childhood Education Center in the municipality of Itapipoca. The analyses were based on the reflective reports produced by the teams after the experience, in which the students described what occurred, the adaptations made in relation to the original plan, and the learning identified during the process. title: Effects of Adaptive and Non-Adaptive Serious Games on Secondary Students' Mathematics Learning Gains
abstract: Adaptivity has emerged as a promising design feature in serious games, enabling learning experiences to be tailored to individual learner needs, performance, and progression. Despite its growing adoption, empirical evidence regarding the educational benefits of adaptive serious games remains limited, particularly in secondary school mathematics contexts. This study investigates the effectiveness of adaptivity in serious games by evaluating MathMystery, a mastery-driven adaptive mathematics game that integrates Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) and Generative AI (GenAI)-supported scaffolding. Using a comparative design, the adaptive version was evaluated against a non-adaptive version with identical learning content and core game mechanics among 254 secondary school students. A quasi-experimental pretest–post-test design was conducted to examine the impact of personalized adaptation on mathematics learning gains, with data analyzed using a mixed repeated-measures ANOVA. The findings indicate that students who engaged with the adaptive serious game achieved significantly greater learning gains than those who used the non-adaptive version. Further analysis indicates that students with lower prior knowledge benefited more from the adaptive condition than their higher-knowledge peers. These findings advance understanding of how knowledge tracing and GenAI can be integrated into adapt…

title: Dinamika Struktur Peran dan Akuntabilitas Kelompok dalam Cooperative Learning Pembelajaran PAI: Dari Free Rider ke Partisipasi Aktif
abstract: Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) berperan penting dalam pembentukan karakter siswa dan memerlukan model pembelajaran yang mendorong keaktifan seperti cooperative learning. Namun, penerapannya masih menghadapi kendala berupa rendahnya partisipasi siswa, munculnya free rider, serta belum optimalnya tanggung jawab individu dalam kelompok. Penelitian kualitatif studi kasus di Madrasah Baiturrahim Cirebon ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan cooperative learning, menggali perancangan serta pelaksanaan pembagian peran dan akuntabilitas, menganalisis dinamika keterlibatan dan transisi menuju partisipasi aktif, serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi dan wawancara mendalam terhadap empat informan, yang terdiri atas seorang guru PAI dan tiga siswa kelas V. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) penerapan cooperative learning dilaksanakan melalui perencanaan kelompok heterogen, pelaksanaan diskusi berbasis fasilitator, dan evaluasi proses-hasil yang komprehensif; (2) pembagian peran terstruktur (ketua, pencatat, penyaji) beserta penegakan tugas individu berhasil menguatkan akuntabilitas; (3) perilaku free rider yang dipengaruhi oleh kondisi lingkungan fisik dan ekspektasi sosial dapat diminimalkan melalui strategi pemanggilan siswa secara acak, penguatan partisipasi individual, dan pemberian umpan balik konstruktif; serta (4) ik…

title: Linguistic Politeness of the Indonesian Language in Teacher-Student Interactions During Learning Activities at MA Alkhairaat Tomini
abstract: This study aims to identify forms of Indonesian linguistic politeness in teacher-student interactions during classroom learning at Madrasah Aliyah (MA) Alkhairaat Tomini. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. Data consisted of teachers' and students' utterances and interview responses collected through observation, non-participant listening, audio recording, note-taking, documentation, and interviews. Data analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. Based on Geoffrey Leech's politeness principle, 68 utterances were identified across six maxims: tact (38), agreement (21), generosity (4), approbation (3), modesty (1), and sympathy (1). The tact maxim was the most dominant in classroom interactions. The madrasah principal, teachers, and students demonstrated positive attitudes toward linguistic politeness across cognitive, affective, and conative dimensions. Politeness was understood as an expression of ethics, respect, and character development. Its implementation was reflected in mutual respect, consideration, polite language, seeking permission, appropriate tone, and consistent teacher role modeling to promote a harmonious learning environment.

title: VISTA Magellanic Clouds deep observations of Classical Cepheids. Precision distances and a collision-driven Small Magellanic Cloud
abstract: The central regions of the Magellanic Clouds are crucial for understanding galaxy interactions and calibrating the cosmic distance scale, yet they remain observationally challenging due to extreme stellar crowding. We utilised deep VISTA observations (VMCDeep) to determine the highest-precision near-infrared period-luminosity (PL) and period-Wesenheit (PW) relations to date for Classical Cepheids (δ Cep class, DCEPs) in the dense central regions of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC). We analysed J and K_s time-series data covering the central 1.77 ^ deg 2 of each galaxy. Utilising approximately 40 epochs per filter and point spread function (PSF)-based photometry, we derived high-quality light curves for 573 and 2090 DCEPs in the LMC and SMC, respectively. We derived exceptionally precise PL and PW relations, exhibiting the lowest photometric dispersion published so far for the Magellanic Clouds. Fourier parameters calculated from the light curves indicate that pulsational models incorporating a mildly non-canonical mass-luminosity relation and a mixing-length parameter of α=1.7 best reproduce the observations. Age derivations confirm a bimodal star formation history in the SMC centre. El derecho a (cambiar) la ciudad disputado. Procesos de organización de la economía popular en un municipio del centro bonaerense en Argentina
abstract: This article examines the appropriation and contestation of urban public space at the local level, taking as case studies two popular economy organizing experiences in a municipality in the central region of Buenos Aires province, Argentina. The selected processes—both belonging to the Excluded Workers' Movement (Movimiento de Trabajadores Excluidos, MTE) in the city of Olavarría—correspond to a cooperative of street market vendors and a cooperative of informal waste pickers (cartoneros). The article examines the collective practices, strategies, and alliances deployed by these workers, taking into account the forms of state regulation that, in addition to conditioning, constrain and shape the arenas of contestation. Territorial tensions emerge from conflicts around existing regulations, involving participants from both cases.Along these lines, the article explores how the struggle over public space reflects the broader struggle over the city and the right to inhabit it, permeating the everyday life and work of both collectives. The argument draws on an ethnographic approach, with data derived from fieldwork conducted by both authors as part of their doctoral and postdoctoral research.

ESTRATÉGIAS TRANSNACIONAIS E CONCENTRAÇÃO DE MERCADO NA ERA DIGITAL: UMA ANÁLISE ECONÔMICA-EMPRESARIAL DO ECOSSISTEMA META
abstract: This article analyzes the imperfect competition corporate strategies of Meta Platforms from the perspective of International Political Economy. The central objective is to understand how the company acts as a transnational corporation to suppress competition and consolidate a global monopoly in the digital social media sector. To this end, the research is grounded in the concepts of platform capitalism and the structural power of knowledge. Methodologically, it adopts a qualitative, exploratory approach based on literature review and the documentary analysis of economic and antitrust reports.

title: Smart AI Trading Chatbot: A Conversational Stock-Market Analysis and Decision-Support System
abstract: Smart AI Trading Chatbot is proposed as a browser-based application for stock search, historical price visualisation, watchlists, and AI-assisted questions. It combines HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with a Python Flask backend, a separate stock-data provider, an AI service, Chart.js, and SQLite. Flask validates market responses and supplies relevant facts to the AI service for plain-language explanation. The analysis layer may calculate returns, moving averages, RSI, MACD, and volatility. Only when data are sufficient and documented rules are met may it show an explained Buy, Hold, or Sell research label with source, timestamp, and risk notes. The AI service does not supply live prices, and the prototype does not execute trades or guarantee returns.

title: Bond Price‐Level Mispricing: A Multifactor Identity
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper develops a new estimator of abnormal bond prices, defined as the deviation of market prices from the present value of future coupon payments and accrued interest under a multifactor stochastic discount factor (SDF). Existing price‐level approaches rely on restrictive assumptions and single‐factor SDFs that are poorly suited to fixed‐income markets. We propose an identity‐based estimator grounded in the Fama and French five‐factor bond model (FFBM). It mirrors traditional abnormal return tests while avoiding overlapping return windows and reducing sensitivity to SDF measurement error. We document four findings. First, the FFBM leaves substantial valuation gaps in bond prices. Second, Credit Risk, Downside Risk, Default Risk, Liquidity Risk, Economic Policy Uncertainty and Market Returns strongly predict abnormal price. Third, a novel composite signal, refined value, parsimoniously captures systematic mispricing. Fourth, refined value subsumes the explanatory power of 23 firm‐ and market‐level characteristics. The results highlight the importance of price‐level analysis in fixed‐income markets.

title: Administracja gospodarcza wobec algorytmów i administracja gospodarcza przez algorytmy
abstract: Artykuł stanowi jedną z części cyklu poświęconego regulacji algorytmicznej w prawie publicznym i obejmuje płaszczyznę ustrojową. Państwo występuje wobec systemów algorytmicznych w podwójnej roli: jako regulator cudzych systemów oraz jako podmiot posługujący się systemami własnymi. Analiza pierwszej roli obejmuje trzy modele egzekwowania prawa rynku cyfrowego w Unii Europejskiej, polski wybór organu kolegialnego dla nadzoru nad sztuczną inteligencją, przebieg wdrożenia aktu o usługach cyfrowych oraz kryteria lokalizacji kompetencji nadzorczych. Analiza drugiej roli obejmuje typologię zastosowań analityki algorytmicznej w aparacie administracyjnym, charakter prawny czynności analitycznych organu i przesunięcie rzeczywistego momentu rozstrzygnięcia do fazy analitycznej. U podstaw artykułu leżą dwie tezy. Pierwsza, że organy nadzoru rynku cyfrowego tworzą odrębny typ ustrojowy organów funkcjonalnie niezależnych, wywodzący się z prawa unijnego. Druga, że algorytmizacja aparatu wymaga dwufazowej kwalifikacji czynności analitycznych, a także zachowania przez organ zdolności zrozumienia stosowanych przez siebie narzędzi. Rozważania zamykają postulaty de lege ferenda dotyczące podstaw prawnych wykorzystania narzędzi analitycznych w działalności organu, dokumentowania jej wyników i granic automatyzacji rozstrzygnięć.

Leveraging Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Ensemble Learning for Feature Selection in Stock Market Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of sectoral stock indices is important for understanding short‐term market dynamics. This study investigates machine learning, deep learning, and ensemble learning approaches for predicting the NIFTY Auto Index, which represents the performance of the Indian automobile sector. Historical multivariate index data obtained from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were processed using chronological train–test partitioning, lag generation, Min–Max normalization, and outlier screening. Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) network, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Random Forest (RF) models were developed with and without XGBoost‐based feature selection, while Grid Search was used for hyperparameter optimization. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was employed to interpret predictor contributions. Model robustness was examined using 10‐fold expanding‐window cross‐validation and a 30‐day forecasting horizon. Performance was assessed using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), with Random Walk Baseline (RWB) and Simple Moving Average (SMA) benchmarks. RF + FS and XGBoost + FS obtained the same overall mean rank of 1.67 and overall rank of 1 (tie). Seed‐based analysis indicated stable RF performa…

title: Regulating the Grey Market: A Legal Analysis of Zero-Day Vulnerability Brokering under Indian Cyber Law
abstract: Zero-day vulnerability brokering, the discovery, valuation and sale of undisclosed software and hardware flaws, has evolved from an informal practice among hobbyist researchers into a structured, high-value global market involving cybercriminals, brokers, security vendors and state actors. Historically, zero-day vulnerabilities were exploited opportunistically, as seen in landmark incidents such as Stuxnet’s exploitation of Windows flaws to sabotage Iranian centrifuges, and later in the HAFNIUM attacks on Microsoft Exchange Servers, attributed by Microsoft to a group it assessed to be state-sponsored, and the Log4Shell (Log4j) exploit, both of which demonstrated how undisclosed vulnerabilities can be weaponised for espionage, ransomware deployment and large-scale data breaches. Commercial brokering has since matured into a lucrative underground and quasi-legal economy, with new vulnerabilities reportedly fetching between $5,000 and $250,000, and firms such as the NSO Group commercialising exploit-based spyware (e.g., Pegasus) for sale to government and law-enforcement clients, raising documented concerns before India’s Supreme Court regarding privacy, surveillance overreach and the absence of adequate statutory safeguards. The current regulatory position remains fragmented: India’s Information Technology Act, 2000 (Sections 43 and 66) penalises unauthorised access but offers no…

title: From Accession Conditionality to Market Imperatives: The Politics of Carbon Border Adjustment and EU–Turkey Climate Convergence
abstract: Abstract This article examines Turkey's 2025 Climate Law as a case of European Union (EU) external governance after accession conditionality declined. Using theory‐guided process tracing and analysis of legislation, debates, documents and stakeholder positions, it traces how the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism altered the costs of regulatory non‐alignment. The findings identify a transmission–transformation gap: market‐access incentives accelerated adoption of an EU‐compatible legal and institutional framework, including an emissions trading system mandate, without comparable change in costly areas such as coal phase‐out, interim targets and limits on executive discretion. The article distinguishes the Brussels Effect as external regulatory transmission, Europeanisation as the depth of domestic change and external differentiated integration as the institutional form of selective alignment. It describes this pattern as defensive integration: instrumental adaptation driven by the need to limit economic losses whilst preserving domestic policy autonomy. Developments through August 2026 indicate institutional development, but implementation outcomes remain unresolved.

Contested Sustainability: Analysing Civil Society Organisations' Mobilisation on EU Sustainable Finance
abstract: Abstract This article aims to shed light on the mobilisation of civil society organisations (CSOs) in European Union (EU) sustainable finance policy as a new area of the EU single market in finance. As both the definition and the policy instruments of sustainable finance are contested, we investigate CSOs' positions in the EU's Platform on Sustainable Finance (Platform) and the extent to which these positions reflect two distinctive policy logics: a ‘financial’ one and a ‘sustainability’ one. We find important differences between CSOs inside and outside the Platform, with the largest divergence between finance CSOs inside the Platform and environmental CSOs outside it. The analysis suggests that CSOs within the Platform self‐selected or were socialised into more mainstream, economic positions, speaking to recent findings that increased civil society engagement from the inside of financial regulation may lead to a ‘financialisation’ or ‘marketisation’ of civil society.

title: When Climate Incentives Matter: CEO Compensation Design and Stock Market Responses to Climate Transition Risk in Europe
abstract: ABSTRACT As climate transition risk becomes increasingly priced in capital markets, firms face growing pressure to demonstrate their preparedness for the low‐carbon transition. Climate‐linked CEO incentives have emerged as a prominent governance mechanism, yet their market relevance remains unclear. Using a sample of listed European firms from 2018 to 2022, we examine when climate‐linked CEO incentives are associated with stock market responses to climate transition shocks. We find that a greater economic weight of climate‐linked compensation is associated with more favorable market responses. This association varies with incentive design and context. Transition‐oriented KPIs exhibit the largest association, whereas process‐oriented KPIs also show a positive association. Broader environmental KPIs, by contrast, show no significant association, although this result may partly reflect their low prevalence in the sample. Moreover, the association is stronger when transition risk is more economically material, emerges under stronger internal climate governance, and is further strengthened by greater responsible capital ownership. These findings contribute to the literature by showing that the market relevance of climate‐linked executive compensation varies with incentive design, transition risk materiality, and the broader governance environment.

title: A car for recognition: The heterogeneous market responses to the emergence of electric vehicles
abstract: Abstract In automobile markets where consumers attach social recognition to car ownership, how does the introduction of a lower‐cost alternative influence the market outcomes of traditional internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs)? Leveraging high‐frequency sales data covering China's entire automobile market from 2018 to 2022, we examine heterogeneous market responses to the emergence of electric vehicles (EVs) across different price segments. Overall, the rise of EVs is associated with lower ICEV sales but higher total automobile sales. More importantly, while EV penetration is negatively correlated with ICEV sales in the low‐ and mid‐end segments, it is positively correlated with ICEV sales in the high‐end segment. Further evidence suggests that the rise of EVs amplifies the symbolic value of high‐end ICEVs, boosting sales of ICEV models with strong social recognition.

title: ICT Infrastructure, Digital Market Access, and the Productivity of Informal Enterprises in Nigeria: The Mediating Role of Digital Transaction Efficiency
abstract: Nigeria is dominated by informal enterprises and their productivity is low. In this study, the relationships between ICT infrastructure, digital market access and productivity of informal enterprises in Nigeria were examined as well as whether digital transaction efficiency mediates between the relationships examined. The cross-sectional survey design was followed in which 412 informal enterprise operators were sampled from four geopolitical zones and completed a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, reliability and validity tests, ordinary least-squares regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis were performed on data. According to the results, ICT infrastructure (β = 0.21), digital market access (β = 0.18) and digital transaction efficiency (β = 0.34) are all positively and significantly directly affecting the productivity. The relationships of ICT infrastructure and digital market access with productivity are partially mediated by digital transaction efficiency, which explains 37 to 38 per cent of the overall effects. The study finds that mere connectivity is not enough; the gains come only when access is transformed into speedy, affordable and dependable transactions. Policy should thus be accompanied by payment interoperability and supporting digital skills, alongside investment into infrastructure.

Emotional self-regulation in athletes of different age groups: implications for psychological support in sports
abstract: Background and purpose The purpose is to conduct a comparative study of emotional maturity, emotional intelligence, and emotional regulation difficulties among young and adult female athletes. Materials and methods The comparative study involved n = 260 athletes, including n = 116 young female athletes (Group 1) and n = 144 adult female athletes (Group 2). At the time of the survey, respondents regularly participated in sports, trained according to the general curriculum, and took part in numerous all-Ukrainian and international sports competitions. The female athletes’ ages met regulatory requirements: young female athletes were 17 to 21 years old (М = 18.96; SD = ±1.59), and adult female athletes were 22 to 36 years old (М = 26.96; SD = ±5.22). Valid, reliable, and representative psychodiagnostic tools were used. Results It was established that respondents’ emotional dysregulation did not exceed clinical reference ranges. A comparison of emotional self-regulation parameters between young and adult female athletes revealed expected superiorities: Group 1 – in “Expressivity” (d = 0.621), “Non-Acceptance” (d = 0.358), “Strategies” (d = 0.449), and “Clarity” (d = 0.603); Group 2 – in “Self-Regulation” (d = 0.367) and “Emotion Recognition” (d = 0.380). The largest effect size was measured in Group 1 for “Expressivity” (d = 0.621). A comparison of correlation matrices revealed stro…

title: Nanocatalytic Pyroptosis Synergizes With High‐Frequency Irreversible Electroporation for Dual Biochemical/Physical Membrane Perforation in Prostate Cancer
abstract: ABSTRACT The recurrence of residual tumor foci after focal therapy for prostate cancer persists as a significant and unresolved clinical hurdle. High‐frequency irreversible electroporation (H‐FIRE), as a cutting‐edge energy ablation technique, has been shown to reduce the survival rate of residual tumors. However, enhancing the efficacy of tumor cell membrane permeabilization through H‐FIRE presents a highly promising approach for the complete elimination of remaining malignant cells. To address this issue, we designed a copper metal‐organic framework (CuMOF@G/S) encapsulating glucose oxidase (GOx) and simvastatin (SIM) to serve as a multifunctional nanocatalytic system capable of synergistically inducing pyroptosis and amplifying H‐FIRE therapeutic outcomes. The CuMOF@G/S composite leverages its Fenton‐like catalytic activity and enzymatic properties to deplete intratumoral glucose, suppress glutathione biosynthesis, acidify the tumor microenvironment, and sustain reactive oxygen species (ROS) overaccumulation. Complementarily, the encapsulated SIM potentiates ROS‐mediated pyroptosis, with increased Gasdermin D (GSDMD) cleavage, thereby augmenting biochemical perforation of tumor cell membranes. This combinatorial strategy establishes a dual‐perforation mechanism, integrating physical membrane disruption via H‐FIRE with biochemical perforation driven by nanocatalyst‐induced py…

title: Evaluation Of The Mandatory Biodiesel Policy On Diesel Imports, Oil And Gas Trade Deficit, And Energy Price Volatility In Indonesia
abstract: This research aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the mandatory biodiesel policy in reducing diesel imports, reducing the oil and gas trade deficit, and mitigating energy price volatility in Indonesia. The study is driven by high dependence on energy imports, which leads to external vulnerability and macroeconomic instability. A quantitative approach was employed using multiple linear regression analysis on secondary annual data from 2005 to 2023. The results indicate that the mandatory biodiesel policy has a significant negative effect on diesel import volumes, where increasing renewable energy blends effectively substitute fossil fuel needs. Furthermore, the policy contributes significantly to reducing the oil and gas trade deficit through substantial foreign exchange savings. The findings also reveal that domestic energy price volatility due to global crude oil fluctuations can be dampened, indicating the effective role of biodiesel as a "strategic buffer" for national energy stabilization. In conclusion, the mandatory biodiesel policy is a vital instrument for maintaining economic and energy stability, particularly in supporting the upcoming B50 implementation. This research provides a comprehensive understanding of biodiesel's macroeconomic impact on national resilience.
venue: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)

title: Variable Effects and Recovery of Coastal Wetland Vegetation in the First Five Years Following ‘Black Summer’ Fires
abstract: Abstract ‘Black Summer’ fires burned extensive areas of Australia’s east coast between July 2019 and March 2020, including coastal wetlands that are typically characterised by regular inundation and waterlogged soils. We combined field surveys and remote sensing across three estuaries in New South Wales (Clyde River, Candlagan Creek and Wonboyn Lake) to assess fire effects and recovery trajectories in mangrove forests, saltmarshes and supratidal forests. Fire impact and recovery patterns varied markedly among ecosystem types and geomorphic settings. In mangrove forests, effects to Avicennia marina ranged from partial defoliation to tree mortality. Recovery has been variable, with epicormic regrowth more common along seaward margins and in some cases occurring up to ~ 42 months after fire. Regeneration via tidally dispersed propagules was spatially variable, and we found little evidence of recovery of Aegiceras corniculatum either through epicormic regrowth or new recruitment. In contrast, rush-dominated saltmarshes recovered rapidly: 96% of the saltmarsh at Wonboyn Lake burned but had regained its extent within 3.5 years, and aboveground biomass at Candlagan Creek showed no difference between burnt and unburnt areas within 18 months. Melaleuca ericifolia, dominant in supratidal forests, showed widespread regeneration by basal resprouting. The limited recovery of heavily impacte…

title: The Influence of Product Quality, Price, and Brand Image on The Body Shop Purchasing Decisions
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of product quality, price, and brand image on purchasing decisions of The Body Shop products at Grand Batam Mall Branch, Batam, both partially and simultaneously. The study uses a quantitative approach with primary data obtained through questionnaires. The study population was 1,950 consumers, while a sample of 95 respondents was determined using the Slovin formula and purposive random sampling techniques. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results showed that product quality had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions with a t-value of 4.909 and a significance of <0.001. Price did not have a significant effect on purchasing decisions with a t-value of 0.417 and a significance of 0.677. Meanwhile, brand image had a positive and significant effect with a t-value of 5.916 and a significance of <0.001. Simultaneously, the three variables had a significant effect on purchasing decisions with an F-value of 91.423. The R² value of 0.751 shows that 75.1% of the variation in purchasing decisions can be explained by product quality, price, and brand image.

Forecasting Twin Pregnancy Outcomes Using Classical Time Series Models: A Comparative Study of ARIMA, ETS, and SARIMA
abstract: Twin pregnancies carry substantially higher risks than singleton pregnancies, particularly in low-resource settings where access to quality maternal care is constrained. This study aimed to analyze and forecast key maternal and neonatal health indicators in twin pregnancies using classical time series models. A dataset comprising 2,000 clinical records from the Rivers State University Teaching Hospital (RSUTH) in the Southern Niger Delta Region of Nigeria was analysed. Three models Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Exponential Smoothing (ETS), and Seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA), were developed and validated using a train–test split. The ARIMA (1,1,1) model attained a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.246, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.277, while the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) is 9.91%, demonstrating a moderate performance in predicting birth weight. The ETS model performed best for Apgar scores, with MAE = 0.387, RMSE = 0.471, and MAPE = 4.85%, and it reproduced stable trends over time. The SARIMA model (1,1,1,2) captured some variations in the mode of delivery but revealed higher forecast errors (MAPE = 31.3%), likely due to variance in monthly deliveries; however, it led to the lowest MAE (0.201) and RMSE (0.230), indicating accurate trend alignment. Findings revealed a rising trend in twin births and a high prevalence of preterm deliveries among women …

title: O USO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA PREVISÃO DA DENGUE E DA INFLUENZA COMO APOIO AO PLANEJAMENTO DE INSUMOS LABORATORIAIS
abstract: This study examines the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in forecasting dengue and influenza and its contribution to laboratory supply management. A literature review was conducted, with a mixed-methods approach and descriptive design, based on scientific articles, official documents and public databases. Predictive models indicate in advance changes in disease behavior, although performance varies by region, period, variables and method. In the laboratory context, supply availability influences the diagnostic flow, and sudden changes in demand impair restocking. There is no evidence that this integration is already established. It is concluded that AI has potential to support laboratory management, provided that its forecasts are validated.

title: A TROMBOFILIA E SEUS IMPACTOS NA CAPACIDADE REPRODUTIVA DA MULHER
abstract: Infertility is defined as the absence of pregnancy after 12 months of regular attempts without contraception and may result from female, male, or combined factors. Thrombophilia, whether inherited or acquired, increases the tendency to form blood clots and has been investigated for a possible association with implantation failure and pregnancy complications. This study aimed to analyze the relationship between thrombophilia and female infertility through a literature review. PubMed, SciELO, NCBI, and Scopus were consulted, and nine relevant articles were selected. The literature describes plausible mechanisms, such as hypercoagulability and microthrombi formation, which may impair uteroplacental circulation; however, findings remain controversial and do not establish definitive causality. It is concluded that investigation should consider each patient’s clinical and reproductive history, rather than recommending indiscriminate screening.

title: Electrolyte‐Facing Interfacial Engineering of Organic‐Inorganic Hybrid Cathodes for High‐Capacity and Stable Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The distinct chemical reactivities of organic and inorganic active materials toward electrolytes are generally considered a major source of interfacial instability, yet this disparity can be leveraged as a powerful design principle for hybrid cathodes. Herein, we exploit this chemical contrast by spatially and interfacially regulating which active material is exposed to the electrolyte. This strategy is demonstrated in a hybrid cathode comprising high‐crystallinity LiFePO 4 nanoparticles (LFP NPs) and iodine‐doped nickel phthalocyanine (I‐NiPc), assembled through well‐defined interfacial interactions without inactive binders. The electrolyte‐facing LFP layer facilitates the formation of a thin, stable cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), thereby suppressing dissolution and parasitic reactions of the underlying I‐NiPc while enabling complementary electrochemical functions of the organic and inorganic components. Consequently, the LFP NP/I‐NiPc composite cathode retains 94.6% of its initial capacity after 3000 cycles at 400 mA g −1 . Increasing the fraction of the high‐capacity organic component while preserving the LFP‐terminated interface further boosts the specific capacity to 427 mAh g −1 and the specific energy to 1091 Wh kg −1 on an active‐material basis, while maintaining 93.9% capacity retention over 2000 cycles. These results establish electrolyte‐facing interf…

title: ANÁLISE DA CAPACIDADE FUNCIONAL DE INDIVÍDUOS DIABÉTICOS FISICAMENTE ATIVOS
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the functional capacity of physically active individuals with diabetes mellitus and prediabetes. The sample consisted of 17 participants, including 15 women and 2 men. The assessment included anthropometric measurements, laboratory test analysis, the sit-to-stand test, the 6-minute walk test, and the Romberg test. The results indicated similar performance in functional capacity, while both groups had lower performance in the walking test. Glycated hemoglobin showed a higher mean in the group of individuals with diabetes. The findings allow the description of functional capacity aspects in the evaluated population and reinforce the importance of regular physical exercise, alongside glycemic control indicators.

Treatment Burden, Person-Centred Nursing Care, and Self-Management Capacity Among Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Diabetic foot ulcers impose substantial clinical and treatment-related demands that may challenge patients' self-management capacity. Although person-centred nursing care supports individualized treatment planning, the relationships between perceived nursing care, treatment burden, and self-management capacity remain insufficiently understood in hospital-based settings. Aim: To examine the associations of treatment burden and person-centred nursing care with self-management capacity among patients with diabetic foot ulcers Approach: This multicentre cross-sectional study analysed simulated data for 232 adults with diabetic foot ulcers from an initial population of 246 patients. Continuous patient-reported scores were examined using multivariable linear regression and exploratory mediation analysis, adjusting for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Results: A total of 232 patients were included (mean [SD] age, 60.2 [10.9] years). Higher person-centred nursing care scores were associated with greater self-management capacity (adjusted B = 0.322; 95% CI, 0.205–0.438; P < .001), whereas treatment burden showed an inverse association (B = −0.011; 95% CI, −0.016 to −0.005; P < .001). Conclusions: Simulated findings suggested opposing associations of person-centred nursing care and treatment burden with self-management capacity. Longitudinal studies using observ…

title: Thermal Dynamics as a Non‐Invasive Indicator for Cycle Life Prediction of LiFePO 4 /Graphite Batteries Under Fast‐Charging
abstract: ABSTRACT Resistance‐induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium‐ion batteries under fast‐charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature‐based prognostic approach for the early prediction of battery cycle life, focusing on LiFePO 4 /graphite cells cycled under a fixed family of multistep fast‐charging protocols at 30°C. The charging process was segmented into four state‐of‐charge (SoC)‐resolved constant‐current regions (CC1–CC4). Voltage and temperature analyses revealed that the initial SoC region (CC1) is particularly sensitive to overpotential development, where a high current density is associated with a premature transition to the constant‐voltage (CV) mode and intensified heat generation. At advanced stages of cycling, temperature behavior exhibited correlations with cycle life consistent with voltage responses. Based on these observations, temperature evolution during the early cycles (third to 10th) was employed to construct a cycle life prediction model. Among the CC‐resolved regions, temperature‐related features from CC1 and CC4 showed higher predictive relevance than those from CC2 and CC3. These results suggest that non‐invasively measured surface temperature can serve as a physically meaningful indicator for early‐stage cycle life prognosis under the studied fast‐charging conditions. title: A IMPORTÂNCIA DO USO DE CAPACETE NA PREVENÇÃO DE FRATURAS CRÂNIO FACIAIS CAUSADAS POR ACIDENTES COM VEÍCULOS ELÉTRICOS
abstract: The use of electric vehicles has grown in recent years, driven by their convenience, yet they are frequently linked to accidents, largely because their use is strongly associated with a failure to wear helmets. This article reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 to gather data demonstrating the importance of helmet use with electric vehicles. Evidence was found regarding the consequences of not using protective gear, specifically the high incidence of head and facial injuries, and, conversely, the extent to which helmet use mitigates these risks, resulting in an 88% reduction in the risk of severe bodily injury. The study concludes that the use of helmets with these vehicles is essential worldwide and that fostering market competitiveness could improve users' quality of life.

title: Development of a Data-Driven Model or Predicting the State of Health of the Li-ion Battery in an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are a key enabler of sustainable aviation, yet their gradual degradation poses a critical safety and reliability challenge, particularly for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in high-temperature environments. This study develops a data-driven model for predicting the State of Health (SOH) of Li-ion batteries using machine learning (ML). The NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) Li-ion Battery Aging Dataset (Battery #5) was used to train and test a Random Forest (RF) regression model, with features selected to capture the effects of high-temperature operation and voltage behavior. The proposed RF model was benchmarked against a Linear Regression (LR) baseline and achieved highly accurate SOH estimation, with a coefficient of determination (R^2 score) of 0.9077 and low error values, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.2578 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.2185. These results also provide a reliable foundation for estimating the battery's Remaining Useful Life (RUL). The proposed approach supports UAV reliability and safer flight operations in high-temperature environments.

title: MARKETING DE BAIXO CUSTO COMO ESTRATÉGIA DE COMPETITIVIDADE NO VAREJO ALIMENTAR DE PROXIMIDADE
abstract: This article analyzes low-cost marketing as a competitiveness strategy in local food retail, focusing on a food market in Santos, São Paulo, Brazil. The study aimed to identify communication, relationships, and promotional practices that could strengthen brand positioning and customer loyalty. An exploratory and descriptive study was conducted using qualitative methods, including a case study, field research, and questionnaires administered to the manager and consumers. Convenience, strategic location, and personalized service were identified as strengths, while limited digital presence, the lack of planned promotions, and formal loyalty initiatives were identified as weaknesses. Accessible strategies, such as WhatsApp Business, themed offers, and a loyalty program, may increase customer retention and business competitiveness.

title: ESG Data Governance for Sustainable Business: Ownership, Authority, and the Strategic Role of HR
abstract: ABSTRACT The growing institutionalization of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting raises questions about how organizations allocate authority over ESG information. While existing research addresses reporting requirements and data governance structures, the organizational processes through which ESG data ownership emerges remain insufficiently theorized. This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework in which ESG data ownership is understood as the institutionally recognized allocation of governance authority over the definition, interpretation, validation, and use of ESG information. It identifies four interacting mechanisms through which this authority is formed: authority claiming, allocation of decision rights, interpretative alignment, and institutional stabilization. The framework distinguishes finance‐centered, sustainability‐centered, and matrix governance configurations as alternative outcomes of formation processes shaped by institutional and organizational conditions. Drawing on contrasting governance traditions in France and Germany, it highlights the context‐dependent nature of these arrangements. Particular attention is given to human resources (HR), whose expertise in producing and interpreting social ESG information does not necessarily translate into recognized decision‐making authority. title: AS MARCAS DAS PALAVRAS: A ALTERIDADE COMO ESTRATÉGIA PEDAGÓGICA PARA A DESCONSTRUÇÃO DO TERMO "ÍNDIO" NO ENSINO DE HISTÓRIA, UMA PROPOSTA DE SENSIBILIZAÇÃO SOBRE IDENTIDADE, LINGUAGEM E RESPEITO AOS POVOS INDÍGENAS NO 7°ANO - PIBID
abstract: This paper presents a pedagogical experience developed with seventh-grade elementary school students within the Institutional Teaching Initiation Scholarship Program (PIBID). The proposal aimed to problematize the generalized use of the term “Indian” and promote discussions about identity, language, otherness, and the diversity of Indigenous peoples. The study is characterized as a qualitative and descriptive experience report. The activity was organized into stages involving the anonymous recording of offensive words and expressions previously experienced by students, the construction of a visual representation of the marks produced by language, a group discussion, and the presentation of the video Índio é uma palavra inventada by Indigenous writer Daniel Munduruku. Subsequently, relationships between forms of naming, historically constructed generalizations, and recognition of the diversity of Indigenous peoples were discussed. During the experience, student participation, reports concerning the effects of offensive language, and expressions recognizing the existence of different Indigenous peoples and identities were observed. The results refer to responses observed during a specific intervention and do not allow conclusions about permanent changes in attitudes or conceptions. It is concluded that activities combining everyday experiences, historical problematization, and In…

title: Aprendizaje de teoría de la imagen con inteligencia artificial generativa (text-to-image)
abstract: Esta investigación tiene como objetivo diseñar, implementar y evaluar una prompt battle como estrategia metodológica para favorecer la comprensión y consolidación de conceptos clave de teoría de la imagen. Metodológicamente, la prompt battle se fundamenta en el aprendizaje basado en problemas, el aprendizaje colaborativo, la gamificación y el aprendizaje basado en prompts. El estudio describe su diseño e implementación en la asignatura Teoría de la Imagen del Grado en Comunicación Audiovisual, expone los resultados del análisis de 1070 prompts, 110 prompts e imágenes evaluativas, las votaciones del alumnado y una encuesta final y examina las limitaciones de la IA generativa.

title: MANAGING THE GROWTH OF A VENTURE THROUGHDIVERSIFICATION STRATEGY IN A COMPETITIVEBUSINESS ENVIRONMENT
abstract: This paper examined the strategic understanding of Businessdiversification as it concerns managing the growth of a venture in theever changing competitive business environment. In Nigeria today,Ventures are essential tools necessary for the achievement of microeconomic objectives in terms of employment generation, productand service delivery and the utilization of local technology. Venturesin Nigeria today are faced with the challenge of competition fromrival firms and hence the need to keep reinventing strategies to attractand maintain their customers by producing products/services thatmeet ever changing needs. The specific concern of this paper is how aventurepreneur designs and implement strategies to succeed in adynamic global marketspace. “Crafting a strategy involves shapingthe market offerings.''Ventureprenuers are saddled with theresponsibility of how to produce successful performance of venturesby building a stronger long term competitive position. Thisnecessitated the study to focus on diversification strategy inmanaging the growth of a venture in a competitive global businessenvironment. The study adopted the qualitative research methodbecause of its descriptive and historical nature which relied onsecondary source of information. Major findings indicated thatdiversification can be the only option left for business growth andexpansion in which a venture can be succes…

title: Effect of Electrodeposition Strategy on Ni–Co Catalysts for Electrochemical HMF Oxidation to FDCA
abstract: The conversion of biomass-derived molecules into sustainable raw materials for bioplastics has attracted significant attention, particularly for the oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA). In this study, Ni–Co bimetallic catalysts were synthesized via three electrodeposition strategies: stepwise (Ni-first and Co-first), mixed, and pulse deposition. The influence of the deposition strategy on morphology, composition, and electrochemical performance was investigated. Scanning electron microscopy revealed distinct morphologies, with the pulse-deposited sample exhibiting a highly uniform and densely packed nanostructure. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirmed that the catalyst composition was governed by the deposition method. Variations in these properties influenced electrocatalytic performance during HMF oxidation reaction (HMFOR) and the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The pulse-deposited sample exhibited superior overall performance, achieving current densities of 187 and 165.8 mA cm−2 for HMFOR and OER, respectively, at 1.72 V vs. RHE. A comparison based on the required potential showed that the pulse-deposited catalyst exhibits a lower onset potential (~1.33 V vs. RHE) and required lower potentials to reach 10 and 25 mA cm−2, indicating improved energy efficiency. It also demonstrated the lowest Tafel slope (98.9 mV dec−1) an…

title: A LUTA DA REPRESENTATIVIDADE FEMININA NA POLÍTICA: ANÁLISE DOS MOVIMENTOS HISTÓRICOS E A INSERÇÃO DAS MULHERES NOS ESPAÇOS DE PODER
abstract: This article analyzes the trajectory of female representation in politics, addressing the main historical movements that contributed to the insertion of women in spaces of power. Initially, it addresses the historical exclusion and social construction of gender roles, analyzing the feminist and suffrage movements, with emphasis on the conquest of women's suffrage in Brazil in 1932. Finally, the work addresses the challenges still faced by women in politics, such as low representation, gender stereotypes and violence. In this way, it seeks to demonstrate that despite the advances, political equality between genders still depends on overcoming social and institutional barriers.
venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica

title: DO RELIGAMENTO CONVENCIONAL À DECISÃO INFORMADA: REVISÃO CRÍTICA DE TRÊS ESTUDOS SOBRE RELIGAMENTO ADAPTATIVO E SELF-HEALING EM SISTEMAS DE POTÊNCIA
abstract: Fixed dead-time reclosing does not check whether the fault persists; smart grids allow measurement-based decisions. This work critically reviews three papers, selected purposively and non-systematically, on adaptive reclosing in transmission and self-healing in distribution, and produces a comparison matrix, a table of extracted results and a list of gaps. In the test networks of one study, the MISOCP reference solution decided in under 1 s, and the faster reinforcement learning policy served 7.9% to 18.9% less energy. The distribution studies lack field validation, and the review reports no tests of its own; integrating decision-making with protection and communication remains open.
venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica

title: GERENCIAMENTO DA CADEIA DE SUPRIMENTOS NA IMPORTAÇÃO DE PRODUTOS SAZONAIS: PLANEJAMENTO DO LEAD TIME DO PORTO DE NINGBO AO VAREJO NA GRANDE SÃO PAULO
abstract: This study analyzes the logistics flow of stationery products, especially notebooks and calendars, from the Port of Ningbo, China, to retail in Greater São Paulo. The research aims to analyze how lead time planning contributes to ensuring product availability during periods of peak demand, considering the stages of transportation, customs clearance, and domestic distribution, seeking to assess the importance of supply chain planning in efficiently meeting the seasonal demand of the back-to-school period.

title: Quantifying the Implied Monetary Value of Specific 2-BDR Residential Property Attributes using Hedonic Pricing Model in Uyo Metropolis
abstract: This study measures the implied monetary value of structural, locational, and environmental attributes for 2-BDR residential properties in Uyo Metropolis, addressing a critical practical gap in local real estate valuation. Utilizing a crosssectional design and stratified random sampling of 387 households, the study employed Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), a disaggregated Hedonic Pricing Model (HPM), and Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM). Unlike constrained single-index models, the fully specified hedonic regression established that structural, locational, and environmental attributes collectively account for 71.4% (𝑹 𝟐 = 𝟎. 𝟕𝟏𝟒, 𝒑 < 𝟎. 𝟎𝟎𝟏) of the variation in residential property rental values. Results establish that structural features serve as the primary value-determinants, while specific locational and environmental variables exhibit nuanced, significant impacts on market pricing. These findings challenge traditional valuation subjectivity, providing a data-driven framework for practitioners to enhance appraisal accuracy, stabilize market prospects, and inform sustainable urban land-use policies amid the city’s rapid population growth.
venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology

title: FERROPTOSE COMO ESTRATÉGIA TERAPÊUTICA NO TRATAMENTO DE CÂNCER DE MAMA TRIPLO NEGATIVO
abstract: Research on the role of ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has highlighted its potential as a promising therapeutic strategy through the regulation of tumor cell metabolism, as well as the identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this context, the modulation of ferroptosis-related metabolic pathways may induce the selective death of cancer cells, expanding the prospects for the development of innovative treatment strategies for TNBC. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis still faces several challenges, including limitations in selectivity, tumor resistance mechanisms, and difficulties associated with its interaction with the immune system. Despite these obstacles, various approaches are being investigated to enhance ferroptosis induction and improve therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer.
