title: AVES DO SABOÓ: A EDUCAÇÃO AMBIENTAL COMO ESTRATÉGIA CONTRA A INVISIBILIDADE DA FAUNA URBANA
abstract: Urban fauna is present in everyday city life but is not always recognized by the population in terms of its diversity and ecological importance. This article analyzes an Environmental Education experience developed with seventh-grade students at UME Martins Fontes, located in the Saboó neighborhood of Santos, São Paulo, Brazil, focusing on birds found around the school. The activity involved a preliminary survey of species, preparation of visual materials, student research, and group seminars. Forty-four bird species were selected as references for the project. Activity records indicated different levels of participation between classes, recognition of species previously referred to generically as “birds,” interest in common and stigmatized species, and difficulties related to research, oral presentation, and the critical use of artificial intelligence tools. Barriers to the participation of a student with disabilities were also identified. It is concluded that Environmental Education activities contextualized with the biodiversity present in the local territory can increase students’ attention to everyday wildlife, foster scientific research and communication, and contribute to questioning negative perceptions of urban animals.
venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica

title: From Disclosure to Capability: Sustainability Materiality as Strategic Adaptation Under Institutional Complexity
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability materiality determines which environmental and social issues an organisation treats as significant enough to shape disclosure, governance and resource allocation. Research examines it predominantly as a property of reporting, leaving unexamined how firms build the capacity to make such determinations repeatedly under changing conditions. Integrating organisational paradox theory with the dynamic capabilities perspective, this study asks how that capacity develops under institutional complexity, drawing on interviews and corporate documents from a UK housebuilder reporting voluntarily. Five paradoxical tensions recurred and none were resolved, spanning early adoption, definitional ambiguity, stakeholder plurality, informational balance and supply chain data governance. Engaging them produced a strengthened sustainability function, cross‐functional routines, benchmarking and relational data governance. The paper defines sustainability materiality capability as a construct with interpretive, relational, infrastructural and governance dimensions, distinguishing the capacity that produces determinations from the determinations themselves, and extends both literatures to the privately owned firm reporting voluntarily.

title: STRATEGI GURU DALAM MENANAMKAN NILAI-NILAI PENDIDIKAN KARAKTER PADA SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR: STUDI KASUS DI SDN SUKOWIYONO 2
abstract: Character education is an essential component of developing elementary school students’ attitudes and behavior. Its implementation requires appropriate and consistent strategies to help students apply character values in their daily lives. This study aims to describe teachers’ strategies for instilling character education values in students at SDN Sukowiyono 2, including the challenges encountered during implementation. This research employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through interviews with teachers involved in implementing character education. The data were analyzed through three stages: data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that teachers employ several strategies, including religious activity habituation, role modeling, advice and reprimands, educational consequences, integration of moral messages into classroom learning, extracurricular activities, and collaboration with parents. Teachers perceived students’ religious values and general etiquette as relatively good; however, politeness in language and responsibility in completing assignments still required continuous guidance. These findings suggest that character education requires teachers’ consistency in providing positive examples and guidance, as well as support from families and the school environment. This study is expected to provi…

title: ELEMENTOS LÚDICOS DA CAPOEIRA COMO ESTRATÉGIA INCLUSIVA NAS AULAS DE EDUCAÇÃO FÍSICA
abstract: School inclusion requires pedagogical experiences that recognize student diversity and broaden opportunities for participation, learning, interaction, and belonging. In this context, Physical Education may contribute through bodily practices that combine movement, playfulness, musicality, cooperation, and expression. This article aims to discuss playful elements of Capoeira as an inclusive pedagogical possibility in the early years of Elementary School, particularly considering students with characteristics associated with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). This is a qualitative, exploratory, and bibliographic narrative study based on scientific literature concerning physical activity, executive functions, school inclusion, autism, ADHD, musicality, and bodily practices, as well as Brazilian educational documents. The literature indicates that games, rhythms, songs, clapping, imitation, ginga, evasive movements, motor challenges, and cooperative situations may broaden forms of participation when accompanied by clear instructions, predictability, flexibility, and different possibilities for expression. It is concluded that Capoeira, understood as an Afro-Brazilian cultural manifestation and bodily practice, can broaden the repertoire of inclusive Physical Education, provided that it is not presented as a treatment for diagnoses an…

title: DETECÇÃO DE RANSOMWARE EM PADRÕES DE ACESSO A ARMAZENAMENTO COM GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS: GENERALIZAÇÃO PARA FAMÍLIAS INÉDITAS E O PAPEL DA REGRA DE DECISÃO
abstract: Deep learning ransomware detectors are usually evaluated on the same families used for training. A graph representation of storage regions, processed by GraphSAGE, was evaluated on the RanSMAP dataset under complete family exclusion and hardware change. Across eighteen training runs the model reached an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.999 per window and perfect per-execution accuracy within distribution, yet lost two thirds of the executions of a family withheld from training, with no degradation signalled by validation. The failure proved to be one of calibration, not discrimination: the per-execution AUC remained at 1.000. Replacing the fixed threshold by a decision relative to local benign executions restored full sensitivity without retraining.

title: Glucose‐Mediated Charge Transport and Dielectric Energy Storage Behavior in Aloe vera Revealed by Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Glucose plays an important role in plant metabolism and signaling; however, its influence on the electrical behavior of living plant tissues remains largely unexplored. In this study, the effect of glucose treatment on the charge transport and dielectric behavior of Aloe vera leaves was investigated using electrical impedance spectroscopy over a frequency range of 20 Hz–5 MHz. Plants were treated with 1, 5, and 10 mg/L glucose solutions for 7 days, and the electrical response was evaluated using impedance, conductivity, dielectric, and electric modulus analyses. The Nyquist spectra exhibited depressed semicircular arcs, indicating non‐Debye electrical behavior. Glucose treatment significantly increased the electrical resistance, with grain resistance increasing from 2.45 Ω in the control to 305 Ω at 5 mg/L, whereas grain‐boundary resistance increased from 10.2 to 18,193 Ω. The lowest DC conductivity was also observed at 5 mg/L, compared with that for the control, indicating restricted charge transport. Dielectric constant and dielectric loss decreased after glucose treatment, suggesting reduced charge accumulation and polarization within the leaf tissue. Electric modulus analysis further revealed concentration‐dependent changes in charge carrier relaxation. Overall, the results demonstrate that glucose can significantly modify the electrical and dielectric response of …

title: Sustainability Uncertainty, ESG Performance, and Firm Financial Outcomes: Evidence From European Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between sustainability uncertainty, corporate profitability, and financing costs, with particular emphasis on the moderating role of firm‐level sustainability performance. Using 6887 firm‐year observations from 890 publicly listed firms across 10 European countries during 2015–2025, the study employs pooled ordinary least squares regressions. The findings reveal that sustainability performance exhibits relatively weak and inconsistent associations with accounting profitability, while its relationships with financing costs are more pronounced. Interestingly, higher Sustainability Uncertainty Index (SUI) is associated with lower weighted average cost of capital (WACC), contrary to conventional uncertainty‐risk expectations. However, given the composite nature of SUI, this relationship cannot be attributed directly to greater sustainable‐finance development or specific regulatory conditions. Furthermore, the positive interactions between SUI and sustainability performance suggest that the financing‐cost advantages associated with stronger environmental, social, and governance and Biodiversity Impact Reduction (BIR) performance tend to weaken as SUI increases. Additional robustness tests provide consistent support for this moderating relationship in the WACC models, particularly for BIR. These findings highlight the conditional nature o…

title: Financial Literacy, Lifestyle, and Financial Technology Use as Predictors of Financial Behavior Among University Students
abstract: Financial behavior relates to the ability to understand financial information, manage one’s income, and prioritize the use of funds. Financial behavior, particularly among students, is often influenced by lifestyle, social circles, and the ease of transactions—such as following trends or acting on emotional impulses without rational consideration. Financial literacy helps students develop wiser financial behavior, while lifestyle reflects patterns of fund usage in daily life. On the other hand, the development of financial technology provides ease of transaction that has the potential to influence students’ financial behavior. This study aims to explain the influence of financial literacy, lifestyle, and financial technology on the financial behavior of students in the Faculty of Economics and Business at Mahasaraswati University, Denpasar. The sample in this study consisted of 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The analytical tool used to test the hypotheses is multiple linear regression. The results of the study indicate that financial literacy has a positive and significant influence on the financial behavior of students at the Faculty of Economics and Business, Mahasaraswati University, Denpasar, whereas lifestyle and financial technology do not influence the financial behavior of students at the Faculty of Economics and Business, Mahasaraswati University, D…

title: The effects of financial distress and audit delay on audit quality: Firm size as a moderator in Consumer Cyclicals manufacturing companies
abstract: Audit quality is a critical concern because a company's financial condition and audit timeliness may influence its choice of reputable auditors. This study examines the effects of financial distress and audit delay on audit quality and tests the moderating role of firm size. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data from 41 manufacturing companies in the Consumer Cyclicals subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2023–2025, yielding 123 firm-year observations. The data were analyzed using Firth logistic regression. The results indicate that the Z-Score has a positive and significant effect on audit quality, whereas audit delay has no significant effect. Firm size is the strongest predictor, while the interaction between the Z-Score and firm size is positive and significant, although its significance is sensitive to GEE testing. These findings indicate that financial condition and company scale are associated with the likelihood of engaging Big Four audit firms, with firm size strengthening this relationship. INFLUENCE OF EMPLOYEE ATTITUDE ON ORGANISATIONAL PERFORMANCE IN SELECTED MANUFACTURING COMPANIES IN ADAMAWA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Employee attitude has long been recognized as an important determinant of organizational performance; however, the relative influence of its cognitive, affective, and behavioural dimensions remains inconclusive, particularly within the manufacturing sector in developing economies. This study examined the influence of employee attitude on organizational performance in selected manufacturing companies in Adamawa State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study assessed employees' cognitive, affective, and behavioural attitudes, examined employees' perceptions of organizational performance, and determined the influence of each attitude dimension on organizational performance. A quantitative research approach employing a descriptive survey and explanatory research design was adopted. The target population comprised employees of selected manufacturing companies in Adamawa State, from which a sample of 199 respondents was drawn using appropriate sampling procedures. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on a fivepoint Likert scale and the instrument was subjected to validity and reliability tests, while the data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations) and multiple regression analysis. Diagnostic tests confirmed that the assumptions of regression analysis were satisfied. The regression results showed tha…

title: DO DIREITO À INCLUSÃO AO DIREITO DE APRENDER: PRÁTICAS FLEXÍVEIS E SUPORTES INDIVIDUALIZADOS NA ESCOLARIZAÇÃO DE ESTUDANTES COM DEFICIÊNCIA
abstract: School inclusion is a right guaranteed to persons with disabilities, but its implementation cannot be reduced to enrollment or physical presence in the regular classroom. This study discusses the limitations of rigid conceptions of full inclusion when they are not accompanied by adequate teaching conditions, accessibility, qualified professionals, and individualized supports. This is a qualitative, bibliographic, and reflective study based on the author’s educational experiences in public and private schools and on the analysis of Brazilian and international legislation and literature concerning Special Education. Contributions from Mendes, Fuchs and Fuchs, and Lacerda are discussed, as well as principles associated with multi-tiered support systems, co-teaching, Universal Design for Learning, and flexible organization of educational services. The analysis indicates that a student’s physical placement is not a sufficient criterion for evaluating the quality of inclusion. Participation, learning, communication, development, and access to necessary resources must guide pedagogical decisions. It is concluded that inclusive education committed to the right to learn requires individualized planning, professional training, accessibility resources, collaboration among professionals, and continuous assessment of the barriers and needs presented by each student.

title: MEDIATING EFFECT OF SERVANT LEADERSHIP ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ORGANISATIONAL CULTURE AND EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE IN TERTIARY INSTITUTIONS IN ADAMAWA NORTHERN SENATORIAL DISTRICT, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the mediating effect of servant leadership on the relationship between organisational culture and employee performance in tertiary institutions in the Adamawa Northern Senatorial District. The study was motivated by the need to explain how organisational conditions are translated into employee performance, particularly given the limited empirical evidence on the intervening role of servant leadership in tertiary institutions within Northern Nigeria. A quantitative research approach and cross-sectional survey design were adopted, which enable data to be collected from employees of tertiary institutions in the study area using a structured questionnaire. The descriptive statistics was used to explain the characteristics of the respondents and the regression analysis via the Hayes’ process macro 5.0 was used fr mediation analysis. The analysis established that servant leadership partially mediated the relationship between organisational culture and employee performance, indicating that organisational culture influences employee performance both directly and through servant leadership. The study therefore highlights the need for tertiary-institution management to develop organisational cultures and leadership practices that jointly support sustained employee performance. The study concludes that employee performance in tertiary institutions is enhanced where fav…

title: Health Equity Implications of the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program in Safety-Net Hospitals: Policy Challenges and Reform Opportunities
abstract: The Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) was developed to reduce avoidable 30-day returns to the hospital through financial penalties directed at hospitals with excess readmission rates. Although the program has been associated with modest reductions in readmissions, growing evidence suggests that it disproportionately penalizes safety-net hospitals serving populations facing structural barriers to care. Current risk-adjustment strategies inadequately account for social determinants of health (SDOH), structural inequities, and barriers to outpatient care, contributing to inequitable penalty distribution and resource depletion in underserved communities. This article examines the limitations of the HRRP through a policy and health equity lens using the RE-AIM framework. Key concerns include inadequate social risk adjustment, state-level variation in Medicaid stratification, increased reliance on observation stays and emergency department revisits, and potential unintended harms including increased mortality in certain populations. Evidence-based reforms are proposed in 2 main areas, which are policy reforms, including equity-focused penalty modifications and comprehensive SDOH-based risk adjustment, and practice reforms, including reinvestment into the infrastructure of safety-net hospitals.

title: KD4MT: A Survey of Knowledge Distillation for Machine Translation
abstract: Abstract Knowledge Distillation (KD) as a research area has gained a considerable traction in recent years as a compression tool to address challenges related to ever-larger models in NLP. Remarkably, Machine Translation (MT) offers a much more nuanced take on this narrative: in MT, KD also functions as a general-purpose knowledge transfer mechanism that shapes supervision and translation quality as well as efficiency. This survey synthesizes KD for MT (KD4MT) across 105 papers. We begin by introducing both MT and KD for non-experts, followed by an overview of the standard KD approaches relevant to MT applications. Subsequently, we categorize advances in the KD4MT literature based on (i) their methodological contributions and (ii) their practical applications. Our qualitative and quantitative analyses identify common trends in the field and highlight key research gaps as well as the absence of unified evaluation practice for KD methods in MT. We further provide practical guidelines for selecting a KD method in concrete settings and highlight potential risks associated with the application of KD to MT such as increased hallucination and bias amplification. Finally, we discuss the role of LLMs in re-shaping the KD4MT field. To support further research, we complement our survey with a publicly available database summarizing the main characteristics of the surveyed KD methods and a…

Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Copper Solids from Material-Constrained Atomic Optimization
abstract: Abstract Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets enable systematic complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation in molecular quantum chemistry, but their diffuse atom-optimized primitives can lead to severe linear dependence in periodic solids, particularly metals and metal-containing compounds. Here, we introduce material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO), which preserves the atomic and correlation-consistent character of Gaussian basis sets while penalizing overlap-matrix ill-conditioning in representative solid-state environments. As a proof of concept, we develop Dunning-style MCAO-cc-pVXZ (X = D, T, Q) basis sets for Cu with nonrelativistic and scalar-relativistic all-electron potential, effective core potential, and pseudopotential treatments. The resulting basis sets exhibit robust numerical stability across bulk Cu, Cu-containing compounds, and Cu surfaces while accurately reproducing plane-wave reference structural properties and electronic band structures. Their correlation-consistent construction enables CBS-extrapolated random-phase approximation calculations for bulk Cu and CO adsorption on Cu(111), providing a systematic framework for assessing basis-set, relativistic, and core-treatment errors in correlated electronic-structure calculations of transition-metal solids.

title: First Report of Diaporthe melonis Causing Stem Blight of Eggplant in China
Instrumental convergence and power seeking
abstract: Abstract Recent years have seen increasing concern that artificial intelligence may soon pose an existential risk to humanity. One leading ground for concern is that artificial agents may be power-seeking, aiming to acquire power and in the process disempowering humanity. I show how the argument from power-seeking rests on a strong version of a claim known as the instrumental convergence thesis. I explore leading defenses of the instrumental convergence thesis and argue that none establishes the thesis in a strong enough form to ground the argument from power-seeking. I discuss implications for longtermism, the governance of artificial intelligence, and the methodology of studying risks posed by artificial agents.

title: Linking Solvation Structure, Activity, and Electronic Structure to Electrochemical Stability in Lithium-ion Battery Electrolytes
abstract: Abstract Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level understanding of how salt concentration influences electrochemical stability remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, a lattice fluid theory, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), density functional theory (DFT), and electrochemical measurements to quantitatively link solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to the electrochemical stability of LiPF6 in EC/EMC (3:7 v/v) across a wide concentration range. We derive simple analytic expressions for species activities, parametrized using coordination numbers obtained from Raman spectroscopy, and validated against both MD simulations and experiment. Increasing salt concentration promotes PF6– participation in the Li+ solvation shell while suppressing free solvent populations, leading to systematic changes in the activities of species and an expanded electrochemical stability window. The lattice fluid theory directly links concentration-dependent solvation structure to measurable shifts in redox potentials via the Nernst equation, in good agreement with both computational predictions and experimental observations. DFT-predicted shifts in the unoccupied electronic states are confirmed by XAS measurements. These results establish a quantitative framework lin…

title: Demand for Labor and Manpower to labor Market in Kaysonephomvihan city Savannakhet Province
abstract: This study examines labor Demand for Labor and Manpower to labor Market in Kaysone Phomvihane city, Savannakhet province. The sample group is made up of corporations and educational institutions, which are separated into two groups: those that use labor 120 units and those that produce labor 7 institutions. Data was collected using questionnaires, interviews were conducted utilizing development methods, and the SPSS program was used for data analysis. The study's findings revealed: In terms of general labor requirements, the majority of entrepreneurs are female 60.8 percent with 46 percent being under the age of 30. Entrepreneurs have increased demand, particularly for workers with less than a bachelor's degree, who account for 27.46 percent, followed by workers with a bachelor's degree 17.86 percent. The majority of the subjects of study that entrepreneurs require are accounting fields, accounting for 23.25%. Commercial sectors account for 18.67 percent; non-specific subjects account for 17.11 percent; and mechanical engineering accounts for 15.78 percent. Entrepreneurs will require 51.37 percent of labor in 2024, while both public and private educational institutions can create 48.63 percent of labor to meet labor market demands. Regarding the result of the business units' labor shortage, there are many laborers who have to negotiate about salary or wages (28.68 percent), lab…

title: Market analysis of chondroitin and glucosamine as dietary supplements
abstract: Abstract Chondroitin and glucosamine are widely used as dietary supplements for osteoarthritis (OA), despite inconsistent clinical evidence and limited regulatory oversight. Concerns remain regarding efficacy, bioavailability, safety and discrepancies between marketed claims and scientific data. To investigate the characteristics of marketed chondroitin and glucosamine dietary supplements and to evaluate the clinical evidence regarding their efficacy and safety in OA. This study combined a cross-sectional market analysis of 110 dietary supplements with a structured review of clinical studies. Supplements were analyzed with respect to composition, dosage, pricing, labelling and marketing strategies. A PubMed search was conducted to identify clinical trials and meta-analyses investigating orally administered chondroitin and/or glucosamine in OA patients. Eligible studies were analyzed descriptively due to heterogeneity. The product analysis revealed highly variable pricing, with substantial cost differences and no clear link between price and clinical effectiveness. Marketing strategies often relied on packaging and presentation to imply scientific validation, frequently without sufficient supporting evidence. The available clinical evidence does not provide a consistent or robust basis for confirming the efficacy of chondroitin and glucosamine in OA. The effectiveness of chondro…

title: Importancia del lavado de manos para prevenir enfermedades infecciosas en comerciantes del Mercado Central
abstract: Se analizó el lavado de manos como medida de prevención de enfermedades infecciosas en los comerciantes del Mercado Central de Tulcán, desde la teoría del entorno de Florence Nightingale. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo y transversal; de una población de 170 trabajadores se encuestó a una muestra aleatoria de 90 (confianza del 90 %, error del 6 %) con un cuestionario cerrado. El 92,2 % tenía acceso a agua y jabón y el 83,3 % usaba jabón al lavarse las manos. Después de tocar dinero o superficies compartidas, el 33,7 % se lavaba siempre las manos y el 42,7 % a veces. El 81,1 % creía que el lavado previene enfermedades y el 28,9 % lo promovía siempre entre compañeros y clientes. Los comerciantes reconocen la utilidad del lavado de manos, pero lo practican de forma irregular; se requieren educación sanitaria y un suministro constante de agua y jabón.

The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth and cognition in middle childhood
abstract: Abstract Background The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth, and cognition in childhood is unknown. This study aimed to characterize associations between (i) regional brain growth from birth to 6–8 years and socio-environmental factors; and (ii) regional brain growth and cognitive outcomes in middle childhood. Methods One hundred and thirty-seven 6–8-year-old children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neonatal and paediatric brain MRI and a full-scale IQ assessment. Data on household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation, and early cognitively stimulating home environment were collected. Regional brain growth (extracerebral CSF, ventricles, cortical grey matter, white matter, deep grey matter, cerebellum, brainstem) from the neonatal period to 6–8 years was assessed using Gaussian process regression. Results Low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth (B, 95% CI −1.14, −1.88 to −0.396; p FWE = 0.044) and extracerebral CSF expansion (−1.55, −2.51 to −0.585; p FWE = 0.042). Higher cortical grey matter (3.89, 1.12–6.65; p FWE = 0.038) and brainstem (3.24, 0.894–5.58; p FWE = 0.038) growth were associated with better full-scale IQ. Brainstem ( p = 0.014), but not cortical grey matter ( p = 0.177), remained significant after adjustment for socio-environmental factors. Conclusions Support for financ…

Machine learning based prediction of thermo-hydraulic performance in solar air heaters with phase change material and polygonal ribs
abstract: Abstract This study presents a machine learning (ML) framework to predict the thermal and airflow efficiency of solar air heaters (SAHs) enhanced with a polygonal ribbed absorber plate and phase change material (PCM). Using experimental data from varied mass flow rates of 0.062 kg s −1 , 0.028 kg s −1 , and 0.01 kg s −1 , an XGBoost model was trained to forecast thermo-hydraulic performance to achieve an R 2 of 95% precision against experimental test results. By replacing complex physical experiments with rapid ML predictions, this approach offers a cost-effective tool for optimising SAH designs, cost and simulation duration. The integration of PCM for heat storage (paraffin wax) and rib (Polygonal rib) induced turbulence improves energy retention while minimising pressure drops. The model demonstrates potential for rapid prediction capability, enabling dynamic adjustments to operating parameters, enhancing system thermal efficiency under fluctuating ambient conditions. This synergy of geometric innovation, thermal storage, and data-driven modelling underscores a scalable strategy to advance solar thermal technology, bridging thermal performance, affordability, and sustainability. The work aligns with global renewable energy targets by accelerating the deployment of efficient, low-carbon heating solutions through intelligent design optimisation .

title: Systematic evaluation of machine learning and explainable AI for NOx emission prediction in gas turbine systems
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for improving environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency in gas turbine systems. However, the complex nonlinear interactions among environmental and operational variables make reliable emission forecasting challenging using conventional modeling approaches. This study presents a comprehensive machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework for NOx emission prediction using the Gas Turbine CO and NOx Emission dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Ten regression algorithms, including linear, tree-based, ensemble, and gradient-boosting models, were systematically evaluated and optimized using Grid Search, Random Search, and Bayesian Optimization. Model performance was assessed using multiple regression metrics, including R², MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE, EVS, and MedAE. Among all evaluated approaches, Bayesian-optimized LightGBM achieved the best predictive performance with an R² score of 0.8928 and an RMSE of 3.7694. To enhance model transparency, multiple complementary XAI techniques, including SHAP, Permutation Feature Importance, Partial Dependence Plots, Individual Conditional Expectation, LIME, surrogate modeling, and residual analysis, were employed. title: CardioAI: A Multi-Modal Stacking Ensemble Platform for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction and 12-Lead ECG Classification with Explainable AI
abstract: Heart disease is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and early prediction plays a crucial role in reducing mortality and improving patient outcomes. This paper presents a comparative study of machine learning and deep learning approaches for heart disease prediction using different types of medical data, including clinical records, ECG signals, and echocardiography images. Traditional machine learning models such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest are effective for structured clinical data, while deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are used for processing ECG signals and medical imaging data. In addition, multimodal approaches combining multiple data sources are also explored to improve prediction performance. To support the comparative analysis, three modules were implemented: Echo, ECG, and Clinical. The Clinical stacking model achieved the highest accuracy of 94.54%, followed by the ECG CNN-based model with 82.08%, and the Echo MobileNetV2 model with 80.7%. The results show that structured clinical data provides more reliable predictions, while signal and imaging data require larger datasets and more complex models. Despite improvements in prediction accuracy, challenges such as small dataset sizes, lack of interpretability, and high computational cost still exist. This study highlights the importance of …

title: Pathway-Aware Multimodal Transformer for Explainable Survival Prediction in Bladder Cancer
abstract: Abstract - Clinical survival prognostication in Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA) is hindered by the translational disconnect between spatial histopathology and molecular genomics, where conventional models suffer from genomic overfitting or uninterpretable late-fusion concatenation. We present OncoBot, a Pathway-Aware Multimodal Transformer (PAMT) that unifies gigapixel Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) with bulk RNA-Seq transcriptomics. OncoBot regularizes 4,500 gene features into 320 canonical KEGG cancer pathways via a sparse bipartite binary mask, utilizing pathway vectors as Queries to guide asymmetric multi-head cross-attention over 384-dimensional morphological tokens extracted by a self-supervised DINO ViT-S/16 backbone across 1,024 tissue patches. An optimized preprocessing pipeline resolves OpenSlide C-level memory leaks through dynamic thumbnailing and controlled multiprocessing, slashing tiling latency from 120s to 15s while compressing 4GB WSIs into 1.5MB latent tensors. Optimized via a joint objective combining Cox Proportional Hazards and InfoNCE contrastive mutual information loss on 403 TCGA-BLCA patients, OncoBot achieves a state-of-the-art Harrell’s C-index of 0.784, outperforming unimodal transcriptomics (0.672), vision MIL (0.698), and late concatenation (0.718) by up to 16.7%. Finally, high-resolution spatial cross-attention hea…

title: DynaCDR: dynamic graph learning for accurate cancer drug response prediction
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate prediction of cancer drug response is essential for precision oncology, yet existing computational methods, particularly static graph-based models, suffer from two fundamental limitations: information leakage arising from global graph construction that inadvertently mixes training and test instances, and insufficient integration of multi-modal biological data with context-dependent relational reasoning. Results To overcome these challenges, we propose DynaCDR, a multi-modal framework built upon a dynamically constructed batch-local heterogeneous graph strategy. Unlike static global graphs that risk leaking test information through fixed topological connections, DynaCDR constructs local subgraphs exclusively from samples within each training batch, ensuring strict separation between training and test instances while capturing context-dependent drug-cell line interactions. Extensive experiments on the GDSC dataset demonstrate that DynaCDR achieves superior predictive performance ( RMSE = 0.7836, R 2 = 0.8817), outperforming the leakage-free static baseline, indicating that the gains arise from dynamic, context-dependent relational learning rather than from leakage avoidance alone. The model exhibits remarkable robustness in few-shot scenarios (using only 5–20% of training data) and exceptional generalization to unseen cell lines. More importantly, und…

title: A cross-method performance study: DOE-based regression, physics-based simulation, and sensor-based machine learning for injection molding quality prediction
abstract: Abstract Quality monitoring in injection molding can be achieved through various modeling techniques, yet no clear framework exists to guide practitioners in selecting the most appropriate approach for their specific application requirements. Understanding which data sources and modeling strategies are needed, based on the required degree of accuracy, transparency, and cost constraints, remains an important and unresolved research gap in the industry. This study aims to address this challenge by presenting a comparative analysis of three predictive modeling methodologies for evaluating injection molded part quality, each representing a distinct level of complexity and cost: (1) multivariate regression modeling using design of experiments (DOE), the simplest and lowest-cost approach relying solely on machine data, which achieved an average MAPE of 0.95%; (2) physics-based simulation using Moldex3D, which requires commercial software licensing and performed well under normal fill conditions but was substantially penalized by short shot cycles that the simulation could not accurately represent, resulting in an average MAPE of 2.03%; and (3) machine learning (ML), utilizing a nested deep learning architecture based on long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, the most resource-intensive approach requiring in-mold sensors and data acquisition systems, which achieved an average MAPE of…

From Expected Demand To Actual Consumption: An Exploratory Study Of Food Surplus In Event Catering
abstract: Event catering involves substantial demand uncertainty because meal preparation decisions are generally made before actual consumption occurs. Although inaccurate demand forecasting has been identified as an important contributor to food surplus and waste in foodservice operations, relatively limited research has examined this issue using event-level operational data, particularly in temporary, time-sensitive catering environments. This study explores the gap between expected meal demand, prepared quantities, and recorded food surplus using anonymized operational data from an event catering provider. The dataset comprises 49 catering service records collected between 2025 and 2026, representing 2,351 prepared meals. Descriptive statistics and exploratory non-parametric analyses were employed to examine patterns associated with meal preparation, catering format, food surplus, workforce deployment, and operational exceptions. The results show that expected meal quantities were identical to prepared quantities in all 49 service records; nevertheless, 439 meals were recorded as remaining after service, representing an aggregate recorded surplus proportion of 18.7%. Food surplus was recorded in 39 of the 49 service observations. title: Clinical, Genetic, MR Spectroscopy characteristics and Response to Flunarizine in Episodic Ataxia Type 2: The Sheffield Ataxia Cohort
abstract: Abstract Episodic ataxia type 2 (EA2) is an autosomal-dominant calcium channelopathy caused by pathogenic mutations in the CACNA1A gene, characterized by episodic cerebellar symptoms and marked phenotypic heterogeneity. Data on real-world clinical features and treatment responses, particularly in the era of major genetic advances, remain limited. This is a retrospective observational single-centre case series of 58 individuals from 38 families with genetically confirmed EA2. Clinical, demographic, genetic, and treatment data were extracted from medical records using a standardized Excel-based data collection tool. Symptom patterns with associated neurological features, genetic characteristics, and treatment responses were analyzed descriptively. Paired MRI imaging including MR spectroscopy (MRS) of the cerebellum at baseline and follow up data, and medication efficacy were assessed using patient-reported benefit, and statistical analysis was performed using Wilcoxon signed rank test and Exact binomial testing respectively. The mean age at diagnosis was 35.2 ± 21.5 years, and a positive family history was identified in 48 patients (82.70%). The most frequent clinical manifestations were gait instability (87.93%), dysarthria (39.66%), headache (58.62%) and isolated dizziness (48.28%). Financial Inclusion and Economic Development: The Role of Digital Banking and FinTech in Reducing Poverty
abstract: Financial inclusion has become an important component of contemporary economic-development strategies because access to affordable, secure, and appropriate financial services can influence household welfare, entrepreneurship, savings, investment, employment, and resilience to economic shocks. The expansion of digital banking and financial technology (FinTech) has transformed the delivery of financial services by reducing transaction costs, overcoming geographical barriers, enabling mobile payments, facilitating digital credit and savings, and connecting previously underserved individuals and small enterprises to formal financial systems. This paper examines the relationship between financial inclusion and economic development, with particular emphasis on the role of digital banking and FinTech in poverty reduction. Using a conceptual and systematic literature-review approach, the study analyzes the mechanisms through which digital financial services can improve economic participation and household welfare. The analysis indicates that digital banking and FinTech can support poverty reduction by expanding payment access, facilitating savings, improving access to productive credit, supporting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), enabling remittances, strengthening social-transfer delivery, and improving households' capacity to manage financial shocks. title: LJWOA: A Lévy-Flight-Enhanced Jaya–Whale Hybrid for Latency- and Power-Aware Microservice Placement in Fog-Cloud Environments
abstract: Placing containerized microservices across a fog-cloud continuum requires jointly optimizing network latency, node power consumption, and load balance. This paper studies LJWOA, a three-stage hybrid metaheuristic that adds a Jayastyle elitist refinement and a Lévy-flight restart of the weakest individuals to the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Evaluation uses six benchmark functions (dimension 30) and synthetic fog-cloud placement instances with 50–300 microservices (CPU workload 200–1500 MI, payload 1–50 MB) on 12–36 heterogeneous fog and cloud nodes, with 15–30 independent runs per setting and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. In the original experiments LJWOA attains a lower weighted objective than Jaya, GWO, and PSO at all five scales and than WOA at 50 and 100 microservices, is statistically indistinguishable from WOA at 150–200, and is significantly worse at 300. Additional experiments requested during review use an equal function-evaluation budget and an independent re-implementation: LJWOA remains ahead of Jaya, GWO, SMA, and NSGA-II at every scale and ties with PSO, but its advantage over WOA is not significant at 50–200 and reverses at 300 (0.612 vs. 0.576), and GA and L-SHADE reach lower objective values at all scales. The Lévy stage improves on the twostage variant on held-out instances (raw p < 0.01 at every scale), whereas the stage order has no consi…

title: Early Detection of Common Infant Illnesses (0–3 Years) Using Explainable Machine Learning: A Symptom-Based Decision Support System for Caregivers
abstract: Background: Early identification of common infant illnesses is essential for reducing diagnostic delays and improving child healthcare outcomes, particularly in resource-limited settings where timely access to pediatric specialists may be challenging. Objective: This study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for the early prediction of common infant illnesses using symptom-based and demographic information collected from Bangladesh. Methods: A clinically validated dataset comprising 2,552 infant health records representing eight disease categories was developed from hospital records and caregiver reports. The dataset was divided using a stratified 80:20 train–test split, while five-fold cross-validation was employed during hyperparameter optimization to prevent overfitting and ensure robust model selection. Four supervised machine learning algorithms, namely Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were trained and evaluated. Randomized Search CV with five-fold cross-validation was employed to optimize the best-performing model. Model robustness was further assessed using bootstrap confidence intervals, calibration analysis, and an ablation study, while explainability was achieved through feature importance analysis and SHAP. Results: Among the evaluated models, the optimized Random Forest classifier achieved the…

title: Estrategias de manejo del estrés en enfermeras de unidades de cuidados intensivos: revisión bibliográfica
abstract: Se identificaron las estrategias de manejo del estrés descritas para enfermeras de unidades de cuidados intensivos. Se realizó una revisión bibliográfica narrativa de nueve estudios publicados entre 2014 y 2021 y localizados en PubMed, SciELO y Dialnet, agrupados en factores de estrés e intervenciones. El agotamiento se asoció con las horas nocturnas, el número de pacientes por turno, la falta de personal y el ruido, y el apoyo social moderó su relación con la ansiedad. El entrenamiento cognitivo-conductual y el mindfulness redujeron el estrés laboral y el cansancio emocional; los programas de mindfulness y resiliencia fueron factibles y el yoga redujo el cansancio emocional. Las recomendaciones de expertos priorizaron cambios en el entorno de trabajo. El manejo del estrés en enfermeras de cuidados intensivos combina intervenciones individuales con medidas institucionales sobre la dotación de personal, los turnos y el apoyo social.

U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions And Their Influence On Canadian Perception, National Sentiment And Consumer Behaviour
abstract: This study investigates how recent U.S. threatened and imposed tariffs under the Trump administration have influenced Canadian public sentiment and consumer behaviour. While traditional economic analysis of tariffs focuses on macro-level indicators such as GDP and trade balances, this research explores the sociopsychological and behavioural impacts of economic protectionism on individuals. Specifically, it examines the extent to which Canadian consumers’ awareness of tariffs correlates with negatives perceptions of Americans, increased nationalism, consumer ethnocentrism and retaliatory purchasing behaviour. Drawing upon theories such as social identity theory, consumer ethnocentrism and reactance theory, the study develops a conceptual framework linking tariff awareness to five key hypotheses. A cross-sectional, quantitative survey was conducted with 123 Canadian residents, collecting data on demographic variables, attitudes toward the U.S., national sentiments and purchasing patterns. The validated instruments consisted of both self-developed scales and pre-established scales including the CETSCALE (Shimp & Sharma, 1987) and Kosterman & Feshbach’s Nationalism scale (1989). Statistical analyses revealed significant relationships across several variables. Greater awareness of U.S. tariffs was associated with more negative perceptions of Americans, heightened national pride, a s…

Reconocimiento y abordaje de falsa vía en pulpectomía de molar temporal: reporte de caso
abstract: Se describe el reconocimiento y el abordaje de una falsa vía generada durante la pulpectomía de un molar temporal, mediante un reporte de caso clínico único, descriptivo, basado en el registro clínico y radiográfico de una paciente de 8 años y 6 meses con caries de la dentina y necrosis pulpar del órgano dental 7.4. La pulpectomía se planificó en tres sesiones. En la segunda, la radiografía de conductometría reveló una perforación del piso pulpar en la furca causada por la lima mesial; el instrumento se reposicionó, la perforación se limpió con clorhexidina y suero fisiológico y se selló con Biodentine e ionómero. El control radiográfico durante la conductometría permitió identificar y sellar oportunamente la falsa vía; se requiere seguimiento para establecer el pronóstico.

title: Biochar in Insect Pest Management: Mechanisms, Effectiveness, and Research Gaps
abstract: Biochar is a carbon-rich material produced through the thermochemical conversion of biomass under oxygen-limited conditions. Its agricultural applications have attracted interest because of potential improvements in soil structure, nutrient availability, water retention, microbial activity, and carbon storage. This review examines the mechanisms through which biochar may influence insect pest populations and interactions between plants and soil arthropods. The mechanisms discussed include changes in soil physicochemical properties, adsorption of volatile compounds, modification of rhizosphere microbial communities, and induction of plant defence responses. Evidence from the studies considered indicates that biochar can affect insect feeding, development, survival, and reproduction, but the direction and magnitude of these responses vary. Outcomes differ according to feedstock, pyrolysis conditions, application rate, soil characteristics, pest species, and insect developmental stage. Studies involving planthoppers, aphids, stored-product beetles, termites, and lepidopteran herbivores illustrate these variable responses. Biochar applications may also alter soil arthropod communities, including springtails and ants, with implications for organisms that contribute to soil functioning. Although biochar has potential as a component of integrated pest management, available evidence do…

title: Analisis Usability Media Pembelajaran Inklusif Berbasis Canva dan Heyzine Flipbook dengan System Usability Scale
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis usability media pembelajaran inklusif berbasis Canva dan Heyzine Flipbook menggunakan System Usability Scale (SUS). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif. Responden berjumlah 67 orang yang berasal dari kalangan pendidik, mahasiswa pendidikan, dan praktisi pendidikan inklusif. Responden diminta mencoba media pembelajaran terlebih dahulu, kemudian mengisi kuesioner SUS yang terdiri atas 10 pernyataan dengan skala respons lima tingkat. Skor SUS dihitung mengikuti prosedur standar, yaitu dengan mengonversi skor item ganjil dan genap, menjumlahkan hasil konversi, kemudian mengalikannya dengan 2,5. Hasil perhitungan menunjukkan skor rata-rata 82,95 (dibulatkan menjadi 83), dengan rentang skor individual 50–100. Berdasarkan interpretasi adjective rating, skor tersebut berada pada kategori excellent. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa responden menilai media relatif mudah digunakan. Namun, skor SUS merupakan ukuran persepsi usability dan belum secara langsung membuktikan aksesibilitas media bagi seluruh peserta didik dengan kebutuhan yang beragam. Evaluasi lanjutan melalui uji aksesibilitas dan pelibatan langsung peserta didik diperlukan untuk memperoleh gambaran yang lebih menyeluruh.

title: Control del dolor y manejo postoperatorio en cirugía oral de pacientes sistémicamente comprometidos
abstract: Esta revisión narrativa analizó la evidencia sobre el control del dolor y el manejo postoperatorio en cirugía oral de pacientes sistémicamente comprometidos. Se buscó en PubMed y SciELO (2013-2025) con descriptores sobre cirugía oral, dolor postoperatorio, analgésicos y enfermedades sistémicas; se seleccionaron 15 documentos, organizados en cuatro categorías temáticas. La combinación de ibuprofeno y paracetamol mostró la mejor relación entre eficacia y seguridad, mientras que los opioides aportaron menos beneficio y más efectos adversos. En la diabetes, la cicatrización alveolar fue más lenta; en la enfermedad renal y la hepatopatía se requiere evitar o ajustar fármacos, y los antifibrinolíticos locales reducen el sangrado en pacientes anticoagulados. La analgesia en estos pacientes debe individualizarse según la comorbilidad, con valoración preoperatoria y seguimiento coordinado.

title: Climate and management associations with Bonsmara steer performance in a tropical semi-intensive beef production system
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the joint influence of climatic variables and herd management practices on the productive performance of Bonsmara steers in Namaacha, Maputo Province, Mozambique. A retrospective cohort design integrated historical production records from the CattleMax system (2021–2023) with field observations and microclimatic monitoring ( n = 30 steers). Climatic parameters (air temperature, relative humidity, precipitation, and Temperature-Humidity Index, THI) were assessed alongside management indicators across pre- and post-weaning phases. Performance metrics included birth weight, weaning weight, final weight, average daily gain (ADG), and phase duration. Seasonal differences were tested with Welch’s t-test (α = 0.05). Multivariate relationships were modelled by Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA), with significance assessed via Wilks’ lambda (Λ). Mean birth weight was 34.60 ± 7.25 kg, weaning weight 200.07 ± 38.35 kg (at 233.87 ± 64.36 days), and final weight 326.27 ± 74.56 kg. Pre-weaning and post-weaning ADG averaged 0.76 ± 0.29 and 0.41 ± 0.16 kg day⁻¹, respectively. No statistically significant differences in productive traits were detected between rainy- and dry-season cohorts ( p > 0.05). After removal of THI due to collinearity with air temperature (VIF > 20,000), CCA identified significant canonical associations between climate and performance in b…

title: Endoscopic diagnosis and treatment of early gastric cardia neoplasms: Efficacy and management of non-curative resection
abstract: BACKGROUND Gastric cardia cancer is a distinct clinicopathological entity with an increasing global incidence. Because of its location at the esophagogastric junction and complex submucosal architecture, early gastric cardia neoplasms pose significant challenges for accurate endoscopic diagnosis and depth assessment. These difficulties may lead to pathological underestimation and high rates of noncurative resection (NCR) after endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). Although additional surgery is generally recommended for NCR, this strategy may lead to overtreatment in selected low-risk patients. Therefore, evaluating the diagnostic performance of endoscopic modalities and exploring individualized management strategies after ESD are important clinically. AIM To evaluate ESD efficacy and safety for early gastric cardia neoplasms and explore individualized management for patients undergoing NCR. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 155 patients with 163 early gastric cardia mucosal lesions treated by ESD between March 2014 and June 2025. Diagnostic accuracy of white-light endoscopy, magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging, and endoscopic ultrasonography was evaluated using postoperative pathology as the reference standard. ESD outcomes, management of NCR, and long-term survival were assessed. Logistic regression identified factors associated with NCR, and survival was analyz…

Smart Liquid-Cooled Geared Motor System with ESP32-Based Automatic Temperature Control for Electric Bicycles
abstract: Electric bicycles (e-bikes) are widely used for commuting, delivery and recreation, but their geared motors can overheat during continuous operation, uphill riding and heavy loading, which lowers efficiency and shortens service life. Natural air cooling, commonly used in e-bike motors, has limited heat-removal capacity and cannot respond to changes in motor temperature. This paper presents the design and prototype implementation of a smart liquid-cooled geared motor system for an e-bicycle. A water-based coolant is circulated by a 24 V DC pump through a cooling jacket around the motor and through a fan-assisted radiator. An ESP32 microcontroller reads a motor-mounted temperature sensor, compares the reading with a predefined limit and switches the pump and fan through a relay, while a display shows motor temperature and cooling status. The system is powered by a 24 V, 30 Ah battery, with a regulated supply for the control electronics. The assembled prototype was subjected to circulation, sensor, controller, electrical and load tests, and it activated cooling automatically when the set temperature limit was reached. The work demonstrates a low-cost, practical approach to temperature-controlled cooling of e-bike motors; quantitative thermal characterisation is identified as future work. Key Words: Electric bicycle, geared motor, liquid cooling, thermal management, ESP32, temperat…

title: The Accounting Discretion Dilemma: A Conceptual Review of Efficient and Opportunistic Earnings Management for Audit Practitioners
abstract: Accounting discretion allows management to exercise professional judgment in preparing financial statements. The same flexibility may be used opportunistically through earnings management, and both uses operate within accounting standards, which makes them difficult for auditors to distinguish. This article examines the conceptual distinction between efficient and opportunistic earnings management, maps the factors that shape the nature of accounting discretion, and discusses the challenges auditors face in evaluating it. A structured conceptual literature review with thematic synthesis of reputable journal publications is used. The review indicates that discretion is shaped by corporate governance, ownership structure, compensation incentives, market pressure, the regulatory environment, and business complexity, while auditors face four obstacles: limited observability of motives, the absence of a universal benchmark, independence pressure, and the complexity of principle-based standards. The article proposes the Accounting Discretion Evaluation Matrix (MEDA), a two-dimensional framework (Informational Content and Agency Incentive Intensity) supplemented with indicators, a preliminary scoring rule, audit responses for each quadrant, and propositions for empirical testing. MEDA is conceptual and has not yet been tested empirically.

title: Reconstructing a Framework for the Analysis of Education Policy Based on Quality, Equity, Effectiveness and Efficiency
abstract: The analysis of education policy requires an integrated approach to quality, equity, effectiveness and efficiency, particularly when considering the relationships and potential tensions between these dimensions. This study aims to reconstruct a framework for the analysis of education policy based on the position, function and interrelationships of these four dimensions. The study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review oriented towards conceptual synthesis. The literature was sourced through searches on Google Scholar, GARUDA, the SINTA portal, and relevant policy documents. These four dimensions have complementary relationships, whilst also harbouring the potential for context-dependent tensions. Based on these findings, this study has produced a reconstructed analytical framework that integrates analytical functions, conceptual indicators, and the mapping of six pairs of inter-dimensional relationships across the formulation, implementation and evaluation stages of education policy. title: Sistema de Inteligencia Artificial como Herramienta de apoyo a la Toma de Decisiones Arbitrales en el Futbol
abstract: El arbitraje en el fútbol profesional exige una precisión extrema bajo condiciones de alta presión psicológica y velocidad de juego. El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar la efectividad de un sistema de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) como herramienta de apoyo pedagógico y tecnológico para optimizar la toma de decisiones arbitrales en situaciones complejas de juego. La investigación adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo, con alcance correlacional-explicativo y diseño pre-experimental de corte transversal, utilizando una muestra no probabilística por conveniencia de 38 árbitros profesionales y semiprofesionales. La metodología se articuló en tres fases: diagnóstica, diseño de una estrategia de capacitación apoyada en IA y evaluación mediante pre-test y post-test, complementada con la validación de contenido por 15 expertos mediante el método Delphi. Los resultados diagnósticos iniciales revelaron marcadas deficiencias en el manejo analítico de herramientas tecnológicas y desorden en los criterios de juzgamiento ante acciones ofensivas y defensivas dinámicas. La prueba de Shapiro-Wilk evidenció la no normalidad de las distribuciones (p < 0.05). Tras la implementación de la propuesta, la prueba de Rangos con Signo de Wilcoxon demostró una mejora estadísticamente significativa en la precisión arbitral (Z = -5.382, p < 0.001), incrementando la media de aciertos de 11.26 a 17.18 sobre 20 esc…

title: Growth parameters and leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris L. at the juvenile stage of regenerating at the ash dump of the Reftinskaya power station
abstract: Plant growth parameters, biomass allocation, and leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris L. juveniles were studied during natural regeneration on the reclaimed (ash + soil) and non-reclaimed (ash) areas of the ash dump of the Reftinskaya state district power plant (Sverdlovsk Region). It was shown that at this stage of ontogenesis, the seedlings had significant differences in biomass allocation and root system morphology. On the ash substrate poor in nitrogen and phosphorus juvenile plants allocated significantly more biomass to the root system, which was accompanied by an increase in the length and branching of horizontal roots. Changes in the parameters of photosynthetic apparatus were also observed in juvenile plants on the plot with pure ash, which manifested themselves in a significant increase in the leaf thickness and leaf surface area, at lower values of the leaf mass ratio (LMR) and leaf area ratio(LAR), compared to seedlings on the plot soil+ash. Plant growth parameters (plant height and trunk diameter), as well as the mass of the trunk, needles, and the total mass of the plant, did not depend on the edaphic conditions and had similar values for seedlings from different ecotopes. Work Motivation, Service Innovation, and Public Service Performance: Evidence from Ambon City’s Civil Registration Office
abstract: Civil registration services shape residents’ access to education, health care, and social protection, yet evidence linking staff motivation and service innovation to citizen-rated performance remains limited. This article critically reappraises questionnaire summaries from the Population and Civil Registration Office of Ambon City, comprising 40 employees and 40 service users who responded to a shared 36-item, five-point Likert instrument. Descriptive indices were reported at 79.98% for work motivation, 82.56% for service innovation, and 77.48% for service performance, with service speed the lowest-scoring performance indicator (76.25%). The source also reports positive regression coefficients for motivation (0.428) and innovation (0.367), with R² = 0.666. However, no participant-linked data were available, the two groups were sampled differently, and one diagnostic table was labelled as simulated data. The regression estimates therefore cannot be independently validated, and hypotheses H1–H3 remain untested. The article contributes a transparent assessment of measurement and descriptive patterns, and specifies the conditions for a defensible analysis: employee-only motivation measures, independent user surveys, and units linked across time and service.

title: The Effects of AI Readiness, HRM Practices, and Continuous Learning Culture on HR Analytics Capability in Public Service Organizations
abstract: The study aims to investigate the effect of AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture to HR Analytics Capability in public sector enterprises in Indonesia. The research was conducted based on a quantitative approach and the survey technique. The research participants consisted of the workers of public sector organizations who have expertise in the use of digital information systems and management of personnel data. The data were collected using an online questionnaire through Google Forms. The questions used a five-point Likert scale. The sampling technique used purposive sampling. Multiple linear regression was used to explore HR Analytics Capability in relation to the three independent variables. The proposed study model indicates that AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture are positively related to HR Analytics Capability. AI Readiness is expected to have the highest relative impact. Artificial intelligence preparation may enhance the organizational capacity to integrate, analyze and use personnel data. Quality information is available with good human resource management practices. Moreover, a culture of continuous learning promotes the enhancement of employees’ analytical skills, teamwork and flexibility. The report provides practical implications for public service companies in terms of the value of strengthening AI infrastructure, da…

title: Multi-Echelon Network Optimization for Supply Chain Efficiency: Balancing Service Levels with Cost Performance
abstract: Abstract Supply chain network design decisions determine up to 80% of total logistics costs, yet the majority of enterprises continue to optimize individual echelons in isolation, generating systemic inefficiencies across the end-to-end value chain. This paper examines the theoretical underpinnings and practical implementation of multi-echelon network optimization (MENO), a holistic approach that simultaneously determines facility locations, inventory positioning, and product flow across all tiers of the supply chain. Drawing on published case study evidence from leading fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and manufacturing enterprises, secondary data from Gartner, EY, and McKinsey surveys conducted through 2024, and a review of 27 academic and practitioner sources, the study synthesizes a four-phase transformation framework for MENO adoption. Documented outcomes include facility footprint reductions of 18–22%, order-fill-rate improvements exceeding 8 percentage points, and aggregate logistics cost reductions in the range of 10–15%. Results further indicate that organizations sustaining multi-echelon optimization as a continuous capability, rather than a one-time project, achieve productivity gains of 5% or more year-over-year over a ten-year horizon. The paper concludes with prescriptive recommendations for supply chain leaders, network planners, and technology providers seeking…

title: Melt Strength Regulation of Cellular Structure and Thermal–Acoustic–Mechanical Synergy in ZnO/Polyethylene Composite Foams
abstract: Abstract Combining thermal insulation, sound insulation, and load-bearing capacity in lightweight polymer foams remains challenging. Here, melt-strength regulation and microchannel-assisted gas transport were combined to prepare multifunctional ZnO/polyethylene foams. Low-melt-strength polyethylene (2426H) was blended with high-melt-strength polyethylene (LD605), and porous sheets were produced by grinding and cold pressing before physically confined supercritical CO2 foaming. Preconstructed microchannels shortened gas diffusion paths, enabling a saturation time of 30 min. Varying the LD605 content from 0 to 80 wt % regulated cellular morphology and cell-wall crystallization. At 40 wt % LD605, long-chain-branch entanglement and strain hardening promoted stress-induced crystallization. The replacement of a cold-crystallization peak by a melting peak in differential scanning calorimetry, together with an increase in storage modulus from approximately 5 to 55 MPa, supported a transition from growth-dominated to nucleation-dominated foaming. The foam containing 80 wt % LD605 exhibited a thermal conductivity of 0.085 W/(m·K), a temperature difference of 61.7 °C across a thickness of 10 mm, an average broadband sound transmission loss of 37.6 dB, and a dielectric loss tangent of 0.003. Field Aging of Biochar Drives SOC Accumulation by Promoting Photosynthetic Carbon Input and Shifting Soil Microbial Communities
abstract: Abstract Biochar application is an effective strategy for enhancing the soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. However, the extent to which biochar aging affects the SOC sequestration remains unclear. In this study, we investigated SOC dynamics, photosynthetic carbon allocation patterns, and soil microbial characteristics across a 1- to 5-year biochar aging gradient in a wheat farmland. The results revealed that the SOC content increased by 20.7% after 1 year of biochar application, primarily because of an increase in particulate organic carbon (POC), and increased by an additional 14.8% over the next 4 years, which resulted from additional increases in both POC and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC). The total 13C assimilation increased by 19.9% and 33.0% after 1 and 5 years of biochar application, respectively. Moreover, biochar application promoted the accumulation of 13C in POC, while 5 years of biochar application also increased the assimilated 13C in MAOC. Furthermore, biochar aging altered the soil bacterial community and increased the abundance of saprotrophic fungi, which were strongly related to SOC dynamics. In summary, our results indicate that biochar aging promotes SOC sequestration by promoting photosynthetic carbon assimilation and facilitating the transformation of plant-derived carbon into SOC related to shifts in the soil microbial community.

abstract: Abstract Natural science has been integrated into early childhood education (ECE) for many years. With the growing digitalization of society many experts call for the integration of technology and computer science (CS) into ECE with the goal of fostering students’ problem-solving skills. While many research projects integrate technology and CS into ECE, curricula, e.g. in Germany, stay the same and so does the current practice. Given this starting point, this study aimed to explore the reasons behind the lack of technology and CS in ECE from the perspectives of the teachers. As recent research highlights the lack of this perspective. A multiple case study consisting of N = 11 kindergarten teachers (between 25 and 64 years old) was conducted using problem-centred interviews and applying qualitative content analysis. The results indicate that most of the teachers have a low interest and self-concept in both fields. Most of the teachers think that technology and CS education at the preschool level (age 4 to 6) is important. However, several reasons in conformance with prior research are stated why they do not integrate it. The findings from this case study indicate that only through systematic changes made in curricula and pre-service teacher training can a sustainable change reaching all kindergarten students occur. abstract: Abstract Low energy availability (LEA) is a concern among athletes, particularly in weight-dependent sports, where high training demands and weight-management practices are associated with LEA risk. This multicentre cross-sectional study estimated LEA risk and examined its associations with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour among Indian athletes. A total of 271 athletes in five weight-dependent sports (174 males and 97 females; aged 15–23 years) completed the Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire (LEAF-Q), Low Energy Availability in Males Questionnaire (LEAM-Q), and validated questionnaires. Overall, 38.7% of athletes were classified as being at risk of LEA, including 51.1% of males classified using the LEAM-Q and 16.5% of females classified using the LEAF-Q ( P < 0.001). LEA risk exceeded 40% among athletes from Delhi andHaryana, junior athletes, those participating in grappling sports, and the middle-weight category. Among female athletes, LEA risk was associated with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour. Female athletes with disordered eating had 4.4-fold higher odds of LEA risk (OR = 4.42, ​95% CI: 1.08–18.21; P = 0.039), whereas no significant associations were observed among male athletes. abstract: Electricity distribution utilities must examine large volumes of smart-meter readings to find consumption patterns that may indicate non-technical losses, yet unusual readings can equally arise from changes in occupancy, seasonality, solar generation, meter faults or data errors. Published work concentrates mainly on detection models, whereas the workflow around data quality, explanation and human review is less often documented as one reproducible system. This paper presents GridIntel, a web-based platform that integrates comma-separated-value (CSV) data ingestion, data-quality auditing, sixteen customer-level statistical features, feeder-month energy-balance analysis, Isolation Forest anomaly scoring and, when sufficient labels exist, Random Forest, XGBoost and ensemble scoring. Scores are expressed as cohort-relative percentile rankings with feature-based explanations and feed an investigation workflow with case snapshots, an append-only audit trail and CSV and portable-document-format (PDF) reports. The platform also provides a separate past-bill analysis using browser-side optical character recognition (OCR) and a dataset-grounded assistant. It is implemented with React, TypeScript, FastAPI and Python analytics libraries. From Digital Submission to Data Integration: SIASN Pension Services in Maluku
abstract: This study examines why digital pension submissions through Indonesia's Civil Servant Information System (SIASN) still rely on manual verification at the Maluku Provincial Civil Service Agency. The paper reports the author's qualitative master's research, drawing on five purposively selected institutional informants, observation descriptions, and procedural documents from September 2026. Interviews and source accounts were re-examined using an interactive data-analysis approach and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework. Results distinguish three connected constraints: inconsistent and outdated source records, dependence on one pension-service operator and central system access, and interagency document clarification involving OPDs, the provincial agency, and BKN. The national platform enables electronic forwarding and tracking, but these functions should not be equated with complete data interoperability or verified time savings. The article contributes a distinction between digital transmission, record readiness, and cross-agency workflow integration, with proposed actions for earlier validation, staffing continuity, incident monitoring, and coordinated follow-up. The evidence is a single-agency qualitative case; the proposed improvements have not been outcome-tested.

abstract: Este artigo apresenta o desenho e a avaliação técnica de um portal de telemedicina orientado à privacidade para os cuidados de HIV na Província de Benguela, Angola. O abandono da terapia antirretroviral continua expressivo na Província, com 1.231 casos em adultos em 2025, e o estigma e o receio de divulgação do estado serológico figuram entre as barreiras reconhecidas ao cuidado. O estudo adota a design science research e deriva os requisitos do artefacto a partir das dimensões do estigma, com base em relatórios do Gabinete Provincial da Saúde de Benguela e em entrevistas com profissionais. O portal utiliza Blazor WebAssembly, ASP.NET Core 9, SignalR e videoconsulta via Twilio. A avaliação técnica combina testes unitários e de integração, um teste de carga com 50 utilizadores simulados e 62.697 pedidos, e uma análise de segurança com OWASP ZAP. O teste de carga regista tempo médio de resposta de 266 ms (percentil 95 de 533 ms) sem erros HTTP, e a análise de segurança não identifica alertas de gravidade crítica ou alta e regista quatro alertas de gravidade baixa ou informativa, relacionados com a configuração do servidor e do frontend. Os resultados demonstram a viabilidade técnica em ambiente controlado e propõem uma matriz de rastreabilidade entre estigma, requisitos, desenho e evidência. abstract: The article analyzes the dynamics of plant species constancy in three groups of relevés of virgin grass phytocenoses on the flat interfluves of the Streletsky site of the Central Chernozem Nature Reserve (Kursk Region). The first group includes relevés of «original» virgin steppes with regular hay-mowing and pasture use, made in 1928–1934, before the foundation of the Nature Reserve. The second group consists of steppe communities with an absolutely protected regime, described in 1962–1964 and already exhibiting significant signs of transformation characteristic of reserve succession. They are included in the analysis for the first time and are of great interest as an intermediate link of the succession series. The third group comprises phytocenoses described in 2005–2014 in absolutely protected areas. They have lost the signs of steppes and represent fringe vegetation. According to the specifics of the change in constancy over 86 years, plant species are divided into 10 groups (Table 1), for each of which a detailed description is given in the article. To confirm the direction of succession, special attention is paid to the species of three classes: Festuco–Brometea Br.-Bl. et Tx. ex Soó 1947 (steppes), Trifolio–Geranietea sanguinei T. Müller 1962 (fringe vegetation), and Molinio–Arrhenatheretea Tx. 1937 (glycophytic meadows).
