title: Comprehensive Plant Biomarker Profile for Tracing Detection of Sulfur Mustard and Lewisite Exposure and Its Application to Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapon Samples
abstract: Abstract Sulfur mustard (HD) and lewisite (L, mainly containing L1 and L2) from Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapons (JACWs) in China have persisted for nearly a century, posing ongoing risks to ecological environments and public health. Plants can serve as monitoring sentinels for tracing detection of chemical exposure. However, specific plant biomarkers for HD/L remain unidentified, and their transformation in plants remains unveiled. By nontargeted metabolomics and high-resolution mass spectrometry, 30 novel plant adducts of HD/L were identified. Twelve of these adducts, along with 5 degradation products, were evaluated and assembled into a plant biomarker profile for retrospective detection of HD/L exposure. A sensitive UHPLC–TQ MS method was developed with LODs as low as 0.0200 ng/mL. The profile was detectable in 12 plant species for at least 90 days after exposure. Adduction, hydrolysis, oxidation, and trimerization of HD/L agents have been detected in plants, and transformation diagrams were portrayed. Real samples from JACW remediation sites in northeastern China were analyzed, and free biomarkers were detected at obviously higher levels in plants than in soil. Analytical results indicate that plant leaves may serve as sensitive monitoring media for the exposed agents. This work provides a reliable approach for long-term monitoring of JACW exposure and shows that possib…

abstract: In the context of global climate change and increasing human impact on natural resources, assessing the raw material resources of economically valuable plant species in key regions is essential for the sustainable use and conservation of Kazakhstan's botanical diversity. The cadastral assessment of botanical resources in the Ulytau Region, covering steppe, semi-desert, and desert landscapes and conducted during 2024–2026, continues Kazakhstan's comprehensive botanical investigations. Literature and archival analysis indicate that previous studies in the region have focused mainly on floristics, whereas data on the raw material resources of certain medicinal plant species from the Ulytau Mountains remain limited, localised, and outdated. An updated assessment of these resources is therefore both timely and necessary. This study was conducted in the Ulytau Region, established on 8 June 2022 in central Kazakhstan. The area features hilly uplands, low-mountain terrain, and plains, with a sharply continental and extremely arid climate. Resource assessment surveys identified and quantified the air-dry biomass of 16 economically valuable plant species belonging to nine families. Effect of actinomycete Streptomyces griseoviridis on plant drought tolerance: an experimental study
abstract: The relevance of this study stems from the need to find environmentally friendly approaches to increasing the stress tolerance of agricultural crops. The actinomycete Streptomyces griseoviridis is considered as a promising agent. The study yielded a mutant clone resistant to drought conditions in vitro, and its effect on wheat plant (Triticum aestivum) growth in a climate chamber was assessed. The CarD gene, which is involved in the regulation of ribosomal gene transcription and links metabolic processes with stress adaptation, was sequenced. It was shown that the mutation alters the nucleotide composition and structure of the gene and increases the strain's biostimulating activity under high temperatures and moisture deficits.

abstract: The paper presents the results of an inventory of plant species listed in the Red Data Book of the Kirov Region and cultivated on the territory of the botanical garden of Vyatka State University. Based on the results of three-year research (2022–2024), the state of 26 species of rare plants from the main list and 17 species that require constant monitoring and observation in the region is described. It was revealed that 18 species (41.9 % of the total number of protected plants) are cultivated in the steppe plant exposition; 16 species (37.2 %) are grown in the medicinal and aromatic plant exposition; 12 species (27.9 %) are found in several sections, including steppe and medicinal plants. It is shown that the composition of the collection and the number of individuals of protected plants on the territory of the botanical garden periodically change. title: Structure and dynamics of populations of rare plant species in the Mount Kopeyka Protected Area (Samara Region)
abstract: The structure and population dynamics of 34 rare plant species growing within the Mount Kopeyka (Gora Kopeyka) natural monument of regional significance in the Samara Region were studied. Data from the authors' studies for the 1999–2000 and 2024–2025 periods were compared. Changes in the number of individuals and the spatial and ontogenetic structure of populations were identified for most of the growing species. A decrease in both the number of individuals and their density was noted for 19 rare plant species. For 12 species, population indicators remained approximately the same, indicating adequate self-sustainment. Only three species (Astragalus macropus, Globularia punctata, and Oxytropis floribunda) showed an increase in the number of individuals and an increase in the density of individuals within cenopopulations, indicating effective self-regeneration. However, the most critical changes in the ontogenetic structure occurred in the populations of four rare steppe plant species: Astragalus helmii, Atraphaxis frutescens, Ferula caspica, and Polygala sibirica. The population status of two species, Astragalus helmii and Polygala sibirica, was considered unsatisfactory. Factors influencing changes in the population structure of rare plant species in the Mount Kopeyka (Gora Kopeyka) Protected Area and their status include livestock grazing, fires, and soil pollution.

title: Adaptation features and development dynamics of a number of useful plant species from different geographical zones in the collection of the SEC – Botanical Garden of Moscow State University
abstract: The article discusses the results of introducing a number of medicinal and economically valuable plant species from different climatic zones, with the aim of growing them in a moderately continental climate as a sustainable source of valuable raw materials (medicinal and fodder resources). The paper examines their potential for adaptation to the natural and climatic conditions of the SEC – Botanical Garden of MSU, including consideration of the seasonal development of the introduced species and the identification of periods of greatest vulnerability within their annual vegetation cycle. The study notes that plant species originating from Northeastern and Central Asia, the Mediterranean, and North America proved to be fairly resilient under the conditions of the “Useful Plants” plot located within the territory of the SEC – Botanical Garden of MSU. Long‑term trials made it possible to assess and rank the studied plant species according to their suitability for the moderately continental climate of central European Russia: Glaucium flavum, Macleaya cordata, and Sida hermaphrodita were classified as promising, while Salvia officinalis was deemed poorly suited. In addition, several valuable medicinal plants disappeared from the collection within a relatively short period: Ziziphora pamiroalaica, Hedysarum neglectum, Rhodiola integrifolia and Rhodiola quadrifida.

title: Value Chain Analysis of Hybrid Corn in Labuan District
abstract: This study compares the observed marketing pathways, price spreads, farmers’ price shares, and marketing cost ratios for hybrid corn in Labuan Toposo and Labuan Panimba, Donggala Regency, Indonesia. Data were obtained from 82 farmer interviews and linked marketing-actor observations in 2025. Transaction-level prices and costs were aggregated using quantity weights. Four channels were identified: local processors (6.10% of farmers), Gudang Talise (1.22%), PT Loan (6.10%), and middlemen supplying PT Japfa (86.59%). The first three direct channels showed a 100% farmers’ price share at the observed buyer boundary. In the middleman channel, the volume-weighted farmer price was Rp4,553.79/kg versus Rp5,100/kg at PT Japfa, resulting in a gross spread of Rp546.21/kg and a farmers’ share of 89.29%. After recorded marketing costs of Rp329.13/kg, the residual spread was Rp217.08/kg before other costs. Marketing cost ratios across channels 1–4 were 2.61%, 4.80%, 2.87%, and 6.45%, respectively. The results highlight the importance of both price distribution and who pays for logistics. Collective marketing, transparent grading, and alternative financing may improve market access, although downstream value added and welfare effects were not directly measured.

Home storage of medicines and associated factors among household heads in Jigjiga Town, Eastern Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background Household medication storage can be associated with adverse drug reactions, accidental poisoning, and antimicrobial resistance. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the prevalence of household medication storage and its associated factors among residents of Jigjiga Town, Somali Regional State, Ethiopia. Methods A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 348 households in Jigjiga Town, Eastern Ethiopia, from June 10 to 30, 2026. A multistage sampling technique was employed to select the study participants. Data were collected from household heads or their representatives using a structured questionnaire. title: Equalising in Level, Uniform in Share: What Transfers Do to District Revenue Distribution
abstract: Whether an intergovernmental transfer system equalises depends on what is measured, and two standard measures give opposite impressions of the same system. Using realised revenue returns for all 508 Indonesian district-level governments in the fiscal year 2024, this article shows that transfers reduce the Gini coefficient of district revenue from 0.633, the figure for own-source revenue alone, to 0.342 once transfers are included. The top tenth of jurisdictions holds 50.8 per cent of all own-source revenue but receives only 23.6 per cent of transfers, while the bottom tenth holds 0.5 per cent of own revenue against 4.1 per cent of transfers. On this evidence the system equalises substantially. Measured instead as a share of each jurisdiction's own total revenue the picture inverts: the transfer share has a coefficient of variation of 0.163 against 0.832 for the own-revenue share, and the two correlate at minus 0.954, so that the transfer share is very nearly one minus the own-revenue share and carries almost no information of its own. The article argues that the share measure describes an accounting identity rather than a policy outcome, that the level measure is the one that answers the equalisation question as it is normally posed, and that on that measure transfers close roughly half the gap they inherit.

abstract: ABSTRACT The disconnect in children's reading habits between classrooms and home environments poses a critical challenge to strengthening primary school literacy, particularly within farming communities facing limited reading materials and parental time constraints. This qualitative case study at Detukou Catholic Private Elementary School analyzes school and family involvement, maps supporting and inhibiting factors of reading activities, and formulates opportunities to strengthen literacy networks between home and school. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, participatory observations, and documentation involving twenty-one informants selected via purposive sampling, comprising one principal, nine teachers, and eleven parents, and analyzed manually through data condensation, thematic coding, matrix presentation, and triangulation. Field findings reveal that a fifteen-minute morning reading routine and tiered teacher guidance foster initial literacy engagement, whereas afternoon accompaniment by farming parents occurs informally amid work schedules alongside a need for practical guidance and two-way teacher communication. These findings confirm that a reading culture ecosystem in agrarian communities relies on aligning school routines with family time capacities, implying the need for concise home literacy guides and book-lending circulation. title: Strategy for adaptation of tussock to existence in the semi-arid highlands of the Altai Republic
abstract: This paper analyzes the correlation between the structure of herbaceous shoots and fibrous root systems of the large-bunchgrass graminoids (tussock) life form and the developmental rhythms that determine the adaptation of these plants to the specific habitats of the semiarid highlands of the Altai Republic. With a good water supply, tussocks quickly create a relatively large assimilation surface, ensuring high productivity (pulsed development). This is facilitated by more stable temperatures within the tussock turf than in the surrounding environment, and their relatively weak tolerance to high temperatures is offset by transpiration. When the soil water supply is depleted, tussocks quickly dry out and enter a state of summer dormancy. The ecological characteristics of the tussock life form limit their distribution in the semiarid mountains, where they are typical of the upper vegetation zones with cooler and more humid summers, while in the mountain steppe zone they occupy the most humid habitats.

The Markov chain modelling in the Terrset software was used to assess the spatiotemporal dynamics of LULC in Pakse City over the same period. The results include classified LULC maps for the years 2004, 2014, and 2024. LULC was categorized into five types: water bodies, built-up areas, forest areas, agricultural areas, and miscellaneous areas. The findings also demonstrated a significant change in LULC during the study period, with built-up area increasing significantly from 4.19 km² (2004) to 32.73 km² (2024), or 681.64%, while forest and agricultural areas decreased by 9.46% and 12.75%, respectively. abstract: Elementary mathematics instruction requires innovative approaches that integrate concrete learning experiences, multisensory activities, and active student engagement. Integrating music into mathematics instruction represents an alternative that requires empirical investigation to determine its contribution to learning outcomes. This study aimed to analyze changes in students' mathematics learning outcomes following the implementation of Musical GASING, compare learning gains between experimental and control groups while accounting for prior ability, and identify variations in achievement across classes. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group pretest–posttest design was employed. The participants were 131 elementary school students in Bangka Tengah Regency, Indonesia, comprising 65 students in the experimental group and 66 in the control group. Data were collected through pretest and posttest achievement assessments and analyzed using descriptive statistics, gain-score comparisons, and exploratory analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). The results indicated improvements in both groups, with mean gains of 20.54 points in the experimental group and 18.71 points in the control group. title: The Flipped Classroom Model for Enhancing Self-Directed Learning, Technological Skills, and Collaborative Learning
abstract: The flipped classroom instructional model is an approach to organizing teaching and learning activities that emphasizes learner-centered learning. Previous studies have demonstrated that this model has positive effects on academic achievement and effectively enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of the teaching and learning process. Consequently, this study focused on promoting the flipped classroom model in relation to the development of self-directed learning skills, technological skills, and learning participation among first-year students in the Finance and Banking program, Faculty of Business Administration, Savannakhet University. The participants consisted of 62 first-year students enrolled in the course Statistics for Economics. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis. The research findings revealed positive developments in students’ self-directed learning abilities and their level of engagement in learning activities. Furthermore, this study contributes empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of the flipped classroom model in enhancing self-directed learning skills, promoting the use of technology to support effective and efficient teaching and learning processes, and fostering collaborative learning among students in the Finance and Banking program.

This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The research was conducted in three cycles involving 25 fourth-grade students of Class IV C at SDS Islam Al-Falah 2 Jambi, Indonesia. Data were collected through collaboration and communication observation sheets, teacher activity observations, interviews, and documentation. The data were analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative analysis. The success criterion was set at a minimum average achievement of 76% for both collaboration and communication skills. The results showed a consistent improvement in students’ collaboration and communication skills following the implementation of PjBL integrated with TPACK. Collaboration increased from 42.8% in the pre-cycle, categorized as very poor, to 62.8% in Cycle I, 76.6% in Cycle II, and 90.0% in Cycle III, categorized as very good. Privacidad y seguridad en sistemas de aprendizaje federado: revisión de métodos y desafíos computacionales
abstract: Federated learning enables model training on distributed information without necessarily centralizing raw records. Nevertheless, parameter exchanges, participant coordination, and malicious behavior create threats that do not disappear when data remain at their source. This paper examines privacy and security safeguards in federated learning systems and their computational trade-offs. A structured narrative literature review was conducted through a targeted search of verifiable academic sources and thematic analysis of foundational studies, methodological contributions, and surveys. Findings distinguish inference and reconstruction attacks, model poisoning, backdoors, and server-related threats, and compare differential privacy, secure aggregation, robust optimization, and verification mechanisms. The reviewed literature suggests that no single method simultaneously guarantees confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Appropriate protection depends on the threat model, architecture, accuracy requirements, communication overhead, and computational constraints. Trustworthy deployment, therefore, requires complementary safeguards, explicit evaluation metrics, and reproducible tests tailored to each use case.

The sample group for this study consisted of 25 Grade 5 students from the Primary Demonstration School of Savannakhet Teacher Training College, selected through purposive sampling. The research instruments included: lesson plans, 12 sets of skill practice exercises, and a 30-item multiple-choice academic achievement test. Data analysis was conducted using statistical measures, including Mean (𝑋̅), Standard Deviation (S.D.), and hypothesis testing (t-test). The research results revealed that: 1) The efficiency of the developed skill practice sets reached 82.53/84.4, demonstrating that the tools meet the established standards and can be effectively implemented in teaching and learning management. 2) The academic achievement of Grade 5 students after learning through the skill practice sets was significantly higher than before learning at the .05 level of statistical significance. Uncertainty and Real Estate Return Predictability: Evidence from U.S. REITs
abstract: Abstract We show that fluctuations in financial uncertainty generate substantial and predictable variation in U.S. real estate returns. Using six real estate return series and a comprehensive set of predictors, we document strong forecasting performance both in-sample and out-of-sample, with out-of-sample $$R^2$$ exceeding 8%. A one standard deviation increase in financial uncertainty is associated with an approximately 1.5% decline in next-month REIT returns. To uncover the mechanisms behind this predictability, we apply the Campbell–Shiller present-value decomposition, which separates unexpected returns into cash-flow news, capturing revisions to expected future earnings, and discount-rate news, capturing revisions to expected returns. These components are derived from a parsimonious VAR that includes asset-specific dividend–price ratios, allowing us to trace the information content of financial uncertainty. The evidence reveals that financial uncertainty is associated primarily with negative cash-flow news, rather than innovations in expected returns. Relative to the aggregate stock market, real estate assets respond more strongly and persistently to uncertainty shocks, potentially reflecting both information frictions and delayed changes in underlying real estate fundamentals. In line with these findings, simple forecast-based strategies deliver economically meaningful gain…

abstract: Abstract We develop a method for the transfer of an uncertainty principle for the short-time Fourier transform or a Fourier pair to an uncertainty principle for time–frequency representations that are parametrized by a symplectic matrix, known as metaplectic Wigner distributions. In particular, we derive Beurling-type and Hardy-type uncertainty principles for these time–frequency representations.

We integrated maternal host genomics and vaginal microbiome profiling to identify subtype-specific risk for PTB. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of PTB and vaginal bacterial traits (VBTs) were further conducted. Evolution of Election in Ancient India: A Historical and Legal Analysis of Representative Institutions, Voting Practices and Local Self-Government
abstract: The evolution of electoral practices in India is often read through the development of modern parliamentary democracy. However, historical sources indicate that ancient India had several institutional practices involving collective deliberation, leadership selection and local administration. This article traces the development of these practices from the Vedic assemblies of Sabha and Samiti to the republican institutions of the Mahajanapada period, the decision-making procedures of the Buddhist Sangha and the village administration of the Chola dynasty. Particular attention is given to the Kudavolai system described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions, which prescribed eligibility conditions, selection procedures and accountability mechanisms for village committee membership. The article uses a historical and doctrinal approach, relying on ancient literary texts, epigraphic evidence and constitutional provisions. It argues that although these institutions cannot be equated with modern universal electoral democracy, they demonstrate the historical presence of organised collective governance and provide an important perspective on the evolution of representative and local self-government institutions in India.

title: Who Owns the Improvement? Employee-Created Improvements and Patents of Addition under Indian Patent Law
abstract: A patented invention may occasionally be improved upon or modified by staff members working on it. When both the employer and the employee assert rights to the improvement, particularly after the employee leaves the company, this can become problematic. A patent of addition may be used to protect improvements in or modifications of an existing invention under Section 54 of the Patents Act, 1970. However, it is not clear how ownership of such an improvement should be determined when it is created by an employee and the original patent belongs to the employer. This study explores the question in Indian patent law, focusing on the relevant provisions of the Patents Act, 1970 and the significance of employment and assignment agreements. It also examines the Indian cases and compares the position with that in the United Kingdom, Germany and Japan. It asks whether the current Indian legal framework is sufficient to determine who should own an employee-created improvement and whether clearer guidelines are required to protect the interests of both employers and employees.

title: ChatGPT for Ideation, QuillBot for Revision? Exploring Tool Complementarity in AI-Assisted Scientific Writing among Maritime Cadets
abstract: Artificial-intelligence writing tools are increasingly embedded in university writing practices, yet evidence remains limited on whether students differentiate tools according to stages of the scientific-writing process. This study investigated whether maritime cadets perceived ChatGPT primarily as an ideation and structuring tool and QuillBot primarily as a revision tool, and whether competence with both tools was associated with scientific-writing readiness. A cross-sectional post-training survey was completed by 107 Diploma-IV Nautika cadets at an Indonesian maritime higher education institution on 28 August 2026. The instrument measured ChatGPT competence and use, QuillBot revision competence, scientific-writing readiness, submission progress, and open-ended perceptions. Descriptive statistics, multi-response frequencies, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson and Spearman correlations, multiple regression, and thematic coding were applied. ChatGPT was most frequently used for topic development (83.2%) and outlining (67.3%). Composite scores were high for ChatGPT ideation competence (M = 4.07), QuillBot revision competence (M = 4.03), and scientific-writing readiness (M = 4.10). QuillBot competence showed the strongest association with readiness (r = .863), and remained a significant predictor when ChatGPT competence was controlled (β = .697, p < .001). title: The Influence of Debt and Liquidity Policies on Financial Distress at PT Sepatu Bata Tbk 2013-2025
abstract: This research is motivated by the deteriorating financial condition of PT Sepatu Bata Tbk, which is characterized by an increase in the debt ratio, decreased liquidity, and a negative Altman Z-Score value at the end of the observation period. This study aims to analyze the effect of debt and liquidity policies on financial distress, both partially and simultaneously. The study uses a quantitative approach with a descriptive method. The population and sample of the study are the financial statements of PT Sepatu Bata Tbk for the period 2013–2025, with 13 years of observation. Secondary data were collected through financial statement documentation. Debt policy is measured using the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), liquidity using the Current Ratio (CR), and financial distress using the Altman Z-Score. Data analysis includes descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, and coefficients of determination. The results show that DER has no significant effect on financial distress (p = 0.207), while CR has a positive and significant effect (p < 0.001). Simultaneously, DER and CR have a significant effect on financial distress (F = 23.597; p < 0.001), with an Adjusted R Square of 0.790. title: Decentralizing betting: leveraging blockchain technology for a transparent and inclusive future
abstract: Abstract Traditional centralised online betting platforms can be opaque, raising concerns about transparency, fairness, and access. This paper presents a proof-of-concept peer-to-peer betting platform implemented with Ethereum smart contracts and evaluates three prototypes with increasing realism: (SC1) an on-chain lottery/random game, (SC2) a sports bet settled via administrator-reported results, and (SC3) a VM/Python pipeline that emulates oracle-driven settlement using a historical match dataset. We assess functional correctness, gas cost, settlement latency, scalability with users/markets, and user experience. Results highlight a core trade-off: fully on-chain settlement maximises transparency and automation but increases cost and interaction friction, while manager/oracle-based designs reduce on-chain complexity but introduce trust, governance, and security dependencies. We conclude with a security-focused roadmap toward production deployment, including verifiable randomness, decentralised oracle integration with dispute and timeouts, L2 deployment, and a compliance layer for KYC/AML and responsible gambling.

title: Green intellectual capital disclosure, board independence, and financial performance: Evidence from Indonesian consumer cyclical firms, 2021–2025
abstract: Consumer cyclical firms depend on household demand and stakeholder trust, yet evidence on how green and governance resources relate to their profitability remains limited and inconsistent. This study examines whether Green Intellectual Capital (GIC) disclosure, the proportion of independent commissioners, and audit committee size are associated with the financial performance of consumer cyclical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in 2021–2025. GIC disclosure is measured by an index of green human, structural, and relational capital, and financial performance by Return on Assets (ROA). Multiple linear regression is applied to 150 firm-year observations from 30 companies that were profitable in at least four of the five years. GIC disclosure and the proportion of independent commissioners are positively and significantly associated with ROA, whereas audit committee size is not; the model explains a large share of the variation in ROA. Because loss-making firms are excluded and the pooled model has no control variables, the findings are associations rather than causal effects. The study adds evidence from an emerging-market, consumer-facing sector and suggests that oversight quality and credible green integration, rather than minimum compliance, are linked to profitability.

title: Brain-derived exosomes mediate antibody-resistant PRV transmission and blood–brain barrier disruption
abstract: Abstract Exosomes are critical mediators of virus–host interactions and can transfer viral and host components that influence viral replication and tissue injury. Pseudorabies virus (PRV), a neurotropic alphaherpesvirus, has been reported to disrupt the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and cause severe neurological disease. However, the role of exosomes in PRV-induced neuropathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we systematically investigated the functional role of brain-derived exosomes generated during PRV infection. Exosomes were isolated from PRV-challenged and mock-treated mouse brains using differential ultracentrifugation coupled with cluster of differentiation (CD)9-/CD63-/CD81-based immunomagnetic enrichment. Purity was confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and western blotting, which excluded intact virion contamination. Notably, multimarker enrichment yielded higher recovery than CD63 alone. PRV-associated exosomes contained viral genomic DNA and glycoproteins and mediated efficient viral transmission in porcine kidney (PK)-15 cells. In a Transwell-based BBB model composed of bEnd.3 endothelial cells and astrocyte type I clone (C8-D1A), these exosomes induced significant barrier dysfunction. Consistently, intracranial administration of exosomes from PRV-infected mice resulted in neurological deficits and increased BBB permeability in viv…

title: The Effect of Financial Literacy, Financial Inclusion, Financial Technology, and Locus of Control on MSME Financial Behavior in Tangerang City
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of financial literacy, financial inclusion, financial technology (fintech), and locus of control on the financial behavior of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Tangerang City. The background of this research is the vulnerability of MSMEs to business discontinuity, as indicated by survey evidence that most MSMEs can survive only a few months on their available capital. The study uses a quantitative approach with a causal research design, employing primary data collected through questionnaires distributed via Google Form to 400 MSME actors selected by random sampling, with the sample size determined using the Slovin formula. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. The results indicate that financial literacy, financial inclusion, financial technology, and locus of control each have a positive and significant effect on MSME financial behavior. Financial literacy is identified as the most dominant variable, followed by locus of control, financial inclusion, and financial technology. The model explains 89.2% of the variance in financial behavior. title: The Influence of Corporate Governance and Company Performance on Fraudulent Financial Statements
abstract: This study investigates the factors associated with the likelihood of financial statement fraud, focusing particularly on corporate governance mechanisms and financial performance. Corporate governance is represented by the proportion of independent commissioners on the board and audit committee financial expertise, while financial performance is measured using firm size, leverage, and profitability. The likelihood of financial statement fraud is evaluated using the Beneish M-Score and converted into a binary variable, where a value of 1 indicates that a company is classified as a potential financial statement manipulator, whereas a value of 0 indicates that it is classified as a non-manipulator. The study uses data from banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) over the 2019–2023 period. The data are examined through binary logistic regression analysis. The findings reveal that the proportion of independent commissioners and audit committee financial expertise are not significantly associated with the likelihood of financial statement fraud. Conversely, firm size, leverage, and profitability exhibit statistically significant relationships with the likelihood of potential financial statement manipulation. Design Requirements And Conceptual Architecture Of A Digital Financial Learning Platform For University Women Entrepreneurs
abstract: Financial literacy is a fundamental determinant of entrepreneurial sustainability, financial inclusion, and informed decision-making in increasingly digitalized environments. This study examined digital financial literacy among university women entrepreneurs, examined the psychometric properties of a multidimensional measurement instrument, and proposed the conceptual architecture of a digital financial learning platform. A quantitative, exploratory-descriptive, cross-sectional design was employed with a purposive sample of 57 university women entrepreneurs from southern Mexico. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire comprising four dimensions: financial knowledge, digital competencies, financial attitudes, and financial behavior. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega, while the instrument’s internal structure was explored through principal component analysis (PCA) with Varimax rotation. The results demonstrated satisfactory reliability for financial knowledge, financial attitudes, and financial behavior, whereas digital competencies exhibited moderate internal consistency. title: Artificial Intelligence Capability and Environmental Reporting Quality: The Moderating Role of Corporate Governance in Listed Non-Financial Firms in Nigeria
abstract: Aims: To examine whether artificial intelligence (AI) capability improves the environmental reporting quality of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria and whether corporate governance strengthens that effect. Study Design: An ex post facto longitudinal panel design was employed. Place and Duration of Study: Annual and sustainability reports of 42 non-financial firms in environmentally sensitive sectors listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, covering the period from 2015 to 2024. Methodology: Environmental reporting quality was measured using a 20-item index based on the GRI environmental topic standards, AI capability using a 10-item AI disclosure index, and corporate governance using a six-item governance index, all derived by content analysis of 420 firm-year reports. Pooled, fixed-effects and random-effects panel models were estimated; a robust Hausman test selected the fixed-effects estimator, and moderation was tested with a mean-centred interaction term. Results: AI capability had a positive and significant effect on environmental reporting quality (β = 0.405, P < .001), as did corporate governance (β = 0.189, P < .001). AI capability and corporate governance were positively correlated (r = 0.401, P < .001). title: Rational Ligand Design to Enforce the fac-fac Coordination Geometry
abstract: Abstract Controlling coordination geometry is a central concern in transition metal catalysis. This geometric control is evident in industrial processes, such as olefin polymerization, that demand thermal stability of a metal complex to maintain catalyst performance. A modular ligand scaffold that would allow for the tuning of catalyst properties while restricting ligand isomerization would be highly desirable for process optimization. Here we describe the substituted 2′,2′′-di(pyridin-2-yl)-[1,1′:3′,1′′:3′′,1′′′-quaterphenyl]-2,2′′′-diol (PQPD) ligand, a conformationally constrained scaffold that can be synthesized on a multigram scale, is amenable to structure–function studies, and maintains the fac-fac coordination geometry in neutral and cationic forms of Zr and Hf complexes as determined by X-ray crystallography and DFT calculations (ωB97X-D4/def2-TZVPD//ωB97X-D4/def2-SVPD). The design principles to maintain the fac-fac geometry were used to develop the diMe-PQPD (11) ligand that was complexed with Zr and Hf to demonstrate a platform for olefin polymerization catalyst development.

abstract: Generative assistants and shopping agents increasingly choose which consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands shoppers see, yet no published study has measured brand visibility in these habitual, repeat-purchase categories. This paper introduces a reproducible measurement framework built on five constructs: Citation Share (with a rank-weighted variant), the probability that a brand is named for a brand-free query; Basket Capture Rate, the share of agent-assembled basket items won by one manufacturer; Portfolio Halo, the gain in a manufacturer’s chance of winning a basket slot after winning the previous one; Source Provenance Ratio, the mix of cited domain classes; and the Paid-Presence Index, a count of visible sponsored placements that does not measure advertising spend. All data are simulated. The framework is demonstrated on 12,000 simulated responses (six US CPG categories, 60 anonymized brands, 300 queries, four anonymized engines, two waves eight weeks apart) calibrated to published studies; results show what the framework can detect, not the behavior of any real engine, brand or manufacturer. title: Sustainable Together? Consumer Responses to Firms’ Collaborative Sustainable Behaviour
abstract: Collaboration among businesses is increasingly viewed as essential for achieving a sustainable future; however, little is known about how consumers interpret such collaborative efforts. Drawing on interdependence theory, this research investigates whether, how, and when firms’ collaborative sustainability behaviour influences consumer responses to sustainable products and services. Across three experimental studies, we find that presenting sustainability initiatives as collaborative rather than individual increases preference for sustainable options and willingness to pay, an effect mediated by inferred sustainability effectiveness. However, when explicit effectiveness information is provided, the influence of collaboration is attenuated, indicating that collaboration primarily functions as a cue from which consumers infer sustainability effectiveness. Together, these findings advance our understanding of consumer responses to collaboration for sustainability and offer practical guidance on when firms should emphasise collaboration versus verified impact metrics in their sustainability communications.

title: The Real Effects of Credit Ratings on Credit Default Swap Market: The Sovereign Ceiling Channel
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether credit ratings convey incremental information to the credit default swap (CDS) market. We use sovereign‐ceiling‐induced rating downgrades as an exogenous shock in a difference‐in‐differences model to identify the effect of rating changes on CDS spreads. We find that CDS spreads of treated firms increase by 25.96% more than those of control firms following sovereign downgrades. The effect is stronger for firms with lower earnings performance, R&D, intangible assets, and higher leverage, particularly in countries with less private bank lending. CDS portfolio strategies based on these downgrades generate abnormal returns, indicating that rating downgrades convey non‐public information.

abstract: Background: Tomato leaf diseases significantly reduce tomato productivity and economic returns for farmers worldwide. Early and accurate detection of these diseases is essential for effective crop management and yield preservation. Traditional disease identification depends on manual inspection by agricultural experts, which can be time-consuming, subjective and difficult to scale across large farming areas. Recent advancements in deep learning have introduced automated and scalable solutions for plant disease detection. This study presents a comparative analysis of two pretrained CNN architectures, ResNet101 and VGG16, for binary classification of Tomato Bacterial Spot and Tomato Early Blight. Methods: The dataset used in this study consists of 3,127 labeled tomato leaf images. It was divided into 80% training data (2,501 images), 10% validation data (313 images) and 10% testing data (313 images). Transfer learning was applied using pretrained convolutional backbones for both ResNet101 and VGG16. The convolutional layers were frozen to preserve learned feature representations and custom fully connected classification heads were added for the binary classification task. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy. Result: ResNet101 demonstrated superior classification performance compared to VGG16. title: Capital Structure, Firm Performance, and Market Competitiveness: A Review of Recent Evidence with Reference to the Pakistani Textile Sector
abstract: Literature about the three is diffuse and at times contradictory, but in corporate finance, these are essential questions that are intertwined: how a corporation finances itself, how effective its performance is, and how much competition it faces. A review of the current (2024-2026) literature - both empirical and theoretical- is conducted in this study to interpret the findings in the context of a sector faced with stress: Pakistani textiles. The review synthesizes over 40 open-access studies of the financing–performance nexus and classifies the work into two streams: theoretical perspectives (the irrelevance, trade-off, pecking-order, agency, signalling, strategic-commitment, and deep-pocket perspectives) and thematic results addressing the leverage–performance nexus, liquidity and working-capital effects, firm-characteristic moderators like size or age, the financing–competitiveness nexus, and the innovation, ESG, and governance channels to competitive outcomes. There are three patterns: the effect of leverage on performance is bar more than bar in most cases, and often not linear for asset-based debt compared with equity-based debt; competitiveness isn't all about finance; it's about the investments in innovation and capability that finance makes possible; and evidence about emerging markets and sectors remains relatively scarce. abstract: Legacy resistance spot welding (RSW) timers on many automotive body-in-white lines expose weld parameters only through a handheld teaching pendant, which blocks automated quality logging. This paper presents the design of a non-intrusive, read-only data-acquisition (DAQ) node for the Obara STN21 single-phase AC weld timer, developed for a digitalisation project at a commercial vehicle OEM in South India. Analysis of the controller manual shows that its only documented machine-readable fieldbus is an optional DeviceNet slave interface with a 5-byte input image, not the RS-485 link assumed in the project brief, so the node measures the process externally. Two circuits are compared in a ten-criterion matrix: Option A, with per-channel AMC1200 isolation amplifiers, a 6N137 status optocoupler, and an RS-485/Modbus link, and Option B, with whole-node isolation, PC817 status inputs and isolated Ethernet. Option A was selected for the first build. Design calculations expose integrator-range, ADC-throughput, and component-rating issues in both drafts, including load-cell grounding, and propose corrections; the integrator and load-cell corrections are built into the selected Option A design, while the ADC-simultaneity limitation remains open. Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy SVC Control for Critical Clearing Time and Voltage Recovery in the Nigerian 330 kV Grid: An Ajaokuta–Benin Corridor Simulation Study
abstract: Voltage recovery and transient rotor-angle stability are interconnected challenges in long-distance high-voltage transmission corridors. This study investigates an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) controller for a 200 Mvar static var compensator (SVC) positioned at the midpoint of a nominal 250 km, 330 kV Ajaokuta–Benin corridor model. MATLAB/Simulink time-domain studies compared the uncompensated system with proportional-integral (PI), artificial neural network (ANN), and ANFIS-based SVC control under three-phase faults and loading levels from 80% to 120% of nominal. At Ajaokuta, the critical clearing time increased from 0.145 s without compensation to 0.195 s with PI-SVC, 0.225 s with ANN-SVC, and 0.265 s with ANFIS-SVC, corresponding to an 82.8% increase over the uncompensated case. At 120% loading, the ANFIS-SVC voltage recovery time was 1.3 s, compared with 3.2 s for PI-SVC and 5.5 s without compensation. In the nominal-load fault comparison, ANFIS-SVC reduced the reported voltage dip to 0.22 p.u., limited overshoot to 2.1%, and increased the damping ratio from 0.08 to 0.31. The simulation results indicate that neuro-fuzzy modulation of shunt reactive support can improve fault tolerance and post-fault voltage restoration in the investigated corridor model. The findings support further evaluation of adaptive SVC control using detailed network data and implement…

title: Social Media Hype, Investor Sentiment and Retail Investor Participation in the Nigerian Capital Market: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The use of social media as platforms for communicating financially has increased the avenues through which retail investors obtain investment information, share market views, and react to investment chances. Nevertheless, the dissemination of investment advice, speculation, and market narratives via social media may affect the sentiment of the investor and the behavior traits like herding and Fear of Missing Out (FOMO). This research aims at examining the connection between social media hype, investor sentiment, and participation of retail investors in the Nigerian capital market. The research focuses on the effects of social media hype on investor sentiment, the connection between investor sentiment and retail participation, the behavioral effects of social media hype, herding and FOMO on investment decisions, and digital financial communication and its role in developing investment sentiments. A systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines was employed. Articles written in the English language from January 2021 to 2026 were obtained using Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, complemented by a manual search of reference lists. Among the 232 references obtained from the search process, 19 studies were noted as meeting the inclusion requirements and were included for analysis. The Effects of Smart Workplace Technology, Employee Technology Readiness, and Digital Learning Culture on Digital Workplace Experience in the Public Service Sector
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Smart Workplace Technology, Employee Technology Readiness, and Digital Learning Culture on Digital Workplace Experience in the public service sector in Indonesia. The research is planned to be conducted with a quantitative approach using survey technique to workers of public sector organizations which have used digital technology in their job operations. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling. The criteria of the respondents are the current workers with a minimum work period of 1 year and consistently use digital information systems. Data were collected through an online questionnaire distributed using Google Form with 5-point Likert scale. Data analysis was performed using multiple linear regression. The model of the study presented here shows positive relations among Smart Workplace Technology, Employee Technology Readiness, Digital Learning Culture and Digital Workplace Experience, with Smart Workplace Technology expected to have the highest relative contribution. The results of this study have practical implications for public service organizations to improve the quality of digital infrastructure, employee technology readiness, and digital learning culture to enhance digital workplace usability, employee digital satisfaction, digital collaboration experience, perceived technological support, and digital work effectiveness.

Цель статьи состоит в уточнении содержания конструкта «управленческая зрелость» и обосновании концептуальной модели структуры опросника. Методом исследования выступил теоретический анализ компетентностного, ресурсного, субъектно-деятельностного и ценностно-смыслового подходов к оценке руководителя. Анализ отечественных работ дополнен данными европейских, китайских и казахстанских исследований мотивации служения и ценностных оснований лидерства. Показано, что управленческие компетенции неотделимы от личности руководителя, а мотивационные и ценностно-смысловые образования составляют самостоятельный слой оснований управленческой деятельности, который должен быть представлен в диагностическом инструменте. title: Exploring the experiences of service users with serious mental health conditions living in community residential facilities: A scoping review
abstract: Introduction: People with serious mental illness (SMI) may face challenges living independently or maintaining stable tenancies. As a result, residential services, including 24-hour staffed residences in community settings, can play a vital role in providing support and rehabilitation for this population. This review aimed to identify and map the available literature on the experiences of residents with SMI living in 24-hour staffed community residential facilities. Methods: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute guidance for conducting scoping reviews and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) reporting guidelines. Six databases were searched. Results: Nineteen studies were included, reporting the experiences of 1024 participants. Findings are presented under five themes: (1) varied experiences of staff support and relationships in recovery, (2) valued opportunities for meaningful activities, (3) skills development, (4) residential facilities as a springboard to community living and (5) residential environment impacts on quality of life. Conclusion: This review highlights the central role of skill development, meaningful activity engagement, vocational participation, community connection and peer support in promoting recovery among people with SMI living in residential settings.

I Believe in You: Robot Identity Design and Service Initiative
abstract: Some public-service tasks involve requests for personal information, making a robot's presented role and service behavior relevant to users’ privacy perceptions. We examine professional identity cues and service proactivity in a simulated Chinese government-service setting. Semi-structured interviews ( \(n=17\) ) informed the study design; a pilot study ( \(n=34\) ) checked the manipulations; and a 2×2 within-subjects virtual study ( \(n=36\) ) measured self-reported privacy sensitivity and the depth of simulated disclosure. In the main study, participants reported lower privacy sensitivity with robots presented as having a professional identity, and service proactivity interacted with identity presentation. Interviewees differed in their preferences: some found passive service less intrusive, whereas others valued proactive assistance for anticipating their needs. These findings concern perceptions and choices in a simulation, not the robot's actual institutional authorization or data security. They inform context-sensitive interaction design without treating increased disclosure as a goal or professional appearance as proof of privacy protection.

title: Heterodyne-Detected Sum-Frequency Generation Spectroscopy at Two-Dimensional Material–Water Interfaces: A Practical Guide
abstract: Abstract Water at two-dimensional (2D) material surfaces plays a central role in catalysis, electrochemistry, and nanofluidics. Molecular-level insights into their structure and dynamics at buried 2D material/water interfaces are essential for understanding interfacial mechanisms and guiding the design of functional systems. Heterodyne-detected sum-frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy provides a direct probe of interfacial water, but its quantitative application to 2D materials has been limited by the difficulty of extracting the intrinsic interfacial molecular response, which requires accurate phase measurement and rigorous Fresnel-factor corrections. In multilayer 2D material geometries, this challenge is further compounded by nanoconfined water trapped between the 2D material and its supporting material, the finite nonlinear response of the 2D material itself, and its crystallographic symmetry, all of which modulate both the amplitude and phase of the measured signal. Here, we present a practical protocol that enables robust, quantitative HD-SFG measurements at thin-film 2D material/water interfaces by explicitly accounting for thin-film interference and nanoconfined water as well as the intrinsic nonlinear response of the 2D material. title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. title: The role of emotion regulation and the valence of memory integration in trauma-related self-defining memories in individuals with alcohol use disorder
abstract: Abstract Introduction Patients with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) exhibit difficulties integrating self-defining memories (SDMs), which play a central role in the development of personal identity. Negative memories are more frequently integrated than positive ones, as they challenge identity and promote self-reflection. Individuals with AUD show high prevalence of trauma exposure. The impact of these experiences may be influenced on whether individuals interpret these experiences as shaping their identity positively or negatively. This study aims to assess whether patients with AUD were less likely than controls to integrate trauma-related SDMs, taking into account the valence of integration. It also explores the associations among trauma exposure during childhood and adulthood, as well as emotional regulation in this process and its association with length of abstinence. Method The sample included 62 AUD patients and 54 controls. Each participant recalled 5 SDMs that were analyzed according to different dimensions: theme, integration and valence of integration (positive vs. negative). Trauma exposure during childhood and adulthood, as well as emotional regulation strategies, were assessed using questionnaires. abstract: Introduction: Homeostatic Medicine and Tetratherapy is a therapeutic proposal developed by the author. It attributes a causal role to continuous exposure to technology-generated electromagnetic radiation, termed Global Radiation, in conditions ranging from fatigue, anxiety and insomnia to chronic diseases. Objective: to describe and systematize the conceptual foundations, techniques and protocols of the model, and to identify the degree of empirical support with which they are presented. Method: a documentary study with a qualitative approach and a descriptive-analytical scope, based on a full reading of the reference work (2nd ed., 2019; 256 pp.) and its coding into seven analytical categories, with each statement located by page. Results: the model is organized on four levels: (a) aetiological postulates (Artificial Global Electromagnetic Radiation, Human Transducer Syndrome and the notion of “mobile antennas”); (b) three principles of action (cellular signalling, biochemical mimetization and molecular reorganization), supported by eight invoked physical phenomena; (c) four fields of health (physical, biological, emotional and energetic), associated with four colours; and (d) six intervention procedures: biometric breathing, bioenergetic homologation over 17 main circuits, neurofractalization, synergic oleotherapy, neurobiological and sensory psychotherapy, and virtual coding…

Serum Vitamin D Levels and Antihistamine Treatment Response in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is often refractory, and some patients do not achieve control with second-generation H1-antihistamines (sgAHs). Vitamin D has immunomodulatory effects relevant to mast cell biology, but its relationship with sgAH treatment response, as distinct from disease presence or severity, is poorly characterized. We investigated the association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels and sgAH response in CSU. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included patients with active CSU who had a 25(OH)D measurement within the 3 months preceding diagnosis or on the day of diagnosis. Patients who received vitamin D therapy within 6 months before diagnosis or during follow-up, and those with hepatic, renal or systemic autoimmune disease or prior glucocorticoid or immunosuppressant use, were excluded. Treatment response was assessed with the Urticaria Control Test (UCT) after at least 4 weeks on a stable regimen. Patients reaching UCT ≥12 on sgAH monotherapy, at the licensed dose or after updosing, were classified as sgAH-responsive; those with UCT <12 after at least 4 weeks at four-fold dosing were classified as sgAH-refractory. Analyses included univariate comparisons, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and age-and sex-adjusted logistic regression. Results: Of 167 patients, 93 (55.7%) were sgAH-responsive a…

Quaternary Ammonium Calix[4]arene-Engineered PLA/PEG Films: Antibacterial Activity and Cell-Type-Dependent Biological Response
abstract: Abstract The development of biodegradable polymer surfaces combining strong antibacterial activity with controlled mammalian-cell responses remains challenging because increasing cationic antibacterial functionality may also adversely affect cellular behavior. To address this limitation, a quaternary ammonium-functionalized calix[4]arene derivative (Calix-2QA) was synthesized and incorporated into poly(lactic acid)/poly(ethylene glycol) (PLA/PEG) films at different loadings. Calix-2QA was characterized by 1H NMR, FTIR, and MALDI-TOF-MS analyses. The resulting films were evaluated for structural, thermal, morphological, antibacterial, and biological properties. FTIR analysis indicated Calix-2QA incorporation through noncovalent intermolecular interactions. Thermal analysis showed restricted matrix mobility and delayed cold crystallization; the decomposition onset decreased from 259 °C for PLA/PEG to 188 °C at 10 wt % Calix-2QA, while char yield increased from 0.2% to 2.2%. SEM and EDX analyses revealed composition-dependent morphological changes, including rough and pore-like features, nitrogen-based evidence of additive incorporation, and pronounced agglomeration at the highest loading. Effects of propofol in addition to isoflurane anesthesia on the immune response within the microcirculation: An intravital microscopy study
abstract: Background General volatile anesthesia is widely used in human medicine and the standard approach in many experimental animal procedures. In certain clinical situations, intravenous propofol may be added to inhalational anesthesia. Both types of anesthetics are known to have immunomodulatory effects, however, the effects of combining them on the immune response remain insufficiently understood. Methods Twenty male C57BL/6J mice received either isoflurane alone or a combination of isoflurane and propofol. The mice were challenged with either endotoxin or placebo. Intravital fluorescence microscopy of the intestinal submucosa was performed to quantify leukocyte rolling flux and adhesion in collecting (V1) and post-capillary (V3) venules. Additionally, functional capillary density (FCD) was measured in the mucosa and muscularis layers to evaluate microvascular perfusion. Results The addition of propofol to isoflurane anesthesia attenuated the inflammatory response to endotoxin, as shown by reduced leukocyte adhesion and preservation of rolling flux in the intestinal microcirculation. Intestinal FCD remained unchanged across both mucosal and muscular layers in both anesthetic regimens under baseline and inflammatory conditions. Conclusions Propofol appears to have anti-inflammatory effects. The consequences of these effects should be considered in the clinical context of pre-existi…

Administrative Competencies Required for Effective School Management: A Mixed-Methods Study of School Heads in Southern Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: School heads in Pakistan are usually promoted on the basis of seniority and take charge of staff, finances, records, infrastructure and instruction with little formal preparation. This study identified the administrative competencies that school heads consider essential for effective school management and the priority areas for their training. A convergent mixed-methods design was used. A 56-item questionnaire covering seven competency areas was completed by 300 school heads and education managers from eleven districts of Southern Punjab, and two focus group discussions were held with ten heads in Bahawalpur and Multan. The questionnaire showed excellent reliability (α = 0.944). All 56 competencies were endorsed at high or very high levels (overall M = 4.24, SD = 0.42), and every competency area was rated well above the neutral point (t(299) = 38.61 to 47.17, p < .001). Professional Ethics, Accountability and Technology ranked highest (M = 4.31), and Planning and Organization lowest (M = 4.17). The lowest-rated individual competencies were mobilising community resources (M = 3.94), using digital tools for administration (M = 4.03) and emergency planning (M = 4.04). The seven areas were moderately inter-correlated (r = 0.54 to 0.65). title: Évolution du cadre institutionnel et des mécanismes de conduite de la politique monétaire au Maroc (1983-2025)
abstract: Ce travail retrace l’évolution de la politique monétaire marocaine de 1983 à 2025, une période de profondes mutations de son cadre opérationnel et institutionnel. Il analyse la transition graduelle d’une gestion reposant sur des outils administratifs et sur le contrôle direct du crédit vers un dispositif fondé sur un taux directeur, une cible opérationnelle de taux interbancaire et des instruments indirects de régulation de la liquidité. L’étude porte aussi sur les mutations institutionnelles de Bank Al-Maghrib, en particulier les statuts de 2006 puis la loi n° 40-17 de 2019, qui ont consolidé son autonomie, ainsi que sur la flexibilisation progressive du régime de change engagée en 2018. Elle s’intéresse en parallèle à l’environnement macroéconomique : désinflation, choc inflationniste de 2022-2023, finances publiques, croissance et emploi. En combinant lecture historique, analyse institutionnelle et examen d’indicateurs issus de Bank Al-Maghrib, du Haut-Commissariat au Plan et du ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, l’article montre comment la modernisation des outils monétaires, les réformes institutionnelles et la quête de stabilité se sont mutuellement influencées. Il met également en évidence le coût de la stabilité des prix en termes de croissance et d’emploi.

abstract: This book review examines John J. Mearsheimer’s The Tragedy of Great Power Politics, focusing on offensive realism and great-power competition. It evaluates the book’s theoretical contributions, limitations, and relevance to contemporary U.S.–China strategic rivalry, particularly in the context of technological competition and international security.

title: Analysis of the Development Needs of Digital Interactive Learning Media of the Circulatory System to Facilitate Critical Thinking of Elementary School Students
abstract: This study aims to analyze the needs for the development of digital interactive learning media for the human circulatory system and identify its suitability in facilitating the critical thinking skills of elementary school students. The research uses mixed methods with a multiphase design which is carried out in two phases. Phase 1 involves 30 grade VI teachers and 39 grade VI students through a needs survey, initial tests of critical thinking skills, and open questions to teachers. Quantitative data is analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data is analyzed thematically and integrated through joint displays. Phase 2 was carried out by demonstrating the Circulatory System to 30 teachers in Karangkobar District, then continued with a response survey and open-ended questions. The results of Phase 1 showed that students had difficulty in visualizing blood flow (87.1%) as well as difficulties analyzing information, determining solutions, and making conclusions (89.8%). The initial test of critical thinking ability obtained an average of 51.01, with the lowest achievement in the evaluation indicator of 44.2%. All teachers and students also showed the need for more visual, interactive learning media, equipped with simulations, exercises, and feedback. title: Forecasting Sugarcane Area, Production and Productivity in Uttarakhand, India, up to 2029-30: A Rolling-origin Comparison of Time-series Models
abstract: This study examined trends in sugarcane area, production and productivity in Uttarakhand and its Kumaon and Garhwal divisions and developed forecasts to 2029–30. The analysis used 26 crop seasons (2000–01 to 2025–26) from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, audited against the state Sugarcane Department series. Thirteen candidate procedures, comprising benchmark, trend-regression, exponential-smoothing, ARIMA and combination models, were compared using rolling-origin out-of-sample evaluation. A structural break around 2018–19 was assessed and treated through a level-shift adjustment. Production forecasts were derived from area and productivity, while divisional area forecasts were reconciled with the state forecast. State sugarcane area declined by 1.27% annually (P < .001), whereas productivity increased by 1.61% annually (P < .001), with much of the productivity increase occurring as a step change around 2018–19. State production showed no significant trend (P = .35). For 2029–30, the state forecasts were 79.8 thousand ha for area (95% prediction interval: 69.3–90.2), 6,025 thousand t for production (4,703–7,347) and 75.5 t ha⁻¹ for productivity (60.0–91.0). In the post-break nested holdout, the selected procedures did not outperform the naive forecast for eight of the nine series. Divisional forecasts were also sensitive to the structural break and inconsistencies i…

abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics cause household net load to change sign and vary seasonally. We evaluate a PV-aware temporal convolutional quantile network with horizon-delayed conformal calibration on 300 Australian homes and a 299-home portfolio aggregate. The network predicts seven non-crossing quantiles at 48 nominal half-hour forecast horizons. On the original eight selected horizons, PV-TCQN has a 6.82% lower aggregate seven-quantile score (QS7) than the original LightGBM-Q configuration, with the largest gains at short leads; the selection chronology is unknown. Across all 48 equally weighted horizons, PV-TCQN is 0.50% worse numerically, with no statistically conclusive difference. The household comparison, based on one neural seed, is also inconclusive and establishes neither superiority nor equivalence. Rolling-window adaptive conformal inference (RW-ACI) improves the evaluated household home–month–horizon coverage-tail metric relative to rolling CQR, while increasing mean prediction-set length by 4.2–4.4%. Approximately 90% pooled coverage nevertheless coexists with household coverage of 78.64% during high-PV cases and 71.98% during large ramps. These overlapping, outcome-defined retrospective regimes are diagnostics, not conditional-coverage guarantees. title: The Effect of Product Availability, Service Quality, Price Fairness and Store Trust on Repurchase Intention (A Study at Sari Jaya Tani Agricultural Store)
abstract: This study analyzes the effects of product availability, service quality, price fairness, and store trust on repurchase intention among customers of Sari Jaya Tani, an agricultural input store in Brebes Regency. A quantitative survey was conducted with 100 customers selected through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The four variables jointly had a significant effect on repurchase intention and explained 86.5% of its variance. Service quality, price fairness, and store trust each had a positive and significant effect, whereas product availability had no significant partial effect. Price fairness was the strongest predictor. The non-significant effect of product availability is discussed in relation to its overlap with store trust and the predominance of loyal customers in the sample. Agricultural input retailers should prioritize fair pricing, advisory service, and trust building while keeping stock reliable during planting seasons.

title: A Spatial Skip-Connected Attention-based LSTM for urban traffic forecasting using air quality data
abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of smart cities requires intelligent systems that are capable of addressing the growing complexity of urban environments. Urban traffic forecasting in smart cities remains challenging because of complex spatiotemporal dependencies and the presence of noisy, incomplete, and spatially heterogeneous sensor data. Existing forecasting models fail to preserve multiscale spatial relationships and long-term temporal dependencies, thereby reducing prediction accuracy under urban sensing conditions. To overcome these issues, this research proposes a Spatial Skip-Connected Attention-based Long Short-Term Memory (SSCA-LSTM) framework for traffic forecasting using air quality data. The proposed model integrates a U-shaped hierarchical spatiotemporal structure with spatial skip connections and spatial weighting mechanisms, thereby enabling it to learn both spatial and temporal dependencies at multiple urban scales. The spatial skip connections ensure gradient stability and fine-detail preservation at encoding and decoding, whereas the spatial weighting module adaptively identifies high-impacted regions based on spatial significance, thereby enhancing adaptive learning. Moreover, the hierarchical structure provides multiscale feature abstraction, capturing macro-level trends such as traffic flow and micro-level variation such as pollution patterns. Experimental an…

abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the laminar–turbulent transition is critical for the design of hypersonic vehicles. However, established physics-based methods, such as linear stability theory (LST), are computationally intensive. The development of efficient surrogate models to overcome these limitations is particularly challenging for blunt-nosed vehicles. Strong non-similar flow effects caused by the entropy layer render simplified profile parameterizations inadequate in the case of these vehicles. To address this, the present paper proposes a methodology for creating surrogate models trained on a comprehensive database of laminar Navier–Stokes simulations and LST computations for a 7 $$^\circ $$ ∘ blunt cone. A pivotal element is the utilization of the boundary layer impedance inflection point for feature extraction, which provides a compact parameterization of the acoustic waveguide and reduces the reliance on boundary layer edge quantities, which are ambiguous in the presence of an entropy layer. Two modeling frameworks are employed and compared in this study: radial basis function (RBF) interpolation and eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Both models agree closely with the LST benchmark at the freestream conditions of the MF-1 flight experiment. In the implementations examined here, XGBoost can be trained on the complete high-resolution database, whereas the partitioned…

title: Chemical Language Models for Prediction of Radiolytic Transformation Products from Molecular Structure
abstract: Abstract Assessing the fate of organic compounds under ionizing radiation requires knowing which degradation products form, yet identifying them experimentally is slow and costly. We ask how well machine-learning models can generate those products from a parent compound’s structure alone. Because reported product distributions depend on irradiation conditions that studies record inconsistently, we target a condition-agnostic screening task: recovering the set of products reported for a parent under any condition. We compile a curated benchmark of 446 experimentally reported reactant–product pairs across 128 parent compounds from the primary radiolysis and photolysis literature, and cast prediction as one-to-many SMILES generation under reagent-level repeated cross-validation. GT4SD achieved the highest mean Hit@10 among the models evaluated under shared cross-validation, recovering at least one reported product for 59.4% of parent compounds, compared with 41.1% for nearest-neighbor retrieval. These results demonstrate the potential of chemistry-pretrained language models to generate radiolytic transformation-product candidates for experimental follow-up. Open-weight models further enable local deployment and control over molecular data, supporting their practical use in radiolysis research.

title: Prediction of Thrombosis Risk in Atopic Dermatitis Patients Treated with JAK Inhibitors: Development of the Thrombo-JAK score
abstract: We developed and validated the Thrombo-JAK score, a machine-learning–derived thrombosis risk model for adults with atopic dermatitis treated with JAK1-selective inhibitors. Among 305 patients, the model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.72) and identified clinically meaningful laboratory thresholds that stratified thrombosis risk from 3.4% to 31.0% across score categories. This simple, interpretable tool may support individualized risk assessment and safer prescribing of JAK inhibitors in dermatologic practice.

A Hybrid Linear Discriminant Analysis and Artificial Neural Network Framework for High-Accuracy Prediction of Chronic Kidney Disease
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is becoming an increasingly important global health issue and it is currently one of the major causes of death, predicted to become the fifth leading cause of years of life lost by 2040. It is challenging to detect it during its early stages as the disease is typically asymptomatic at this point, and nonrenal factors can interfere with the traditional diagnostic indicators. This paper describes a hybrid machine-learning approach that uses Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) for supervised dimensionality reduction and feature extraction and Bayesian-optimized Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for nonlinear classification. Using the publicly available UCI Chronic Kidney Disease dataset (consisting of 400 cases and 25 clinical and laboratory attributes), the method handles missing values, encodes the categorical variables, ranks the clinically relevant features, projects the data onto a maximally discriminative subspace, and classifies the patients using a regularized multilayer perceptron. The hybrid LDA–ANN model obtained an accuracy of 98.75% on the independent test set, with precision, recall, and F1-scores varying between 0.97 and 1.00, significantly beating logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machines, random forests, and standalone LDA (96.25%).
