Development of a Road Accident Prediction Model to Enhance the Safety of Gravel Road Maintenance: A Case of Monduli District, Tanzania
abstract: Gravel roads managed by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA) in Monduli District serve pastoral, agricultural and tourism communities, yet their maintenance is scheduled by routine condition-based cycles rather than by safety risk. High-risk sections therefore receive no priority, and TARURA has no quantitative means of showing how maintenance reduces accidents. This study developed a road accident prediction model to enhance the safety of gravel road maintenance in Monduli District. A mixed-methods, cross-sectional design was used. A structured questionnaire administered to 83 stakeholders, comprising TARURA engineers, contractors, project managers, road safety stakeholders and road user representatives, rated twelve road condition variables, which were ranked with the Relative Importance Index (RII). Seven variables met the threshold of RII ≥ 0.75: maintenance quality (0.930), drainage adequacy (0.911), surface condition (0.880), clear zone (0.851), sight distance (0.819), horizontal alignment (0.790) and carriageway width (0.759). These were used as predictors in a multiple linear regression (MLR) model of a section Safety Index, an accident risk index on a 0–10 scale anchored to police and TARURA accident records, using 83 section-level assessment records from 25 sampled road sections split 70/15/15 into training, validation and test sets. CAPACITY WITHOUT LOAD: A 30-FOLD DENOMINATOR TRAP AND STARTUP ENERGY INTENSITY IN A SEVEN-YEAR KILN PANEL
abstract: Specific energy consumption is meaningful only when the energy numerator and production denominator cover the same boundary and period. This archival field study reconstructs 81 monthly observations from January 2016 to December 2022 for the biscuit and glost kilns of an anonymised porcelain tableware manufacturer, combining kiln-loading records, annual factory-performance workbooks and a capacity-expansion plan. Two linked findings provide the contribution. First, cells labelled In Ton in the 2020 and 2021 workbooks calculate average tonnes per day; summing those cells as annual tonnage produces 11,031 and 10,725 m3 of gas per tonne, while reconstructing period tonnes from stored piece counts and the workbook's 0.45 kg-per-piece assumption yields 367.7 and 357.5 m3 per tonne, an exact 30-fold correction. Second, a new glost kiln began reporting gas in March 2022; the plan allocated 688,000 pieces per month to it while its active-month average was 335,897 first-pass pieces, or 48.8% of plan. Its gas intensity was 0.255 m3 per first-pass piece versus 0.192 for the legacy kiln, and combined glost intensity rose from 0.177 to 0.209, a 17.6% increase. The study does not claim a causal technology penalty. It shows how denominator governance and utilisation regime determine what an energy-performance indicator means, and proposes a reproducible control protocol.

title: “Sit Nice!”: Peer Culture, Teacher Capacity, and Joint Socialization Efforts in Preschool
abstract: Preschools instill soft skills that are crucial to children’s life outcomes. As preschool access expands, research and policy often focus on improving teacher quality. This focus downplays how much teachers’ efforts may depend on children’s peers. Drawing on two years of ethnography, I highlight two important aspects of socialization: teachers’ capacity to deliver messages in the moment, and peers’ tendency to support those messages. I compare socialization processes at two race- and class-segregated preschools. Three interrelated classroom conditions—children’s enrollment, attendance, and challenging behaviors—mattered for socialization interactions. Teachers at both preschools pursued socialization goals of instilling safe and formal classroom behaviors. At the affluent, majority-White preschool, teachers had a greater capacity to coach children in the moment, and peers had a culture of supporting teacher messages. At the low-income, racially diverse preschool, children placed the authority to coach classroom behavior in their teachers, who were pressed for time. I argue that socialization agents jointly influence behavior. In segregated preschools, teachers may shape classroom behavior to unequal extents, preventing early learning settings from disrupting future inequalities.

title: Effect of Drying on Bioaccessibility of Phenolic Compounds and Antioxidant Capacity of Indonesian Bay Leaf Decoction during Simulated Gastrointestinal Digestion
abstract: Indonesian bay leaf (Syzygium polyanthum Wight) is commonly consumed in Indonesia as a decoction, but the bioaccessibility of its bioactive compounds following gastrointestinal digestion remains poorly understood. This study evaluated changes in antioxidant capacity (DPPH, FRAP, and ABTS methods), total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), and bioaccessibility index (BI) in decoctions prepared from fresh Indonesian bay leaves (FBLD) and leaves dried using a fluidized-bed dryer at 45–50 °C (DBLD) following simulated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion. Before digestion, DPPH antioxidant capacity, TPC, and TFC were comparable between FBLD and DBLD, whereas drying reduced FRAP and ABTS antioxidant capacities by 21 and 19%, respectively. After intestinal digestion, DPPH and ABTS antioxidant capacities and TPC in DBLD were 55, 72, and 42% lower, respectively, than those in FBLD. The intestinal-phase BI (BI PI) for ABTS antioxidant capacity in FBLD and for TPC and TFC in both decoctions exceeded 100%, indicating increased recovery of assay-responsive components after digestion. In contrast, BI PI values for DPPH antioxidant capacity in DBLD and FRAP antioxidant capacity in both decoctions were below 37%. FBLD also exhibited higher BI PI values for TPC and DPPH and ABTS antioxidant capacities than DBLD. Overall, drying and gastrointestinal digestion differentially af…

title: A Two-Stage Adjustable Robust Optimization Model for Integrated Allocation of Beds, Medical Staff, Medicines and Equipment under Uncertain Patient Arrivals and Limited Capacity
abstract: Hospitals must commit beds, staff, medicines and equipment before they know how many patients will arrive, and a plan built on average demand may fail exactly when demand surges. This paper develops a two-stage adjustable robust optimization model for the integrated allocation of these four resources under uncertain, class-specific patient arrivals and limited capacity. First-stage capacities are fixed before the planning horizon; second-stage admission, overtime and emergency-procurement decisions respond to arrivals observed up to each day and are restricted to non-anticipative linear decision rules. Arrival uncertainty is described by a budgeted polyhedral set whose budget Γ controls the number of classes that may simultaneously reach their worst case in a day. The robust counterpart is an exact linear program. Four formal results are established: dualisation of the budgeted constraints, feasibility and attainment of the optimum, monotonicity in the budget, and a Hoeffding-based calibration rule that also shows when a probabilistic guarantee is uninformative. In a synthetic three-class hospital instance, the robust counterpart was verified on 3,000 sampled scenarios (maximum constraint violation 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁵) and compared with a nominal model and a sample average approximation on 2,000 out-of-sample scenarios under a non-anticipative admission policy. title: Molecular Interaction between Ovalbumin and Quercitrin: Binding Mechanism and Functional Enhancement
abstract: Abstract To elucidate the interaction mechanism between ovalbumin (OVA) and quercitrin (QUE) and its effects on the structural and functional properties of the resulting complex, an OVA-QUE system was constructed and characterized using spectroscopic techniques, differential scanning calorimetry, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that QUE formed a complex with OVA and quenched its intrinsic fluorescence through a mechanism consistent with predominantly static quenching, with binding constants on the order of 104 L·mol–1 and approximately one binding site. Synchronous fluorescence, three-dimensional fluorescence, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that QUE binding altered the microenvironment surrounding the aromatic amino acid residues and induced local conformational changes in OVA, with a more pronounced effect on tryptophan residues. Molecular docking identified one plausible binding pocket composed of both polar and hydrophobic residues, in which QUE may interact with key residues through hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic contacts. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that the Mode 1 predicted OVA-QUE pose remained stably accommodated throughout the trajectory without disrupting the overall protein fold while reducing the local flexibility of binding-pocket residues. title: Structural insight into dynamic switching mechanism o​f the SAM-IV riboswitch revealed by molecular simulations
abstract: Abstract S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-responsive riboswitches regulate essential metabolic pathways in many bacteria and represent attractive structured-RNA targets for chemical modulation. Among these, the SAM-IV riboswitch remains comparatively less explored at the level of ligand-dependent conformational dynamics despite the availability of apo and SAM-bound cryo-EM structures. Here, we investigated four structural states of the SAM-IV riboswitch—6UES-Apo, 6UET-bound, 6UES-Docked and 6UET-NoLig—using two independent 4 µs molecular dynamics simulations for each system, providing an aggregate sampling time of 32 µs. Structural stability, regional flexibility, hydrogen-bond persistence, clustering, combined principal component analysis, free-energy landscape mapping, dynamic cross-correlation analysis, pairwise residue-contact analysis, MM-GBSA calculations and ensemble docking were integrated to compare the conformational ensembles sampled in the presence and absence of SAM. Across the replicate simulations, the SAM-bound state generally displayed a comparatively restricted ensemble and lower local fluctuations, whereas ligand removal was associated with broader structural variability and redistribution of tertiary contacts. title: Band Gaps of Halide Perovskites from an Orbital Cluster Expansion: Mechanism, Iodide Bias, and a Hybridization Channel
abstract: Abstract Linear descriptors are cheap, interpretable, and trainable on hundreds of labels. What they lack is an account of why they work and where they break. We address both for the band gap of halide perovskites. We label 1784 CsPbX3-type supercells, 1241 of which are distinct under symmetry, with scalar-relativistic density-functional theory and fit an orbital cluster expansion: a linear model over counted atomic figures and distance-binned electrostatics. Under cross-validation grouped by the A/B-cation family, with the ridge penalty selected on a grouped split too, it reaches 0.151 eV (95% interval 0.140–0.160), 0.20 of the target standard deviation, and a 29% error reduction relative to Magpie. The path there is nonmonotonic: bonded angular figures make the fit worse than the composition, and only the distance-binned electrostatic channel recovers it─an ionic perovskite’s gap responds to the electrostatic environment, not to the bonded geometry. Densities of states identify the mechanism: the halide dominates the gap (effect size η2 = 0.386) and the B cation modulates it; the scalar-relativistic Pb/Ge gap ratio jumps from 1.26× in the fluoride to about 5× in the three heavier halides. The residual is biased in one halide only: iodide gaps are underestimated by a median of 0.085 eV, while the other halides are centered within 0.03 eV. A second-order hybridization channel r…

HYDRA-YOLOv10: An automated approach for detection and classification of Monkeypox skin lesion stages using YOLOv10 Adapted with Circular-Responsive Attention (CRA) and Normalization-Based Attention Mechanism (NAM)
abstract: Abstract Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease whose clinical manifestations often resemble other dermatological conditions, making accurate and timely diagnosis a challenge. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as PCR, are accurate but costly, time-consuming, and often inaccessible in low-resource environments. This study proposes HYDRA-YOLOv10, a deep learning-based architecture designed to automatically detect and classify Mpox skin lesions across five clinical stages: macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, and scabs. The model incorporates key architectural innovations, including hybrid backbone connections, extended use of the C2f module for multi-scale feature fusion, and the replacement of the SPPF module with the Circular-Responsive Attention (CRA) mechanism-designed to better capture the geometry of rounded lesions using polar-aware convolutions. Additionally, the Normalization-based Attention Mechanism (NAM) replaces conventional spatial attention, enhancing feature integration and robustness to visual variations. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s superiority over state-of-the-art approaches, achieving 95.4% precision, 94.8% recall, 95.1% F1 score, 95.5% mAP@0.5, and 83.4% mAP@0.5:0.95. These results validate HYDRA-YOLOv10 as a reliable and scalable solution for automated Mpox diagnosis, offering valuable support for clinical decision-making and public health res…

title: N‐Doped Coral Carbon for Synergistic Iodine Anchoring in High‐Capacity and Long‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising energy storage candidates owing to their high capacity and environmental friendliness. However, reported cathode materials suffer from low energy density and rapid capacity decay. In this study, a coral‐like N‐doped carbon with in situ grown surface carbon nanotubes (CNC‐CNT) was synthesized as iodine host material through the pyrolysis of bimetallic core‐shell metal‐organic frameworks. This nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon framework with well‐developed micro/mesopores enables both chemical adsorption of C–I species and physical immobilization of iodine, while providing substantial additional electric double‐layer capacitive contributions. The specific capacity reaches 690.00 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 , significantly surpassing that of the AC cathode host of 558.00 mAh g −1 . Consequently, the I2@CNC‐CNT cathode delivers stable cycling over 8000 cycles and retains 464.40 mAh g −1 even at 5 A g −1 . The pouch cell delivers an iodine‐normalized capacity of 501.33 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , yielding a material‐level energy density of ∼780 Wh kg −1 at 1.55 V including host capacitance. The host‐subtracted iodine‐redox capacity is 422.00 mAh −1 . This study presents a CNC‐CNT‐derived carbon cathode strategy with facile synthesis, which leverages its hierarchical coral‐like architecture to significantly enhance the specific capacity a…

title: Tribological Performance and Interfacial Lubrication Mechanism of PTFE/PEEK Composites Modified with PMPS@PSF Microcapsules
abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-based composites are promising self-lubricating materials, yet pure PTFE suffers from poor wear resistance and unstable transfer films. Here, polymethylphenylsiloxane@polysulfone (PMPS@PSF) core–shell microcapsules were prepared by solvent evaporation and incorporated with polyetheretherketone (PEEK) into PTFE. The effects of composition, load, and rotational speed on tribological performance were systematically evaluated. Increasing PEEK content markedly reduced wear but slightly increased friction. The composite containing 30 wt % PEEK and 10 wt % PMPS@PSF exhibited the best overall performance, with a COF of 0.0462 and a wear-loss rate of 0.0185 g/h at 30 N and 300 rpm, representing reductions of 57.30% and 90.28%, respectively, compared with pure PTFE. Mechanistic analysis and worn-surface characterization support a proposed bilayer lubrication mechanism involving PTFE-rich fluorinated species and PMPS-derived components, whose synergistic lubrication contributes to improved friction reduction and wear resistance.

New approach for occupational hazard risk assessment with dual-path feedback mechanism and WASPAS method
abstract: Abstract Occupational health and safety risk assessment (OHSRA) is an interdisciplinary activity to identify, assess and prioritize the risk of occupational hazards for ensuring the health and safety of workers. In this study, a hybrid OHSRA model integrating a dual-path feedback mechanism and the weighted aggregated sum product assessment (WASPAS) approach is proposed to assess and rank the risk of occupational hazards 2A5 School of Economics and Management, Tongji University, . First, the probabilistic linguistic term sets (PLTSs) are employed to capture the uncertain risk assessment information provided by experts. Second, a dual-path feedback mechanism is introduced to iteratively reconcile discrepancies and improve the group consensus level among experts. Then, an extended entropy-based approach is utilized to derive weights of risk criteria. Moreover, the WASPAS method is modified to determine the risk priority of the identified occupational hazards. Finally, an illustrative case is performed for demonstrating the proposed OHSRA model, followed by the sensitivity analysis, comparative analysis and validation analysis. The results demonstrate that the proposed model is practical for describing the complex and uncertain linguistic risk assessments of experts, and prioritizing the risk of occupational hazards in OHSRA.

abstract: Aims: To assess the extent and magnitude of variation in the physical and electro-chemical properties and organic carbon content of soils in the Southern High Hills (agro-ecological unit 14, AEU 14) of Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, and to group its five panchayaths in the district for soil management. Methodology: Surface soil (0–15 cm) and core samples from 122 fields were analysed for texture, bulk density, water holding capacity, pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon. The data were subjected to descriptive statistics, analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, linear regression and principal component analysis. Results: Soil acidity was the main property that separated the panchayaths. More than half of the samples (54.9%) had a pH of 5.5 or below; Peringamala had the most acidic soils (mean pH 5.10) and Aryanad (6.10) and Kallikad (5.93) were the least acidic. abstract: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. The results demonstrated the incorporation of urea-derived functionalities onto the CNT surface. title: Co-Feeding C1/C2 Substrates and Glucose Reshapes Carbon Partitioning During Fed-Batch Lipid Production in Yarrowia lipolytica
abstract: Abstract Glucose is the predominant carbon source for industrial biomanufacturing, but its utilization is inherently accompanied by carbon loss through CO2 generation during catabolism, limiting product yield and process sustainability. Alternative one-carbon (C1) and two-carbon (C2) feedstocks, such as formate and acetate produced from chemical or electrochemical CO2 conversion, offer an attractive route to improve carbon efficiency. In this study, formate or acetate was co-fed with reduced glucose during fed-batch lipid fermentation by wild-type and engineered strains of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica to evaluate their potential to enhance microbial lipid production. Under the tested co-feeding conditions, acetate supported higher cell growth and lipid accumulation than formate. The experimental co-feeding results were further used in a conceptual carbon-balance analysis to assess the potential benefit of integrating fermentation with CO2 capture and conversion technologies, in which fermentation off-gas CO2 is recycled into fermentable acetate or formate. For the wild-type strain Y. lipolytica ATCC 20362, recycling CO2 as acetate increased the carbon yields from 15.9% to 27.4% for biomass and from 5.4% to 10.8% for lipids, while reducing citrate byproduct yield from 31.2% to 13.6%. title: Bamboo‐Derived Oxygen‐Rich Porous Carbon Cathode Enabling High‐Performance Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries (4eZIBs) are promising for high‐energy aqueous energy storage, yet their practical performance is limited by the instability of reactive I + species and the associated irreversible iodine loss. Herein, an oxygen‐rich hierarchical porous carbon (PC) derived from bamboo powder is developed as an iodine host to regulate interfacial iodine chemistry. A zinc nitrate hexahydrate assisted solution combustion carbonisation strategy simultaneously constructs interconnected micro/mesopores and enriches oxygen‐containing surface functionalities. The resulting PC‐15 provides abundant accessible sites for iodine immobilisation, whereas its oxygen‐rich surface modulates the local iodine coordination environment and mitigates I + hydrolysis. The synergistic regulation of pore confinement and surface chemistry leads to enhanced iodine utilisation and favourable interfacial reaction kinetics. Consequently, the PC‐15 cathode delivers a specific capacity of 447.9 mAh g −1 at 0.8 A g −1 and retains a high rate capacity of 340.9 mAh g −1 at 8 A g −1 . Upon prolonged cycling at 5 A g −1 , it retains a capacity of 182.8 mAh g −1 after 4000 cycles with an average coulombic efficiency of 99.6%. These results demonstrate that integrating hierarchical pore confinement with oxygen‐rich surface chemistry can effectively reconcile iodine retention with rapid redo…

title: Molecular Investigation on the Transformation of Carbon Nanotube Bundles Into Carbon Fibers During Annealing
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we uncover the atomistic mechanism governing the transformation of highly aligned carbon nanotube fibers into graphitic carbon fibers during thermal annealing. Under sustained thermal loading, the constituent nanotubes coalesce with their neighbors to form progressively larger tubular structures. This irreversible structural evolution is driven by the elastic recoil that accompanies the release of strain energy stored in the highly curved nanotube walls; because larger tubes carry less curvature strain, coalescence proceeds only toward larger diameters. In parallel, the fiber cross section first undergoes a transient porosification and then densifies into an ordered graphitic arrangement. The development is closely tied to the diameter‐dependent compressive modulus of the nanotubes, allowing the internal voids to collapse and the structure to transition from a tubular assembly to a fully densified state. Mechanical evaluation shows that the resulting fibers attain an exceptional axial modulus of 748 GPa. This mechanical enhancement stems from a seamless, interconnected carbon network that minimizes dangling ends and enables efficient load transfer. Collectively, these results position carbon nanotubes as compelling precursors for advanced carbon fiber manufacturing and provide theoretical guidance for refining the annealing process toward high performanc…

abstract: Floodplain wetlands are highly dynamic ecosystems that play a crucial role in regulating greenhouse gases through the process of carbon sequestration. In addition, they deliver a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon cycling, hydrological and nutrient cycling, aquatic food production, habitat provision, water purification, and flow regulation. The present investigation was conducted in a floodplain wetland (Dandua beel) located in the Central Brahmaputra Valley Zone of Assam, with a total water-spread area of 52.36 ha. The sediment organic carbon (SOC) exhibited marked seasonal variability, ranging from 0.41 to 1.21% (0.65 ± 0.14%) during the pre-monsoon period, 0.40 to 1.84% (1.14 ± 0.3%) during the monsoon season, 0.42 to 2.85% (0.93 ± 0.47%) during the post-monsoon period, and 0.44 to 0.69% (0.59 ± 0.04%) during winter. The results indicated a progressive decline in sediment organic carbon content with increasing sediment depth (0–30 cm), with values of 24.05 Mg C ha⁻¹ in the 0–10 cm layer, 2.48 Mg C ha⁻¹ in the 10–20 cm layer, and 5.22 Mg C ha⁻¹ in the 20–30 cm layer. The mean carbon sequestration rate of the wetland was estimated at 1.6 Mg C ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Interplay of delayed inter-coupling and synchronous coupling in a Kuramoto–Winfree ensemble
abstract: We study the collective dynamics of a mixed Kuramoto–Winfree ensemble with delayed inter-couplings and instantaneous intra-couplings. For homogeneous ensembles with zero natural frequencies, an energy method yields asymptotic frequency death under a small-delay condition. For heterogeneous ensembles, we establish frameworks for complete or partial phase boundedness. The rotation numbers of the corresponding oscillators therefore exist and vanish. Complete phase boundedness, together with an additional small-delay condition, also yields asymptotic frequency death. Assuming eventual small-amplitude bounds, suitable coercivity conditions, and a sufficiently small delay, we prove exponential decay of the velocity energy and exponential convergence to an equilibrium. The general boundedness conclusions alone do not guarantee these eventual bounds. Under a further small-amplitude restriction, the equilibrium is unique within the prescribed region.

title: Modeling and solving the large scale EV charger location planning problem: a case study of Atlanta
abstract: Abstract We develop a model for the Electric Vehicle (EV) charger location planning problem with a focus on vehicles used for daily commuting in cities. Using mixed integer programs with branch-and-bound techniques, the method provides solutions even for large cities, overcoming the limitation of previous meta-heuristic methods. EV users are assigned to charging stations that are within a short distance from their home or work. We explore serving all commuters, serving only those who do not have access to home charging, and prioritizing those who live in disadvantaged areas. Our model and methodology for data collection can be used for any city in the USA, and globally if similar data are available. Although we use data for the city of Atlanta, the solutions yield several general insights. When maximizing commuters served for a limited number of chargers, the optimal solution puts most chargers at work locations, serving commuters with short commutes and thus low charging needs. As the number of chargers increases (beyond 25,000 stations in the Atlanta case), more are placed at larger distances from the city center, providing more commuters with charging near home. For those without home charging, equity goals can be met with minimal effect on the number of commuters served and the distribution of chargers. Instructional Model to Promote Creativity of Product Design Students: Development and Validation
abstract: This article reported the development and validation of an instructional model based on constructivist principles and design-thinking processes to enhance creativity in product design among Chinese undergraduates. The model was developed by a literature synthesis and a needs analysis. The analysis utilized questionnaires and interviews to assess classroom management requirements of product-design students and instructors. The instructional model comprises six components: principles, objectives, steps, learner and teacher roles, learning materials, and evaluation. Five experts rated the model and lesson plans on five-point scales. All components were judged very appropriate (overall means = 4.52 and 4.60 respectively) and the intra-class correlation coefficients (ICCs) showed good inter-rater reliability (ICCs ≥ 0.76). After a small piloting (n=6), student showed a positive attitudes toward the learning process. Based on their feedback and recurring issues, the content, activities, assessment methods, and tools in each lesson were revised to better align with learners’ needs and time balancing. The findings offer a theoretically grounded and contextually relevant framework for creativity-oriented design education, providing actionable guidance for curriculum development and future empirical research in Chinese higher education.

title: Studyflow: Evidence-Informed Design and Prototyping of an AI-Assisted Academic Workload and Cognitive Support Platform for University Students Aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: University students, particularly those who also work or hold organizational roles, frequently experience academic overload, stress, and burnout. Existing digital tools tend to address either task management or well-being, rarely both, and many lose users within days. This study reports the evidence-informed design of StudyFlow, a mobile-first platform that helps students turn unstructured academic demands into a prioritized, actionable plan, and examines how its design aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A design science research approach was followed. A targeted narrative review of literature published from 2021 to 2026 on student stress, working students, digital well-being interventions, engagement, and gamification informed a proto-persona, eight use cases, and nine functional requirements. A high-fidelity interactive prototype was generated through a five-stage natural-language prompt sequence in Google Stitch and refined in Google AI Studio. The intended feature set was compared with four widely used productivity and well-being applications, and each feature group was mapped to SDG targets with measurable evaluation indicators. The review yielded seven design implications, each traced to specific requirements and interface decisions. title: Artefact use in design research around taboo
abstract: There has been an increase in scholarly work mentioning the use of artefacts as researcher-participant mediators in research around topics that might be perceived as a taboo. Simultaneously, there is a lack of guidance and evidence about the roles artefacts could play and the effects they could have in these contexts. Through desk research, a questionnaire to 34 design researchers, and 11 semi-structured interviews with design researchers with experience working around taboo topics, we have sought to understand how these artefacts are created and used in design research processes. Our research revealed which types of artefacts are created and the purposes for which they are used. We propose to look at artefacts in design research about taboo as mediators of distances between the people involved but also between people and taboo topic, sharing implications for design practice, design research, and design education.

title: Endophytic microbial platforms for sustainable production of plant-derived anticancer metabolites
abstract: Abstract Cancer continues to pose a major global health challenge, with increasing incidence and mortality worldwide. Although modern cancer therapies have advanced significantly, many clinically important anticancer drugs still originate from plant-derived secondary metabolites due to their structural diversity and potent bioactivity. Compounds such as Podophyllotoxin, Paclitaxel, Vincristine, and Camptothecin have transformed cancer treatment and serve as precursors for several clinically used therapeutics. However, their production relies largely on extraction from slow-growing and often overexploited medicinal plants such as Podophyllum hexandrum , Taxus brevifolia , Catharanthus roseus , and Camptotheca acuminata , making supply environmentally and economically unsustainable. Endophytic microorganisms have emerged as promising alternative biofactories for sustainable production of these high-value metabolites. Several fungal and bacterial endophytes, including species of Fusarium , Alternaria , Chaetomium , and Taxomyces andreanae , have been reported to produce anticancer compounds or stimulate their biosynthesis in host plants. title: Force and Power Testing in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Literature: A Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Background Force and power testing has been recognised as a key aspect of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) rehabilitation. However, a literature synthesis is required to examine how these physical characteristics have been assessed due to pronounced heterogeneity in the methods used. Objectives To synthesise and describe the existing literature on force and power testing post-ACLR. Methods A scoping review of the electronic databases MEDLINE (PubMed), SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library and PEDro was conducted including studies adopting at least one force or power test in patients post-ACLR. The search methodology followed the Joanna Briggs Institute Manual for evidence synthesis and included the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Results In total, 1625 studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Seven main device categories were identified, with different rates of implementation over the years (1981–2023) and throughout the recovery process: (1) isokinetic dynamometry (IKD; 64.9%), (2) jump (without force platform; 32.2%), (3) force platform (28.0%), (4) traditional gym equipment and bodyweight exercises (6.2%), (5) hand-held dynamometry (4.0%), (6) manual muscle testing (1.5%) and (7) other devices (5.5%). title: Phytosulfokine‐α Alleviates Chilling Injury in Peach Fruit by Activating PpbHLH93‐Mediated Energy Metabolism
abstract: ABSTRACT Peach fruit are highly susceptible to chilling injury (CI) during postharvest cold storage, which causes significant quality loss and reduces commercial value. Peach fruit were immersed in 200 nM phytosulfokine‐α (PSK‐α) and stored at 5°C for up to 28 d. PSK‐α alleviated CI, as shown by a lower internal browning index and better‐maintained respiratory activity; after 21 d at 5°C, the browning index was 60.5% lower than that of the control. Transcriptome profiling combined with gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that PSK‐α‐responsive genes were mainly enriched in energy‐metabolism pathways. PSK‐α also increased the activities and transcript levels of cytochrome c oxidase (CCO), succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), H + ‐ ATPase and Ca 2+ ‐ ATPase . PpbHLH93 was identified as a nucleus‐localized transcription factor responsive to PSK‐α. Dual‐luciferase assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays using unlabeled competitor and mutated E‐box probes showed that PpbHLH93 directly recognized E‐box elements in the promoters of PpCCO , PpSDH2 and PpH + ‐ ATPase and activated their transcription. Transient PpbHLH93 overexpression increased the transcript levels of these three genes, whereas silencing generally reduced them. These results support 200 nM PSK‐α as a potential postharvest treatment and show that PpbHLH93 regulates energy‐metabolism genes associated with chil…

title: Energy, Exergy and Exergoeconomic Analyses of Solar-Powered Cooling Systems for Data Centers
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of meeting the continuous cooling demands of data centers using an inherently intermittent solar-powered cooling system. To overcome weather dependency, the developed system integrates thermal energy storage with phase change materials to ensure a consistent thermal supply during non-solar hours. The proposed numerical model is validated against experimental data, demonstrating high reliability with a maximum relative error of less than 10% (a minor deviation of approximately 2°C). The system's performance is comprehensively evaluated through energy, exergy, and exergoeconomic analyses across three major Canadian cities: Vancouver, Toronto, and Montreal. The numerical results indicate that Montreal consistently exhibits the highest exergetic efficiency, reaching a maximum of 20.6%, although it incurs the highest overall cost. Conversely, Toronto proves to be the most economically viable location, achieving the lowest total cost rate of approximately 40.0 $/h. Furthermore, the thermodynamic evaluation demonstrates a highly favorable maximum coefficient of performance of 0.817 for the integrated system, depending on the selected operating temperatures.
venue: Transactions of the Canadian Society for Mechanical Engineering

title: Occupancy-Gated Fuzzy Logic Control for Energy-Efficient Air-Conditioning in Context-Aware Smart Homes
abstract: Air-conditioning is the largest single electrical load in many homes, and the on/off thermostats that still govern most units run at full power, cycle the compressor often, and keep cooling empty rooms. This study designs and evaluates a context-aware fuzzy logic controller that reads two signals, room temperature and occupancy, and sets air-conditioner power. A single room was modelled as a first-order thermal plant and controlled by Mamdani fuzzy inference system. An initial design, V1, treated occupancy as a soft influence and overcooled empty rooms. A corrected design, V2, writes occupancy into the rule base as a gate with an explicit off state, so an empty room drives cooling to zero. The controllers were re-implemented in Python and compared against an on/off thermostat and an occupancy-aware thermostat under a fixed 180-minute test, a 24 h day, and 300 randomised scenarios, with switching counted for every controller by one threshold-crossing metric. With the room occupied throughout the fixed test, V2 stayed in the comfort band 99.2 % of the time on 1.05 kWh against 1.13 kWh for the thermostat, without switching. On realistic days V2 cut mean daily energy by 18.5 %, but occupied comfort fell to 88.7 % on average against 97.1 % for the thermostat, a trade-off of about eight points, and V2 still restarted the compressor about five times a day against 129 for the thermosta…

title: Modulation of Quantum-Cutting Energy Transfer in Yb3+-Doped CsPbCl3 Thin Films through Precursor Composition
abstract: Abstract Yb3+-doped lead halide perovskites are promising quantum-cutting (QC) materials for near-infrared (NIR) wavelength conversion, yet the factors governing their excitation-density-dependent efficiency in thin films remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the precursor- and excitation-density-dependent QC photophysics of Yb3+-doped CsPbCl3 thin films. Despite a 5-fold increase in the Yb3+ precursor concentration, the incorporated Yb3+ content remains nearly constant at approximately 0.5 atom %, whereas the NIR emission efficiency increases substantially. Combined absolute photoluminescence quantum-yield and time-resolved measurements reveal that the host-to-Yb3+ QC energy-transfer efficiency increases from 57% to 69%, while the intrinsic Yb3+ emission efficiency remains nearly unchanged. The NIR quantum yield also increases markedly toward lower excitation densities, whereas the Yb3+ excited-state lifetime shows only minor variation. Power-dependent measurements reveal a transition from nearly linear to sublinear NIR emission with increasing excitation density, consistent with progressive saturation of QC-active sensitization pathways. Although the characteristic saturation threshold shows no clear dependence on precursor concentration, the degree of sublinearity at high excitation densities decreases systematically with increasing precursor concentration. …

title: Unsteady Jeffrey Fluid Flow, Heat and Mass Transfer Along a Stretching Cylinder with Arrhenius Activation Energy
abstract: In the present work, the unsteady flow, heat transfer and mass transfer of a Jeffrey fluid over a stretching cylinder has been formulated. There is a modified Arrhenius reaction in the concentration equation and the concentration reaction-heat contribution to the energy equation. The conservation laws are mapped to a coupled, 8th order boundary value problem which is integrated numerically with MATLAB code bvp4c and compared to 2 independent Newtonian benchmarks within 4×〖10〗^(-4). The next parameter sweep shows a clean separation of the parameters which influence the model, namely the skin-friction coefficient is only sensitive to the curvature, the unsteadiness and the two Jeffrey parameters, the momentum equation has no feedback on the thermal and concentration field, and the thermal and concentration field is sensitive to the other nine parameters. Of these, activation energy is the most influential, and is able to reduce the Sherwood number by nearly 25% of the range tested, whereas the Schmidt number is able to more than double the Sherwood number. The analysis reveals that the higher the curvature parameter and the Deborah number, the higher the rates of heat and mass transfer; however, the higher the ratio of relaxation-to-retardation time, the lower the rates of heat and mass transfer, and that this is a design parameter which a flat-plate treatment cannot offer.

title: Cd Vacancy‐Mediated Orbital Hybridization and Ultrafast Charge Separation in Pt Single‐Atom Photocatalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Zn x Cd 1−x S (ZCS) solid solutions are promising photocatalysts for H 2 evolution but suffer from rapid electron‐hole recombination. Density functional theory (DFT) predicts that Cd vacancies narrow the band gap and reduce the hole effective mass from 0.80 to 0.59 m 0 , suppressing bulk recombination. Guided by this, Cd vacancies (V C ) were introduced into ZCS as anchoring sites for Pt single atoms (Pt SA ), forming Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS. Aberration‑corrected high‐angle annular dark‐field scanning transmission electron microscopy and X‑ray absorption fine structure confirm atomic Pt dispersion. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy shows Cd vacancies localize photogenerated holes at defect states while Pt single atoms dominate ultrafast electron extraction (ca. 4.10 ps, 81.5% pre‐exponential weight). This vacancy‐mediated synergy switches the dominant carrier pathway from intrinsic interband recombination to spatial charge separation. DFT further shows that p–d hybridization optimizes hydrogen adsorption free energy to −0.11 eV and delocalizes electrons at adjacent sulfur sites. The optimal Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS achieves a H 2 evolution rate of 142.86 mmol g −1 h −1 under visible light, 16.8 times that of pristine ZCS, with an apparent quantum yield of 7.48% at 420 nm and >90% activity retention after cycling. This work reveals how cation vacancies and single atoms enhan…

title: CARD READER, VOTERS CONFIDENCE AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: A STUDY OF THE 2015 GENERAL ELECTIONS IN NIGERIA
abstract: Generally, the history of election in Nigeria have been characterized by so many electoral malpractices, challenges and problems thereby making such elections very unpopular. In line with this, many Nigerians builds impression that electoral malpractice cannot be eradicated in the country. These maladies usually occur as a result of government negligence in the implementation of its good policies into reality. This has paved the way for the elected offices to continue in power which intentionally create difficulties to the incumbent parties. While to others, they view it from the aspect of politicians who threatens the electoral officials to perpetrate so many illegalities during election period to manipulate the results. It is against this background that many policies were been executed by different governments with respect to the electoral bodies yet the situation remain as it is with so many irregularities. Nevertheless, the introduction of electronic machine (card reader) in the election process has proven a success in reducing so many malpractices at the election venues. This change has generally increased the level of public confidence and turnout. Hence, electorates now can have the feelings that they will participate without fear of their votes. This paper therefore intends to emphasize the use of voter's card reader in the forthcoming elections. Moreover, the paper ad…

title: Physical Stability and Carotenoid Retention of a Pasteurized Red Palm Oil Emulsion Beverage during Storage
abstract: Red palm oil (RPO) is a rich natural source of carotenoids (500–700 ppm) and is a promising ingredient in functional beverages to increase provitamin A intake and support the prevention of vitamin A deficiency. Thermal pasteurization and storage may affect emulsion stability and carotenoid retention, which are critical for product quality and nutritional efficacy of functional beverages. This study aimed to examine the effects of pasteurization and storage on the physical stability and carotenoid preservation of RPO emulsion beverages. The emulsion was formulated using 10% (w/w) of RPO and 4% (w/w) of whey protein concentrate (WPC) as an emulsifier, followed by rotor-stator homogenization. Pasteurization was performed by a batch thermal process at 65 °C for 30 min. The product was stored for 21 days at room temperature (±25 °C) and refrigerator (13±3 °C). The pasteurized RPO emulsion beverage exhibited particle size (D90) of 13.888±0.740 µm, zeta potential values between (−17) and (−14) mV, and carotenoid content of 30.6244±2.3689 mg/kg. The pasteurization increased viscosity by 2.6-fold and centrifugal creaming index by 22.82%, while oil globule morphology remained structurally intact. During storage, the emulsion beverage maintained good physical stability at both storage temperatures, with particle size (D90) of 13–16 µm and zeta potential values between (−15) and (−11) mV. …

title: Zein–zinc oxide nanofibrous coating containing a cumin essential oil pickering emulsion: effects on the quality of Kurdish cheese during refrigerated storage

Ion Transport in Block Copolymer Battery Electrolytes Predicted by Large-Scale Simulations
abstract: Abstract This work addresses the ion conductivity of lamellar poly(ethylene oxide)-polystyrene (PEO–PS) block copolymers with added LiTFSI using a Single-Chain-in-Mean-Field (SCMF) approach that combines a particle-based description of the polymer degrees of freedom and a field-based diffusion equation for the ion fluxes. This highly efficient simulation methodology allows addressing microscale systems (lateral dimensions ∼ 0.2–1 μm) and thus captures the presence of multiple grains in the material. Our model allows the calculation of the conductivity of the block copolymer normalized by that of pure PEO, κn, which was measured in previous experiments. We show that the effective Flory–Huggins parameter, χeff, which incorporates the effect of salt content on the Flory–Huggins parameter, is a good predictor of κn in samples prepared using the same (simulated or experimental) annealing protocol. κn is predicted to decrease with increasing grain size, in agreement with experiments. This effect is explained in terms of a highly heterogeneous distribution and nonoptimal orientations of the local ion currents in materials with large grain sizes. However, the magnitude of the effect is shown to be more important for thin block copolymer films than for bulk materials, which indicates an important dimensionality effect. In the case of bulk PEO–PS electrolytes, simulation predictions only…

title: High Charge Storage and Tissue-Matching Mechanics in PEDOT:PSS Hydrogels Achieved by Competitive Acrylic Acid Treatment
abstract: Abstract Conductive hydrogels hold considerable promise for applications in bioelectronics. Among conductive polymers, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) hydrogels stand out for their good electronic properties and biocompatibility. However, simultaneously optimizing electrical transport, mechanical reinforcement, and biocompatibility remains challenging. Herein, we reported a simple and scalable preparation method for PEDOT:PSS hydrogel reinforcement. This method permits precise performance modulation simply by controlling the acrylic acid (AA) concentration gradient during soaking, without the need for complex equipment or harsh conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to elucidate the underlying molecular interactions. Mechanistically, competitive interactions between AA and PEDOT:PSS complexes progressively displace PSS chains and promote the ordered rearrangement of PEDOT chains, resulting in a continuous and dense conductive network. Meanwhile, the construction of a synergistic secondary network within the gel pores yields a high conductivity. Its compressive modulus can be tuned over a wide range, substantially improving the compressive load-bearing capacity of the pristine hydrogel. The hydrogel exhibits a cathodal charge storage capacity (CSC) as high as 630.24 mC/cm2 and extremely low interfacial impedance, demonstrati…

The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

title: CFD-guided aerodynamic redesign of an electric bus for lower drag and energy demand
abstract: Abstract Electric buses face range and battery-temperature limits, and aerodynamic drag is a major part of their energy demand at higher speeds. This study examines how three features of an electric bus, the windshield inclination, the ground clearance and the roof transition angle, affect its aerodynamics, using steady computational fluid dynamics simulations of a 1:10 model of the BYD K9. Each feature was varied in turn, and the final combined design was simulated directly. Grid convergence was confirmed on four meshes, and the normalized flow fields did not depend on Reynolds number over the simulated range. Inclining the windshield to 27° reduced the drag coefficient by 5.7%. Raising the ground clearance from 370 to 430 mm reduced it by a further 2.3%, while lowering the estimated underbody convective heat transfer by 1.2%. A 45° roof transition gave the largest single reduction and brought lift close to neutral. The final design lowered the drag coefficient from 0.603 to 0.501, a 16.9% reduction, which cuts the aerodynamic energy demand at 100 km/h from 0.70 to 0.58 kWh/km. The results come from steady, zero-yaw simulations without experimental validation.

title: PDE-Based Thermo-Electric Analysis and Optimization of a Bimetallic (Cu/St) 630 〖mm〗^2 Conductor for 1000 MW / 500 kV Power Transmission Tropical Environments
abstract: This paper validates the technical compliance of a stranded bimetallic (copper core, steel casing) with a cross-section of 630 mm^2 for transmitting 1000 MW of power at a voltage of 500 kV. Using Partial Differential Equation (PDE) modeling solved in MATLAB, the thermal behavior is analyzed by considering the zenithal solar radiation of the DRC, the Joule effect, the corona effect, and voltage drop. Simulations demonstrate that a 630 mm^2 section stabilizes the steady-state temperature at a safe threshold of 64.2°C, thereby preventing copper annealing and guaranteeing the long-term operational sustainability of the line.

title: Global sensitivity analysis of parameters for medium and low-speed maglev vehicle-bridge coupling system based on an improved Sobol method
abstract: To identify the key parameters of a medium and low-speed maglev vehicle–bridge coupling system, a quantitative parameter sensitivity analysis is essential. To address the heterogeneous parameter dimensions, the difficulty of globally evaluating time-varying responses, and the prohibitive cost of applying the Sobol method directly to the coupling model, this paper proposes an improved Sobol global sensitivity analysis method integrating an error integral performance indicator with a Levenberg–Marquardt Back-Propagation (LMBP) neural network surrogate. The time-varying suspension-gap response is first scalarized by the error integral indicator, which eliminates dimensional differences among the parameters and condenses the global dynamic behaviour. The surrogate then establishes the mapping from the system parameters to the indicator, avoiding repeated time-consuming simulations of the original model. Based on the surrogate, Sobol-sequence sampling is performed and the parameter sensitivities are computed, revealing the interaction mechanisms of the parameters on the dynamic behaviour and providing a theoretical basis for engineering parameter optimization.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Talking AI, doing less? Economic policy uncertainty and AI strategy-implementation misalignment
Urban Districts as an Economic Development Strategy: The Potential of Cell Phone Data for Evaluation
abstract: Since urban agglomeration theory suggests that districts can stimulate local economic growth, economic development practitioners often designate innovation, cultural, and downtown districts. However, despite a significant number of studies, many in Economic Development Quarterly , empirical evidence on effectiveness remains limited due to data constraints and challenges in identifying causal impacts. This commentary examines whether location-based services (cell phone) data can improve evaluation of district designation by tracking activity patterns within district boundaries over time. Recent post-pandemic recovery studies indicate that while downtown districts have lagged in returning to pre-pandemic activity levels, neighborhood districts have performed more strongly. These findings highlight both the promise and limits of activity-based indicators. Although cell phone data alone cannot determine whether districts generate net new jobs or businesses, combining it with employment, firm creation, and survey data offers a powerful framework for assessing whether district-based economic development policies influence metropolitan spatial activity patterns and growth outcomes.

title: Retail Consolidation in Pakistan: Channel Strategy Dilemma at Sitarah Consumer Products Ltd.
abstract: This teaching case explored the strategic dilemma faced by Sitarah Consumer Products Ltd., a fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company in Pakistan, as it confronted growing pressure from modern retail chains, particularly Imtiaz Stores, and the resulting channel conflict. Set in 2023, the case followed Adeel Khan, national sales manager, as he considered Imtiaz Stores’ demand for a 28% margin on Sitarah’s flagship shampoo line. The case outlined the evolution of Pakistan’s retail landscape across three stages and highlighted tensions among the company’s sales, finance and brand functions. It enabled students to assess the trade-offs between maintaining distributor loyalty and responding to retail consolidation by examining sales volumes, margins and channel dynamics.

title: High-Performance Strain-Sensing Fibers via a Multidimensional Percolation Network Strategy for Intelligent Speech System
abstract: Abstract Flexible strain sensors often face trade-offs among sensitivity, sensing range, resolution, and stability under deformation. Here, we report a multidimensional percolation strategy for high-performance strain-sensing fibers by integrating 0D Ag microparticles, 1D carbon nanotubes, and 2D carbon sheets into a ternary conductive network through wet spinning. The fibers exhibit a maximum gauge factor of 4640.1, a sensing range up to 65%, and a strain resolution of 0.025%, which is retained under 20% prestrain. Their microstrain sensitivity enables the detection of mechanical signals associated with magnetic microrobot locomotion and the identification of bionic insect model movements using a biomimetic spider-web network. Coupling the fibers with deep learning yields 98.7% recognition accuracy across 21 spoken-word classes. Integration with virtual reality further demonstrates a speech-driven interface in which recognized speech triggers predefined virtual-character responses. These results provide a route toward high-performance fiber sensors for intelligent human–machine interaction.

title: “I TAKE CARE OF MY BODY” MEDIA: AN AUDIOVISUAL-BASED REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH EDUCATION STRATEGY FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS
abstract: Children with special needs are vulnerable to sexual violence because they may struggle to understand body boundaries, distinguish safe from unsafe touch, and report uncomfortable experiences. This study analyzed short-term changes in reproductive health and self-protection knowledge among children with special needs before and after education using the “I Take Care of My Body” audiovisual media, rather than testing its effectiveness. A pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design without a control group was applied at Amal Mulia Special School, Bengkulu City, from August to September 2026, with 57 students aged 10–18 years recruited through total sampling. Knowledge was measured with a picture-based questionnaire before and after 2–4 sessions, categorized as poor (1), moderate (2), or good (3), and analyzed with a paired-samples t-test. Poor knowledge fell from 71.9% to 47.4%, moderate rose from 24.6% to 40.4%, and good from 3.5% to 12.3%. The mean category score rose from 1.32 to 1.65 (difference 0.33; 95% CI 0.20–0.47; p<0.001; Cohen’s d=0.65). These findings describe a short-term improvement accompanying the sessions, not evidence of effectiveness; controlled trials that also measure self-protection behavior are needed.

title: ВЗАИМОСВЯЗЬ ИМПУЛЬСИВНОСТИ С ВЫБОРОМ КОПИНГ-СТРАТЕГИЙ ПОДРОСТКАМИ В СИТУАЦИИ ПРЕДЭКЗАМЕНАЦИОННОГО СТРЕССА
abstract: Актуальность исследования обусловлена значимостью подросткового возраста как периода индивидуализации, формирования Я-концепции, осознанных представлений о своем будущем, выработке стратегий поведения в жизненно важных ситуациях, связанных с первичным самоопределением личности. Цель: выявление и анализ связи выбора копинг-стратегий с импульсивностью у подростков, разработка рекомендаций по организации психологического сопровождения подростков в ситуации предэкзаменационного стресса. Гипотеза: существует связь между показателем импульсивности и предпочтением определенных копинг-стратегий у подростков в ситуации предэкзаменационного стресса: 1) чем больше выражена импульсивность, тем подростки чаще выбирают непродуктивные копинг-стратегии; 2) чем меньше выражена импульсивность, тем подростки чаще выбирают продуктивные стратегии; 3) психологическая готовность к ОГЭ влияет на связь импульсивности и выбора копинг-стратегий. Участники: 41 учащийся девятых классов общеобразовательной школы г. Москвы в возрасте 14–16 лет. title: IMPLEMENTATION OF BUKITTINGGI MAYOR’S DECREE NUMBER 188.45-210-2023 REGARDING “BALING BAMBU,” A STRATEGY FOR ACCELERATING REGIONAL POVERTY ALLEVIATION IN 2023
abstract: This study aims to analyse the implementation of the Baling Bambu Program as a strategy for povertyalleviation in Bukittinggi City. The primary focus is on the execution of the policy by implementing actors,namely the Bukittinggi City Social Affairs Office, BPRS Jam Gadang, BAZNAS Bukittinggi City, LKKSBukittinggi City and Pioneer Families, who contribute to the program’s success. This research employsthe policy implementation theory proposed by Daniel Mazmanian and Paul A. Sabatier as the analyticalframework, which emphasizes three key variables : (1) the tractability of the problem being addressed,(2) the ability of the policy to establish an effective implementation process, and (3) external factorsinfluencing implementation. The method used is descriptive qualitative, with data collected through indepth interviews and documentation. The findings reveal that the involvement of implementing actorssignificantly affects the success of the programs., particularly through clear commitments based on MoUand SOP, along with strong public support for the continuation of the Baling Bambu Program’s. However,the implementation process still faces several obstacles, including weak coordination between thegovernment and stakeholders, unclear empowerment mechanisms for Pioneer Families, inaccuratebeneficiary data, inconsistencies between policy content and actual field practices, limited f…

title: Dual foraging trip strategy in short-tailed shearwaters: spatial and temporal variation in foraging effort
abstract: Abstract Background In marine environments, resource availability for predators strongly varies spatially and temporarily. For central place foragers, such as seabirds, the need to return to the breeding site affects their ability to respond to this spatiotemporal variation. However, to respond to this variation, most procellariid seabirds employ a dual foraging strategy, alternating between short local trips for chick provisioning and long distant trips for self-maintenance. Short-tailed shearwaters ( Ardenna tenuirostris ) forage locally in southern Australia and on long distant trips in Antarctic waters. However, little is known of the spatiotemporal variation in their foraging behaviour on short and long trips. Methods In the present study, GPS and dive behaviour loggers were deployed on chick-rearing individuals across three breeding colonies in south-eastern Australia to quantify spatial and temporal variation in foraging effort and diving behaviour during both long and short trips. Results Key foraging hotspots were identified near the breeding colonies, around the Polar Front, and along the edge of the sea-ice. Dives during long trips were longer, deeper and more frequent than during short trips, and dive foraging effort increased compared to short trips. Conclusion Increased foraging effort and diving activity on long trips is likely a result of both high prey availabi…

title: Optimizing additive and subtractive hybrid manufacturing strategy for GH3536 turbine blade
Poly Aryl Ether Sulfone Films Covalently Grafted with Two Pyridine-Based Donor–Acceptor Chromophores for Optical Power Limiting
abstract: Abstract Practical solid-state organic optical limiting (OL) devices are constrained by their reliance on physical doping into polymer matrices, which often leads to microphase separation and compromised performance uniformity. Herein, a covalent quaternization anchoring strategy is reported to graft two pyridine-based donor–acceptor (D–A) chromophores, bearing dimethylaminophenyl and diphenylaminophenyl donors, respectively, onto poly aryl ether sulfone (PAES) side chains. The resulting polymer films, fabricated by solution casting, exhibit excellent transparency, thermal stability, and uniformity. Femtosecond Z-scan at 532 nm supports two-photon absorption (TPA) in both films, with PAES(HC) showing an apparent cross-section three times that of PAES(TPAHC). Nanosecond Z-scan measurements reveal strong nonlinear absorption (NLA) in both films. PAES(HC) exhibits a stronger initial TPA response followed by short-lived excited-state absorption (ESA), whereas PAES(TPAHC) undergoes longer-lived ESA initiated by weak one- or two-photon absorption. The PAES(HC) film demonstrates superior NLA and OL performance, with an effective NLA coefficient β of 707.41 cm GW–1. This covalent grafting strategy for fabricating nonlinear optical solid-state films provides insights into the structure–property design of organic molecules and promotes their practical applications in the OL field.

title: A 2012–2024 energy-carbon input-output dataset with new power-system detail and integrated energy-flow accounts for China
abstract: Abstract China’s energy transition is reshaping the power system and energy flows across production, transformation and consumption. Yet existing input-output data rarely distinguish storage activities within the new power system while maintaining linked accounts across these stages. Here, we present an energy-carbon input-output dataset for China covering 2012–2024. The benchmark tables for 2012, 2017 and 2023 contain 167, 177 and 235 sectors, respectively, including 35 energy subsectors. They distinguish power-generation technologies, transmission and distribution, pumped-hydro storage, generation-, grid- and user-side storage, and fossil energy extraction, processing and supply. The dataset links monetary input-output flows to integrated energy-flow accounts for 43 energy products across production, transformation and consumption, and to stage-specific CO 2 emissions accounts. Machine-learning-based annual extension yields a harmonised 177-sector series for 2012–2024. The dataset supports analyses of new power-system development, storage deployment and changes in the generation mix, as well as economy-wide energy-flow tracing and climate policy assessment.

title: The Rhetorical Power of Political Slogans: Perceived Influence on Public Opinion and Governance
abstract: Political slogans shorten political identities, policy statements and emotional appeals through a condensing process so that they can be easily recognized and repeated. This study investigates the perception of the audiences about the impact of slogans on public opinion, political judgment and political governance. Two hundred and eight respondents participated in an on-line, cross-sectional, quantitative survey with a structured questionnaire comprising of 15 closed-ended questions. Descriptive percentages were used as the sample is very small and cannot be generalized to the population level as this is a non-probability sample. Results show good perceived effects. The percentage of respondents who said that slogans impact the perceptions about the government policy was around three quarters, whereas 85.7% said that slogans impact the assessment of the effectiveness and trustworthiness of the government. 75.0% thought that emotional language had a greater influence than neutral language, and 92.8% said that the emotional impact had partial or full significance when assessing the impact of slogans. The media, amplification and historical context were also considered significant. Meanwhile, 92.1% agreed that slogans can be too simple to formulate complex political issues and can lead to misleading the public. The findings thus suggest that slogans are ambivalent democratic tools…

Arthrogram findings of displaced annular ligament in paediatric Monteggia injuries: Introducing the “Rose Thorn” sign of the elbow
abstract: Purpose In paediatric Monteggia injuries, persistent radial head instability despite anatomic ulnar reduction creates a difficult intra-operative dilemma. A displaced annular ligament has been described as a potential cause, but no reliable intra-operative test has been reported. We describe a novel arthrographic finding, the “Rose Thorn” sign of the Elbow, which correlates with annular ligament displacement and ongoing radial head instability. Methods Skeletally immature patients with acute Monteggia injuries who underwent intra-operative arthrography at a tertiary paediatric centre over 12 months were included. Arthrograms were assessed for a characteristic wedge-shaped anterior contrast defect within the radiocapitellar space and subsequently correlated with intra-operative findings at open reduction. Elbows without the arthrographic sign served as controls. Results Thirteen patients met inclusion criteria. Six demonstrated a positive Rose Thorn sign following ulnar reduction. All six had persistent anterior radial head instability and were found to have an interposed annular ligament at open reduction. Reduction of the annular ligament resolved the Rose Thorn sign and restored radiocapitellar alignment and stability. Patients without the sign had no residual radiocapitellar instability. Conclusion The Rose Thorn sign is an indicator of annular ligament displacement. We prop…

title: Sustainability in Charity Retail: Conflicts in (In)Sufficiency
abstract: Abstract Sufficiency has been receiving attention as a means to achieve sustainability. Insights on how to operationalise sufficiency in practice are limited and absent in the context of ecologically constrained organisations, such as, charities. Charities are viewed as critical to sustainability due to their reuse business model; however, charity income is dropping due to the saturation of low-quality and value clothing donations generated by ever-increasing production and consumption of (ultra)fast fashion. This is placing resource (e.g. reliance on volunteer labour) and ecological (e.g. finding reuse routes) burdens on an already constrained sector, highlighting the urgency for charities to future proof the retail businesses foundational to their fundraising efforts. To address this challenge, this research adopts an ethic of sufficiency to introduce business model innovation to charity retail. Drawing on interviews and observations with charity staff, collaborating experts and consumers as donor and retail users, we examine transition to a clothing rental model offering social and ecological sufficiency. We find that the two competing ethics of: (1) sufficiency representing enough and driving deceleration and (2) insufficiency representing not enough and driving acceleration, compete for primacy. While sufficiency can counter challenges arising from insufficiency, competiti…

When Shared Demand Data Softens Competition in Hospitality Pricing
abstract: Hotels and other capacity-constrained service firms increasingly rely on revenue management systems and benchmarking platforms that incorporate forward-looking demand information, including bookings on hand and occupancy forecasts. These metrics improve forecasting, but when they are pooled across competitors they may also change pricing incentives. We develop a stylized duopoly model to show when shared demand information affects equilibrium prices. Our model has an uncertain market size (either low or high) where customers choose between the two firms and an outside option based on prices. Without information sharing, each firm sets a single price knowing only the distribution of market size. With sharing, a common signal reveals whether market size is low or high before prices are set, allowing firms to condition prices on the demand state. When capacity is slack, shared information has little effect as firms price at the same unconstrained benchmark. When capacity binds in both states and the no-sharing price clears capacity in the low state, sharing raises expected revenue by allowing a higher scarcity price when demand is strong. In the mixed case, where capacity binds only in the high state sharing can increase or reduce expected revenue. Any high-demand scarcity gain must be weighed against the low-demand pricing effect, since under certain conditions the no-sharing equ…

Relationship Between the Professional Learning Community (PLC) Practices and the Development of Elementary Public School Teachers' Collaborative Skills
abstract: This study examined the relationship between Professional Learning Community (PLC) practices and the development of collaborative skills among Grade 6 teachers in selected public elementary schools in District 6, Manila, as a basis for proposing a PLC model. Using a quantitative correlational design, data were collected from 100 purposively selected teachers across ten schools through a validated, researcher-developed questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation. PLC practices were manifested to a very great extent (M = 3.65), with Observational Learning and Modeling receiving the highest rating (M = 3.73). Teachers strongly agreed with the perceived development of their collaborative skills (M = 3.65), particularly Professional Dialogue and Reflective Practice (M = 3.68). All 25 examined relationships were positive and statistically significant (r = 0.634–0.798, p < 0.001), indicating that stronger assessments of PLC practices were associated with higher assessments of collaborative skills. The findings support the relevance of collaborative professional learning without establishing causality. Schools should sustain peer observation, strengthen collaborative planning and structured professional support, and pilot the proposed PLC model. The study's purposive sampling, self-reported measures, and single-district correlational design limit gen…

The arc of uncertainty across clinicians’ interactions with AI
abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used in various clinical settings to support clinical reasoning and decision-making. Although they have demonstrated strong performance on medical knowledge and reasoning tasks, and early studies suggest potential to reduce medical errors, emerging evidence also highlights important safety concerns, including clinically significant management errors in outputs that may not be readily apparent to users. How these tools can be integrated into clinical practice to consistently lead to improved patient outcomes remains an open question. AI-assisted reasoning unfolds across a sequence of decisions: whether to use AI for the clinical question, how to engage with the tool, how to interpret its output, and whether to act. Each stage in this sequence introduces distinct risks, including inappropriate tool selection, incomplete or biased inputs, overconfidence in fluent responses, and failure to recognize error or appreciate nuance. These risks are further shaped by the same clinician factors that generally affect clinical reasoning such as experience, workload, and uncertainty management. Viewing the AI-clinician interaction as a process rather than a single moment highlights several key points of vulnerability but also opportunities for training. Ultimately, the safe use of AI may depend less on the quality of the model and m…

title: Integrated optimization of the inventory routing problem under logistics collaboration and heterogeneous customer segments
abstract: Abstract Collaborative supply chain management is essential for businesses seeking to stay competitive and enhance operational effectiveness. Customer segmentation also stands out as an essential strategy in supply chain management, providing substantial advantages. Companies can improve customer satisfaction and loyalty by providing customized services that meet the unique preferences and needs of different groups of customers. This study introduces a mathematical model for the inventory routing problem, considering demand uncertainty, heterogeneous customer segments, and their collaborative efforts. The main decisions are centered on optimizing channel selection, distribution planning, and inventory replenishment strategies of customers classified into different segments. To efficiently solve large‐scale instances of the proposed problem, two complementary heuristic solution approaches are developed: a matheuristic with local branching and a mixed‐integer programming–based heuristic that serves as a benchmark for comparison. These approaches are designed to balance solution quality and computational efficiency while capturing the complex interactions between routing, inventory, and collaboration decisions. The results of the study highlight the strategic importance of heterogeneous customer segments and collaboration in inventory routing problems. The study provides a detaile…
