Alliance Ties, Structural Barriers, and Unrealized Export Potential in the Global Trade of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Four-Component Stochastic Frontier Gravity Analysis
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are commercially produced goods whose transfer is rationed by alliance politics and export controls, and conventional gravity models can measure neither the trade foregone relative to potential nor whether barriers are durable or transitory. Using bilateral flows for Harmonized System subheadings 880220 and 880230, we assemble 13,132 directed-dyad-year observations over 2012–2021 and estimate the four-component stochastic frontier model of Kumbhakar et al. (2014), which separates persistent inefficiency, transient inefficiency, pair heterogeneity, and noise. The average country pair realizes only about one-fifth of its UAV export potential (mean overall efficiency = 0.202). Because persistent efficiency (0.504) exceeds transient efficiency (0.401), the binding constraint operates on the year-to-year margin. At the same time, joint NATO membership is associated with substantially lower persistent inefficiency (−2.321, p < 0.001), a pattern that also appears in a single-step Battese and Coelli (1995) re-estimation. Geographic distance shows no statistically significant relationship with efficiency in the estimated model, a common language is associated with higher efficiency, and common colonial ties with lower efficiency. These associations suggest that UAV trade follows institutional and geopolitical lines more than geographic ones, which bear…

title: MBS Core Shell Optimization and Alpha SAN Modification for Improved Mechanical and Thermal Properties of PVC Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Balancing impact toughness and heat resistance remains a challenge for rigid poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC), because rubber toughening often reduces thermal performance. Here, methyl methacrylate‐butadiene‐styrene (MBS) core‐shell particles are synthesized by emulsion graft polymerization and used to toughen PVC. Increasing MBS content induces a pronounced brittle‐to‐ductile transition, and 12 wt% MBS increases the impact strength from 3.17 to 91.5 kJ/m 2 . Although 14 wt% MBS produced a higher impact strength, 12 wt% was selected for subsequent structural optimization as a compromise with yield‐strength retention. An St/MMA mass ratio of 6/4 and a PB core/shell mass ratio of 6/4 provided favorable mechanical performance, with an impact strength of 102.4 kJ/m 2 . Subsequent addition of SAN or α‐SAN increased HDT and VST but reduced impact strength. Compared with SAN, α‐SAN provided better impact‐strength retention at equivalent loadings. At 20 wt% α‐SAN, the composite exhibited an impact strength of 12.7 kJ/m 2 , an HDT of 74.7°C, and a VST of 88.8°C. DMA results were consistent with a reduced phase‐separation tendency in the α‐SAN‐containing composites, although complete thermodynamic miscibility could not be established. These findings provide comparative insights into the relationships between MBS architecture, heat‐resistant modifier structure, and the mechanical and t…

title: Reliability Modeling and Closed-Loop Optimization of a Non-Contact Profile Detection System Using Fuzzy AHP and Grey Relational Analysis
abstract: Limited failure data and uncertain expert judgments complicate reliability allocation and prediction during preliminary design. This study develops a closed-loop framework for a non-contact profile detection system for axisymmetric thin-shell workpieces. Five functional subsystems are modeled using a series reliability block diagram and fault tree analysis. A two-level comprehensive factor model with fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (AHP) allocates failure-rate targets, while similar-product prediction integrating ordered weighted averaging (OWA), intuitionistic trapezoidal fuzzy numbers, and grey relational analysis (GRA) corrects historical rates. Comparison identifies the optical measurement and numerical-control rotary table subsystems as having the smallest reliability margins. Under the benchmark scenario, optical power control, dual-camera redundancy, sealing, thermal management, and dual-grating redundancy reduce the predicted baseline system failure rate from 775.007 × 10-6 h-1 to 650.031 × 10-6 h-1 and increase mean time between failures (MTBF) from 1290.3 to 1538.4 h. Sensitivity scenarios yield MTBFs of 1421.5–1676.3 h; For the same increment in subsystem failure-rate reduction fractions, the sensitivity of the system failure rate to S4 improvement is approximately 2.08 times that to S3 improvement. The framework supports allocation, prediction, redistribution, and …

title: Teachers’ Perceived Readiness for the Career Progression System (ECPS) in the Public Elementary Schools: A Basis for the Expanded Career Progression Development Program
abstract: This study assessed public elementary school teachers’ perceived readiness for the Expanded Career Progression System (ECPS) and identified priorities for a proposed career development program. A descriptive-comparative design was employed among 150 purposively selected Teacher I–III personnel from selected schools in District 4, Schools Division Office of Manila. Data were obtained through a validated 25-item, four-point questionnaire and supplementary semi-structured interviews, then analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, analysis of variance, and thematic analysis. Respondents reported very high overall readiness (M = 3.40, SD = 0.61), with training and professional development highest (M = 3.58) and experience and length of service lowest (M = 3.28). Significant differences in readiness were found according to age, educational attainment, and teaching experience, but not sex or Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers career stage. The principal challenges involved extensive documentation, limited preparation time, competing workloads, and restricted promotion opportunities. Thus, favorable self-assessments did not eliminate procedural and institutional barriers to career advancement. The proposed Expanded Career Advancement and Readiness Enhancement (ECARE) Program should prioritize eligibility guidance, service-record verification, portfolio preparation, me…

title: An integrated multimodal neural network framework for early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment combining genomic, neuroimaging, and behavioral modalities
abstract: Abstract In the field of biomedical informatics and the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, the swift and precise detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and its early stage, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), presents a considerable obstacle in precision medicine. Traditional diagnostic techniques generally rely on singular data sources, thus failing to adequately capture the complex biological and behavioral interrelations that influence disease advancement. This study presents a novel multimodal deep learning architecture designed to amalgamate genetic information, neuroimaging techniques, and behavioral assessments to improve early detection proficiency. The suggested framework consists of three simultaneous analytical pathways: a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) designed for the extraction of morphological characteristics from MRI data, a densely interconnected neural network focused on the analysis of genetic variants, and a non-diagnostic longitudinal assessment of behavioral trajectories and cognitive measurements. To efficiently integrate these diverse data streams, an attention-driven adaptive modality gating mechanism is utilized, which dynamically adjusts the impact of each modality. Validation employing harmonized multimodal data from ADNI and UK Biobank demonstrates that the integrated multimodal model exceeds unimodal alternatives regarding predi…

title: Digital TVET transformation and youth workforce readiness in Ghana: a conceptual framework for an integrated skills information architecture
abstract: Abstract Ghana’s youth labour market shows a persistent gap between the competencies produced by education and training and those employers demand. Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) should narrow this gap but is constrained by fragmented information systems, an incompletely harmonised qualifications landscape, uneven digital capacity and weak incentives to act on labour-market intelligence. This conceptual paper aims to develop a framework for digitally transforming Ghana’s TVET system to strengthen alignment between skills provision and youth workforce readiness. An integrative review of 57 peer-reviewed, policy, institutional and statutory sources was undertaken, with grey literature appraised using the AACODS checklist and findings synthesised thematically through an evidence-to-framework matrix. Human capital, signalling, public-sector dynamic capabilities and socio-technical systems perspectives informed the analysis. Findings indicate that Ghana already has key building blocks (a Labour Market Information System, a planned TVET Management Information System, a National TVET Qualifications Framework and the Ghana Card), but these are unlinked and separately governed. The synthesis also suggests that better information is necessary but not sufficient: alignment is likely only where interoperability, decision rights and accountability incentives coexist.…

title: Adaptive stabilization of strict-feedback nonlinear systems using the fully actuated system approach and neural network approximation
abstract: This paper studies the adaptive stabilization of a class of strict-feedback systems (SFSs) with unknown nonlinearities and bounded matched disturbances. Using the fully actuated system (FAS) approach, the strict-feedback system is transformed into a high-order form with a single lumped unknown nonlinear term and a bounded disturbance, which leads to a more compact controller design. An Radial basis function (RBF) neural network (NN) is used to approximate the lumped unknown nonlinearity online, while a smooth robust term is introduced to compensate for the approximation error and the external disturbance. An adaptive controller is then developed based on this formulation. Lyapunov analysis shows that the transformed state and the neural network weight-estimation error are uniformly ultimately bounded. The original system states ultimately enter and remain within a neighborhood of the origin, while the neural network weight estimate and the control input remain bounded. The proposed method is further compared with an adaptive RBF neural network backstepping controller in a numerical example and an resistor-inductor-capacitor (RLC) circuit. In both cases, the proposed method achieves lower root-mean-square error, steady-state root-mean-square error, and control effort.

title: AMORe: An Agnostic Multi-Objective Framework for Recommendation
abstract: Recommender systems increasingly need to balance relevance with beyond-accuracy objectives, including fairness and long-tail exposure. Existing multi-objective approaches often rely on objective-specific loss designs, which limit reuse when target metrics or their numerical scales change. We propose AMORe , a scale-aware framework for optimizing multiple decomposable top- \( k \) recommendation objectives within gradient-based recommender training. AMORe combines differentiable ranking approximators with a lightweight top- \( k \) smoothing component and a unified loss that minimizes normalized deviations from user-specified utopia points. Experiments on four public datasets and three recommendation backbones show that AMORe exposes controllable tradeoffs between relevance and beyond-accuracy objectives, with improvements in beyond-accuracy metrics over corresponding vanilla backbones in most evaluated settings. Comparisons with representative fairness-aware baselines, together with ablation and efficiency analyses, clarify when AMORe improves tradeoff stability and quantify the computational overhead introduced by multi-objective training. We release code and datasets at: https://github.com/vincpapa/Agnostic-Multi-Objective-Recommendation .

title: Integrative Multi-omics Approaches for Characterizing Antibiotic Resistance Mechanisms in Bacterial Pathogens: Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AMR) is no longer merely a genetic characteristic but a complex dynamic phenotype arising from interacting molecular networks. Conventional diagnostic methods such as minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) test, PCR or even Whole-Genome Sequencing (WGS) have a limited understanding of resistance since they regard it as stable and unable to portray occurrence of phenomena like hetero-resistance, persistence and dissociation between genotype and phenotype. This review will highlight how integrative multi-omics (genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and metagenomics) is in a position to overcome these shortcomings by advancing the course of events starting from static gene catalogs to dynamic molecular networks. It also presents the idea of how integrative multi-omics can be employed to understand the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in bacterial infections, with a focus on the existing issues and possible perspectives. This review derives from an elaborate literature analysis performed on online resources such as PubMed, Google Scholar, and Web of Science. This review highlights multi-omics approaches as suitable tools to counteract antibiotic resistance, illustrating the transition from static gene catalogs to dynamic molecular networks. Further, it addresses urgent issues in the field and considers possible advances in this context. The …

Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivota…

title: Beyond Community Welfare: The Moderating Role of Institutions in Sustainable Slum Management in Bengkalis, Indonesia
abstract: Sustainable slum management requires an integrated approach that considers community welfare and institutional support. However, the extent to which institutional factors strengthen the relationship between community quality of life and sustainable slum management remains insufficiently clarified in the context of local settlement governance. This study examines the moderating role of institutional factors in the relationship between community quality of life and sustainable slum management in Bengkalis Regency, Riau, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory design was employed using questionnaire data collected from 86 household heads residing in designated slum areas across 21 villages. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that community quality of life is positively associated with sustainable slum management (β = 0.269, t = 3.142, p = 0.002). Institutional factors also exhibit a positive and statistically significant moderating effect on this relationship (β = 0.195, t = 3.420, p = 0.001). However, the interaction effect size is small (f² = 0.086), suggesting that the additional explanatory contribution of institutional factors is limited. These findings indicate that institutional support may strengthen the association between community quality of life and sustainable slum management,…

Cognitive Ambidexterity: Balancing Algorithmic Efficiency and Contextual Judgement in AI-Enabled Decision Systems
abstract: AI-enabled decision systems make algorithmic recommendations appear objective and ready for action before contextual, ethical, and stakeholder concerns are fully considered. This study examines how leaders preserve judgment under these conditions. We develop cognitive ambidexterity as a leader-level meta-cognitive capability through which managers balance algorithmic exploitation with contextual exploration in AI-mediated decisions. Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, we first examine five U.K. procurement and infrastructure organizations and identify four mechanisms of cognitive ambidexterity. We then examine these mechanisms through vignette experiments with managers. The findings show that leaders preserve contextual judgment by treating AI outputs as interpretive cues, calibrating trust under ambiguity, slowing decisions when reflection is needed, and building supports that make algorithmic recommendations contestable. The study extends ambidexterity theory by showing how exploration–exploitation tensions are cognitively regulated when exploitation is embedded in algorithmic decision processes. It also uses leadership cognition and Upper Echelons Theory to explain why leaders differ in their capacity to enact this regulation. Together, these insights position cognitive ambidexterity as a critical leader-level capability for using AI’s efficiency gains whil…

title: Prudential Regulatory Compliance and Financial Performance of Microfinance Banks in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya
abstract: Microfinance banks (MFBs) support financial inclusion, but their sustainability depends on sound prudential practices and financial performance. This study examined associations between liquidity regulation, loan classification regulation, financial reporting regulation, capital adequacy regulation and perceived financial performance among MFB employees in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya. A cross-sectional survey targeted 193 employees in five occupational strata. Using Yamane’s formula and proportional stratified sampling, 130 employees were selected; 89 valid questionnaires were returned (68.46%). The structured questionnaire assessed regulatory practices and financial performance using predominantly five-point Likert items. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and multiple linear regression. All four regulatory dimensions correlated positively with perceived financial performance, with the strongest bivariate correlation observed for financial reporting (r = 0.619). The regression model was significant, F(4, 84) = 26.240, p < 0.001, explaining 55.6% of the variation in perceived financial performance (adjusted R² = 0.534). Financial reporting (B = 0.356, β ≈ 0.350, p < 0.001), liquidity (B = 0.236, β ≈ 0.309, p < 0.001) and capital adequacy (B = 0.264, β ≈ 0.240, p = 0.009) showed significant positive associations. Loan classification was not indep…

title: A qualitative exploration of the psychosocial and financial outcomes for cancer survivors with ostomies
abstract: Abstract Purpose Rural cancer survivors with ostomies face multiple healthcare utilization issues including cost. The purpose of this study was to identify ostomy-related modifiable factors that are expected to impact the total cost of care. Methods Cancer survivors with ostomies were identified in three geographically diverse areas (Southern California, North Dakota, Pennsylvania). Individual open-ended, semi-structured interviews were conducted to elicit participant descriptions of the explicit and implicit costs of ostomy management. Results Eleven of 24 participants described explicit financial burden from their ostomy. Additional costs that were inferred included unreimbursed ostomy supplies, waste due to trial and error, new clothing due to ostomy placement, travel for treatment, and co-pays. When queried about daily life with an ostomy, participants identified additional “hidden” costs of adapting to new social, emotional, and functional realities. Conclusions Direct and indirect financial burdens for many cancer survivors with ostomies are often unanticipated and a major long-term concern. Anticipatory guidance should account for the role that emotions play in integrating critical information regarding post-surgical ostomy management.

title: Florida AIDS Drug Assistance Program Cuts Will Increase HIV Transmission – And Will Be Costly
abstract: Abstract The federal Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program (RWHAP) and its subprogram, the AIDS Drug Assistance Program (ADAP), have been essential in providing access to medications and HIV-related care for people living with HIV (PWH) in the US. Rates of viral suppression among ADAP recipients are substantially higher than among all PWH, reflecting the program’s effectiveness in connecting vulnerable individuals to high-quality treatment. Florida, the state with the third highest rate of new HIV diagnoses, announced cuts to ADAP that removed first-line antiretroviral therapy from its formulary, restricted income-eligibility requirements, and ended health insurance payment-assistance programs. As researchers studying HIV in Florida, we modeled the potential impact of these funding changes projecting more than 1000 new infections over five years in Miami-Dade County alone and over $1 billion in additional lifetime healthcare costs. Funding cuts to ADAP in Florida and other states will lead to increased HIV transmission and healthcare costs.

title: E-Accounting and Digital Financial Reporting: Challenges and Opportunities for Modern Businesses
abstract: Digital transformation is fundamentally changing accounting and corporate financial reporting. Traditional paper-based and manually intensive accounting systems are increasingly being replaced by electronic accounting platforms, cloud-based applications, enterprise resource planning systems, automated transaction processing, artificial intelligence, data analytics, application programming interfaces, and structured digital reporting technologies. These developments have created opportunities for faster transaction processing, real-time financial information, improved accessibility, automated reconciliation, enhanced analytical capabilities, remote collaboration, and more efficient regulatory reporting. At the same time, e-accounting and digital financial reporting create significant challenges involving cybersecurity, data privacy, system integration, implementation costs, technology dependence, data quality, digital skills, internal controls, algorithmic accountability, and regulatory compliance. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with e-accounting and digital financial reporting through a systematic conceptual and literature-review approach. Particular attention is given to cloud accounting, ERP systems, robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, data analytics, blockchain, XBRL, continuous reporting, and cybersecurity. The paper propose…

title: Fraud Hexagon dan Risiko Fraudulent Financial Reporting pada Perusahaan Sektor Keuangan di Bursa Efek Indonesia 2022-2024: Pengujian Moderasi Reputasi KAP
abstract: Fraudulent financial reporting mengancam lembaga keuangan karena lembaga ini mengelola dana masyarakat dan bergantung pada kepercayaan publik. Bank, perusahaan asuransi, perusahaan pembiayaan, dan perusahaan efek juga bergantung pada estimasi kompleks, seperti cadangan kerugian kredit dan cadangan teknis asuransi. Hasil penelitian Fraud Hexagon di Indonesia belum konsisten, dan masih sedikit studi yang menguji apakah reputasi auditor mengubah hubungan tersebut pada sektor keuangan. Penelitian ini menguji apakah enam elemen Fraud Hexagon (Vousinas, 2019) berhubungan dengan risiko salah saji dan apakah reputasi kantor akuntan publik (KAP) memoderasi hubungan tersebut. Sampel terdiri atas 65 perusahaan sektor keuangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia selama 2022-2024, atau 195 observasi perusahaan-tahun yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling. Risiko salah saji diukur dengan indeks aditif komponen F-Score (Dechow et al., 2011). Indeks ini menjadi proksi risiko, bukan bukti terjadinya fraud. Keenam elemen diwakili oleh leverage, proporsi komisaris independen, pergantian auditor, pergantian direksi, jumlah foto CEO, dan koneksi pemerintah. Reputasi KAP diukur dengan afiliasi Big Four. Analisis memakai regresi data panel. Tidak satu pun dari enam proksi signifikan secara statistik (seluruh p > 0,05; R-squared = 0,0076). Keenam koefisien interaksi antara proksi dan afiliasi Big F…

title: Ownership Structure and Financial Performance of Listed Consumer Goods Firms in Nigeria. Evidence from 2016 to 2025
abstract: This study investigates the impact of ownership structure on the financial performance of listed consumer goods companies in Nigeria between 2016 and 2025. Ownership structure was categorised into managerial, institutional and foreign ownership. Return on Assets (ROA) was used to measure the financial performance of the companies, while firm size and leverage were used as control variables. Based on agency theory and stewardship theory, an ex-post-facto research design was adopted. A total of seventeen (17) companies’ annual reports were used as a source of secondary data, giving a total sample size of 170 firm-year observations. Descriptive statistics, spearman’s correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis were performed on the data. Results obtained showed that managerial ownership (β = 0.104, p < 0.01), institutional ownership (β = 0.014, p < 0.05), and foreign ownership (β = 0.043, p < 0.05) had a positive and significant relationship with ROA, while leverage showed a significant negative relationship (β = -0.425, p < 0.01). The model explained 25.1% of the variation in ROA. It is recommended that a structured equity scheme should be provided to managerial staff, institutional investors should be engaged actively and policies to attract strategic foreign investors should be put in place. Debt should also be managed prudently.
venue: African Journal of Business and Economic Development

title: Impact of Transmission Distance on Signal Quality in Multi-Channel Optical Fiber Networks Using WDM Technologies: A Comparative Performance Analysis of CWDM and DWDM
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous comparative evaluation of Coarse Wavelength Division Multiplexing (CWDM) and Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) in multi-channel optical communication networks. The study systematic evaluates a 16-channel optical fiber infrastructure operating at 10 Gbps per channel under Non-Return-to-Zero (NRZ) modulation over standard single-mode optical fiber (ITU-T G.652) across transmission distances of 10 km, 50 km, 75 km, and 100 km. To strictly isolate the physical mechanics of transmission distance, linear attenuation, and chromatic dispersion, the baseline simulation model intentionally excludes optical amplifiers (EDFA) and dispersion compensation units (DCF). Key signal quality metrics—including Quality Factor (Q-Factor), Minimum Bit Error Rate (Min BER), and Eye Diagram opening—are quantitatively extracted using OptiSystem 7.0 simulation tools. Results demonstrate that CWDM exhibits superior numerical stability in unamplified links, achieving a peak Q-Factor of 80.0 (BER ≈ 0) at 10 km for the central channel (Ch8, 1411 nm), whereas DWDM yields an average Q-Factor of 11.48 (BER = 3.68 × 10^-31). At 75 km, both technologies enter a critical transition phase: CWDM drops to Q = 8.39 (Ch1), while DWDM degrades to Q = 3.46 (BER = 2.70 × 10^-4). At 100 km, DWDM suffers complete eye closure (Q = 0, BER = 1.0) due to severe attenuation and crosstal…

title: Systematic Review of Mpox Outbreaks in Africa: Epidemiology, Transmission Dynamics, and Challenges
abstract: Pendahuluan: Mpox, yang sebelumnya dikenal sebagai cacar monyet (monkeypox), telah muncul sebagai ancaman kesehatan masyarakat yang kian berkembang di seluruh Afrika. Ancaman ini ditandai dengan meningkatnya penularan antarmanusia, perluasan cakupan geografis, serta berbagai tantangan kesehatan masyarakat yang signifikan. Tinjauan sistematis ini bertujuan untuk menyintesis epidemiologi, dinamika penularan, dan tantangan sistemik terkait wabah Mpox di negara-negara Afrika. Metode: Pelaporan disusun berdasarkan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Pencarian studi dan laporan mengenai epidemiologi Mpox, tingkat kematian kasus (case fatality rate), serta respons kesehatan masyarakat dilakukan melalui PubMed dan sumber-sumber kelembagaan, termasuk WHO dan Africa CDC. Rentang waktu publikasi yang disertakan adalah 1 Januari 2020 hingga 31 Oktober 2024. Sebanyak enam sumber yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2022 dan 2024 dimasukkan dalam tinjauan ini. Temuan disintesis secara naratif. Hasil: WHO melaporkan 7.535 kasus terkonfirmasi di seluruh Afrika dari tanggal 1 Januari hingga 6 Oktober 2024, dengan 6.169 kasus di antaranya terjadi di Republik Demokratik Kongo (RDK). Bukti dari wilayah timur RDK menunjukkan adanya penularan antarmanusia yang berkelanjutan dari klad Ib. Laporan yang ditinjau mengidentifikasi adanya kesenjangan dalam deteksi kasus, kapasitas diagnostik, dan akses terhadap vaksin. Kesimpu…

title: Legal Liability for Harm Caused by Artificial Intelligence and Algorithms: A Comparative Study of Criminal, Civil, and Administrative Liability in the European Union and the United Arab Emirates
abstract: This research examines the topic of “Legal Liability for Harm Caused by Artificial Intelligence and Algorithms: A Comparative Study of Criminal, Civil, and Administrative Liability in the European Union and the United Arab Emirates.” It aims to explain the legal framework governing the use and processing of data and information, and to identify the harm that may result from algorithmic outputs, particularly violations of privacy, damage to reputation, the spread of misleading information, fraud, identity theft, and the unlawful disclosure of personal data. The research uses a descriptive, analytical, and comparative approach. It describes and analyses relevant legal provisions and compares the legal protection measures, oversight mechanisms, and penalties in the European Union and the United Arab Emirates. The study also examines civil liability, including its main elements and the conditions for compensation for material and non-material damage. It addresses administrative liability in terms of regulatory obligations, supervision, and penalties. In addition, it examines criminal liability, including the elements of a crime and the attribution of criminal acts to natural or legal persons, depending on the nature of the act. The findings show that the involvement of multiple parties in developing, operating, and using artificial intelligence systems makes liability more complex.…

title: ПРИНЦИП «ЗАБРУДНЮВАЧ ПЛАТИТЬ» І ФІНАНСОВЕ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯ РЕКУЛЬТИВАЦІЇ ГІРНИЧИХ ОБ'ЄКТІВ: АДАПТАЦІЯ ЗАКОНОДАВСТВА УКРАЇНИ ДО ПРАВА ЄС (НА ПРИКЛАДІ КРИВОРІЗЬКОГО БАСЕЙНУ)
Never Break the Chain
abstract: Introduction On the morning of 18 March 2023, two crowds occupied the steps of Victoria’s Parliament House on Spring Street. The primary group had gathered for the “Let Women Speak” rally, an event on the Australian tour of the British anti-transgender activist Kellie-Jay Keen-Minshull (also known as Posie Parker), and was addressed by then-Liberal MLC Moira Deeming, former federal Liberal candidate Katherine Deves, and other gender-critical feminists. Another group of approximately thirty men in black clothing and balaclavas from the National Socialist Network (NSN) marched along Spring Street chanting “white power”, unfurled a banner which read “destroy paedo freaks”, and performed the Nazi salute – then lawful in the state (Elkin). Moira Deeming is not affiliated with proscribed far-right extremist organisations, and yet, through her involvement in the “Let Women Speak” rally, she was discursively aligned with a neo-Nazi organisation, resulting in then-Opposition Leader John Pesutto moving to expel her from the parliamentary party (Kolovos). In this article, we ask how this affiliation was made legible. Gender-critical and far-right discourses were not strangers to one another before Spring Street. Hines has demonstrated extensive links between gender-critical feminism and the far-right in the United Kingdom. Mayer and Sauer have also shown how “gender ideology” can function…

title: Quantifying Physical Climate Risk in Extractive Industries: Stress-Testing Framework for Financial Disclosure and ESG Governance
abstract: Background: Hydropower-dependent mining is exposed to hydrological variability, yet methods for translating hydrological conditions into traceable financial estimates remain limited. As a result, physical climate risk is often disclosed qualitatively.Purpose: This study develops a stress-testing framework to express physical climate risk in financial terms for disclosure and risk management.Design/methodology/approach: A deterministic single-case study combines public reports and measured rainfall summaries. A U-shaped function links inflow ratios to production losses using US$888,6 million in exposed revenue. Five-year discounted losses and indicative asset exposure are calculated from stated scenarios, assumptions, and disclosed carrying values.Findings/Results: At a 10% discount rate, four scenarios yield five-year discounted revenue losses of US$168.4–2,021.1 million and indicative asset exposure of US$23.1–925.4 million. At equal deviations from normal inflow, dry conditions produce greater assumed losses; wet conditions act through a different operational channel.Conclusion: The framework translates stated hydrological scenarios into transparent and reproducible financial estimates, subject to the assumptions and data limitations disclosed.Originality/value: The study links physical climate-risk scenarios to financial estimates relevant to IFRS S2-informed disclosure and …

title: Development of An Inclusive E-Module Based On Universal Design For Learning (UDL) For Fundamental Motor Skills Learning In Sports Science Students
abstract: This study aims to develop a valid inclusive e-module based on Universal Design for Learning (UDL) for fundamental motor skills learning among Sports Science undergraduate students. Employing a Research and Development (R&D) method using the 4-D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate), this research focused on the first three development stages to examine product validity. The research subjects comprised students, course lecturers, as well as subject-matter experts, inclusive education experts, and instructional media experts. Data were gathered through interviews, observations, and validation sheets, then analyzed using percentage techniques and mean score calculations. The results demonstrated that the UDL-based e-module achieved an overall mean validity score of 86.0%, falling into the "Highly Valid" category. The specific evaluation breakdown includes content feasibility at 86.6%, linguistic feasibility at 87.8%, UDL presentation feasibility at 86.5%, and media feasibility at 84.5%. In conclusion, the UDL-based inclusive e-module is proven to be highly valid and satisfies both accessibility and graphic design standards; thus, it is eligible for further field testing to facilitate flexible and adaptive fundamental motor skills learning for all students, including students with special needs.

title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design
abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs). Despite rapid advances in PROTAC development, successful translation depends on interconnected determinants, including target degradability, ubiquitin ligase (E3) recruitment, warhead and linker properties, ternary-complex formation, ubiquitination efficiency, intracellular exposure, and pharmacokinetic behavior. This review provides an integrated, mechanism-oriented analysis of these determinants by linking PROTAC design, ubiquitination biology, computational approaches, and clinical development. We examine key principles governing PROTAC-mediated degradation, with emphasis on E3-ligase selection, linker design, ternary-complex geometry and cooperativity, ubiquitin (Ub)-acceptor lysine (Lys) accessibility, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme (E2)/E3 context, proteasomal engagement, inefficient degradation, and the hook effect. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for degradation-activity prediction, E3-ligase/POI pairing, liga…

title: Machine Learning‐Assisted Nanozymes: From Design to Application
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanozymes are synthetic nanomaterials engineered to mimic the catalytic functions of natural enzymes, characterized by facile synthesis, ease of surface modification, low cost, and high stability, and they have been widely applied in various fields. However, the rational design and synthesis of nanozymes remain complex, and their activity is challenging to predict. In recent years, the advent of machine learning (ML) has shown great promise in addressing these issues. This review first systematically elucidates the fundamental principles and common algorithms of ML, followed by an exploration of its role in nanozyme research, with a focused discussion on the synergistic applications of ML and nanozymes in the biomedical field. Finally, this review analyzes the key challenges faced by researchers in applying ML to nanozyme studies as well as the corresponding solutions and provides an outlook on future development directions. Furthermore, given the relatively limited reports on ML‐assisted nanozyme research to date, this study aims to deepen the understanding of nanozymes and more effectively advance nanozyme research toward the era of artificial intelligence.

Design, Validation, and Reliability Study of the Social Capital Scale for Parents
abstract: The Purpose of this study was to develop the Social Capital Scale for Parents (SCSP), to test its reliability and validity. The research used a correlational design. Data were collected from two independent samples: 295 parents for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and 121 parents for Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). The EFA indicated that the SCSP includes three subscales: Capital in Social Interaction, Trust Capital, and Altruistic Capital, and Confirmatory Factor Analysis showed good fit indices. As a result of the reliability analysis, it was observed that the overall Cronbach’s Alpha internal consistency coefficient was .85, and McDonald’s Omega coefficient was .89. Based on these results, it was concluded that the scale can produce reliable and valid measures of parents’ social capital.

The Implementation of Restorative Justice Based on the Reform of National Criminal Law: From a Retributive Approach to a Restorative Approach
abstract: The research problem addressed here concerns the application of restorative justice (RJ) within Indonesia's criminal justice system, specifically regarding the shift in legal paradigm from a retributive approach to a restorative one. The application of RJ in Indonesia represents an effort to transform the legal paradigm from a retributive approach toward a restorative approach that is more humane and participatory. However, the implementation of RJ faces various challenges, notably limited human resources, a lack of training for officials, and resistance from law enforcement personnel accustomed to the retributive approach. This study aims to analyze the application of RJ in Indonesia's criminal justice system within the context of this paradigm shift. The author employs a doctrinal or normative approach, specifically a descriptive-analytical method. The findings indicate that the application of restorative justice in Indonesia shifts the focus of the criminal justice system from punishment or retribution to the restoration of conditions and social relationships to their prior state. The New Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) provides a clearer legal basis for applying restorative justice across various stages of the criminal justice process. Nevertheless, implementation remains hindered by limited technical regulations, a law enforcement paradigm that remains retributively orient…

Beyond Technology: A Strategic Framework for Building Sustainable and Resilient Health Systems Through Organizational Strategy, Operational Excellence, and Workforce Capability
abstract: Health systems worldwide face converging pressures from demographic transition, rising chronic disease burdens, workforce shortages, fiscal constraints, and recurrent shocks ranging from pandemics to climate related emergencies. Over the past decade, digital transformation has dominated the health system improvement agenda, with substantial investment directed toward electronic records, telehealth, analytics platforms, and artificial intelligence. Yet accumulating evidence indicates that technology alone does not produce sustainable performance gains, and in some settings has amplified inefficiency, clinician burden, and inequity. This paper argues that durable health system performance rests on three mutually reinforcing non technological pillars: organizational strategy, operational excellence, and workforce capability. Drawing on strategic management theory, quality improvement science, health workforce research, and the emerging literature on health system resilience, the paper develops an integrated strategic framework that positions technology as an enabler rather than a driver of transformation. Organizational strategy provides direction, resource alignment, and adaptive governance. Operational excellence converts strategic intent into reliable, efficient, and continuously improving care processes. Workforce capability supplies the skills, engagement, and psychological s…

title: Health risks and public safety concerns of illicit alcohol in Uganda: alcohol content, hygiene & sanitation in production and retail
abstract: Introduction Illicit alcohol, produced or distributed outside formal regulation, presents public-health concerns related to alcohol strength, chemical and microbiological contamination, and unsafe production and retail practices. In Uganda, informal alcohol production and sale remain important regulatory and public-health challenges. Aim This study assessed alcohol strength, methanol and microbial contamination, and hygiene and sanitation practices in illicit alcohol production and retail settings in Uganda. Methods A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted in Kampala and Arua between October and November 2024. Data was collected from 400 producers and retailers using surveys and structured observations. Laboratory analyses assessed alcohol content, methanol levels, and microbial contamination. Twenty key-informant and in-depth interviews supplemented the quantitative data. Results Findings revealed inconsistent and often under-declared alcohol strength up to 44.2%, with methanol concentrations in some spirits exceeding safe limits up to 640.59 mg/L. Opaque beers showed contamination with Staphylococcus aureus , linked to poor hygiene during handling and storage. Observation scores highlighted widespread unsanitary practices, including unsafe water source 36.7% in Arua and 63.3% in Kampala, dirty production areas 44.2% in Arua and 55.8% in Kampala, pest infestation, a…

title: Comparative Analysis of Objective Weighting Approaches in Multi-Criteria Decision Making Using WASPAS
abstract: Selecting the best-performing honorary employee is a multi-criteria decision-making problem because employee performance is influenced by several criteria with different levels of importance. This study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of objective weighting approaches in the Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment (WASPAS) method for evaluating honorary employee performance and examining the stability of the resulting rankings. Eight alternatives, namely HE-A to HE-H, were evaluated using five criteria: Work Performance, Discipline, Cooperative Ability, Initiatives and Problem Solving, and Communication Skills. Twelve objective weighting methods, namely Entropy, G2M, RECA, LOPCOW, CRITIC, MEREC, WENSLO, LOGSTA, LODECI, ITARA, SITDE, and DAM, were independently applied to determine criterion weights. The resulting weights were then integrated into WASPAS to generate alternative rankings under different weighting scenarios. The results show that HE-F consistently achieved the first rank across all objective weighting approaches, while HE-E consistently occupied the eighth position. The ranking comparison further indicates that most methods produce ranking patterns close to the original ranking, although MEREC introduces greater changes in several alternative positions. Spearman rank correlation analysis confirms a strong consistency of the resulting rankings, with the h…

title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

title: Mean Energy variation of Diffuse Aurora Observed with the ASIS Spectrograph
abstract: We analyze more than 20 000 spectra of diffuse aurora recorded by the ASIS spectrograph over two winters, focusing on events classified as diffuse by an AI-based system, with pulsating auroras forming an important but non-exclusive subgroup. Mean-energy proxies were derived from calibrated red/blue emission ratios using a lookup-table approach based on forward modeling. A Bayesian analysis shows that the precipitation systematically hardens toward the morning sector and confirms that this trend remains robust despite the large intrinsic variability of the dataset. A complementary hierarchical analysis performed at the night-by-night level further shows that the common MLT dependence remains present after accounting for systematic differences between observing nights. Although the strongest predictive support is obtained for a transition near 04:00 MLT, neighbouring transition times remain statistically plausible, indicating that the hardening does not occur at a uniquely defined MLT. Using the AE index as a proxy for geomagnetic activity, we further show that the statistical expression of the MLT-dependent hardening depends not only on the instantaneous activity level but also on geomagnetic conditions over the preceding hours. These results provide new spectroscopic constraints on the statistical evolution of diffuse-auroral precipitation hardness.

title: EXPRESS: Causal Inference With Endogenous Price Response
abstract: The authors study the estimation of causal treatment effects on demand when treatment is randomly assigned but prices adjust in response to treatment. They show that regressions of demand on treatment or on treatment and price lead to biased estimates of the direct treatment effect. The sign of the bias in both cases depends on the sign of the correlation of price with treatment, and the two biases point in the same direction. In most cases including an endogenous price control reduces bias but does not remove it. The authors also show how to test whether bias from an endogenous price response arises and how to recover an unbiased direct treatment effect using a price instrument. They apply the approach to the estimation of feature advertising effects across several product categories using supermarket scanner data and show that the bias when not instrumenting price can be substantial.

title: LymphGen-Sig: Integrating Genetic and Transcriptional States to Predict Therapeutic Response in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
abstract: PURPOSE Genetic classification may advance precision medicine in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), but existing tools like LymphGen (LG) are limited by complexity and incomplete classification and do not incorporate nongenetic features that affect disease biology and therapeutic outcomes. To address these limitations, we developed LG-sig (LGsig), a gene expression–based platform that classifies all DLBCLs and harmonizes both genetic and nongenetic dimensions of the disease. METHODS LGsig was built on the distinct subtype-specific gene expression signature of each LG class using paired genomic and transcriptomic data (National Cancer Institute/British Columbia Cancer Agency; N = 764). Model development was restricted to DLBCLs classified into MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations (MCD), BCL6 translocation and NOTCH2 mutations (BN2), EZH2 mutations and BCL2 translocation (EZB), or SGK1 and TET2 mutations (ST2). Gene features were selected by differential gene expression, with 294 genes being optimal for classification using a nearest shrunken centroid classifier. LGsig classifications were designated as MCDsig , BN2sig , ST2sig , and EZBsig . The final model was applied to RNAseq from archival samples from the POLARIX trial (N = 678) to assess outcomes after polatuzumab vedotin-R-CHP (pola-R-CHP) or rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) for…

title: A Novel MPSI Weighting and Proximity Indexed Value Framework for Multi-Criteria Selection of Marketplace Logistics Partners
abstract: In facing the increasingly intense competition in the logistics industry, companies are often confronted with challenges in selecting the most appropriate logistics partner due to the many performance criteria that must be considered simultaneously. This study aims to evaluate and determine the best logistics partner using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making approach through the integration of the MPSI method for criteria weighting and PIV for the alternative ranking process. The criteria used include Transit Time, On-Time Delivery, First-Attempt Success, Attempt Rate, and Package Volume, which are analyzed based on the performance data of each alternative. The weighting results indicate that Package Volume and Transit Time are the most dominant factors in the evaluation process. Based on the PIV method calculations, the ranking results were obtained, with NJ Logistics Partner occupying the first rank with a score of 0.46408, followed by TK Logistics Partner in second place with a score of 0.44014, and JT Logistics Partner in third place with a score of 0.39282. Sensitivity tests through various weight change scenarios showed that the ranking structure remained consistent, indicating that the model has a high level of stability and resilience to parameter variations. Overall, the proposed approach is able to produce decisions that are objective, measurable, and reliable as a basis…

title: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to visual short-term memory (VSTM). However, the neural mechanisms through which hippocampal activity supports the maintenance of VSTM representations remain largely unknown. Here, using intracranial EEG recordings from human participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task for naturalistic objects, we investigated the role of hippocampal ripple activity—brief high-frequency oscillations associated with memory replay—in VSTM maintenance and hippocampal-neocortical communication. We found that hippocampal ripple rates progressively ramped up during the maintenance period and supported successful VSTM. More critically, hippocampal ripples were temporally coupled with the ripples in the lateral temporal lobe (LTL), and these coupled ripples were associated with memory reactivation in the LTL. These findings provide direct evidence that hippocampal–neocortical interaction via coupled ripples supports VSTM, extending the role of hippocampal ripples from long-term consolidation to short-term mnemonic processes and offering new insights into the dynamic coding mechanisms of working memory.

title: From Fredholm determinants to AdS/CFT observables: a universal strong-coupling framework
abstract: A bstract We investigate the trans-series structure of the cusp anomalous dimension of 𝒩 = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and the dynamically generated mass gap of the O(6) sigma model at strong ’t Hooft coupling. We consider the one-parameter deformation of the cusp anomalous dimension, known as the tilted cusp, and review its strong-coupling expansion obtained through its representation in terms of Fredholm determinants with a matrix Bessel kernel. The advantage of this deformation is that the non-perturbative scales separate naturally, revealing structures that remain hidden in the physical limit. Motivated by this observation, we introduce the tilted mass gap, which reduces to the physical O(6) mass gap at a special value of the deformation parameter and exhibits a deep connection with the tilted cusp. This formulation allows us to determine the complete strong-coupling trans-series and resurgence structure of the O(6) mass gap, while extending and proving conjectured relations between successive non-perturbative corrections. Building on the underlying Fredholm determinant representation, we construct an Alien calculus that generates all non-perturbative sectors of these AdS/CFT observables directly from their perturbative expansions. Finally, we derive an exact all-orders relation between the strong-coupling trans-series of the O(6) mass gap and the cusp anomalous dime…

Hybrid Modification Preference Selection Index with Optimized Pairwise Ratio Analysis Method for Multi-Criteria Decision Making: An Integrated Weighting and Ranking Approach
abstract: Multi-criteria job candidate selection requires an objective and systematic approach because candidates are evaluated using multiple criteria with different levels of importance. This study proposes a hybrid Modification Preference Selection Index with Optimized Pairwise Ratio Analysis (MPSI–OPARA) framework that integrates objective criteria weighting and alternative ranking. MPSI is used to determine criterion weights based on normalized performance variation, while OPARA is applied to rank candidates through adjusted pairwise comparisons. The framework is demonstrated using six job candidates evaluated across six criteria: educational background, work experience, technical competence, communication skills, problem-solving ability, and interview performance. The results show that educational background and work experience are the dominant criteria, with weights of 0.5600 and 0.3422, respectively. OPARA produces Candidate IMS as the first-ranked candidate, Candidate GTB as the second-ranked candidate, and Candidate RDH as the third-ranked candidate. Furthermore, comparisons with SAW, SMART, WASPAS, and MOORA produce identical ranking positions, demonstrating consistent ranking outcomes. These findings indicate that the proposed MPSI–OPARA framework provides a systematic and consistent approach for objective criteria weighting and job candidate selection.

title: The impact of bureaucratic management style on employee health: the mediating role of emotional exhaustion and the moderating role of innovative role modelling
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of a bureaucratic management style on employee’s physical health, highlighting emotional exhaustion as a mediator and innovative role modelling (IRM) as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the job demands-resources (JD-R) model, the study employed a structured questionnaire to gather data from 350 public sector employees. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings The results demonstrate that a bureaucratic management style significantly worsens physical health by increasing emotional exhaustion. Emotional exhaustion partially mediates this relationship. In addition, IRM moderates the effect of emotional exhaustion on physical health, reducing its negative impact and indicating the protective role of adaptive leadership. Research limitations/implications As a cross-sectional study using self-reported data, causality cannot be firmly established and potential common method bias may affect results. Future research could adopt longitudinal designs and incorporate objective health measures. Practical implications Organizations – especially in the public sector – should adopt interventions that reduce bureaucratic rigidity, support emotional well-being and encourage innovative leadership to mitigate health-related risks. title: High-energy electronic excitations in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 by time-resolved optical spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Recently, high-temperature superconductivity has been established in bilayer La 3 Ni 2 O 7 , which exhibits a density-wave (DW) transition at ~ 150 K under ambient pressure. The DW order is believed to be linked to superconductivity, as it is suppressed upon the emergence of superconductivity at high pressures. Here, we explore the ultrafast dynamics of high-energy electronic excitations from 10 K to room temperature under ambient pressure using time-resolved optical spectroscopy. Two high-energy electronic excitations at ~1.8 and ~ 2.4 eV, arising from distinct interband transitions, are identified. They exhibit different DW gaps of approximately 54 and 67 meV, respectively, along with relaxation dynamics that can be well described by the Rothwarf-Taylor model. In addition, we observe four coherent Raman-active phonon modes that exhibit distinct coupling with different electronic excitations. The phonon softening with increasing temperature can be well described between ~100 K and room temperature by a semi-quantitative model, which includes thermal expansion and anharmonic phonon-phonon coupling. At cryogenic temperatures, deviations from the measured temperature-dependent phonon frequencies and the model fits suggest an additional contribution from electron-phonon coupling. Our study provides direct evidence of the complex gap structure and phonon dynamics in this m…
