title: Three financial behaviours, three health meanings: market participation and non-housing debt, but not investment returns, are associated with poorer self-rated health (CFPS 2018–2022)
abstract: Objective Market participation, borrowing and investment returns are usually treated as interchangeable, yet their health meanings differ, most studies examined only one, and participation evidence is double-edged. We estimated all three together and tested whether their associations with self-rated health (SRH) are directionally consistent. Methods Three-wave CFPS data (2018/2020/2022; 56,606 person-wave observations) were analysed in three stages: cross-sectional ordered logit models (L1); baseline exposures predicting health 2 years later with propensity-score matching and weighting (L2); fixed-effects, change-score and lagged models (L3). Debt was modelled as a state (any non-housing debt; primary) and as a size (log amount). Sensitivity analyses covered threshold models, Oster delta, E-values and imputation. Results Holding non-saving products (OR 0.822, 95% CI 0.774, 0.872) and being in non-housing debt (OR 0.788, 95% CI 0.753, 0.825) were associated with lower SRH, mainly lower probability of very good health. Within debtors the amount showed no gradient or predictive value, although the two were collinear ( r = 0.990). Investment returns showed no association with SRH (OR 0.983, 95% CI 0.926, 1.044). Baseline holding (OR 0.906, 95% CI 0.837, 0.980) and debt status (OR 0.837, 95% CI 0.785, 0.893) predicted worse health 2 years later, whereas baseline health predicted lat…

title: Benchmarking analysis of governance of Pakistan’s formative carbon market framework against China and India
abstract: Abstract Currently, Pakistan faces twin challenges; extreme climate vulnerability and macroeconomic instability, both of which demand forward looking climate finance mechanisms. In this study, we evaluate Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Carbon Markets: 2024 through a structured qualitative comparative analysis against two regional models: China’s compliance-based National Emissions Trading System (ETS) and India’s evolving Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS). We examine these frameworks across four core governance pillars: policy mandates, Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems, sectoral coverage, and economic resilience. The study identifies critical institutional capacity gaps in Pakistan, including the absence of mandatory industrial compliance obligations and a fully operational national carbon registry. Using the Porter Hypothesis and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) as interpretive frameworks, the study suggests that the absence of mandatory carbon pricing may weaken incentives for industrial green innovation (SDG 9) and climate action (SDG 13). We recommend that Pakistan adopt a phased, hybrid transition model like India’s CCTS before shifting toward a mature compliance system like China’s National ETS.

title: State, capital and labour: an analysis of the government–market relationship under the socialist market economy
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to clarify the essence of the government–market relationship under the socialist market economy by examining it through the combined perspectives of commodity circulation and capital circulation and Marx's dual nature of managerial labour, arguing that this relationship is fundamentally a relationship among the state, capital and labour rather than a simple opposition or complementarity between government and market. Design/methodology/approach The paper employs a Marxist political economy approach, combining analysis of commodity and capital circulation to reveal the essence of the market, and applying Marx's framework of the dual nature of managerial labour to examine the essence of government, thereby reconstructing the government–market relationship as a relationship among the state, capital and labour. Findings The paper finds that the essence of the market is the capital–labour relation dominated by capital, and that government is both an executor of state functions as a committee for managing the common affairs of the ruling class and a provider of public services at the level of technical relations. It demonstrates that properly handling the government–market relationship requires curbing excessive marketisation, making state-owned enterprises stronger and better and giving effect to socialist labour relations. Originality/value This paper innova…

title: Forecasting bond-market responses to rating events using LLM-structured rating information and historical market outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study develops event-conditional forecasts of bond-market responses to rating disclosures, using a large language model (LLM) to structure report information and statistical models to estimate subsequent outcomes. Design/methodology/approach LLM-assisted extraction is combined with rating histories and pre-announcement market conditions. The sample comprises 19,871 linked rating events and 119,683 eligible event–bond observations in China's exchange-traded bond market. A retrospective expanding-window design evaluates forecasts of transaction-price formation, repricing intensity, trading attention, cross-bond propagation and credit direction out of sample. Findings Cross-bond propagation shows the most consistent gains over the market-state benchmark. For 20-day transaction-price formation, the full-information model lowers Brier scores from 0.2148 to 0.1507 in the issuer-expanded channel and from 0.1501 to 0.1077 for directly rated bonds relative to the event-metadata benchmark. The remaining rating variables provide no statistically detectable improvement when market-state and bond-set controls are shared. Repricing forecasts have lower mean absolute errors than the market-state benchmark in both channels, while incremental ranking evidence is more limited. Trading-attention and credit-direction evidence is weaker. Practical implications The framework can support…

title: Phillips’ go-to-market strategy: creating human capital for value co-creation
abstract: Learning outcomes After the completion of this case study, students will be able to: Case overview/synopsis The business case “Phillips’ Go-to-Market Strategy: Creating Human Capital for Value Co-creation” is written on Phillips’ unconventional “Go-to-Market Strategy” aimed at creating a market for Phillips products by tapping the core stakeholders who are tomorrow’s machinists trained for the company’s products. The case dwells on the concept of value creation, which is a win-win model for businesses/other stakeholders across the value chain. The organization is trying to set a growth trajectory, keeping in view the business aspects of creating the market for Phillips products by tapping into the potential workforce and customers and simultaneously building a skill set. The business model for Phillips education is stakeholder-centric, focusing on skilling the workforce to be industry-ready as Machinists, specifically trained for the company’s products. This workforce, in turn, will create a micro-ecosystem for the company’s products in the future. The case can be viewed from the perspective of corporate strategy on business value creation and stakeholder engagement, in which the business model seeks to align financials, meet the social bottom line and undertake community engagement to create human capital. The case can also be seen from the perspective of human resources, as P…

title: From Circular Production to Consumer Value: Transparency and Layered Consumer Information as Market Mechanisms in Circular Agri-Food Systems
abstract: Circular production systems can reduce resource dependency, retain nutrients and bio-mass in productive use, and valorize unavoidable side-streams, but their economic viability de-pends partly on whether consumers recognize and reward circular attributes that are often invisible at purchase. This conceptual article develops a Circular Value Translation Framework linking circular production to verified transparency and traceability, trust, perceived consumer value, willingness to pay (WTP), and value transmitted back to producers. Its two core contributions are a layered consumer information architecture combining a visible standardized verified core with optional channel-appropriate depth under realistic low-involvement food-choice conditions, and a value-capture feedback loop making producer adoption conditional on premium pass-through, bargaining power, and transition costs. Ten falsifiable propositions specify causal links, label substitution or complementarity, individual moderators, situational frictions, and value transmission. The synthesis integrates circular-food evidence with agricultural-economics research on technology adoption, credence labeling, market power, and vertical price transmission, and proposes prioritized empirical tests and practical implications for producers, cooperatives, certification bodies, retailers, and policymakers.

title: Do institutional investors’ exit threats mitigate managerial myopia? Evidence from China’s A-share market
abstract: Purpose Guiding firms toward long-term value creation and mitigating managerial myopia is essential for high-quality development. This study examines whether and how institutional investors’ exit threats mitigate managerial myopia, with attention to the underlying influence mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from China’s A-share listed firms over the period 2008–2022, comprising 31155 observations from 2077 companies, this study examines the impact of institutional investors’ exit threats on managerial myopia. Baseline regressions, channel analysis, threshold tests and heterogeneity analyses are employed to identify the effect and uncover the mechanisms through which exit threats influence managerial myopia, as well as to examine how this effect varies across firm characteristics and institutional settings in an emerging market context. Findings The results show that institutional investors’ exit threats significantly curb managerial myopia. Further channel analysis indicates that this effect operates through lowering agency costs, improving information transparency and easing financing constraints. Threshold analysis reveals a double-threshold effect of institutional ownership, indicating that the governance role of exit threats depends on shareholding intensity. Heterogeneity analysis indicates stronger effects among non-state-owned firms, those with hig…

title: Conversational Implicature in Buying-Selling Transactions at Bambu Kuning Market, Bandar Lampung: A Pragmatic Study
abstract: Buying and selling transactions in traditional markets are forms of communication that often contain implied meanings in the utterances of sellers and buyers. This study aims to describe conversational implicatures based on sentence types in buying and selling transactions at Bambu Kuning Market, Tanjung Karang Pusat District, Bandar Lampung City. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach. The data consist of oral utterances produced by sellers and buyers, collected through observation, note-taking, and recording techniques. Data analysis was conducted by identifying, classifying, and interpreting implied meanings based on the context of the utterances. The results show that seven speech events containing conversational implicatures were identified, consisting of two declarative sentence implicatures, two interrogative sentence implicatures, and three imperative sentence implicatures. Declarative sentence implicatures are used to indirectly reject price offers and convince buyers. Interrogative sentence implicatures are used to ask about prices while implying the intention to purchase, whereas imperative sentence implicatures indicate the buyer’s agreement and decision to proceed with the transaction. These findings demonstrate that understanding conversational implicatures in buying and selling transactions requires consideration of the context and communicative pu…

title: POTENTIAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE FOR DATA CENTER DEPLOYMENT IN NORTHEASTERN BRAZIL: A TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES AND ELECTRICITY AVAILABILITY
abstract: A expansão dos serviços digitais tem pressionado a demanda por data centers, e instalar um empreendimento desse tipo exige energia elétrica disponível sem interrupção e condições operacionais adequadas. Diante disso, a pergunta que orientou esta pesquisa foi: em que medida o potencial de geração solar e eólica, somado à infraestrutura de transmissão e distribuição de eletricidade, à confiabilidade do fornecimento e às condições de refrigeração, sustenta a implantação de data centers no Nordeste brasileiro, diante de suas demandas energéticas contínuas e exigências operacionais? O objetivo geral foi analisar em que condições se encontra a infraestrutura energética da região para receber esses empreendimentos, considerando a disponibilidade de fontes renováveis, a confiabilidade do fornecimento, a capacidade da rede elétrica e as exigências ligadas à refrigeração e à continuidade operacional. Metodologicamente, o trabalho seguiu uma abordagem qualitativa, desenvolvida por meio de pesquisas bibliográfica e documental: a primeira, de caráter exploratório e descritivo, concentrou-se em publicações do período de 2018 a 2026; a segunda cobriu normas técnicas, relatórios, planos de expansão e documentos institucionais referentes ao setor elétrico e à infraestrutura de data centers. O material foi organizado em três eixos temáticos, a saber: geração e integração de fontes renováveis, in…

title: EMERGENT URBAN RESILIENCE AND SOCIO-SPATIAL INEQUALITIES IN HOUSEHOLD ELECTRICITY SUPPLY DURING WARTIME: THE CASE OF UKRAINE
abstract: Large-scale disruptions to electricity supply during the Russo-Ukrainian war have created a unique context for examining how cities adapt to prolonged infrastructural crises and how bottom-up responses interact with existing social disparities. The study aims to identify manifestations of emergent resilience in household electricity provision and to assess the extent of socio-spatial inequalities in access to its enabling instruments. A mixed-method approach was applied, including regional analysis of the distribution of technical devices (“svitlobots”) that inform consumers about the presence or absence of electricity during blackouts, and intra-urban field observations focused on autonomous lighting in residential buildings during outages. The findings reveal pronounced territorial and social disparities. The vast majority of digital resilience tools were concentrated in Kyiv and its metropolitan region, with significantly lower diffusion elsewhere. Newer and more affluent housing areas demonstrated higher adoption rates of both digital solutions and autonomous energy technologies, while households in older buildings showed considerably lower levels of adaptive capacity. Emergent resilience plays a crucial role in crisis adaptation but develops unevenly, often reinforcing existing inequalities. While digital initiatives partially mitigate disparities through shared informatio…
venue: Journal of Urban and Regional Analysis

title: Remote cross-regional bid evaluation and public procurement market openness: evidence from Fujian's service procurement threshold
abstract: In January 2025, Fujian Province lowered the budget threshold for mandatory remote cross-regional bid evaluation in general services from RMB 10 million to RMB 5 million. This study examines 3,600 procurement projects in 2024 and 2025. A difference-in-discontinuities design compares the jumps at the cutoff in evaluation adoption and first-round awards to suppliers outside the buyer's city. In the main window (RMB 4.2–5.8 million), the jump in adoption increased by 66.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 55.6 to 77.2), and the jump in out-of-city awards increased by 20.4 points (6.2 to 34.6). Awards to suppliers outside Fujian accounted for 15.4 points of the latter increase, and awards to suppliers in other Fujian cities accounted for 5.0 points. At bandwidths of RMB 0.6 million and RMB 1 million, the estimates for out-of-city awards were 15.3 points (−1.2 to 31.8) and 16.6 points (3.6 to 29.7), respectively. The increase in out-of-city awards corresponded chiefly to a decline in local awards.
venue: Journal of Fintech and Business Analysis

title: SDG ADHERENCE IN BRAZILIAN MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES: A THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK LINKING PERCEIVED RESPONSIBILITY, COMPETITIVENESS AND MARKET PERFORMANCE
abstract: A pesquisa sobre o engajamento empresarial com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) apoia-se, em grande parte, em evidências de empresas grandes o bastante para publicar relatórios de sustentabilidade, condição amostral que deixa de fora as micro e pequenas empresas (MPEs), ainda que elas representem a maior parte das empresas ativas no Brasil. Este artigo conceitual pergunta por quais mecanismos a aderência aos ODS pode se relacionar com responsabilidade percebida, competitividade e desempenho de mercado em MPEs brasileiras e sob quais condições essa relação deve se sustentar. Adotando um desenho de síntese teórica (Jaakkola, 2020), o texto articula a teoria dos stakeholders (Freeman, 1984; Parmar et al., 2010), a visão baseada em recursos e sua extensão aos recursos naturais (Barney, 1991; Hart, 1995) e a teoria institucional (DiMaggio; Powell, 1983; Scott, 2014) a estudos empíricos sobre relato de ODS, práticas de sustentabilidade em pequenas empresas e relação entre responsabilidade social corporativa e desempenho. Daí resultam cinco proposições, segundo as quais a prática orientada aos ODS funciona como recurso cujo valor depende da integração às rotinas centrais, do canal institucional de adoção, da percepção pelos stakeholders diretos, da inserção local da empresa e da visibilidade ambiental do setor. Em seguida, o artigo especifica um protocolo misto sequen…
authors: Diógenes Eldo Carvalho de Barbosa Sobrinho

title: Leveraging large language models for cross-cultural innovation research: a cost-effective approach to understanding market perceptions
abstract: Purpose This study assesses how Large Language Models (LLMs) can support cross-cultural market sensing by approximating social survey responses. Design/methodology/approach Responses from five LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, LLaMA, DeepSeek) were compared with the European Social Survey (ESS) Round 11 data for nine questions on gender perceptions in healthcare, employment, and law enforcement in Spain and Finland. Statistical similarity was assessed using the Jensen–Shannon Distance (JSD), Hellinger Distance (HD), and Relative Mean Absolute Difference (RMAD). Findings LLM outputs can approximate survey distributions but cannot substitute for them; in 17 of 18 question–country pairs, at least one model attained high or very high similarity (JSD and HD < 0.2; RMAD <5%). This represents the upper envelope of the five-model portfolio rather than the performance of any single model selected. Models replicated personal experiences better than collective cultural perceptions. No model consistently outperformed across contexts, and substantial divergence across model-question combinations made this instability a central finding. Research limitations/implications This study covers two countries and one thematic module. Future research could examine other contexts and domains. Practical implications LLMs can support lower-cost preliminary market sensing, with validation across multi…

title: A HYBRID AHP–COMPARABLES VALUATION FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS MLB TEAM MARKET VALUE AND COMPETITIVE BALANCE (2010–2024)
abstract: This study examines whether economic disparities in Major League Baseball (MLB) franchise values translate into persistent advantages in sporting performance. We propose a hybrid decision-making framework that integrates the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to synthesize team performance across batting, fielding, pitching, and success metrics with a comparables-based valuation ratio adapted from Atlanta-estate appraisal to sports teams. A complementary methodological feature is a reduced-question elicitation procedure that compresses expert input from to judgments, thereby reducing respondent burden in hierarchical weighting exercises. Using team statistics and inflation-adjusted franchise valuations over fifteen seasons (2010–2024), we compute an AHP-based ranking and an annual market value for each team. Comparing market value against franchise value enables the identification of undervalued and overvalued teams. Results indicate that higher franchise valuations do not consistently imply superior on-field outcomes, with financially modest teams frequently achieving competitive parity. The proposed framework is generalizable to other sports and management contexts where multicriteria performance assessment must be integrated with economic valuation. In addition, the elicitation procedure may be useful in applications involving a large number of criteria, although its assumptio…
venue: International Journal of the Analytic Hierarchy Process

title: Digitally Enabled and Personalised Income Tax Advisory for Indian Defence Personnel: An Operational and Service-Delivery Study of ITR Filing at udChalo
abstract: Background. Income tax return (ITR) filing in India is increasingly digital, yet taxpayers with non-standard income structures still depend on intermediaries. Indian defence personnel are one such group: their salaries include service-specific allowances, some exempt under Section 10(14) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and they often serve in remote postings with limited time and connectivity. Problem. Intermediaries serving this group must handle high-volume, deadline-driven filing, incomplete documentation, low awareness of the old versus new tax regime, and correct treatment of allowances, while keeping returns accurate. Purpose. The study documents and analyses a hybrid (telephone, WhatsApp, and on-site camp) ITR filing model at udChalo, a defence-focused services platform, and identifies what makes such a model work and where it falls short. Methodology. A descriptive, exploratory, single-organisation case study based on participant observation and operational records. Primary data are the author's own work records: 250 prospective clients contacted, 180 returns filed (135 ITR-1 and 45 ITR-2), and a team of seven. Five anonymised illustrative cases are used to compare tax liability under the old and new regimes. Secondary data come from statutes, government portals, and scholarly literature. Analysis uses descriptive statistics, process mapping, and comparative tax computatio…
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: Strengthening MSME Digital Marketing through Google Business Profile and Social Media Content Optimization: A Community Engagement Program for Air Talago
abstract: Many local food micro, small, and medium enterprises still depend on walk-in customers and word-of-mouth promotion, which limits their digital discoverability and market reach. This community engagement article presents an integrated digital marketing program for Air Talago, a Padang-food microenterprise in Puri Anggrek, Serang. The program responds to three baseline challenges: incomplete local business information, irregular social media activity, and the absence of simple digital marketing governance. A participatory design combines initial observation, interviews, digital-channel auditing, practical training, mentoring, and outcome monitoring. The intervention consists of Google Business Profile creation or claim, information completion, product and location documentation, review-management training, social media profile improvement, content-pillar development, a one-month content calendar, and a simple operating procedure. Evaluation uses a completion checklist, pre-test and post-test, practical demonstrations, and platform insight indicators. The program contributes a practical model that links local search visibility, content communication, and partner capability rather than treating account creation as the final outcome. It is designed to improve the partner’s ability to manage digital marketing independently and continuously.

title: CURRENT ISSUES OF THE POLICE PATROL SERVICE OF THE REPUBLIC OF ARMENIA
abstract: The article examines certain issues related to the reforms of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Armenia in connection with the establishment and operation of the police patrol service. It discusses the main goals and objectives of the police patrol service, the specific features of patrol duty, and the key challenges arising in the process of implementing new standards within the police system.

title: Psychological distress and mental health service use among Asian New Zealanders: evidence from linked national survey and administrative data
abstract: aim: This study examined psychological distress and mental health service use among Asian New Zealanders, disaggregated into Chinese, Indian, and Other Asian sub-groups, compared with sole Europeans. We also assessed socio-demographic factors and unmet health needs as predictors. methods: We used linked New Zealand Health Survey (2011/2012–2018/2019 pooled) and administrative data from the Integrated Data Infrastructure. Psychological distress was measured using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale. Mental health service use was identified via publicly funded hospitalisations for mood and anxiety disorders and dispensing of antidepressants and anxiolytics. Weighted Poisson regression estimated relative risks (RRs) comparing Asian sub-groups with sole Europeans and examined predictors within sub-groups. results: There were no meaningful differences in risk of high psychological distress across groups. All Asian sub-groups were less likely to use mental health services compared with sole Europeans (adjusted RRs [aRRs] 0.32–0.59). Unmet need for primary care predicted higher psychological distress (aRRs 2.24–4.53) and greater service use across all sub-groups (aRRs 1.99–2.37). Gender and New Zealand –born patterns varied by sub-group and were obscured in aggregated analyses. conclusion: Asian New Zealanders are not homogeneous in mental health service use. Inequities exist des…

title: General practitioners’ experiences with pathology laboratory services and service disruptions in Aotearoa New Zealand: a qualitative study
abstract: aims: The aim of this study was to assess general practitioners’ (GPs) knowledge about the medical laboratory landscape: how do they use laboratory services and what are their views on the strikes and current system? methods: Sixth year medical students conducted open-ended interviews with a convenience sample of 17 GPs using a protocol developed from the literature and discussion with a laboratory scientist. Interviews were recorded and transcribed. Transcripts were abductively coded. results: Four themes were identified: GPs were satisfied with their local laboratory service; there was variation in GP knowledge about laboratory structures; affected GPs struggled with the impact of the strikes but questioned whether there was significant public awareness of the strikes in among the various challenges in the healthcare system; laboratory service processes varied and GPs had many improvement suggestions. conclusions: GPs work closely with laboratories and value the relationships they have with skilled laboratory scientists. Current systems put pressure on laboratories’ ability to function effectively, which poses risks to equity, transparency and system resilience.

Ferry transport services as an international tourism booster for the islands: assessing the challenges of achieving optimal service efficiency and safety
abstract: Purpose Ferry transport is vital for island economies, yet persistent operational challenges threaten service reliability and sustainability. This study aims to systematically prioritise key challenges in Langkawi's ferry services to guide targeted improvements. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory sequential mixed-method approach was used. Content analysis first identified the key operational challenges, which were then ranked using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) based on stakeholder perceptions. Findings High operating costs, ferry system failures and management inefficiencies emerged as the highest-ranked challenges. Workforce shortages, scheduling inefficiencies and lack of security and safety awareness were moderately ranked, while infrastructure limitations and navigation constraints were ranked as lower-priority challenges but relevant long-term concerns. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on Langkawi's ferry system; thus, the findings may reflect contextual characteristics specific to island-based operations. However, the methodological framework provides a basis for comparative studies in similar maritime settings. Practical implications The prioritised mitigation framework supports operators and policymakers in implementing cost optimisation, predictive maintenance of assets and infrastructure, workforce training and digitalisation strateg…

title: Contextual contingencies in robot-enabled service encounters: how innovation attributes shape customer experience evaluations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how customers’ evaluations of service-robot innovation attributes shape their experiential evaluations of robot-enabled service encounters and whether the salience of these attributes differs across service contexts. Design/methodology/approach Diffusion of innovation (DOI) theory provides the primary explanatory lens, while uses-and-gratifications theory (UGT) offers a complementary perspective on effort-related and hedonic evaluations. The model examines how relative advantage, compatibility and observability relate to perceived ease of use and perceived enjoyment, which are associated with experiential evaluations of robot-enabled service encounters. Survey data were collected from customers with prior robot-service exposure in Taiwan (n = 415) and India (n = 510). Multi-group structural equation modelling was conducted after establishing measurement invariance. Findings Perceived ease of use and enjoyment are positively associated with experiential evaluations in both contexts. Relative advantage is more salient in the Indian sample, whereas compatibility is more salient in the Taiwanese sample. Observability is non-significant in both samples. title: Exploring millennials' purchasing intentions for genetically modified plant-based meat alternatives in UK quick-service restaurants: application of theory of planned behaviour
abstract: Purpose This study applies the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) to predict millennials' intentions to purchase genetically modified plant-based meat alternatives (GM-PBMAs) in quick-service restaurants (QSRs) in the UK. Design/methodology/approach A structured survey was conducted among 341 UK millennials, measuring TPB constructs and perceptions of GM-PBMAs. Structural equation modelling (SEM) tested the relationships between attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control (PBC), and purchase intentions. Findings Low purchase intentions among UK millennials for GM-PBMAs, despite attitudes, subjective norms, and PBC being positively and significantly associated with the intention to purchase GM-PBMAs. Millennials generally have unfavourable perceptions of GE technology, which appears to dampen their willingness to adopt these novel foods, despite reporting moderate levels of social support and perceived control over their choices. Practical implications The study highlights the importance of current scepticism and subjective norms for QSR managers and policymakers to address the unfavourable attitudes about genetic engineering if they wish to promote the adoption of GM-PBMAs as sustainable food options. Originality/value This study investigated UK millennials' attitudes and behavioural intentions towards GM-PBMAs within the QSR context using the TPB framework. By in…

title: RAQAMLI TA’LIMNING MAZMUN-MOHIYATI VA PEDAGOGIK IMKONIYATLARI: BO‘LAJAK O‘QITUVCHILARNI TAYYORLASH KONTEKSTIDA
abstract: Ushbu maqolada raqamli ta’limning mazmun-mohiyati, uning elektron ta’lim va onlayn ta’limdan farqi, o‘ziga xos xususiyatlari va afzalliklari hamda bo‘lajak o‘qituvchilarni tayyorlashdagi pedagogik imkoniyatlari nazariy tahlil qilingan. Xalqaro manbalar va milliy me’yoriy hujjatlarga tayangan holda raqamli ta’limning afzalliklari hamda cheklovlari birga tahlil qilingan. title: Adaptive Pricing and Consumer Trust Enhancement to Sustain a Padang Culinary MSME: A Community Engagement Program for Air Talago
abstract: Culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises face simultaneous pressure from raw-material price volatility, intense competition, changing consumer expectations, and the need for transparent digital communication. This community engagement article presents an integrated program for Air Talago, a Padang-food MSME in Serang. The proposal-based baseline identifies two connected priorities: the absence of a data-informed adaptive pricing system and the need to strengthen consumer trust through hygiene, halal assurance, consistent taste, service, and transparent information. The program applies participatory action research and asset-based community development. Activities include cost-of-goods calculation, competitor and customer review, value-based pricing, limited bundling and time-based offers, transparent price communication, hygiene and service procedures, recipe standardization, digital review management, simple bookkeeping, and monitoring. Evaluation is designed around a baseline, practical training, demonstrations, checklists, and follow-up indicators such as menu cost sheets, price lists, positive reviews, customer questions, and available transaction records. The article contributes an integrated community-engagement framework in which adaptive price decisions and consumer trust are developed together to support the continuity of a local culinary MSME.

High-impact service-learning: College student reflections on out-of-school programming for youth with type 1 diabetes
abstract: This qualitative study examined college student reflections on participation in high-impact, service-learning courses that designed, implemented, and evaluated a diabetes day camp for youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D). Situated within a four-year Mountain West university, the course intentionally integrated collaborative assignments, service-learning, and undergraduate research to address a community need while supporting student learning. Across two academic semesters, eight undergraduate students completed semi-structured written reflections focused on planning, facilitation, evaluation, and personal growth. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were identified: collaborative experiential learning; understanding and empathy for youth with T1D; creating belonging and supportive communities; and professional growth and program development. Findings suggest that integrating multiple high-impact practices within recreation courses can deepen student learning while expanding responsive, community-based programming for youth with T1D.

title: From fear to fluency: a scaffolded online speaking intervention for EFL pre-service teachers
abstract: Oral proficiency is both a learning outcome and a professional resource for pre-service English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers, who must use English to teach, explain, model, and participate in professional discourse. This curriculum, instruction, and pedagogy article describes Speak Up Cycles, a yearlong synchronous online intervention developed through action research at one teacher education college in Israel. The intervention used five increasingly demanding speaking contexts, progressing from pair interaction to department wide events and preparation for seminar defenses. ACCESS, an original descriptive design structure developed for the intervention, comprises six interdependent features: autonomy, collaboration, communication, empowerment, scaffolding, and safety zones. It is presented as a structural design map, not as a validated theoretical framework. The study examined participants’ perceptions of factors supporting oral participation and described changes in matched oral assessment outcomes. Eleven of the 30 course participants completed interviews, and matched CEFR aligned assessment data were available for 19 participants. Among these 19 participants, the proportion meeting the program's B2 passing threshold increased from 37% to 84%, a descriptive within group increase of 47 percentage points. Without a comparison group, this improvement cannot be attribute…

title: Kegagalan Layanan (Service Failure) dan (Service Recovery) sebagai Strategi Mempertahankan Kepercayaan Pasien di Rumah Sakit: Literature Review
abstract: Patient trust is an important aspect of sustaining healthcare relationships and may be compromised by service failures, such as administrative delays, inadequate communication, and patient safety incidents. Service recovery is one of the strategies employed by hospitals to address such failures while maintaining patient trust. This literature review aims to analyze the forms of service failure in hospitals, service recovery strategies, and the mechanisms involved in maintaining and restoring patient trust. This review employed a structured narrative synthesis approach to scientific literature obtained through targeted searches of PubMed, journal publishers’ websites, and cross-referencing. Based on a bibliographic audit, 18 unique publications were identified, of which 12 were directly relevant and included as sources for thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that effective service recovery strategies should include transparent and empathetic communication, appropriate apologies, fair complaint resolution, corrective actions, and continuous follow-up. Perceptions of distributive, procedural, and interactional justice also play a role in shaping patients’ evaluations of hospital responses. Furthermore, systematic complaint management can serve as a means of organizational learning and healthcare quality improvement. In conclusion, service recovery that prioritizes safety, tr…

title: Modeling Robot Head-Direction Duration and Switching Frequency During Side-by-Side Walking with a Human
abstract: Recent advancements in robotics have led to extensive research on social robots capable of moving alongside humans. However, existing studies on mobile robotics have largely overlooked head-direction behavior in the context of side-by-side interactions during walking. As an initial step toward addressing this gap, the present study investigated human head-direction behavior during side-by-side conversational walking. We developed a robot head-direction model based on the collected data and examined its implementation in a mobile robot. This approach provides a data-driven basis for designing robot head-direction behavior during side-by-side walking, rather than relying solely on fixed or manually specified head movements. Specifically, we conducted experiments comparing three conditions: (1) a data-driven condition, in which the robot’s head-direction behavior was governed by the data-driven model; (2) a control condition, in which head-direction durations were randomly assigned based on a uniform distribution between the minimum and maximum values of the data-driven model; and (3) a baseline condition, in which the robot exhibited no head-direction behavior. The results demonstrated that the robot in the data-driven and control conditions received significantly higher ratings than those in the baseline condition, with no discernible difference between the data-driven and contr…

title: The Relationship Between Perceived Mindful Parenting, Emotion Regulation, and Psychological Well-Being Among High School Students
abstract: This study aims to examine the relationships among perceived mindful parenting, emotion regulation, and psychological well-being in adolescents. A quantitative, cross-sectional correlational research design was employed. The participants consisted of 261 students from Sunan Giri Menganti High School, aged 15–18 years. Data were collected using the Interpersonal Mindfulness in Parenting Scale (IM-P), an emotion regulation scale, and a psychological well-being scale, with responses scored on a 1–4 scale. Data analysis was conducted using Spearman’s rho correlation. The results indicate that perceived mindful parenting is positively and significantly associated with both emotion regulation (ρ = 0.238; p < 0.001) and psychological well-being (ρ = 0.257; p < 0.001). Emotion regulation also shows a positive and significant correlation with psychological well-being (ρ = 0.574; p < 0.001), with this pair yielding the highest correlation coefficient. These findings highlight the interconnections between adolescents' perceptions of parental care, their ability to manage emotions, and their psychological well-being, though they do not establish a causal relationship. Further testing of discriminant validity is required to empirically distinguish between these constructs. This study provides insight into how family-relational factors and intrapersonal capacities relate to the psychological…

Too good to resist? Affective engagement and a competence–regulation gap predict self-reported over-reliance on generative AI among vocational foreign-language learners
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has been adopted by students faster than nearly any earlier educational technology, yet over-reliance remains underexamined precisely among the learners inspiring that concern. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study identified predictors of self-reported over-reliance among foreign-language majors ( n = 249) at a Chinese higher vocational college. Quantitative findings revealed two patterns. First, affective factors dominated: fear of missing out ( β = 0.50) and anthropomorphic attachment ( β = 0.27) were the strongest predictors, whereas neither self-regulated learning nor perceived AI literacy was related to over-reliance on its own ( r = −0.03 and 0.08, both ns). Because these two overlap substantially ( r = 0.67), the opposite-signed coefficients they take in the model cannot be interpreted in isolation. What mattered instead was their gap: the discrepancy between feeling AI-literate and reporting that one regulates one’s own learning predicted over-reliance ( β = 0.21), persisting even under controls for acquiescent responding. Second, person-centered and configurational analyses agreed: learners low in affective engagement reported the least over-reliance ( M = 3.19). Parental emotion regulation and preschoolers’ social-emotional competence in Chinese families: the mediating role of child emotion regulation and the moderating role of parental psychological flexibility
abstract: Background Young children’s social-emotional competence serves as a crucial foundation for their early development and is associated with psychological adjustment, academic achievement, and long-term outcomes. Based on the extended process model of emotion regulation and family systems theory, this study constructed and tested a moderated mediation model examining the associations among parental emotion regulation, children’s emotion regulation, children’s social-emotional competence, and parental psychological flexibility in caregiving. Methods Using convenience sampling, an online questionnaire survey was conducted with parents of children aged 3–6 years from multiple provinces in China, including Sichuan and Guangdong. A total of 566 questionnaires were collected, and after data cleaning, 556 valid responses were retained (valid response rate: 98.2%). Participants included 253 fathers and 303 mothers. Measurement tools included the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, the Emotion Regulation Checklist, the Parental Psychological Flexibility Questionnaire, and the Social-Emotional Learning Scale (Parent Version). title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
abstract: Abstract We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. title: Early Depression After First Ever Minor Stroke — Frequency, Course and Important Risk Factors — Case-Control Study
abstract: Early post-stroke depression (PSD) is associated with poor outcome after a stroke. The aim of our study was to examine the risk factors, frequency and severity of early PSD after a minor stroke. Material and methods: We examined 109 post-stroke survivors with minor strokes and 112 control subjects. The control subjects were examined once, the stroke patients were examined on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd day and in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd months after the incident via Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS). All results were interpreted at a 95% confidence level (p < 0.05). Results show that PSD was with high frequency during the first three days after the stroke and its prevalence and severity decreased over time to 30% by the 3rd month. It is associated with ageing, female gender, high-level formal education, loneliness, stroke severity and disability and number of vascular risk factors, but not with stroke location. This study shows that early post-stroke depression in patients with minor stroke is a common and multifactorial condition associated with a complex clinical course and several important risk factors.

title: The warning effect of regulatory texts: retail investors’ risk perception from the perspective of exchange inquiry letters
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how retail investors recognize risk signals from exchange annual report inquiry letters, and reveal the transmission mechanism: internal control deficiencies retail risk perception stock price correction in China’s retail dominated capital market. Design/methodology/approach Using 2018–2024 A-share data and text analysis, the authors measure retail investors’ risk perception from East Money Stock Forum, and adopt an event study and mediating effect model for empirical tests. Findings Internal control deficiency information in inquiry letters significantly triggers retail risk perception, which fully mediates the relationship between inquiry text features and short-term price correction. The warning effect is more pronounced in firms with poor information environments, pessimistic pre-event sentiment or earnings losses. Regulatory signals and contextual factors jointly shape retail investors’ risk perception. Research limitations/implications Sentiment data reflect online posts only; unobserved factors may affect retail sentiment. Practical implications Regulators should optimize the expression and structure of inquiry letters to enhance the clarity and identifiability of core risk signals, so that retail investors can accurately capture and interpret regulatory warnings, thereby improving the efficiency of non-punitive regulation and capital m…

title: The Validity of Algorithm-Based Automated State Administration Decisions in the Single Submission Online System Reviewed from Hans Kelsen's Norm Individualization Theory
abstract: Indonesia’s Online Single Submission (OSS) system has automated various aspects of risk-based business licensing, raising legal questions concerning the validity of electronically issued state administrative decisions and accountability for potential administrative errors. This study examined the legal validity of automated administrative decisions across different business licensing risk categories and analyzed the role of algorithmic decision-making through Hans Kelsen’s theory of norm individualization. The study employed doctrinal legal research, integrating statutory and conceptual approaches with grammatical and systematic interpretations of relevant legislation and an examination of legal scholarship. The findings indicated that electronic administrative documents could satisfy the legal requirement of written form, provided that their authenticity, origin, and content were verifiable. However, the validity of automated administrative decisions also depended on lawful administrative authority, procedural compliance, and conformity with substantive licensing requirements. Automated issuance was most readily justified for low-risk business activities, whereas medium-low-risk activities relied on applicants’ declarations of compliance and remained subject to subsequent administrative oversight. title: Research on the Daily Frequency Time Structure Components of China’s Real-Time Carbon Emissions —Based on the Prophet Framework Model
abstract: To accurately characterize the time structure of China’s daily CO 2 emissions, this study uses daily data from the Carbon Monitor database spanning 2019–2025, covering total emissions and six sectoral categories: domestic aviation, ground transport, industry, international aviation, power, and residential. The Prophet framework is adopted to decompose the emission time series into four components: long-term trend, nonlinear seasonal component, holiday effect term, and COVID-19 impact term. Results show that the model achieves excellent fitting accuracy, with outstanding performance in international aviation and residential sectors, and low error levels across all sectors. In terms of long-term trends, total emissions exhibit a steady decline after 2022, the industry and power sectors are significantly influenced by the “dual carbon” policy and energy structure adjustment, whereas the transport sectors display phased recovery corresponding to changes in travel demand. For seasonal components, periodic peaks are observed in the residential and power sectors, fluctuations in ground transport align with travel demand patterns, and aviation sectors present weak seasonal characteristics with more moderate fluctuations during the pandemic. Effect of wingbeat frequency and stroke plane angle on aerodynamic efficiency and stability in hovering flight
abstract: Flapping insects must balance energetic efficiency, stability, and maneuverability, yet the physical interrelationships among these objectives remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed a validated computational fluid dynamics framework integrating aerodynamics and flight dynamics to investigate how the wingbeat frequency and stroke plane angle affect the hovering flight of the hawkmoth. Starting from previously measured hovering kinematics, we varied each parameter independently in a numerical analysis (without new animal experiments). Our analyses revealed a trade-off between energy efficiency and lateral dynamic stability. Kinematic adjustments that improve energy efficiency by increasing spatial utilization (e.g., maximizing the actuator disk area) tend to reduce the roll damping, the stabilizing aerodynamic effect that resists lateral tilting disturbances, thereby increasing lateral instability. Conversely, kinematics that enhance roll damping require substantially higher mechanical power. Consequently, the measured natural kinematics of the hawkmoth lie within an intermediate region of this efficiency–stability trade-off in the explored parameter space, providing a stability margin that may support active postural control while limiting energy expenditure. These findings suggest that the diversity of insect wing kinematics and morphologies may be influenced by t…

title: A Living Law Based Model for Regional Regulation Drafting Regency under Law Number 1 of 2023
abstract: The model for drafting regional regulations discussed in this article is motivated by the enactment of Law No. 1 of 2023 concerning the Criminal Code (KUHP), which replaces its predecessor . The revised KUHP accommodates the concept of living law to preserve the living culture continuously transmitted within regions . To operationalize this, regional regulations serving as implementation frameworks are essential . The enactment of Law No. 1 of 2023 further underscores the importance of establishing such regulations. Previous research across various disciplines has examined this issue: constitutional law studies have focused on the legislative drafting for regional regulations; criminal law studies have highlighted the challenges uncodified living law faces within the formal hierarchy of legislation; and legal sociology studies have examined the sociolegal conditions surrounding the societal acceptance of living law in contemporary settings. . Given these conditions, this study aims to formulate an appropriate model for guiding the drafting/formulation of Regional Regulation drafts incorporating living law ensuring that the resulting regulations can be effectively implemented.

title: Influence of source expertise on the detection and regulation of comprehension difficulties in reading science texts: failing to understand the world vs. failing to understand the text
abstract: This study investigates how source expertise influence readers’ reporting of comprehension difficulties in science texts, their assessment of text comprehensibility, and the attribution of causes for the reported problems. Secondary school students were presented with challenging science paragraphs supposedly taken from textbooks or from other students’ science reports. The participants had to explicitly point out comprehension difficulties and provide a quantitative assessment of the difficulty of each paragraph. Expertise conditions did not present significant differences regarding the total number of reported problems or text comprehensibility scores. However, the source of low expertise was significantly associated with students attributing comprehension difficulties to an external cause: the linguistic representation and the author. The difference in the attribution of these difficulties suggests that future research should consider a different influence of source expertise on the detection and regulation stages.

title: Glycyrrhizin ameliorates vitiligo by regulating HMGB1-induced M1 macrophage polarization and mediating inflammatory response
abstract: Vitiligo is an autoimmune depigmenting disorder characterized by melanocyte destruction, with progressive vitiligo posing therapeutic challenges due to unclear molecular mechanisms. This study investigated the role of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1)-mediated macrophage polarization in vitiligo progression. Methods included suction blisters collection from progressive vitiligo patients at vitiligous and normal sites, measurement of mRNA levels of HMGB1 and interleukin-18 (IL-18) by RT-qPCR, cytokines (interleukin-1β [IL-1β], C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 9 [CXCL9], CXCL10, and interferon-γ [IFN-γ]) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and analysis of macrophage markers (CD68, CD86, CD206) in skin biopsies via immunohistochemistry. In vitro , RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells were stimulated with HMGB1, with or without caspase-1 small interfering RNA (siRNA) transfection, and co-cultured with normal human epidermal melanocytes (NHEMs) to assess melanin content and tyrosinase (TYR) activity. Moreover, a vitiligo mouse model was established and treated with glycyrrhizin (HMGB1 inhibitor) for 21 days. RT-qPCR showed increased HMGB1 and IL-18 mRNA levels, while ELISA revealed elevated IL-1β, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ protein levels in blister fluid from patients with progressive vitiligo. Enhancing diagnostic ability in oral mucosal lesions using a flipped classroom and audience response system
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate whether a flipped classroom–based online course supported by active learning tools improves diagnostic performance and self-confidence for diagnosing oral lesions among undergraduate dental students. Methods A 14-week online course on oral mucosal lesion diagnosis was conducted between August and December 2021 with 27 undergraduate dental students. The course adopted a flipped classroom model, combining asynchronous learning with weekly 90-minute synchronous sessions focused on clinical case discussions. An audience response system was used to promote active participation. The syllabus covered common oral mucosal lesions, including ulcers, nodules, erosions, and plaques. Educational effectiveness was assessed using a pre- and posttest design based on a 30-item image-based quiz that required classification of lesions as benign, potentially malignant, or malignant. Participants’ self-confidence was assessed using a two-item Likert-scale instrument adapted from previous studies that measured confidence in diagnosing oral lesions. Moreover, students’ perceptions of the teaching strategy were evaluated through a post-course questionnaire. Results A significant improvement in diagnostic performance was observed after course completion ( p < 0.01, Wilcoxon test), with a mean increase of 25.1% in correct answers. title: Self-Reported State Empathy in Response to Video Stimuli: Comparing the Measurement Characteristics of Cognitive and Affective Empathy
abstract: In this study, we propose an 8-item self-reported state empathy scale comprising four cognitive empathy (CE) and four affective empathy (AE) items to evaluate empathic responses to video stimuli on a per-trial basis and examine its measurement characteristics. For a scale to function as a state measurement, its scores must fluctuate according to the nature of the presented scene, rather than only with stable between-participant differences. Therefore, we had 10 participants repeatedly respond to 24 video stimuli and decomposed the variation in the resulting 240 trials into stimulus effects, participant effects, and residuals. We further conducted correlation analyses using the inclusion of other in the self (IOS) scale and emotion congruence as external criteria for AE and video accuracy rate as an external criterion for CE. In the AE subscale, 42.8% of the variance was attributed to stimulus effects and 8.9% to participant effects, and AE correlated positively with the IOS ( r =.772) and emotion congruence ( r =.308). Conversely, in the CE subscale, the participant effect (33.9%) exceeded the stimulus effect (12.0%), no positive correlation with the video accuracy rate was found, and the CE scores remained high even in incorrect emotion recognition trials. These results suggest that AE captures affective empathic responses that vary with video stimuli, whereas CE, whose intern…

title: Case Report: Aortic valve Haemophilus parainfluenzae infective endocarditis complicated by a fistulating aortic root abscess and refractory atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
abstract: This report details the case of a gentleman in his 50s, with a background of previous bicuspid aortic valve infective endocarditis 28 years prior, presenting to hospital with non-specific symptoms, including shivers, headaches and myalgia. Objective clinical findings included pyrexia, hypotension and atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response (AF RVR). He was initially provided with empirical intravenous antibiotics and isotonic fluids to treat an infection of unclear origin. Despite equivocal preliminary imaging findings, blood cultures isolated Haemophilus parainfluenzae , an organism implicating endocarditis, and his antibiotics were switched to Ceftriaxone. Even with this change in antibiotics, he consistently remained febrile, developed a significant Troponin-I leak, and his AF RVR exceeded 200 bpm – unamenable to pharmacological rate and rhythm control therapy. Transoesophageal echocardiography later confirmed an aortic root abscess fistulating into his left ventricular outlet tract, where the patient thereupon underwent an aortic valve replacement with patch reconstruction. Post-procedure, his AF was now responsive to Amiodarone, successfully restoring sinus rhythm. title: Longitudinal blood multi-omics identifies immune-inflammatory trajectories associated with recurrence and response during immune checkpoint inhibitor-containing therapy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
abstract: Background Immune-inflammatory states in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) evolve across surgery, recurrence, systemic therapy, response, and progression, whereas most circulating biomarkers are measured at one time point. Methods This retrospective analysis of prospectively banked biospecimens included a discovery cohort of 240 patients treated from 2018 to 2020 and a temporally independent validation cohort of 160 patients treated from 2021 to 2022 at The Affiliated Huaian No.1 People’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University. Longitudinal whole-blood transcriptomics, plasma proximity-extension proteomics, and plasma liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry metabolomics were obtained before and after resection or immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-containing therapy. The five-feature Multi-Omics Immune Trajectory Score (MITS) was defined before outcome modeling and scaled with locked discovery-baseline parameters. Postoperative analyses used a day-30 landmark, ICI progression analyses used a week-6 landmark, and orthogonal assay agreement was evaluated with patient-clustered repeated-measures methods. Results Immune-inflammatory factor 1 explained 66.6% of cross-omics variance, and MITS was strongly correlated with this factor (Spearman ρ = 0.97). After resection, mean MITS decreased from -0.19 to -0.66 SD units but rebounded in patients with recurrence. In day-30 landmark…

title: Effects of exercise type and dose on anxiety symptoms in university students: a systematic review, Bayesian network meta-analysis, and dose–response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Background Structured exercise may improve anxiety symptoms in university students, but comparative effects across exercise types and dose–response relationships remain uncertain. We synthesized randomized controlled trial evidence to evaluate overall effects, compare exercise modalities, and examine measurement-phase and continuous dose–response patterns. Methods Randomized controlled trials in university or other higher-education students were eligible if structured exercise lasted at least 2 weeks and anxiety was assessed with validated scales. Effects were expressed as Hedges’ g , with positive values favoring exercise. Bayesian multilevel network meta-analysis compared exercise types at post-intervention. A multilevel model synthesized eligible non-baseline effects across during-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up measurements while accounting for within-study dependence. Continuous relationships were examined for exercise intensity, per-session dose, and weekly dose, with alternative models and influence analyses used to assess robustness. Results Thirty-seven independent trials (2,968 participants) contributed to the post-intervention network. Compared with non-exercise controls, aerobic exercise ( g = 0.517, 95% CrI 0.167–0.866), yoga ( g = 0.670, 0.336–0.994), and traditional Chinese mind–body exercise ( g = 0.608, 0.297–0.919) showed CrIs excluding 0. title: A novel secretome rewrites the immune response in viral acute respiratory distress syndrome
abstract: Background Hyperinflammatory syndromes such as viral acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) demand immunotherapies that are safe and effective at suppressing cytokine storm. Cell-free secretomes such as PRS CK STORM, derived from cocultures of M2 macrophages and mesenchymal stromal cells, may represent a novel treatment strategy for ARDS. Methods A preclinical animal study was performed to test the effects of PRS CK STORM in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice infected intranasally with 10 5 PFU of SARS-CoV-2 BE.1.1. This was complemented by an in vitro mechanistic analysis of this secretome using transcriptomic, cytokine secretion, and COX2 enzymatic activity studies, as well as a compositional analysis of its proteomic and miRNA profile. Results In a lethal SARS-CoV-2 ARDS mouse model, PRS CK STORM significantly improved lung histopathology to a degree on par with corticosteroids, while stimulating angiogenesis in damaged lung tissue. Early and late cytokine profiling showed marked reductions in IFN-γ. In response to PRS CK STORM treatment, transcriptomic analyses in inflamed macrophages revealed robust downregulation of key proinflammatory drivers (MyD88, TRAF6, IKK2, NF-κB, COX2). In vitro enzymatic assays confirmed potent, dose-dependent inhibition of COX2, with high inter-batch reproducibility. title: Esplenectomía como factor de riesgo de infecciones del sistema nervioso central: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre la esplenectomía como factor de riesgo de infecciones del sistema nervioso central. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: cohortes, revisiones y guías de práctica clínica. Resultados: la pérdida de la función esplénica reduce la eliminación de bacterias encapsuladas, principales causas de meningitis bacteriana. Una cohorte de 8149 veteranos mostró un riesgo de meningitis más del doble tras la esplenectomía. El riesgo persistió durante años y varió según la indicación y la edad. La vacunación, la profilaxis antibiótica y la educación del paciente fueron las medidas preventivas recomendadas. Conclusión: la esplenectomía aumenta el riesgo de meningitis bacteriana y exige prevención sostenida.

title: CEOs’ job-hopping experience and supply chain relationships: insights from the attention-based view
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the attention-based view, this study examines how CEOs’ job-hopping experience shapes supply chain relationships through managerial attention to supplier search and market expansion, and how CEOs’ R&D and production-line experience moderate these effects. Design/methodology/approach Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2024, this study hand-codes CEOs’ job-hopping experience from resumes and measures supplier and customer concentration based on disclosed top-five trading partner shares. We use fixed-effects models, mechanism and moderation tests and a series of robustness and endogeneity analyses. Findings Firms led by CEOs with more job-hopping experience exhibit higher supplier and customer concentration. Upstream, CEOs devote less attention to alternative supplier search, reflected in fewer tender projects and lower procurement-related recruitment, concentrating purchases among established suppliers. Downstream, CEOs give lower priority to market expansion, reflected in lower advertising expenditure and sales- and marketing-related recruitment, concentrating sales among established customers. CEOs’ R&D experience strengthens the supplier-side association, whereas their production-line experience strengthens the customer-side association. Both associations are stronger in non-state-owned firms and those facing greater performance pressure or high…

title: Women’s entrepreneurial agency in context: evidence from maritime shipping
abstract: Purpose Female entrepreneurship research has focused predominantly on structural conditions, offering limited insight into individual agency. Using the 5M framework (money, market, management, motherhood and the macro/meso environment), this study aims to examine how Angeliki Frangou, CEO and Chairwoman of Navios, enacts agency as a female entrepreneur within the structural conditions of her background and the maritime shipping industry, extending the female entrepreneurship literature’s predominantly structural focus. Design/methodology/approach The authors conduct an in-depth single-case study of Frangou, drawing on public-domain sources, including interviews, speeches and media coverage. Findings Although the 5M framework captures structural dimensions of Frangou’s path, these alone do not fully explain her actions and outcomes. Elements of entrepreneurial agency: ability, motivation, opportunity, institutions and process skill are visible within each 5M dimension, shaping how she interprets and manages resources, opportunities and constraints. This is most evident in how she reframes conditions typically read as threats (e.g. market downturns, crises) as opportunities for strategic action. Research limitations/implications Our single-case design offers a theoretically grounded account; future comparative studies could extend our findings across entrepreneurs with differing …

title: A decentralized approach to construction project management using blockchain technology
abstract: Purpose This study addresses limitations of centralized construction project management systems, including lack of transparency, accountability and collaboration, and aims to develop and validate a decentralized blockchain-based approach for construction project management. Design/methodology/approach Using the Design Science Research methodology, a decentralized platform integrating Ethereum, InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) and Node.js was developed for asset tracking, progress monitoring and performance evaluation. The framework was validated across six large-scale construction projects in Egypt using project documents, blockchain records and system reports. Performance, latency, storage efficiency and expert assessment were evaluated, with smart contracts supporting asset versioning and progress control and IPFS enabling traceable off-chain storage. Expert assessment involved 15 construction professionals and project managers. Findings Application across six construction projects (49 Master Reports and 335 Progress Reports) demonstrated the framework's operational feasibility for near-real-time monitoring and traceable information management. Transaction and query latencies were below 5 and 2 s, respectively, while IPFS-based off-chain storage reduced on-chain requirements by up to 99.91%. The ZED Towers Phase 1B case confirmed traceable linkage between progress records an…

title: Electron-Donation and Hydrophilicity Synergy in Side-Chain Engineered COFs: Enhanced Photocatalytic U(VI) Reduction
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic U(VI) reduction is vital for radioactive wastewater treatment, yet covalent organic frameworks (COFs) face limitations in charge carrier separation and transport, with insufficient studies on functional group effects. Herein, three donor–acceptor COFs (TfBD, TfBD-CH3, and TfBD-OH) were synthesized to investigate electron-donating group modifications. Enhanced light absorption, narrowed bandgaps, increased photocurrent density, and reduced impedance were confirmed. Consequently, the reduction efficiency of U(VI) increased from 73% for TfBD to 77% for TfBD-CH3 and 91% for TfBD-OH, with stronger electron-donating ability leading to superior performance. TfBD-OH exhibited comparable removal efficiency in uranium-spiked seawater due to its synergistic effect of hydrophilicity and electron-donating groups. DFT calculations showed that TfBD-OH had the lowest adsorption energy for U(VI), while photogenerated H2O2 promoted U(VI) removal via formation of (UO2)O2·2H2O precipitates. This study demonstrates a viable strategy for side-chain-modified COFs in photocatalytic uranium enrichment.

title: O‘ZBEKISTON RESPUBLIKASI SUD TIZIMIDA GENDER TENGLIK: 2018–2026-YILLARDA AYOL SUDYALAR ISHTIROKINING DINAMIKASI VA HUDUDIY TAHLIL
abstract: Ushbu maqolada O‘zbekiston Respublikasi sud tizimidagi gender tenglik masalalari 2018–2026-yillar kesimida dinamik rivojlanish va hududiy-funksional tahlil asosida tizimli tadqiq etilgan. Tadqiqotda soʻnggi yillardagi institutsional islohotlar va milliy qonunchilikdagi oʻzgarishlar, xususan, 2019-yilgi O‘RQ-562-sonli Qonun doirasidagi amaliy natijalar va strategik vazifalar tahlil qilingan. Sudyalar Oliy kengashi va xalqaro tashkilotlar (BMTTD, USAID) ma’lumotlari asosida ayol sudyalar ulushining 2020-yildagi 11,9% dan 2026-yilda 15,4% gacha oʻsish tendensiyasi koʻrsatilgan. Yakunda sud tizimida gender muvozanatni ta’minlash boʻyicha amaliy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan.

Room-Temperature Magnetoelectric Behavior in a Photoferroic SbCoSI Chalcohalide System
abstract: Abstract Significant experimental efforts have been undertaken to investigate the optical processes that facilitate charge transfer and influence the magnetic and transport properties of a transition element-doped chalcohalide system, consisting of 1.0 mol % Co-substituted SbSI microrods synthesized via a sonochemical route. Consequently, the collective and complementary evidence from Rietveld refinement of XRD data, elemental compositional analysis, EDAX elemental mapping, optical absorption measurements, and Raman spectroscopy strongly supports the successful incorporation of cobalt into the host lattice through atomic substitution at the Sb site. Magnetic measurements reveal a broad anomaly near 200 K, characteristic of superparamagnetic blocking, while the low-temperature response exhibits ferromagnetic-like behavior. Moreover, the M versus H/T curves collapse onto a single curve above 200 K, providing further evidence for superparamagnetic behavior. A field-induced enhancement of permittivity near the blocking regime demonstrates a positive magnetodielectric response, indicating coupling between magnetic and dielectric degrees of freedom. The linearity of the Δε′(H) vs M2 plot is phenomenologically described with the Ginzburg–Landau theory with the magnetoelectric coupling term γP2M2. Moreover, the photoinduced enhancement of dielectric response under magnetic fields highl…

title: SmartPost AI: An AI-Assisted Framework for Intelligent Professional Content Creation and Automated LinkedIn Management
abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has had a significant impact on the area of AI-assisted content generation, providing capabilities to generate coherent context-aware text for different purposes. However, current solutions of AI writing assistants are limited in terms of addressing all aspects of professional content management, which include contextual information retrieval, organization, scheduling, persistent cloud storage, and automated publishing. Therefore, users are required to use several separate solutions, making their workflow less efficient and more labour-intensive. In this paper, we introduce SmartPost AI - an end-to-end framework for AI-assisted professional content creation and LinkedIn management. The framework utilizes the combination of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LLMs, cloud-based data management, and LinkedIn API-based publishing, all integrated in one multi-layered architecture. The proposed framework enables users to provide either text prompts or web-based content, retrieve relevant contextual information, generate LinkedIn posts in professional format, convert Markdown output into Unicode-based formatting, and manage content centrally via secure storage, scheduling, and publishing capabilities. The framework is deployed as a cloud-based full-stack web application using Next.js, FastAPI, Supabase , and LinkedIn APIs. Deploy…

title: Cold chain logistics capability and agri-food product quality performance: The moderating role of supply chain financing
abstract: Background: Maintaining agri-food product quality in sub-Saharan Africa remains challenging because of inadequate cold chain infrastructure and financing constraints. Although cold chain logistics capability is essential for reducing post-harvest losses, little is known about how supply chain finance orientations influence its effectiveness. Objectives: This study examines the effect of cold chain logistics capability on agri-food product quality performance and investigates whether relationship-oriented and financial institution-oriented supply chain finance moderate this relationship. Method: Survey data were collected from 631 agribusinesses in Ghana and Nigeria. Covariance-based structural equation modelling and moderated regression analysis were used to test the hypothesised relationships. Results: Cold chain logistics capability significantly improves agri-food product quality performance. Relationship-oriented supply chain finance weakens this relationship, whereas financial institution-oriented supply chain finance has no significant moderating effect. Further analysis shows that combining relationship- and financial institution-oriented financing enhances the quality benefits of cold storage operations but not refrigerated transport. Conclusion: The quality benefits of cold chain logistics capability depend on firms’ financing arrangements. While cold chain investments…

title: An Event-Driven Edge AI Surveillance System with Real-Time Automated Alerting
abstract: Traditional surveillance networks rely on continuous video recording, which demands immense data storage, consumes high network bandwidth, and serves primarily as a passive forensic tool rather than an active deterrent. While basic motion-activated systems mitigate storage waste, they suffer from critically high false-alarm rates triggered by environmental noise. To resolve this, we propose an event-driven Edge AI surveil-lance architecture using a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ paired with an OV5647 NoIR camera. The system utiliz-es a time-domain decoupled approach: an NS312 PIR sensor acts as a strict zero-power hardware interrupt, keeping the processing pipeline dormant until physical motion is detected. Upon activation, an onboard OpenCV Haar Cascade classifier executes instantaneous face verification to definitively confirm human presence, completely eliminating false positives. The Python-based firmware employs multithreaded concurrency to simul-taneously trigger a localized 5V active piezo buzzer for on-site deterrence, dispatch annotated visual alerts via the Telegram Bot API, and maintain a thread-safe Flask MJPEG web stream. Physical validation on Debian 13 "Trixie" demonstrates stable zero-light operation, miti-gation of I2C brownouts, and sub-3-second alert latency without reliance on cloud-based AI.
