title: A Dynamic Safety System for Mitigating the Severity of Motor Vehicle Accidents
abstract:
The advent of crash prediction systems creates the opportunity to mitigate crash severity by applying a pre-crash acceleration pulse to the seat (and occupant). The “Preflex system,” patented by Broadhead/Zinke in 2026, is unique in that the strategic timing of the Preflex pre-crash pulse works in concert with the impending crashpulse to significantly reduce occupant injury risk.
With Preflex, a pre-crash rearward acceleration pulse is applied to the seat milliseconds before the impact. The vehicle crashpulse then stops the seat’s rearward motion prior to reaching a rearward excursion limit. As the crashpulse continues, subsequent forward movement of the seat further extends the time and distance over which the occupant’s energy is dissipated. This seat motion is controlled by a Variable Force Thruster System (VFTS) that provides force profiles to the seat (and occupant) parallel to the longitudinal crash force component.
The Preflex was explored by computer modeling and full-scale frontal sled tests with a Hybrid III Anthropomorphic Test Device (ATD). Baseline tests of a conventional restraint system without Preflex were conducted for comparison.
The dynamic testing of the Preflex demonstrated that, by init…

title: Increased cover crop biomass and exposure time reduces spring emergence of the navel orangeworm in a Mediterranean almond system
abstract: Almonds are an economically important specialty crop for the United States, which produces approximately 80% of the global almond crop. Most of this production comes from California, where almond growers have become more interested in incorporating winter cover crops to promote soil health and improve orchard sustainability. However, the benefits of winter cover crops could potentially extend to pest abatement as well. The main arthropod pest of almonds is the navel orangeworm, Amyelois transitella Walker, which directly attacks the developing new crop nuts, leading to reduced yield and quality. Crop sanitation is considered the foundation of A. transitella management, as the moths overwinter in remnant nuts and rely on them as a reproductive substrate in the spring. Natural mortality of overwintering A. transitella is known to occur, and there is evidence that this may be enhanced when infested remnant nuts reside within ground covers. However, the effects of functionally diverse ground covers on overwintering A. transitella have yet to be explored. In this study, remnant mummy nuts infested with A. transitella were placed for varied exposure durations into six different cover crop mixtures, along with an untreated, weedy control and a weed-free herbicide control over two winter seasons. Vegetative biomass, remnant mummy nut degradation, and spring emergence of overwintered A.…

title: Integrated physiology and transcriptomics reveal effects of summer-autumn canopy management on spring tea growth and quality
abstract: Canopy management in summer and autumn plays a critical role in regulating the yield and quality of subsequent spring tea. However, the physiological and molecular mechanisms underlying canopy management responses in tea plants remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated three summer-autumn canopy management practices through integrated phenotypic and transcriptomic analyses to elucidate their effects on tea plant growth and tea quality. Our findings revealed that summer-autumn pruning practices significantly influenced subsequent spring shoot traits. The NP (shoot retention without pruning) maintained shoot length comparable to the CK (conventional plucking and pruning), but significantly reduced 100-bud weight by 22.4% at the bud stage, while consistently increasing fresh leaf yield by 7.9-15.9% relative to CK across all tenderness grades. Retention treatments (especially NP) significantly increased water extract content by 7.6-12.5% and tea polyphenol accumulation, while also elevating caffeine content at early stages compared with CK. Amino acid content was generally suppressed under retention treatments relative to CK. Besides, NP significantly increased ester-type catechins (particularly epigallocatechin gallate, gallocatechin gallate, and epicatechin gallate), conversely CK maintained higher levels of theanine and glutamic acid contents. Through transcriptomic…

title: Estrategias de eliminación y manejo de la morbilidad de la filariasis linfática: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre las estrategias de eliminación de la filariasis linfática, la eficacia de los esquemas de administración masiva de medicamentos y el manejo de la morbilidad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: ensayos clínicos, evaluaciones de programas, revisiones y análisis económicos. Resultados: el programa mundial redujo de forma considerable la población en riesgo y evitó millones de casos. El tratamiento triple con ivermectina, dietilcarbamazina y albendazol eliminó la microfilaremia con mayor frecuencia que los esquemas de dos fármacos y fue seguro. La morbilidad crónica persistió después de interrumpir la transmisión. Conclusión: la eliminación requiere administración masiva con alta cobertura, vigilancia sostenida y atención continua del linfedema y el hidrocele.

title: Decision Support System for Production Machine Maintenance Prioritization Using LOPCOW Weighting and SPOTIS
abstract: Maintenance of production machines is essential for maintaining production continuity and minimizing the risk of downtime and operational losses. However, limited maintenance resources, including budget, technician availability, maintenance time, and spare parts, require organizations to establish appropriate maintenance priorities. This study proposes a Decision Support System (DSS) for objectively prioritizing production machine maintenance using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) approach that integrates the LOPCOW and SPOTIS methods. LOPCOW is applied to determine objective criterion weights based on the characteristics and variation of the maintenance data, while SPOTIS is used to rank production machines according to their distance from the ideal solution. The results show that C7 obtains the highest criterion weight of 0.2616, followed by C5 (0.2134) and C6 (0.1937), while C2 obtains the lowest weight of 0.0412. The SPOTIS results produce the maintenance priority sequence M4, M7, M2, M5, M1, M8, M3, and M6, with M4 achieving the highest priority with a final value of 0.0000, while M6 has the lowest priority with 1.0000. These findings demonstrate that the proposed LOPCOW–SPOTIS framework can provide a systematic, objective, and transparent basis for identifying maintenance priorities and supporting more consistent allocation of limited maintenance resources.

title: The interplay between management and business models in B2B contexts: a case study in the pharmaceutical industry
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the interplay between management model (MM) and business model (BM) in complex business-to-business (B2B) environments. Specifically, it analyzes how the MM, viewed through management control systems (MCS), may operate as an internal enabling layer for BM effectiveness in the regulated pharmaceutical sector. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a holistic qualitative case study design within a Brazilian pharmaceutical company. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 14 managers, document analysis and direct observation. Temporal Bracketing was used to compare the pre-change period (T0) and post-change period (T1), with triangulation across interview, documentary, observational and financial evidence. Findings The case suggests that, in B2B markets characterized by powerful downstream actors, BM effectiveness depends not only on value proposition and market positioning, but also on internal managerial mechanisms that support value capture. Planning routines, contribution margin reports, business intelligence (BI) dashboards, profitability-based targets and revised incentives were associated with greater margin visibility, more disciplined negotiations and improved control over discounts, trade funds and bonus policies. Financial indicators after the transformation were consistent with this process-based interpretati…

Derecho a la identidad cultural y protección de los pueblos indígenas en el ordenamiento jurídico ecuatoriano
abstract: La Constitución ecuatoriana de 2008 define un Estado intercultural y plurinacional con derechos colectivos indígenas, pero la distancia entre ese reconocimiento y su eficacia sigue en debate. El estudio analizó el derecho a la identidad cultural y los mecanismos de protección de los pueblos indígenas en Ecuador. Con enfoque cualitativo descriptivo-analítico, se analizaron documentalmente la Constitución, el Convenio 169 de la OIT, la Declaración de Naciones Unidas sobre pueblos indígenas, jurisprudencia constitucional e interamericana y doctrina indexada. Los resultados muestran un marco amplio que vincula identidad, territorio, consulta previa y justicia propia, con tensiones en la consulta, el reconocimiento territorial y la coordinación entre jurisdicciones. Se concluye que proteger la identidad cultural exige desarrollo legislativo y aplicación intercultural efectiva.

title: Prediction models for reimagining human spatial cognition (queue congestion management)
abstract: Research on smart cities has paid considerable attention to vehicles, yet the movement of people through stations, shops, stadiums, and public buildings raises a different set of questions. Pedestrians do not simply follow the shortest available route. They read architectural cues, relate their position to one another, negotiate personal space, and apply different reactions to uncertainty. This article develops a theoretical model for predicting and managing queue congestion in human-centered environments. Rather than treating environmental data as a direct count of occupants, this article calls on using data only as contextual evidence and acknowledges its uncertainty. The study contributes a structured connection between traffic-prediction research, spatial cognition, and pedestrian queue management. It also sets out limitations concerning sensing accuracy, cultural variation, accessibility, privacy, and evaluation. Because the proposal has not been tested empirically, it is presented as a research framework rather than a validated operational system.

title: Unveiling patent strategies: hybrid-weighted analysis of the global semiconductor industry
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify strategic patent portfolio archetypes in semiconductors through data-driven clustering, revealing how firms balance patent quality and volume to achieve competitive advantage. Design/methodology/approach K-means clustering is applied to 728 semiconductor firms holding 99,777 USPTO patents (2019–2024) using patent volume and Essential Patent Index (EPI) as clustering dimensions. We introduce hybrid assignee importance weighting (40% employees, 30% revenue, 30% patents), enhancing citation-based quality metrics beyond traditional patent-only approaches. Validation employs silhouette analysis, external outcome prediction and robustness checks. Findings Three distinct strategic archetypes emerge with exceptional cluster separation (silhouette = 0.496). Elite Impact Leaders (12.9% of firms) achieve 25.0 times higher patent efficiency than Mainstream Followers (68.0%) despite comparable portfolio sizes, leveraging breakthrough patents cited by organizationally significant competitors. Volume Diversifiers (19.1%) pursue scale strategies with large portfolios (median 202 patents) and moderate quality. Geographically, 25.3% of U.S. firms are Elite Impact Leaders, while Japan (75.4%) and China (78.9%) exhibit elevated Mainstream Followers concentrations, suggesting context-dependent strategic positioning. The Effect of Exchange Rates And Interest Rates on The Composite Stock Price Index on The Indonesia Stock Exchange 2015-2025 Period
abstract: This study examines the effect of exchange rates and interest rates on the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2015–2025. A quantitative approach was applied using secondary data from 11 annual observations. The exchange rate was measured by the year-end Rupiah-to-US Dollar middle rate, the interest rate by the year-end Bank Indonesia benchmark rate, and the JCI by its annual closing value. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS Version 26. The results show that the exchange rate has a positive and significant effect on the JCI (coefficient = 0.763; t = 5.404; p = 0.001), whereas the interest rate has no significant partial effect (coefficient = 0.316; t = 0.411; p = 0.692). Simultaneously, both variables significantly affect the JCI (F = 16.594; p = 0.001). The model's R-square is 0.806, while its adjusted R-square is 0.757. These findings indicate that exchange rate movements are significantly associated with JCI fluctuations during the observation period.

The price of knowledge: costs, access, and equity in scholarly publishing
abstract: Scholarly publishing currently determines who can publish their research and who can access others’ work. This Perspective identifies two challenges: a publishing barrier, in which article processing charges (APCs) and editorial practices influence who can afford to publish; and an access barrier, in which subscription paywalls determine who can afford to read. Structural factors, including geography, language, and reviewer representation, further shape these barriers. Recent bibliometric and survey evidence indicates that global spending on APCs nearly tripled between 2019 and 2023; a major commercial publisher reported an adjusted operating margin of 38.4% in its Scientific, Technical and Medical division in 2024; and researchers in the Global South reported lower institutional access to major publisher databases. Additional evidence highlights geographical imbalances in peer review and disparities in informal access to paywalled articles. Although journals incur legitimate costs and publishing models vary, the magnitude of financial and access disparities raises significant questions about equity within the current system. This Perspective proposes that publishers, funders, institutions, editors, and researchers must address both publishing and access barriers, rather than assuming that a general shift toward open access will resolve either issue on its own.

title: Startup sustainability forecasting through natural language processing of business plans
abstract: Abstract Recent surveys show that only 1 in 400 startups secure funding and achieve post-fund sustainability. Startup assessment is becoming increasingly complicated due to the evolving entrepreneurial landscape, which is affected by too many factors, compelling venture capital firms to harness state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI). Natural Language Processing (NLP) offers a promising approach for startup assessment, by analyzing documents that summarize key factors of long-term success. Although startup sustainability research is active, modern NLP for assessing business plans has received limited attention. Specifically, the majority of previous works consider only short text descriptions of startups instead of complete business plans, and do not offer adaptability to the varying investment criteria of different investors. In this paper, we propose ForeStart, a startup sustainability forecasting system powered by a transformer-based language model that offers seamless adaptability to the particular needs of users. The proposed system can analyze business plans of unlimited length, including also startup-related content such as pitch deck presentations and company websites. ForeStart is based on a hierarchical Distilled Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (DistilBERT–BiLSTM) architecture trained using both unsupe…

title: A Geospatial Intelligence System for Land Price Modelling and Property Management: An Offline/Online Android Application for Nyamata Sector, Rwanda
abstract: Property valuation and management in Rwanda face challenges such as fragmented data, manual valuation methods, inconsistent pricing, and limited use of geospatial technologies, leading to inaccurate valuations and inefficient land administration. To address these challenges, this study developed a Geospatial Intelligence System integrating GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and an Android offline/online application for property management and land price modelling in Nyamata Sector, Bugesera District. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study integrated spatial and non-spatial data from cadastral records, satellite imagery, valuation databases, socio-economic datasets, and GPS/GNSS field surveys. Data were collected through satellite imagery, field observations, questionnaires, interviews, and institutional records. A purposive sample of 105 stakeholders, including land officers, valuers, GIS specialists, planners, regulators, telecom professionals, and property owners, participated in the study. Advanced analytical tools such as ArcGIS, QGIS, Python, Multiple Linear Regression, Geographically Weighted Regression, Random Forest, Neural Networks, and XGBoost were used for analysis. The results showed successful integration of over 85% of datasets, with more than 90% of land parcels linked to thematic information. The AI-based valuation model demonstrated excellent…

title: High-Speed Railway Train Delay Prediction Based on Improved CTGAN Generative Data Fusion
abstract: To address the issues of imbalanced and insufficient delay samples in training datasets for high-speed railway (HSR) delay prediction, this study proposes an HSR train delay prediction method based on improved Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) data fusion. This method employs an enhanced CTGAN for delay data generation, in which a transformer is integrated into the generator to better capture the spatiotemporal correlation features constructed from train operation scenarios. The quality of the generated delay data was rigorously analyzed using statistical and distribution similarity metrics, thereby validating the rationality of fusing the generated samples with the original data. Subsequently, a training delay prediction model based on CBLA (CNN-BiLSTM-Attention) was constructed and trained on the augmented dataset derived from data fusion. The output performance of the trained model was tested, and the optimal data fusion ratio was determined. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating CTGAN-generated data significantly enhances the prediction accuracy. Specifically, when the generated data were fused at an optimal ratio of 4:1, the mean absolute error was reduced by approximately 38% and the root mean square error by approximately 78%.

title: Physics-guided TCN–transformer with multi-objective loss for real-time rate-of-penetration prediction in deep geothermal drilling
abstract: Abstract In deep geothermal wells, accurate real-time prediction of rate of penetration (ROP) is crucial for increasing drilling efficiency and minimizing operational costs. Existing machine learning (ML) approaches used for ROP prediction are limited by either not accounting for the basic principles of the physics of drilling or how their architectures are designed, wherein they have a very limited temporal receptive field to capture long-term dependencies of sequential downhole data. Our proposed method combines a TCN (temporal convolutional network) and Transformer (TCT-Phy) model that was trained using a physics-guided multi-objective loss to jointly optimize for empirical accuracy, consistency of MSE (mechanical specific energy), and the constraint regarding physical monotonicity. The proposed model was tested using the Utah FORGE MU-ESW1 dataset, which contains 6,748 quality-filtered records of drilling from a deep geothermal well. The average MAE (mean absolute error) of the proposed method was 4.50 ± 0.43 ft/hr, and the R² coefficient of determination was 0.917. Therefore, the proposed method outperformed a strong background gradient boosting baseline (MAE 8.48), plain TCN (MAE 5.14), and an ablated version without physics guidance (MAE 5.24). Additionally, the presence of the physics loss improved the consistency of MSE by 17.4% compared to the architecture-only ablati…

title: A controlled ablation study of clinically motivated engineered features for heart disease prediction on the Statlog dataset
abstract: Heart disease prediction models increasingly combine machine learning with structured clinical knowledge and explainable artificial intelligence. However, performance claims on small benchmark datasets can be difficult to interpret when feature construction, data partitioning, and metric calculations are not fully reproducible. This study evaluates 13 clinical predictors and eight deterministic, clinically motivated indicators using the UCI Statlog (Heart) dataset (270 records). A fixed stratified 80:20 train–test split (seed 42) was used, with five-fold stratified cross-validation restricted to the 216-record training partition. The indicators were derived directly from the original predictors; the original OWL/SWRL ontology, terminology mappings, source code, and historical prediction artifacts were unavailable. The experiment therefore evaluates deterministic feature augmentation, not formal ontology reasoning. On the 54-record test set, the clinical-only DNN achieved 83.33% accuracy, 80.00% precision, 83.33% recall, 81.63% F1-score, and 0.867 ROC-AUC. The augmented DNN achieved 79.63% accuracy, 72.41% precision, 87.50% recall, 79.25% F1-score, and 0.879 ROC-AUC. These single-split differences are descriptive and should not be interpreted as evidence of improvement: all five cross-validation mean metrics favoured the clinical-only model. The original SHAP figure could not be…

Clinical value of a soft voting ensemble model based on routine clinical indicators for risk prediction and biopsy decision-making of prostate cancer in Chinese men with PSA in the 4–10 ng/mL
abstract: Objectives The differential diagnosis of prostate cancer (PCa) in men with serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels in the 4–10 ng/mL range remains a clinical challenge, and there is currently no reliable quantitative tool to guide biopsy decisions. We sought to build a machine-learning-based model using routine clinical indicators to assist individualized prostate biopsy decisions in this population. Methods A total of 100 patients who underwent prostate biopsy at our center between July 2024 and February 2026 with PSA levels in the 4–10 ng/mL range were retrospectively enrolled, including 18 pathologically confirmed PCa cases and 82 benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) cases. Five routine indicators were included: free-to-total PSA ratio (f/t PSA), prostate health index (PHI), p2PSA, PSA density (PSAD), and prostate volume. A soft voting ensemble model was constructed via Optuna hyperparameter tuning and class imbalance correction, and internal validation was performed using repeated 5-fold cross-validation (20 repetitions). Results The constructed ensemble model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.904 (95% CI: 0.836–0.972), with diagnostic efficacy significantly superior to all single indicators (P < 0.05). The optimal cutoff value determined by maximizing Youden’s index was 0.1726, yielding a negative predictive value (NPV) of …

title: Multimodal lymph node radiomics combined with clinical features for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer: a multicenter study
abstract: Objective To investigate the value of a combined model based on T1-weighted enhancement (T1CE), T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequences of lymph node radiomics features combined with clinical features in the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in rectal cancer. Methods A retrospective cohort from two hospitals (June 2019–Jan 2025) included rectal cancer patients with preoperative MRI. Lymph nodes from Yangpu Hospital (135 nodes, 40 patients) were split into training (n=108) and internal test (n=27) sets; 51 nodes from Shanghai Fourth People’s Hospital served as external test set. Radiomic features from segmented T1CE/T2WI/DWI images and clinical risk factors were used to develop radiomics, clinical, and combined clinical–radiomics models, evaluated for discrimination and calibration. Results The standalone clinical model exhibited suboptimal performance in the training, test, and external test sets, with AUCs of 0.699, 0.779, and 0.663, respectively. Although each individual radiomics model achieved relatively high AUCs in the training set, a general decline in performance was observed in the external test set. The combined model maintained high AUCs across all datasets (training set: 1.000; test set: 0.888; external test set: 0.848). Calibration curve and decision curve analyses also indicated that the combined model had be…

title: Hybrid Ensemble Learning for Diabetes Mellitus Prediction Using SMOTE and RL-Driven Bat Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is a major chronic disease whose early prediction is hindered by complex nonlinear clinical relationships and class imbalance in medical datasets. Existing ensemble and non-ensemble Machine Learning (ML) methods are often degraded by this imbalance, especially for minority-class patients. To Address this problem, this study proposes an adaptive ensemble learning framework that combines the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), Reinforcement Learning (RL), the Bat algorithm, and an AdaBoost-based fitness function to construct an optimized ensemble. SMOTE first balances the training data by generating synthetic minority samples. Then an RL-Driven Bat algorithm explores the ensemble search space to find an optimal set of base classifiers, while the AdaBoost-based fitness function evaluates candidate ensembles and drives performance maximization. The proposed model evaluates on the PIMA Indians Diabetes (PID) dataset, the framework attains 0.95 accuracy and 0.98 specificity. Further, to validate the significance of the proposed framework, a Wilcoxon Signed-Rank (WSR) test is conducted between the proposed model and other ensemble and non-ensemble classifiers. This test shows that p < 0.05 for all traditional ensemble and non-ensemble models, indicating the statistical significance of the proposed model. An ablation study quantifies the i…

title: High-Temperature Damage Recovery of Waste Glass Cementitious Materials: Thermodynamic Prediction and Experimental Validation
abstract: Abstract A critical challenge for fire-resilient infrastructure lies in the inherent thermal instability of conventional cementitious composites under extreme temperatures. To address this gap, this study investigated the dosage-dependent effects of recycled glass powder (GP) in the high-temperature response of cementitious materials. Thermodynamic simulations were first used to predict GP dosage-dependent liquid-phase formation, melt viscosity, and phase assemblage evolution, and the predicted sintering window was then experimentally evaluated. The results showed that GP incorporation promoted the formation of thermally stable crystalline phases, such as rankinite, akermanite, and gehlenite, while reducing the generation of detrimental free CaO and γ-C2S. At 30% GP replacement, the paste exhibited the most favorable recovery after exposure to 1200 °C, retaining 79.3% of its initial compressive strength. After heating, moderate GP incorporation induced viscous flow assisted sintering, pore and crack closure, and ceramic-like microstructural reconstruction. In contrast, excessive GP incorporation generated an overabundant low-viscosity liquid phase, causing over-melting-related dimensional instability. Quantitatively, the residual compressive strength showed strong correlations with the content of thermally stabilized silicate phases and the liquid fraction, with R2 values of 0.…

title: Interpretable machine learning for procedure-specific mortality prediction after open surgical necrosectomy or video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement in infected pancreatic necrosis
abstract: Objective Infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN) carries substantial mortality, and patients undergoing open surgical necrosectomy (OSN) or video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) may exhibit different prognostic profiles. Given the limited clinical data available for surgically treated IPN, this study aimed to develop interpretable, procedure-specific mortality prediction models and characterize distinct prognostic patterns associated with each surgical strategy. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 143 patients from Ruijin Hospital after propensity-score matching on age and sex and subsequent exclusion of one VARD patient, including 96 patients treated with OSN during 2014–2018 and 47 treated with VARD during 2019–2024. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 90 days after the first necrosectomy. Separate CatBoost models were developed using preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables. Internal evaluation included repeated feature selection under fixed CatBoost settings and an additional 10-repetition nested cross-validation analysis with hyperparameter and feature selection confined to each outer training set. Calibration and conditional bootstrap intervals were evaluated using stored predictions from the earlier fixed-parameter analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) characterized global and individual feature-prediction associations. Indep…

title: Establishment and validation of a sepsis risk prediction model for critically ill patients based on neutrophil CD64 combined with clinical indicators
abstract: Objective The construction and validation of a sepsis risk prediction model for critically ill patients based on neutrophil CD64 (nCD64) combined with clinical indicators. The model is applicable for dynamic risk stratification based on clinical data within 24 h after admission. Methods A total of 200 patients treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of our hospital from January 2021 to July 2024 were divided into a modeling group ( n = 140) and a validation group ( n = 60) in a 7:3 ratio. The efficacy differences were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. A nomogram was constructed and subgroup analysis was performed by gender, infected lesion sites, and severity. Independent risk factors were screened by univariate and multivariate logistic regression. The model was validated using the C-index, ROC curve, calibration curve and Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was used to evaluate the clinical net benefit. Results ICU stay time, Sequential Organ Failure Score (SOFA), nCD64, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) were risk factors for sepsis in critically ill patients ( P < 0.05). The C-indices of the modeling group and validation group were 0.877 (95% CI: 0.745–0.956) and 0.849 (95% CI: 0.720–0.933), respectively. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test results showed that the P values of the modeling group ( χ …

title: Student Academic Risk Prediction and Personalized Learning Recommendation Research Based on User Portraits of Learning Situation
abstract: Early identification of students with academic difficulties is challenging in traditional teaching scenarios. This study builds an academic-risk early-warning framework based on educational data mining on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). After missing-value handling and min–max normalization of online learning records, key features such as learning duration, assignment completion rate and test scores are extracted to establish multi-dimensional student profiles, from which low-, medium- and high-risk labels are constructed. A classification model (Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) combined with the multi-dimensional profile features) is applied for academic-risk prediction, and the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is adopted to achieve model interpretability and mitigate the black-box defect of machine learning models. Comparative and ablation experiments show that the proposed model achieves an Accuracy of 0.831 and a macro-F1 of 0.808, exceeding the F1 scores of Logistic Regression and Random Forest by 0.095 and 0.051, respectively, and that each component (the profile module and the early-stopping mechanism) improves overall prediction performance. SHAP analysis quantifies how different learning features affect academic outcomes, helping teachers screen at-risk students and design personalized intervention strategies. Limited by the single…

title: Clinical and genomic characterization of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection: risk factors and development of a clinical prediction model
abstract: Objectives Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) can cause invasive bloodstream infection (BSI) associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and genomic features of hvKP BSI and develop a clinical prediction model to support early risk assessment and identification. Methods Patients with K . pneumoniae BSI were retrospectively enrolled at Fujian Medical University Union Hospital, China, from October 2022 to February 2024. Virulence genes were screened by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and hvKP was defined by the presence of peg-344 together with at least one of rmpA/rmpA2 and at least one of iroN/iucA . Whole-genome sequencing characterized the genomic features of hvKP isolates. Clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable logistic regression and used to develop a clinical prediction model. Results Among 145 non-duplicate K. pneumoniae BSI isolates, 28 (19.3%) were hvKP. Fourteen sequence types (STs) were identified, with ST23 (6/28, 21.4%) being the predominant lineage, while KL2 (7/28, 25.0%) was the most common capsular type. Three isolates (3/28, 10.7%) were carbapenem-resistant hvKP (CR-hvKP) and all belonged to ST11-KL64-OL2, sharing an identical plasmid replicon profile. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified community-acquired BSI, diabetes mellitus, and respiratory diseases were ind…

title: Epistemic blind spots in protein function prediction: uncertainty, homology bias and failure modes in deep learning models
abstract: Protein function prediction has advanced from homology-based annotation transfer to deep learning, protein language models, and multimodal foundation models. Yet improved benchmark performance does not resolve a more basic problem: these systems learn from biological knowledge that is incomplete, heterogeneous in evidential support, and strongly structured by evolutionary relationships. We organize this problem as two sequentially dependent epistemological levels. The first concerns biological knowledge: what functional states become observable, with what evidential support and evolutionary structure. The second concerns what models can legitimately infer from that supervision, including representation sufficiency, uncertainty, generalization, and the scope of a universal computational blueprint for protein function inference. Because limitations at the first level enter the learning problem before model fitting, benchmark performance and model uncertainty cannot by themselves establish certainty about latent biological function. Trustworthy protein AI therefore requires explicit attention to applicability domains, distribution shift, uncertainty, and the limits of inference from available biological knowledge.

title: Can AI Personalise Meaningfulness? Bodies, Prediction, and Postdigital Health and Physical Education
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly woven into Health and Physical Education (HPE) through motion analysis, wearable data, adaptive task design, automated feedback, and generative support for teachers. These developments are often associated with personalisation and, by extension, with the possibility of making learning more meaningful for individual students. This conceptual article questions that connection. Drawing on Kretchmar’s philosophy of meaning in movement, Meaningful Physical Education (MPE), and postdigital accounts of entangled pedagogy and technological mediation, it argues that meaningfulness is not a personalised output but a postdigital accomplishment. It emerges through embodied activity, relationships, material settings, cultural practices, interpretation, and time. Particular AI-supported arrangements may expand or constrain these conditions, but no technical adjustment can guarantee what an experience will come to mean. The analysis develops four tensions: personal relevance between dialogue and prediction; challenge between embodied negotiation and adaptive optimisation; fun, sociality, and delight beyond engagement analytics; and biographical meaning in relation to computational memory. It shows how personalised systems can also influence whose movements, preferences, and histories become visible and valued. The article concludes with fi…

Establishing Effective Diagnostic Criteria for Vulval Lichen Sclerosus in adults: A study to develop risk prediction model and subsequent diagnostic test accuracy study (SHELLS)
abstract: Background Vulval lichen sclerosus (LS) is an inflammatory condition affecting predominantly vulval, perineal and perianal skin. It causes distressing symptoms which impact on daily life, and complications include scarring as well as an increased risk of vulval cancer. LS affects an estimated 1 in 100 women. Symptoms and complications can be minimised by effective treatment. LS is often misdiagnosed, leading to delayed diagnosis and treatment. The study objective is to establish the best predictors for vulval LS in adult females and subsequently develop a diagnostic tool to help differentiate from other vulval conditions. Methods Women (≥18 years) referred to UK-based secondary care specialist clinics with a vulval skin complaint are eligible to participate. A diagnosis of LS (cases) or an alternative vulval condition (non-cases) will be made by a clinician experienced in vulval diseases. All participants complete a single research visit on the same day or within two weeks of the initial appointment, for diagnostic criteria assessment by a trained investigator, blinded to diagnosis. This study uses clinical expert diagnosis as the reference standard, and diagnostic criteria assessment as the index test. A sample size of 370 participants (185 cases and 185 non-cases) is needed to aim for a confidence interval of 0.45–0.55 for the overall outcome proportion of 0.5 and to target a…

title: Drip irrigation combined with film mulching improves maize yield components and grain nitrogen content by enhancing resource use capacity in arid agricultural region
abstract: Introduction Integrating film mulching with irrigation provides a practical approach to improving maize productivity and resource use capacity in irrigated agricultural regions. However, how different film types and irrigation methods jointly regulate soil water dynamics, canopy light utilization, and yield formation remains unclear. Methods Field experiments were conducted during the 2018 and 2019 maize growing seasons in the Hetao Irrigation District, northwestern China. Five management practices were evaluated: CK, TFBI, BFBI, TFDI, and BFDI, corresponding to no mulching with border irrigation, transparent film with border irrigation, black film with border irrigation, transparent film with drip irrigation, and black film with drip irrigation, respectively. We evaluated soil water storage (SWS), leaf area index (LAI), relative chlorophyll content (SPAD), net photosynthetic rate (A), radiation intercept ratio (FIPAR), grain yield, and resource use efficiencies. Results Compared with CK, film mulching under border irrigation increased SWS by 11.40% on average during the maize growing seasons. Compared with BFBI, TFBI further increased LAI, SPAD, and A at tasseling by 5.57%, 6.90%, and 14.35%, respectively. When combined with drip irrigation, film mulching further stabilized root zone water supply and enhanced canopy photosynthetic performance, increasing FIPAR, radiation use e…

East-West Coordination and Economic Dispatch of Libya's Power System: Economic Value and Transmission Capacity Sensitivity
abstract: Independent day-ahead scheduling in interconnected regions can meet the needs of each region, the system-level economic efficiency is low due to the failure to fully utilize the limited exchanges between regions in the scheduling sequence. This paper constructs a 24-hour mixed-integer linear programming model for the Libyan power system to coordinate and optimize unit combination, start-up and shutdown decisions, economic dispatch, and the total east-west exchange variable. Controlled experiments were conducted under three frameworks with the same regional demand, initial state, unit constraints, time constraints, and calibrated cost coefficients: independent scheduling with zero exchange, coordinated scheduling with an exchange limit of 349.6 MW, and a virtually unconstrained mixed baseline. The study is evaluated based on data from 19 authorized operating days starting in 2025, consisting of 25 thermal power plant modules. The MATLAB optimization toolbox provides the main solution, while independent SciPy/ HiGHS reconstructions validate the objective function, completeness, regional balance, ramp-up capability, and minimum time residual. Throughout the sample, coordinated operation reduced the total target capacity from 97.759 million comparative cost units (CUs) to 97.094 million, achieving 86.17% of the combined economic value, reducing the average committed operating units…

Misinformation and organizational capacity in extension and advisory services: building resilience in the age of artificial intelligence
abstract: Extension and Advisory Services (EAS) play a critical role in connecting research, policy, and practice to support millions of farmers worldwide. However, the increasing complexity of information systems and the emergence of powerful digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have introduced both opportunities and challenges for these organizations. EAS institutions, already constrained by limited budgets and workforce shortages, are under pressure to integrate digital tools while maintaining trust, accuracy, and inclusivity in information dissemination. Historically, EAS organizations have adapted to successive waves of technological change, from the introduction of mobile phones and ICT-based platforms to the widespread use of social media for agricultural communication. Each transformation has required not only technical adaptation but also organizational learning, communication restructuring, and capacity development—both within EAS and among their primary clients, the farmers. The integration of AI technologies presents a new and more complex frontier. While AI can enhance decision support, automate communication, and strengthen data management, it also amplifies risks related to misinformation, data bias, ethical use, and erosion of human-centric extension principles. This perspective paper proposes to examine how misinforma…

An Integrative Model of the Relationship Between Attachment and Adaptive Capacity Among Young People in Small Settlements
abstract: This paper proposes an integrative model explaining the relationship between at tachment and adaptive capacity among young people living in small settlements. Grounded in at tachment theory, Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological model, and the transactional theory of stress and coping, the model assumes that contextual characteristics such as high social transparency, lim ited anonymity, and strong informal social control may contribute to the development of insecure attachment patterns. The relationship between attachment and adaptation is mediated by emotion regulation, cognitive beliefs, interpersonal functioning, and coping strategies. The model highlights the impact of these processes on mental health, resilience, and psychosocial functioning, while em phasizing the dynamic and non-deterministic nature of adaptation across development.

MRI Imaging Recognition Model for Spinal Lesions Based on Multiple Attention Mechanism
abstract: Manual detection of spinal pathologies is a labor-intensive process that relies heavily on clinical expertise; thus the development of automated identification systems is clinically imperative. However, distinguishing among spinal lesions—specifically spinal tumors, spinal brucellosis (a rare infectious disease), and spinal tuberculosis—presents a significant challenge due to their high radiological mimicry. These conditions share overlapping imaging features, including vertebral bone destruction, intervertebral space narrowing, and paravertebral soft tissue swelling. Furthermore, the extent of the lesions and the specific vertebral segments involved lack fixed patterns, leading to frequent feature confusion. To address these issues, we propose an improved computational framework. Firstly, we introduce a bidirectional feature pyramid network backbone based on ResNet-101. Deformable convolution is employed instead of traditional convolution across various layers to extract richer semantic features. Concurrently, multiple attention mechanisms, including self-attention and soft attention, are integrated into different modules to effectively fuse the most informative feature components. Finally, an improved balanced cross-entropy loss function is implemented to mitigate the data imbalance issue arising from the rarity of both spinal tumors and brucellosis. The proposed model was va…

title: Mechanism and Coordinated Control Technology for Large Deformations of Deep Roadway under High Mining Stress: A Case Study
abstract: Abstract Deep roadways under high mining stress suffer remarkable asymmetric deformation and severe floor heave. Support failure mainly arises from inadequate consideration of asymmetric deformation and stability interactions among surrounding rock zones. To address large deformation control of deep roadways under high mining stress, this study investigates the roof–rib–floor coordinated control mechanism and technology via theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and field tests. The results show that high mining stress, soft rock mass, and absent floor support dominate the deformation and failure of the 1103 roadway. Enhancing roof–rib support strength mitigates floor deformation and plastic zone depth, while strengthened floor support reduces rib deformation and plastic zone depth. Stable floor and ribs further improve roof stability. A roof–rib–floor coordinated support technology is proposed by integrating roof–rib hierarchical support and grouted floor cable bundles. For the roof and ribs, short and long cables construct a hierarchical support structure with strong shallow and weak deep reinforcement to achieve mechanical coupling between supports and surrounding rock. For the floor, high-strength cable bundles combined with grouting reinforcement improve deformation resistance. The corresponding control parameters for the 1103 roadway are determined and verified by fi…

title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism
abstract: Differentiated cells of the intestinal villus are not a monolith of equivalent cell types, but an exquisitely patterned continuum of transdifferentiated cells with evolving functions. Villus patterning requires BMP signaling; however, the transcriptional regulators downstream of BMP are unclear. We find that SMAD1 and SMAD5 are necessary for middle villus pattern. Spatial transcriptomics reveal a homeotic-like shift in the villus pattern of SMAD1/SMAD5 mutants, with the villus bottom and tip domains expanding at the expense of the middle. Disruption of mid-villus patterning corresponds to decreases in lipid uptake and runted pups in SMAD1/5 mutants. Unexpectedly, SMAD1/5 is not required for regulation of villus tip identity, which is dependent on SMAD4. Epigenomics approaches reveal a mechanism in which SMAD1/5 directly activate some mid-villus genes and control others via a transcription factor hierarchy, including TBX3. An intestine-specific TBX3 mutant phenocopied the SMAD1/5 mutant. These findings contribute mechanistic details to intestinal villus patterning.

title: Practice-based ideological education and meaning-making among youth: a narrative identity mechanism
abstract: Universities in China have expanded practice-based ideological and political education (IPE), a curriculum format that sends students into volunteer service, field investigation, and community programs, yet little is known about how such participation relates to students’ psychological meaning-making. Drawing on the meaning-making model and narrative identity theory, this mixed-methods study tested whether awareness of narrative identity carries an indirect association between practice-based IPE participation and presence of meaning in life. In Study 1,600 undergraduates from four universities in Fuzhou, China, completed a self-developed ten-item participation scale, the Awareness of Narrative Identity Questionnaire, and the Meaning in Life Questionnaire. Mediation analysis with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples showed that participation was positively associated with presence of meaning (total effect b = 0.487), and that narrative identity carried a significant part of this association (indirect effect = 0.219, 95% CI [0.173, 0.273]); no association was found with search for meaning. In Study 2, narrative interviews with 20 students selected to contrast participation levels were analyzed thematically (143 coded segments, Cohen’s kappa = 0.84). Four themes described the narrative patterns behind the statistical model: redemptive sequencing, agency and role consolidation,…

title: Leader status-leveling behavior and leadership effectiveness: the roles of warmth-based mechanism and leader gender
abstract: Purpose In response to growing organizational efforts to promote diversity, equity and inclusion, many leaders are encouraged to adopt behaviors that reduce hierarchical distance, known as status-leveling behavior. While prior research has emphasized its benefits for employees, little is known about its effects on leaders themselves. This study aims to shift the focus to examine whether, how and for whom leader status-leveling behavior enhances leadership effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach To investigate these relationships, this study adopted a multi-method approach. This study conducted a video-based scenario experiment (n = 155) and a two-wave field survey (n = 212) to test the proposed theoretical model. Findings The video-based scenario experiment and multi-wave survey results showed that leader status-leveling behavior could promote leadership effectiveness through employee’s perceived leader warmth rather than competence. In addition, the status-leveling behavior of male leaders is more effective than that of female leaders in promoting leadership effectiveness through perceived leader warmth. Originality/value This study advances leadership research by repositioning status-leveling as a strategically effective leadership behavior. It contributes to theory by clarifying the mechanism (warmth perceptions) and boundary condition (leader gender) through which status…

title: 4D Aviation Emission Inventory Data of China estimated with QAR data in 2023 (4D-AEID-2023)
abstract: Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a high-resolution, four-dimensional aviation emission inventory for purely domestic civil aviation flights within mainland China in 2023, built directly from onboard Quick Access Recorder (QAR) measurements covering 4.52 million flights (∼96.8 % of national commercial movements). Integrating 1 Hz per-engine fuel-flow measurements with observed flight trajectories, ambient temperature and pressure, and specific humidity profiles via the Boeing Fuel Flow Method 2 and atmospheric corrections, this dataset yields temporally and spatially explicit emission estimates for CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , PM, CO, and HC. In 2023, domestic civil aviation consumed 23.7 Mt of fuel, emitting 74.6 Mt CO 2 , 311.84 kt NO x , 73.5 kt CO, 6.02 kt HC, 23.69 kt SO 2 , and 2.00 kt PM. Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and Shapley variance decomposition demonstrate that physical observations constrain activity and fuel-flow uncertainties, narrowing the coefficients of variation (CV) to 1.5 %–20.0 % across pollutants and revealing that residual inventory variance is now dominated by emission-index parameterizations. At the process level, 1 Hz resolution successfully resolves…

title: Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations for carbon footprint awareness in health sciences students: a controlled trial
abstract: Background This study evaluated the effectiveness of Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations in improving carbon footprint awareness among health sciences students. Design A three-arm randomized controlled trial. Methods The study included 122 health sciences students allocated to a Pecha Kucha group ( n = 43), a conventional presentation group ( n = 40), and a control group ( n = 39). Participants in the intervention groups received a four-session carbon footprint education program over two weeks, while the control group received no intervention. Outcomes were assessed using the Carbon Footprint Scale (CFS). Data were analyzed using mixed-design ANOVA and ANCOVA. Results Post-intervention carbon footprint awareness scores were significantly higher in both the Pecha Kucha and conventional presentation groups compared with the control group ( p < 0.05). A significant Group × Time interaction indicated different patterns of change across groups over time ( p = 0.025). Improvements were particularly evident in the waste management dimension of carbon footprint awareness ( p < 0.001). No significant differences were found between the two educational methods. Conclusions Both Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations were associated with improved carbon footprint awareness compared with the control group, although a significant within-group improvement was observed only in…

title: Quantifying the Vehicle Emission Reduction Required to Offset Warming-Driven Ozone Increase in Beijing
abstract: Abstract Vehicle emissions (VE) reductions are a key pathway for mitigating urban ozone pollution, but their effectiveness under the condition of warming-driven biogenic emission responses remains unclear. An ozone formation path tracing (OFPT) method coupling an observation-based model (OBM) with Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was used to quantify the contribution of different VOCs for different emission sources to the ozone production rate (PO3). In this study, initial VOC concentrations were reconstructed by correcting for photochemical losses, and an additional constraint on isoprene was applied to improve the assessment of ozone production in Beijing. The results show that initial VOC reconstruction substantially increased PO3 and changed source attribution. Biogenic emissions became the largest single contributor to PO3, whereas VE remained the dominant controllable anthropogenic source because it supplied both VOCs and NOx. After considering the temperature response of isoprene emissions, a 10.7 ± 3.5% reduction in VE was required to offset the O3 increase caused by a 1 °C temperature rise under current conditions. Future-scenario simulations showed that the required VE reductions were lower under the Clean Air scenario (7.1 ± 0.7%) than under the Baseline scenario (11.3 ± 0.1%). These results highlight the need to integrate vehicle electrification, biogenic VOC res…

title: Quantitative Steric Hindrance to Determine Pressure-Induced Emission Harvesting
abstract: Abstract Pressure engineering enables distinctive pressure-induced emission (PIE) and piezochromism in halide perovskites, yet structural reversibility generally prevents ambient condition retention of high-pressure metastable states (HPMS), limiting their practical optoelectronic applications. This perspective compares PIE retention behavior across all-inorganic, aliphatic-cation, and aromatic-cation hybrid halide perovskites. Insufficient steric hindrance yields fully reversible responses in inorganic and aliphatic systems, whereas rigid aromatic cations elevate phase-transition barriers and kinetically trap HPMS after decompression. The steric-effect index (SEI, critical threshold 2.3) quantitatively distinguishes reversible systems from those capable of HPMS retention, establishing a link between cation molecular geometry and PIE persistence. We highlight outstanding quantitative structure–property challenges and outline future research directions, including machine-learning-guided screening, advanced high-pressure characterization, and new strategies for metastable-state stabilization. Extending PIE to phosphorescent and chiral luminescence further expands opportunities for applications in optical anticounterfeiting, information storage, sensing, and display technologies.

title: Banana peel-derived hierarchical porous carbon for high-performance supercapacitors
abstract: Banana peel-derived carbon offers a sustainable route for developing low-cost electrode materials for electrochemical energy storage. In this study, hierarchical porous carbon (HPC) was prepared from banana peel waste through carbonization followed by KOH activation and evaluated as a supercapacitor electrode. Structural, morphological, surface-chemical, textural, and electrochemical properties were investigated using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, nitrogen adsorption–desorption, cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge–discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. KOH activation substantially enhanced the porous structure, increasing the BET surface area from 214 to 1680 m 2 g -1 and the total pore volume from 0.18 to 1.42 cm 3 g -1 . The Raman (I D /I G ) ratio increased from 0.85 for the precursor carbon to 1.12 for HPC, indicating increased structural disorder. The HPC electrode delivered a specific capacitance of approximately 360 F g -1 at 0.1 A g -1 and retained approximately 210 F g -1 at 10 A g -1 , corresponding to a capacitance retention of 58.3%. These findings highlight the potential of banana peel waste as a sustainable precursor for producing hierarchical porous carbon with promising charge-storage performance for electrochemical energy-storage applications.

Access to positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography in the management of lung cancer in Te Manawa Taki Midland Region of New Zealand
abstract: background: This study examines access to 18-F fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (FDG PET-CT; PET-CT) scans among lung cancer patients. data and methods: Patients diagnosed with lung cancer in 2011–2021 were identified from the Midland Lung Cancer Register and the New Zealand Cancer Registry. Patients were linked to the National Non-Admitted Patient Collection to determine if they underwent PET-CT. Logistic regression was used to estimate the odds ratios of having PET-CT, adjusting for age, gender, ethnicity, year of diagnosis, socio-economic status, cancer stage, cell type, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status and comorbidities. results: We identified 613 patients with stage I, 300 with stage II and 3,722 with stages III and IV lung cancer, with 75% of stage I and 68.3% of stage II undergoing PET-CT. PET-CT has become more common over time. Patients aged 80 years and over, Māori, those with frailty (ECOG 2+), and those with stages II–IV of disease were less likely to receive PET-CT. Gender, socio-economic status and comorbidities did not influence the use of PET-CT. conclusion: PET-CT is a standard of care for patients with early-stage lung cancer, suitable for curative treatment. The disparity of access to PET-CT for Māori needs to be addressed.

title: Structure Engineering of Multilayer Nanolayer N-Doped Carbon NiS2/CoS2 Heterojunctions to Enhance the Cycling Stability of Magnesium–Lithium Hybrid Batteries
abstract: Abstract Magnesium–lithium hybrid batteries (MLHBs) have emerged as promising energy-storage systems owing to the resource abundance of magnesium and the favorable reaction kinetics introduced by Li+. However, the practical development of MLHBs remains hindered by the sluggish Mg2+/Li+ transport, limited accessibility of electrochemically active sites, and structural degradation of cathode materials caused by repeated conversion-induced volume changes. Therefore, rationally designed cathode architectures that simultaneously improve reaction kinetics and structural stability are highly desirable. Transition-metal sulfides stand out among candidate cathode chemistries because they deliver high specific capacity and prolonged cycle life, offering exceptional application potential. To address these challenges, we rationally design and synthesize a multilayer nanosheet N-doped NiS2/CoS2 heterojunction as an advanced cathode for MLHBs. The intimate NiS2/CoS2 heterointerface, together with the open multilayer nanosheet architecture, facilitates electron/ion transport and improves the electrochemical reaction kinetics. Polyvinylpyrrolidone serves both as a structure-directing agent and as the carbon/nitrogen precursor, generating an N-doped carbonaceous component intimately coupled with the NiS2/CoS2 heterostructure during sulfidation. The ultrathin nanosheet subunits enlarge the elect…

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving relationships of household consumption-based carbon emissions in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Introduction As living standards continue to rise, reducing household consumption-based carbon emissions through changes in the consumption structure is essential for reconciling consumption upgrading with the green and low‐carbon transition of household living. Methods Using China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) data from 2014 to 2022, this study applies kernel density estimation, consistent partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLSc‐SEM), and XGBoost‐SEM to examine the spatiotemporal differentiation, category composition, and driving relationships of household consumption‐based carbon emissions in the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Results First, aggregate emissions from the sampled households increased, subsequently declined, and then rebounded across the survey waves. Residential emissions accounted for 71.94% ‐80.28% of the total, while residential, food-related, and transportation and communication emissions jointly accounted for 90.3% ‐95.6%. Provincial means for the three major categories were generally higher in the downstream region, although Guizhou and Hunan in the middle and upper reaches also exhibited local high values for residential and transportation and communication emissions. Synthesis of Lignans from the Biobased Platform Chemical Itaconic Acid Using Pd-Catalyzed Coupling Reactions
abstract: Abstract Itaconic acid diesters and monoesters undergo a Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction with arene diazonium salts at ambient temperature and under ligand- and base-free conditions. The products can be further elaborated in two steps to the CL1-subtype lignans gossypidien and jatrodien or to CL2-subtype lignans with a dibenzylbutenolide or an α-arylidene-γ-butyrolactone structural pattern in three or two steps, respectively. For the synthesis of both CL2-subtype lignans, the Pd-catalyzed Heck-type coupling of α-methylene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones and arene diazonium salts was investigated. While the dibenzyl-butenolide pattern is accessible under base-free conditions with a regioselectivity higher than 98:2, the presence of a base leads to the preferred formation of exo-α-arylidene butyrolactones with an exo/endo-ratio up to 5:1, as determined by 1H NMR spectroscopy. The exo-α-arylidene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactone pattern was more selectively synthesized through an aldol condensation–elimination sequence from β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones. Eventually, the hydrogenation of these α-arylidene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones catalyzed by Pd/C was investigated as a stereoselective method for the synthesis of cis-α,β-dibenzyl-γ-butyrolactones. title: Cytogenetic Characterization of Seven Zoysia Cultivars using Fluorescent in situ Hybridization and Flow Cytometry
abstract: Zoysia spp. are economically important warm-season turfgrasses widely used in landscaping. Despite their horticultural importance, cytogenetic differentiation among Zoysia cultivars remains poorly characterized. This study compared seven cultivars using pre-labeled oligonucleotide fluorescence in situ hybridization (PLOP-FISH) and flow cytometry. We investigated chromosome number and morphology, 5S and 45S rDNA distribution and signal intensity, telomeric repeat distribution, and nuclear DNA content. All seven cultivars possessed 2n = 40 chromosomes, consistent with previously reported tetraploidy. 5S rDNA distribution was highly conserved, with two loci in every cultivar. However, their signal intensity differed: ‘Halla Green 10’, ‘Halla Green 7’, ‘Anyang Joonggi’, ‘Jangsung Chorok’, and ‘Zenith’ exhibited two strong 5S rDNA signals; whereas ‘Sechan’ and ‘Jangsung Saetbyeol’ exhibited one major and one minor 5S rDNA signal. In contrast, 45S rDNA was more varied: ‘Halla Green 10’, ‘Jangsung Chorok’, ‘Jangsung Saetbyeol’, and ‘Zenith’ had two major signals; ‘Halla Green 7’ exhibited one major and one minor signal; while ‘Sechan’ and ‘Anyang Joonggi’ had two major and two minor signals. The latter two cultivars possessed a colocalized pair of 5S-45S rDNA loci, with the colocalized 45S signal weaker than the major 45S signal. Each chromosome contained telomeri…

title: Effects of zinc-enriched and acid-modified biochar on soil physicochemical properties and wheat growth in calcareous soils
abstract: In calcareous soils, where zinc (Zn) fixation restricts crop productivity, modified biochars have been proposed as promising carriers for micronutrient management. This study aimed to characterize the Zn adsorption–desorption behavior of olive pruning waste-derived biochar (BC) produced at 400 °C and modified with 1 mol L -1 HNO 3 (NA), H 3 PO 4 (PA), and H 2 SO 4 (SA), and to evaluate the agronomic performance of Zn-enriched biochars under wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) cultivation. Adsorption experiments (0–400 mg L -1 Zn) showed that Zn retention depended strongly on modification type. The original BC followed an H-type isotherm and removed 91% of the added Zn at an initial concentration of 100 mg L -1 , whereas the acid-modified materials showed S-type behaviour and removed only 1-10%, reflecting the strongly acidic post-contact solution conditions (pH 1.26–2.03) maintained by residual acid. Desorption in 0.01 M CaCl 2 released 1.6-17.8% of the Zn retained by the original BC but a considerably larger proportion of that retained by the acid-modified materials. In the greenhouse pot experiment, biochar was applied at 1% (w/w) and prepared at nominal target Zn loadings of 30, 300, and 1000 mg kg -1 Zn in a completely randomized design using the Bayraktar 2000 bread wheat cultivar. Wheat dry weight increased from 1.37 g pot -1 in the control to 4.93 g pot -1 under PA+BC+Zn 300 .…

title: Salicylic acid-mediated stress tolerance in Tulsi plant (Ocimum sanctum L.) under salinity stress and mercury toxicity
abstract: Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) is a medicinally important plant and it is sensitive to environmental stress such as salinity and mercury toxicity. Abiotic stresses like mercury toxicity and salinity adversely affecting the growth of the plant, metabolism and the productivity of the plant by disturbing the physiological and biochemical processes. The saline stress and mercury toxicity causes severe plant damage in soil leading to ionic imbalance, osmotic stress and formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which causes oxidative damage to the cells of the plant. To counter this from the oxidative stress the plant boosts its antioxidant Defense system. Salicylic acid (SA) is a plant growth regulator and Signaling molecule and it also regulates the antioxidant enzyme activity by improving the stress adaptation. Salicylic acid plays a role in controlling the salinity and mercury toxicity which induces the oxidative stress and can be an effective method to improve plant tolerance against both the abiotic stress. This review provides a better comprehension of how salicylic acid helps in mitigating the harmful effect of stress induced by salinity and mercury toxicity

title: ANÁLISE BIBLIOMÉTRICA SOBRE O USO DA REALIDADE VIRTUAL COMO RECURSO TERAPÊUTICO EM CUIDADOS PALIATIVOS
abstract: Introdução: A realidade virtual tem se destacado como uma tecnologia inovadora na área da saúde, sendo empregada como recurso complementar em diferentes intervenções terapêuticas. No contexto dos cuidados paliativos, essa tecnologia apresenta potencial para contribuir com o manejo da dor, da ansiedade, do sofrimento emocional e da qualidade de vida dos pacientes. Entretanto, embora existam estudos que investiguem sua aplicação clínica, ainda são escassas as pesquisas que analisem, de forma quantitativa, a evolução e as características da produção científica sobre essa temática. Objetivo: Mapear e analisar a produção científica sobre o uso da realidade virtual como recurso terapêutico em cuidados paliativos, no período de 2020 a 2025. Método: Trata-se de um estudo bibliométrico, de caráter descritivo e quantitativo, realizado por meio da base de dados Web of Science. A estratégia de busca utilizou os descritores relacionados à realidade virtual e aos cuidados paliativos, combinados por operadores booleanos. Os registros recuperados foram processados no software Bibliometrix, por meio da interface Biblioshiny, sendo analisados indicadores relativos à evolução temporal das publicações, fontes de publicação, impacto científico, distribuição geográfica, redes de colaboração entre países e coocorrência de palavras-chave. title: Influence of sowing methods and nano-urea supplementation on canopy development, biomass partitioning and seed yield of mustard (Brassica juncea (L.) Czern.)
abstract: Mustard (Brassica juncea (L.) Czern.) productivity in the Indo-Gangetic Plains is constrained by suboptimal agronomic practices and low nitrogen (N) use efficiency (NUE). A two-year field experiment was conducted during the rabi seasons of 2023–24 and 2024–25 at Integral University, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, to assess the effects of sowing method and foliar nano-urea application on mustard growth, biomass accumulation and seed yield. The experiment used a split-plot design with 3 sowing methods (ridge-furrow, flat-bed line sowing and broadcasting) in main plots and 4 N treatments in subplots: 100 % recommended dose of nitrogen (RDN) through urea, three nano-urea sprays without soil-applied urea, 75 % RDN through urea plus one nano-urea spray and 50 % RDN through urea plus 2 nano-urea sprays. Plant height, leaf area index (LAI), soil plant analysis development (SPAD) value, fresh and dry biomass and seed yield were recorded at 30, 60 and 90 days after sowing and at harvest. Flat-bed line sowing produced better canopy development and approximately 17–18 % higher seed yield than broadcasting, while ridge-furrow sowing showed intermediate performance. Full N application improved LAI, SPAD values and biomass production; however, replacing 25 % of urea N with 1 nano-urea spray maintained seed yield at 16.1–17.1 q ha-1, comparable to full urea application. title: Appearances may mislead: explicit and implicit consumer responses to virtual anchors' form realism in live-streaming commerce
abstract: Purpose As virtual anchors become increasingly humanlike in live-streaming commerce, it remains unclear whether higher form realism consistently elicits more favorable consumer responses. This study examines how virtual anchors' form realism shapes consumer responses across explicit, implicit and neurophysiological levels. Design/methodology/approach Two laboratory studies compared human anchors with virtual anchors varying in form realism. Study 1 combined self-reported evaluations with an affective priming measure of implicit evaluation, whereas Study 2 combined self-reports with electroencephalography to examine neurophysiological processing. Findings Across both studies, high-form-realism virtual anchors received more favorable explicit evaluations than low-form-realism anchors and did not differ significantly from human anchors. In Study 1, however, high-form-realism virtual anchors received less favorable implicit evaluations than human anchors, while low-form-realism anchors did not differ significantly from either group. Study 2 revealed differentiated neurophysiological responses: human anchors elicited greater frontal theta power than high-form-realism virtual anchors and greater frontal gamma power than both virtual-anchor types, whereas low-form-realism virtual anchors elicited greater central and parietal theta power. title: An analysis of women's political representation, household power and the public–private paradox in Namibia
abstract: Introduction Despite unprecedented gains in women’s political representation across the Global South, increased inclusion often fails to translate into substantive household decision-making authority. This exploratory comparative case study examines community perceptions of women’s political representation and perceived barriers to political decision-making in Ohangwena (rural) and Windhoek East (urban). Methods The study integrates a descriptive survey of 69 women (33 in Ohangwena and 36 in Windhoek East), eight key-informant interviews, and a review of policy, legal, and NGO documents. Results Ohangwena women report household domestic responsibilities as significant barriers to public decision-making participation (median = 2) and express indecisiveness about women’s political representation and legal protections (median = 3). In contrast, Windhoek East women are satisfied that household responsibilities do not constrain participation (median = 4–5) and strongly affirm that rights and opportunities support empowerment (median = 5). Both constituencies agree that men can effectively represent women’s issues. Qualitative testimony reveals that even politically empowered women navigate a ‘double mandate’: the expectation to conform to traditional household roles while performing representational labour. title: Characterization of an electromagnetic impact-driven needle-free injector with enhanced pulsed control in a low-jet-power regime
abstract: Abstract This study elucidates the development and performance characterization of an advanced electromagnetic impact-driven jet injector version 3 (IDM-v3), specifically engineered to achieve controllable jet formation within a low-jet-power regime. To overcome the excessive kinetic energy challenges observed in its predecessor (IDM-v2), several critical technical refinements were implemented, including the integration of a high-force solenoid, a calibrated 94 g projectile, and a reduced maximum impact stroke of 6 mm. Experimental results indicate that impact force, the calculated impact peak pressure metric, and exit jet velocity are highly sensitive to the impact configuration. The 0.2 mm nozzle produced the highest impact peak pressure, P peak , of approximately 206 MPa, calculated from the measured peak target force using P peak = F peak / A n . The corresponding jet power, calculated separately from the measured exit jet velocity, was approximately 2 W. In contrast, the 0.4 mm nozzle produced a higher calculated jet power of approximately 6 W because of its larger nozzle-orifice area. High-speed temporal analysis revealed a multi-pulse response in the area-normalized target-force signal and stable jet morphology within the initial millisecond of actuation. Stability analysis of field pea (Pisum sativum L.) genotypes across sowing windows and locations using the Eberhart and Russell model
abstract: The field pea (Pisum sativum L.) is an important pulse crop worldwide and one of the major pulses grown in India, cultivated over an area of 0.64 million hectares with an annual production of 0.896 million tonnes. To evaluate environmental adaptability, this study was conducted at Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, Kumarganj, Ayodhya during two consecutive years 2023–24 and 2024–25 with two growing seasons i.e. early and late using a randomised complete block design. The stability analysis of 8 genotypes was performed across four different environments to assess yield and yield related traits by utilising the Eberhart and Russell model of additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) stability models. The pooled analysis of variance and stability parameters revealed significant genetic diversity among the studied genotypes, with strong genotype × environment interactions influencing trait expression. The linear component was high for most of the variability, while the non-significant deviation from regression indicated predictable and stable performance across environments. Stability parameters identified IPF 14-13, Pant P-243, Pant P-200 and Pant P-347 as superior performers, combining high-yield potential with broad adaptability.
