title: Enterobacter hormaechei P6 enhances salt tolerance in the halophyte Reaumuria soongorica by regulating plant physiological responses and rhizosphere soil multifunctionality
abstract: Soil salinization is a major environmental stress that restricts plant growth and ecosystem productivity in arid and semi-arid regions. In this study, we used Enterobacter hormaechei ( E. hormaechei ) P6, a halotolerant bacterium isolated from the rhizosphere of the halophyte Reaumuria soongorica , as the test strain. The strain exhibited multiple plant growth-promoting traits, including phosphorus solubilization, nitrogen fixation, and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) production, and grew in LB medium supplemented with up to 400 mmol L -1 additional NaCl. Using pot experiments, we evaluated the effects of P6 inoculation on the growth and salt tolerance of R. soongorica seedlings under saline conditions. The results showed that, compared with salt stress alone, combined P6 inoculation and salt treatment significantly improved the root architecture of R. soongorica , reduced the levels of hydrogen peroxide and malondialdehyde in its leaves, and simultaneously increased soluble sugar content, photosynthetic pigment levels, and superoxide dismutase activity. In addition, P6 treatment reduced Na + accumulation in the aerial parts of R. soongorica and lower the Na + /K + ratios in both the aerial parts and roots. title: An artificial intelligence-driven virtual patient for communication skills training in medical education: an exploratory pilot study of usability and perceived educational value
abstract: Background Effective communication is a core competency in medical education, but traditional training is resource-intensive and hard to scale. Virtual patients based on large language models (LLMs) may help, yet evidence on their usability and perceived value outside English-language settings is limited. Methods In this cross-sectional pilot study, 102 medical students at the University of Málaga completed two Spanish-language history-taking encounters with a GPT-4-based virtual patient and received automated feedback. They completed an anonymous, self-developed questionnaire (0–10 ratings and open-ended questions). Analyses were descriptive, plus an exploratory logistic regression of gender on perceived training need. Results Participants were mostly women (73.5%) and fourth-year students (85.3%). 86.3% (88/102) rated the tool easy or very easy to use and 60.8% (62/102) reported no need for prior training. Most feedback statements had mean ratings of 7.4 or more (0–10), highest for usefulness in exploring the reason for consultation and the patient's history (8.3); agreement that AI feedback does not replace tutors was moderate (6.14). Women were less likely than men to report needing prior training (OR: 0.29, 95% CI: 0.11–0.73; exploratory hypothesis-generating). Quality Evaluation and Shelf-Life Study of Ready-to-Eat Panang Curry Reformulated with Plant-Based Milk
abstract: This study was conducted to evaluate the microbial stability, physicochemical characteristics, and nutritional quality of Dusita ready-to-eat (RTE) beef Panang curry reformulated with corn-based plant milk as a healthier alternative to coconut milk. The objectives of this study were to: (1) evaluate microbial shelf-life under chilled (4°C), frozen (−18°C), and retort pouch sterilization conditions; and (2) investigate physicochemical properties (L*, a*, b*, pH, and total soluble solids) together with nutritional quality. Microbiological quality was evaluated using total plate count (TPC) and yeast and mold counts for chilled products, TPC and coliform enumeration for frozen products, and thermal lethality (F0) validation for retort-processed products. Physicochemical characteristics and nutritional labeling were also determined. Results indicated that (1) under chilled storage, TPC exceeded the acceptable limit of 105 CFU/g by day 9, defining a practical shelf-life of approximately 8–9 days; (2) frozen storage effectively maintained microbial stability for at least three months, with no coliforms detected throughout storage; and (3) retort pouch sterilization achieved a thermal lethality (F0) value of ≥6 min, ensuring product safety while inducing moderate physicochemical changes, including a color difference (ΔE≈9.91), increased pH, and reduced soluble solids. title: La integración de los patinetes eléctricos en el marco legal del tránsito en Ecuador
abstract: Los patinetes eléctricos se han incorporado a la movilidad urbana como alternativa de menores emisiones, pero su circulación plantea problemas de seguridad vial, uso del espacio público y responsabilidad que la normativa ecuatoriana de tránsito no previó. El estudio analizó su integración en esa normativa. Se realizó un análisis documental cualitativo, descriptivo-analítico, de la Constitución, la Ley Orgánica de Transporte Terrestre, Tránsito y Seguridad Vial, la regulación española como referente comparado y doctrina indexada. Los resultados muestran que el marco vigente se organiza en torno al vehículo motorizado y al conductor habilitado, lo que deja sin respuesta clara la clasificación del patinete, su espacio de circulación y la responsabilidad por daños. Se concluye que se requiere una categoría legal específica.

title: Awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in biology teaching among science teachers: Toward the development of a training program
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support instructional planning, the development of learning materials, assessment, and student engagement. However, the extent to which science teachers are aware of, utilize, and pedagogically integrate AI tools in Biology teaching remains an important concern. This study determined the awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of AI tools among junior high school science teachers in the Division of Tagbilaran City, Bohol, and examined the predictive contribution of these variables to teachers’ perceived teaching effectiveness and ability to promote student engagement. A quantitative approach using a descriptive-predictive research design was employed. The respondents were 32 junior high school science teachers teaching Biology in public secondary schools, selected through total enumeration. Data were gathered using an adapted structured questionnaire administered through Google Forms and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and multiple linear regression. ChatGPT was the most recognized, currently used, and most useful AI tool. Teachers were aware of AI tools (M = 3.81), frequently utilized them in Biology instruction (M = 3.74), and occasionally integrated them pedagogically (M = 3.35). abstract: Abstract 1,3-Butadiene (1,3-BD) is one of the most commercially significant petrochemical monomers, underpinning the global synthetic rubber and plastics industries. Precursor aging homogenizes PbI 2 sol-clusters for humidity-tolerant fabrication of perovskite solar cells
abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent a promising next-generation photovoltaic technology. Two-step sequential deposition is widely used for the scalable ambient-condition fabrication of perovskite films because of its high processing tolerance and reproducibility, with the predeposited lead iodide (PbI2) layer acting as a vital scaffold for perovskite crystallization and largely determining the final device performance. Despite extensive progress in PbI2 layer regulation through additive and solvent engineering, the physicochemical evolution of precursor systems during the early stages of aging (prior to apparent deterioration) is insufficiently understood. Herein, we investigate the effects of early-stage PbI2 precursor aging on the growth of perovskite films and device performance via ambient two-step deposition. We identify a moderate-aging processing window, in which the spontaneous evolution of the PbI2 solution yields a desirable physicochemical state for the subsequent thin-film deposition. The PSCs fabricated using an additive-free precursor solution at a relative humidity of 40%-50% exhibit a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24.52%. title: Surfactant-Assisted CO2 Flooding in Kerogen Nanopores: Molecular Mechanisms for Enhanced Oil Recovery in the Fengcheng Formation Shale, Mahu Sag, Junggar Basin
abstract: Abstract Surfactant-assisted CO2 flooding offers a promising route to enhance oil recovery from unconventional shale reservoirs, yet the molecular-level mechanisms governing surfactant performance in organic-rich kerogen nanopores remain insufficiently understood. Unlike North American marine shales (e.g., Bakken) which produce light oil from free-state pores, the Fengcheng Formation of the Mahu Sag is a continental alkaline shale with heavier oil and significant adsorbed oil, meaning that surfactant mechanisms established on mineral surfaces cannot be directly applied. In the Fengcheng Formation of the Mahu Sag, Junggar Basin, primary depletion recovers less than 10% of original oil in place, with the remaining oil trapped within a nanoporous organic matrix by capillary and adhesion forces. The reservoir is characterized by ultralow permeability, complex pore networks, and Type II kerogen with high aromaticity, imposing specific constraints on surfactant performance. These characteristics necessitate systematic molecular-scale investigation to establish a mechanistic basis for surfactant selection. Here, we systematically compare three surfactants of different ionic types (cationic CTAB, nonionic Tween 80, and anionic SDS) within a realistic Type II-C kerogen slit-pore model using molecular dynamics simulations under reservoir conditions (348 K, 40 MPa). title: Association between energy-adjusted dietary inflammatory index and atrial fibrillation: a prospective cohort study from UK Biobank
abstract: Objective Emerging evidence increasingly suggests a potential link between dietary patterns and atrial fibrillation (AF) incidence. Leveraging extensive UK Biobank data, this study investigated the link between dietary inflammatory potential, quantified by the energy-adjusted dietary inflammatory index (E-DII), and AF risk. Methods Cox proportional hazards regression analyses, including both univariate and multivariate models, were used to evaluate the E-DII-AF association, with sequential adjustment for confounding factors. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was further applied to assess the relationships between continuous E-DII and both AF risk and AF-related mortality. We also performed subgroup analyses to identify differences across variables and used lasso regression, a penalized variable-selection method, as an exploratory approach to rank the dietary constituents according to the magnitude and direction of their penalized coefficients for AF risk. Results Among 203,776 participants [10,163 (4.98%) AF cases], the overall linear estimate from the primary model indicated a modest inverse association between E-DII and AF risk (HR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.96–0.99). Because a single hazard ratio is a linear summary statistic, non-linearity was assessed using restricted cubic splines (RCS) and quartile analyses. title: The illusion of clean energy: unveiling biohazardous PFAS risks from lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Abstract The sharp rise of CO 2 and other greenhouse gases has accelerated the global push toward clean energy technologies, with lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) emerging as a cornerstone of this transition. From powering smartphones and laptops to driving the rapid adoption of electric vehicles, LIBs are celebrated for enabling cleaner air and reducing CO 2 emissions. Yet beneath this promise lies a troubling paradox: these same batteries rely on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of highly persistent “ forever chemicals ” in their manufacturing. This dependence risks transforming a climate solution into a new source of pollution during production, operation, or end-of-life recycling. Without careful oversight, the pursuit of lower greenhouse gas emissions could inadvertently substitute one form of pollution for another, compounding global environmental challenges. This perspective highlights the overlooked risks, pathways of exposure, and regulatory blind spots surrounding the use of PFAS in LIBs.

Cesium Iodide Post-Surface Treatment for Efficient Sb2S3 Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Antimony sulfide (Sb2S3) is a promising photovoltaic absorber owing to its low cost, low toxicity, ease of synthesis, and excellent stability. However, its practical application is limited by low-power conversion efficiency (PCE). Here, we report a facile cesium iodide (CsI) post-surface treatment to enhance the photovoltaic performance of Sb2S3 solar cells. The CsI post-surface treatment not only improves the film morphology and optoelectronic properties of Sb2S3 thin films but also passivates surface defects and improves energy-level alignment, enabling a champion PCE of 7.5%. These results demonstrate that CsI post-surface treatment is a simple and effective strategy for improving Sb2S3 thin-film quality and device efficiency.

title: Challenges affecting fire safety considerations during the design stages of commercial building projects in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Purpose This paper identifies and ranks the challenges affecting fire safety considerations during the design stages of commercial building projects in Saudi Arabia. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed method design was used. The literature review identified twelve candidate challenges. Ten purposively selected experts with 6–15 years of relevant experience validated and refined the identified challenges, after which an online questionnaire completed by 93 authority/regulatory implementers, designers and stakeholders was analyzed using the Effect Index (EI). Findings Weak fire safety culture, insufficient training, limited firefighting access, lack of inspections and cultural attitudes toward safety were the most influential concerns. The results show that Saudi fire safety design challenges are technical, institutional and behavioral. Practical implications The paper proposes a design-stage framework linking concept strategy, schematic review, design development coordination, construction-document verification and occupancy feedback. Originality/value The study integrates empirical ranking with a critical safety culture, institutional and risk governance explanation, then converts the resulting mechanisms into decision and verification checkpoints across commercial building design stages.

Advancing Crop Improvement through Honeycomb Selection Design: Principles, Statistical Frameworks, Software Tools, and Applications: A Review
abstract: Field evaluation of genotypes is confounded by soil heterogeneity and interplant competition, which inflate error and lower the heritability of yield traits. The Honeycomb Selection Design (HSD), conceived by A. C. Fasoulas and refined by Tokatlidis and co-workers, evaluates individu-al plants in a hexagonal grid at ultra-wide spacing, comparing each plant with a moving ring of equidistant neighbours under nil competition. This review synthesises HSD’s principles, geometry and statistical framework, and compares it with conventional designs and spatial mixed models. It examines selection indices, the rhoneycomb R package and recent doubts about the homeostasis index. Applications in sunflower, barley, durum wheat, lentil and alfalfa are summarised, along-side long-term evidence from rice, mungbean and cotton. Limitations include land requirement, dependence among overlapping ring-adjusted values, and extrapolation to dense stands. Integration with UAV phenotyping, spatial mixed models, genomic prediction and microbiome-assisted selection offers the most promising route to climate-resilient cultivars.

abstract: Purpose This study examines hotel guests’ performance and importance evaluations of biophilic design elements in real hotel environments. The study assesses six biophilic design factors, including plants and greenery, views to nature, water features, sensory/atmospheric elements, natural light and natural materials, and their influence on guests’ revisit intention. Design/methodology/approach A post-occupancy evaluation approach was adopted using importance-performance analysis (IPA), classifying design attributes into a four-quadrant matrix based on guest ratings. Data were collected from 302 hotel guests in Qingdao, China, via an online survey and on-site intercept sampling. Structural equation modeling tested relationships between the six biophilic factors and revisit intention. Findings Plants and greenery and views to nature fell into Quadrant I (high importance, low performance) and were the strongest predictors of revisit intention. Water features and sensory/atmospheric elements fell into Quadrant II (high importance, high performance) and significantly predicted revisit intention. Natural materials fell into Quadrant III (low importance, low performance) and natural light into Quadrant IV (low importance, high performance); neither significantly predicted revisit intention. abstract: Background Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) disease integrates metabolic, renal, and cardiovascular systems. Learning in probability samples is challenged by rare outcomes, unequal sampling, clustered dependence, and miscalibration. This study aimed to develop a design-consistent, calibration-first framework for concurrent CKM multimorbidity classification in complex surveys and quantify the consequences of ignoring survey design. Methods We analyzed the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–March 2020 data for U.S. women aged 20–44 years. CKM multimorbidity was defined as the coexistence of at least two of the following: hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and clinical cardiovascular disease. Five learners were compared using 20×5 whole-PSU design-aware cross-validation, fold-contained preprocessing, survey-weighted loss functions, and cross-fitted sigmoid recalibration. The evaluation used design-based and survey-bootstrap procedures across key performance metrics. A 6,000-replicate survey-plasmode benchmark was used to evaluate bias, RMSE, and 95% coverage against finite-population truth. Results Among 1,743 classifiable women, 44 unweighted cases yielded a survey-weighted prevalence of 1.97% (95% CI, 1.30%–2.65%). title: Can liquid biopsy proteomics revolutionize clinical trial design and drug development? Early phases as a prespecified substudy, late phases not yet
abstract: Retinal drug development depends on visual acuity and imaging endpoints that are slow to change and say little about mechanism. Proteomic analysis of ocular fluid, often called liquid biopsy, can now measure thousands of proteins in a few microliters of aqueous humor and infer, through integration with single-cell transcriptomic atlases, the retinal cell types from which many of them are likely to originate. Whether this capability should change how trials are designed is contested. This Perspective sets out both sides of a debate first held at the 16th Congress on Controversies in Ophthalmology. The case for holds that liquid biopsy proteomics can stratify patients by molecular state, show that a drug reaches the eye and shifts its pathway, and support earlier development decisions. The case for caution holds that no ocular fluid biomarker has been validated against clinical outcome, that the published human evidence is small and exploratory, and that sampling, cost and scale limit its use in large trials. We agree on a phase-dependent position: ocular fluid proteomics is promising as a prespecified exploratory or pharmacodynamic substudy in selected phase 0 to 2 trials where the mechanism can be read in fluid; it belongs in a prespecified substudy, not the primary analysis, in phase 3 and 4; and no surrogate endpoint claim should be made until prospective validation exists. title: Explaining Patent Citation Lag Through Inventor Networks, Prior Knowledge Bases, and Atypical Recombination: Evidence from Battery Electric Vehicle Technologies
abstract: Timely recognition of technological knowledge is critical in rapidly evolving industries such as battery electric vehicles (BEVs). Prior research on patent citation lag has mainly examined patent-level and team-level attributes. Building on this, this study broadens the framework to consider factors such as social network position, prior knowledge bases, semantic proximity to established technological positions, atypical recombination, and repeated collaboration. Analysis using BEV-related patent data and Cox proportional hazards models revealed that patents with a diverse prior art base tend to be cited earlier, while those closer to established positions in the technological space of the industry are more strongly associated with early citation. In contrast, patents containing technological co-occurrences that are rare across the industry tended to experience delayed first citation. Taken together, these findings suggest that patents are recognized earlier when they draw on diverse technological bases while remaining semantically close to established industry technology, whereas excessively atypical technological combinations may delay early recognition. This study advances research on patent citation lag, knowledge diffusion, and innovation strategies in BEVs.

abstract: Purpose Thermal energy storage (TES) technology is crucial to improving the energy system flexibility and enabling efficient utilization of renewable energy. However, the low thermal conductivity of phase change materials (PCMs) limits the effectiveness of TES systems. To address this issue, this study proposes a combined heat transfer enhancement strategy that integrates fin inclined angle optimization with rotational conditions. Design/methodology/approach This study proposes a combined heat transfer enhancement strategy that integrates fin inclined angle optimization with rotational condition. A numerical model of a shell-and-tube TES unit with annular fins was developed, and the influence of upward-inclined and downward-inclined fins with inclined angles ranging from 5° to 75° and rotational speeds up to 1 rad/s on the charging process was investigated. Findings The results indicated that the D-10 small-angle downward-inclined fins cut the complete melting time by up to 8% at 0.5 rad/s, owing to their ability to direct heat toward the bottom area and enhance convective heat transfer. In contrast, large-angle downward-inclined fins and upward-inclined fins hinder heat transfer and exacerbate temperature nonuniformity. title: Beyond expectancy: knowledge storage and security as key drivers of blockchain adoption in public healthcare
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the factors influencing information technology (IT) professionals' behavioural intentions (BI) to adopt blockchain technology (BT) for knowledge storage (Kst) in public healthcare institutions. Grounded in the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology II (UTAUT2), the study incorporates perceived security and examines Kst as a mediating mechanism between security and BI. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a questionnaire survey using a correlational cross-sectional design, resulting in 322 valid responses. Preliminary analyses were conducted using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 26. The measurement and structural models were subsequently evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 3.9 to assess reliability and validity and test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The results indicate that performance expectancy (PE), effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), facilitating conditions (FC) and price value (PV) significantly influence IT professionals' BI to adopt BT. Perceived security also contributes to adoption indirectly through Kst, with Kst demonstrating a significant mediating effect. title: Two-qubit charger-battery system subject to weak, continuous measurements with quantum point contacts
abstract: Abstract Quantum batteries modeled as two-qubit systems coupled to Markovian thermal reservoirs have been shown to benefit from measurement-assisted charging, where projective measurements enhance the charging rate at an infinite thermodynamic resource cost. In this work, we consider weak, continuous measurements implemented via quantum point contact detectors (QPCs), which enhance the charging rate at a definite and quantifiable resource cost. We analyze three measurement configurations, namely, a single QPC, two independent QPCs, and a series-coupled (coherent) two-QPC scheme, and study their effect on the peak transient charging rate, defined as the rate of energy flow from the charger qubit to the battery qubit, relative to the unmeasured baseline. We find that the charging rate enhancement is non-monotonic as a function of the temperature and potential gradients required to drive the QPCs, exhibiting a plateau of near-optimal enhancement. Comparing the three configurations, the plateau of optimal enhancement contracts toward lower temperature and chemical potential for both cases with two QPCs compared to the single-QPC case. The coherent measurement further shows a lowering of the resource requirement relative to the two-independent-QPC case for achieving the same enhancement. title: Thermal annealing-induced charge storage enhancement in WO 3 / β -Ga 2 O 3 nanowire heterostructures for MOS capacitive memory
abstract: Abstract This paper examines non-volatile metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) capacitive memory based on WO 3 / β -Ga 2 O 3 heterostructure nanowire (NW) arrays. The WO 3 / β -Ga 2 O 3 vertical oriented axial heterostructure NWs (VAHNWs) were synthesized using glancing angle deposition technique installed in an RF sputtering system. The fabricated VAHNWs were also subjected to air annealing at 600 °C for 1 h. The interface trap density ( D i t ) decreased from 1.7 × 10 10 eV − 1 cm − 2 (as-deposited) to 1 × 10 10 eV − 1 cm − 2 (annealed) which is consistent with a reduction in electrically active interface states. The MOS capacitor exhibited a significant memory window of approximately 5.35 V at ±8 V and stable endurance over 2000 programming/erasing cycles. Moreover, a charge retention duration as long as 3.5 × 10 4 s was observed after annealing. These enhanced parameters can be ascribed to the annealing-induced modification of electrically active defects together with improved interface quality. The results demonstrated the thermally annealed WO 3 / β -Ga 2 O 3 VAHNWs as a promising candidate for future non-volatile memory technologies.

abstract: Introduction In forestry, motor manual chainsaw operations not only involve a high risk of occupational accidents but also long-term exposure to noise, vibration, and carbon monoxide among workers. Advances in battery technology have increased the use of battery-powered chainsaws as an alternative to internal combustion chainsaws in forestry. Methods The objective of this study was to determine the noise and hand-arm vibration (HAV) exposure levels of operators during log bucking when using different chainsaw models, which are commonly used in forestry. Accordingly, operator exposure to noise and hand-arm vibration was examined during the log bucking of debarked black pine and fir logs in two diameter classes (20–30 and 30–40 cm), using two battery-powered chainsaw models (Stihl MSA 300C and Husqvarna 535i XP) and one petrol-powered model (Husqvarna 372 XP). Results The operator’s 8-h daily hand-arm vibration exposure levels, A(8), were determined to be 3.79, 3.89, and 4.00 m/s 2 for the Husqvarna 535i XP, Stihl MSA 300C and Husqvarna 372 XP, respectively. The daily personal noise exposure levels, LEX,8 h, were 90.62, 97.75 and 102.12 dB(A), respectively. title: HYBRID RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEMS APPLIED TO DATA CENTERS: CRITERIA FOR SIZING, ENERGY STORAGE, AND INTELLIGENT ENERGY SUPPLY MANAGEMENT
abstract: Data centers dependem de energia elétrica o tempo todo, e essa dependência cresce junto com o volume de dados que essas instalações processam e armazenam; integrar fontes renováveis ao suprimento delas é uma forma de diversificar essa matriz e reduzir a dependência de uma única fonte centralizada. Este trabalho teve como objetivo analisar a aplicação de sistemas híbridos de energia renovável no suprimento de data centers, levando em conta os critérios técnicos de dimensionamento das fontes fotovoltaica e eólica, as tecnologias de armazenamento, os sistemas inteligentes de gerenciamento de energia e os requisitos de confiabilidade, eficiência e continuidade operacional que essas instalações impõem. A pesquisa seguiu abordagem qualitativa, apoiada em levantamento bibliográfico e documental. Não houve revisão integrativa: o levantamento bibliográfico assumiu um perfil exploratório e descritivo, priorizando publicações entre 2018 e 2026, e o levantamento documental cobriu normas técnicas e documentos institucionais sobre armazenamento de energia, sistemas de alimentação ininterrupta e eficiência energética dessas instalações. title: Pakistan’s missing indigenous satellite launch vehicle and the search for orbital sovereignty
abstract: In the 21st century, outer space has become a decisive domain of national power. Space Race 2.0 is gaining momentum as space barriers are brought down and the launch capability of a state into space has become a criterion of its strategic autonomy. While Pakistan is a nuclear-power state and has a robust ballistic-missile program, it lacks an indigenous Satellite launch Vehicle (SLV). The operational satellites of Pakistan, including EO-3 launched in April 2026, continue to rely on foreign launch providers. This presents a strategic paradox that forms the central focus of this paper. Using comparative qualitative analysis of available open-source material, the paper undertakes a comparative assessment of Pakistan's space capabilities. It also assesses the technological trajectories and strategic approaches of countries like India, China, Iran, and Israel, while recognizing China’s role as a key technological partner. Further, this paper argues that dependence on external launch services constrains Pakistan’s orbital sovereignty, operational flexibility and the growth of the domestic industrial base. Although, partnerships, particularly with China, have strengthened Pakistan's downstream and midstream space capabilities but have not yet addressed its upstream launch-capability gap. Driving Growth Through Direct Selling: A Study of Herbalife’s Global Marketing Strategy
abstract: This paper examines how direct selling was implemented in a local Herbalife distributor network in Pune, Maharashtra, through an Internship placement undertaken from 6 July to 8 September 2026. The study connects prospecting, product presentation, customer interaction and follow-up with relationship marketing and sales-funnel concepts. It uses the descriptive, experiential evidence recorded in the Internship report, including indicative weekly figures of 50 contacts, 22 leads and approximately 10 customer conversions. These figures imply contact-to-lead, lead-to-customer and contact-to-customer rates of 44.0%, approximately 45.5% and 20.0%, respectively. They are activity estimates, not audited sales records or evidence of causal effects. Field observations identify students, working professionals and fitness-oriented customers as relevant segments. Price sensitivity, hesitation, competition, limited product awareness, lead quality and inconsistent responses to follow-up were recurring practical challenges. AIDA, the personal selling process and the marketing funnel provide complementary lenses for interpreting these observations, while relationship-marketing research explains why trust and continuity matter. title: Elevation-based coastal protection strategy for tsunami risk mitigation in tourism-dense zones: A case study of Kuta Beach, Bali
abstract: High-density, tourism-centric coastal zones are highly vulnerable to nearshore tsunami hazards because of their low-lying topography and intense socioeconomic configurations. This study evaluated the hydrodynamic performance of structural and ecological mitigation strategies at Kuta Beach, Bali, via the Computer-Aided Design for Marine Structures Surf 2D numerical framework. Three specific layouts were tested against a worst-case 8.0 m offshore wave scenario: baseline unmodified contours (Scenario AA), a 100 m-wide vegetative buffer (Scenario BB) and an engineered stepped elevation profile (Scenario CC). The numerical outputs indicate that while vegetative barriers provide localised wave attenuation, the stepped elevation configuration demonstrates superior hydrodynamic resilience. The CC scenario successfully attenuated the maximum nearshore wave height from 6.0 m down to 1.5 m at 600 m inland, representing a 75% reduction in inundation depth. Concurrently, the stepped topography disrupted the forward hydrodynamic thrust, decelerating the velocity to 3.0 m/s at the middle of the beach. These findings demonstrate that microscale topographic reengineering offers an effective, space-optimised disaster risk reduction framework. abstract: Purpose Amid escalating global environmental and social pressures, corporate sustainability performance (CSP) has become a critical strategic imperative, particularly for highly polluting sectors. Drawing on the natural resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study aims to examine the impact of tacit knowledge management process (TKMP), particularly knowledge acquisition, sharing and application on the CSP of steel industry in China. Furthermore, it explores the dual mediating mechanisms of green business strategy (GBS) and generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in translating TKMP into CSP, while examining top management support (TMS) as a boundary condition moderating the relationship between the TKMP dimensions and GBS. Design/methodology/approach The study gathered data from 357 employees of steel manufacturing companies in China using survey questionnaires. abstract: Fresh cheeses are highly perishable products due to their high moisture content, near- neutral pH, and nutrient-rich composition, which make them susceptible to contamination by spoilage microorganisms such as Pseudomonas spp. and foodborne pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus . The dairy industry faces the challenge of extending shelf life while ensuring food safety, particularly in response to increasing consumer demand for natural, clean- label preservatives. This study investigated the antimicrobial and synergistic effects of three commercial essential oils (clove, rosemary pepper, and African basil) combined with nisin against a blue-pigment-producing Pseudomonas sp. isolate obtained from spoiled ricotta cream and S. aureus ATCC 14458. abstract: Background and aim Proximal humeral fracture is the third most common osteoporotic fracture and predominantly affects older women; most such patients require surgery under general anaesthesia with tracheal intubation and neuromuscular blockade, an approach that carries a respiratory cost in its own right—pulmonary complications occur in approximately 5% of patients, and 30-day mortality reaches 19.5% among those who develop them. We describe a three-component respiratory-preserving strategy—costoclavicular block for analgesia, laryngeal mask airway general anaesthesia with pressure-controlled ventilation, and complete avoidance of neuromuscular blocking agents—in two elderly patients with limited respiratory reserve, in whom the simultaneous use of all three has not previously been reported. Case presentation Two women aged 87 and 85 years underwent open reduction and internal fixation of proximal humeral fractures. In both cases, costoclavicular block (0.33% ropivacaine, 30 mL) was performed while the patients were conscious, followed by laryngeal mask airway general anaesthesia with pressure-controlled ventilation, without any neuromuscular blocking agent. Tadqiqotning asosiy manbasi sifatida Usmonli davlatiga aloqador maxsus tuzilma - “Tashkilot-i Maxsusa”ga tegishli hujjatlarda keltirilgan ma'lumotlarga alohida e'tibor qaratiladi. Shu bilan birga, maqolada milliy va xorijiy tarixshunoslikda keltirilgan ma'lumotlar bilan qiyosiy tahlil amalga oshiriladi. Tadqiqotda 1917-yil arafasida Turkistondagi mustamlakachilik boshqaruvi, yer-suv munosabatlari, iqtisodiy tanglik, aholining ijtimoiy tarkibi, milliy-madaniy cheklovlar va 1916-yil qoʻzgʻolonlarining oqibatlari sovet hokimiyatining oʻrnatilishi uchun mavjud boʻlgan siyosiy sharoitni tushunish nuqtai nazaridan koʻrib chiqiladi. title: Frequency Characteristics of High-Voltage Power Semiconductor Gate Drive Circuit Using Resonant Inductive Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper investigates the frequency characteristics of a high-voltage gate-drive circuit using resonant inductive wireless power transfer (RIWPT). In the proposed RIWPT system, both the control and carrier signals are transmitted simultaneously through magnetically coupled coils, then rectified and applied to the gate of a SiC MOSFET to ensure reliable switching operation. For given amplitudes of the control and carrier signals, the achievable transfer distance is analyzed at different carrier frequencies. For the 44-turn α-wound coil, with a 15-V control signal and a 30-V carrier signal, a maximum power transfer distance of 151 mm is obtained at a carrier frequency of approximately 260 kHz. For the 44-turn spiral coil, with the same control signal and a 10-V carrier signal, a maximum transfer distance of 200 mm is achieved at a carrier frequency of approximately 193 kHz. Both maximum transfer distances satisfy the required coil separation distance to ensure adequate insulation for a system operating at a high voltage of 28.3 kV. Furthermore, the frequency-dependent variation in the turn-on and turn-off times with respect to the carrier frequency and gate–source drive voltage is also investigated. Based on the analysis, an optimization is implemented through simulation. The optimized turn-on and turn-off time are significantly reduced to 14 µs and 7 µs, respectively. In this …

title: Empowering Women, Empowering Energy: The Role of Intra-household Bargaining Power in Alleviating Multidimensional Energy Poverty in Rural China
abstract: Abstract Improving women’s intra-household bargaining power (IHBP) and reducing energy poverty in rural areas contribute to achieving the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, such as achieving gender equality, empowering all women and girls (Goal 5), and ensuring access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all (Goal 7). This study explores the impact of rural women’s IHBP on multidimensional energy poverty (MEP), using data from the 2014-2020 China Family Panel Studies and a conditional mixed-process model. We construct a composite index to measure rural women’s IHBP, accounting for dimensions of asset ownership, labor allocation/labor market participation, household financial management, household expenditure allocation, and household decision-making power. Our results suggest that women’s IHBP is negatively and significantly associated with household MEP. A one-unit increase in rural women’s IHBP is associated with an 8.0-percentage-point reduction in the probability of household MEP. The negative association between women’s IHBP and MEP remains stable across male- and female-headed households, although the estimates for the two subgroups do not differ significantly. Meanwhile, all variables used to construct women’s IHBP are negatively and significantly associated with MEP. The mediation analysis suggests that women’s IHBP is associated with …

Limits on the Amending Power: A Comparative Study of India's Basic Structure Doctrine, Germany's Eternity Clause and Colombia's Substitution Doctrine
abstract: Formal amendment procedures are designed to allow a constitution to change, but they have been repeatedly used to dismantle checks and balances, capture judiciaries and extend executive tenure. This paper examines three responses to that problem: Germany’s express eternity clause in Article 79(3) of the Basic Law, India’s judicially developed Basic Structure Doctrine, and Colombia’s Substitution Doctrine. It also traces the journey of these models to Bangladesh and Malaysia. The study finds that the three doctrines are founded on the same premise: a power derived from a constitution cannot be used to destroy or supersede the original constituent power from which it is derived. They vary in the source of the limit, the identification of the protected core and the institutional risks they pose. Germany gives textual certainty, but the clause still needs to be interpreted. India provides flexibility at the cost of an open-ended list and the prospect of judicial supremacy, as the NJAC verdict demonstrates. Colombia provides a structured test, but its fundamental notion of an “essential element” is vague. The paper takes seriously the counter-majoritarian objection that unelected courts invalidate amendments. It concludes that such limits are defensible only where courts employ them sparingly to protect the democratic order itself. It proposes a “Democratic Minimum Test”, under whic…

title: Digital technical and operational quality in online retail: effects on online advocacy and future purchase intention through digital consumption appraisal
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how the digital technical quality (DTQ) and digital operational quality (DOQ) influence consumers' digital consumption appraisal (DCA), shape their online advocacy behavior (OAB) and drive their future purchase intentions (FPI). It also examines whether gender plays a moderating role in these relationships, providing insights into how different consumers respond to digital service quality in online retail contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 410 active online consumers through a structured online survey. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to assess both direct and indirect relationships among the study variables. Findings The findings indicate that both DTQ and DOQ have a positive effect on DCA, which significantly mediates their relationships with OAB. Specifically, DCA provides complementary mediation in the relationship between DTQ and OAB, as both the direct and indirect effects are significant, whereas it provides indirect-only mediation in the relationship between DOQ and OAB, as the indirect effect is significant while the direct effect is not. Furthermore, OAB strongly predicts future purchase intention (FPI), highlighting its critical role in fostering long-term customer engagement. Contrary to prior literature, gender does not significantly moderate the relationship bet…

A study on pricing decisions in dual-channel fresh agricultural product supply chains considering risk aversion and blockchain technology
abstract: Pricing decisions in the fresh agricultural produce supply chain face multiple challenges, including product perishability, information asymmetry, and market demand uncertainty. The dual-channel sales model and blockchain technology offer new opportunities to enhance consumer trust and operational efficiency. This paper constructs a Stackelberg game model for a dual-channel fresh agricultural product supply chain comprising producers and retailers, in which producers determine wholesale prices, online direct-sales prices, and the level of preservation efforts, while retailers determine offline retail prices. A mean-variance utility function is used to characterize the degree of risk aversion among participants. Under two scenarios—with and without blockchain—the study derives equilibrium decisions for four risk-aversion combinations: both producers and retailers are risk-neutral; only producers are risk-averse; only retailers are risk-averse; and both are risk-averse. Theoretical derivations are validated through numerical simulations. The study found that risk aversion among fresh agricultural product producers has a significant suppressing effect on wholesale prices, online prices, and the level of freshness preservation efforts, and this effect holds true in both scenarios—with and without blockchain technology. The impact of retailers' risk aversion is moderated by the leve…

title: Contraceptive discontinuation among adolescent and young women aged 15–24 years in Malawi and Zambia: a calendar-based survival and machine-learning analysis
abstract: Introduction Contraceptive continuation is central to preventing unintended pregnancy. Although method-specific discontinuation, switching, side effects and fertility intentions are well described in earlier DHS research, contemporary episode-level evidence for adolescent girls and young women in Malawi and Zambia is limited. We estimated 12-month contraceptive method discontinuation, defined as ending a method episode whether by switching to another method or stopping use altogether, and interpreted the findings as a contemporary, confirmatory comparison rather than as evidence of novel causal relationships. Methods We analysed 2024 DHS-8 reproductive calendar data from Malawi and Zambia using contraceptive-use episodes as the unit of analysis. Weighted episode-level survival methods estimated 12-month discontinuation, with 500 bootstrap replicates resampling PSUs within DHS strata for the country contrast. Adjusted associations were examined using weighted generalized estimating equations (GEE) with woman-level clustering, while gradient boosting and elastic-net logistic regression were used as confirmatory predictive analyses with woman-grouped five-fold cross-validation. The calendars overlap the pre-COVID-19, pandemic and later periods, but no causal pandemic effect was estimated. Results Twelve-month contraceptive method discontinuation, including switching and transition…

title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
abstract: Spinel oxides have emerged as promising catalysts for polysulfide conversion, yet a comprehensive design strategy that elucidates the underlying structure–property relationship across diverse spinel oxides remains elusive. The complex multistep conversion processes make single descriptors insufficient to capture the full catalytic behavior, whereas identifying cooperative descriptors introduces additional complexity that challenges manual analysis. Here, we employ a machine-learning–assisted approach to uncover universal cooperative descriptors and accelerate the discovery of high-performance spinel catalysts. We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe 2 CoO 4 and Fe 2 NiO 4 as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning in Islamic banking: insights using lexicon and machine learning-based models
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) within the Islamic banking sector, focusing on sentiment analysis of these technologies across annual reports from 71 full-fledged Islamic banks in 16 countries between 2015 and 2023. Design/methodology/approach The authors used five sentiment analysis models, TextBlob, valence aware dictionary and sentiment reasoner, AFINN, long short-term memory (LSTM) and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT), to assess sentiment polarity and word frequency of AI and ML terms using Python. Sentiment distributions and trends were analysed across time, country and individual banks using visualisations from R Studio. Findings The results indicate a predominantly positive sentiment towards AI and ML in Islamic banking, with advanced models like LSTM and BERT capturing nuanced sentiment more accurately than traditional models. Regional differences emerged, with countries like Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE demonstrating notably higher positive sentiment levels. The findings reveal significant sentiment variations among models, countries and banks, emphasising AI and ML’s perceived value in enhancing efficiency, compliance and customer experience. Research limitations/implications The study’s reliance on annual reports may limit sentiment scope, suggesting futu…

title: FedPRISM: a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for personalized academic recommendation and early intervention in smart education environments
abstract: Educational risk models are often assessed by aggregate accuracy, although false alarms and leakage in model-selection procedures can materially change their practical value. We present FedPRISM as a reproducible, privacy-aware federated simulation for at-risk screening and preliminary academic guidance, evaluated on SAPEx-D (494 students; 86 encoded predictors). A stratified 80/20 split (395/99) is used; scaling and F-ANOVA selection are fitted within training folds, and a logistic stacking model is trained on five-fold out-of-fold detector scores. The primary input comprises 30 selected non-personality predictors plus all five Big-Five traits (35 dimensions); an ablation uses the 30 non-personality predictors alone. Four approximately equal IID clients are simulated rather than mapped to actual departments. On the held-out set, the stacked model achieves accuracy 0.828, precision 0.825, recall 0.767, F1 = 0.795, false-alarm rate (FAR) = 0.125, and ROC-AUC = 0.889. The Random Forest alone is similar (accuracy 0.818, F1 = 0.775, FAR = 0.107, AUC = 0.894); paired tests do not establish a performance difference. Ablation results indicate that the Random Forest supplies most of the discriminative signal: removing it lowers accuracy to 0.636 and F1 to 0.438. Removing the autoencoder reduces accuracy to 0.816, F1 to 0.781, and ROC-AUC to 0.875, while removing the Isolation Forest yi…

title: Development and validation of a malnutrition assessment model for patients with liver cirrhosis: an interpretable machine learning study
abstract: Background and objective Malnutrition occurs in 30%–80% of patients with cirrhosis, increasing mortality, hospital stay, and disease burden. Early identification is crucial, but standardized and practical tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for assessing malnutrition in cirrhosis. Methods Patients with cirrhosis hospitalized at the Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical University from October 2020 to November 2023 formed the derivation cohort ( n = 405), while those from August to December 2025 were prospectively enrolled as the temporal validation cohort ( n = 163). Malnutrition was defined according to the GLIM criteria. Features were selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Six ML models were developed: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), support vector machine with RBF kernel (RBF-SVM), elastic net (EN), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and soft voting ensemble (SVE). The final model was selected by a prespecified composite ranking of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and F1 score in internal validation, and evaluated in the temporal validation cohort. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used for interpretability. Resu…

Microplastic removal using upcycled magnetic biochar with experimental data-driven modelling and interpretable machine learning algorithms
abstract: Abstract Microplastic (MP) pollution poses a persistent environmental challenge, and the disposal of spent adsorbents after treatment can generate additional waste. This study developed a circular remediation strategy by upcycling regenerated microplastic-spent adsorbents into magnetic carbon material (MCM) for the removal of polystyrene (PS) microplastics, coupled with interpretable machine learning (ML). Magnetic modification enhanced the surface area and pore characteristics of the material, enabling MCM to achieve approximately 90% PS removal, substantially outperforming unmodified carbon material. Adsorption was best described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R 2 = 0.9932) and Langmuir and Sips isotherms (R 2 > 0.999), indicating predominantly near-monolayer adsorption. Mechanistic evidence suggested that PS removal involved complementary electrostatic, hydrophobic, and π–π interactions, as well as physical entrapment within the mesoporous structure. MCM maintained substantial removal performance in real water matrices, although efficiency decreased with increasing ionic and organic interference, particularly in seawater and cigarette-butt-derived wastewater. Regeneration experiments further demonstrated operational reusability over eight adsorption–desorption cycles. University students’ perceptions of digital access barriers, institutional digital inclusion, and platform usability in digital learning environments
abstract: This study set out to examine university students' perceptions of barriers to digital access, institutional digital inclusion, and the usability of their university's digital education platform, and to determine how these perceptions relate to one another. Conducted as a cross-sectional study, the study used a convenience sample of 304 undergraduate and graduate students who studied at universities in the Russian Federation. The data was collected in May 2026 via online questionnaire which incorporated the Barriers to Digital Access (BDA) and Digital Inclusion (DI) subscales, adapted from the Questionnaire for Digital Equity and Accessibility in Higher Education, along with the System Usability Scale (SUS), and analysis was performed with the help of descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, independent-samples t -test, one-way ANOVA, and hierarchical multiple linear regression. The findings show that students' perceived barriers to digital access were somewhat low, their perception of institutional inclusion was above average, and the platform's usability score fell below the commonly cited benchmark. Access barriers were negatively related to inclusion and usability, but inclusion and usability were positively related. Digital inclusion varied significantly between genders, showing a tendency among males, although there was no significant gender gap in usability or perceiv…

title: Transformational leadership and change management in post-digital organisational environments: a study of practices, resistance and collective learning within the framework of the “leadership and organisational management for change” model
abstract: Purpose In a context marked by digital acceleration, growing organisational complexity and the constant need for adaptability, organisations face the challenge of transforming themselves without losing cohesion or shared meaning. This study presents the LiGO (Leadership and Organisational Management for Change) model, a theoretical and empirical proposal aimed at analysing how transformational leadership, change management, psychological safety, resistance to change and organisational readiness are articulated in sustainable transformation processes. Design/methodology/approach The model integrates five approaches consolidated in the literature: transformational leadership (Bass and Avolio, 1995), change management (Kotter, 1996), psychological safety (Edmondson, 1999; Edmonson and Lei, 2014), resistance to change (Oreg, 2003) and organisational readiness for change (Weiner, 2009; Holt et al., 2007). A quantitative descriptive-correlational study was conducted with a sample of 402 professionals from Spanish organisations, using a structured questionnaire designed ad hoc. Findings The results show moderate levels of agreement on aspects related to communication of purpose, clarity of change and collective readiness to learn. Spearman’s correlational analysis reveals high and statistically significant relationships between transformational leadership, change management, psycholog…

title: Using TikZ and tkz-euclide to Create Accurate Visual Media for Concave Mirror Image Formation
abstract: Background: Visual representations are essential for teaching geometrical optics, particularly ray paths and image formation. However, static diagrams may not consistently preserve the geometric relationships of the underlying optical model.Aims: This study develops a parametric visual generator using TikZ and tkz-euclide to construct and quantitatively verify geometrically consistent concave-mirror diagrams.Methods: An educational design research approach was used to develop and evaluate the computational visual instrument. The object distance s served as the principal input parameter for generating object coordinates and two incident rays: one parallel to the principal axis and the other forming an angle θ with the axis. The image position was determined from the intersection of the reflected rays, and the image distance s'TikZ was measured using tkz-euclide. It was independently compared with s'Theoretical obtained from the Gaussian mirror equation. Four object-distance configurations were evaluated at f=7.50 cm.Results: The generator produced geometrically consistent representations across the four principal concave-mirror conditions. Relative errors ranged from 0.00% to 0.23%, with the maximum occurring for s>2f.Conclusion: The proposed TikZ/tkz-euclide workflow provides a reproducible method for generating and quantitatively verifying concave-mirror representations. title: Sparse-to-dense cross-attention for multimodal climate representation learning and data fusion
abstract: Integrating multimodal environmental observations poses severe data engineering challenges, including sparse policy document context, varying social text streams, and inconsistent temporal records. In this work, we present an end-to-end multimodal data fusion framework that uses exponential-decay weighting (α = 0.7) for historical text imputation, along with a sparse-to-dense cross-attention mechanism, across 12,684 policy document chunks. Evaluated on national-level climate data from Ukraine, our results show that incorporating cross-attention provides crucial contextual regularization and improves numerical representation robustness, reducing test prediction error by approximately half (MSE = 0.1477 ± 0.0188) compared to the non-attention transformer-based baseline (MSE = 0.2910 ± 0.045). However, for the self-supervised data fusion approach evaluated on reconstruction loss, the no cross-attention approach yields the lowest error (MSE = 0.0784 ± 0.0016) compared with other modality sets (MSE ≈ 0.2938 ± 0.0397) due to the specifics of self-supervised learning evaluation. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis demonstrates that expanding the retrieval window [ K ε (200, 1,000)] yields higher attention entropy, preventing attention collapse across multi-modal environmental applications.

Long-term health-related quality of life and tremor outcomes after unilateral versus bilateral vim/PSA deep brain stimulation for essential tremor: a registry-based comparative study
abstract: Background Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an established treatment for medication-refractory essential tremor (ET); however, the long-term effects of unilateral DBS, particularly on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), have remained uncertain. Therefore, this study compared short-, mid-, and long-term HRQoL and tremor outcomes after unilateral versus bilateral ventralis intermedius/posterior subthalamic area (Vim/PSA) DBS. Methods In this single-centre, registry-based, retrospective study, prospectively collected data of 35 patients with ET were analysed to compare outcomes of unilateral versus bilateral Vim/PSA DBS. Outcomes were assessed at 1, 2–5, and ≥6 years. The primary outcome was HRQoL assessed by the Summary Index of the Quality of Life in Essential Tremor Questionnaire. Secondary outcomes included the 5-dimension 5-level European Quality of Life Questionnaire, Schwab and England Activities of Daily Living Scale, and Fahn-Tolosa-Marin Tremor Rating Scale Parts A, B, and C. Between-group differences were assessed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric tests, while longitudinal outcomes were analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA and ordinal logistic mixed-effects models. Results No significant between-group differences in HRQoL were observed at any follow-up. Bilateral DBS was associated with greater overall tremor reduction, with significant time×group int…

Self-healing digital twins for fault-tolerant building energy management: a physics-informed hybrid architecture with an exploratory pilot demonstration
abstract: Purpose This study develops a self-healing digital-twin architecture for fault-tolerant building energy management in which anomaly detection is linked directly to control recovery. Design/methodology/approach A two-state RC thermal model, identified online by recursive least squares as an ARX approximation, is combined with an LSTM residual corrector. The hybrid-model residual drives a nine-state fault detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR) machine that reconfigures a stochastic model predictive controller (MPC). The architecture was tested in an eight-week residential pilot with 50 software-emulated faults and in a virtual hardware-in-the-loop test. Findings The architecture ran on a Raspberry Pi 4 (maximum MPC solve time 4.21 s). In the summary results of the original pilot analysis, 40 of 43 emulated non-cyber faults were correctly classified (93.0%; 95% CI 80.9–98.5%). As the original logs and data partitions were not retained, these results are descriptive, not held-out estimates. Research limitations/implications The evidence comes from one building and emulated faults and cannot be independently re-analysed; comfort is assessed with a model-based PMV estimate. A prospective study with pre-specified data partitions is required. title: Structured Peer-Led Biostatistics Education Improves Research Confidence and Applied Competency Among Preclinical Medical Students
abstract: Abstract Background Early exposure to clinical research methodology and biostatistics remains limited within many medical school curricula despite increasing emphasis on evidence-based medicine and scholarly productivity. Peer-assisted learning models may offer a scalable approach to improving research education while minimizing faculty burden. This study evaluated a structured, peer-led applied biostatistics curriculum for preclinical medical students. Methods The Clinical Data Analysis and Research Team (CDART) curriculum was delivered to two cohorts of first-year medical students at a single medical institution during the 2025–2026 academic year. The curriculum consisted of four core instructional sessions focused on statistical analysis, data interpretation, and practical use of IBM SPSS Statistics software. Pre- and post-session confidence surveys and a curriculum-level Applied Biostatistics Knowledge Assessment were administered. Paired-samples t-tests, Cohen’s d effect sizes, and Cronbach’s alpha reliability analyses were performed. Results Thirty-four first-year medical students completed the curriculum. Confidence scores improved significantly across all instructional sessions, with mean paired increases ranging from 11.27 to 20.27 points (all p < 0.001). title: Study on the impact of clean energy use on the health of farmers and herders in Xizang
abstract: Introduction Air pollution is a major global public health challenge. Clean energy use is widely recognized as a key pathway to improving air quality and protecting public health. Against this backdrop, this study examines the impact of clean energy use on the health of farmers and herders in Xizang and its underlying mechanisms. Methods Using data from the 2023 Xizang Livelihood Development Research (XLDR, 2023), this study systematically examines the relationship between clean energy use and the health of farmers and herders in Xizang. It further explores potential mechanisms, including new media exposure and social capital, and conducts heterogeneity analysis across income groups, groups with different levels of reliance on traditional energy, and households at different altitudes. Results The findings show that clean energy use alleviates the harm to farmers’ and herders’ health caused by burning traditional biomass. Clean energy use is significantly and positively associated with the health level of farmers and herders. New media exposure and social capital may be two potential mechanisms. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that the promoting effect is more pronounced among low-income groups, groups with deeper reliance on traditional energy, and high-altitude farmer and herder households. title: Instructional equivalence and differential affordances of peer tutoring and AI-assisted learning in IUPAC nomenclature: an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study
abstract: IUPAC nomenclature in Organic Chemistry remains a challenging procedural domain requiring precision and rule-based reasoning. While peer tutoring and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools have been introduced to support learning, empirical evidence with the comparison of learning functions with traditional instruction remains limited. This study examined both the instructional equivalence and functional roles of a blended intervention integrating peer tutoring, ChatGPT, and OrgoSolver. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed involving 27 undergraduate students assigned to control ( n = 14) and experimental ( n = 13) groups. A 30-item validated test was administered as pretest and posttest. Quantitative results showed that both groups improved significantly ( p < .001), with the experimental group demonstrating a larger numerical gain ( d = 1.38) than the control group ( d = 1.17). Although the experimental group obtained higher posttest scores, ANCOVA indicated no statistically significant difference. Given the small sample size, the quantitative findings should be interpreted as preliminary and exploratory. Qualitative findings revealed four complementary affordances of the blended intervention: (1) cognitive affordances through conceptual understanding and cognitive triangulation, (2) social affordances fostered by peer tutoring, (3) technological…

title: A Human-Centric Decision Framework for Selecting Artificial Intelligence Collaboration Strategies Under Uncertainty in Industry 5.0
abstract: Abstract Effective collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence (AI) in industry 5.0 demands technological systems with human social-cognitive processes, such as trust calibration and shared mental model. This study introduces human-centric decision-making framework for configuring human-AI collaboration in smart manufacturing systems. As Industry 5.0 evolves, finding the best synergy between human intelligence and collaborative robots (cobots) becomes crucial for enhancing adaptability, safety, efficiency, and sustainability. The proposed methodology uses neutrosophic Z-numbers (NZN) to capture uncertainty with three components: truth, indeterminacy, and falsity with their associated reliabilities, and the NZN weighted arithmetic averaging (NZNWAA) operator to combine individual preferences of decision-makers. Afterward, the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method is used to objectively determine the importance of each criterion by analyzing contrast intensity and inter-criteria correlation. The ranking of alternatives is then obtained using the compromise ranking of alternatives from distance to ideal solution (CRADIS) method. This hybrid NZN-CRITIC-CRADIS approach is applied to a real-world case study of BMW manufacturing systems, assessing four human-AI collaboration strategies: full AI automation, partial cobot integration, human-l…

title: Rumination mediates the association between self-uncertainty and generalized anxiety disorder symptoms
abstract: Self-concept clarity (SCC), the extent to which self-beliefs are clearly defined, internally consistent, and stable, has been linked to anxiety, yet the processes translating self-uncertainty into generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) symptoms remain underexplored. Grounded in control and goal-progress accounts of repetitive negative thinking, the present study tested whether rumination mediates the association between SCC and GAD symptoms in young adults. A cross-sectional sample of 251 university student participants (Mage = 22.21, SD = 1.56) completed the Self-Concept Clarity Scale, the Perseverative Thinking Questionnaire, and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale. Pearson correlations showed that SCC was negatively associated with both rumination (r = -.51, p < .001) and GAD symptoms (r = -.44, p < .001), whereas rumination was positively associated with GAD symptoms (r = .58, p < .001). The mediation analysis indicated mediation, with rumination mediating the link between SCC and GAD symptoms (b = −0.081, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.110, −0.055]); the outcome model explained 37.9% of the variance in GAD symptoms (R² = .379), after adjustment for age, gender, education level, and demographics. These findings suggest that reduced SCC is associated with elevated GAD symptoms partly through heightened rumination, identifying self-concept structure and repetitive negative thin…

Scenario-based life cycle assessment of beef production in Colombia: intensive silvopastoral transition scenarios under uncertainty
abstract: Introduction Beef production in Colombia is associated with high methane emissions, low land-use efficiency, and pressure on forested landscapes. This study evaluates whether silvopastoral intensification can reduce product-level greenhouse-gas intensity while explicitly distinguishing such reductions from territorial emissions and land-use effects. Methods A scenario-based life cycle assessment combined with Monte Carlo simulation was developed to compare an extensive reference cattle system (BAU-F) with moderate (SSPi-M) and intensive (SSPi-I) silvopastoral configurations. The cradle-to-farm-gate model used 1 kg of live-weight gain (LWG) as the functional unit and represented biological dependence among stocking rate, animal productivity, methane emissions, manure, and nitrogen excretion. Production-related greenhouse-gas emissions were quantified separately from land-use-change burdens and carbon-sequestration credits, which were evaluated through structural sensitivity analyses. Results Across 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations, mean greenhouse-gas intensities were 13.88 kg CO 2 eq kg −1 LWG for BAU-F, 8.49 for SSPi-M, and 7.10 for SSPi-I, corresponding to modeled reductions of 38.84% and 48.82%, respectively. These reductions were driven primarily by higher productivity rather than lower territorial emissions. Mean production-related emissions increased from 1,464 kg CO 2 eq ha…

title: Direct and inverse source problems for a stochastic Riemann–Liouville time-fractional equation with a singular spatial potential
abstract: Abstract Direct and inverse source problems are studied for a stochastic Riemann–Liouville time-fractional equation with a singular spatial potential. The spatial operator contains a negative potential of the form − μ | x | β , where β ∈ [ − 2 , + ∞ ) , and is defined rigorously through a coercive symmetric bilinear form. The spectral structure of the associated elliptic operator yields a modal representation of the projected evolution equations. The Riemann–Liouville initial conditions generate explicit leading singularities in the homogeneous solution; after separating these singular terms, continuity and energy estimates are obtained for the corresponding remainder. For the zero-initial nonhomogeneous stochastic problem, mean-square regularity estimates follow from the spectral representation, Mittag–Leffler kernel bounds and Itô’s isometry. The inverse analysis uses terminal statistical observations, following the established spectral moment approach. The terminal mean identifies the deterministic source on its visible spectral modes, whereas the terminal modal variances determine the squared modal intensities of the stochastic source when the temporal stochastic profile is nontrivial. The results characterize identifiable deterministic modes, recovery of stochastic squared modal intensities, and the stability and regularized reconstruction of these quantities. Spectral Tik…

title: A small-scale CMOS potts machine for multi-state memory and optimization
abstract: This work presents a resistively coupled 2 × 2 all-to-all oscillatory neural network (ONN) based on ring oscillators (ROSCs) that implements a hardware oscillator-based Potts machine (OPM) for grayscale associative memory and graph coloring. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS technology, the ONN supports multi-state spin operation through nine-stage ROSCs with accessible delay elements and a five-bit tunable resistor bank enabling programmable coupling. Leveraging the Potts model, the OPM reliably retrieves horizontal, vertical, and diagonal (inverse) patterns encoded in 5 gray tones and efficiently solves multiple graph coloring problems using phase-encoded multi-state spins. Operating at 1.91 MHz with a power consumption of 12.6 μ W , the network consistently reaches steady-state solutions within three oscillation cycles for associative memory tasks and within 37 cycles for one iteration of the planted graph coloring task. Although compact in scale, this is, to the best of our knowledge, the first OPM chip to demonstrate both associative memory and combinatorial optimization with up to nine distinguishable phase states.

title: Optimization Problem for Star Covers of Graphs without Four Cycles
abstract: The symmetric nonnegative trifactorization of matrices motivates the study of the SNT-rank of graphs. We focus on the family of graphs characterized by three forbidden closed $4$-walks and show that the calculation of the SNT-rank of graphs from this family can be formulated as an optimization problem for star covers on graphs. Unlike traditional optimization that minimizes the number of stars, our objective is to minimize the number of components used in the cover, where each star is a join of two components. We introduce a graph parameter $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ and show that for a graph $G$ from the family in question it is equal to the difference between the number of vertices in the graph and the minimal number of components needed in any star cover of $G$. We develop an algorithm for computing $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ consisting of three main steps: (1) transformation of $G$ to a weighted multigraph $\Gamma$, (2) reduction of $\Gamma$ to a multigraph $\tau(\Gamma)$ with all edge weights equal to $0$ and all vertex degrees at least three, (3) iterative process for computing $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ by removing vertices in $\tau(\Gamma)$. While steps (1) and (2) are straightforward and control the $\operatorname{gap}$, step (3) is computationally complex but allows us to compute the $\operatorname{gap}$ for any graph in the considered family.

Utilization of Technology-Integrated Applications in Mathematics and Technological Competence: Effects on the Engagement and Achievement of Public Junior High School Learners
abstract: Access to educational technology does not guarantee its use, and how extensively technology is utilized may determine whether learners benefit. This descriptive-correlational study examined the utilization of technology-integrated applications in mathematics and teachers’ technological competence and their effects on the engagement and achievement of public junior high school learners in the Trinidad 1 and Trinidad 2 Districts, DepEd Schools Division of Bohol, in School Year 2025–2026. Data from 42 mathematics teachers and 323 learners, gathered with pilot-tested scales (α = .82 to .87), were analyzed using weighted means, chi-square, and Pearson correlation. Utilization declined from content delivery (M = 3.22, Utilized) and problem-solving (M = 2.62) to classroom engagement (M = 2.23), use of digital tools (M = 2.20), and assessment practices (M = 2.05), all Less Utilized in every indicator, with an overall mean of 2.46. Teachers’ trainings, experience, education, and position, and learners’ internet access, gadgets, income, parental education, and school were significantly related to utilization. Teachers were Competent but weakest in content development (M = 2.98); learners were Highly Engaged in motivation (M = 3.34) and confident in concept understanding (M = 3.28). Utilization correlated positively with teachers’ competence (r = .412), learners’ engagement (r = .385), an…

title: Postherpetic neuralgia-associated secretory protein biomarkers related to major depressive disorder: an integrated bioinformatics, clinical, and experimental study
abstract: Background Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) is a debilitating neuropathic pain disorder that is frequently accompanied by depressive symptoms. Increasing evidence suggests that immune dysregulation contributes to depression. However, the molecular mechanisms linking PHN and major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify PHN-associated secretory protein biomarkers potentially involved in MDD and to evaluate their biological and clinical relevance. Methods A PHN whole-blood RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) dataset (PRJNA1142765) and three blood-derived major depressive disorder (MDD) datasets (GSE76826, GSE32280, and GSE39653) were analyzed. PHN-associated secretory protein genes were identified through differential expression analysis and integration with a curated secretory protein gene set, whereas MDD-related genes were identified using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Protein-protein interaction network analysis, functional enrichment analysis, and machine-learning algorithms were applied to identify hub genes and construct a diagnostic nomogram. The identified biomarkers were subsequently validated in an independent clinical cohort and an HSV-1-induced PHN-like mouse model. Results A total of 133 PHN-associated secretory protein genes and 702 MDD-related module genes were identified. Integration analyses and machine-learning …
