title: The System for Assessing the Effects of Investment Projects in the Knowledge Base of IEIE SB RAS
abstract: The article examines the development of approaches to data analysis and structuring using the example of the development of the Knowledge Base of the The Institute of Economics and Industrial Engineering within the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IEIE SB RAS). The main purpose of creating a knowledge base is to transform the source data on resources, facilities, technologies, the state and development of the Asian Russia macro-region, which will provide a qualitatively new understanding of complex processes of synergy in the economy based on network combinations of chains of objects interconnected by the movement of natural, financial, labor, information resources, products, technologies, supported by development institutions. Special attention is paid to the task of assessing the effects of the implementation of investment projects. To solve it, the knowledge base accumulates data on investment projects, companies, socio-economic indicators and technologies. The text describes concepts and approaches to creating a consistent model package, including a model and analytical apparatus for evaluating effects at the macro, meso, and micro levels. The described model complex includes a block of intersectoral models, network and cognitive models, forecasting models for socio-economic statistics, assessment systems for commercial and indirect effects, as well as a …

title: Urinary multi-omics meets artificial intelligence in bladder cancer: from liquid biopsy to clinical decision-making
abstract: Bladder cancer is among the most recurrence-prone malignancies, and its management remains anchored to invasive cystoscopy and cytology, which have limited sensitivity. Urine, which is in direct contact with the tumor, carries a rich molecular cargo, including urinary tumor-derived DNA (utDNA), the tumor-derived fraction of urinary cell-free DNA, alongside methylation marks, extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo, and exfoliated cells. These components can now be interrogated through multi-omics profiling and interpreted using artificial intelligence (AI). In this Mini Review, we integrate these layers into a single translational framework: microfluidic “urine-on-chip” technologies convert a drop of urine into standardized, analysis-ready multi-omic data, while machine learning and deep learning models—increasingly governed by STARD-AI/TRIPOD + AI reporting standards—transform these data into diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-response predictions. We highlight clinically mature anchors, including the utMeMA methylation assay (90.0%/83.1%), the Uromonitor mutation test (TERT/FGFR3/KRAS; 80.2%/96.9%, meta-analysis), chip-based cytometry for detecting high-grade disease, and an externally validated autonomous urine cytology system. These figures are assay-specific and should not be interpreted as platform-wide benchmarks. Finally, we define the priorities—pre-analytical standardizat…

title: BADF-Net: a boundary-aware dynamic fusion network for robust multi-anatomical structure segmentation in abdominal ultrasound
abstract: Introduction Automated segmentation of multiple anatomical structures in abdominal ultrasound could enhance clinical decision–making by providing consistent quantitative measurements for disease monitoring. However, ultrasound–specific artifacts including speckle noise, low contrast and weak boundaries challenge existing deep learning models. Materials and methods We propose BADF-Net, an architecture that integrates a Boundary-Aware Dynamic Attention (BADA) module with Boundary Confidence Estimation (BCE) at every stage of a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) recalibrated ResNet-34 encoder, a Cross-Scale Boundary Fusion (CSBF) module that adaptively combines multi-scale boundary cues into a shared guidance feature and a boundary-guided decoder with attention-gated skip fusion, to improve boundary localization and tissue discrimination. Results On a multi-anatomical kidney and spleen ultrasound dataset, BADF-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.8174, Pixel Accuracy of 0.9703 and Mean Pixel Accuracy of 0.8521, outperforming 11 baselines with the lowest HD95 (11.49), and showing the largest gains in low-contrast structures such as kidney cortex and medulla. Agreement with expert radiologist annotations was strongest for well-defined structures such as the spleen (0.9786). By reducing operator dependency and inter-observer variability, BADF-Net can serve as a reliable second-reader tool in high…

Building effective digital post hospital discharge services for older adults in social care. Protocol for a mixed methods multi-site process evaluation using the NASSS framework.
abstract: Background Delayed hospital discharge is a persistent challenge for UK health and social care, harming older people’s health, increasing caregiver burden, and costing the NHS an estimated £1.9bn annually. Digital post hospital discharge and reablement services (PHDRS) combining telecare with household smart technologies are being developed to address this challenge. However, evidence for these services is restricted to small pilots with limited evidence about what helps or hinders their implementation, or the conditions needed to scale services up. Aim To identify what helps or hinders delivery, implementation, adoption and scale-up of digital PHDRS for people aged 65+ with additional support needs. Methods This four-year mixed methods process evaluation will be conducted in three sites in England. The project is guided by the Non-adoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework and its complexity assessment toolkit (NASSS-CAT). Five empirical work packages are planned: WP1) Scoping reviews of academic and grey literature will synthesise evidence for services. WP2) mapping routinely collected service and technology data to develop, where feasible, data visualisation and cost-collection tools for service self-evaluation. WP3) Ethnographic observation and interviews with commissioners, staff, clients, and informal carers, to explore factors influencing…

title: Physics-informed hierarchical graph neural network with multi-scale feature extraction for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Abstract In modern industry, bearing fault diagnosis is important for maintaining the reliability and safety of rotating machinery. With the widespread deployment of the industrial internet of things, large volumes of sensor data have become available, supporting the application of end-to-end deep learning models in this field. The limited physical interpretability of purely data-driven models can constrain their reliability under changing operating conditions. The multi-scale nature of bearing vibration signals also makes it difficult for conventional deep learning methods to capture non-local dependencies across different time segments. This paper develops a physics-informed hierarchical graph neural network (PI-HGMN) for bearing fault diagnosis. PI-HGMN constructs a dual-dimensional physics-constrained representation framework that embeds time-domain bearing-dynamics priors and frequency-domain fault characteristic-frequency priors into feature learning. A hierarchical graph construction strategy with edge-level physical residuals is designed to form a weighted graph whose relative connectivity reflects both feature similarity and physical consistency. A multi-scale hierarchical graph network then integrates local fault details with broader operational patterns. Experiments on five public benchmark datasets and one industrial dataset show competitive and stable diagnostic pe…

title: Global research trends on gut microbiota and myocardial infarction based on the microbiota-gut-heart axis: a multi-database bibliometric analysis and cross-validation study
abstract: Background Myocardial infarction (MI) is closely linked to the gut microbiota via the gut-heart axis, and the intricate bidirectional interactions between them have emerged as a prominent and extensively investigated research frontier. This study is the first to adopt bibliometric approaches to systematically delineate the knowledge architecture, evolutionary trajectory, research hotspots and emerging frontiers within this field, thereby comprehensively illustrating its developmental landscape. Methods Data for the present study were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) covering publications published between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2025. After rigorous screening, a total of 581 relevant publications were ultimately included for analysis. CiteSpace, VOSviewer, R software and Microsoft Excel were utilized to conduct systematic visual analyses covering disciplinary distribution, annual publication output, national/regional contributions, institutional collaborations, authors, journals, references and keywords. Meanwhile, cross-database validation and comparative analyses were further performed based on the Scopus and PubMed databases to assess the robustness of our findings and explore characteristic discrepancies across different databases. Results The annual publication volume showed an overall upward trend with distinct phased characteristics acr…

title: An intricate dynamic interference environments self-organised fission-fusion control of UAV multi-swarms
abstract: Purpose In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm technology has garnered significant attention. Among them, UAV swarm fission–fusion control has gradually developed. However, traditional fission–fusion methods are limited to controlling swarms with an equal number and only two swarms, which restricts the normal flight in a dynamic interference environment. In other words, in a multidynamic interference environment, swarms require more flexible fission–fusion control to enhance their adaptability. The purpose of this paper is to achieve UAV multiswarm fission–fusion control in complex dynamic interference environments. This includes developing an interaction model, a control framework, a multiswarm fission algorithm and a multiswarm trapping adversarial algorithm. Design/methodology/approach To address this problem, the authors first extend the existing starling flock interaction structure to implement a starling-inspired intermittent topological interaction model. Second, the authors introduce a self-organized multiswarm fission–fusion control framework, enhancing the velocity consistency term of the social force model to achieve velocity differentiation across multiswarms. Finally, the authors propose a multiswarm trapping and adversarial algorithm to respond to a complex interference environment, tracking and uncertain dynamic disturbances. Findings The results de…

title: A multi-decadal dataset of surface damage on Antarctic ice shelves (1999–2024)
abstract: Many Antarctic ice shelves have undergone accelerated thinning and retreat in recent decades, weakening their buttressing effect on grounded ice and increasing the risk of further sea-level rise. Surface damage, including crevasses, rifts and heavily fractured areas, is an important indicator of ice shelf structural integrity, but there is limited understanding of its long-term evolution across Antarctic ice shelves. Here we present a new surface damage dataset for nine representative Antarctic ice shelves, derived from Landsat optical imagery covering the period 1999–2024. These ice shelves include Amery, Brunt, Crosson, Dotson, Holmes, Pine Island, Scar Inlet, Thwaites and Totten, and encompass a range of change behaviours from relatively stable to rapidly changing systems. A deep-learning image segmentation model was trained on a manually annotated dataset from diverse Antarctic ice shelves to automatically map surface damage. To extend the usable record, Landsat 7 scan-line-corrector-off imagery was restored using a diffusion-model-based framework fine-tuned for Antarctic imagery. The final dataset contains 170 surface damage maps at 30 m resolution, each representing a single ice shelf for a specific year. Temporal coverage varies among ice shelves owing to differences in the availability of usable imagery. Evaluation on two independent test sets indicates that the model g…

title: Evaluating Decision Criteria for Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting Retrofits in Institutional Buildings: A Critical Integrative Review
abstract: Rooftop rainwater harvesting retrofits in institutional buildings require evidence on water performance, affordability, constraints, and operations, yet inconsistent boundaries limit transferability. This critical integrative review examines the decision criteria and evidentiary requirements supporting institutional retrofit decisions. A purposive sample of 83 full-text publications, screened from 309 Web of Science records, was systematically evaluated against 24 predefined criteria spanning financial, environmental, technological, structural, innovation, and social dimensions. Following a targeted verification audit across 1,992 publication–criterion pairs, the resulting evidence matrix documented 205 direct and 402 indirect construct correspondences. Financial and maintenance-related criteria received substantially broader coverage than thermal, structural, and innovation criteria. Direct correspondence spanned diverse forms of support from conceptual inclusion and design assumptions to modelled and measured outcomes. Financial recovery depended heavily on expenditure boundaries and tariff assumptions, while long-term runoff retention and event-scale discharge control represented non-interchangeable hydrological outcomes. A proposed decision architecture separates building context and mandatory eligibility screening from stakeholder preferences and alternative-specific perfo…

title: Gender Neutrality in Personal Law: A Critical Analysis
abstract: Gender neutrality in personal law remains one of the most contested questions in Indian constitutional jurisprudence. Personal laws governing marriage, divorce, succession, maintenance, guardianship, and adoption evolved within patriarchal structures and are deeply tied to religion, custom, and community identity. Although Articles 14, 15, and 21 guarantee equality, non-discrimination, and dignity, these laws continue to contain provisions that are either overtly discriminatory or that perpetuate inequality in practice. This paper critically examines whether Indian personal law has evolved sufficiently to reflect constitutional morality, dignity, and inclusiveness. The paper begins with the constitutional framework, highlighting the tension between equality guarantees and religious freedom under Articles 25 and 26. It traces the judicial journey from State of Bombay v. Narasu Appa Mali (1952), which placed personal laws outside Article 13, to Joseph Shine and Navtej Singh Johar (2018), which emphasised constitutional morality over patriarchal and customary norms. The analysis then turns to Hindu personal law. Despite codification, patriarchal traces persist in the restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (T. Sareetha; Saroj Rani), in the “natural guardian” provision of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 (Githa Hariharan), and in …

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title: Stress–Innovation Dynamics in Public Disaster Management Organizations: A Conditional Process Analysis
abstract: Abstract Although the importance of innovation in disaster response is acknowledged, limited research has examined innovative behavior (IB) within disaster management institutions. This study employs the Job Demands-Resources model, Conservation of Resources theory, and the challenge-hindrance stressor framework to investigate how job environment (JE) is associated with IB through job stress (JSt), with the moderating roles of job satisfaction (JS) and knowledge sharing (KS). Using survey data from 131 disaster management officials across provincial and municipal levels in South Korea, conditional process analysis reveals a paradoxical pattern: a deficient JE is associated with higher JSt, which in turn is conditionally associated with greater IB. High JS serves as a buffer, while strong KS amplifies the JSt–IB relationship. Notably, the conditional indirect effect of JE on IB via JSt is strongest when JS is low and KS is high. These findings provide insights into the dynamics of stress and innovation in disaster contexts, informing theory and policy for resilience-building in resource-constrained organizations.

title: Nociplastic Pain: Beyond the Pain Generator – Rethinking Diagnosis and Redefining Successful Pain Management
abstract: Nociplastic pain is increasingly recognised as an important mechanism underlying chronic pain that cannot be adequately explained by ongoing tissue damage or a lesion of the somatosensory nervous system. Introduced by the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) as a third mechanistic descriptor alongside nociceptive and neuropathic pain, it represents altered nociceptive processing and pain modulation. Its recognition has important implications for the assessment and management of patients with persistent pain, particularly those whose symptoms appear disproportionate to structural findings or respond poorly to conventional interventions.This editorial discusses the evolving understanding of nociplastic pain, its clinical features and the challenges associated with diagnosis. It highlights the importance of recognising pain hypersensitivity, widespread or regional pain, and associated symptoms such as fatigue, sleep disturbance and cognitive difficulties. Nociplastic mechanisms may coexist with nociceptive and neuropathic mechanisms, making individualised assessment essential. Management should move beyond a purely tissue-centred approach towards multimodal, person-centred care incorporating pain education, graded physical activity, psychological interventions, appropriate pharmacotherapy and attention to sleep and emotional wellbeing. title: Socioeconomic determinants of financial inclusion in OECD countries (2004–2023)
abstract: Introduction Financial inclusion is a multidimensional phenomenon associated with economic and social development. However, differences in physical banking access across developed economies remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the socioeconomic factors associated with financial inclusion in 38 OECD countries over the period 2004–2023, using commercial bank branches per 100,000 adults as a proxy for its physical-access dimension. Methods A quantitative, non-experimental, longitudinal research design was adopted using World Bank data. This operationalization enables a comparative assessment of traditional banking infrastructure while recognizing that financial inclusion encompasses additional dimensions, including financial-service usage, account ownership, and digital access. Descriptive analysis was complemented by panel econometric estimation using country and year fixed effects and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE), with a common AR(1) error structure. A complementary Common Correlated Effects Pooled (CCEP) specification was used to assess the sensitivity of the estimates to unobserved common factors. Results The results indicate positive and statistically significant associations between physical banking access and GDP per capita and unemployment, whereas internet use and ICT goods exports exhibit negative and statistically significant associations. Dis…

title: Real-world evaluation of the positive predictive value and transmission burden of a novel implantable cardiac monitor with a remote reprogramming capability: insights from a single-center experience
abstract: Background Implantable cardiac monitors (ICMs) are widely used for long-term arrhythmia surveillance but are often limited by a high false-positive alert rate, increasing the workload for device clinics. The LUX-Dx™ ICM incorporates dual-stage detection algorithms and remote reprogramming features designed to improve diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency. Objective To assess the real-world performance of the LUX-Dx™ ICM across all detectable arrhythmias, evaluating positive predictive value (PPV), transmission burden, and the impact of remote reprogramming. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 133 consecutive patients who received a LUX-Dx™ ICM between July 2023 and October 2024 with follow-up data collected through June 2025. Device episodes and transmissions were reviewed over a median 13-month follow-up. PPV was calculated at both patient- and episode-levels. Changes in PPV before and after remote reprogramming were also assessed. Results A total of 55,064 episodes and 5,192 transmissions were recorded (4.0 episodes and 1.2 transmissions per patient-month). Overall patient-level PPV was 87% (110/126), highest for bradycardia (100%) and lowest for pauses (71%). Overall, 93 of 126 patients (74%) with adjudicated episodes had at least one false-positive detection during follow-up. Episode-level PPV was 82% (95% CI: 82−83). Remote reprogramming was performed in 34% of patie…

title: Structure and Priority of Strategic Factors in Indonesian Real-World Asset Tokenization: An ISM–MICMAC Approach
abstract: Background: Real-world asset (RWA) tokenization has entered implementation in Indonesia ahead of a comprehensive regulatory framework, leaving regulators and the industry without a structured basis for ordering interventions.Purpose: This study models the structure and priority of the strategic factors for RWA tokenization in Indonesia. "Priority" denotes a factor's position in an expert-elicited influence hierarchy and its driving power, not an estimated policy effect.Design/methodology/approach: Using a Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framing, this study applies Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) to pairwise judgments from a purposive panel of four experts (regulator, industry issuer, IT and cybersecurity practitioner, and blockchain academic). Fifteen factors were aggregated by majority rule (at least three of four). Seventeen of 105 pair decisions were set by the research team rather than by majority; one of them, the treatment of the F1–F14 relation (coded mutual by three experts and analytically resolved so that F14 does not influence F1), determines whether an informative hierarchy exists. Sensitivity analyses cover alternative F1–F14 codings, per-expert reruns, leave-one-out aggregates, alternative tie rules, and MICMAC midpoints. The model reflects expert judgment, not observed poli…

title: Desempleo juvenil y su impacto socioeconómico en el cantón Babahoyo, 2024: análisis jurídico del derecho al trabajo
abstract: El desempleo juvenil compromete el derecho al trabajo, la autonomía de los jóvenes y la cohesión social de territorios con economías poco diversificadas. El estudio analizó su impacto socioeconómico en el cantón Babahoyo en 2024 desde el derecho al trabajo. Con enfoque cualitativo descriptivo-analítico, se analizaron documentalmente la Constitución, el Código del Trabajo, el Pacto Internacional de Derechos Económicos, Sociales y Culturales y doctrina indexada. Los resultados muestran que el ordenamiento reconoce a los jóvenes como actores productivos, pero carece de instrumentos específicos y exigibles de inserción laboral juvenil con enfoque territorial. Se concluye que el desempleo juvenil en Babahoyo debe abordarse como un problema de garantía de derechos, con políticas locales articuladas.

title: Determinants of Operational Efficiency in Indonesian Conventional Banks: The Role of Internal Bank Factors
abstract: Background: This study examines the development of operational efficiency in Indonesian commercial banks and investigates the effects of bank size (SIZE), capital adequacy ratio (CAR), non-performing loans (NPL), and loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) on the cost-to-income ratio (CIR) among conventional commercial banks.Design/methodology/approach: This study uses panel data from 43 conventional commercial banks in Indonesia over the 2021–2025 period. The relationships between the explanatory variables and CIR are examined using panel regression with a random effects model (REM).Findings: The results show that SIZE, CAR, NPL, and LDR are jointly significant in explaining variations in CIR. Individually, SIZE and CAR have significant negative effects on the CIR, whereas NPL has a significant positive effect. LDR has a negative but statistically insignificant effect on the CIR.Conclusion: The findings suggest that larger banks and banks with stronger capital positions tend to operate more efficiently, whereas higher credit risk is associated with greater operating costs relative to operating income. Although lending intensity may be relevant to operational efficiency, its effect was not statistically significant in this study. These results highlight the importance of scale, capital adequacy, and credit risk management in improving banks’ operational efficiency.Originality/value: This s…

title: Burnout in Medical Students: The Role of Learning Disabilities and Perceived Financial Stability
abstract: Abstract Burnout is a psychological syndrome resulting from chronic occupational stress, characterized by exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced personal accomplishment. Among medical students, burnout is highly prevalent and has long-term implications for physician well-being and patient safety. This study examined the prevalence and severity of burnout among medical students, focusing on the interface of learning disabilities (LDs) and socioeconomic status. Burnout was measured using the Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT), which evaluates both core symptoms–exhaustion, cognitive, and emotional impairment–and secondary symptoms, including psychosomatic and psychological manifestations. Participants provided demographic data on LD status, gender, and financial background. Findings revealed that burnout among medical students is multifactorial, influenced by both personal and structural factors. Students reporting financial insecurity or self- or medically diagnosed LDs demonstrated significantly higher BAT scores across both core and secondary domains. Females, financial instability, and presence of a LD were significant predictors of psychosomatic and psychological burnout symptoms, while students from lower-income backgrounds or with substantial debt reported greater emotional exhaustion and disengagement. ESG performance, capital expenditure and profitability: the moderating role of corporate governance in French firms
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) and its subdimensions on capital expenditure and the financial performance of French firms, while exploring the moderating effect of board attributes. Design/methodology/approach The authors examined a sample of 671 company-year observations from French companies listed on the SBF 120 index. They used generalized method of moments estimation, alternative measures and a sample of non-family firms as a robustness check. Findings Strong ESG performance significantly reduces Capex and return on equity, while its effect on return on assets depends on governance characteristics. Several board attributes moderate the ESG–Capex and ESG–performance relationships, and the results are partially confirmed in the non-family sample. Originality/value This study makes three contributions. First, it clarifies the crowding-out mechanism linking ESG to Capex. Second, it reconciles conflicting ESG-profitability findings by showing that the negative impact falls mainly on equity holders’ returns. Third, it provides new French evidence that governance mechanisms operate differently than in other contexts.

title: Impacto financiero de los toques de queda nocturnos en vendedores informales de Babahoyo: un análisis jurídico-documental
abstract: Los toques de queda nocturnos, adoptados como medidas de estados de excepción, restringen la libertad de tránsito y reducen los ingresos de quienes trabajan por cuenta propia en el espacio público. El estudio analizó el impacto financiero de estas medidas sobre los vendedores informales, con Babahoyo como contexto, desde el marco jurídico ecuatoriano e internacional. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo, de alcance descriptivo-analítico, mediante análisis documental jurídico de la Constitución, la Ley Orgánica de Garantías Jurisdiccionales y Control Constitucional, tratados de derechos humanos y doctrina indexada. Los resultados muestran que la Constitución protege expresamente el trabajo autónomo en espacios públicos y exige proporcionalidad, temporalidad y territorialidad en las restricciones, pero el ordenamiento no prevé medidas de mitigación económica para los trabajadores informales afectados. Se concluye que la proporcionalidad de los toques de queda debe valorarse incluyendo su costo económico para los grupos vulnerables y acompañarse de medidas compensatorias.

Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Quality of Msme Financial Reports: The Role of Digital Financial Recording Systems And Human Resource Competence
abstract: Financial report quality is a crucial aspect in achieving transparency and accountability in the financial management of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). However, a pre-survey of MSMEs in Bandar Lampung City indicates low utilization of digital financial recording systems and limited human resource competence in financial management, resulting in suboptimal financial report quality. This study aims to analyze the impact of using digital financial recording systems and human resource competence on the quality of MSME financial reports in Bandar Lampung City. A quantitative approach with an explanatory design was employed. Primary data were collected via online and offline questionnaires distributed to 165 MSME owners selected through purposive sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS Version 4 software. The results show that the use of digital financial recording systems has a positive and significant effect on financial report quality (path coefficient 0.681; t-statistic 6.571; p-value 0.000). Human resource competence also has a positive and significant effect on financial report quality (path coefficient 0.250; t-statistic 2.460; p-value 0.014). These findings confirm that simultaneously enhancing the use of digital systems and human resource competence can improve the quality of MSME f…

title: Financial Distress Analysis of PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations Tbk Using the Altman, Zmijewski, Springate, and Grover Models Period 2022 – 2025
abstract: This research is motivated by indications of financial distress at PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations Tbk, as seen from the company's financial condition during the 2022–2025 period. This study aims to determine and analyze the level of financial distress based on the Altman Z-Score, Springate S-Score, Zmijewski X-Score, and Grover G-Score models. The study uses a descriptive quantitative approach with secondary data in the form of financial reports and stock market data. The study population is all financial reports of PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations Tbk, while the sample is financial report data from 2022–2025 required in the calculation of the four models. The research instruments include data on current assets, current liabilities, total assets, total liabilities, retained earnings, sales, EBT, net income, interest expense, interest income, share price, and the number of shares outstanding. The analysis was carried out by calculating the ratios and scores of each model and classifying the results based on their criteria. The results show that all four models consistently categorize the company in financial distress during 2022–2025. In conclusion, PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations Tbk faced consistent financial pressures throughout the study period.

title: Prueba no solicitada y derecho a la defensa: análisis crítico del problema planteado en la consulta 716-2023-P-CNJ
abstract: La incorporación al proceso de pruebas que ninguna de las partes solicitó oportunamente tensiona el principio dispositivo, la igualdad procesal y el derecho a la defensa. El estudio analizó críticamente el problema jurídico que plantea la consulta 716-2023-P-CNJ de la Corte Nacional de Justicia sobre la prueba no solicitada y su incidencia en el derecho a la defensa. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo, de alcance descriptivo-analítico, mediante análisis documental jurídico de la Constitución, el Código Orgánico General de Procesos, el Código Orgánico Integral Penal, el Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial, jurisprudencia constitucional y doctrina procesal indexada. Los resultados muestran que el ordenamiento admite de forma excepcional la prueba no anunciada o dispuesta de oficio, siempre que se garantice la contradicción, y que las absoluciones de consulta carecen de fuerza vinculante general. Se concluye que la prueba no solicitada solo es compatible con la defensa si es excepcional, motivada y sometida a contradicción efectiva.

abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh hambatan akses vertikal ruang layanan yang masih bergantung pada tangga. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis kondisi ruang layanan Perpustakaan Universitas PGRI Semarang berdasarkan perspektif Universal Design yang dikembangkan oleh Spina. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan studi kasus. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi dan wawancara terhadap lima informan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldana. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kondisi ruang layanan berdasarkan aspek Architectural Features, Fixtures, Lighting, Furniture, dan Signage masih memiliki beberapa keterbatasan. Hambatan ditemukan pada mobilitas antar lantai, distribusi fasilitas, pencahayaan ruang, penataan fasilitas belajar, serta sistem navigasi. Mobilitas pemustaka masih bergantung pada tangga karena belum tersedianya lift. Selain itu, distribusi fasilitas toilet belum merata pada setiap lantai layanan, sementara penataan rak koleksi, kondisi pencahayaan pada area tertentu, dan pengaturan ruang belajar turut memengaruhi kenyamanan dan kemudahan pemustaka dalam memanfaatkan perpustakaan. title: PRIORITIZING E-LEARNING CHALLENGES IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES’ HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS USING DELPHI-AHP FRAMEWORK WITH AI-ASSISTED DESIGN SUPPORT
abstract: The widespread use of the internet has accelerated a shift from conventional pedagogy to e-learning environments in higher education institutions (HEIs), enabling greater learner autonomy and flexibility. While many countries have successfully integrated e-learning into their educational systems, HEIs in developing countries, such as Nigeria, continue to face significant implementation challenges, including infrastructure and connectivity limitations. Existing studies often enumerate these challenges without adequately prioritizing them, given the financial and operational constraints common in such contexts. This study, therefore, investigates the prioritization of critical e-learning challenges in Nigerian HEIs. An empirical approach was adopted, using surveys grounded in prior literature and a Delphi questionnaire administered to e-learning experts at public and private universities. Descriptive statistical screening and expert-based categorization techniques were used to refine and group the identified challenges, while a Delphi Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) framework was applied to determine their relative importance. To improve the formulation of both the Delphi and AHP instruments, an AI-assisted methodological calibration based on a customized GPT-supported framework was used to optimize expert-panel configuration, procedural planning, and Delphi-AHP instrument desig…

title: Biomaterials and biofabrication in the Netherlands: state of the art in 2026
abstract: Abstract Biomaterials and biofabrication are multidisciplinary and rapidly evolving fields that enable innovations that are crucial for addressing current healthcare challenges. The Netherlands has a broad, active, and collaborative research community that is developing advanced biomaterials and cutting.edge biofabrication methods, with applications in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, in vitro disease modeling, and biomedical devices. Dutch researchers have pioneered advanced biofabrication, supramolecular and inorganic chemistry for creating biomaterials, organoids and organ-on-chip in vitro platforms, and regenerative medicine. This paper presents recent work on biomaterials and biofabrication and their applications from 11 prominent research institutions across the Netherlands, and it describes joint initiatives that target broader goals within the field. Contributors from each institution provide insights into recent progress, key scientific contributions, and forward-looking perspectives. By presenting the state-of-the-art research landscape, this article serves as a reference for scientists actively engaged in or planning to initiate biofabrication or biomaterials-related research, offering guidance on technology selection, experimental design, academic collaboration, and translational development.

title: Influence of urban view factors on seasonal outdoor thermal conditions: implications for sustainable residential neighbourhood design in hot semi-arid climates
abstract: Purpose Urban geometry plays a critical role in shaping the thermal environment of cities, particularly in hot and semi-arid climates. While the Sky View Factor (SVF) is widely used to represent urban openness, it does not fully capture the complexity of urban form. Existing studies often overlook the combined influence of built and vegetative components on urban microclimates. Design/methodology/approach This study addresses this gap by quantifying the role of SVF, Building View Factor (BVF), and Tree View Factor (TVF) across residential areas and examining their spatial and temporal influence across Local Climate Zones (LCZs) on air temperature and thermal comfort. The analysis was conducted across 11 residential neighbourhoods in Jaipur, India, covering 66 locations of interest. Micrometeorological and morphological data were collected during summer and winter at 14:00 and 20:00, representing peak heating and nocturnal cooling periods. Findings SVF showed a weak positive association with air temperature during summer and winter daytime (r = 0.11–0.27), reversing to a moderate negative association at winter night (r = −0.335). BVF exhibited weak negative daytime associations (r = −0.11 and −0.07) but a moderate positive association at winter night (r = 0.417), indicating restricted nocturnal cooling. TVF remained weakly negative across conditions (r = −0.04 to −0.18). PET sho…

title: Design features and adolescents’ perceived safety in forest parks: evidence from Nanjing, China
abstract: Forest parks can support adolescents’ health, nature experience, and outdoor activities, but their use may depend partly on how safe these environments are perceived to be. Responding to limited evidence on adolescents’ perceived safety in Chinese forest parks, this study examined variation in perceived-safety ratings across 24 landscape design features and investigated the relationship between preference and perceived safety. A photo-assisted questionnaire was administered to 551 adolescents aged 13–19 in three national forest parks in Nanjing, China. Perceived-safety ratings differed significantly across the 24 features. Higher ratings were associated with open grassy areas, organised planting, clear signs, proximity to buildings, and wide paths, whereas damaged facilities, stagnant water, damaged path surfaces, fallen or leaning trees, and damaged signs received the lowest ratings. Several features, including multiple paths, curved paths, and dominant shadows cast by tree canopies, received intermediate ratings. Preference and perceived safety were positively associated for all 24 matched features (r = 0.37–0.71, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), although their mean ratings were not equivalent for many features. The findings highlight the importance of visibility, legibility, maintenance, environmental order, and perceived support in adolescent-oriented forest-park design, while …

title: Design Priorities for Portable Corn Shellers in Smallholder Farming
abstract: Portable corn shellers are intended to reduce the time and labor required to separate kernels from cobs, but design decisions must balance throughput, kernel quality, mobility, safety, maintainability, and cost. This article presents a design-oriented narrative review of published corn-sheller studies and postharvest guidance, with emphasis on the requirements of smallholder farmer groups. Relevant literature identified in the project’s reference base was examined alongside accessible journal and institutional sources. The studies were compared according to shelling mechanism, drive system, separation features, operating parameters, reported performance indicators, and limitations. Published work shows that corn-sheller designs vary from manually operated devices to engine- or motor-driven systems and automated configurations. Rotational speed, crop moisture, shelling contact surfaces, and separation arrangements are recurring design considerations. The review proposes a practical evaluation framework that treats capacity as only one of several criteria and distinguishes demonstrated performance from untested claims about portability and economic benefit. For the portable prototype developed in the associated project, mobility is currently supported by the wheeled configuration, whereas pushing force, field maneuverability, fuel consumption, maintenance cost, and user acceptanc…

title: Personal Law Reform in Nigeria and Bangladesh: Reconciling Universalism and Cultural Relativism
abstract: Abstract This paper critically analyzes and compares the challenges and possibilities associated with internalizing international human rights norms in two contrasting political societies, Nigeria and Bangladesh. It examines the customary and religious legal regimes that shape polygamous practices among Muslim, Christian, and Hindu communities in both jurisdictions. It further evaluates and compares relevant statutory, judicial, and political interventions, assessing their effectiveness and explaining the conditions underlying their success or failure. The paper’s central objective is to illuminate why controversies surrounding “Western” liberal human rights values arise in the Global South, and how such disputes are articulated, negotiated, and institutionally processed. Drawing on Benvenisti and Harel’s theoretical framework of “discordant parity,” it argues that the tension between reform and resistance is genuine and cannot simply be disregarded; normative disagreement should not be treated merely as evidence of irrationality or political obstruction. Human rights advocates should therefore engage seriously with conservative social perspectives rather than dismissing them outright or advancing uncompromising forms of universalism and liberalism. Aggressive universalist rhetoric is frequently counterproductive, reinforcing an equally assertive cultural exceptionalism. Princi…

title: An Analysis of the Teaching Reform Path of the Business Russian Course from the Perspective of Industry-Education Integration: A Case Study of Qingdao Institute of Technology
abstract: In the context of the integration of industry and education, the teaching of Russian major courses in applied undergraduate education urgently needs to strengthen the connection between language competence cultivation and professional practice requirements. With Business Russian course in Qingdao Institute of Technology as an instance and by integrating the current teaching conditions of the course with the exchange between schools and enterprises and other practical teaching resources related to international issues, this paper will discuss the need to optimize the teaching of the course. Focusing on the steps involved in cross-border e-commerce business processes, the author explores the directions of reform in four areas, including integration of the teaching materials, innovation of the teaching methods, conversion of practical resources, and enhancement of diversified evaluation to facilitate the combination of Business Russian language instruction with professional environments and serve as a guide to developing applied undergraduate Russian major courses and cultivating applied personnel.

title: The moral infrastructure of financial markets: public regulatory discourse and the pillars of market justification
abstract: Abstract Recent research on morality and financial regulation has focused on the role of moral reasoning in episodes of post-crisis regulation. Adopting a processual approach, this paper argues that moral reasoning continuously and dynamically shapes regulatory logic, even in ordinary times. Combining insights from pragmatic sociology and social research on financial markets, it claims that regulatory logic is structured by an imperative to sustain two “pillars of market justification”: the notions that financial markets are just and societally beneficial. Strains that undermine these pillars recur continually, yielding ongoing regulatory responses aimed at reestablishing justifiability in the pillars’ terms. Though these responses are subject to political controversy, the controversy itself is structured by the imperative to sustain the pillars. To demonstrate this, I analyze texts published by American regulatory agencies in 2016–2022, focusing on strains stemming from financial product complexity. The analysis illuminates the entanglement of morality, regulation, and political controversy.

title: Determination of Some Air Pollutant and Meteorological Parameters in Abak Market, Abak Municipality of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: The determination of some Air Pollutant and Meteorological Parameter in Market, Abak Local Government Area was carried out using standard analytical method; gaseous measuring instrument was used for the analysis. The pollutant monitored were; NO2, SO2, H2S, CO, NH3, Cl2, HCN, TVOC, CH2O, PM2.5, PM10,Temperature, Relative Humidity (RH), Pressure and wind speed ( WS). The results for the concentration of air pollutant and their air quality index AQI reveals as follows; NO2:(0.15± 0.04 (ppm), AQI = 150), SO2: (0.20 ± 0.07 (ppm), AQI = 40), H2S: (0.14 ± 0.06 (ppm), AQI = 70), CO: (4.01± 0.53 (ppm), AQI = 80.2), NH3: (5.13 ± 0.2 (ppm), AQI = 102.6), Cl2: (0.48 ± 49.5 (ppm), AQI = 480), HCN: (1.59 ± 0.56 (ppm), AQI = 15,900), TVOC: (3.95 ± 0.74 (mg/m3 ), AQI = 790), CH2O (0.06 ± 0.07 (mg/m3 ), AQI = 3,000), PM2.5: (83 ± 8.54 µm/m3 ), AQI = 3.32), PM10: (145 ± 4.18(µm/m3 ), AQI = 245.76), Temperature: (33.0 ± 0.00 (0C), Relative Humidity: 66.0 ± 0.00 (0%), Pressure: (1002 ± 1.79kpa), and Wind Speed: (0.78 ± 0.69 (m/s). The result showed that pressure, NO2 NH3, Cl2, HCN, TVOC, CH2O, PM2.5, PM10, Temperature and Relative Humidity were higher than FEPA safe limit while SO2, H2S, CO and Wind Speed were within the FFPA safe limit. This result is an indication of presence of possible air pollutants in the air of the study area which may result in many health problem.

title: ALTERNATIVE DIGITAL FINANCE IN THE GLOBAL FINANCIAL MARKET SYSTEM: CURRENT TRENDS AND STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATIONS
abstract: The article examines current trends and structural transformations in alternative digital finance within the global financial market. It systematises changes in market geography, business models, funding sources, data and technology use, regulatory approaches, and systemic integration. The study identifies a shift from predominantly P2P models towards hybrid forms combining digital platforms, banks, institutional investors, and technology companies. It highlights the growing role of the United States and the Americas following the contraction of China’s P2P segment, as well as the increasing importance of institutional funding, embedded finance, and automated credit assessment. It is argued that the sector’s development reflects not the displacement of traditional intermediaries, but the platform-based reintermediation of financial relations.

Two Decades of Bevacizumab Utilization in Croatia: The Impact of Biosimilar Market Entry on Consumption Trends
abstract: Background: Bevacizumab is an extensively used biological anticancer medicine, while the introduction of biosimilars has created opportunities to increase competition, improve access, and reduce treatment costs. We aimed to evaluate long-term trends in bevacizumab utilization and expenditure in Croatia, with particular emphasis on the impact of biosimilar market entry. Methods: National bevacizumab utilization and pharmaceutical expenditure data for 2006 to 2025 were obtained from the IQVIA database. Utilization was assessed according to total consumption, vial size, brand, and market share, while average expenditure per vial was calculated. Trends before and after biosimilar introduction were evaluated. Results: Total bevacizumab consumption increased substantially, from 127 400 mg in 2006 to 10 044 600 mg in 2025. Following biosimilar introduction in 2020, utilization rapidly shifted from Avastin ® to biosimilar products, with biosimilars accounting for more than 94% of utilization by 2025. During the same period, average vial prices decreased substantially. Conclusion: Biosimilar market entry was associated with rapid market transformation, increased competition, and lower unit costs while overall bevacizumab utilization continued to increase.

title: An Industrial-Deployable Vision Framework for Online Resistance Spot-Weld Inspection of Automotive Tailor-Welded Blanks
abstract: This paper develops and validates an industrially deployable vision framework for online resistance spot-weld (RSW) inspection, integrating weld localization, three-level appearance-quality classification, and shop-floor deployment. The framework combines controlled imaging for reflective sheet metal, a HALCON deep-learning detector with a compact SqueezeNet backbone, a three-class Good/Medium/Bad labeling strategy to account for ambiguous weld appearances, and a C#-HALCON deployment program supporting confidence-threshold adjustment, ROI filtering, alarms, and image traceability. The Medium class is further intended as a warning category for potential process drift; this early-warning function is formulated as a hypothesis and has not yet been validated with time-resolved production data. On an in-house dataset of 500 line-acquired images containing 2061 labeled welds, the optimized model achieves 97.6 ± 0.3% recall and 93.3 ± 0.4% precision (mean ± standard deviation over three independent training runs with different random seeds), with a network inference time of 28.1 ms per image. An independent field test on 2312 welds demonstrates a controllable precision–miss-rate trade-off, achieving 93.4–98.3% precision and a 2.3–4.7% miss rate under different confidence thresholds. Comparisons with YOLOv8, RT-DETR, and lightweight detectors further demonstrate the practical effective…

title: The Norwegian Market Investigation Tool: an analysis in the EEA/EFTA context
abstract: Abstract This article examines the Norwegian Market Investigation Tool (MIT) within the European Economic Area/European Free Trade Association (EEA/EFTA) competition law framework, analysing both its institutional design and its implications for enforcement and legal certainty. It pays particular attention to how the MIT fits into the EEA’s two-pillar system, characterized by substantial alignment with EU competition law but more limited procedural convergence. The MIT empowers the Norwegian Competition Authority (NCA) to address structural market problems through a two-step procedure of investigation and remedial intervention without requiring proof of infringement. It is premised on the view that traditional enforcement tools may not always be sufficient to address market conditions that weaken effective competition. At the same time, the instrument raises concerns relating to procedural safeguards, including predictability and legal certainty, while also illustrating the uncertain scope of the national margin of manoeuvre within the EEA competition law framework. The analysis highlights tensions between effective competition enforcement and the protection of undertakings’ rights within a hybrid regime combining ex ante and ex post elements. It argues that the MIT represents a legally uncertain addition to the Norwegian enforcement framework, the practical significance of whi…

title: Determinants and Constraints of Smallholder Vegetable Market Participation in Zuru Local Government Area Kebbi State, Nigeria
abstract: Transitioning smallholder farmers from subsistence to commercial agriculture requires a deep understanding of the factors driving market participation and the barriers hindering it. This study investigates the determinants and constraints of smallholder vegetable market participation in Zuru Local Government Area, Kebbi State, Nigeria. Using a multi-stage sampling technique, primary data were collected from 212 smallholder vegetable farmers. Data were analyzed using a binary logistic regression model and a five-point Likert scale. The binary logistic regression model was statistically significant (LR χ² = 36.815, df = 12, p < 0.001, McFadden pseudo-R² = 0.188). Results indicate that access to market information is the strongest positive determinant of participation (Exp(B) = 4.114, p < 0.01), followed by household size (p < 0.10) and access to credit (p < 0.10). Conversely, distance to market exerts a significant negative influence (Exp(B) = 0.861, p < 0.05). Constraint analysis reveals that the high cost of inputs (Mean = 4.25), inadequate capital/lack of credit (Mean = 4.20), exploitation by middlemen (Mean = 4.13), and lack of storage facilities (Mean = 4.10) are the most severe bottlenecks. The study concludes that transaction costs, financial exclusion, and post-harvest infrastructural deficits heavily constrain commercialization. It is recommended that policymakers establ…

title: Gendered Labor Market Trajectories After Job Loss: Unemployment Insurance and Workers with Children in the United States
abstract: This study examines the gendered associations of Unemployment Insurance (UI) with labor market outcomes for unemployed workers with children following job separation in the United States. Using a feminist social provisioning perspective and the panel data from the 2008 Survey of Income and Program Participation, this study analyzed how UI benefit receipt and caregiver-friendly state UI provisions relate to labor-force and caregiving-related withdrawal, employment, hours, and earnings over three years after job separation. UI receipt was associated with larger reductions in labor-force and caregiving-related withdrawal overall, with a pronounced association among women. In later periods, UI receipt was associated with larger increases in work hours and employment among women, but larger decreases among men. In contrast, the Compelling Family Reason (CFR) provision showed limited and exploratory evidence of associations with larger increases in caregiving-related withdrawal and larger decreases in late-period employment and work hours among women. This research informs broader policy discussions on gender disparities in caregiving and labor force reentry during macroeconomic instability, highlighting the potential role of UI benefits and the limitations of caregiver-friendly provisions alone in addressing gender inequality.

title: Asymmetric Dynamic Associations of Real Estate Market Cycles and Household Sector Credit Changes: Evidence from Monthly Panel Data of 70 Cities in China
abstract: This paper examines whether the marginal association between household-sector credit and city-level housing price growth differs between upturn and downturn regimes of the real estate market cycle. Based on monthly panel data of 70 Chinese cities from January 2015 to December 2025, we take the month-on-month growth rate of new commercial residential housing prices as the dependent variable and construct a predetermined market regime variable using the three-month lagged moving average. After standard data cleaning to address missing values and ensure the availability of lagged variables, our final baseline sample consists of 9,055 city-month observations. We employ a two-way fixed effects model with city and month fixed effects, and adopt local projections to estimate the relationships across horizons from ℎ = 0 to ℎ = 12 months. The results show that the interaction coefficient between household loan growth and the upturn regime is 0.0113 (SE = 0.0031, p < .001), indicating a stronger positive marginal association during market upturns. This interaction term remains significantly positive when the dependent variable is replaced by second-hand housing prices and when the regime identification window is adjusted to a lagged six-month moving average. Local projection estimates indicate that the regime difference is positive at all horizons, peaking at 0.0345 in month 6 and remain…

title: State, Market, and Trust Production
abstract: Digital dating platforms increasingly shape relationship formation while raising concerns about fraud, identity deception, privacy, safety, and accountability. This article examines Tokyo Enmusubi, a publicly commissioned matchmaking service, through comparative legal and policy analysis of the United States (US), European Union (EU) , United Kingdom (UK), and Australia. It compares market-oriented, regulated-platform, government-supported industry, and public-provision arrangements, focusing on how institutions allocate trust-related functions, costs, and accountability. The analysis distinguishes identity assurance, data protection, and responses to harmful conduct, explaining why safeguards in one area cannot establish overall trustworthiness. Tokyo Enmusubi combines registration checks, contracted operations, and governmental oversight, but reported participation and marriage figures do not demonstrate superior safety or effectiveness. Its significance lies in extending platform-governance analysis to public provision and the accountability questions it creates. The article proposes proportionate responsibilities, independent review, measurable indicators, and conditions for adapting institutional functions across jurisdictions. Direct public provision requires justification against feasible alternatives. Public involvement should address demonstrated needs while preserving…

title: Investors’ Perception regarding the Price Risk and their knowledge on Derivatives Market, its Products and Mechanism: Bangladesh perspective
abstract: This paper aims to reveal the perception of stock market investors regarding price risk and their knowledge of the derivatives market, its products and mechanism in the context of Bangladesh. A structured questionnaire has been used to get response from the participants and the collected data has been analyzed by using statistical methods. The results show that the investors' perception of price risk is significantly influenced by their level of knowledge, trading experience, and risk appetite. The study also reveals that investors have limited knowledge about the derivatives market and its products, especially their associated risks and returns. The study concludes with recommendations for improving the education and awareness of prospective investors on the derivatives market and its products to promote informed decision-making and mitigate risks associated with the stock market of Bangladesh. title: “It is impossible to put a ceiling price on an artist’s mind”: Government Regulation and Post-war British Fashion, 1945–1949
abstract: Abstract Examining post-war government regulation of the clothing industry, and responses to this regulation, disrupts existing historiographies of British fashion in the 1940s. Focusing on the impact of ceiling prices and the implementation of II0II and R.M.H.O. regulations between 1945 and 1949, this article explains what these regulations were, how they differed from Utility regulations, and the economic and political circumstances of their origin. It then analyses their impact on how high-end ready-to-wear—or “wholesale couture”—fashions were produced, promoted, and understood (and misunderstood) by consumers. Using a combination of archival material, fashion images, and extant garments, this article argues that the often-overlooked years of the post-war 1940s were a time of considerable dynamism and agency in high-end British ready-to-wear. It highlights how, despite the challenges it created, regulation imposed by the Labour government contributed to this dynamism by encouraging wholesale couturiers to innovate and collectively organize. By forcing processes of introspection and articulation about what made British wholesale couture distinctive, it argues that regulation actually helped the sector prepare to take advantage of the growing economic prosperity of the 1950s, laying strong foundations for the future success of British womenswear in subsequent decades.

title: Disaster Risk Forecasting, Data Analytics, Strategic Foresight and The Future of Disaster Risk Management
abstract: Forecasting and data analytics have advanced rapidly, but better information about hazards does not automatically reduce disaster losses. This narrative review brings together research and policy evidence on hazard and impact forecasting, vulnerability analytics, strategic foresight, and anticipatory action. It uses Nigerian flood episodes from 2022 and 2024, alongside the 2025 Annual Flood Outlook, as illustrative cases. Sources were purposively selected from peer reviewed studies, multilateral reports, and Nigerian official records. Bibliographic details and selected quantitative claims were checked against accessible publisher and institutional records. A structured comparison of the cases distinguishes the availability of forecasts, information about infrastructure, actionable protocols, and reported consequences. Because the analysis relies on secondary accounts, it does not claim causal attribution. The paper proposes a four-function decision architecture that brings together probabilistic warnings, evidence on exposure and vulnerability, scenario-based foresight, and pre-authorised action protocols, with feedback and accountability built in. Its contribution lies not in a new forecasting algorithm, but in operationalising these functions through testable governance indicators. Priorities for Nigeria and other African institutions include interoperable risk information, a…

title: Directional Forecasting of the BIST Tourism Index and the Incremental Value of Machine Learning over Simple Benchmarks
abstract: This study assesses machine learning’s incremental forecasting value for the Borsa Istanbul Tourism Index through directional, probabilistic, and intraday economic evaluations. Twenty-three market-based predictors from daily 2010–2026 data were used at 1644 forecast origins in 2020–July 2026. Hyperparameters were selected using outcomes realized before 2020, and models were refitted quarterly. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and long short-term memory networks were compared with majority, historical-prevalence, directional-persistence, and first-order probabilistic-persistence benchmarks. Paired circular moving-block bootstrap inference addressed serial dependence and multiple comparisons. Inference was conditional on selected configurations and fitted models, excluding uncertainty from repeated hyperparameter selection and model fitting. Directional persistence achieved the highest Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), 0.110, versus approximately 0.088 for logistic regression and random forest. No fitted model established MCC superiority over persistence. XGBoost’s Brier score was 0.24610, versus 0.24888 for historical prevalence and 0.24738 for probabilistic persistence; primary adjusted comparisons did not establish superiority over either benchmark. abstract: Abstract We present an overview of the MINERVA survey, a 259.8 hr (prime) and 127 hr (parallel) Cycle 4 treasury program on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). MINERVA is obtaining eight-filter NIRCam medium-band imaging (F140M, F162M, F182M, F210M, F250M, F300M, F360M, and F460M) and two-filter MIRI imaging (F1280W and F1500W) in four of the five CANDELS extragalactic fields: Ultra Deep Survey (UDS), COSMOS, AEGIS, and GOODS-N. These fields were previously observed with seven to nine NIRCam filters by the PRIMER, CEERS, and JADES programs. MINERVA reaches a 5 σ depth of 28.1 mag in F300M and covers ∼542 arcmin 2 , increasing the area of existing JWST medium-band coverage by ∼7×. The MIRI imaging reaches a 5 σ depth of 23.9 mag in F1280W and covers ∼275 arcmin 2 . When combined with existing imaging, these data will provide a photometric catalog with 26–35 filters (depending on field). This paper presents a detailed breakdown of the filter coverage, exposure times, and field layout relative to previous observations, as well as an overview of the primary science goals of the project. These include uncovering the physics of enigmatic sources hiding in current broadband catalogs, improving systematics on stellar mass functions and number densities by factors of ≳3, and resolved mapping of stellar mass and star formation at 1 < z < 6. When complete, MINERVA will become an integr…

title: Subgrid Orographic Drag and Winter Surface Wind Forecast Skill in WRF over the Korean Peninsula and East Sea
abstract: Abstract Accurate winter predictions of coastal and offshore surface winds remain difficult along the east coast of Korea, where the Taebaek Mountains lie immediately upstream of the East Sea. This study evaluates subgrid-scale orographic drag in February 2022 WRF-ARW hindcasts with nested 20- and 4-km domains. Five experiments were compared: a no-drag control, a gravity-wave-drag plus low-level-blocking baseline, and experiments that include small-scale stable boundary layer drag, turbulent orographic form drag, or both. Against land and marine stations, the large-scale baseline drag alone provides only limited and spatially inconsistent skill at 4 km, whereas the additional lower-tropospheric drag terms reduce wind-speed errors more systematically. Over the East Sea buoys in the 4-km domain, the combined lower-tropospheric drag experiment reduced RMSE from 3.57 to 3.38 m s −1 (0.19 m s −1 or 5.3%) relative to the no-drag control. The buoy winds (3.6–4.0 m) were used without height adjustment; a neutral height adjustment lowers the gain to 0.13 m s −1 while the FD-containing experiments remain best. Component attribution indicates that turbulent orographic form drag provides the dominant incremental correction, whereas stable boundary layer drag contributes modestly and is most evident at night. Developing quality of care indicators for community-based pharmacist prescribing of ambulatory conditions and contraception in British Columbia, Canada
abstract: Abstract Background: Community-based pharmacists can prescribe for ambulatory conditions and contraception in many jurisdictions. Evidence that describes the measures of a high-quality prescribing service delivered by pharmacists is lacking. Methods: We sought to develop measures that could inform potential quality indicators to evaluate pharmacists’ prescribing in the community setting in British Columbia. This study used a qualitative methodology comprising 1:1 semi-structured interviews with patients, pharmacists, physicians/nurse practitioners, and leaders from stakeholder organizations to identify measures of a high-quality prescribing service delivered by pharmacists. Data analysis was completed using reflexive thematic analysis. A constructive workshop with a sample of participants was conducted to validate and prioritize the quality measures and determine implementation feasibility. Results: Sixty-four interviews were analyzed (16 patients, 12 pharmacists, 23 physicians/nurse practitioners, and 13 stakeholder organization leaders). Thirty-three measures were proposed, aligning with 5 major themes: patient experience, efficacy, safety, access, and cost-effectiveness. Patients emphasized the importance of privacy and the use of appropriate pronouns within the theme of patient experience, while physicians/nurse practitioners focused on clinical efficacy, suggesting that ad…

title: A modular deep learning framework with exact Shapley attribution for explainable stock market forecasting and risk-aware decision support
abstract: Abstract Explaining a fused trading decision usually requires an approximation. Agentic-Forecast is a modular architecture in which the explanation is exact: forecasting, technical, fundamental, sentiment and risk components each compute a bounded signal, a decision layer fuses these signals into a discrete call, and the small coalition lattice is enumerated in full, so that every Shapley attribution is exact for an explicitly stated cooperative game. The architecture specifies five modules, but the sentiment module produced no usable signal, so the system evaluated empirically fuses four signals. The second contribution is an integrated validation protocol for financial machine learning, comprising a purged walk-forward of the complete pipeline, dependence-aware inference, a leakage audit, a multi-seed study and an analysis of Shapley reference sensitivity. On two years of S&P 500 and DJIA data, and in an extended nested walk-forward over ten years and three indices (about 1,800 out-of-sample decisions per index), the protocol gives a largely negative predictive verdict. Across four purged folds the fused layer averages 38.70% accuracy against a 44.92% majority-class rate. abstract: Rigid (concrete) pavements built on district roads in Dar es Salaam under the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project are maintained by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA), which has no locally calibrated tool for predicting their condition. This study developed and validated a performance prediction model for rigid pavements in Ubungo District. A questionnaire survey of 86 practitioners from TARURA, the City Council, contractors and consultants rated twelve technical factors on a five-point scale, and the factors were ranked with the Relative Importance Index (RII). Eight factors met the RII ≥ 0.70 threshold: slab thickness (0.928), traffic volume (0.863), drainage condition (0.853), concrete curing quality (0.821), rainfall intensity (0.770), axle load (0.767), joint spacing and dowel bars (0.751) and subgrade compaction (0.737). Each factor was converted to a 1–5 condition score, with 5 the most favourable, and the scores were related to the Pavement Condition Index (PCI) by multiple linear regression. The model was significant (F(8, 51) = 48.96, p < 0.001; R² = 0.885, adjusted R² = 0.867, RMSE = 1.95 PCI points); all eight coefficients were positive and significant (p < 0.001), and curing quality had the largest effect (3.10 PCI points per score level). title: Clinical risk factors and prediction of acute kidney injury in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
abstract: Acute kidney injury is a frequent and clinically significant complication in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and is associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes. Early identification of high-risk patients may facilitate timely prevention and individualized management. This study aimed to investigate the clinical risk factors for acute kidney injury in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and to develop a practical prediction model. This retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction treated at our institution between January 2022 and December 2025. Acute kidney injury was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria. Demographic data, comorbidities, admission clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, imaging parameters, and treatment-related variables were collected. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of acute kidney injury. A logistic regression model was subsequently established, and its performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. A total of 265 patients were included, of whom 58 (21.9%) developed acute kidney injury during hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified age ≥65 years, diabetes mel…

title: Atom-Wise Allocation of Message-Passing Scale for Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Abstract Molecular properties depend on chemical structure at different ranges, from local polar groups governing solvation to extended substructures shaping bioactivity, yet graph neural networks usually fix one propagation scale for every atom. We present PRISM (Per-atom Routing over Intermediate States of Message Passing), in which each atom’s encoded features produce a bounded scalar that positions a unimodal distribution over retained message-passing states and matching circular-fingerprint radii. Because one coordinate translates the whole profile, allocated depth responds to the routing scalar in closed form: at fixed temperature it is nondecreasing, its sensitivity scales with the profile variance, and it saturates in the clipped regions. Beyond providing closed-form analyzability, this constrained one-parameter profile matches or significantly outperforms parameter-matched, unconstrained node-wise gates and Jumping Knowledge attention. Under scaffold partitions with equal tuning budgets against eight graph, fingerprint, and geometric baselines, PRISM trained from scratch without three-dimensional coordinates achieves the lowest mean error on aqueous solubility and hydration free energy and strong accuracy on BACE and BBBP. As a general layer-combination rule, PRISM transfers directly to GCN, GIN, and GAT backbones, reducing hydration free energy error by up to 29% rela…

A HYBRID BIAS-MITIGATION FRAMEWORK FOR FAIR CLINICAL READMISSION PREDICTION
abstract: Machine-learning models increasingly guide the allocation of clinical care, yet models optimised for aggregate accuracy can encode substantial disparities in error rates across demographic groups. This study addresses fair prediction of 30-day hospital readmission for diabetic inpatients under two constraints that are common in practice but rarely modelled together: the deployed model must not use a protected attribute at decision time, and the positive class is rare. We propose FAIR-Health, a hybrid bias-mitigation framework that couples Kamiran Calders instance reweighing (pre-processing) with a differentiable equalized-odds surrogate penalty embedded in the training objective (in-processing). The result is a single attribute-blind model with one tunable control over the fairness/accuracy trade-off. Using the UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals cohort (71,518 patients after leakage-free, patient-level deduplication), we benchmark FAIR-Health against pre-, in-, and post-processing baselines across ten random data splits (seeds) with paired significance testing. Compared to the unmitigated gradient-boosted model, FAIR-Health reduced the equalized-odds difference by 44.7% for gender and 65.6% for race, at a within-model-family AUROC cost of at most 0.004 and with no loss of calibration. abstract: Background and Objectives: There is a need to accurately determine long-term prognosis without exposing the vulnerable pediatric population to excess radiation. Their development and care plan may be impacted by traumatic brain injury (TBI) and further impeded by complications and side effects related to conventional imaging or obtaining other prognostic indicators. Biomarkers present an alternative means of determining TBI prognosis. This review seeks to compare contemporary findings regarding these biomarkers to determine which is optimal for pediatric TBI prognosis and predicting long-term outcomes. Materials and Methods: Literature pertaining to pediatric traumatic brain injury was obtained from the PubMed database within the date range of 2010-2026 on August 5th, 2026, and examined to identify validated, accurate, sensitive and specific biomarkers for long-term outcomes. Reports were excluded on the basis of their relevance to the study (i.e., articles pertaining to non-human patients or non-pediatric or non-TBI patients only, or which did not address prognosis or long-term outcomes) and accessibility (available English-language or English-translated manuscripts). Results: Ultimately, 56 qualifying reports were collected, with 14 among those identified providing sensitivity and specificity information, while the remaining 42 elucidated the roles of each biomarker.
