abstract: This study examined how demand uncertainty, consistent energy accounting, and storage selection affected the appraisal of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and solar thermal water heating for a 31-room commercial hotel in Dodoma, Tanzania. We audited an existing site-inventory workbook and dissertation, reproduced their calculations in Python, and compared alternative heating configurations using a continuous synthetic year with explicit tank losses, PV temperature effects, a storage high-limit, and power-limited auxiliary heating. The estimated volume of 2,110 L/day required 88.3 kWh/day when heated from 24 to 60°C; calendar integration of twelve supplied inlet-temperature scenarios gave 32.7 MWh/year. Interpreting the same volume as mixed water at 40°C reduced the reference requirement to 39.3 kWh/day. Correcting the irradiation–irradiance error yielded 25.7–32.4 kWh/day of potential PV energy delivered to the selected array. A battery-free configuration with 28.7 m² of collectors and approximately 1.06 m³ of thermal storage supplied 82.2% of annual useful heat from renewable sources, but retained temperature-service shortfalls under the assumed draw peaks. Against a modelled existing-solar baseline, its conditional net present value was TSh 25.5 million, compared with −TSh 32.5 million for the battery alternative. Character over competence? Ministerial expectations of Civil Service policy advisers
abstract: Abstract The ministerial perspective on individual policy capacity has been almost entirely absent from the literature, despite the centrality of the minister-official relationship to the Westminster Model. This article addresses that gap by reporting findings from a Delphi Method study involving former UK Government ministers, in which participants reached consensus on the capacities required for effective policy advising. Ministers reinforced the technical and analytical requirements identified in the existing literature but also identified four further requirements, neglected or insufficiently incorporated within that literature, all of which are dispositions: integrity, moral courage, political impartiality, and self-awareness. This suggests that competence and dispositions operate on different terms: officials’ technical and analytical shortcomings are treated by ministers as remediable, whereas deficits in disposition are treated as closer to a disqualification, which sits in tension with the dominant technocratic framing of the individual policy capacity literature. The article concludes that the Policy Profession Standards, which prescribe competency requirements for policy officials, are deficient in their dispositional content and should be revised to incorporate the ministerial perspective, for which this article provides empirical evidence.

title: Between Public Service and Animal Welfare: The Legal Protection of Working Dogs in Polish Customs and Tax Service
abstract: Working dogs employed by the Polish Customs and Tax Service perform specialized tasks in customs control and fiscal enforcement, including the detection of prohibited and undeclared goods. Their public-service role raises important questions concerning the adequacy of the legal framework governing their welfare. This study examines the legal protection of working dogs in the Polish Customs and Tax Service and assesses whether applicable regulations provide comprehensive safeguards throughout their service life. The analysis is based on a doctrinal examination of Polish legislation concerning animal protection, the organization and functioning of the Customs and Tax Service, and the status of service animals, supplemented by an assessment of relevant institutional and welfare standards. The study combines a legal-dogmatic analysis of Polish legislation and relevant animal welfare literature with empirical research based on information obtained from the Polish Customs and Tax Service under the Polish Act on Access to Public Information. The empirical data for the years 2025–February 2026, collected in 2026, are assessed against established animal welfare standards, including the Five Domains Model. The study identifies regulatory fragmentation concerning working conditions, workload, veterinary care, training, retirement, and post-service arrangements. Although Polish law establi…

title: Self-reflection journal goes digital: Fostering a reflective practice for English pre-service teachers
abstract: Reflective practice is essential in teacher education, yet preservice teachers often struggle to engage in systematic reflection and obtain supervisory feedback during teaching practicum. This study aimed to develop a web-based self-reflection journal and investigate its contribution to reflective practice among English preservice teachers. Employing a research and development approach guided by the ADDIE model, the study involved 20 English preservice teachers and four practicum supervisors. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, expert validation, reflective journal entries, and user evaluations. The journal incorporated Greenaway’s F4 framework (Facts, Feelings, Findings, and Future) and a supervisor feedback feature. The findings indicated that participants perceived the journal as useful for organizing their reflections and accessing supervisory feedback. Analysis of journal entries further revealed that structured prompts helped participants articulate classroom experiences, develop pedagogical interpretations, and formulate plans for subsequent teaching. Supervisor feedback also helped connect reflective insights with planned pedagogical actions. Overall, the findings provide preliminary evidence of the feasibility and perceived usefulness of structured digital reflection in the context of EFL teaching practicum.

Multifunctional Microdomain Regulation in Ether-Free Anion Exchange Membranes for High-Performance Fuel Cells
abstract: Abstract Anion exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs) are promising alternatives for next-generation energy conversion due to their potential for reduced cost and high efficiency. However, achieving a balance between hydroxide conductivity, dimensional stability, and alkaline durability remains a major challenge for AEMs. Herein, a multifunctional molecular engineering strategy was developed by incorporating 2-mercaptobenzoxazole (MBO) into an ether-free poly(m-terphenylpyridine) backbone, enabling simultaneous regulation of hydrophilic and hydrophobic microdomains. The multifunctional MBO unit may influence water distribution and ionic aggregation through potential hydrogen-bonding and cation–dipole interactions, respectively, thereby promoting microphase separation and the formation of continuous hydroxide transport pathways. Meanwhile, the rigid, ether-free aromatic backbone may help maintain dimensional stability while supporting hydroxide transport. As a result, the optimized QPBOPD-20 membrane exhibited a hydroxide conductivity of 178.88 mS/cm at 80 °C, a swelling ratio of 29.71%, and retained over 80% of its initial conductivity after alkaline treatment at 80 °C for 1000 h. Furthermore, the assembled AEMFC delivered a peak power density of 1.068 W/cm2 at 80 °C. title: An enhanced U-shape architecture network with cross-scale attention and frequency-domain perception for robust colorectal polyp segmentation
abstract: The early detection and removal of colorectal polyps can help reduce colorectal cancer and mortality rates. The segmentation of colorectal polyps in colonoscopy images is difficult due to multi-scale morphology, blurred boundaries, and complex background interference.To solve this problem, we propose a network of cross-scale attention and frequency domain perception of encoder-decoder architecture.The network has two new modules: first, Scale-Aware Cross Attention Skip Connection (SCAS) uses multi-head attention mechanism and multi-scale pyramid fusion to fuse multi-scale features from encoder and decoder to enhance the model to capture polyp features of different sizes.Secondly, Dual-domain fusion (D2F) separates and assigns weights of low-frequency global information and high-frequency detail information of the feature map at bottleneck stage, improving the model to analyze spatial and frequency domains and improve polyp boundaries.Multiple public colorectal polyp segmentation datasets show that our method is competitive and performs better than existing mainstream approaches in terms of mIoU and mDice: On the CVC-ClinicDB dataset our model produces mDice of 0.922 and mIoU of 0.863, outperforming UNet, UNet++, PraNet, ACSNet, DCSAU-Net, HarDNet-CPS, ProMamba, FoBS. These results validate its strong segmentation capability and effectiveness in accurately delineating polyp regi…

title: Hydrogel-Mediated Cancer Immunotherapy: Material Design, Immune Regulation and Translation
abstract: Durable responses to cancer immunotherapy remain difficult to achieve in many solid tumors, where rapid clearance and inadequate intratumoral exposure combine with immunosuppression and systemic toxicity to limit treatment benefit. Local hydrogel delivery offers a way to concentrate immunomodulatory signals at the lesion, although its performance varies with the formulation, payload, and tumor setting. Drawing on melanoma, breast cancer, and other solid-tumor models, this review relates hydrogel design to payload-mediated immune regulation, combination therapy, and preclinical translation. Injectable and in situ-forming systems have prolonged local exposure to immunogenic cell death inducers, adjuvants, cytokines, and checkpoint inhibitors, while also supporting adoptive cell delivery. Some multicomponent formulations release their payloads at different times, but the contribution of this sequence to efficacy remains unresolved. Selected syngeneic studies report improved local control and reduced recurrence or metastasis, with abscopal responses or rechallenge protection in some cases. Across these studies, retention and release kinetics, considered together with the payload, appear more informative than material class alone. Because most reports evaluate individual immune endpoints, coordinated regulation across the cancer–immunity cycle has yet to be demonstrated. Durable cli…

title: Plastid competence, pigment fate, and tissue-specific regulation of cucurbit fruit coloration
abstract: Abstract Cucurbit fruit coloration offers a comparative framework for examining how plastid state, pigment metabolism, and tissue identity are coordinated during fruit development. Previous syntheses have generally been structured around individual species, visible traits, or pigment classes, which limits direct comparison of homologous mechanisms across Cucurbitaceae. Here, we synthesize genetic, genomic, multi-omics, cellular, and functional evidence from melon (Cucumis melo), watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), cucumber (Cucumis sativus), and other cucurbit crops within a framework centered on plastid competence and pigment fate. Plastid competence, the capacity of a tissue to establish, maintain, or remodel chloroplast- and chromoplast-rich states, directly constrains chlorophyll- and carotenoid-associated coloration. ARABIDOPSIS PSEUDO-RESPONSE REGULATOR 2 (APRR2)-like genes represent the most consistently conserved entry point for chloroplast-rich pigment accumulation. Conversely, flavonoid-associated pigmentation is considered separately as a limited, non-plastid-centered route in cucumber peel and melon rind tissues. Flesh color has diversified through lineage-dependent combinations of chromoplast differentiation, pathway flux, branch allocation, isomerization, sequestration, and turnover. The ORANGE (OR)-centered mechanism is particularly prominent in melon, whereas waterm…

title: Bioactive Janus Scaffold Dressing with In Situ Self-Pumping Fluid Regulation for Chronic Wound Regeneration
abstract: Abstract Both diabetic wounds and nasal wounds generate abundant wound exudate. The inflammatory mediators contained in exudate can trigger persistent local inflammation, interfere with the tissue repair process, and cause severe damage to patients. However, the traditional single-layer dressings have insufficient liquid absorption capacity, which can lead to the accumulation of exudate at the wound site and delay the healing process. Herein, we have developed a type of self-pumping wound dressing by using electrospinning technology to load PAN/Zein/Cs fiber membranes onto the surface of natural nonwoven fabric. Self-pump dressings can effectively absorb wound exudate and maintain an environment conducive to wound healing. The self-pump dressing has excellent anti-inflammatory properties. Due to the combined effect of corn protein and Cirsium setosum extract, it can significantly reduce the expression levels of pro-inflammatory factors (IL-6, TNF-α) and increase the expression levels of anti-inflammatory factors (IL-10, TGF-β). Furthermore, the self-pumping dressing can promote early angiogenesis, facilitate the adhesion and proliferation of skin cells, and accelerate wound re-epithelialization and tissue repair by upregulating the expression of VEGF and CD31. In summary, the self-pump dressing has excellent fluid regulation capabilities, providing a approach for the treatment …

Integrating Meta-Analysis and Root Ion Flux Profiling Reveals That Exogenous Hydrogen Sulfide Alleviates Salt Stress in Foxtail Millet via Coordinated Regulation of Redox and Ion Homeostasis
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an important gaseous signal in plant salinity responses, yet its effects on root ion exchange and the physiological basis of salt tolerance remain incompletely understood. A multilevel meta-analysis combined with physiological experiments and real-time ion flux measurements in foxtail millet (Setaria italica L.) showed that exogenous H2S consistently decreased malondialdehyde content and Na+/K+ ratio under salt stress and generally increased total chlorophyll, whereas superoxide dismutase activity changes were context-dependent. In millet seedlings, pretreatment with 200 μM NaHS (24 h) before 100 mM NaCl (7 d) alleviated root growth inhibition, reduced O2− and H2O2 accumulation, decreased malondialdehyde and electrolyte leakage, and coordinated superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase activities. NaHS also partially restored root activity and reduced the salt-induced accumulation of soluble sugars and proline. Non-invasive micro-test technology revealed marked changes in net Na+, K+, and H+ fluxes at the root surface, indicating that NaHS pretreatment is associated with altered instantaneous ion transport under salinity. Conclusions: These results associate NaHS-mediated salt-stress alleviation with reduced oxidative injury, altered antioxidant responses, and changes in root ion exchange, supporting a physiological framework for further investiga…

title: Hepatic Superoxide Dismutase Activity and Total Antioxidant Capacity in Oreochromis mossambicus Fed Green-synthesized Copper Oxide Nanoparticles
abstract: Oxidative balance is an important component of fish physiology, and hepatic antioxidant biomarkers can help describe responses to dietary nanomaterials. This study describes the superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC) profiles presented for Oreochromis mossambicus reportedly fed diets containing copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) synthesised using Mesosphaerum suaveolens. The manuscript reports five dietary treatments containing 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 mg CuO NPs/kg diet, with measurements displayed at days 14, 28, 42 and 56. The described allocation involved 300 fish distributed among five treatments, with three replicate tanks and 20 fish per tank. Visual examination of the supplied figures indicates differences in plotted hepatic SOD and T-AOC responses among treatments and sampling days. Both figures show the highest visible bars in the 4 mg/kg group, with the greatest plotted response at day 42 and lower plotted values at day 56. These results describe graphical patterns only and are not substitutes for original measured values. Replicate-level data, detailed assay records, verified units and complete statistical outputs were unavailable for independent confirmation. Consequently, the available evidence does not support conclusions about statistical significance, protection against oxidative damage, fish health, safety or an optimal dietary in…

title: Multifunctional Hybrid Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) Silane Coatings: Coupling Corrosion Barrier Performance with Water Vapor Adsorption Capacity
abstract: This work investigates the development of dual-functional hybrid coatings on aluminum 6061 substrates, designed to simultaneously provide corrosion protection and water vapor adsorption for advanced thermal energy management applications, such as sorption-based cooling systems. The coatings were synthesized using a sol–gel technique by embedding hydrophilic MIL-100(Fe) metal–organic framework (MOF) crystals into a protective hydrophobic silane matrix at varying filler loadings (25 to 40 wt.%). Morphological characterization confirmed uniform crystal distribution, while pull-off tests validated suitable coating–substrate adhesion and matrix cohesion. Water vapor adsorption measurements confirmed that the embedded MOF pores remain fully accessible, preserving the thermodynamic moisture-exchange capacity essential for green climate control technologies. The stability of the barrier capabilities in the composite coating was monitored for up to 72 h in a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Results revealed that intermediate loading configurations (S-M30, S-M35) maintain high electrochemical stability, preserving a protective low-frequency impedance modulus three orders of magnitude greater than bare aluminum. This multifunctional framework provides a potentially suitable corrosion-resistant interface tailored for next-generation sustainable hea…

title: Growing Cargo Volumes, Operational Efficiency and Port Capacity: A Comparative Analysis of Brazil's Waterway Sector (2024–2025)
abstract: This study examines changes in cargo handling and operational performance in Brazil's waterway sector between 2024 and 2025, focusing on cargo profiles, vessel activity, operational productivity and port infrastructure requirements. A quantitative-descriptive approach supported by qualitative interpretation was adopted, using secondary data from the annual waterway performance reports published by the Brazilian National Waterway Transportation Agency (ANTAQ). The analysis compared cargo volumes and growth rates across the main cargo categories and examined available indicators of vessel activity and container handling. The findings show that total cargo handling increased by 6.1% in 2025, although growth varied across cargo segments. Containerized cargo recorded the highest growth among the main categories (7.2%), while general cargo showed a more modest increase (0.8%). The results also indicate that increased cargo volumes do not necessarily correspond to higher operational productivity, as greater cargo handling per vessel may coexist with longer operating times and lower hourly productivity. The study contributes to logistics and operations management by connecting sector-level cargo expansion with operational and infrastructure challenges. Its practical implications include the need for more comprehensive performance monitoring, differentiated operational planning and coor…

title: Measuring Photosynthetic Rates and Capacity in Maize Using Gas Exchange Systems
abstract: Photosynthesis drives plant carbon uptake and is a key determinant of yield potential in crops such as maize. Quantifying photosynthetic capacity in maize—a C4 plant—can help identify environmental conditions that limit productivity and select genotypes that are more productive in different environments. Infrared gas exchange systems are portable and enable nondestructive estimates of stomatal conductance and photosynthetic CO 2 assimilation rates, and have long been the gold standard for measuring leaf-level CO 2 assimilation. While there are many protocols available for gas exchange measurements, these are typically specific to C3 species and/or require specialized technical training. Here, we provide a protocol for obtaining meaningful and accurate photosynthetic CO 2 and H 2 O fluxes from maize leaves using commercial gas exchange systems. We describe two different steady-state measurement approaches, namely, survey measurements and net CO 2 assimilation ( A ) measured at a range of intercellular CO 2 concentrations ( C i ), that is, A / C i curves. Survey measurements of leaf gas exchange provide an instantaneous measurement of net CO 2 assimilation in an environment that closely matches the natural environment the leaf is exposed to, along with estimates of stomatal conductance ( g s ) and intercellular CO 2 concentrations. These measurements can be used to study diurnal …

title: Kink instability as a particle acceleration mechanism in X-ray binaries and the connection to the outburst cycle
abstract: Abstract We consider whether the kink instability can explain particle acceleration in hard state ‘compact’ X-ray binary jets. We apply a 1D model to assess the expected growth rate of the instability for a variety of jet models, then scale results from simulations to estimate a dissipation rate for the magnetic energy in the jet. We then consider the effects of radiative cooling on the system. We find that hard state ‘compact’ X-ray binary jets are likely to be unstable to the kink instability within their acceleration zones across a plausible parameter space. We further find that depending on the parameters of the model, the jets may radiate over a variety of length scales ranging from length scales attributable to a ‘failed’ jet scenario, to those in keeping with resolved radio observations of ‘compact’ jets. We discuss the expected evolution of this model through the outburst cycle.

Dual evaluation mechanism of artificial intelligence enabled fintech discontinuance for sustainable financial inclusion in India
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now underpins FinTech services that support digital financial inclusion and sustainable economic growth, yet AI-enabled fraud threatens users' trust in this innovation. Some users intend to discontinue AI-enabled FinTech services even when they are satisfied and habituated, a pattern that traditional continuance explanations do not explain. This study examines a Dual Evaluation Mechanism in which discontinuance intention forms through an internal path (confirmation, satisfaction, and habit) and an external path (vicarious exposure to AI fraud and perceived AI fraud risk), and tests whether perceived AI fraud risk moderates the relationship between habit and discontinuance intention. The study employs cross-sectional survey data from 507 Indian users of AI-enabled FinTech services, analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling and complemented by predictive, importance-performance, endogeneity, and necessary condition analyses. The results show that confirmation raises satisfaction (β = 0.648), satisfaction raises habit (β = 0.578), and habit lowers discontinuance intention (β = −0.330). Vicarious AI fraud exposure raises perceived AI fraud risk (β = 0.588), which raises discontinuance intention (β = 0.507), and the interaction between risk and habit is positive (β = 0.174); all paths are significant at p < 0.001. The model explain…

title: Data Visualization Literacy as an analytical capacity in the public sector: Latent structure and response processes under time constraints
abstract: The digital transformation of the public sector has made data visualizations a key interface between analytics and decision-making. Measurement of data visualization literacy (DVL) in public administrations remains limited, and timed performance is treated as a direct proxy for competence. Such scores, however, combine two different things: whether an answer is produced in time and whether it is correct. This study addresses both gaps by examining Mini-VLAT structure and timed-score interpretation in 1,306 public employees. DVL was measured with the Mini-VLAT, a twelve-item graphical interpretation test administered under its standard 25-second-per-item limit. The analysis combines confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), testing whether the twelve items measure a single ability, with a two-part model separating response emission from accuracy and testing individual, organizational, and item correlates. Results support an essentially unidimensional DVL structure. However, response participation and interpretive accuracy show distinct correlates across the workforce: age is negatively associated with both, education mainly with accuracy, and administrative rank with both. Stacked compositional items are associated with lower performance at both stages, consistent with higher processing demands. Timed performance should not be read as a direct measure of competence. These distinctions…

title: Pathways to Practice: Evaluating Blue Carbon Capacity Development in Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Blue carbon (BC) ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their roles in climate action, biodiversity conservation and community livelihoods. As interest in their protection and restoration grows, so does the need for capacity development that can support effective project design, implementation and sustained action. However, evidence of whether training translates into sustained practice and long‐term outcomes remains limited. This exploratory study examined 18 BC capacity development programmes in Africa, assessing programme design, alumni‐reported learning and application and conditions influencing progression from training to practice. Structured questionnaires were administered to training providers and alumni of programmes delivered between 2015 and 2025. Results indicate that training was primarily delivered by NGOs (50%) and universities (22%), with activity concentrated in East Africa. Programmes were predominantly face‐to‐face, field‐based and free of charge (69%), emphasising mangrove ecology (48%), restoration (24.4%) and community engagement (17.8%). Participating alumni reported high satisfaction, perceived knowledge gains, increased confidence and professional benefits. However, specialised competencies, including carbon accounting and finance, remote sensing and policy integration, received less attention (< 10%). Post‐training support and long‐term e…

title: METHODOLOGICAL TOOLKIT FOR EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF IMBALANCES IN UKRAINE’S FOREIGN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY AS A COMPONENT OF THE EFFICIENCY MONITORING MECHANISM
abstract: The article substantiates a methodological toolkit for the early diagnosis of imbalances in Ukraine’s foreign economic activity as a component of the mechanism for monitoring its efficiency. The study is based on the need to move beyond retrospective assessment of already established changes and toward the timely identification of structural deviations that may subsequently adversely affect the performance of foreign economic activity. A system of diagnostic indicators is proposed, covering the balance of foreign trade flows, the agri-food orientation of exports, the machinery and transport component of exports, the structural relationship between the respective components of exports and imports, and the geographical orientation of merchandise exports toward the EU market. The proposed approach is tested using Ukraine’s foreign trade data for 2022–2024. The results show that the most persistent adverse signals were concentrated in the commodity and functional structure of foreign trade: the export-to-import coverage ratio remained substantially below its 2022 level, the share of agri-food products in exports increased, while the coefficient reflecting the ratio of the machinery and transport component in exports to that in imports declined from 0.330 to 0.234. title: Low-dose carbon monoxide in cardiovascular surgery: mechanisms, monitoring, and therapeutic potential
abstract: Carbon monoxide has been regarded as a toxic gas for a long time, however, recent studies have demonstrated that carbon monoxide, as an endogenous gaseous signaling molecule generated via the heme oxygenase system, plays an important regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes. Physiologically, endogenous carbon monoxide production is approximately 400–500 μmol per day, whereas freely diffusible carbon monoxide remains very low, at about 0.002 μM, or approximately 2.5 ppm as an equivalent gas-phase concentration. At low concentrations, carbon monoxide exerts diverse biological effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, vasoregulatory, mitochondrial-modulating, and anti-remodeling actions. These properties are particularly relevant to cardiovascular surgery, especially procedures involving cardiopulmonary bypass, where systemic inflammation, ischemia–reperfusion injury, hemolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory disturbance contribute substantially to perioperative morbidity. During cardiopulmonary bypass, endogenous carbon monoxide production may increase and can be indirectly assessed by carboxyhemoglobin and exhaled carbon monoxide, suggesting a potential role for carbon monoxide-related measurements as dynamic biomarkers of hemolysis, inflammation, and surgical stress. abstract: This article analyzes the relevance of integration between the State and civil society through strategic planning applied to public security, focusing on the citizen security paradigm. Historically translated by a purely reactive model, contemporary public security demands a systemic, preventive, and participatory approach. The objective of this study is to examine how strategic coordination between state security forces and social actors enhances crime prevention and strengthens democratic governance. Using a bibliographic and documentary review methodology, the paper discusses the transition from national security to citizen security, highlighting the role of strategic planning in optimizing resources and building sustainable public policies. The results indicate that social co-responsibility, combined with accurate situational diagnoses and results-based management, reduces crime rates and rebuilds social capital in communities. It is concluded that the effectiveness of crime prevention lies in overcoming institutional isolation, consolidating collaborative intelligence and community action networks.

title: Genome-wide identification and osmotic-stress-responsive expression of the SRS gene family in mango (Mangifera indica L.)
abstract: Abstract SHI-related sequence (SRS) proteins constitute a family of plant-specific zinc-finger regulators involved in plant development and responses to environmental stresses. However, the SRS gene family remains largely unexplored in mango ( Mangifera indica L.). In this study, we identified 10 MiSRS genes in the mango genome and systematically characterized their chromosomal distribution, conserved domains, gene structures, phylogenetic relationships, and promoter cis -regulatory elements. Expression profiling of the mango cultivar ‘Dashehari’ under polyethylene glycol (PEG-6000)-induced osmotic stress (5%, 15%, and 25% w/v) revealed distinct, concentration-dependent transcriptional responses among MiSRS family members. Physiological analyses further demonstrated stress-associated changes in chlorophyll status, malondialdehyde accumulation, antioxidant enzyme activities, and proline content. Transient expression assays in Nicotiana benthamiana revealed contrasting subcellular localization patterns, with MiSRS9–GFP predominantly accumulating in the nucleus and MiSRS10–GFP primarily localized to the cytoplasm. Complementary analyses of Arabidopsis thaliana SRS-homolog mutant lines provided indirect evidence supporting potential roles of SRS proteins in osmotic-stress responses. title: First Report of Fusarium falciforme Causing Postharvest Fruit Rot of Hami Melon ( Cucumis melo var. saccharinus ) in China
abstract: Hami melon ( Cucumis melo var. saccharinus ) is an economically important fruit crop in Xinjiang, China (Zhu et al., 2021). In June 2024, approximately 25% (278 of 1,110 fruits) of Hami melon (cv. Xizhoumi 25) developed postharvest fruit rot after 20 days of storage at 20°C at the Research and Development Center for Facility and Specialty Agriculture of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Shanshan, Turpan, Xinjiang, China (42°52′48″N, 90°13′12″E). Symptoms began as sunken, yellowish-brown circular lesions, followed by fruit rot with white to yellow fungal growth. Tissue segments (5 × 5 mm) from lesion margins of four separate symptomatic fruits were surface-disinfested (75% ethanol, 60 s; 1% NaClO, 3 min), rinsed three times with sterile water, dried, and plated on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 25°C for 3 d. Emerging hyphae were transferred to fresh PDA. Four isolates (XJ-NJ1 to XJ-NJ4) with identical morphology were obtained and identified as Fusarium sp.. Colonies were circular, flat, and white, with creamy to yellowish pigmentation, reaching 7.00 ± 0.50 cm in diameter after 7 d at 25°C. Macroconidia were sickle-shaped, straight to slightly curved, 3- to 5-septate, with papillate apical cells and barely notched basal cells, measuring 18.15 to 44.60 × 3.10 to 6.34 μm (mean = 31.38 × 4.72 μm, n = 100). title: Maize-based cropping systems in India: dynamics, drivers, and pathways towards climate-resilient sustainable intensification
abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) is emerging as one of the most significant cereals in India because of its growing importance in food, feed, fodder and industry. Maize-based cropping systems are evolving toward sustainable intensification at an increasing rate, driven largely by climate variability, resource limitations, technological advances, and shifts in market demand. In this review, the status, dynamics, and future prospects of maize cropping systems in India are summarized through a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 framework. The studies were selected for qualitative synthesis to include a total of 84 studies. This review examines the evolution of significant maize-based farming systems across various agro climatic regions of India, their impact on productivity, resource utilization efficiency, soil health and agricultural profitability. It also highlights the key drivers of cropping system change, including climate variability, soil and water constraints, improved hybrids, mechanization, policy support, and market demand. Recent developments in conservation agriculture, integrated nutrient management, precision agriculture, and climate smart agriculture are discussed for their potential to enhance resilience and sustainability. Residual Herbicides at Soybean Sowing Compensate for Reduced Mulch Cover under Contrasting Grazing Intensities in an Integrated Crop–livestock System
abstract: Abstract In integrated crop–livestock systems, winter cover crops are often grazed to diversify farm income, but grazing reduces the surface residue that contributes to weed suppression, and high grazing intensities intensify this effect by reducing both the physical barrier and the allelopathic potential of cover crop residues. A two-year field study evaluated whether residual herbicides applied at soybean sowing can compensate for reduced residue-mediated weed suppression, and under which conditions. A mixture of black oat and Italian ryegrass was grazed at two intensities, defined by target post-grazing sward heights of 10 cm (high) and 25 cm (moderate). At soybean sowing, three residual herbicide treatments were applied: clomazone (720 g a.i. ha⁻¹), diclosulam (33.6 g a.i. ha⁻¹) and a premix of pyroxasulfone (120 g a.i. ha⁻¹) plus flumioxazin (80 g a.i. ha⁻¹), alongside an untreated control. Weed density was assessed at the V4 and R8 stages, weed biomass at R8, and grain yield at harvest. All herbicide treatments reduced weed density and biomass relative to the untreated control, although efficacy varied between seasons: the Herbicide × Year interaction was significant for weed density ( p < 0.001) and for weed biomass ( p = 0.021), and clomazone did not differ from the untreated control at V4 under high grazing intensity in 2022/23 (IRR = 0.74; 95% CI 0.40–1.38). Beyond cost: a critical review of battery trade-offs for just energy transitions in developing and emerging economies
abstract: Stationary battery selection in developing and emerging economies involves trade-offs between access to capital, reliable service, lifecycle burdens, and local governance. This review examines how these dimensions affect technology choice. This structured critical review integrates selected technical, lifecycle, and energy-justice literature. Evidence is distinguished by application, geographical transferability, and commercial maturity. The literature is synthesized qualitatively; an illustrative multicriteria template specifies possible weighting scenarios without calculating technology scores or rankings. Lead–acid and lithium-ion batteries have established applications, but their relative whole-life costs depend on operating conditions, usable capacity, replacement, and financing. Evidence on lithium iron phosphate supports its consideration for stationary services without establishing universal superiority. Sodium-ion and iron-based flow batteries offer diversification opportunities with greater uncertainty in long-term field performance. Environmental comparisons depend on lifecycle boundaries and local end-of-life practices. Priorities should be defined for a specified service and jurisdiction with affected users, operators, and authorities. title: Production of primordial black holes in the double D3-brane-anti-D3-brane inflation model
abstract: A bstract A natural extension of the successful $$ D3\text-\overline{D}3 $$ D 3 - D ¯ 3 -brane inflation model in string theory is one with two $$ D3\text-\overline{D}3 $$ D 3 - D ¯ 3 -brane pairs, giving rise to a novel feature in string-theory. When the first pair annihilates, D 1-strings and F 1-strings are produced. Following the non-commutative geometric properties in string theory, it is shown by Myers [1–3] that the presence of the D 3-charge field strength of the remaining $$ D3\text-\overline{D}3 $$ D 3 - D ¯ 3 -brane pair leads to the formation of dielectric 3-branes — neutral, finite-size bound states of 3-branes with D 1-strings. They behave as matter with little or no pressure. Spanning a wide range of masses, they seed primordial black holes in the early universe.

title: The Pulsar Wind Nebula Origin of the High-energy Gamma-ray Sources HESS J1857+026 and HESS J1837–069
abstract: Abstract With a time-dependent one-zone leptonic model, we investigate the radiation mechanisms and physical properties of the Galactic very-high-energy (VHE) γ -ray sources HESS J1857+026 and HESS J1837−069. We carry out unified modeling of multiwavelength observations spanning radio, X-ray, and GeV–TeV γ -ray bands. With appropriate parameters, the broadband emission of HESS J1857+026 is well reproduced within a pulsar wind nebula (PWN) dominated leptonic framework, without requiring an additional hadronic component. For HESS J1837−069, the model can broadly account for the overall GeV–TeV spectral trend, although noticeable deviations remain when all published γ -ray detections are included. These results place representative constraints on the radiative properties of PWNe with characteristic ages of roughly 20 kyr and provide useful reference cases for future studies of PWN evolution and high-energy particle acceleration processes.

title: Decisions in Photovoltaic Power Supply Chains Considering Energy Storage Modes and Subsidies
abstract: The intermittency and volatility of photovoltaic (PV) power generation are key challenges that constrain renewable energy consumption and undermine the efficiency and economic performance of power system operations. To alleviate PV curtailment and the supply–demand imbalance, this paper introduces two energy storage modes—self-built energy storage and energy storage leasing—and incorporates government subsidy policies for energy storage. It aims to determine the optimal time-of-use pricing and energy storage capacity decisions in a PV power supply chain, to compare the self-built and leasing modes, and to examine how government subsidies affect these modes. A multi-agent game model comprising power generators, electricity retailers, energy storage operators, and power users is developed to analyze the coordinated decision-making of retail prices during PV-available and PV-unavailable periods and energy storage capacity. Specifically, it addresses three questions: (1) How are time-of-use pricing and energy storage capacity jointly determined under the self-built and leasing modes? (2) How do power generators choose between the two modes? (3) How do government energy storage subsidies differentially affect different modes? title: Edge-AI Firmware for Machine Anomaly Detection Using EWMS and Spectral Energy Shift
abstract: FFT amplitude thresholds raise false alarms when machine load changes, and storing a full spectral history exceeds microcontroller memory. This paper presents edge-AI firmware that runs the whole decision, from spectrum to alarm, on a microcontroller-class node without a network. Three modules process each vibration frame. An exponential weighted moving spectrum stores a normal fingerprint in one vector. Spectral energy distribution shift scores the frame by the Kullback–Leibler divergence of the normalized spectrum against that fingerprint, so a global gain change cancels out. The alarm threshold is updated only from frames that did not alarm. Tests used 400 synthetic frames of normal running, bearing fault, imbalance, and load drift, against an FFT-peak rule and a total-energy z-score. The 16-bit fingerprint used 512 bytes, 400 times smaller than a 200-frame floating-point buffer. Bearing-fault scores averaged 1,651 times the normal score, while a 30 percent load rise stayed at or below normal. On a 350-frame timeline the proposed threshold kept a 100 percent true-positive rate through the fault, against 4 percent for a conventional adaptive threshold. The mixed-set area under the ROC curve was 1.000 and the F1 score was 0.976, with no missed faults. Proton Dynamic Confluence Effect Enables Self‐Synchronized *H Source‐Storage‐Sink for Electrocatalytic Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia from Fertilizer Wastewater
abstract: ABSTRACT Fertilizer‐plant rinse wastewater is high‐concentration, low‐flow, sparsely distributed point‐source nitrate pollution, with nitrate‐nitrogen reaching thousands of ppm. Renewable‐energy‐driven electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR) can convert nitrate into ammonia, but limited by flux imbalance between generation and consumption of active hydrogen (*H). Conventional catalysts cannot match *H supply and demand, causing hydrogen evolution or intermediate accumulation. We propose a Proton Dynamic Confluence Effect (PDCE) and design Co 2 P/Cu/LaPO 4 ternary heterojunction. Co 2 P supplies *H via water dissociation; surface PO 4 3 − on LaPO 4 acts as a dynamic proton buffer through reversible protonation (PO 4 3 − ⇌ HPO 4 2 − ); Cu is the consumption sink, activating nitrate and facilitating hydrogenation. This creates self‐synchronized source–storage–sink *H flux. In alkaline media, it achieves a maximum ammonia yield rate of 135.04 mg h − 1 cm − 2 and 94.9% Faradaic efficiency at −0.8 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy captures reversible PO 4 3 − protonation and fast‐in–fast‐out intermediate kinetics; kinetic isotope and quenching experiments confirm a low‐free‐energy‐change PCET process. In real fertilizer‐plant wastewater (initial NO 3 − ‐N 3221 ppm) over 120 h operation, it achieves 99.85% nitrate removal, 35.15 g ammonia, and >90% Faradaic efficiency. PDCE shifts c…

title: Measurement Protocol Dependence in Early-Life Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Estimation: A Controlled Study Using NASA PCoE Cells
abstract: Battery management systems must estimate state of health (SOH) early in a cell’s life. This study examines how much of the reported estimation accuracy depends on the measurement protocol rather than the estimator. A physics-based fade curve, Random Forest, XGBoost version 3.3.0, a physics-assisted hybrid and a gated recurrent unit are compared using leave-one-cell-out validation on four NASA PCoE cells over early-life windows of 20–100 cycles. Training and evaluation observations are both drawn from cycles 1 to W; therefore, the primary task is cross-cell SOH estimation within an observed window, not future-cycle forecasting. A separate temporal evaluation yields higher forecasting RMSE, by factors of 1.9–4.3 relative to in-window estimation. At 50 cycles, XGBoost achieves a pooled RMSE of 0.024 SOH units, compared with 0.044 for the fade curve. Removing the recorded discharge duration feature increases RMSE by 34%. In a separate diagnostic comparison, a single time-under-load feature achieves lower RMSE than the full nine-feature set. Neither the fade curve estimate nor cycle index improves XGBoost when added as a feature. On common SOH support, the increase in R2 with window length is attributable to the widening test target distribution. A comparative analysis of four variable-current cells provides complementary evidence.

abstract: This article examines the design and validation of a leadership-mediated internal communication strategy aimed at strengthening the organizational culture of Outsourcing S.A.S. BIC. The study adopted a qualitative approach, incorporating descriptive elements and an exploratory and propositional scope. The diagnostic phase included document analysis, the Organizational Culture Assessment Instrument (OCAI), audience surveys, and focus groups. Two iterative prototyping cycles followed in Outsourcing S.A.S. BIC’s UARIV telephone account: a problem prototype validated with seven middle managers and a solution prototype implemented with 78 employees working remotely fromdifferent locations across Colombia. At the interim assessment, conducted six weeks after the strategy was launched, improvements in shift adherence (from 60.05% to 96.09%) and productivity (from 53.08% to 93.16%) coincided with the prototype activation period, although the research design does not establish a causal relationship. Findings highlight the relevance of leadership- driven cultural mediation supported by narratives, rituals, microformats, and continuous listening. Artificial intelligence proved useful as an analytical and support tool without replacing human interaction.

title: Application Of Computed Tomography-Based Three-Dimensional Reconstruction Compensation Strategy for Femoral Rotational Morphology in Precise Alignment of Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Simulation Study
abstract: Objectives: To investigate, through computer simulation, whether the intraoperative femoral morphology in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) can be predicted from the initial pre-resection plane, and to calculate the theoretical compensation angle required for the secondary resection to align the osteotomy plane with the surgical transepicondylar axis (sTEA). Material and Methods: Preoperative CT data from 130 patients with varus knee osteoarthritis were utilized for three-dimensional reconstruction and osteotomy simulation. The final osteotomy plane was defined on the sagittal view as the most distal position where the anterior femoral cortex remains intact (no notching). On the axial view, this final plane was externally rotated 4° relative to the posterior condylar axis (PCA), based on the mean posterior condylar angle of 4° ± 1.4° reported in a large CT-based anthropometric study of 2,637 knees and translated 2 mm anteriorly to define the precutting plane. All initial osteotomies were performed on this pre-resection plane. According to the proposed criteria, the morphology was classified into three groups based on the ratio of medial to lateral vertical diameters (M/L) of the pre-resection plane: Piano sign group (M/L: 0.62–0.67, n= 45), Boot sign group (M/L < 0.62, n= 50), and Butterfly sign group (M/L > 0.67, n= 35). title: Strain‐Inversion Strategy Enables MOCVD Growth of 53 µm Ultra‐Thick, Stress‐Free, Buffer‐Free III‐Nitride Heteroepitaxial Films
abstract: ABSTRACT As the semiconductor industry increasingly pivots toward “More than Moore” and “More Moore” paradigms, heterogeneous integration has emerged as a pivotal strategy for achieving system‐level performance breakthroughs. However, residual stress inherent to the integration of dissimilar materials represents a critical bottleneck, directly threatening the integrity and reliability of these advanced systems. Heteroepitaxy, as a representative example, is inherently constrained by stress accumulation, which limits epilayer thickness, increases threading dislocation density (TDD), and degrades device reliability. Here, we present a strain‐inversion strategy that effectively transfers misfit‐induced stress from the epilayer into the substrate stack. Through co‐designed theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we introduce 4H‐SiC/SiO 2 /polycrystalline‐ceramic‐AlN integrated substrates, and demonstrate metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) growth of 53‐µm‐thick, stress‐free heteroepitaxial GaN films. The films exhibit outstanding structural quality, with full‐width‐at‐half‐maximum (FWHM) values of x‐ray rocking curve of 83 and 119 arcsec for the (002) and (102) planes, respectively, and a TDD of 5 × 10 7 cm −2 . These results not only set a new thickness record for MOCVD‐grown heteroepitaxial GaN but also achieve crystal quality comparable to state‐of‐the‐art b…

title: Influence, bargaining, and moral hazard in US alliances in Asia
abstract: Abstract Since the 1950s, the United States has sought to utilize its alliance network in Asia to pursue two overarching yet occasionally conflicting goals: enable the United States to impede its adversaries through both military deterrence and economic containment; and exert influence over the allies themselves, restraining them from military adventurism and seeking a variety of policy concessions. While these two purposes have remained broadly consistent fixtures of US alliances, Washington’s prioritization of specific goals—and its ability to pursue them—have changed. This short essay traces these changes. In recent years, the rise of China and the United States’ turn against free trade, and, more recently, aspects of the liberal international order have led Washington to encourage its allies to simultaneously constrain and counter Chinese influence, while also assenting to US protectionism. These developments have shaped the United States’ goals in its relationships with Asian allies, as well as the barriers it faces to pursuing its goals, with particular emphasis on moral hazard problems.

title: Strategic Leadership and the Adaptation of Indonesia's National Defense Strategy in Addressing Multidimensional Security Threats
abstract: This article examines the role of strategic leadership in adapting Indonesia's national defense strategy to multidimensional security threats. Using a qualitative conceptual design and narrative literature review, it synthesizes scholarship on strategic leadership, dynamic capabilities, civil-military relations, hybrid threats, cyber deterrence, collaborative governance, and social resilience. The study develops a model of non-military deterrence in which adaptive strategic leadership functions as the driver, social resilience and legitimacy as the foundation, and multidimensional policy integration as the enabler. Together, these components strengthen decision-making, public trust, cross-sector coordination, policy learning, and systemic resilience. The findings indicate that Indonesia should enhance interoperable coordination, real-time decision support, crisis exercises, digital literacy, strategic communication, and continuous evaluation.

title: The Ross procedure: Technical principles, operative strategy, and pitfalls for long-term success
abstract: The Ross procedure remains an attractive aortic valve replacement strategy for children, adolescents, and selected young adults. Pulmonary autograft replacement provides excellent hemodynamics, freedom from anticoagulation, growth potential in children, and favorable long-term survival in appropriately selected patients. These advantages, however, come at the cost of substantial technical complexity. Small imperfections during autograft harvest, implantation, coronary transfer, or root reconstruction can result in early dysfunction, coronary complications, or late autograft dilatation and failure. The purpose of this review is to summarize a practical and reproducible approach to the Ross procedure with emphasis on operative strategy, technical details, Ross–Konno modifications, autograft stabilization techniques, and avoidance of common pitfalls. Rather than advocating a single technique, we emphasize fundamental principles that permit adaptation to patient anatomy while maintaining the geometric integrity of the left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, and pulmonary root.

title: Viscosity-Engineered Coaxial Electrospinning of BaTiO3 Nanotubes for High-Power Piezoelectric Nanosensors
abstract: Abstract We successfully fabricated barium titanate nanotubes (BaTiO3 NTs) via a viscosity-engineered coaxial electrospinning process. Using a constant sol–gel precursor shell solution (11.3 wt % PVP) and varying the PVP concentration in the ethanol core fluid (15.9, 20.2, and 24.1 wt %), we maintained stable composite jetting across a broad rheological window. Notably, we successfully fabricated stable nanotubes when the shell solution viscosity was lower than that of the core liquid, stabilizing compound jetting and eliminating structural defects. Morphological characterization revealed that the uniform, defect-free BaTiO3 nanotubes depend heavily on core-to-shell rheological properties (core viscosity 4.27 Pa·s and shell viscosity 0.55 Pa·s, at a shear rate of 1.85 s–1). To evaluate device-level performance, we fabricated a piezoelectric nanosensor by aligning the arrays perpendicular to the interdigital electrode (IDE) fingers, ensuring optimal electromechanical utilization of the entire nanotube length. Nanosensors calcined at 850 °C achieved a maximum output power of 228.14 nW and an exceptional surface power density of 1141 nW cm–2. These values represent a ∼60% performance enhancement over counterparts processed at 750 °C. The optimized sensor exhibited a stable output voltage of 0.60 V and maintained stable performance after 2000 s of loading–unloading cycles at 0.41 N…

title: Effect of Microwave Power and Solvent Ratio on Pectin Extraction Characteristics from Manalagi Apple Pomace: A Two-Factor Factorial Study
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of microwave power (450, 540, and 630 W) and material-to-solvent ratio (1:15, 1:20, and 1:25 g/mL) on the yield, equivalent weight, methoxyl content, galacturonic acid content, and degree of esterification of pectin extracted from Manalagi apple pomace using 0.1M citrate buffer (pH 2). A 3 × 3 factorial design with two independent extraction runs per treatment (18 observations) was analyzed by two-way ANOVA (? = 0.05), followed by Duncan’s multiple range test. Microwave power significantly affected all five responses. Solvent ratio significantly affected yield, equivalent weight, methoxyl content, and degree of esterification, but not galacturonic acid content. The power × ratio interaction was significant for all responses except equivalent weight (p = 0.070). The 540 W and 1:20 combination gave the highest numerical means for all responses (yield 15,09%, equivalent weight 791.725 mg/meq, methoxyl content 8.830%, galacturonic acid content 72.380%, degree of esterification 69.245%), although for yield it did not differ significantly from 630 W and 1:20 (14.010%). With only two runs per treatment and no confirmation runs, 540 W and 1:20 is best regarded as the most promising of the nine tested combinations, not as a verified optimum. Data expansion and local tuning: A strategy for effective clinical deployment of AI in pulmonary nodule screening
abstract: Background The clinical performance of pulmonary nodule screening systems may be influenced by training data size and differences in imaging characteristics across institutions. Improving model performance and cross-center adaptability is important for clinical deployment. Objective To investigate the effects of data expansion and localized fine-tuning on a pulmonary nodule screening system (PNSS) and evaluate its clinical utility for pulmonary nodule detection and classification. Methods Lung CT scans from Weifang People's Hospital and Shandong Provincial Hospital were retrospectively analyzed to assess PNSS performance with different training dataset sizes. Localized fine-tuning was further applied to improve cross-center adaptability. A prospective study at Weifang People's Hospital compared PNSS with experienced radiologists in routine clinical practice. Results Data expansion increased detection sensitivity from 0.7703 to 0.9428 and classification accuracy from 0.7029 to 0.9486, with performance gains gradually approaching saturation. Localized fine-tuning improved cross-center diagnostic accuracy from 53.57% to 85.36% and sensitivity from 0.5495 to 0.8736. In the prospective evaluation, PNSS achieved a sensitivity of 0.9302 for malignant nodules, 13.95 percentage points higher than radiologists. Overall diagnostic accuracy was 0.92 compared with 0.85 for radiologists. PNS…

title: Assessment of Household Lime Juice (Citrus aurantifolia) Washing as a Remediation Strategy for Sniper-Contaminated Black-Eyed Beans
abstract: Dichlorvos contamination of stored black-eyed beans raises concerns about food quality and the effectiveness of household treatments. This study evaluated the effects of dichlorvos contamination and fresh lime juice treatment on the pH, proximate composition, and phytochemical profile of black-eyed beans (Vigna unguiculata). Three experimental groups were investigated: untreated cooked and air-dried beans (Sample A), dichlorvos-contaminated beans (Sample B), and contaminated beans treated with fresh lime juice prior to cooking and drying (Sample C). Physicochemical and biochemical assessments were conducted using pH determination, proximate analysis, and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The control sample exhibited a slightly alkaline pH of 7.34 ± 1.03, whereas pesticide contamination was associated with a lower pH of 6.95 ± 2.02, indicating mild acidification of the bean matrix. Following lime juice treatment, the pH was slightly higher at 7.01 ± 2.02, suggesting partial buffering activity. Proximate analysis revealed pronounced nutritional deterioration after pesticide exposure. Crude protein content decreased by 64% in the contaminated sample and by 75% after lime washing relative to the control. Crude fat content declined by 28% in Sample B and by 72% in Sample C, while carbohydrate content decreased by 85% and 86%, respectively. Total nitrogen content showed a…

title: When Does Business Strategy Increase Climate‐Change Exposure? The Contingent Role of Managerial Ability
abstract: ABSTRACT Why does the same business strategy simultaneously mitigate and amplify firms' exposure to climate‐related risks? Prior research offers conflicting predictions regarding the environmental implications of innovation‐oriented Prospector strategies, suggesting that they can both mitigate and amplify risk. We address this puzzle by developing a contingency framework that reconceptualises climate‐change exposure as arising from how firms organise and govern strategic flexibility. Drawing on organisational theory, the natural resource‐based view and a Neo‐Durkheimian perspective on risk governance, we argue that Prospector strategies embed a fundamental flexibility–control tension that simultaneously enhances adaptive capacity and increases coordination complexity. Climate‐change exposure therefore reflects how organisations manage and resolve this tension. We conceptualise managerial ability as a governance‐structuring capability that organises attention, prioritises competing risk signals and aligns dispersed activities under uncertainty. Using 13,547 firm‐year observations of US public firms from 2001 to 2024 and a machine learning‐based measure of climate‐change exposure derived from earnings call transcripts, we find that Prospector strategies are associated with higher exposure, but this relationship is attenuated in firms with higher managerial ability. Our findings a…

title: Circular Supply Chain Strategies for Mitigating Partial and Full Disruptions in Distribution Centres
abstract: ABSTRACT Supply chain disruptions are unwanted events that can create problems in maintaining the flow of goods and services, delivering and fulfilling demand, managing costs, and potentially hurting resilience performance. Adopting appropriate strategies and the use of precise decision‐making models can help mitigate the disruptions and improve profitability and resilience performance. Previous studies developed models and generated mitigation plans using resilience strategies. However, there are limited studies that quantitatively investigate the usefulness of circular strategies in mitigating disruptions. This study makes the first attempt to develop quantitative models and generate supply chain mitigation plans for mitigating partial and full disruptions in distribution centres (DCs). To do so, we develop a mathematical modelling and simulation approach to develop models under three situations: an ideal plan when there is no disruption, the impacts of disruptions when no strategies are used, and mitigation plans with circular strategies. We use a distribution plan of a smartphone in Australia to demonstrate the results and findings. The results reveal that full disruptions in multiple DCs have the most damaging impacts on demand fulfilment and total profit. Results also reveal that the use of circular strategies, such as utilisation of spare capacity, repair and reuse of pr…

title: Optimization Of Shariah-Based Digital Marketing Strategy To Increase Smartfren Brand Loyalty Through Customer Engagement According To Islamic Economic Concept
abstract: This study aims to optimize sharia-based digital marketing strategies to enhance Smartfren's brand loyalty through customer engagement according to the concept of Islamic economics. The background of this research is the low optimization of sharia principles in the digital marketing practices of telecommunication operators in Indonesia, particularly in the aspects of moderation (al-wasathiyyah) and justice (al-haq wa al-adl), as well as the gap between high attitudinal loyalty and the company's financial performance. This study employs a quantitative method with a survey approach. Data were collected through online questionnaires distributed to 200 Smartfren customers in the Greater Jakarta area, interviews with 30 customers at Smartfren outlets, observation of @smartfrenworld social media activities over three months, and documentation from company reports and official publications. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive and inferential statistics with Pearson correlation. The theoretical frameworks include Islamic Marketing Theory (Kartajaya & Sula, 2006), Customer Engagement Theory (Brodie et al., 2011), Brand Loyalty Theory (Oliver, 1999), and Maqashid Sharia Theory (Asy-Syatibi). The results show that the optimization level of Smartfren's sharia-based digital marketing is moderate (mean 3.51 out of 5), with the highest indicator being the absence of content violatin…

title: Преемственность как стратегия развития диагностической компетентности будущего педагога в условиях цифровой трансформации образования
abstract: В статье актуализируется проблема недостаточной сформированности диагностической компетентности будущих педагогов в условиях цифровизации образования. Цель исследования – теоретически обосновать, разработать и экспериментально проверить технологию преемственного диагностического практикума как средства развития диагностической компетентности будущего педагога в системе непрерывного образования. Под диагностической компетентностью педагога понимается интегративное профессионально-личностное образование, характеризующееся наличием системы специальных знаний, умений и навыков в области педагогической диагностики, сформированных профессионально значимых качеств (наблюдательность, рефлексивность, критическое мышление, эмпатия), а также мотивационной готовностью к эффективному выполнению профессиональных задач на диагностической основе. Содержание процесса развития диагностической компетентности на основе принципа преемственности включает преемственность всех компонентов педагогической системы развития диагностической компетентности субъекта непрерывного образования, преемственность в требованиях к диагностической компетентности обучающихся на каждом уровне образования, преемственность в развитии у обучающихся профессионально-диагностических качеств личности. Bayesian hierarchical uncertainty quantification of a helical-path tortuosity predictor for modeling hydraulic conductivity in sandstone aquifers
abstract: Abstract Hydraulic conductivity and effective diffusivity in saturated sandstone aquifers depend on the square of tortuosity, so using a point estimate of tortuosity leaves its contribution to uncertainty unquantified in groundwater-flow and contaminant-transport models. A Bayesian hierarchical framework quantifies uncertainty in a published helical-path tortuosity predictor using a dataset of 51 sandstone samples spanning three formation classes: Tight German sandstones, clean Fontainebleau-analogous sandstones, and unconsolidated high-connectivity sandstones. The framework propagates uncertainty to hydrogeological quantities using the existing model and published data. Posterior predictions of tortuosity agree with the observations, with a mean absolute percentage error of approximately 3.3% and conservatively calibrated predictive intervals. Convergence was assessed using rank-normalized split $$\widehat{R}$$ R ^ , effective sample sizes, and autocorrelation times, and out-of-sample performance was assessed using Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out and five-fold cross-validation (held-out mean absolute percentage error near 5.1%). Static–Dynamic Optimization of the Ecological Security Pattern to Enhance Resilience: A Case Study of the Dongting Lake Ecological Economic Zone
abstract: The Dongting Lake Ecological Economic Zone faces simultaneous ecological degradation and landscape fragmentation, which call for a dynamic and highly resilient ecological security framework. Conventional static assessments are inadequate because they neglect the nonlinear effects among resistance factors. To address this gap, we propose a progressive framework comprising static baseline characterization, retrospective dynamic characterization over three observation periods, resilience diagnostics, and spatial optimization. Ecological sources are delineated by jointly evaluating ecosystem services and landscape ecological risk, and an ecological network is then constructed by coupling the XGBoost–SHAP model with circuit theory to quantify resistance factors and their relative contributions. Structural robustness is examined using topological metrics and robustness simulations. The main findings are as follows: (1) ecosystem services show a high-periphery, low-center pattern with an overall declining trend, whereas high ecological risk occurs mainly in forest–farmland ecotones; (2) SHAP analysis identifies land use (38.1%) and the normalized difference vegetation index (30.8%) as the dominant determinants of ecological resistance, with high-resistance zones concentrated in the central and urbanized sectors and low-resistance corridors aligned with peripheral forestlands; (3) a st…

title: From Topology Optimization to Experimental Verification: Development of a Compact Compliant Gripper for Robotic Kiwifruit Harvesting
abstract: Robotic kiwifruit harvesting requires compact grippers that accommodate fruit-size variation while transmitting sufficient force without excessive stress. This study examined the effects of the compliance constraint, volume fraction, and intermediate pseudo-density threshold on a displacement-driven topology-optimized gripper, then re-optimized a selected layout within a shortened domain and refined critical features. The monolithic PA2200 gripper was manufactured by selective laser sintering and assessed through finite element analysis, stereo digital image correlation, and load-cell testing. The 132 mm × 102 mm × 10 mm prototype weighed 17.96 g. Simulations predicted approximately ±11 mm of unloaded finger motion and per-finger reaction forces of 50.99 and 59.17 N at representative small- and large-fruit positions, respectively. The predicted peak stress reached 27.96 MPa during extended opening, remaining below the allowable stress of 28.2 MPa established using a safety factor of 1.5. With measured input displacements imposed in simulations, trial-averaged mean absolute output-displacement errors were below 0.06 mm. Loaded comparisons using measured input forces and output positions as boundary conditions showed a maximum absolute per-finger force difference of 0.97 N. These results show that the compact design can retain nominal motion and force transmission while satisfyin…

title: Modeling and vibration analysis of involute spline pairs with fretting wear transmission effects
abstract: Due to factors such as tooth clearance and fretting wear during the transmission process, the vibration generated by splined pairs not only negatively impacts the stability of the entire transmission system, but also affects ride comfort. To reveal the vibration and fretting wear mechanisms of splined pairs in the transmission system of new energy vehicles, firstly, a comprehensive time-varying meshing stiffness model of splined pairs considering the actual number of meshing tooth pairs is established. Combining the pure torsional dynamics model of involute splined pairs with the lumped parameter method, the vibration displacement and velocity of involute splined pairs are investigated, considering the tooth side clearance and load variations. Then, a fretting wear calculation model is constructed based on the FEM model to investigate the influence of fretting wear-induced tooth side clearance increase on the meshing stiffness of splined pairs. Finally, fretting wear is incorporated into the theoretical dynamics model to study its impact on the dynamic characteristics of splined pairs, thereby verifying the accuracy of the theoretical model and conclusions, and providing reliable theoretical support for the optimized design of involute splined pairs.

title: Right to Disconnect in India: Assessing the Need for a Statutory Framework for Digital Work-Life Boundaries
abstract: Today many workplaces in India use tools and remote communication all the time creating a culture where people are always on duty. This constant connectivity leads to digital tele pressure and makes many workers feel burned out especially those in knowledge‑intensive jobs. India’s current laws, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 contain a major gap: they focus mainly on physical offices and do not set limits on the hours that white‑collar, manager and IT workers can work leaving off‑the‑clock digital overreach completely unregulated. The main idea of this paper is that the Right to Disconnect is more than a workplace rule; it is a core right that comes from personal freedom, personal choice and human dignity as protected by Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Using the Puttaswamy privacy case and the right to rest mentioned in Re: Ramlila Maidan Incident, this study builds a set of rules that say people should control when and where they work, protecting them from companies that try to enter their time or space without permission. The paper also looks at how basic rights can apply to companies, not just the state after the Supreme Court decision in Kaushal Kishor v. State of UP. It talks about the difference between the court forcing a company to obey a writ and the State’s duty to make laws that protect workers trying to balance workers’ tim…

title: Optimal Design of a Two-Stage Helical Gearbox via NSGA-II and MAIRCA: Balancing Transmission Efficiency and Structural Compactness
abstract: A hybrid optimization and decision-making framework for the best design of a two-stage helical gearbox is presented in this research. The primary objective is to simultaneously maximize mechanical efficiency under different transmission ratio conditions and minimize the entire gearbox volume, indicating structural compactness. The bi-objective optimization problem is solved using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), which produces a variety of Pareto-optimal solutions. The Multi-Attributive Ideal-Real Comparative Analysis (MAIRCA) technique is incorporated as a multi-criteria decision-making tool to determine the most balanced design from the Pareto front. To ensure that the solutions are practically feasible, a comprehensive computer-based model is created to assess gear geometry, load distribution, and power losses. The findings show that the suggested NSGA-II-MAIRCA method successfully manages the volume and efficiency trade-off, producing high-performance and small gearbox layouts. For gearbox designers looking for effective solutions under performance and space constraints, this work provides useful data.

Financial Development, Trade Openness and Economic Growth: Evidence from Nigeria
abstract: This study empirically examines the effect of financial development and trade openness on economic growth in Nigeria from 1990 to 2025. In order to achieve the objective of the study, relevant annual time series data needed were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin and the World Bank. The data obtained were tested for stationarity in order to establish if the time series have unit root using the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test. Johansen cointegration test was used to establish if the time series variables in the model were cointegrated or have long run relationship. Lastly, the study employed Error Correction Model to investigate the short-run parameters among the variables. Data analysis was facilitated by E-views 12 statistical package. The findings of the study showed that broad money supply, credit to the private sector, bank deposits and trade openness have positive and significant effects on real gross domestic product in Nigeria. Based on the findings of this study, it can therefore be concluded that financial development and trade openness play a vital role in promoting economic growth in Nigeria. title: O split payment na reforma tributária brasileira: os limites da arrecadação automatizada diante da capacidade contributiva, da livre iniciativa e da neutralidade tributária
abstract: The Brazilian tax reform, introduced by Constitutional Amendment No. 132/2023 and regulated, among other provisions, by Complementary Laws No. 214/2025 and No. 227/2026, has brought substantial changes to consumption taxation, particularly through the establishment of the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS), the Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS), and a tax collection mechanism operating at the financial settlement of transactions, known as split payment. This article aims to critically examine the constitutional compatibility of this mechanism with the principles of ability to pay, freedom of enterprise, proportionality, and tax neutrality, particularly in light of its potential effects on corporate cash flow and working capital. The research adopts a qualitative approach based on the legal-dogmatic method, using bibliographic and documentary research, as well as a comparative analysis of international experiences. It examines the legal framework of automated tax collection, its relationship with the non-cumulative taxation system, and the risks associated with accelerated collection, excessive withholding, and delays in making financial resources available to taxpayers. The study concludes that split payment is not inherently incompatible with the Brazilian Constitution, provided that its implementation is proportionate, transparent, and supported by effective safeguards fo…

title: Paradox of Marriage Law Reform: Progressive Statutes versus Ingrained Indonesian Legal Culture
abstract: Marriage law reform constitutes part of the state’s effort to develop a unified national legal system while responding to evolving social challenges related to marital practices. The enactment of Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage marked an important milestone in the unification of marriage law in Indonesia, replacing the previously pluralistic legal framework influenced by customary, religious, and colonial legal traditions. This study examines the dynamics of marriage law reform in Indonesia, particularly the minimum marriage age, and its implications for society’s legal culture, using a normative legal approach based on statutory, conceptual, and literature analysis. The findings show that the reform of marriage law, particularly the amendment of the minimum marriage age through Law No. 16 of 2019, reflects an effort to align legal regulations with constitutional principles of equality and non-discrimination while enhancing legal protection for women and children. Nevertheless, the study reveals that changes in legal substance do not automatically translate into uniform compliance in societal practices, as customary traditions, religious interpretations, and living social norms continue to influence the implementation of marriage regulations across both rural and urban contexts. Therefore, the effectiveness of marriage law reform is not determined solely by legislative…
