Risk-Constrained Energy Storage Scheduling Under Electricity Price Forecast Uncertainty
abstract: Electricity price uncertainty can turn anticipated storage arbitrage gains into concentrated financial losses when forecast errors coincide with scheduled charging or discharging. Improved prediction scores alone therefore provide insufficient evidence that a forecasting and scheduling system delivers reliable economic value. A unified residual scenario interface connects Ridge, quantile LightGBM, and quantile TCN to identical battery constraints and scenario CVaR scheduling. Controlled ablations vary state conditioning and temporal pairing while preserving forecast means or empirical marginals. Chronological evaluation combines NSW1 testing, regional retraining, probability diagnostics, paired bootstrap intervals, and sensitivity analyses across budgets and battery configurations. Under the reference NSW1 configuration, Ridge CVaR scheduling increased annual net profit from 99,931 to 116,254 AUD and reduced realized daily loss CVaR95 from 608.40 to 504.98 AUD. Stronger predictors did not consistently dominate economically. State conditioning barely improved high volatility coverage, and complete paths offered no observed advantage. The 1 MWh configuration increased tail risk relative to deterministic scheduling. The evidence supports conditional economic benefits rather than guaranteed loss protection. VIC1 and SA1 extend regional scheduling validation, while DE and PJM assess…

title: Las decisiones didácticas como mecanismo para explicar el desarrollo de habilidades para la vida y el trabajo en la educación superior
abstract: Higher education faces the challenge of preparing students to respond to increasingly complex social and professional contexts. Although the literature recognizes the importance of life and work skills, a gap remains in explaining how teaching practice contributes to their development. This article aims to address that gap by proposing a conceptual framework that explains the role of didactic decisions in this process. Based on a conceptual review of the specialized literature, it proposes the concept of didactic decisions, understood as the set of intentional pedagogical choices through which faculty transform curricular goals into learning experiences. As a result, the Conceptual Model of Didactic Decisions for the Development of Life and Work Skills (MDD-HVT, by its Spanish acronym) is presented. It comprises five dimensions that explain how teaching practice can foster the development of these skills.

title: Green power consumption scheduling via CatBoost–LightGBM forecasting and hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning
abstract: The increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic generation creates uncertainty and coordination challenges for power-system operation. This paper develops an integrated green-power scheduling framework that combines a CatBoost–LightGBM forecasting ensemble with hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning. Feature-specific routing, weighted fusion, and residual correction are used to represent heterogeneous meteorological and temporal information. A regional deep Q-network (DQN) agent coordinates distributed virtual power plant (VPP) agents based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm. A constrained multi-objective formulation links renewable-energy utilization, operating cost, carbon emissions, and power balance. Forecast intervals are retained as uncertainty descriptors, although calibrated scenario-based reinforcement learning remains to be validated. Adaptive penalties and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) are used to explore feasible scheduling trade-offs. The framework is evaluated using operational data from an industrial-park VPP in Yunnan, China. The results indicate that forecast quality, coordinated control, storage flexibility, and weather conditions influence scheduling performance. Computational cost, static objective weighting, limited extreme-weather coverage, and scalability to larger VPP populations remain important…

title: Eliminating Make-Whole Uplifts with a Minimum-Cost Uniform Price Adder
abstract: Co-optimizing energy and flexible ramping reserves may dispatch generators at locational marginal prices (LMPs) below their submitted energy offer prices, necessitating out-of-market make-whole payments. Such payments create discriminatory settlements among generators and may incentivize strategic bidding for higher profits. This paper proposes LMP+U, an in-market uniform price adder to LMP for transmission-constrained networks, which minimizes demand payments subject to zero out-of-market make-whole uplift, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and provides locally truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators. We also identify conditions under which a price-taking generator can increase its profit by inflating its energy offer under conventional LMP with make-whole uplift. Numerical simulations illustrate the properties of LMP+U and its advantages over conventional LMP in congested networks.

title: An Investigation on Deformation Behaviors of Energy Absorbers for Passenger Coaches
abstract: Thin-walled structures is used commonly as energy absorbers at the front and back of the coaches. These parts should be designed to minimize the damage to the vehicle and prevent the passengers from fatality and/or injury by absorbing the collision energy in railway transportation. In this paper, deformation behaviors of tube like structures with truncated cone under the axial impact load were investigated by means of finite element analysis (FEA). The energy absorbers having tube like structures were modelled at the same weight and have three different wall thickness and taper angle. As a result of FEA, the performances of straight and truncated cone type energy absorbers were compared in terms of energy absorption capacities and an optimization study was done to determine the effects of thickness and taper angle on energy absorbing performances of the members. The analysis of variance in 95% confidence level was applied in order to determine the effects of design parameters on total efficiency (TE). Besides, optimum design parameters for TE were determined by using Taguchi optimization methodology. Thickness was found as the most significant parameter on total efficiency with 60.52% percentage contribution ratio according to ANOVA results.
venue: Periodicals of Engineering and Natural Sciences (PEN)

title: Analyzing the Impact of Carbon Accountability, Public Debt Sustainability, and Natural Resource Rents on Green Economic Growth: The Mediating Role of Digital Financial Innovation
abstract: This study explores the interactions between carbon accountability and the sustainability of public debt and the rents of natural resources and the growth of green economies through the impact of digital financial innovations as an intervening variable. Based on a balanced panel dataset of 88 economies (including developed and developing countries) in nine geographic regions between the period of 2015 and 2024, the study uses the following estimation versions: Pooled Ordinary Least Squares, Fixed Effects, Random Effects, and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors. percentage of forest cover is used to measure carbon accountability, central government debt as a sector of the GDP is used to measure fiscal sustainability and natural resource rent as a percentage of GDP is used to measure natural resource wealth. Digital financial innovation is proxied by the number of secure internet servers per million people, whereas gross capital formation expressed as a percentage of GDP is green economic growth. The fixed effects specification is preferred, as confirmed by the Hausman test. It is shown that carbon accountability (forest area) and natural resources rents have a strong positive influence on gross capital formation, and public debt has a strong negative influence on sustainable development. Digital financial innovation mediates three relationships, increasing the growth impact of carbo…
venue: Journal of Sustainable and Economic Development

title: Evaluation of marginal and average sectorial GHGs emissions abatement costs using an open-source energy system optimization model: the Italian case study
abstract: Abstract To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide marginal abatement costs and sectorial and sub-sectorial average abatement costs with a multi-sectoral energy system optimization model. The approach compares the total system cost and emissions of a sequence of whole-system optimizations under progressively stricter emission constraints. The constraints are applied along the entire decarbonization trajectory rather than to a single target year. The resulting marginal costs are then allocated to the sectors and technologies that deliver each emission reduction step. Since every point of the curve corresponds to a consistent system configuration, technology interactions and sector coupling are preserved, and each cost level can be traced back to the technology transitions and input assumptions that drive it. The methodology is demonstrated on the Italian energy system with the open-source TEMOA-Italy model, considering emission reduction targets of up to -90% in 2050. The results show that marginal abatement costs rise steeply as the targets become more ambitious, and that abatement costs vary widely across sectors. The power sector is the cheapest to decarbonize, thanks to mature renewable te…
venue: Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change

title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

title: Nitrogen Effects on Barley Plant (Hordeum vulgare) Phenotype and Anatomy
abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) is one of the most significant field crops in Iraq because of its high adaptation capacity to marginal environmental conditions. Inadequate nitrogen fertilization remains a major constraint to barley productivity. In this study, the impact of application of urea fertilizer at a rate 160 kg/dunum as compared to the non-treated control on some phenotypic and anatomical traits for two barley cultivars (Abaya99 and Abaya265) was evaluated. The field study was carried out at the College of Agriculture, Samarra University by using Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) for 2024 winter season. The plant height, spike length, and contents of number of grains, thousand-grain weight and grain weight per spike under nitrogen supply were significantly higher than those of the control. Similarly, anatomical traits, including sclerenchyma, xylem, phloem, upper epidermis, and palisade layers, increased significantly. Abaya99 had higher values than Abaya265 for all characteristics and the interaction of Abaya99 with nitrogen treatment had the highest values. Overall, applying 160 kg/dunum of nitrogen in two splits enhanced vegetative and anatomical traits, resulting in higher production and improved market quality for barley. The cultivar Abaya99 consistently recorded higher values than Abaya265 for all studied traits. The interaction between nitrogen fertilization…

title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) or its active ingredients for osteoarthritis
Renewable Energy Consumption, Financial Inclusion and Fintech as Drivers of Environmental Quality: The Moderating Role of Green Finance in selected South Asian Economies
abstract: Environmental challenges require innovative, inclusive, nature-based, and financial solutions. In this regard, renewable energy consumption, financial inclusion, fintech and green finance bring greater opportunities for mitigating CO2 emissions. Previous studies have identified numerous determinants of environmental quality including renewable energy consumption, financial inclusion and fintech. However, their combined impact on environmental quality remains underexplored. This is a novel study which has examined the moderating role of green finance in the relationship between fintech and environmental quality. Therefore, the current study examines the impact of renewable energy consumption, financial inclusion and fintech on environmental quality. While the interaction of green finance between fintech and environmental quality has also investigated. Data from selected South Asian countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan Maldives and Nepal) for the period 2004–2024 has collected. The findings of CS-ARDL Model shows that renewable energy consumption, fintech and foreign direct investment reduced Co2 emission and enhanced the environmental quality both in short run and in long run. While financial inclusion and green finance enhanced co2 emission and declined the environmental quality in both long run and short run. Moreover, green finance positively moderates …
venue: Journal of Sustainable and Economic Development

title: Financial Inclusion, Energy Transition, and Human Capital Impact on Economic Sustainability: Mediating Role of Digital Transformation
abstract: This study examines how financial inclusion, energy transition, and human capital investment influence economic sustainability in developing economies and takes digital transformation as an intermediate variable. Based on a balanced panel dataset of 44 developing economies from 2015-2024, the study applies Pooled Ordinary Least Squares, Fixed Effects and Random Effects models. Financial inclusion is represented by domestic credit to the private sector, energy transition is represented by access to clean fuels to cook, and human capital is represented by government spending on education. Economic sustainability by the level of foreign direct investment is in terms of net inflows as a percentage of GDP and the mediating variable in digital transformation is the integration of digital technologies across operations, including broadband, internet usage, digital skills, and ICT infrastructure. The Hausman test tests whether individual effects are correlated with the regressors. If correlated, then Fixed Effects model is preferred otherwise the Random Effects model is more appropriate. Empirical evidence of this study shows that financial inclusion, energy transition, and human capital investment have a very positive relationship with FDI-measured by indicators such as GDP growth stability, environmental-economic balance and inclusive growth. Digital transformation mediates all three…
venue: Journal of Sustainable and Economic Development

title: Optimal free energy requirements for managing disruptive and unexpected organizational change
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a systems-theoretic framework to understand how organizations maintain adaptive functioning amid disruptive, unexpected environmental change. Drawing on the free energy (FE) principle, the paper conceptualizes organizational FE as an adaptive reserve capacity that enables organizations to absorb, interpret and respond to environmental uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Using archival data from Canadian manufacturing sectors during the COVID-19 disruption period, the study explores whether pre-pandemic levels of FE, operationalized through manufacturing capacity utilization, were associated with post-pandemic organizational resilience and GDP growth between 2019 and 2023. The analyses also examine the potential roles of automation, government stimulus and supply-chain disruption within a moderated mediation framework. Findings The analysis provides no evidence that FE directly predicts post-pandemic GDP growth. However, FE consistently predicts sector-level organizational resilience measured through absorptive, adaptive and recovery capacities. These findings suggest that adaptive reserve capacity may operate more meaningfully at organizational and sectoral levels than as a direct driver of macroeconomic performance. Practical implications The study contributes to resilience and systems research by reframing FE as a resilience-oriented sy…

title: Using a Gaussian process emulator to approximate short-term climate response patterns to greenhouse gas and aerosol forcings
abstract: We present a Gaussian process emulator for estimating fast surface temperature response patterns to a range of different climate forcing agents, including both long-lived greenhouse gases and short-lived pollutants such as aerosols. This emulator is trained on simulations driven by perturbations to emissions (for short-lived pollutants) and concentrations (for long-lived greenhouse gases) using a full-complexity global climate model and predicts the response in the first five years after the forcing, at a small fraction of the computational cost. We outline the emulator design, including the choice of pollutant perturbations and the input space covered by the training data. We show that the emulator performs well in most regions of the chosen input space, except under very large aerosol perturbations. A global sensitivity analysis is carried out to characterize and understand emission-response relationships for each pollutant. We find similar large-scale patterns of sensitivity to aerosol pollutants released in different regions. Our work demonstrates the potential for rapid climate change projections subject to various climate forcing agents, focusing on the short-term response. This paves the way for the future development of more policy-relevant emulators, that can target decadal and multi-decadal timescales.

title: Dynamic flow promotes airway MPS maturation and host response to viral infection
abstract: Background High attrition rates in infectious disease drug and vaccine development are partly attributed to preclinical models that inadequately recapitulate the human airway microenvironment. Although dynamic flow microphysiological systems (MPS) have been proposed as more physiologically relevant alternatives to static culture, direct benchmarking in respiratory infection models remains limited. Methods We directly compared primary human airway MPS established under static conditions or continuous basolateral perfusion. Tissue organisation, epithelial differentiation, barrier integrity, spatial infection phenotypes, and host transcriptional responses were assessed following infection with SARS-CoV-2 variants (Pre-alpha, Delta, and Omicron BA.5). Results Dynamic flow promoted improved epithelial organisation without major alterations in baseline gene expression, consistent with accelerated differentiation kinetics rather than shifts in cell composition. Both static and dynamic systems supported productive SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, dynamic flow cultures demonstrated reduced inter-replicate variability and improved robustness of quantitative readouts. Spatial imaging revealed reproducible higher-order phenotypes, including variant-dependent syncytia formation. Transcriptomic analyses showed increased effect sizes and reduced variance under dynamic flow, resulting in improve…

title: Reference values for refractive error of the Spot Vision Screener in children under 3 years of age
abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare manufacturer and referral criteria for the Spot Vision Screener (SVS) for refractive errors and investigate the optimal cutoff value for patients under 3 years of age using the Youden index (YI). Study design Retrospective study. Methods Patients who presented from February 2016 to March 2024 were screened using the SVS before examination by pediatric ophthalmologists masked to the SVS results. All children underwent a comprehensive eye examination, including cycloplegic refraction. Participants were subdivided by age (6–11, 12–35, and 36–47 months) to determine gold standard results according to American Academy of Ophthalmology guidelines. The SVS effectiveness was compared by age group between the manufacturer and referral criteria. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of the cutoff value and investigated the cutoff value that maximizes the YI. Results Five hundred three children were included. The sensitivity and specificity of the SVS using manufacturer criteria were both 84.1% while using referral criteria they were 71.0% and 93.9%, respectively. False positives decreased in all categories using referral criteria. Most false-negative cases were astigmatism and hyperopia. Regarding anisometropia among 12-35 months old children, the cutoff value that maximized the YI improved specificity without compromising sensitivity. Conclusion The SV…

title: Working more than desired: determinants of over-employment in Australia
abstract: Abstract Over-employment is an important but often under-specified dimension of working-time mismatch. While research has paid considerable attention to under-employment, it has paid less attention to workers who work more hours than they would prefer. This paper examines over-employment in Australia using Waves 16 to 23 of the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey, covering the period 2016 to 2023. Over-employment is defined as working at least five hours more per week than preferred, with robustness checks using alternative thresholds and a continuous actual-preferred hours gap. The findings show that over-employment is more common among older workers, managers and professionals, non-casual workers, workers with longer employer tenure and partnered workers. Higher working-time flexibility and higher hourly wages are associated with a lower probability of over-employment. The results also show no significant net gender difference once occupation, employment status, job characteristics, household circumstances and period are controlled. Descriptive analysis confirms that over-employment is concentrated among long-hours workers but is not reducible to long hours, as some part-time and standard full-time workers are also over-employed. The paper contributes a descriptive panel-based account of over-employment as a structured form of working-time mismatch rathe…

The role of perceived explainability and fairness in shaping acceptance of AI credit scoring in Vietnam’s P2P lending market
From lab to market: how horizontal and vertical diversity shape university spin-off performance
abstract: Purpose This study examines how founding-team configuration shapes university spin-off (USO) performance by focusing on the conditional role of horizontal and vertical diversity. The main purpose is to investigate whether academic–non-academic profile differentiation translates into stronger economic outcomes and under which team configurations this relationship becomes effective. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a multi-source longitudinal dataset of 155 Italian life-science USOs, combining information from Netval, Orbis, Orbis Intellectual Property and Cineca. Annual accounting data for the period 2014–2024 are organised as an unbalanced firm-year panel. The hypotheses are tested through pooled panel Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regressions with year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors. Performance is measured through sales growth and return on assets (ROA). Findings The results show that profile differentiation is not an unconditional driver of USO performance. None of the hypothesised relationships receives support for annual sales growth, whereas two moderation effects emerge for ROA. Scientific background diversity negatively moderates the relationship between profile differentiation and ROA, a pattern consistent with greater coordination and integration demands as disciplinary variety increases. By contrast, academic status diversity positively mod…

title: Generative Ai-Enabled Financial Forecasting and Strategic Financial Decision Quality in Emerging-Market SMEs
abstract: This study investigates how generative AI enabled financial forecasting capability and business analytics capability shape strategic financial decision quality in emerging market SMEs, with particular attention to the moderating role of AI governance maturity. Grounded in organizational information processing theory and dynamic capabilities theory, the study argues that better financial decisions depend not simply on access to advanced technologies, but on how effectively firms turn AI generated forecasts and analytical information into useful financial judgment. AI governance maturity is expected to strengthen this process by providing appropriate oversight, accountability, validation, and control over the use of AI generated financial information. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 385 respondents who possessed relevant knowledge of SME financial management, business analytics, AI applications, or organizational decision making. Data were collected using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS version 26. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and multiple linear regression were performed, while Hayes’ Process Macro Model 1 was used to test the moderating effect. The results show that generative AI enabled financial forecasting capability (β = 0.613) and business analytics capability (β = 0.487) both have significan…

title: Integrating coastal dynamics, ecosystem service value, and ecotourism suitability for conservation-oriented planning on Sonadia Island, Bangladesh
Digital Financial Service Adoption among Farming and Business Income Earners in Northern Nigeria: Microfinance Experience, Individual Characteristics and Geographic Heterogeneity
abstract: Digital financial services (DFS) have spread rapidly in Nigeria, but use in the North remains low. We study which characteristics of individuals and places are associated with DFS adoption among farm and business earners (adults whose income comes from farming, including some farm wage work, or from their own business) in seven North West and seven North Central states. Using the EFInA Access to Financial Services in Nigeria Survey 2023, we analyse 6,960 farm and business earners (6,936 in the preferred model after dropping 24 with missing age). Adoption is defined as mobile-money transfers or any use of a digital microfinance bank. We estimate survey-weighted logit models with standard errors clustered by enumeration area, in zone and state fixed-effect specifications, and report Firth penalised estimates, discrimination statistics and models for each component of adoption. Weighted adoption is 3.3 per cent: 192 earners use mobile money and 48 a digital microfinance bank (4 use both), and none has borrowed digitally. Post-secondary education, holding a National Identification Number, being male and being younger are associated with higher adoption. The 27 earners with microfinance loan experience, of whom 8 have adopted, have a predicted adoption probability of 26.4 per cent against 3.2 per cent for others (AME 23.2 points, 95% CI 8.4 to 38.0); this large but imprecisely estim…
venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology

title: Warranty and service contracts for reliable service quality: a traceability-based framework
abstract: Purpose This paper develops a conceptual framework for examining how warranty and long-term service agreements may shape maintenance decisions, service quality and auditability in asset-intensive settings. Design/methodology/approach The paper synthesizes literature on warranty management, service contracts, reliability, maintenance documentation and servitization. It presents a Reliability Decision Architecture (RDA), conceptual decision equations, five propositions and three illustrative contractual archetypes. Findings The synthesis identifies four proposed distortion mechanisms: metric narrowing, asymmetric risk transfer, evidentiary under-specification and oversight decoupling. The RDA links contract clauses to feasible maintenance choices and their reviewability. Effects on reliability, availability and lifecycle cost remain propositions requiring validation. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptual. The archetypes vary several clauses together and provide neither causal identification nor empirical validation. A qualitative evidence checklist supports review; numerical scoring and the proposed decision relationships require testing. Practical implications Managers can use the framework to examine whether metrics, evidence duties, escalation rules and review rights support feasible, reviewable maintenance choices. Documentation burdens and excessive r…
venue: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: Ecosystem service relationships and bundle reorganization across alternative land-use scenarios in the Luoxiao Mountains: implications for spatial management
abstract: Accelerating global environmental change and land-system transformation are reshaping mountain ecosystems, increasing the need for ecological assessments that can support robust spatial planning and differentiated management. Taking the Luoxiao Mountains as a representative forest-dominated mountain region, this study integrated intPLUS-based land-use simulation, InVEST ecosystem-service assessment, trade-off and synergy analysis, ecosystem service bundle identification, and cross-scenario management zoning. From 2000 to 2020, carbon storage (CS), habitat quality (HQ), soil conservation (SC), and water yield (WY) all declined, with WY and SC decreasing by 8.87% and 6.60%, respectively. Under all four 2035 scenarios, CS, HQ, and SC continued to decline, whereas WY increased. Ecological protection most effectively maintained forestland, CS, HQ, and the existing bundle structure, while cropland protection caused the greatest CS and HQ losses, the largest WY increase, and the most extensive bundle transitions. Ecosystem-service relationships remained comparatively stable: CS, HQ, and SC were consistently synergistic, whereas WY showed persistent trade-offs with CS and HQ. Four ecosystem service bundles were identified: a WY-dominant bundle, a moderate-to-low overall ecosystem services bundle, a CS–HQ-dominant bundle, and a high overall ecosystem services bundle. Across all four fut…

title: The Legal Validity of Customer Registration Forms in Establishing Contractual Relationships in Delivery Service Disputes Involving Breach of Contract
abstract: A Customer Registration Form (FRP) used in delivery services may function as an administrative record, evidence of contract formation, or part of an agreement defining the parties’ obligations. This normative legal study examines the conditions under which an FRP becomes contractually binding and the allocation of liability for alleged reciprocal breaches, using Tangerang District Court Case No. 289/Pdt.G/2023/PN Tng as its dispute context. It employs statutory and conceptual approaches and treats the case narrative in the original manuscript as unverified allegations because the complete judgment was unavailable. The analysis finds that enforceability depends on proof of consent, authority to contract, identifiable obligations, lawful cause, and incorporation of referenced standard terms. An invoice does not necessarily establish assent to every contractual term, while an allegation of damaged goods does not automatically extinguish the obligation to pay. Damages and setoff require separate examination of default, causation, maturity, and the certainty of competing claims. The article proposes a five-stage analytical framework integrating contract formation, incorporation of terms, performance, proof of breach, and proportionate remedies.

title: The decommodification paradox: value co-creation and institutional work in a non-monetary peer-to-peer service
abstract: Purpose This study examines how value is co-created and how trust and coordination are institutionally sustained in a peer-to-peer (P2P) service in which monetary exchange is prohibited at the operational core. Service-dominant (S-D) logic has increasingly theorised value co-creation as coordinated by institutional arrangements within service ecosystems, yet the institutional arrangements it has examined are overwhelmingly market-based. Taking World Wide Opportunities on Organic Farms (WWOOF) as a critical case, the study develops the concept of the decommodification paradox: the co-existence of a non-monetary dyadic exchange with monetary elements at adjacent layers of the service ecosystem, sustained through participants' ongoing institutional work. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, interpretivist design was adopted. Twenty semi-structured interviews with WWOOF hosts and WWOOFers across 6 Indian states, purposively sampled, were analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. Findings Four themes were generated: (1) value as co-produced labour, learning and dwelling; (2) trust sustained through values-based self-selection, small-community reputation and refusal rather than algorithmic verification; (3) the decommodification paradox, in which the non-monetary dyad is preserved by participants' work of placing monetary elements at the platform and peripheral layers and (…
venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice

title: Viewpoint: human agency as the transcending concept of human service systems
abstract: Purpose This viewpoint positions human agency as the transcending concept of human service systems, provides a practical, evidence-based framework for this new logic, develops the concept of collaborative agency and applies collaborative agency to reconceptualize the role of money in financial service systems. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on transformative service research, this research employs an interdisciplinary synthesis to establish human agency as a strategic design requirement. The methodology involves reframing service system interactions into a hierarchy of dominance and service and developing a practical toolkit based on Elinor Ostrom's core design principles. This synthesis is then applied to demonstrate the redesign of exploitative financial service systems into collaborative commons. Findings The concept of “collaborative agency” is introduced because systems designed for collaboration foster full human agency. When financial service systems are designed as collaborative common-pool resources, they transform from tools of control that undermine agency into enablers that liberate agency. Practical implications Eight core design principles are developed as a practical toolkit for practitioners to design and evaluate service systems that serve humanity. This toolkit provides a detailed framework for redesigning financial service systems, shifting them from exp…

title: An inquiry-based flipped learning framework for developing speaking fluency and critical thinking skills among pre-service EFL teachers: a conceptual model
abstract: This article introduces a conceptually-driven Inquiry-Based Flipped Learning (IBFL) model designed to develop speaking fluency and critical thinking as interdependent, rather than separate, competencies among pre-service EFL teachers. Grounded in Social Constructivism, the Interaction and Output Hypotheses, and the Revised Bloom's Taxonomy, the model organizes instruction into three interconnected stages: Pre-Class Inquiry Activation, In-Class Collaborative Inquiry, and Post-Class Reflection and Transfer. Each has a distinct function of interaction and output, and with cognitive demand generally rising across the cycle. Beyond its linguistic and cognitive aims, the model is positioned to support pre-service teachers’ readiness for the teaching practicum, offering a structured, low-stakes space to rehearse the real-time speaking and reasoning demands of their future classrooms. The article details the theoretical rationale underlying each stage, practical guidelines for implementation, an illustrative example of the model in practice, and a formative assessment methodology aligned with the model's speaking fluency and critical thinking criteria. This framework offers teacher educators a theoretically grounded, replicable model for integrating fluency and reasoning development within EFL teacher preparation programs.

title: Building Customer Loyality for Marning Corn in Bulukumba: The Impact of Brand Image, Service Quality, and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions and Customer Satisfaction
abstract: Marning corn products, typical food, and souvenirs from the Bulukumba district are packaged simply without complete product information. Yet by integrating well-designed packaging with clear and relevant product information that can improve product quality, brands can improve the overall consumer experience, build trust, and foster long-term loyalty. This research aims to analyze the direct and indirect influence of brand image, service quality, and product quality on purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction on consumer loyalty to making corn. The research method used quantitative analysis with structured interview techniques using a sample of corn buyers in Bulukumba Regency. The data analysis used is structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis using the AMOS application. The research results show that consumer satisfaction and brand image have a significant direct influence on loyalty. Brand image and service quality have an impact on purchasing decisions. Product quality, service quality, and brand image influence consumer satisfaction. Meanwhile, the variables of service quality and production quality do not have a significant effect on consumer loyalty through purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction as intervening variables of brand image, service quality, and production quality. Increasing income in the Morning Corn business can be achieved by prioritizing br…
venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences

title: Strategic Planning of Foundation Chairman in Improving Educational Service Quality at Islamic Boarding Schools
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of foundation chairman's planning in improving educational service quality at Islamic boarding schools Mambaul Khairat. The research uses a qualitative approach with case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, and document study at several Islamic boarding school foundations. Data analysis was conducted through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification according to Miles & Huberman. The results show that foundation chairman's planning includes four main stages: (1) planning by involving stakeholders in formulating vision, mission, and school objectives; (2) organizing with clear organizational structure and proportional task division; (3) actuating through effective communication and staff motivation; and (4) controlling with routine monitoring and periodic evaluation. The foundation chairman plays a strategic role as policy maker, coordinator, and external liaison. Participative-strategic leadership is a key factor in achieving financial independence and improving Islamic boarding school educational quality.

abstract: В статье на основе впервые вводимых в историографии в научный оборот материалов следственного дела П.Н. Краснова, А.Г. Шкуро, С. Клыч-Гирея, Г. фон Паннвица, С.Н. Краснова, Т.Н. title: Evaluating the effectiveness of staff training in trauma-informed care in a community older adult mental health service: a service evaluation
abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess the impact of a trauma-informed care (TIC) training programme within an NHS older adult (OA) community mental health service, addressing a gap in trauma-informed implementation for later life populations. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods, within-subjects design was used. Staff self-rated their TIC knowledge and confidence pre- and post-training using Likert scales (N = 32), and post-training questionnaire responses were analysed using both deductive and inductive content analysis. Findings Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicated statistically significant increases in staff knowledge and confidence post-training, both with large effect sizes. Qualitative findings showed strong uptake of core TIC principles – particularly “Safety”, “Trustworthiness”, “Collaboration” and “Empowerment”. Barriers to trauma-informed practice included fear of re-traumatisation and time constraints. Feedback identified the training as relevant and interactive, though improvements were suggested around dementia applicability and content density. Practical implications The findings of this study highlight the value of contextualised, experiential TIC training and the need for structural changes to support sustainable implementation. Tailoring content to dementia care may improve relevance in OA services. Originality/value The evaluation contributes novel evidence…

Negotiating The Visible Self: Identity Regulation on Social Media Among Indonesian Military Wives
abstract: Social-media identity research has established that people manage self-presentation for overlapping and partly imagined audiences, while research on military partners shows that civilian spouses negotiate identities shaped by a service member’s occupation and community. Less is known about how these processes are experienced by spouses whose online self-presentation may also be interpreted through their husbands’ institutional positions. This article examines how Indonesian military wives negotiate the visibility of personal, professional, and military-wife identities across overlapping social-media audiences. It presents a focused Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) of interview material from a broader ethically approved study involving 12 participants, concentrating on seven cases with relevant material in the available transcript-segment and analytic-summary files. Three linked patterns are developed: anticipating audiences through relational consequences; separating, withholding, or changing identity signals across contexts; and calibrating visibility differently for personal and organizational purposes. The analysis suggests that selective visibility can function as a communicative way of managing identity gaps without resolving them. Participants did not simply choose between privacy and publicity: they made some aspects of the selfless legible while preserving…

title: Scenario-recognition-based reinforcement learning dispatch with dynamic preference regulation for power grid supply assurance
abstract: Renewable power shortfalls can threaten supply adequacy during extreme peak demand when upward reserve and stored energy are limited. Fixed dispatch preferences may be overly conservative when response capability is sufficient yet provide inadequate support when it is scarce. This article proposes a reinforcement learning dispatch framework based on scenario recognition and dynamic preference regulation. Historical forecast-error scenarios provide the expected renewable availability and a conservative estimate based on a lower quantile. A supply adequacy risk index relates renewable uncertainty to load pressure, upward reserve, net load ramping, storage energy, and routine supply capability. A proximal policy optimization policy uses this information to select the operating mode, the relative weights of economic and supply adequacy objectives, and the renewable dispatch reference coefficient. Constrained scheduling allocates resources before renewable realization, and real-time corrective dispatch responds to the observed shortfall. The formulation enforces aggregate power balance and resource operating constraints. Offline learning reduces repeated online searches over dispatch preferences while retaining constrained physical resource allocation. In an aggregate multi-resource simulation based on the generation and load parameters of the IEEE 30-bus system, all 10 independentl…

title: Developing Qur’anic Financial Self-Regulation: A Behavioral Finance Framework for Financial Anxiety, Resilience, and Well-Being
abstract: Financial anxiety is increasingly recognized as an important factor in financial behavior and subjective financial well-being. Existing behavioral finance research has examined financial literacy, self-control, self-efficacy, and socioeconomic conditions, yet the mechanisms through which religious values inform financial self-regulation remain insufficiently specified. This study develops Qur’anic Financial Self-Regulation (QFSR) as a conceptual framework explaining how internalized Qur’anic values may guide financial decision-making among Muslims. Employing a thematic conceptual analysis, the study examines purposively selected Qur’anic passages through classical and contemporary exegesis and maps their regulatory principles onto established behavioral finance literature. Five interrelated dimensions are proposed: Balanced Consumption Regulation, Prospective Financial Regulation, Financial Accountability Regulation, Cognitive-Emotional Regulation under Financial Uncertainty, and Prosocial Wealth Allocation. Rather than introducing entirely new financial mechanisms, QFSR conceptualizes how Qur’anic values may activate and coordinate established self-regulatory processes through ethically grounded financial appraisal, planning, accountability, and resource allocation. The framework distinguishes value-guided regulatory capacities from observable financial behaviors and proposes …

title: Accounting for recurrent mutation in the frequency spectrum of rare alleles
abstract: Abstract As whole-genome and whole-exome datasets increase in size, they uncover alleles at lower and lower frequencies in the population. Samples of rare alleles often include recurrent mutations, where derived alleles are identical by state and not by descent. As a result, the site frequency spectrum (SFS) becomes challenging to analyze because it is strongly dependent on the mutation rate. To overcome this hurdle, we define the single mutation frequency spectrum (SMFS), which is the frequency spectrum of alleles descendant from a single mutational event. For rare alleles, the SFS with recurrent mutation is then a weighted sum of the convolutions of the SMFS with itself. This simple, yet powerful, model decouples recurrent mutation from the population genetic processes giving rise to the SMFS, such as genetic drift and selection. We show how both forward-in-time and backward-in-time models with recurrent mutations can be recast in terms of the SMFS. We then develop a method for combinatorial hierarchic estimation of the SMFS (which we name CHES). We apply this simple, yet robust, method to a human exome sequencing dataset to show that the SMFS with recurrent mutation can account for SFS differences between low and high mutation rate sites. The inferred SMFS shows an approximate scaling law with allele frequencies inconsistent with both a constant population size and an expone…

title: Titanium-driven rhizosphere bioprocess regulation promotes ginsenoside biosynthesis in Panax ginseng
abstract: Introduction Titanium (Ti) is a beneficial element with regulatory effects on plant-associated biological processes, However, the mechanisms by which Ti influences rhizosphere processes and medicinal plant quality formation remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, exogenous titanium tetrachloride (TiCl 4 ) was applied to Panax ginseng to investigate its effects on ginsenoside accumulation, rhizosphere nutrient dynamics, and microbial community assembly. Results Low-dose titanium (Ti1, 17.26 mg kg-1) supplementation significantly enhanced ginseng growth and promoted ginsenoside accumulation in roots, stems, and leaves. Titanium treatment improved rhizosphere nutrient availability and enzymatic activities, particularly those associated with phosphorus mobilization and organic matter transformation. High-throughput sequencing revealed that titanium reshaped rhizosphere microbial communities, including higher relative abundance of potentially beneficial taxa such as Mortierella, Trichoderma, Gemmatimonas, and Pseudarthrobacter, and lower relative abundance of potential pathogenic taxa such as Fusarium, Waitea. Correlation analyses showed that titanium-induced microbial shifts were associated with ginsenoside accumulation, suggesting a potential association between rhizosphere microbiome composition and medicinal quality. Discussion Collectively, these findings reveal a micr…

title: White-backed chalky grains of japonica rice caused by heat stress during maturation is associated with morphological and epigenetic regulation
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is strongly affected by heat stress during grain filling. Heat stress is a significant contributor to chalky grain, one of the main causes of quality and yield reductions in rice. Among several types of chalky grains, the white-backed type often occurs under heat stress, but the mechanism underlying this defect is not well studied. Therefore, a better understanding of how heat stress induces the white-backed type of chalky grains is necessary to improve grain quality under heat-stress conditions. Methods After flowering, rice plants were exposed to either control (25 °C) or heat (30 °C) temperature treatments. The occurrence and extent of chalkiness and morphological changes of the aleurone layer were evaluated, together with gene transcription levels and epigenetic regulation. Key Results Heat stress during grain filling significantly increased the occurrence of chalky grains after harvest, compared with the control. White-backed chalky grain was the predominant type observed. The expression of α-amylase isozymes was greatly up-regulated in the heat-stressed grains compared to the control. An increase in the thickness of the dorsal aleurone layer was observed in the white-backed chalky grains. In particular, heat stress at the early stage (0–7 days after flowering) significantly increased the occurrence of white-backed chalky…

title: High-Frequency Ultrasound in Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Correcting Clinical Understaging, Guiding Surgical Margins, And Informing Treatment Decisions
abstract: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic, recurrent, inflammatory disease of the follicular unit whose most consequential lesions, such as fluid collections, dermal tunnels, and interconnected sinus tracts, often develop beneath an apparently limited cutaneous surface. Staging and therapeutic decisions have traditionally relied on clinical systems such as the Hurley classification and the International Hidradenitis Suppurativa Severity Score System (IHS4), both of which depend on inspection and palpation. High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS, at or above 15 MHz) and ultra-high-frequency ultrasound (UHFUS, up to approximately 70 MHz), combined with color Doppler, allow real-time, noninvasive visualization of dermal and hypodermal anatomy and inflammatory activity. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on the role of sonography in HS across three domains: correction of clinical understaging, preoperative mapping of surgical margins, and its influence on medical and procedural management. In a multicenter cohort of 143 patients, ultrasound reclassified 44.7% of clinical Hurley stage I patients into a more severe stage and modified the therapeutic approach, while agreement between clinical and sonographic staging was low. In surgical series, sonographic margin delimitation enlarged the planned excision area in most procedures and was associated with lower short-term re…

A lightweight cross-session EEG emotion recognition network based on high- and low-frequency differential weighting
abstract: Non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) holds promising potential for brain-computer interfaces and neural engineering. However, cross-session distribution shift and the computational overhead of existing models remain major bottlenecks for deployment on wearable devices. To address these challenges, this paper first verifies the effectiveness of full-band features and reveals the complementary patterns between high- and low-frequency features through progressive frequency-band ablation experiments. Building on these findings, we propose FreqW-LiteNet, a lightweight network with frequency-band differentiated weighting. Avoiding complex modules such as multi-source domain adaptation or adversarial training, the model adopts a single-backbone fully connected architecture, a two-stage training strategy, and high-intensity regularization to achieve efficient training on standard CPUs. Systematic validation is conducted on three public datasets (SEED, SEED-IV, and SEED-V) under cross-session protocols using a transductive evaluation setting. All experiments are strictly restricted to these SEED-family datasets. Experimental results show that, on the SEED and SEED-IV datasets, FreqW-LiteNet achieves competitive recognition accuracy compared with state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods and general deep learning models. Notably, the model is extremely compact, with approximately 2…

title: Frequency of hepatitis B virus mutations associated with resistance to current and emerging drugs for functional cure in publicly available hepatitis B virus sequences
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains an immense global health challenge. Despite the availability of antiviral therapies, no curative treatment exists. Only a small proportion of individuals with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) achieve a functional cure. Resistance and vaccine escape mutations (EMs) may compromise current nucleos(t)ide analogs, vaccines and emerging therapies, leading to treatment failure. The present study aimed to assess the frequency of these HBV mutations in >17,000 publicly available patient-derived HBV sequences. Methods Fold-change (FC) data and resistance/escape-associated mutations were retrieved from literature searches. HBV sequences were retrieved from the NCBI Nucleotide and NCBI Virus databases. Human HBV isolates were genotyped using the HBVdb and Stanford HBVseq tools and GenBank data. Genotype-specific alignments were generated using MAFFT v7 and mutations were analyzed across reverse transcriptase (RT), core (C), surface (S) and X regions using in-house Python scripts. Results From 19,192 sequence identifiers retrieved, 17,012 genotyped sequences were analyzed. Genotypes C, B, D and A comprised approximately 85% of the dataset. RT-mutations, L180M + M204V and M204I, were frequent in certain genotypes like A, G, H, AG, and G, respectively. C-mutations, Y38F, I105T, and T109M, were identified in common genotypes. In the S-protein, G145R, E164…

Dynamic connectedness and risk transmission in Indonesia’s Sharia equity sectors: time–frequency evidence and portfolio implications
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine dynamic sectoral connectedness within the Indonesian Sharia Stock Index and its implications for portfolio diversification during major global shocks. It emphasizes the role of Sharia-compliant regulations requiring Islamic funds to allocate at least 80% of their net asset value to equities. Design/methodology/approach Time-varying parameter vector autoregression and frequency-domain connectedness frameworks are applied to analyze intersectoral risk transmission across stable and crisis periods. A connectedness-aware portfolio (CAP) strategy is used to evaluate diversification efficiency under systemic volatility. Findings From January 2019 to August 2025, the Total Connectedness Index increases from approximately 36% in stable periods to over 60% during crises, indicating stronger systemic interdependence. The energy and financial sectors emerge as major risk transmitters, whereas health care and consumer noncyclicals act as safe-haven sectors. The CAP strategy reduces portfolio volatility by 30% and improves the Sharpe ratio by 27% relative to an equal-weighted portfolio. Research limitations/implications The analysis focuses on Indonesia’s Sharia equity market and does not explicitly capture cross-border spillovers from other Islamic financial markets. Practical implications The findings provide guidance for regulators and Sharia fund manag…

Emotional regulation and leadership styles in higher education: a structural equation modeling analysis
abstract: This study aims to estimate and compare the differential and simultaneous effects of cognitive reappraisal (CR) and expressive suppression (ES)—measured as dispositional emotional regulation strategies—on transformational (TL), transactional (TranL), and laissez-faire (L-FL) leadership styles among leaders in higher education, using structural equation modeling. Unlike previous studies that have analyzed these relationships in a bivariate manner or have focused on how the leader’s style affects followers’ emotional regulation, this study reverses the direction of analysis and simultaneously controls for measurement error through prior confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), which provides more accurate structural estimates free from attenuation bias. Using a sample of 100 academic leaders from the Universidad National y Abierta y a Distancia (UNAD), the Emotional Regulation scale and the Multifactorial Leadership scale were administered. Four of the six trajectories were statistically significant. RC was the strongest predictor of TL and was negatively associated with L-FL. ES positively predicted TranL and L-FL. The model’s cross-specificity—reflected in the absence of significant relationships for the two unhypothesized pathways, ER to TranL and ES to TL—reinforces its parsimony and its differential explanatory value. Based on the Conservation of Resources (COR) Theory, the findi…

title: Fiber-optic photoacoustic dual-gas sensor with multi-frequency cooperative noise suppression and cross-orthogonal multiple-reflection excitation enhancement
abstract: A fiber-optic photoacoustic gas sensor (FOPAS) that incorporates multi-frequency cooperative noise suppression and cross-orthogonal multiple-reflection enhanced excitation is proposed for simultaneous detection of trace dual-component gases. The optimized composite buffer chambers effectively suppress the acoustic noise at two independent resonance frequencies corresponding to the resonance tube and the cantilever. Compared with conventional cylindrical buffer chambers, the designed composite structure reduces the background signal by 23% and the noise level by 20%. The cross-orthogonal multi-reflection optical structure enables two excitation lasers to be individually coupled into separate fiber collimators and simultaneously injected into the sensor. This overcomes the inherent channel spacing limitations of conventional wavelength division multiplexers (WDMs) while avoiding wavelength-selective optical losses. The resonance tube and the cantilever exhibit independent resonance peaks at 938 Hz and 1216 Hz, respectively. Dual-gas signals are naturally decoupled by employing two independent resonance acoustic fields, whereby acoustic crosstalk between the channels and cross-interference between the target gases are rendered negligible. The minimum detection limits (MDLs) are 8.2 ppb for CO and 3.1 ppb for H 2 S. The corresponding normalized noise equivalent absorption (NNEA) co…

Digital intelligence, regulation and green growth: evidence from EU countries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on green growth within the context of the European Union. It explores how AI, alongside human capital and renewable energy consumption, influences sustainable development trajectories over time. Design/methodology/approach The analysis covers 27 EU member states over the period 1996–2024, using advanced panel econometric techniques. The correlated effects autoregressive distributed lag model is used to estimate both short- and longrun dynamics, while mean group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group and Augmented Mean Group estimators ensure robustness. Wavelet coherence analysis captures time-frequency variations, and Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality tests examine directional relationships among variables. Findings The results reveal a positive and statistically significant impact of AI on green growth in both the short and long run. Human capital also emerges as a key driver of green development. Surprisingly, renewable energy consumption exhibits a negative relationship with green growth across all model specifications, likely reflecting transitional inefficiencies in renewable infrastructure. Causality analysis indicates bidirectional links between green growth and both renewable energy and human capital, with unidirectional causality running from green growth to AI. Originality/value This study pro…

Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

Prediction on tensile mechanical properties of engineered cementitious composites using a fully automated deep learning method
abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting tensile mechanical properties of Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC), including tensile strength (TS) and ultimate tensile strain (UTS), remains challenging, particularly for the ultimate tensile strain, which exhibits high data dispersion that hinders reliable predictions. While machine learning (ML) has shown significant promise in predicting the mechanical properties of ECC, it faces several challenges: (1) limited predictive accuracy; (2) complexity and time-consuming nature of hyperparameter tuning; (3) insufficient research into predicting the UTS of ECC. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a fully automated deep learning model enhanced by Bayesian optimization for predicting the tensile mechanical properties of polyethylene fiber-reinforced engineered cementitious composites (PE-ECC). First, convolutional neural network (CNN) model was employed to enhance feature extraction and predictive accuracy. Second, Bayesian optimization was utilized to automatically construct the network and optimize various hyperparameters, resulting in an optimized network. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed Bayesian-optimized convolutional neural network (BO-CNN) method in predicting PE-ECC’s TS and UTS, utilizing a dataset of 154 experimental samples from published literature, achieving coefficients of determination (…

title: Machine learning-based performance prediction and Pareto optimization in 3D printing: a case study of PLA/Wood composites
abstract: Purpose This study uses machine learning to predict the performance of PLA/wood composites and identify suitable 3D printing parameters. The aim is to balance mechanical strength, material consumption, and processing requirements. Design/methodology/approach Experimental tensile and compressive strength data were used to develop second-order Ridge regression models. The models were validated using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) and then applied to predict mechanical performance across 3,125 combinations of five printing parameters: nozzle temperature, printing speed, layer height, infill density, and raster angle. Nominal material mass and relative processing burden were estimated for each configuration. Multi-objective Pareto optimization was used to identify trade-offs between mechanical performance and resource requirements. Findings The machine learning models achieved R2 values of 0.9954 for tensile strength and 0.9787 for compressive strength. Among the 3,125 configurations, 35 were identified as Pareto-optimal (1.12%). The selected best-compromise configuration had a nozzle temperature of 210 °C, a printing speed of 40 mm/s, a layer height of 0.15 mm, an infill density of 45%, and a raster angle of 0°. For this configuration, the models predicted a tensile strength of 22.38 MPa and a compressive strength of 33.75 MPa. Originality/value This study uses machine lea…

Explainable Machine Learning for Multi-Class Mental Stress Level Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of Ensemble and Conventional Models
abstract: Students’ and professionals’ mental stress has become one of the most serious public health issues; however, predictive models continue to be black boxes that do not get trusted by clinicians or teachers. In this research paper, we propose a comparison-based machine learning approach to solve the problem of classification of mental stress into three classes (Low, Moderate, High). Six machine learning algorithms such as Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM will be compared based on two feature spaces – all 20 features and the subset of 12 selected with the Mutual Information method. Evaluation was done based on the 1,100 samples survey dataset on psychological, physiological, social, environmental, and academic stressors. The best-performing single split was LightGBM, trained on features selected by the Mutual Information selection process, which resulted in an accuracy of 90.00%, Macro F1 score of 0.900, and Macro ROC-AUC of 0.987. It also showed the best mean cross-validation accuracy of 89.36% ± 0.84%. While tests show that the margin over Random Forest and Logistic Regression is directionally consistent but not statistically significant (as the number of samples is n = 5, therefore p > 0.05), it is statistically significant compared to XGBoost model (paired t-test, p = 0.011). To solve the problem of interpret…

title: Multicenter evaluation of radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for colorectal cancer diagnosis and survival prediction
abstract: Abstract Reliable preoperative classification and outcome prediction could improve management of locally advanced colorectal cancer. We retrospectively studied 879 participants from two centers, including 741 patients with locally advanced colorectal cancer and 138 with benign colorectal lesions. Clinical, radiomics, deep learning, and early fusion models were trained at center A ( n = 615) and independently tested at center B ( n = 264) using pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical data. The clinical-radiomics nomogram achieved a test AUC of 0.957 for benign-malignant classification. For 3-year and 5-year overall survival, radiomics achieved test AUCs of 0.874 and 0.898, while fusion achieved 0.870 and 0.899, respectively. These findings identify CT radiomics as a promising digital biomarker for colorectal cancer stratification and show that early deep learning fusion offers limited incremental value over an optimized radiomics baseline.

title: Deep ECG survival prediction for all-cause mortality under case-mix shift: discrimination, risk underestimation, and recalibration
abstract: Background Accurate mortality ranking does not establish reliable absolute-risk prediction when the clinical population changes. We examined discrimination, calibration, demographic increment, and recalibration of deep ECG survival prediction under case-mix shift. Methods A five-seed ECG-demographic discrete-time survival ensemble was developed using CODE-15% training (183,689 participants; 6,603 deaths), validation (22,974; 828), and internal-test cohorts (22,959; 825). Cross-release waveform hashing and lagged cross-correlation identified four duplicates in the Chagas-focused SaMi-Trop cohort; their exclusion left 1,627 participants and 104 deaths. The fixed models were assessed at 1 and 2 years using censoring-aware metrics, paired patient bootstrap intervals, training-only Cox references, and fivefold out-of-fold recalibration. Input-sensitivity analyses included patient-level uncertainty and numerically verified integrated gradients. Results The concordance index (C-index) decreased from 0.842 (95% CI 0.829–0.854) internally to 0.797 (0.757–0.836) externally, and 1-year area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) decreased from 0.862 to 0.818. External incremental discrimination over ECG-only was unresolved (C-index difference 0.011, − 0.025 to 0.049). At 2 years, mean external predicted mortality was 3.21% vs. 6.27% observed, with calibration-in-the-lar…

title: Independent risk factors and prediction model for tracheostomy in ICU patients: a Firth's penalized logistic regression analysis
abstract: Background Tracheostomy is critical airway management in intensive care unit (ICU) patients. However, the independent risk factors and prediction models remain unclear. Methods This retrospective multicenter cohort study with single-center external validation analyzed adult ICU patients from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) as the derivation cohort and 186 patients from Tianjin First Central Hospital as validation cohort. Firth's penalized logistic regression was adopted to screen independent risk factors for tracheostomy and construct the prediction model. Multicollinearity among candidate variables was evaluated using the variance inflation factor. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curves, and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test. In addition, the association between tracheostomy timing and in-hospital mortality was further explored through adjusted logistic regression models. Results A total of 12,926 patients were included in the derivation cohort [median age 65.00 years (IQR: 54.00–76.00); 56.74% male], of whom 200 (1.5%) underwent tracheostomy. Multivariate Firth's penalized logistic regression identified nine variables independently associated with tracheostomy: ARDS (OR = 3.331, 95% CI: 2.411–4.567), AKI (OR = 2.455, 95% CI: 1.765–3.379), sepsis (OR = 2.393, 95…

Exploring preoperative prediction of conversion in minimally invasive colorectal cancer surgery using Swedish and Danish national register data
abstract: Abstract Purpose Conversion of minimally invasive surgery often adds operative time and may lead to complications. The aim was to develop a preoperative prediction model for conversion and identify predictive risk factors in minimally invasive colorectal cancer resections, to be used in consideration and counselling preoperatively. Methods An observational study based on data from national Swedish registries (CRCBaSE, 2019–2021). Logistic regression models were used to predict conversion, with variable selection based on statistical performance. Model discrimination, calibration, and uncertainty were evaluated using the Brier score, AUC, calibration plots, and bootstrap resampling. External validation was performed in the Danish Colorectal Cancer Registry (2016–2020). Results Minimally invasive surgery was performed on 7,811 patients. Seven preoperative predictors were identified as risk factors of conversion: body mass index (BMI), clinical T stage, age, previous abdominal surgery, sex, robotic approach, and left-sided tumour location. Risk of conversion increased with advanced T stage, left-sided tumours, prior abdominal surgery, extremes of BMI, and age up to 80 years, whereas robotic surgery and female sex reduced the risk of conversion. A 7-variable model was created and achieved an AUC of 0.730 in the Swedish test set but demonstrated reduced discrimination and calibratio…

title: Explainable machine learning with multi-source data for community fire risk prediction
abstract: Fires pose a significant threat to citizens’ lives, property, and overall urban safety. While research has extensively focused on forest fire risk assessment and prediction, comparatively little attention has been given to evaluating fire danger in large metropolitan areas. This study integrates data from Yuncheng City, China – including building characteristics, road networks, population distribution, fire occurrence records, and meteorological parameters to facilitate a geographically informed analysis. Various machine learning models were trained to assess fire risk throughout the city. The findings demonstrate that the XGBoost model exhibits high predictive accuracy and strong spatial correlation, rendering it suitable for geographic analysis. This research identifies potential fire risks within urban areas, offering a scientific basis for the strategic deployment of firefighting resources and informed urban planning to mitigate losses of life and property.

Preoperative prediction of Ki-67 proliferation index in gliomas using multisequence and multi-regional radiomics with machine learning and deep learning integration
abstract: The Ki-67 proliferation index is an important biomarker for evaluating glioma aggressiveness but is conventionally determined by postoperative histopathological examination. We developed and internally validated a non-invasive framework integrating multisequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics, deep learning (DL) features, and clinical variables for preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression in gliomas. A total of 179 patients with pathologically confirmed primary glioma were retrospectively enrolled and randomly assigned to training ( n = 125) and internal validation ( n = 54) cohorts. Handcrafted radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral and multi-scale peritumoral regions on T1-weighted contrast-enhanced, T1FLAIR, and T2-weighted MRI, while high-level imaging features were generated using pre-trained convolutional neural networks. Selected imaging components were integrated with clinical variables to construct multimodal predictive models. The inclusion of peritumoral features showed potential value for improving radiomics-based prediction compared with intratumoral features alone. The multimodal integrated model achieved AUCs of 0.869 (95% CI, 0.803–0.934) and 0.849 (95% CI, 0.744–0.953) in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively, showing a higher observed AUC than the conventional machine learning, DNN-based, and transformer-based m…

title: Prediction of the distribution pattern of Limonium bicolor under climate change based on the Biomod2 ensemble model
abstract: Limonium bicolor (Bunge) Kuntze is a typical salt-alkali tolerant plant with significant medicinal value and ecological restoration functions. Progressive climate change can significantly alter the distribution patterns of species, threatening species survival and the sustainable utilization of plant resources. Predicting distribution shifts and species responses to climate change can provide a scientific basis for biodiversity conservation and management. In this study, we optimized the MaxEnt model using the ENMeval package and constructed an ensemble species distribution model based on the Biomod2 package. We analyzed changes in suitable habitats of L. bicolor under current and three future climate scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, SSP585), identified key environmental factors, and performed Multivariate Environmental Similarity Surface (MESS) and Most Dissimilar Variable (MoD) analyses. The results show that the ensemble model exhibits good prediction accuracy and stability, with AUC = 0.96 and TSS = 0.81. Annual precipitation (bio12) was identified as the dominant environmental factor. MESS and MoD analyses indicated low extrapolation risk of model predictions, with future temperature and precipitation acting as the main drivers of suitable habitat changes. Currently, suitable habitats of L. bicolor are mainly distributed in various provinces within the Yellow River Basin, includ…

title: Prediction of progression-free survival and risk stratification in advanced lung adenocarcinoma patients receiving EGFR-TKI therapy
abstract: Objective We aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and computed tomography (CT) findings associated with progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with stage IIIB–IV epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR )-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LAD) receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and to develop a model for PFS prediction and risk stratification. Materials and methods This retrospective study enrolled patients with stage IIIB–IV EGFR -mutant LAD who received TKI therapy and underwent pretreatment contrast-enhanced thoracic CT between January 2015 and April 2024. The Kaplan–Meier method was used to calculate the median survival time. The log-rank test was used to compare the differences in the survival curves between groups. The clinicoradiological findings associated with PFS were evaluated with a multivariate Cox regression model. The performance of the Cox regression model was assessed using the time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and Harrell’s concordance index ( C -index). Non-parametric bootstrapping with 1,000 resamples was performed as internal validation to evaluate the robustness and discriminative ability of the model. Results A total of 242 patients (102 men and 140 women) with a mean age of 61 ± 11 years were included. The median PFS was 13 months.
