Top management team AI attention and carbon emission in manufacturing: the moderating roles of green innovation and industry IT attention
abstract: Purpose This study draws on the attention-based view (ABV) to examine whether and when the artificial intelligence (AI) attention of top management team (TMT) affects manufacturers' carbon emissions. Building on the idea that attention processes are context-dependent, this study also explores the moderating roles of organizational-level characteristics (green innovation) and industry-level characteristics (industry IT attention). Design/methodology/approach This study collects data on publicly listed manufacturers in North America. This study uses fixed-effect models with endogeneity and selection bias adjustments. Findings This study finds that TMT AI attention is associated with lower carbon emissions in manufacturers. Greater green innovation and industry IT attention can also strengthen the relationship between TMT AI attention and lower carbon emissions. Originality/value This study provides one of the first empirical examinations of the relationship between these factors. This research contributes to extant responsible digital transformation literature by providing evidence that TMTs' attention to AI is associated with lower carbon emissions in manufacturers.

title: Spatio-temporal analysis of carbon balance in rice agroecosystems in tropical regions: a case study in Trenggalek Regency, Indonesia
Institutional environmental intelligence and high-carbon loans: an intellectual capital perspective on government biodiversity attention
abstract: Purpose As biodiversity governance becomes increasingly important for sustainable development, understanding how government-generated intangible knowledge influences financial decision-making remains an underexplored issue in intellectual capital (IC) research. Drawing on IC theory, this study conceptualizes government biodiversity attention (GBA) as institutional environmental intelligence and examines its effect on high-carbon loans (HCL). Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a novel GBA index using machine learning and text analysis of 5,726 Chinese local government work reports from 2003–2023. Using a panel dataset of 287 Chinese commercial banks from 2016–2023, this study employs fixed-effects regression models, instrumental variable estimation, propensity score matching (PSM), and placebo tests to examine how GBA influences HCL. Findings GBA is significantly negatively associated with HCL by financial institutions. This effect is more pronounced in cities with well-developed green finance systems and low-carbon pilot policies, among local commercial banks and banks actively engaged in green credit practices. Further channel analyses indicate that the relationship between GBA and HCL is associated with environmental constraints, capital adequacy, and bank risk-taking. Originality/value This study develops a novel machine learning-based measure of GBA and provi…

title: Institutional substitute or complement? A systematic scoping review of blockchain for carbon accounting and supply-chain environmental, social and governance data in emerging economies
abstract: Exporters in emerging economies face growing demands for verifiable greenhouse gas and environmental, social and governance (ESG) data from EU importers under the carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), domestic carbon pricing schemes and investors. Blockchain is often proposed as the infrastructure for these data, sometimes as a substitute for weak institutions. This study examines that claim. Following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR), 494 OpenAlex records were screened with AI assistance against predefined criteria, 239 studies were mapped and 53 empirical studies were synthesised using institutional theory, the natural-resource-based view and the technology-organisation-environment framework. A document analysis of Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia complemented the review. Models and technical designs dominate the field, empirical studies make up 22% of it, and none focuses on Vietnam. Adoption and outcomes are associated mainly with off-chain carbon data capability, cost and institutional conditions. Of 16 studies with findings relevant to institutions, 15 treat institutions as enabling conditions, and the only evidence resembling substitution concerns private governance by technology providers. Because the evidence is heterogeneous, mostly cross-sectional and coded largely from abstracts, this pattern is tentative. In the layered view proposed, block…

Interfacial Engineering of Highly Dispersed V2O3 Nanoparticles Confined in an Amorphous Carbon Framework Boosting Zn-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for advanced energy storage systems owing to their inherent safety and economic advantages, with vanadium-based compounds being extensively investigated as promising cathodes. However, their practical application is severely hampered by two key issues: the severe vanadium species dissolution and the sluggish Zn2+ diffusion dynamics. In this work, a composite of highly dispersed V2O3 nanoparticles confined in amorphous carbon is fabricated. It displays a high initial specific capacity of 623 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and maintains 170 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1 when used as an AZIB cathode, demonstrating a favorable electrochemical performance. The electrochemical behavior of the composite arises from the synergistic effects of its structural features. The carbon coating suppresses vanadium agglomeration and dissolution, while the uniformly dispersed V2O3 nanoparticles facilitate Zn2+ diffusion. Meanwhile, interfacial defects at the V2O3/carbon boundary promote charge-transfer kinetics and improve the overall electronic conductivity. This work offers a facile structural design route for the structural optimization and performance improvement of high-efficiency cathode materials for AZIBs.

title: DNA Sequence-Programmed Protein Coronas Determine Intracellular Fate and Proteostatic Stress of Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Abstract Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) show promise for optical biosensing, imaging, and drug delivery, but turning them into safe, precision nanomedicine tools requires understanding how nanotube surface chemistry dictates recognition and processing by cells. Like other nanomaterials, carbon nanotubes acquire a biomolecular corona on contact with biological fluids, and corona identity is increasingly recognized as central to sensor performance and drug delivery efficacy. However, whether corona identity also governs the intracellular fate of carbon nanotubes remains largely unknown. Here, we show that the single-stranded DNA wrapping of (6,5)-enriched single-walled carbon nanotubes reprograms their protein corona, intracellular trafficking, and macrophage response. By profiling (AT)15, (GT)15, and (CT)15 wrapped SWCNTs, we show that the wrapping sequence programs both the protein corona and the resulting proteostatic stress on macrophages. Photoluminescence imaging and confocal Raman measurements reported that (AT)15 is internalized the most yet leaves the proteome and nanotube structure largely undisturbed, whereas (CT)15, taken up the least, undergoes the most aggressive intracellular degradation and drives the highest oxidative and proteostatic stress. Corona proteomics indicated that all three tested nanotubes form coronas with distinct functional identities that…

title: Carbon Shell Encapsulated Highly Dispersed Nanocobalt via Biomass Precomplexation Cascade Carbonization for Multiscenario Organic Pollutant Purification
abstract: Abstract Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) are important for organic wastewater treatment but face challenges such as catalyst cost, limited scenarios, and stability. Using durian shell fibers to complex transition-metal ions, we constructed a biochar catalyst with carbon-coated active cobalt species (Co/DC-800) via impregnation-pyrolysis. The Co/DC-800/peroxymonosulfate (PMS) system rapidly degraded over 20 organic pollutants, including ofloxacin, under various conditions, showing stable performance across wide pH values, coexisting ions, and different water qualities. It could be recycled 30 times without activity loss and enabled continuous batch treatment in a purification column, demonstrating its practical potential. Theoretical calculations revealed dual active sites of zerovalent Co and amorphous CoO coactivating PMS, both spontaneously capturing PMS and generating multiple reactive oxygen species, while promoting high-valent cobalt formation, allowing combined oxidant action for rapid degradation in multiple scenarios. This study achieves efficient wastewater treatment while reducing catalyst cost, balancing performance, minimizing environmental impact, and adding value to waste biomass, thereby advancing water treatment technology.

title: Valuation of Carbon Stocks in Forest Area with Special Purpose Gunung Bromo: Efforts to Achieve Indonesia’s FOLU Net Sink 2030
abstract: Achieving the 2030 FOLU Net Sink target requires accurate carbon stock estimation and integrated forest health assessment. This study quantified carbon stocks in the Forest Area with Special Purpose (FASP) Gunung Bromo UNS using the USDA nested-plot design within assessing aboveground tree biomass, litter, understory vegetation, and necromass through tropical allometric equations. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) examined relationships between carbon stocks and environmental variables, including soil temperature, light intensity, air humidity, and soil pH. Dry secondary forest stored the highest carbon (57.79 tC/ha; 22,582.81 tC across 106.58 ha), followed by shrubland (36.79 tC/ha; 84.19 tC across 0.62 ha) and dryland agriculture (7.36 tC/ha; 487.59 tC across 18.07 ha). Higher stocks were associated with more stable microenvironmental conditions, while open and disturbed areas had lower stocks. These results underscore the need to protect secondary forests, restore shrublands, and strengthen agroforestry systems to support the implementation of FOLU Net Sink 2030.

title: Multicomponent Pt&Fe2P&CoP Supported on Nitrogen-Doped Carbon as an Ultra-Low Pt Catalyst for Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: Abstract Herein, a multicomponent Pt&Fe2P&CoP/NC catalyst with an ultra-low Pt loading (∼2 wt % Pt) for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is synthesized by two-step pyrolysis, where the nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) support is first formed from the pyrolysis of ZIF-8, carbon, and melamine; then Fe2P&CoP dual cocatalysts are introduced by the secondary pyrolysis. The conductive carbon component integrated within the NC matrix facilitates charge transport across the heterointerfaces, enabling efficient electron delivery from Fe2P and CoP toward the adjacent Pt sites. Such interfacial charge redistribution modulates the binding strength of oxygen-containing intermediates adsorbed over Pt surfaces. Moreover, Fe2P&CoP also provide metal P and act together with Pt as the active sites. Benefiting from the multicomponent of Pt, Fe2P, CoP, and NC, Pt&Fe2P&CoP/NC exhibits an outstanding ORR performance in 0.1 M KOH: a peak potential of 0.929 V (vs RHE), a half-wave potential of 0.891 V (vs RHE), a Tafel slope of 74.76 mV dec−1, and a nearly direct 4e reaction pathway.

title: A Review of Activated Carbon-Based Materials and Their Performance Tipping Points for Application in CO2 Capture with Future Outlook
abstract: Abstract Carbon capture technologies have been increasingly demanded to achieve the commitments in the Paris Agreement of capturing 10 Gt CO2 per year. This review examines the many facets of activated carbons for CO2 capture applications. Activated carbons are popular research materials for CO2 capture applications because of their high surface area, tunable surface characteristics, and widely available feedstocks. Additionally, activated carbon can be deployed at low temperatures and pressures in fixed bed applications. The analysis reveals a range of “tipping points” that we define as the optimal parameters to maximize performance. The first tipping point is that the optimal average pore size for amine-supported carbons is 10 nm, including cyclic stability. Amine-supported carbons with average pores <2 nm perform poorly in all CO2 benchmarking criteria, whereas materials with average pore sizes >10 nm exhibit limited cyclic stability. Amine-supported carbons also exhibit a tipping point with respect to regeneration temperature. As regeneration temperature exceeds 315 K, the net CO2 capacity retention declines by as much as 12%. Tipping points are also observed in relation to adsorption temperature and amine weight loading. For the best-performing combinations of amines supported on mesoporous carbon, the optimum CO2 adsorption temperature is between 70 and 80 °C. An am…

Measures, Evolutions, and Determinants of Green Efficiency: Evidence from China
abstract: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as an undesirable output. It then traces the temporal evolution and city-size distribution of green efficiency and examines the factors associated with its variation using two-way fixed-effects models. The analysis further tests whether the relationships of economic openness and economic development with green efficiency differ systematically across city-size tiers. The results show that the national mean VRS green-efficiency score is 0.736 and that efficiency follows a non-monotonic pattern across city sizes, with megacities recording the highest average level and large and medium-sized cities exhibiting relatively lower levels. Over time, green efficiency displays marked fluctuations rather than a sustained upward trajectory. The cross-tier pattern is also sensitive to returns-to-scale assumptions, as the relative VRS advantage of small cities disappears under the constant-returns-to-scale specification. In the second-stage analysis, economic openness is positively associated with green efficiency at the national level, while economic development shows no uniform independent association. Their interaction is positive and significant, indicating…

title: Financial Literacy Calibration and Retail Investor Behavior on Digital Trading Platforms: A Literature Review
abstract: The number of young retail investors in Indonesia has surged while capital market literacy remains low, making the role of financial literacy in curbing investor bias a central issue in financial management. This article maps evidence on financial literacy, self-confidence, and retail investor behavior on digital trading platforms and proposes a conceptual framework. An integrative literature review was conducted on 29 sources: 18 empirical or analytical studies, seven reviews or meta-analyses, two theoretical or methodological references, and two contextual data sources. The synthesis shows that the role of literacy in reducing bias is not uniform because it depends on the type of bias and on how literacy is measured; confidence in one's own knowledge can raise market participation as well as trading intensity; and platform design shapes behavior, especially among investors with low literacy. As a conceptual contribution, the article proposes a Literacy–Confidence–Platform (L-K-P) framework centered on the calibration gap between objective literacy and confidence, accompanied by six testable propositions. Future research should combine objective literacy tests with actual transaction data and field experiments on investment platforms in Indonesia.

title: Porous carbon-based materials for electrochemical CO 2 capture by supercapacitive swing adsorption
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical supercapacitive swing adsorption (SSA) is an emerging low-energy CO2 capture technology that couples reversible charge storage with electrically driven CO2 uptake and release. Porous carbon electrodes are central to SSA because they govern charge storage, ion adsorption and transport, and interfacial CO2 enrichment, thereby determining capture performance. However, the relationships between carbon structure, interfacial electrochemistry, and CO2 capture mechanisms remain poorly understood. This review provides a carbon-centered perspective on SSA. First, the fundamentals of SSA, including cell configurations, electrode materials, and proposed capture mechanisms, are summarized, with particular attention to the evolution of carbon electrodes from commercial porous carbons to tailored porous carbons, quinone-functionalized carbons, and covalent organic framework-based composites. Then, emerging structure–performance relationships and derived empirical design principles for SSA electrodes are discussed, focusing on the influence of surface area, pore architecture, and surface chemistry on CO2 capture capacity, kinetics, and energy consumption. Finally, key challenges and opportunities in mechanistic understanding, material and device design, evaluation under realistic conditions, integration of CO2 capture with utilization, and technoeconomic analysis and …

title: A two-phase flow model for low-permeability reservoirs coupling imbibition–displacement dynamics with water-injection-induced fractures
abstract: Abstract High-pressure water injection into low-permeability tight sandstone reservoirs generates cyclic dynamic fractures that enhance flow capacity but risk inducing water channeling. Existing models assume static fractures and a single capillary-pressure curve, and so cannot capture the imbibition-displacement competition operating throughout water injection. Here we combine an embedded discrete fracture model with dual capillary-pressure and relative-permeability models that distinguish imbibition from displacement, yielding an oil-water two-phase flow model coupled to dynamic fracture evolution. Fracture initiation follows the Irwin stress-intensity-factor criterion, fracture geometry and flow properties are updated through an exponential stress-sensitivity equation, and the matrix-fracture equations are solved by a fully implicit finite-difference method. Validation against three core experiments reproduces the multi-peak fluctuation and multi-stage breakthrough of the injection pressure, with a computed breakthrough pressure of 3.0–4.5 MPa matching measurements. Induced fractures shorten the injection-production balance time from 153 to 68 min. An optimal fracture-length interval exists: displacement recovery reaches 61.58% at two-thirds of the fully penetrating length but falls to 40% once the fracture fully penetrates and induces channeling, while the shut-in imbibitio…

title: Chitooligosaccharide–adipose-derived stem cell exosome complex promotes diabetic wound healing through macrophage-mediated immune–vascular coupling
abstract: Background Persistent inflammation and impaired angiogenesis are major contributors to delayed diabetic wound healing. This study investigated whether a chitooligosaccharide–adipose-derived stem cell exosome composite system (Exo-COS) promotes diabetic wound repair through macrophage-mediated immune–vascular communication. Methods ADSC-derived exosomes (ADSC-Exos) were isolated, characterized, and combined with COS to prepare Exo-COS. Under high-glucose conditions, the effects of Exo-COS on macrophage inflammatory–reparative status and migration were evaluated. Macrophage-conditioned medium (MCM) was subsequently used to assess endothelial migration and tube formation. The therapeutic effects were further evaluated in a diabetic rat wound model by histological, immunohistochemical, and wound-healing analyses. Results Exo-COS reduced macrophage CCR7, IL-6, and iNOS expression while increasing Arg-1 and IL-10 expression and enhancing macrophage migration. Exo-COS-treated macrophage-conditioned medium produced the strongest enhancement of endothelial migration and tube formation. In vivo , Exo-COS decreased CCR7 expression, increased Arg-1 expression and CD31-positive microvessel density, promoted collagen deposition and tissue reconstruction, and accelerated wound closure. Conclusion Exo-COS promotes diabetic wound healing by improving macrophage inflammatory–reparative status an…

title: Awakening Latent Diradicals to Enhance Antiferromagnetic Coupling between Localized Organic Spin Centers
abstract: Abstract Connecting persistent radicals through π-conjugated linkers provides a promising route for developing organic magnetic systems. However, the simultaneous realization of localized addressable spins and thermally robust antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling remains challenging. Conventional approaches based on quinoidal versus aromatic resonance forms impose electronic constraints that limit access to this regime. Here, we introduce a molecular design principle in which the latent open-shell character of selected heterocyclic linkers is activated to significantly strengthen AFM interactions between localized radical centers. First-principles calculations reveal that this enhancement: i) originates from increased linker spin polarization acting synergistically with partial quinoidalization, and ii) is robust across a series of diradicals combining an expandable family of linkers with representative persistent radicals. We identify diradicals displaying pronounced open-shell character with unusually large singlet–triplet energy gaps typically associated with closed-shell systems. Extending this concept to two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks, we further show that our approach translates from discrete molecules to strongly AFM materials.

title: Real-Time Academic Platform Integration Design (RAPID): A Descriptive Framework for Course Communication and Support
abstract: Abstract Persistent, channel-organized communication environments give instructors ways to arrange questions, assistance, announcements, and informal interaction alongside a learning management system. Their use depends on how students enter the environment, how information and audiences are organized, who provides assistance, and how participation is experienced. This conceptual article presents Real-Time Academic Platform Integration Design (RAPID), a descriptive framework developed through a focused synthesis of 37 publications and a source-anchored matrix of 750 evidence items. Following a bounded literature search with artificial intelligence support for screening and extraction, the authors reviewed source evidence and selected and refined the framework by comparing model-generated alternatives. RAPID comprises four components: Student Onboarding, Environment Organization, Sustainable Help, and Student Participation and Social Climate, interpreted through an affordance perspective and Community of Inquiry. A constructed LMS-centered baseline, two reflective teaching illustrations, and a literature-informed projection show how it applies across differences in course size, staffing, and participation requirements. The framework’s usefulness, workload implications, and relationship to learning require empirical study.

title: Design Optimization of Surface Ionization Detectors for Quantitative Online Alkali Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Real-time measurements of alkali species are important in thermochemical conversion processes, where Na- and K-containing compounds influence reaction chemistry, bed agglomeration, deposition, and corrosion. Surface ionization detectors (SIDs) have long provided a simple approach to online alkali monitoring, but most reported SIDs have remained semiquantitative because internal transport and ion-collection processes are insufficiently understood. Here, a reconfigurable SID was used to determine how detector orientation, filament placement, and collector design control the response, with the aim of establishing design principles and selecting a configuration for more quantitative measurements. Experiments were interpreted using computational fluid dynamics and a first-order electrostatic model. The results distinguish two coupled processes: buoyancy-driven transport of neutral alkali to the hot Pt filament and subsequent electrostatic ion collection. Among the configurations investigated, horizontal operation with a dead-leg insert, an axially mounted filament, and a grounded plate collector provided the best balance of sensitivity, stability, baseline recovery, and practical operability. Under identical KCl pulse conditions, this configuration produced an approximately fourfold higher plateau response than the earlier SID configuration. Calibration with eight common Na…

title: Exact reconstruction of a hyperbolic-cosine bounce in f(G,T) gravity: Cosmography, energy conditions and matter content
abstract: Standard big-bang cosmology, traced backward in time, ends in an initial singularity. This problem motivates bouncing scenarios, in which the Universe contracts to a finite minimum size and then expands again smoothly. We investigate whether such a non-singular bounce can be realized in [Formula: see text] gravity, where the gravitational Lagrangian depends on the Gauss–Bonnet invariant G and on the trace T of the energy-momentum tensor. On a flat FLRW background, we derive the effective density and pressure of the theory, the corresponding energy conditions, and the modified matter conservation law, and we show how the cosmographic parameters enter the energy conditions. For the exact bounce [Formula: see text], the field equations give [Formula: see text], independently of the model, so the effective null energy condition is necessarily violated. We then reconstruct [Formula: see text] directly from this background. The modified Friedmann equation becomes a linear second-order differential equation, which we solve in closed form in vacuum and for a linear coupling [Formula: see text] to dust that obeys the modified conservation law. The resulting Lagrangian makes the bounce an exact solution of both Friedmann equations, while the dust itself satisfies all matter energy conditions. Inclusive leadership and creative behavior: the role of employee energy
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between inclusive leadership and employees’ creative behavior, focusing on the mediating role of employee energy. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, it considers employee energy as a complementary resource-based explanation of this relationship. Design/methodology/approach The research is based on quantitative data collected from 278 employees working in city hotels in Turkey. Data were gathered through face-to-face surveys using a convenience sampling method. The analysis was conducted using SPSS 27 and AMOS 26, and the proposed relationships, including the mediating effect, were tested through PROCESS Macro (Model 4). Findings Inclusive leadership was positively associated with employee energy and creative behavior. Employee energy was also positively associated with creative behavior, and the mediation analysis indicated a significant indirect association through employee energy. The direct association remained significant, consistent with partial mediation. Originality/value This study extends research on inclusive leadership and creativity by examining employee energy as a resource-based explanatory mechanism. While previous studies have largely emphasized psychological safety and other relational or motivational mechanisms, the findings show that employees’ energetic resources also help explain how inclusive leadershi…

title: Conceptualizing the integration potential of creative industries: a systematic literature review
abstract: Despite growing scholarly interest in creative industries as drivers of innovation, territorial competitiveness, and international cooperation, their integration potential remains insufficiently conceptualized as an independent analytical category. Existing research is characterized by fragmented theoretical perspectives and the absence of coherent frameworks for explaining integration processes and outcomes. This study systematically reviews and conceptually synthesizes the literature on the integration potential of creative industries. Following the PRISMA protocol, the review analyzes 66 peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. The analysis addresses six research questions covering conceptualizations of integration, integration mechanisms, regional and cross-border dimensions, methodological approaches, measurement indicators, and research gaps. The findings demonstrate that integration potential has not yet been established as a distinct analytical category in the academic literature. Instead, integration processes are primarily interpreted through related concepts, including networks, clustering, institutional coordination, innovation ecosystems, and spatial connectivity. Economic, institutional, and network-based integration mechanisms dominate the literature, while qualitative and case-oriented research designs prevail, with measurement approaches…

title: Biomimetic Humidity Deformation Enables COF/PVA Actuators with Self-Powered Sensing Integration
abstract: Abstract Environment-responsive flexible devices are essential for intelligent sensing and microactuation, but integrating actuation and sensing functions simultaneously remains challenging. Inspired by pinecone hygroscopic deformation, a COF/PVA-based humidity-responsive device integrating mechanical actuation, self-powering, and sensing at the material level was developed. The hydrogen-bonded interpenetrating network enhances moisture adsorption, structural stability, and ion transport. The optimized composite exhibits large, rapid, and reversible bending from 20% to 95% relative humidity (RH), good cycling stability over 50 cycles and 15 days, and a near-linear bending angle–RH relationship. Humidity-triggered ion migration and interfacial charge separation enable stable self-powered sensing without external power. Mechanistically, multiscale water evolution from molecular adsorption (≈−0.48 eV) to water clusters and films (≈−3.02 eV) drives stress amplification and efficient charge transport. Applications in smart curtains and noncontact switches demonstrate its potential for passive, self-driven integrated flexible systems.

title: Environmental Sustainability in Pakistan: The Role of Natural Resource Rent, Foreign Direct Investment, and Renewable Energy
abstract: For decades, environmental degradation has become a universal challenge, and for sustainable environmental quality requires an accurate and broader proxy for proper assessment. Pakistan faces serious environmental challenges due to rising emissions, rapid urbanization and heavy reliance on fossil fuels. Several studies used carbon and methane emissions to analyze the global warming issues, these measures provide only a partial view of environmental quality. Therefore, the current study examines the effect of foreign direct investment, renewable energy consumption and natural resources rent on ecological footprint by applying the ARDL-ECM model to Pakistan’s yearly data from 1985 to 2024. The empirical findings show that among all explanatory variables, renewable energy consumption has a significant negative impact on the ecological footprint, indicating that higher use of renewable energy helps reduce environmental pressure. Whereas natural resource rent and FDI have contributed positively to ecological footprint. Finally, the results suggest that increasing renewable energy consumption is the most effective way to reduce environmental pressure in Pakistan's economy. Keywords: Environmental degradation, Ecological footprint, overshoot.

Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems. II. Application to Gaia epoch astrometry of nearby pulsating and convective red giants
abstract: The interpretation of high-precision astrometry for intrinsically variable stars remains challenging, particularly for unresolved binary systems containing asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars. In such systems, large-amplitude pulsations and evolving convective surface structures induce time-dependent photocenter displacements that perturb the observed orbital motion. At the same time, Gaia Data Release 4 and 5 (DR4/DR5) epoch astrometry offers the prospect of deriving accurate orbital solutions and parallaxes for nearby unresolved AGB binaries. We investigate whether Gaia DR4/DR5 epoch astrometry can reliably recover orbital and astrometric parameters for unresolved AGB binaries in the presence of pulsations and convection-induced photocenter variability. Building upon the variability-induced mover (VIM) framework, we extended the astrometric model for unresolved evolved binaries by combining Keplerian photocenter motion, pulsation-induced flux-dependent photocenter shifts, and convection-induced photocenter motion. In the forward simulations, convection was represented either by stochastic photocenter displacements drawn from an exponential correlation function or by photocenter time series extracted from three-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. We then tested a retrieval framework that fits the orbital and VIM signal while incorporating a red-noise covariance mat…

title: FROM DESIGN TO CONSENSUS: EVALUATING A MOBILE LEARNING MODEL USING THE FUZZY DELPHI METHOD
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate expert consensus on the constructs and elements of a mobile learning model for secondary school science education in Malaysia. The study formed part of a Type II Design and Development Research (DDR) project, focusing on the model development phase. The proposed model specification was derived from a preceding modified Nominal Group Technique (mNGT) stage involving nine experts. Subsequently, the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM) was employed to determine the extent of expert consensus on the proposed model constructs and elements. Thirteen experts assessed 47 units comprising six constructs and 41 elements using a seven-point agreement scale. The analysis involved 611 expert ratings and applied triangular fuzzy numbers, threshold distances, expert consensus percentages, and defuzzification scores. The findings showed that all 47 assessment units satisfied the acceptance criteria applied in the study. All six constructs achieved 100% expert consensus, while consensus for the 41 elements ranged from 92.31% to 100%. Mean threshold distances ranged from 0.046 to 0.064 for constructs and from 0.034 to 0.110 for elements. The model specification encompasses mobile-learning pedagogy, scientific literacy incorporating Habits of Mind, students' digital literacy, technology integration, science learning assessment and monitoring, and implementation support. Embracing the challenges of urban biodiversity conservation and regeneration in Australasia: insights from the Urban Biodiversity and Design International Network 2025 conference
abstract: Abstract Urban biodiversity research has historically been concentrated in Europe and North America, leaving a significant knowledge gap in regions facing some of the most acute biodiversity challenges and containing some of the fastest-growing cities on Earth. This paper introduces the Urban Ecosystems special issue and outlines the outcomes and future directions emerging from the ninth Urban Biodiversity and Design International Network (URBIO) 2025 conference, held in Perth, Western Australia — the first URBIO conference specifically oriented toward the Australasian context. Drawing on presentations and discussions from 93 participants across eleven countries, we identify key patterns in urban biodiversity research, planning, and landscape architecture practice across Australia, New Zealand, and the broader Australasian region. We argue that Australasia presents a critical frontier for urban biodiversity scholarship: its cities are expanding into landscapes of extraordinary endemic richness, including globally recognised biodiversity hotspots such as Southwest Australia and the forests of East Australia, Polynesia-Micronesia, and Aotearoa New Zealand, while simultaneously confronting accelerating habitat loss, invasive species pressure, and climate change. The conference revealed the vitality of emerging Australasian research communities and the urgent need for deeper intern…

title: Water Tunnel Design Development Using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) DualSPHysics Analysis
abstract: Water tunnels serve as cost-effective alternatives to wind tunnels for aerodynamic testing, offering key advantages in flow visualization due to higher fluid density and lower required free-stream velocity [1][2]. This study presents the design development of a low-speed hydrostatic water tunnel evaluated through Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis using DualSPHysics software, which employs the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method [3]. Six geometric design variants were evaluated based on modifications to contraction geometry, test section length, outlet diameter reduction, and honeycomb flow straighteners. Evaluation criteria included velocity profile uniformity, turbulence intensity, and Root Mean Square Velocity (RMSV) deviation within the test section [4]. Design 5 — featuring an outlet diameter reduction from 5 cm to 2 cm with a 1-meter test section and 1 meter test section length achieved the lowest turbulence intensity at 14% (XY plane) and 17% (YZ plane), the highest flow uniformity at 85.11%, and minimum RMSV deviation of 0.002 m/s. Validation was conducted via Ahmed Body CFD benchmark comparison and physical particle velocity tracking from experimental footage, yielding accuracy levels of 75–92%. Non-dimensional Reynolds Number analysis confirmed dynamic similarity equivalence with full-scale wind tunnel testing conditions at standard vehicle operating…

Parametric design selection and ambient experimental assessment of a beryllium-copper spiral flexure spring for long-life Stirling cryocooler compressors
abstract: Free-piston Stirling cryocoolers require flexure suspensions that combine low axial stiffness, high radial stiffness, modal separation, manufacturability and long cyclic endurance. This study reports a constrained, one-factor-at-a-time parametric screening procedure for a three-arm spiral flexure disc, followed by ambient experimental assessment of the selected design. Six candidate alloys (AISI 302, AISI 304, Be-Cu C17000, Be-Cu C17200 TH, Ti-6Al-4V and AMPCOLOY® 944) and five geometric variables (arm count, spiral-cut width, sweep angle, disc thickness and disc diameter) were screened using nonlinear static structural, modal and stress-life finite element analyses in ANSYS® Workbench, with photo-etch manufacturability treated as a hard feasibility constraint. The selected configuration was Be-Cu C17200 TH, three arms, 0.6 mm cut width, 0.7 mm disc thickness, 560° sweep, 69 mm diameter and ±5 mm design stroke. For the selected design, analytical, numerical and experimental axial stiffness values were 1495.00, 1451.45 and 1460.25 N/m, respectively; the three routes agreed within 3%, while FEA and experiment differed by 0.6%. Measured and predicted strain agreed within 3%–7% across the stroke. An ambient fatigue campaign reached 100,755,000 fully reversed cycles at ±5 mm and 50 Hz without detected crack initiation, exceeding the adopted 10 8 -cycle run-out criterion by 0.76%. Th…

title: Design, Synthesis, and Antifungal Evaluation of Novel Pyridine-3-amide Derivatives Containing Phenylthiazole Moiety as Potential Succinate Dehydrogenase Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract In search of novel succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor fungicides (SDHIs) for the management of plant fungal diseases, 29 novel pyridine-3-amide derivatives containing a phenylthiazole moiety were designed and synthesized. Among them, compound H18 showed the strongest antifungal activity against B. cinerea, with an EC50 value of 0.06 μg/mL, substantially lower than that of boscalid (1.79 μg/mL). Spearman’s correlation analysis revealed no cross-resistance between H18 and boscalid (ρ = −0.1743, P = 0.6082). Moreover, H18 exhibited strong protective and curative efficacy of 79.98% and 75.57%, respectively, against B. cinerea on tomatoes at a concentration of 100 μg/mL, superior to that of boscalid. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that H18 inhibited SDH activity, leading to ROS accumulation, disruption of mitochondrial energy metabolism, and fungal cell death. Molecular docking suggested that the flexible conformations of the phenylthiazole moiety in H18 may contribute to its potential resistance-overcoming capacity. These findings identify H18 as a promising new SDHI candidate for B. cinerea control, warranting further investigation.

Baseline Functional Capacity and Activities of Daily Living Among Geriatrics in Nairobi, Kenya: A Pre-Intervention Assessment for an Integrated Virtual Reality Physical Activity Programme
abstract: Purpose: The global increase in the population of older adults has led to a significant rise in age-related functional decline, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Kenya. In Nairobi, older adults in institutional care settings are especially vulnerable to reduced functional capacity due to sedentary lifestyles and limited access to engaging and structured physical activity programs. Before evaluating the effectiveness of an integrated virtual reality (VR)-enhanced physical activity program, it was critical to establish the baseline functional capacity and activities of daily living (ADL) of this demographic. Materials and Methods: This study adopted a quasi-experimental research design involving a control group and an experimental group. A total of 42 older adults participated in the baseline assessment, comprising 19 participants in the control group and 23 participants in the experimental group. Participants were assessed at baseline using functional capacity measures including handgrip strength, Five-Times Sit-to-Stand Test (5TSTS), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and De Morton Mobility Index (DEMMI). Data were analyzed using independent samples t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests to establish group equivalence. Statistical significance was determined at p < 0.05. Biosystematic studies of selected Croton species (Euphorbiaceae) from southern peninsular India
abstract: The comparative evaluation of the four Croton species demonstrated a strong correlation between their morphological, anatomical and phytochemical characteristics, highlighting their taxonomic significance and potential pharmacological value. The selected four Croton species were Croton aromaticus L., Croton caudatus Geiseler, Croton persimilis Müll.Arg. and Croton zeylanicus Müll.Arg. Morphological identification and detailed examination of different plant parts were carried out using a LABOMED CSM2 stereo microscope, while anatomical analyses were performed employing standard histological techniques with a LABOMED CXL PLUS compound microscope. Phytochemical profiling of the selected taxa was conducted through preliminary qualitative phytochemical screening and high-performance thin layer chromatography (HPTLC). Among the species studied, C. caudatus exhibited distinct morphological characteristics compared to the other three species. Phytochemical analysis revealed a higher concentration of secondary metabolites in the leaves than in the stem and root tissues. High-performance thin layer chromatography profiling indicated a comparatively higher abundance of phytocompounds in C. aromaticus, whereas lower quantities were detected in C. caudatus and C. zeylanicus. Likewise, species sharing similar anatomical characteristics often display comparable phytochemical profiles, suggest…

title: The Maize Pan-NLRome: a comprehensive atlas of immune receptor diversity across the NAM founder lines
abstract: Background Nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) proteins serve as the primary intracellular receptors in the plant immune system. However, the extreme variability of NLR genes limits the utility of single reference genomes for capturing species-wide immune diversity. Methods Here, we constructed a gold-standard consensus maize pan-NLRome using high-quality assemblies of 26 Nested Association Mapping (NAM) founder lines and systematically integrated our data with three published landmarks to resolve previous architectural conflicts. By transitioning to a 50-kb flanking extension combined with genome-wide BRAKER4 high-precision gene prediction, we identified a total of 3,019 ZmNLR genes. Results Our re-evaluated OrthoFinder clustering resolved past contradictions, delineating 140 orthogroups of which 39 (27.9%) constitute the strict Core present in all 26 genomes; Core and Soft-Core orthogroups jointly retain 66.9% of the clustered NLR genes (2,014/3,012), whereas the Shell and Cloud compartments (54.3% of orthogroups) form the dispensable reservoir that drives adaptive variation. This "two-speed" evolution suggests that maize maintains a vast, dispensable adaptive reservoir to combat diverse pathogens. Phylogenetic and syntenic analyses of the line Oh7B, which carries a chromosome 9/10 rearrangement, revealed a chromosome 10 NLR repertoire that is orthologous to that of …

title: The Invisual Power of the Visible in Raymond Depardon’s Urgences and Jorge Pelicano’s Suddenly my Thoughts Halt
abstract: When it comes to filming patients in the specific context of their psychiatric institution, observing and subsequently constructing a visual point of view becomes a demanding process. Through a particular way of using the camera as a tool to embody a living experience from this setting, French photographer and director Raymond Depardon and Portuguese filmmaker Jorge Pelicano go beyond merely documenting the Hôtel Dieu and Conde Ferreira Hospitals. The grief that emanates from their images concerns the whole of society as they are manifestations of a concrete, yet universal language of suffering. For this reason, they offer a vantage point on how these filmmakers have experienced this environment beyond themselves, embracing Henri Cartier-Bresson’s conception of the camera as a confessor in a self-knowing process. They share a way of seeing the visible dimensions of these psychiatric environments, opening a space in which the viewer might consider the visual and invisual dynamics of the vision they wish to convey.

title: Plant-eating machines: cranial performance and feeding behaviour in sauropodomorpha
abstract: Abstract The evolution of sauropodomorph skulls involved major shifts in cranial architecture, feeding mechanics, and ecological strategies. Here, we integrate finite element analysis, safety-factor estimation, relative bite force, and gape modelling within a standardised framework to compare the early sauropodiform Yizhousaurus sunae , the diplodocid Diplodocus carnegii , and the macronarians Camarasaurus lentus and Sarmientosaurus musacchioi . Y. sunae exhibited the highest relative bite force but also high extrinsic stresses and the most restricted gape, indicating that force transmission and structural robustness were partly decoupled. D. carnegii produced a high absolute bite-force output but the lowest relative bite force and showed pronounced sensitivity to vertical and lateral loading. The two sampled macronarians generally exhibited lower stresses and higher safety margins, although their gape capacities differed. These broad performance differences persisted after surface-area scaling and recalculation of taxon-specific bite forces, indicating that model size alone does not explain the recovered patterns. Rather than supporting a linear progression towards greater robustness, the results reveal distinct functional configurations and a broader diversification of the sauropodomorph feeding apparatus.

title: Predicting individual tree height in natural Pinus yunnanensis forests: a comparison of generalizability between parametric mixed-effects models and data-driven random forest
abstract: Accurate tree height prediction in natural forests requires integrating heterogeneous factors and capturing nonlinear relationships. We compared nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) and random forest (RF) models for predicting individual-tree height of natural Pinus yunnanensis , identified key predictors, and explored pathways for integrating the two frameworks. We used data from 4,106 trees in 413 permanent plots in Yunnan Province, China, and included variables representing site quality, stand density and competition, stand structure, and climate; plots were split into training and independent test sets at a 70:30 ratio. The NLME model (based on the Hossfeld IV equation with plot-level random effects) included three statistically significant predictors: diameter at breast height (DBH), dominant height ( H d ), and temperature difference (TD). A full-variable RF (RF_full) used all features, whereas a reduced RF (RF_reduced) used the same three predictors to separate algorithm effects from variable-selection effects. Although both RF models fitted the training data better than the NLME model, this advantage did not transfer to independent plots: on the test set, the NLME model (RMSE = 1.66 m, MAE = 1.27 m, MAPE = 14.87%) achieved accuracy nearly identical to that of RF_full (1.66 m, 1.27 m, 14.86%) despite using only three predictors, clearly outperformed RF_reduced (1.75 m, 1.36 m,…

title: Neoliberalism And The Desubjectivized Subject: Power, Identity, And The Hollowing Of The Self
abstract: Neoliberalism is not just about the economy. It is a system that slowly strips people of their ability to act freely. It weakens their interior lives, vitality, and freedom is redefined into something more akin to the market. In today’s world, people are also encouraged to use their freedom to climb the economic ladder by building social capital, working harder, managing their time more efficiently, and making “smart” choices based on data and performance metrics, even when those choices aren’t truly free. The neoliberal subject lives in a world where neoliberal ideological formation has done deep cultural work doesn’t just affect policies, it also shapes how we think, limit our ability to dream that another world is possible. Neoliberalism, in this sense, doesn’t just manage the world, it manages our imaginations. Drawing on thinkers such as Michel Foucault, Patric Plesa, Byung-Chul Han, Shoshana Zuboff, and others, the paper examines how neoliberalism fosters a distinct kind of individual, one who relinquishes political power, transforms their inner life into a means of performance, and trades genuine autonomy for market-driven self-management, performing, and conforming within systems shaped by algorithms, debt, and surveillance. Drawing on political theory, sociology, and cultural analysis, explains how neoliberalism reshapes people into economic tools, while erasing the fo…

Genetic diversity and nutritional profiling of Moringa oleifera Lam. half-sib progenies
abstract: Moringa oleifera Lam. ("Miracle tree") is a multi-purpose tropical bioresource valued for combating malnutrition. However, systematic evaluations monitoring proximate principles and mineral concentrations across wild genotypes during early nursery establishment remain limited. This study evaluated the nutritional profiles, proximate principles and biomass determinants of 35 half-sib genotypes collected from wild populations across five sub-Himalayan Indian states after one year of nursery growth. Mature seeds from seven geographical sources were evaluated to be deploying randomised block design. Leaf samples were analysed for total amino acids (TAA), proximate principles and 10 essential macro- and micro-minerals. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed significant variation across all genotypes. Progeny P7 demonstrated target superiority, recording peak values for crude protein CP (27.49 %), TAA (19.12 %), nitrogen (N, 4397.87 mg/100 g) and zinc (Zn, 3.87 mg/100 g). Progeny P18 excelled in iron accumulation (49.60 mg/100 g), while P22 peaked in total ash (10.39 %) and phosphorus (P, 74.68 mg/100 g). Comparative values of phenotypic coefficient of variation (PCV) were higher than genotypic coefficient of variation (GCV) confirming strong genetic control. High broad-sense heritability and genetic advance were evaluated for crude fat, fibre, P, Zn, sulphur (S), iron (Fe) and mangan…

The use of virtual reality in the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder because of sexual abuse – a scoping review
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the current evidence on virtual reality (VR)-based psychological interventions for treating post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) resulting from sexual abuse. Given the high prevalence, clinical complexity and treatment resistance often observed in this population, the review assesses the effectiveness, feasibility and limitations of VR-assisted therapies and identifies gaps for future research. Design/methodology/approach The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Comprehensive searches were performed across 11 electronic databases and additional sources up to October 2023, without restrictions on language or publication date. Eligible studies included adult participants diagnosed with PTSD because of sexual abuse who received a VR-based psychological intervention. Data extraction and study selection were performed independently by multiple reviewers, and findings were synthesized descriptively. Findings From 49,245 records screened, two primary experimental studies and 13 review articles met the inclusion criteria. Interventions involved VR exposure therapy and VR-assisted imagery rescripting. Overall, VR-based approaches showed potential for reducing PTSD symptoms and were generally acceptable to participants. title: Emergency department ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter insertion training with virtual reality
abstract: Background: Ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter (USG-PIVC) insertion is a challenging skill for emergency department (ED) clinicians to master. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising, cost-effective tool for procedural training. Unlike manikins or phantoms, VR enables immersive, repeatable and scalable training with real-time feedback, simulating real ED conditions to improve skill transfer and learner engagement. However, its use in USG-PIVC education within EDs has not been evaluated despite persistent training barriers to USG-PIVC insertion in this setting. Aims: To assess the feasibility of conducting a large-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT) that integrates a VR intervention into USG-PIVC training, addressing these challenges before evaluating effectiveness. Methods: A single-site feasibility RCT will be conducted in an Australian ED. Twenty ED doctors will be randomly assigned to either standard training or standard training plus VR simulation. In addition to feasibility outcomes, the study will assess clinical metrics including first-attempt success rate, number of attempts, time to insertion, vein difficulty, completion of procedural steps, immediate complications, time spent practising, and clinician confidence and satisfaction. Expected outcomes: Although limited by a small sample size and single-site design, the findings from this pilot trial will pr…

title: Effects of subtropical forest gap size on soil invertebrate diversity are primarily season-dependent and secondarily layer-dependent
abstract: Abstract Escalating disturbance is reshaping soil invertebrate communities in subtropical forests, with cascading consequences for belowground processes. Forest gaps of moderate size represent a common form of intermediate disturbance, potentially promote soil invertebrate diversity. However, as disturbances are projected to intensify under ongoing climate change and generate larger forest gaps, the effects of gap size on the diversity of soil invertebrate feeding guilds remain poorly understood. Here, we determined the alpha and beta diversity of soil invertebrates (i.e. predators, detritivores, omnivores, and fungivores) of vertical layers (i.e. soil vs. litter) across four seasons (i.e. winter, spring, summer, and autumn) spanning an increasing canopy-opening gradient: canopy, forest edge, small gap, medium gap, and large gap. We found that increasing forest gap sizes only increased the alpha diversity of fungivores, whereas the diversity of predators, omnivores and detritivores greatly depended on seasons. Increasing forest gap size increased the beta diversity of detritivores and predators, and the interaction with season and layer significantly altered the beta diversity of detritivores, but not of omnivores. Collectively, seasonal variation was the primary driver of alpha and beta diversity of soil invertebrate feeding guilds across gap sizes, with diversity peaking in s…

High-power continuous-wave room-temperature quantum cascade laser at 4.6 μ m with a record 8.2 W output power
abstract: Quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) are the leading semiconductor light sources for the 3–5 μm atmospheric transmission window, yet achieving multi-watt continuous-wave (CW) operation at room temperature remains challenging due to the combined requirements of high optical gain, low carrier leakage, and efficient thermal management. Here, we report high-power 4.6 μm QCLs delivering a record single-facet CW output power of up to 8.21 W at room temperature. The devices use a highly strained active region that combines strong coupling, single-phonon-resonance depopulation, and AlAs barriers to suppress leakage current. The active region was grown by molecular beam epitaxy, and the devices were integrated with optimized thermal packaging based on a diamond-assisted microchannel cooler. A 10-mm-long, 8-μm-wide ridge device achieves a peak pulsed output power of 16.1 W, a maximum wall-plug efficiency of 24%, and a slope efficiency of 6.48 W/A at 298 K. These results establish a new benchmark for room-temperature CW operation of mid-infrared QCLs.

title: The PROCAN-B+ study protocol: early diagnosis of prostate cancer for Black men: a multi-center, two-arm, individually randomized controlled trial of a co-produced, peer-led intervention with a qualitative process evaluation
abstract: Background Black men face double the risk of developing and dying from prostate cancer. We co-designed a peer-led intervention with Black men ( n = 13), underpinned by the Integrated Screening Action Model (I-SAM), to encourage early diagnosis of prostate cancer. The intervention is a 2-h workshop which includes peer led discussions about challenges to accessing prostate cancer health care, health education delivered by a Black GP and video testimonials from survivors, women and religious leaders. Previously, the PROCAN-B pilot study was evaluated qualitatively ( n = 40) and through a pre-post survey design ( n = 41). Qualitative findings indicated that participants found the intervention acceptable and they enjoyed taking part. Quantitative findings demonstrated significant increases in knowledge and more positive attitudes toward accessing prostate cancer health checks and PSA testing. However, the sample was small and the intervention requires more robust effectiveness testing, which is what this follow-on PROCAN-B+ trial aims to do. Methods The PROCAN-B+ trial examines the intervention's effectiveness and usability through a multi-center, two-arm, individually randomized, wait-list controlled trial in community settings across three sites: (1) North-East England including Leeds, (2) London, and (3) Scotland; with a qualitative process evaluation. title: Perceived Values and Peer Influence in Mobile Gacha Game Impulse Purchases in Mobile Game (Gacha Context)
abstract: Background: Gacha-based mobile games monetize randomized virtual rewards, creating opportunities for unplanned in-app spending whose correlates require closer examination. Objective: This study examines the associations of hedonic, utilitarian, and economic value and peer influence with self-reported in-app impulse purchases among gacha-game players. Methods: A quantitative online survey recruited 100 mobile gamers reporting previous spontaneous gacha purchases through non-probability purposive sampling in gaming communities. Four predictors were assessed using Likert-type questionnaire items and multiple linear regression in SPSS 22. Results: All four predictors had positive coefficients: hedonic value (standardized β = 0.300, p < 0.001), utilitarian value (β = 0.165, p = 0.046), economic value (β = 0.261, p = 0.003), and peer influence (β = 0.262, p = 0.004). The model explained 59.1% of the sample variation (R² = 0.591) and was jointly significant (p < 0.001). Conclusion: Perceived values and peer influence are associated with reported impulse purchases in this selected sample. Cross-sectional, purposive sampling does not establish causality or permit population-wide generalization.

title: GenAI as an International Critical Peer: Expanding Perspectives in Learning
abstract: Abstract Generative AI is commonly used to generate answers, assist writing, and provide feedback. This article develops another educational role: the international critical peer for educators. In this role, educators use GenAI to surface assumptions and identify alternative interpretations when planning, designing, or making decisions across cultural and educational contexts. Drawing on work in global competence, intercultural competence, global citizenship education, and GenAI-supported critical feedback, this article presents a guided inquiry process for educators. The process begins with a real question, uses GenAI to surface possibilities, examines those possibilities through relevant evidence and input from people with experience in the setting, and then returns to the original decision. The aim is to expand professional inquiry while keeping interpretation and judgment with the educator.

Trade Openness and Renewable Energy Transition in Nigeria: Trends, Patterns and Policy Implications
abstract: This study looks at Nigeria’s trade openness and renewable energy transition trends and patterns between 2000 and 2025. The study is descriptive in nature and secondary data from the International Energy Agency and World Bank’s World Development Indicators are used to analyze trade openness, GDP growth, CO2 emissions, renewable energy consumption, and renewable power output. The findings reveal that there was a high degree of fluctuation in trade openness over the period studied and generally a decline in trade openness. Renewable energy use was relatively high, but this was largely because of the use of traditional biomass rather than the widespread use of contemporary renewable technologies. Before showing a partial rebound, the output of renewable electricity fell significantly from its early-period level. However, there were different trends for GDP growth and CO2 emissions. In general, the results indicate that the improvements in the selected renewable energy indicators did not necessarily reflect the changes in the level of trade openness. The analysis comes to the conclusion that without complementing policies, trade integration might not be enough to further Nigeria’s transition to renewable energy. It recommends to boost domestic production capacity, step up investment in power infrastructure, enhance access to renewable energy technologies and boost trade and energy …

title: Reaction-Dependent Performance of Ni/CeO2-Al2O3 Synthesis Routes for Ethanol Reforming Reactions
abstract: Abstract The preparation method of mixed oxide supports is a key factor governing the physicochemical properties and catalytic performance of Ni-based reforming catalysts. In this study, Ni catalysts supported on mixed Al2O3–CeO2 oxides prepared by mechanochemical synthesis and co-precipitation were comparatively investigated in ethanol dry reforming (EDR) and ethanol steam reforming (ESR). Although the catalysts possessed the same nominal composition, the preparation route resulted in markedly different Ni dispersions, metal–support interactions, and oxygen vacancy formation ability, leading to distinct catalytic behavior under the two ethanol reforming environments. The catalyst derived from the co-precipitated support (Ni/AC-c) exhibited enhanced CO2 adsorption, improved resistance to Ni sintering, and higher initial activity during EDR. Nevertheless, it underwent faster deactivation despite accumulating a smaller amount of carbon deposits. In contrast, the catalyst prepared from the mechanochemically synthesized support (Ni/AC-m) maintained catalytic activity for a longer period, despite a larger amount of carbon and noticeable Ni sintering observed. Under ESR conditions, the trends were reversed: the Ni/AC-c catalyst displayed stable performance over 7 h on stream with preserved Ni particle size, whereas the Ni/AC-m catalyst gradually deactivated due to Ni sintering and th…

title: High-voltage flat-tubular segment-in-series SOFCs: strategic design of an SrZrO 3 insulation layer
abstract: Flat-tubular segment-in-series solid oxide fuel cells (FT-SIS-SOFCs) offer a promising route for high-voltage SOFC systems; however, current leakage through conductive cermet supports remains a critical challenge, and the design principles for porous insulating layers that simultaneously provide electrical decoupling and sufficient gas transport have not been fully established. Herein, porous insulating layers were introduced between the support and the anode of an FT-SIS-SOFC to suppress current leakage through the cermet support and preserve gas transport. SrZrO3 (SZO) is a promising insulating material as it shows a stable perovskite structure at high temperatures and under a reducing atmosphere, and its resistivity is sufficiently high. Single cells with SZO insulating layer thicknesses from 0 µm to 108 µm were fabricated, and their performance exhibited a nonmonotonic thickness dependence. Thin SZO layers resulted in residual coupling between the anode and support, which introduced additional polarization. By contrast, excessively thick layers increased gas-transport resistance. The maximum A-C power density was achieved at an SZO thickness of approximately 73 µm, while a thickness range of 73-80 µm was identified as the practical optimal window for balancing electrical decoupling and gas transport. Using this optimized design, a 14-cell FT-SIS-SOFC was fabricated, with 12…

abstract: В статье рассматривается энергоаудит как эффективный инструмент повышения энергоэффективности жилых зданий и снижения затрат на энергоресурсы. Описаны основные этапы энергоаудита: подготовительный, измерительный, аналитический и заключительный. Представлены результаты исследований, выполненных в городе Карши, включающие анализ энергопотребления, обследование конструктивных элементов здания, выявление теплопотерь с использованием тепловизора и оценку микроклимата помещений. Определён потенциал энергосбережения и предложены мероприятия по его реализации, включая утепление ограждающих конструкций и внедрение солнечных технологий. Проведены расчёты экономической эффективности и сроков окупаемости. Обоснована целесообразность проведения энергоаудита перед внедрением солнечных энергетических систем.

title: Integrated process modeling and optimization of green hydrogen production in renewable energy systems using a Modified Rao-3 algorithm
abstract: Abstract The growth of renewable energy sources has brought in large scale opportunities for sustainable hydrogen production and for decarbonizing energy infrastructures. Green hydrogen which here produces via water electrolysis using renewable electricity has great environmental value as compared to that from fossil fuels. But the variable character of renewable resources presents operational issues related to electrolyzer use, hydrogen storage, grid interaction, and production cost. To that end this study puts forth an integrated modelling and optimization framework which looks at renewable generation, electricity price prediction, hydrogen production, storage, carbon emission and economic operation. This paper incorporated in framework day ahead electricity price prediction, hydrogen process models, renewable input, and hydrogen storage and also here, the used metaheuristic optimization. For electricity price here used Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and for the process model determined at renewable generation, electrolyzer performance, hydrogen storage, grid energy use, carbon output and hydrogen production cost. This paper validated the framework using the IEEE 30 bus power system which also included solar photovoltaic and wind resources. A Modified version of the Rao-3 algorithm is put in use to determine the hourly electrolyzer operation schedule at the point of balancin…

title: A Multiphysics Approach for Particle Size Optimization in Shales Using Low-Pressure Nitrogen Adsorption Measurements: Investigations from the Damodar Valley Basin, India
abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of complex shale pore networks is critical for various applications ranging from understanding and modeling pore-level changes in caprocks for carbon capture, utilization, and storage sites to unconventional energy exploration. However, the reliability of low-pressure nitrogen adsorption (LPNA) remains hindered by unstandardized sample crushing protocols, introducing an analytical paradox between internal pore accessibility and mechanical structural alteration. Limited studies address this gap, particularly concerning shales in the Indian subcontinent. Furthermore, existing investigations typically rely on restricted sample sets. To address this limitation, this study systematically evaluates the impact of distinct crushed particle sizes, namely M-40 (425 μm), M-120 (125 μm), and M-200 (75 μm), using eight representative core samples from two different formations and sub-basins, namely the Barren Measures (BMF) and Raniganj Formation (RF) from the Raniganj sub-basin (RSB) and Jharia sub-basin (JSB) in the Damodar Valley Basin (DVB), India. A unique multiscale multiphysics approach was deployed, integrating crushed-pore-scale quantitative mineralogy analysis via Rietveld refinement on X-ray diffraction (XRD) data and LPNA parameters of the rock with core-scale high-frequency benchtop ultrasonic analysis. The results indicated that the argillace…

title: A Methodological Framework for Dual-Energy Synchrotron XFM Characterization of Stratified Historical Glass: A Peranakan Bead Case Study
abstract: Abstract We present a technically focused, quantitative workflow for the depth-aware characterization of stratified historical glass using dual-energy synchrotron X-ray fluorescence microscopy (XFM). Demonstrated on a severely degraded Peranakan potash-lead–arsenic glass bead cross-section, this methodological case study establishes a reproducible template for mitigating common confounders in heritage glass analysis, such as self-absorption, matrix effects, and line overlaps. The specimen was embedded and polished to a flat internal surface, enabling coregistered optical, XRF, and scattering measurements under a fixed geometry. A paired excitation scheme was employed: a low-energy beam (7.05 keV) optimized for surface-confined, light-element sensitivity, and a high-energy beam (18.5 keV) for deeper penetration and heavy-element detection. Full XRF spectra were quantified pixel-wise using dynamic analysis (GeoPIXE) and evaluated using robust region-of-interest (ROI) statistics. The dual-energy approach yielded concrete, quantifiable improvements over single-energy methods. The 7.05 keV scan successfully isolated light-element dynamics free from heavy-element interference, revealing a massive depletion of potassium in the altered layer (mean concentration dropping from ∼3.2% to 1.84%, Hedges’ g = −7.19).
