title: Increasing the competence and capacity of Australian workforces to support children’s mental health: a mixed methods evaluation of a multi-sector workforce development initiative
abstract: Introduction There is a pressing need in Australia, as in many other countries, for increased availability of early intervention mental health support for children 0–12 years old. However, there is currently insufficient workforce to deliver these services, and existing specialist children's mental health practitioners are often overburdened treating children with severe and acute needs. The Australian Government established the National Workforce Centre for Child Mental Health (NWC) in 2017 to increase child mental health competence in health, social services and community sector professionals who work with children and parents. Methods This article presents the results of a mixed methods evaluation of the NWC using quantitative and qualitative data collected from 48,498 Australian practitioners engaged with the NWC between 2018 and 2023, in addition to 1,518 respondents to a cross–sectional Australian workforce survey conducted in 2020–21. Results Results show national engagement with the NWC from professionals in a range of sectors in positions to provide early intervention support to children and their families, with self-reported improvements in participants' child mental health knowledge, confidence, skills and practice. Improvement in practices, however, were smaller than gains in confidence and skills, with practitioners reporting common organisational and systemic chal…

title: Biofilm-forming Capacity of Clinical Isolates of Wound Infection Pathogens
abstract: To determine the biofilm-forming ability of clinical bacterial strains isolated from purulent wounds of military personnel, and to assess the prevalence of the biofilm-forming phenotype among wound infection pathogens across individual taxa, in view of the limited efficacy of antibacterial therapy against biofilm-associated infections. A total of 224 clinical bacterial isolates obtained from purulent wounds of service members treated at the Military Medical Clinical Centre of the Northern Region of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine were studied. Biofilm formation was assessed on polystyrene microtiter plates according to the method of L. B. Rodrigues et al., with the optical density of biofilms measured spectrophotometrically (Stat Fax) at a wavelength of 492 nm. Based on the sample optical density and the mean optical density of the negative control, cultures were assigned to four categories: strong, moderate, weak, or no biofilm formation. Each experiment was repeated 3 to 5 times; the data were processed by variation statistics using the χ² test, with differences considered statistically significant at p ≤ 0.05. The research program was approved by the local ethics committee, and all patients signed informed consent. Strong biofilm-forming ability was found in 49.1 % of isolates, moderate in 27.7 %, weak in 18.7 %, while 4.5 % of cultures did not form biofilm. Thus, 76.8 % …

title: Artificial intelligence capacity and environmental sustainability transitions in a resource-dependent economy
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly viewed as an enabler of environmental sustainability, yet its macro-level effects remain uncertain, particularly in resource-dependent economies. This study examines the relationships among AI capacity, economic development, CO 2 emissions, and renewable energy adoption in Qatar using annual data from 2002–2023. Ordinary least squares (OLS) time-series regressions are employed alongside stationarity diagnostics and robustness analyses using GDP-excluded and Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based alternative AI capacity indices. The baseline model identifies a positive association between AI capacity and CO 2 emissions (β = 0.168, p < 0.001); however, this relationship becomes negative and statistically insignificant after controlling for economic development and trade openness (β = − 0.069, p = 0.367). GDP remains strongly positively associated with emissions, while nonlinear estimation provides evidence of a developing Environmental Kuznets Curve. Robustness analysis excluding GDP from the AI index produces a similarly negative but insignificant AI coefficient, whereas the PCA-based specification identifies a significant negative association, demonstrating sensitivity to index construction. AI capacity is also positively associated with renewable energy adoption at the 10% significance level (β = 0.019, p = 0.078). Overal…

title: Building mental health capacity in protracted refugee situations: empirical pointers from Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya populations in India
abstract: Purpose Forcible displacement causes severe and long-term psychological distress, while refugees in the Global South often face major barriers to formal mental healthcare. Existing research largely focuses on Western resettlement settings or acute humanitarian crises, leaving limited understanding of sustainable psychosocial support in protracted refugee situations within non-signatory host countries. Focusing on Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya refugees in India, this study aims to examine how long-term legal uncertainty and camp environments shape mental health outcomes and explore how a transdisciplinary work-based learning approach can inform the development of a mental health training course for professionals working with refugees in India. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study draws on two focus group discussions and seven key informant interviews involving 14 stakeholders, including psychiatrists, policymakers, social workers, humanitarian practitioners and refugee leaders. Using Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, the study analyses how structural exclusion and legal invisibility influence individual and community mental health. Interviews explored gaps in existing services and curriculum development needs related to refugee mental health in India. Findings Findings highlight the need for integrated, context-sensitive approaches that combine evidence-b…
venue: International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care

title: Assessing Agricultural Land Capacity as a Proxy for Drought Resilience Under Climate Change in Mongolia
abstract: This study assesses agricultural land capacity as a proxy indicator of drought resilience under climate change in Mongolia's central agricultural region. Increasing drought frequency and climate variability have intensified environmental constraints on agricultural production, highlighting the need for spatially explicit approaches to identify resilient agricultural areas. Despite increasing climate risks, parcel-level assessments that integrate multiple environmental factors to evaluate agricultural land capacity and drought resilience remain limited. To address this gap, the study develops an integrated Geographic Information System-based Multi-Criteria Analysis framework to evaluate agricultural land capacity across 16,895 agricultural parcels covering 918,360.5 hectares. Nine environmental variables-precipitation, temperature, soil moisture, irrigation availability, elevation, slope, soil organic matter, soil pH, and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index-were standardized and integrated to develop a Land Capacity Index, which was used as a proxy indicator of drought resilience. The results show that 77.5% of agricultural land falls within the low and very low land-capacity categories, suggesting limited environmental capacity to withstand drought across much of the study area. Areas classified as having relatively high or high land capacity account for only 9.5% of the…

title: Russian in the System of Social Interactions: Level of Trust and Support Capacity
abstract: Basing on the data of the representative sociological survey, implemented by Institute of Social Analysis and Forecasting RANEPA in 2023, features of social interactions have been viewed what seems relevant in the context of objectives of support and improvement of Russians’ well-being in terms of both their emotional comfort and opportunities for necessary encouragement and assistance. The results show that most of the population is out of situation of social loneliness, however, less than a half of respondents possess significant circle of trustful communications. Quite high social stated social trust is noted towards representatives of the “close circle”, whereas trust to state institutes and official mass media is significantly lower. The integral indicator of subjective breadth of interpersonal and institutional trust counted by the authors does not exceed of the average level for half of population and is high only for 20%. Actual recipients of regular interpersonal financial transfers are 19% of Russians, and most often - representative of youth and senior cohorts. Resource potential of the population, consisting in prospects of application of social interaction system to overcome appearing difficulties, seems significant, nevertheless problems of deficit in effective institutional channels and presence of deprived groups of population are explicit.

title: Evaluating geological environmental carrying capacity using remote sensing and random forest: A case study of Liuhe County, Jilin Province, China
After being seen: patient social media self-disclosure, audience feedback, and the chain mechanism of health adaptation
abstract: Introduction Social media has become an important arena in which patients narrate illness experiences, seek support, and construct identities. Yet the benefits of disclosure cannot be understood through expression alone: illness narratives enter public or semi-public spaces of audience response and social evaluation. This study investigates the underlying mechanism between patient self-disclosure and perceived health-related benefits. Methods Drawing on the Disclosure Processes Model and the Temporal Need-Threat Model, this cross-sectional survey of 400 patients in Chinese social media communities tested a chain mediation model linking disease stigma sensitivity, self-disclosure, perceived positive audience feedback, psychological need satisfaction, and self-reported health-related benefits. Data were analyzed via structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results The results indicated positive associations from stigma sensitivity to disclosure (β = 0.72), from disclosure to feedback (β = 0.43), and from feedback to both need satisfaction (β = 0.39) and health outcomes (β = 0.41; all p < 0.001). The hypothesized chain mediation pathway from disclosure through feedback and need satisfaction was statistically significant [indirect effect = 0.04, 95% CI (0.02, 0.08)]. Pathways involving need satisfaction accounted for only approximately 21% of the total stigma…

title: Genome mining, characterization, catalytic mechanism and immobilization of a novel GH26 β-1, 4-mannanase from Enterobacter ludwigii
abstract: To reduce mannooligosaccharides (MOS) production costs, a novel GH26 β-1,4-mannanase ElMan from Enterobacter ludwigii was identified via EnzymeMiner. As a single-domain enzyme, ElMan exhibited an optimal pH of 5.0, remained catalytically active across pH 3.0–8.0, and retained more than 70% of its maximal activity after incubation at pH 5.0–8.5, a pH adaptability superior to most reported bacterial β-mannanases. Its specific activity was 17.0% higher than that of the well-characterized Bacillus subtilis 168 mannanase. Furthermore, ElMan also exhibits a certain degree of hydrolysis of xanthan gum. Structural modeling, site-directed mutagenesis, molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested that H182, E183 and E282 are the core catalytic residues, and that D50, R77, K133 and D317 participate in substrate binding. Fermentation optimization by response surface methodology achieved an enzyme activity of 1672.35 U/mL. Sodium alginate–glutaraldehyde immobilization further enhanced its thermostability, storage stability and reusability. Combining favorable pH adaptability, a clarified catalytic mechanism, high-level production and improved operational stability, ElMan is a cost-effective biocatalyst for MOS production.

title: Transcriptome analysis reveals the response mechanism of Bacillus velezensis to sodium selenite stress
First-principles investigation of water adsorption on TiN, ZrN, and HfN nanoribbons: electronic structure and adsorption mechanism
abstract: Abstract Water adsorption on transition metal nitride nanostructures is strongly dependent on the local adsorption environment. Here, density functional theory calculations are used to analyze nine H 2 O adsorption configurations on TiN, ZrN, and HfN nanoribbons, comprising central-region, top-metal, and top-nitrogen placements for each substrate. Dispersion interactions are included through the D3(BJ) correction. The central-region configurations are thermodynamically unfavorable, with adsorption energies of + 5.63, + 6.98, and + 4.87 eV for TiN, ZrN, and HfN, respectively, whereas the top-site configurations are exothermic, with adsorption energies from − 0.960 to − 1.264 eV. The preferred configurations are top-metal for TiN (− 1.116 eV) and top-N for ZrN (− 1.264 eV) and HfN (− 1.243 eV). In every optimized structure, water remains molecular and the nanoribbon framework is preserved. Charge density difference, Bader population, total density of states, band structure, and projected density of states analyses indicate localized interfacial polarization with limited adsorbate–substrate orbital mixing, while finite electronic states persist at the Fermi level. These results establish a site-dependent molecular hydration picture: favorable water uptake at specific surface sites does not, by itself, demonstrate oxidative corrosion, which would additionally require dissociation, …

title: Dual Electron-Pump Mechanism Enabled by Schottky Heterojunction and W Modulation Boosts Intermittency-Resilient Oxygen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
abstract: Abstract Developing high-efficiency, durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) anodes that adapt to intermittent renewable power input is highly desired for sustainable industrial alkaline water electrolysis (AWE). Herein, self-supported W-doped NiFe LDH/Ni3S2 heterostructures on nickel foam (W-NiFe LDH/Ni3S2/NF) were fabricated, featuring a dual electron-pump mechanism. The Schottky interface acts as the first electron pump, driving directional charge transfer from Ni3S2 to NiFe LDH and utilizing interfacial S atoms as an electron reservoir to suppress Fe over-oxidation and lattice leaching. High-valent W acts as the second electron pump, enlarging the work-function gap to accelerate charge transfer, tuning the d-band to optimize intermediate adsorption, and thereby lowering the reaction barrier. Consequently, the electrode exhibits a low overpotential of 288 mV at 1000 mA cm–2. The assembled AWE cell delivers a voltage of 1.79 V at 1.0 A cm–2. Crucially, it exhibits negligible performance degradation after a rigorous 1000 h stability test at 500 mA cm–2, interspersed with 3000 start–stop cycles, confirming excellent resilience to intermittency. A preliminary techno-economic assessment highlights its potential for large-scale application and cost competitiveness. This work provides a synergistic electronic-structure and interfacial-engineering strategy for designing robust AWE a…

title: Research on the Linkage Mechanism between the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor and the High-Quality Development of Chongqing’s Foreign Trade under the Dual-Circulation Paradigm
abstract: Against the backdrop of global value chain restructuring and the new development paradigm of dual circulation, the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor has become an important strategic vehicle for inland regions to advance high-standard opening up. In this context, this paper examines the underlying mechanisms linking the Corridor and the high-quality development of Chongqing’s foreign trade from the perspective of dual circulation, an inquiry of considerable practical relevance. By systematically reviewing the existing industrial, logistics, and digital foundations for their interconnected development, this study finds that the Corridor can help improve the quality and promote the upgrading of Chongqing’s foreign trade by reducing logistics costs, deepening the industrial division of labor, improving cross-border transaction efficiency, and strengthening supply chain resilience. In turn, the expansion of foreign trade, structural optimization, innovation in business models, and market diversification can create pressure for the iterative improvement of the Corridor in the provision of transport capacity, specialized services, digital governance, and the development of overseas networks, forming a feedback loop in which supply and demand reinforce each other. Accordingly, this paper proposes measures for improvement in logistics coordination, industry–trade integration, a…

title: Integrative Omics Reveal the Antiviral Mechanism of Gossypol and Guide the Construction of a Chitooligosaccharide–Gossypol Nanocomposite
abstract: Abstract Gossypol (GOS), a unique cotton sesquiterpenoid, exhibits broad antiviral activity against animal viruses, but its specific effects on plant viruses remain largely unexplored. Using tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) and cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) models, we demonstrated that GOS treatment significantly reduces viral RNA accumulation and alleviates systemic symptoms. Integrating multiple omics approaches, findings suggest that GOS rebalances host hormones by repressing biosynthesis and activating catabolism, curbing excess salicylic acid (SA) and abscisic acid (ABA) while restoring indole acetic acid (IAA) to optimize resource allocation between growth and defense. Additionally, the transcriptional upregulation of antiviral sesquiterpene genes closely aligns with the targeted metabolite accumulation. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays reveal that GOS directly targets viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). Collectively, GOS mitigates plant viral infections through polymerase targeting and defense reprogramming. These insights inspired a highly efficient GOS–chitooligosaccharide (COS) nanocomplex for crop protection in sustainable agriculture.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
abstract: Abstract Maintenance of plant CG DNA methylation requires VARIANT IN METHYLATION (VIM) proteins, a family of E3 ligases that couple hemimethylated CG (hemiCG) with histone ubiquitylation to regulate MET1-mediated DNA methylation. How the hemiCG readout guides VIM proteins for histone ubiquitylation remains unclear. Here we report structure-function characterization of VIM1-mediated histone ubiquitylation, revealing the N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 as the VIM1 substrates. The structures of VIM1 complexed with hemiCG-containing nucleosome and/or E2 UBC11 reveal that VIM1 is positioned over the nucleosome disk surface, with the RING2 and SRA domains anchored to the H2A-H2B acidic patch and linker hemiCG site, respectively, and the RING1 domain mediating UBC11 loading. The RING2-mediated anchoring helps position RING1 near the H3/H4 tails for substrate access, while the SRA-mediated anchoring antagonizes an autoinhibitory state. Together, such dual nucleosome anchoring by RING2-SRA mechanistically links the position-varying hemiCG mark to persistent, yet context-dependent H3/H4 ubiquitylation.

title: The Effect of Storage Conditions on the Viability and Antagonistic Activity of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. Bulgaricus 1Z 03501 Culture Immobilized in Alginate-Pectin Films Following Lyophilization
abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the viability, antagonistic and cultural properties of the probiotic strain Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus 1Z 03501, immobilized in alginate-pectin films with the addition of a protective sucrose-milk-lactose medium (APF SML) or saline solution (APF SS), following freeze-drying and subsequent storage at temperatures of 4 and –20 °C for three months. The lactobacilli were immobilized in films based on a 3% sodium alginate solution and a 3% pectin solution in appropriate proportions, cross-linked by calcium ions, and cultured in Blaurock’s medium for 48 hours. The samples were frozen to –28 °C, followed by vacuum drying with a residual pressure in the chamber not exceeding 50 Pa. Upon completion of the drying process, the samples were placed in airtight polyethylene vacuum bags and transferred to refrigerators and freezers for storage at temperatures of 4 and –20 °C. The titer of viable cells was determined by the serial dilution method after dissolving the films in sodium citrate. Antagonistic activity was assessed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa 9027 based on the width of the growth inhibition zones. Cultural properties were determined visually in Blaurock’s semi-solid medium. It was found that prior to lyophilization, the number of viable lactobacilli cells in the APF SS sample was 9.14 lg CFU/g, and the number of viable cells i…

title: Integrated CO2-EOR and Post-EOR Storage in a Mature Waterflooded UKCS Sandstone Reservoir: Recovery-Retention-Pressure Trade-offs from Compositional Simulation
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates miscible CO2-enhanced oil recovery, post-EOR CO2 storage, and long-term postinjection behavior in a mature offshore sandstone reservoir using compositional simulation. A PVT-tuned Peng–Robinson model gave a pure-CO2 minimum miscibility pressure of 2,528 psia by the multiple-mixing-cell method, and reservoir pressure remained above this value in all CO2-EOR cases. Five strategies (continuous CO2; fixed and tapered water-alternating-gas (WAG); a CO2 slug followed by WAG; and simultaneous water-and-gas injection) were compared from a common 2027 reference state. A 36-month CO2 slug followed by alternating six-month CO2 and six-month water periods was preferred: it produced 69.61 MMstb (8.64% of stock-tank oil initially in place), 50.06 MMstb more than continued waterflooding, and retained 9.86 of 21.42 Mt injected CO2 (46.0%). Post-EOR storage at 140 MMscf/d for 15 years, selected from three rate cases because injectivity rather than nominal rate controlled the stored mass, raised the total retained CO2 to 44.81 Mt (79.5% of 56.37 Mt injected); field-average pressure then declined from 6,955 to 6,385 psia over 100 years of shut-in monitoring. Plume expansion was limited, CO2 partitioned progressively into the oleic and aqueous phases, and mobile gas-phase CO2 decreased. The results show that a single mature, heavily waterflooded UKCS reservoir can del…

title: A hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach to select bio-phase change materials for low-temperature solar thermal storage applications
abstract: Abstract The utilisation of phase change materials (PCMs) for capturing and retaining solar energy within thermal energy storage (TES) systems is prevailing across numerous fields of application. The widespread usage of paraffin-based PCMs creates environmental issues, spurring investigations into bio-based alternatives that are more sustainable and less damaging, such as those derived from natural sources like plant oils or animal fats, which can provide similar thermal performance with lower environmental damage. Therefore, ongoing pressure to decarbonise solar thermal energy storage (STES) necessitates the use of sustainable storage materials. To successfully integrate bio-PCM into the STES system, its thermophysical properties must align with operational conditions. The diversity of bio-PCMs and their attributes impede decision-making. Consequently, the objective of this study is to present a decision-making framework for the selection of bio-PCMs. In this research, a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methodology employing GRA-TOPSIS-VIKOR is utilised to evaluate the energy storage capability of bio-PCM and select it for a low-temperature STES applications. The entropy weight method is used to assign initial weights to each criterion to mitigate uncertainty in the results of the proposed dataset. The weight variation method was employed in a sensitivity study to …

title: The influence of storage temperature on platelet toll-like receptor 2 integrity in platelet concentrates
abstract: Abstract Platelet concentrates (PC) are used for the treatment of thrombocytopenia or platelet-dependent hemorrhage. In addition to hemostasis, platelets are also involved in immunological processes. In this context, platelet toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) mediates important responses to bacterial antigens. Since storage temperature of PC storage essentially interferes with platelet reactivity, it was the aim of this study to investigate TLR2 expression, distribution and function in platelets from PC either stored at room temperature (RT, 20–24 °C) or cold temperature (CT, 2–6 °C). For this purpose, apheresis-derived PC were initially stored at RT before splitting into two parts on day 1. Then, one part was stored at RT and the other part at CT until day 5. On day 1 and 5, samples were drawn for comparative analysis. Flow cytometry was used to analyze TLR2 surface expression, induced uptake of fibrinogen or TLR2 ligand Pam3CSK4, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and CD40L expression. Transmission electron microscopy and high-resolution fluorescence microscopy were performed to visualize TLR2 distribution. TLR2-stimulated secretion of platelet chemokines RANTES, NAP-2, PDGF, PF4 and sCD40L was measured by immunoassays. Regardless of storage temperature, TLR2 surface expression and its subcellular distribution were not substantially changed until day 5. TLR2 was able to stimu…

title: Packing Configuration and the In-pallet Microenvironment, Clove Quality, and Marketable Yield of Garlic under Long-term Storage
Comparative analysis of biochemical and genomic approaches to newborn screening for lysosomal storage disorders in a Chinese cohort
abstract: Abstract Lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs) are severe inherited metabolic diseases for which early diagnosis through newborn screening (NBS) enables timely initiation of disease specific therapies and improves long term outcomes. However, the comparative performance of biochemical screening, genetic screening, and their combination in Chinese populations remains poorly characterized. This prospective, real-world implementation study was conducted at Jinan Maternity and Child Care Hospital between May 2023 and June 2026. A total of 6204 newborns were allocated to three screening strategies based on parental preference: only biochemical screening (NBS, n = 2581), only newborn genetic screening (NBGS, n = 3193), and combined screening (n = 430). Positive predictive value (PPV), disease specific performance, carrier frequency, and minor allele frequency (MAF) were analyzed. NBS identified 27 initial screen positive cases (0.90%), 5 remained positive on repeat testing, of which 2 were confirmed (1 Fabry disease, 1 Krabbe disease), yielding an overall PPV of 7.4% at initial screening. NBGS identified 2 confirmed cases (1 Fabry, 1 Krabbe). Combined screening identified 1 Fabry case. Carrier frequency analysis revealed that 3.78% carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant. GALC c.1901T > C (1.71%), GALC c.2041G > A (0.69%), and GAA c.761 C > T (0.19%) accounted for 6…

Critical Gaps in Understanding Solid-State Battery Interfaces from an Electromechanical Perspective
abstract: Conspectus For two centuries, battery research has predominantly focused on solid–liquid interfaces. However, the advent of fast ion conducting solid-state electrolytes enables solid-state battery technology and introduces critical solid–solid interfaces. A prevailing practice in the field has been to adapt classical electrochemical models to these mechanically constrained interfaces. However, fundamental electrochemical concepts such as the electric double layer and Butler–Volmer kinetics are no longer sufficient to describe these solid–solid interfaces. The core limitation lies in the strong bidirectional coupling between mechanics and electrochemistry. In solid-state systems, ion-induced volume changes cannot be rapidly dissipated because of the absence of fluid. Instead, it generates GPa-level local stresses that directly alter the reaction free energy and kinetics. This bidirectional coupling results in a series of consequences previously negligible in liquids, e.g., stress heterogeneity, mechanical overpotentials, and particle-to-electrode mechanical crosstalk. Therefore, from an electromechanical perspective, there are critical gaps in understanding solid–solid interfacial electrochemistry. In this regard, integration of multiphysics mapping and modeling techniques is necessary. In this Account, we first examine the limitations of adapting classical electrochemical theor…

title: This study examined post-harvest losses (PHL) and their implications for food availability among smallholder fruit and vegetable farmers in Ethiopia's Oromia Region. The study was conducted in six kebeles of Adami Tulu Jido Kombolcha and Dugda woredas using a cross-sectional quantitative survey of 359 fruits and vegetable-producing households selected through multistage sampling method. Data were collected using structured questionnaires administered through KoboCollect App from December 2023 to March 2024. We assessed farm-level post-harvest loss (PHL) using the Aggregate Self-Reported Method, in which farmers reported quantities lost during harvesting and handling, transportation, storage, and marketing; we calculated percentage loss relative to the initial harvested quantity. The estimated producer-level losses were 11.84% for tomato, 8.62% for kale, and 13.81% for papaya. Regional-level PHL estimates were extrapolated by applying the farm-level loss rates estimated in this study to Oromia Region’s annual fruit and vegetable production data for 2013-2022. A deterministic 25% PHL-reduction scenario was used to estimate the quantity of produce that could theoretically be recovered and converted, using a dietary consumption benchmark into annual fruit-and-vegetable person-year supply equivalents. The analysis estimated cumulative fruit and vegetable PHL of 724,071.91 tons over the 2013-2022 period. Under the 25% PHL-reduction scenario, the estimated quantity of produce that could potentially be recovered varied across the study years. In 2022, the recovered quantity was equivalent to the annual fruit-and-vegetable consumption requirement of 832,444 people for one year (832,444.34 person-year equivalents), representing the highest annual estimate during the study period. When the annual estimates for 2013-2022 are summed, they amounted to approximately 3.31 million person-years. This cumulative estimate represented the aggregate annual food-supply equivalent generated over the ten years, expressed as the number of one-person annual fruit-and-vegetable consumption requirements that could theoretically be met by the recovered produce in each respective year. The findings indicated that reducing producer-level PHL could increase the quantity of fruit and vegetables potentially available for consumption, highlighting the importance of improved harvesting, handling, storage, transportation, and marketing practices among smallholder farmers. Key words: Post-harvest loss, smallholder farmers, fruit and vegetables, food availability, Ethiopia

title: Safe and Interpretable Vehicle Platoon Control via Physics-Enhanced Residual Learning
abstract: Abstract Vehicle platoon control in complex dynamic environments necessitates a rigorous balance between physical interpretability safety constraints and nonlinear compensation. This paper presents PERL, a Physics-Enhanced Residual Learning framework that hierarchically integrates Distributed Model Predictive Control (DMPC) with Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. To address the pathological residual action saturation. we propose a residual-magnitude-based action regularization mechanism. This mechanism penalizes large-amplitude residuals to stabilize the policy update and constrain the RL module within a safe, small-amplitude regime, ensuring effective compensation for unmodeled dynamics beyond the physical baseline’s fidelity. Additionally, a spatiotemporal smooth handover and dynamic fusion strategy significantly enhances edge-case safety. Utilizing safety-boundary constraints and dual soft-filtering, the strategy regulates control authority to mitigate violations of Rational Driving Constraints by RL policies while preventing abrupt control mutations. Experiments across four representative scenarios show that PERL converges rapidly and consistently outperforms MPC, PPO, and TD3 in safety, comfort, and platoon stability. Specifically, PERL reduces inverse time-to-collision by 20.3% relative to PPO and improves ride comfort by over 60% compared wi…

title: Parallel object-oriented implementation of thermo-electric topology optimization using OpenMP for DC bus bars
abstract: Purpose The DC bus bar is an essential component in electric vehicles (EVs), as it is used for high-current-density power supply between modules. This study presents a shared memory-based parallel, object-oriented C++ framework for fully coupled thermo-electric multiphysics topology optimization of DC bus bars. Design/methodology/approach A density-based topology optimization approach minimizes thermal compliance while satisfying constraints. The governing thermal and electrical equations are discretized using the finite element method, and the method of moving asymptotes is employed to update the material layout. To address the computational expense associated with fine mesh resolutions and coupled physics, we perform a detailed time analysis of the serial program to identify performance bottlenecks. An OpenMP-based shared-memory parallelization technique has been applied in the program, including element-level matrix computations and the preconditioned conjugate gradient solver. Performance of parallelized code is evaluated using multiple geometric configurations and mesh sizes. Findings The maximum parallel speedup of 10.64 is achieved using 32 threads, and the maximum parallel efficiency of 94% is observed with two threads. Originality/value The framework demonstrates robust scalability and provides a practical tool for high-resolution topology optimization of thermal-elect…

title: A multi-sensor fusion localization method for reconfigurable unmanned vehicle docking based on vision and laser fusion
abstract: Purpose This study aims to improve localization accuracy and robustness for autonomous docking of reconfigurable ground unmanned systems in complex industrial environments, where vision-based localization is sensitive to illumination variations, partial occlusions and observation noise. Design/methodology/approach A multi-sensor fusion localization framework integrating visual and laser range measurements is proposed. A CNN-assisted EKF-based PnP pose estimation framework is developed to enhance motion state estimation under degraded visual conditions. To improve short-range docking accuracy, a laser-based multi-point ranging strategy is introduced. Furthermore, a grey relational analysis–guided Dempster–Shafer evidence fusion framework is developed to handle conflicting sensor information and improve fusion consistency. Findings Experimental results in complex industrial environments demonstrate that the proposed fusion method achieves stable and accurate pose estimation for autonomous docking. Compared with vision-only localization, Kalman filter-based fusion, and weighted averaging fusion schemes, the proposed method exhibits superior robustness under illumination variations and partial occlusions. The system achieves a real-time update rate of 20 Hz, satisfying closed-loop docking control requirements, and provides adaptive down-weighting of unreliable sensor measurements t…

title: Morphology and Specularity of Deuterated Polystyrene- b -Poly(Ethylene Oxide) Thin Films in an Applied Electric Field Revealed by Neutron Reflectometry
abstract: Abstract The nanoscale organization and alignment of a microphase-separated block copolymer thin film can be enhanced by applying an electric field, thereby inducing domains to align parallel to the field direction. Here, we use neutron reflectometry to examine changes in the nanoscale organization of lamellar-forming deuterated polystyrene-block-poly(ethylene oxide) (dPS-b-PEO) thin films as functions of applied electric field and temperature. We find that dPS-b-PEO thin films annealed at 50 °C, which is between the glass transition temperatures of the two blocks, and electric fields below 0.69 V/μm yield horizontal lamellae that display large quantities of off-specular scattering that is quantified by a so-called specularity, which is used to inform the fitting of specular reflectivity data. However, dPS-b-PEO thin films annealed at 0.69 V/μm and 50 °C exhibit lamellar domains aligned both parallel and perpendicular to the field direction. Assessing these morphological responses to applied electric fields and thermal annealing informs efforts to exert control over nanostructure formation, advancing block copolymer thin films for applications such as (bio)sensors, templated surface scaffolds, and optoelectronic devices.

title: Nanoliposome-based malvidin or N-acetylcysteine therapeutics for attenuating mitochondrial dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease: a targeted strategy
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal impairment. Natural antioxidants such as malvidin and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) exhibit antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, thereby help reduce reactive oxygen species (ROS) and support cellular redox balance by strengthening endogenous antioxidant defenses under conditions of oxidative stress and inflammation. By concurrently targeting oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation, these compounds could be promising candidates as multi-pathway metabolic stabilizers capable of mitigating AD pathology. Nonetheless, the therapeutic efficacy of such bioactive compounds is frequently constrained by their poor stability, rapid degradation, lower bioavailability and inefficient delivery to target tissues. Nanoliposome-based delivery systems can address these limitations by offering enhanced biocompatibility, improved stability, and efficient site-specific delivery of vulnerable bioactive compounds. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying mitochondrial dysfunction in AD, examines the individual neuroprotective effects of malvidin and NAC, and highlights the rational and emerging potential of malvidin-loaded and NAC-loaded nanoliposomes as two distinct targeted strategies for attenuating…

title: Analysis Of Asabellia’s Personal Branding Strategy Through Self-Presentation As A Digital Writer On Instagram
abstract: This study analyzes how Asabellia Audida, a digital fiction writer known on Instagram as @asabelliaa with about 86,700 followers, builds her personal brand. Personal branding has become a common practice among social media creators, yet earlier studies often do not describe the concrete form of the brand or the motives behind its presentation. This research aims to describe the strategies used to build a personal brand on Instagram within the context of self-presentation. A qualitative approach with an instrumental case study design was applied. Data were collected through open interviews with the writer and her admin staff, non-participant observation of Instagram content, and documentation, then analyzed with the Miles and Huberman model of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. Informants were selected through purposive sampling, involving Asabellia as the key informant and her admin staff as a supporting informant. Instagram content from feeds, stories, and highlights was collected through non-participant observation and documentation. The two frameworks were used in complementary roles. Montoya’s eight laws of personal branding served as analytical indicators to identify the dimensions of Asabellia’s personal brand (what is built), while Delamater et al.’s self-presentation strategies were used to explain how and why these dimensions were expressed through h…

title: Sanction or strategy? Electoral competition and retaliatory use of no-confidence votes
abstract: No-confidence votes (NCVs) provide a sanctioning mechanism to hold democratically elected politicians accountable. However, national politicians can weaponize NCVs to target potential local rivals to deter future electoral challenge. This perverse form of accountability can undermine the quality of democratic competition, thus obviating the core goal of NCVs. Empirically, I evaluate this argument in the context of a developing democracy. During the 2016 presidential campaign in Benin, mayors who did not endorse the same presidential candidate as the MP from their district were two-thirds more likely to face an NCV. MPs who initiated NCVs against politically incongruent mayors were more likely to win re-election. Additional evidence shows that targeted mayors were less likely to obtain party nominations, while those who regained ballot access disproportionately switched political organizations. This evidence leverages administrative and electoral records. The findings show how democratic institutions and candidate-selection processes can become tools for managing intra-elite competition.

When brand extension strategy meets sensory execution: the interactive effects of brand fit and sensory modality on perceived sub-brand value
abstract: Purpose Drawing on brand ecosystem theory and expectation confirmation theory, this study examines how the interaction between parent-subsidiary brand fit types (high fit, low fit, Janus fit) and sensory modalities (proximal vs distal) influences perceived sub-brand value. It further investigates the mediating role of region-of-origin image and the moderating role of agricultural product category. Design/methodology/approach This study employs two scenario-based experiments (total N = 590 after exclusions). Study 1 manipulates fit type and sensory modality through offline physical exposure combined with sensory transfer guidance; Study 2 replicates and extends the design using online consumer review scenarios with text-based sensory priming, while additionally manipulating agricultural product category (primary vs processed). Findings The results reveal a significant interactive effect between parent-sub-brand fit types and sensory modality on perceived sub-brand value. Specifically, distal (sight/sound) cues outperform proximal (taste/touch) cues under high-fit conditions, whereas the reverse holds under low-fit conditions; Janus-fit extensions generate higher perceived sub-brand value than high-fit and low-fit extensions when averaged across sensory modalities. title: Kidney xenotransplantation as an investigational rescue strategy: a clinical perspective on high-KDPI kidney allograft as a comparator
abstract: Kidney transplantation is the gold standard treatment for end-stage kidney disease. Despite increasing transplant case volume in recent years, its access is limited due to a donor organ shortage, resulting in significant waitlist mortality. Xenotransplantation has the potential to address this unmet need and has made significant progress from early, largely unsuccessful nonhuman-primate experiments in the 1960s to early clinical application in the 2020s: genetically modified pig kidneys have now provided dialysis-independent function in a few living human recipients, sustained for months in some cases. These clinical experiences, together with preclinical nonhuman-primate data, demonstrate that genetically modified pig kidneys can achieve meaningful short-term renal replacement. However, graft durability remains a challenge partly due to immunologic rejection, complement activation, and infection. Given these limitations, kidney xenotransplantation cannot yet be considered a routine alternative to human kidney transplantation. We argue that, at its current stage, it is most appropriately positioned as an investigational rescue strategy for carefully selected patients who face high mortality risk on dialysis and a low likelihood of timely allotransplantation, and that its clinical value should be benchmarked against the expected longevity of high-Kidney Donor Profile Index allog…

title: The Potential of Natural Twin Birth in Boer Goats as a Strategy to Increase Productivity and Achieve Meat Self-Sufficiency
abstract: The importation of meat indicates that the production in Indonesia has not been sufficient to fulfill the growing demand for animal protein. A solution to this problem may be to exploit natural twinning in meat-producing animals, especially Boer goat, as a means of increasing productivity. Natural twin birth, which refers to the production of two animals from the same pregnancy, can improve reproductive efficiency and meat yield, depending on the management situation. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the reproductive performance of Boer goats with natural twin birth and to measure the physiological parameters of the reproductive hormones FSH and LH. It was conducted for six months in Subuh Jaya Farm, Semarang, with 20 adult Boer goats (10 twin-bearing and 10 single-bearing) and 30 offspring. The results showed that twin-bearing dams had lower body weight and chest circumference than single-bearing (P < 0.05), indicating a greater physiological burden during twin pregnancy. In contrast, offspring born from twin-bearing dams (TB) showed better growth performance, with higher body weight, shoulder height, and chest circumference compared to single-bearing dams (SB). FSH levels were also higher in twin groups from both dams and offspring, suggesting increased reproductive activity associated with multiple ovulations, while LH levels remained relatively stable. Job vs leisure: Rethinking physical activity as a precision strategy for mental and cognitive aging in China
abstract: Mental and cognitive decline represent major challenges in aging populations. Physical activity is widely promoted as a key strategy for healthy aging. However, its effects are not uniform and depend on purpose and context. Job-related physical activity (JPA), often characterized by high demands and limited autonomy, may induce chronic stress, insufficient recovery, and adverse neurocognitive outcomes. In contrast, leisure physical activity (EPA) is typically self-directed and socially engaging, supporting improved mood, neural plasticity, and cognitive function. In this review, we reconceptualize physical activity by distinguishing JPA from EPA and propose a precision-oriented framework for mental and cognitive aging. We first examine their differences in psychological meaning, autonomy, and recovery patterns, then discuss the underlying biological, psychological, and recovery-related mechanisms, as well as socioeconomic and contextual influences. Finally, we outline implications for public health and clinical practice, emphasizing a shift from volume-based metrics toward context-sensitive strategies to promote brain health in aging populations.

title: Running on Generators: Self-Generation, Power Outages and Firm Performance in Nigeria after the 2023 Fuel Subsidy Removal
abstract: Nigerian firms have long supplemented the grid with their own generators. In 2023 the petrol subsidy was removed and the naira was allowed to depreciate, and the price of the fuels that run those generators rose steeply. We ask how dependence on self-generation relates to sales, employment and margins among formal Nigerian establishments over FY2021 to FY2024, and whether the employment association differs from 2014. We use the World Bank Enterprise Survey Nigeria 2025 (N = 1,043; analytical samples of 891 to 922 establishments, 372 for the margin) and harmonised measures from the 2007, 2009 and 2014 waves. Survey-weighted logit and least-squares models relate the share of electricity drawn from the firm's own generator and monthly outage hours to real sales growth, employment continuity and a partial operating margin, with stratified design-based standard errors, unweighted, size-split and alternative-measure checks, and a pooled 2014 and 2025 test. In 2025, 86.4 per cent of establishments owned or shared a generator (against 70.7 per cent in 2014), and generators supplied on average 45.6 per cent of their electricity, even though the median number of outages per month had fallen from 30 to 10. title: Study on the influence of cathode position on the performance of a low-power magnetically enhanced hollow cathode thruster
abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence of cathode position on the discharge characteristics, plume characteristics, and propulsion performance of a low-power magnetically enhanced hollow cathode thruster (MHCT), comparative experiments were conducted using center-mounted and externally mounted cathode configurations under different anode voltages and xenon flow rates. The anode current, discharge oscillations, plume ion current density, ion energy distribution, thrust, specific impulse, and thrust efficiency were measured and analyzed. The results show that the center-mounted cathode configuration generally exhibited a higher anode current and could maintain stable discharge at lower anode voltages under low-flow-rate conditions. Compared with the externally mounted cathode configuration, the center-mounted cathode exhibited a higher dominant discharge oscillation frequency and weaker harmonic components. At a total xenon flow rate of 4 sccm, the mass utilization efficiency of the center-mounted cathode configuration reached approximately 58.5%–59.7%, compared with 29.4%–46.4% for the externally mounted cathode configuration. Although the externally mounted cathode produced a higher peak ion current density near the thruster axis and a more concentrated ion beam, the center-mounted cathode generally generated a higher total plume ion current. title: Modality-specific dose-response associations between exercise and brachial artery flow-mediated dilation in adults: a systematic review and network dose-response meta-analysis
abstract: Background Exercise improves vascular endothelial function, but modality-specific dose relationships remain uncertain. We compared aerobic exercise (AE), high-intensity interval training (HIIT), resistance training (RT), and combined aerobic and resistance exercise (CE) and described their associations with brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD). Methods Five databases were searched from inception through 30 January 2026. Arm-level FMD changes were analysed using inverse-variance-weighted dose-response meta-regression with study fixed effects and weekly exposure in metabolic equivalent minutes (MET-min/week). Linear, quadratic, and cubic functions were compared. The quadratic model was selected after assessing information criteria and quantitative stability diagnostics. Uncertainty was estimated using 600 whole-study bootstrap attempts, of which 597 yielded identifiable primary-model fits. Exploratory analyses evaluated age, female proportion, chronic disease, programme duration, baseline FMD, and measurement protocols. Results Forty-seven trials provided usable FMD data for 2,165 participants in 111 arms. In direct comparisons with control, AE (mean difference [MD] 2.60 percentage points, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.99 to 3.22), HIIT (2.61, 1.62 to 3.60), and CE (2.20, 0.53 to 3.86) improved FMD; the RT estimate was uncertain (1.91, −1.57 to 5.40). An analytical approach to the nonlinear dynamic response of blast-loaded composite plates
abstract: Introduction The fully nonlinear transient dynamic response of moderately thick laminated composite plates subjected to extreme blast overpressures is rigorously investigated. To accurately capture structural behavior under high-intensity shock waves, the mathematical formulation integrates First-order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT) with von Kármán large-deflection kinematics, accounting for both transverse shear flexibility and crucial membrane-bending coupling. Methods Spatial discretization of the governing partial differential equations, derived via Hamilton's principle, is executed using the exact Navier double-Fourier series. A primary contribution of this work is the highly efficient resolution of the resulting strongly nonlinear and coupled ordinary differential equations governing the transient dynamic system. This robust mathematical treatment is accomplished by implementing an unconditionally stable implicit Newmark-β time-integration scheme seamlessly coupled with a nested Newton-Raphson iterative algorithm, ensuring rapid convergence even under severe geometric deformations. The explosive load is mathematically modeled utilizing the modified Friedlander exponential function. title: Response of tic and obsessive-compulsive symptoms to striosomal dopaminergic modulation in tic-related OCD: an open-label pilot study
abstract: Objectives This study investigated the therapeutic potential of striosomes in addressing ICSDs, focusing on the treatment response of tic and obsessive-compulsive (OC) symptoms in tic-related OCD (T-OCD) to a pharmacological intervention designed to enhance striosomal dopamine signaling through D1-type receptors (D1Rs). Methods Ten participants with T-OCD [30% male; mean age, 40.5 years (SD 20.1); mean age at onset, 9.2 years (SD 4.1)] received L-DOPA/carbidopa (50 mg) plus chlorpromazine-phenolphthalinate (5 mg), with doses increased stepwise to three times daily over 8 weeks, then maintained for 1 year. We used the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS) and the Yale-Brown Obsessive-Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) for clinical assessments. For statistical analyses, we used repeated-measures ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc tests and calculated partial eta squared (η 2 ) to report effect sizes. Results The study cohort showed significant, sustained improvements in both tics and OCD symptoms. At one-year follow-up, Total Tic Severity Scale scores on the YGTSS decreased by 73.3% ( n = 10; mean difference, −11.0; 95% CI, −13.99 to −8.04; p = 0.0025; η 2 = 0.715) compared with the baseline. In parallel, Y-BOCS scores decreased by 85.1% ( n = 10; mean difference, −13.10; 95% CI, −17.71 to −8.49; p = 0.0004; η 2 = 0.639). No adverse effects were reported during this one-year study. abstract: Objective To compare the PBMC proteome of patients with nAMD and an inadequate response to aflibercept, relative to controls without retinal pathology, with two published monocyte transcriptomic datasets, in order to quantify gene- and pathway-level concordance across molecular layers and to identify features shared across datasets. Participants and controls Twelve patients with nAMD and an inadequate response to aflibercept and 9 controls without retinal pathology were included. For cross-omic comparison, two public monocyte transcriptomic datasets were used: GSE76237, including 14 treatment-naïve patients with nAMD and 15 age-matched controls, and GSE222647, including 27 previously treated patients with nAMD stratified by anti-VEGF treatment burden (15 low-burden and 12 high-burden patients). Methods Proteomics PBMCs were profiled by data-independent acquisition LC/MS-MS. Differential abundance was assessed with limma, followed by network clustering and functional enrichment analysis. The proteomic signature was compared at gene and pathway (Hallmark) level with 2 public monocyte transcriptomic datasets: single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE222647) and microarray (GSE76237). Main outcome measures Differentially abundant protein groups and enriched pathways; overlap and directional concordance of genes and Hallmark pathways between the proteomic and transcriptomic datasets. title: Clinical Factors Associated With Response and Outcomes in Intravenous Ketamine Treatment for Depression
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to explore the clinical factors associated with response in patients receiving ketamine, evaluating changes in suicidality in each treatment session and the side effects of ketamine infusion therapy for depression. Methods: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted using electronic medical records from 90 patients treated with subanesthetic ketamine infusions between 2019 and 2023. Depression and suicidality scores were measured by the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS). Clinical response was defined as a 50% or greater reduction in MADRS score at the final treatment session. The primary outcome was clinical factors associated with response in patients treated with ketamine. Results: Of the 90 patients, 35 were classified as responders. Logistic regression analysis identified baseline suicidality scores on MADRS (adjusted OR: 1.46, P =0.019) and comorbid anxiety disorder (adjusted OR: 4.39, P =0.048) as significantly associated with treatment response. Generalized estimating equation analysis revealed that each additional ketamine session was associated with a significant reduction in MADRS (coefficient =−1.11, P <0.001) and suicidality scores (coefficient =−0.14, P <0.001). Side effects occurred more frequently in nonresponders. Conclusions: These findings suggest that baseline suicidality and comorbid anxiety disorders are import…

title: Experiences From Implementation of a Hospital Ward Sepsis Response Team at a Large Academic Medical Center
abstract: Hospital-onset sepsis is associated with high mortality and dedicated sepsis response teams can expedite identification and interventions for high-risk patients. Many such teams described in the literature are primarily active in emergency departments or intensive care units. For large academic medical centers with multiple care teams and nursing units, a sepsis response team focused on hospital ward (HW) patients may standardize care of hospitalized septic patients before they develop irreversible organ injury and require critical care stabilization. Here we present our experience establishing the Sepsis Emergency Response Team, an Advanced Practice Provider-led team designed to identify patients with early signs of sepsis on HWs across a large academic medical center.

title: Psychological reward and physiological demand in virtual cycling: an exploratory within-subject study
abstract: Virtual environments are often added to exercise equipment to make exercise more engaging, although previous work has often emphasised enjoyment. This exploratory within-subject study compared stationary cycling with screen-based virtual cycling in 15 adults (6 women, 9 men; aged 20–59 years). Each participant completed one 10-min, self-paced session in each condition, in counterbalanced order, on the same recumbent bicycle with fixed resistance. After each session, participants completed the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory and rated their perceived exertion (Borg 6–20); heart rate and cadence were recorded every minute. Enjoyment was higher after virtual cycling (mean difference 2.31 points on a 1–7 scale, 95% CI [1.61, 3.00]), as was value/usefulness (1.38 [0.56, 2.20]); 14 and 12 participants, respectively, reported higher scores. Both paired t-test differences remained after Holm correction. Differences in perceived competence, effort/importance, and pressure/tension were smaller, with confidence intervals including zero. Heart rate (4.9 bpm, 95% CI [-0.04, 9.8]) and cadence (2.8 rpm [-2.4, 7.9]) showed no clear difference between conditions. Perceived exertion was slightly higher during virtual cycling (0.8 points [0.01, 1.59]), but this difference did not remain after correction. Toxoplasma gondii SRS34A mRNA vaccine elicits protective immune response against toxoplasmosis in mice
abstract: Toxoplasmosis is a prevalent zoonotic parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii , which infects nearly all warm-blooded animals including humans. It causes substantial economic losses to the livestock industry and poses a considerable threat to public health. Currently, therapeutic options for toxoplasmosis remain highly limited, and no safe and effective vaccine is widely licensed for human use. In this study, we developed a LNP encapsulated mRNA vaccine encoding SRS34A, a surface localized protein highly expressed across developmental stages of T. gondii . ICR mice ( n = 5 per group) were intramuscularly immunized three times at a dose of 10 μg per mouse with the SRS34A-mRNA-LNP vaccine. Vaccination elicited a balanced Th1/Th2 immune response, as evidenced by high SRS34A-specific IgG titers and significantly elevated levels of both Th1-type cytokines (IL-12, TNF-α, IFN-γ) and the Th2-type cytokine IL-4. Challenge assays showed that vaccination conferred partial protection against T. gondii infection. In the chronic infection model with 100 type II ME49 tachyzoites (i.p.), vaccinated mice achieved an 80% survival rate versus 60% in controls, although the survival difference was not statistically significant. Meanwhile, both the number of brain cysts in vaccinated mice were significantly reduced compared with controls. For acute infection with the virulent type I RH strain,…

title: Students’ Response Given by Welding Engineering Study Program at Politeknik Perkapalan Negeri Surabaya to the Study of Part of Speech in English Learning
abstract: Part of Speech becomes the basic learning of English which must be understood by the students in Learning. This study focused on the students’ response after getting the teaching about the basic patterns of English. The Data of this research was the information given by the students of Welding Engineering in Politeknik Perkapalan Negeri Surabaya. There were 28 students filling the questionnaires after getting the teaching of English Lecture. The data was analysed quantitively by using the diagram to know the students’ responses. The result showed that 78,6 % answered they knew well on the basic patterns and 21,4 % answered the did not understand them well. However, the students stated that 92,9 % learning about the basic patterns helped them speak English better. Even they gave comments that Speaking and Structure were related each other. It could be concluded that learning part of speech help the students understand the sentence accurately so they speak more fluently and accurately.

title: Analytical framework for delay analysis implementation system
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study is to develop an analytical framework for delay analysis implementation system (DAIS) that can perform any method of delay analysis using an Excel-based system while explicitly addressing complicated factors such as float ownership, the treatment of concurrent delays, critical path shifts, multiple calendars and contractual constraints. Design/methodology/approach Delay analysis tools are driven by static, dynamic, additive and subtractive methods. While each method has distinct strengths, it also has some limitations. The calculations involved in DAIS are performed in a Microsoft Excel-based spreadsheet, which automate the implementation of any of the delay analysis methods through a series of mathematical functions and numerical computations. Findings DAIS quantifies project delays and assigns responsibility to the appropriate party. It facilitates granting time extensions and determining liquidated damages. DAIS has been tested in a case and the outcomes are satisfactory. Originality/value No systematic effort has ever been made to establish foundations for an automated system capable of performing each of the four methods of delay analysis and therefore replacing existing labor-intensive and error-prone manual practices. Self-reported confidence in biorisk management after a multisectoral step-down training in Botswana: a cross-sectional post-training evaluation of 26 professionals from 24 institutions
abstract: Background Biosafety and biosecurity capacity across Africa remains low relative to expanding laboratory infrastructure. Continental averages on the Africa Health Security Index stand at 14.9 of 100 for biosecurity and 18.2 for biosafety. The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) Regional Training and Certification Program seeks to address this by certifying regional subject matter experts who deliver training within their own countries. Whether such step-down training reaches beyond the clinical laboratory sector, and where its effects are weakest, has not been well described. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional post-training evaluation of a seven-module biorisk management course delivered in Botswana in 2024 to 26 professionals drawn from 24 institutions across seven sectors, recruited under a One Health framework spanning human/animal health, food safety, environment, defense, regulation, transport, and academia. Curriculum content was adapted from the Sandia National Laboratories core biorisk management materials. Participants completed a 61-item, 5-point Likert scale questionnaire post-course. The outcome measured was self-reported confidence, expressed as the proportion selecting agree or strongly agree (positive response rate) and the mean Likert score. title: Collaborating with Machines: A Qualitative Study on Job Satisfaction Among Banking Employees
abstract: Artificial intelligence is no longer a futuristic concept, it is the defining technology of 21st century, embedding itself into every aspect of our lives. Industry 5.0 communicate the next phase of industrialisation focussing on the association between Human imagination or creativity with the AI driven technology. The swift progress of technologies and artificial intelligence has touched and transformed every sector and the Banking sector is not left out of this either leading to enhanced interaction and dependence of employees and the system. The human-machine collaboration has become a prime component of the workplaces now where employees are working in a data driven environment and presence of both is equally valuable. It refers to the interplay between the technological system and employees of the organisation. The aim of this collaboration is to improve or enhance productivity of the organisation by easing out the task of employees. However, working with machines and automated environment has an impact on the perception and satisfaction level of the employee too. The present study “Collaborating with machines: A qualitative study on Job Satisfaction among Banking employees” examines the influence of human machine collaboration on job satisfaction level of the banking employees. Over the past decade, the banking sector has seen a massive upgradation in the technology adopti…

title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen detection and management in ICU patients with sepsis
abstract: Background Rapid and accurate pathogen identification is essential for precision antimicrobial therapy in sepsis, but conventional microbiological testing (CMT) is often limited by low sensitivity, long turnaround time, and difficulty in detecting fastidious or atypical pathogens. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and clinical utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with sepsis. Methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled 162 adult patients with sepsis admitted to the ICU of the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University between January 2022 and September 2024. Matched clinical specimens from the same infection site were tested using both mNGS and CMT. The diagnostic performance of mNGS, pathogen spectrum, differences according to immune status, clinical adoption of mNGS results, antimicrobial adjustment, and patient outcomes were analyzed. Results Among the 162 patients, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was the predominant specimen (107/162, 66.05%), followed by blood (31/162, 19.14%), the cohort therefore primarily represents severe pulmonary infection rather than sepsis arising from diverse anatomical sources, and the findings should be interpreted in this context. mNGS yielded a significantly higher detection rate than CMT (81.37% vs. 56.17%, P<0.001) and identified 47 pathogenic species…

title: Strategic management accounting on economic performance in Thailand
abstract: Purpose This study examines how sustainability-oriented accounting practices are associated with economic performance (EP) through competitive advantage (CA) and whether digital accounting capability (DAC) changes these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capability theory, partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) is used to analyze multi-source data collected in three waves from 165 Thai listed firms. Environmental management accounting (EMA) is positively associated with strategic management accounting (SMA). SMA and environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance are positively associated with CA, which is positively associated with EP. Findings The indirect effects of SMA and ESG performance on EP through CA are significant, whereas their corresponding direct effects are not. DAC positively moderates the relationship between SMA and CA; however, this effect is small. Although the multi-source time-lagged design provides temporal and source separation among some constructs, the observational design does not establish causality. The findings should be interpreted as context-specific associations consistent with the proposed theoretical ordering, not causal evidence. The findings support an integrated interpretation of these relationships among Thai firms. CA is an important statistical link, wher…

title: The role of incentive mechanisms and intellectual property awareness in retaining R&D personnel in Chinese biopharmaceutical companies: the mediating role of perceived R&D staffing adequacy
abstract: Retaining research and development (R&D) personnel is a strategic challenge for Chinese biopharmaceutical companies because innovation depends on cumulative knowledge, long project cycles, and stable interdisciplinary teams. This study examines how career satisfaction, incentive mechanisms, intellectual property awareness, psychological contract fulfillment, and team collaboration influence R&D personnel retention, with perceived R&D staffing adequacy as a structural mediator. Data were obtained from 650 valid questionnaires collected from R&D employees in 27 biopharmaceutical companies; 900 questionnaires were distributed, yielding a 72.2% valid response rate. Regression, mediation, and firm-size subgroup analyses were conducted. The results show that all five antecedents are positively associated with retention. Career satisfaction has the strongest direct association, followed by psychological contract fulfillment, incentive mechanisms, intellectual property awareness, and team collaboration. Perceived staffing adequacy significantly transmits the associations of career satisfaction and incentive mechanisms with retention, while the continuing significance of the corresponding direct paths is consistent with partial mediation. Firm-size comparisons suggest that career satisfaction, incentives, and staffing adequacy are more salient in small and medium-sized enterprises, wher…

Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis in a Patient with Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report
abstract: Introduction: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus (DM) that may be accompanied by acute kidney injury (AKI), particularly in the presence of severe dehydration and precipitating infections. Case: A 32-year-old male presented with generalized weakness, polydipsia, and polyuria for two weeks. His random blood glucose level was 803 mg/dL. Further evaluation revealed DKA, stage 1 AKI of presumed pre-renal origin, and suspected urinary tract infection (UTI). Discussion: The patient had no previous history of diabetes mellitus or hypertension but had a family history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and reported frequent consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages and a sedentary lifestyle. Management consisted of intravenous fluid resuscitation, insulin infusion, potassium replacement, treatment of the suspected UTI, and close monitoring of metabolic and renal parameters. After three days of treatment, the patient improved clinically and recovered renal function. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of early recognition of DKA and identification of concurrent AKI and potential infectious triggers. Prompt fluid resuscitation, insulin therapy, electrolyte correction, and treatment of precipitating factors are essential to prevent further organ dysfunction and improve clinical outcomes.

title: Beyond behaviouralism: rethinking sustainability governance
abstract: Purpose This paper critically aims to examine behaviouralism as an influential problem-defining orientation in tourism and hospitality sustainability research, focusing on how it shapes problem framing, responsibility allocation and engagement with sustainability transitions. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a critical conceptual problematisation of recurring research logics. Drawing on purposively selected streams of behaviour-centred sustainability research, critical scholarship and alternative theoretical perspectives, it examines how assumptions about agency, causality, actionability and responsibility shape sustainability knowledge. Findings Behaviouralism can narrow sustainability challenges into behaviourally actionable problems, foregrounding individual or firm responsibility while backgrounding governance, political-economic conditions and justice. The analysis shows how ontological and methodological assumptions influence what becomes visible and actionable as a sustainability problem. The Behavioural Governance Matrix distinguishes individual and collective agency across behaviour-centred and governance-centred forms of actionability. Practical implications The matrix provides a basis for examining when sustainability responsibility is concentrated on individual actors and when wider organisational or governance conditions also require attention. Comparative evaluation of integrated weed management strategies for sustainable sunflower production under field conditions in India
abstract: Weeds that emerge early in the season limit sunflower ( Helianthus annuus L.) yields in India, and the rising cost and scarcity of farm labour have made repeated hand weeding increasingly uneconomical. Field experiments were conducted over three consecutive late monsoon (late kharif ) seasons (2023, 2024 and 2025) at the Zonal Agricultural Research Station, University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, under the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Sunflower. Seven weed-management practices, comprising pre- and post-emergence herbicides, mechanical and manual weeding, the farmers’ practice, a weed-free check and a weedy check, were compared in a randomized complete block design with three replications. All treatments were imposed at a single wide-row spacing (75 × 25 cm), so row spacing itself was not an experimental factor. Pre-emergence pendimethalin (1.0 kg a.i. ha −1 ) followed by a directed post-emergence spray of quizalofop ethyl (62 g a.i. ha −1 ) at 15–20 days after sowing was the most effective practical treatment. Among the practical treatments, it recorded the lowest weed dry weight (41.3 g m −2 ) and the highest weed control efficiency (92.7%), and its seed yield (1646.3 kg ha −1 ) was statistically on par with the weed-free check (1730.7 kg ha −1 ) and about 53% higher than that of the farmers’ practice (1073.0 kg ha −1 ). Because i…

title: Optimization of biofertilizer type and application method for partial substitution of inorganic nitrogen in maize under a rice–maize cropping system
abstract: Abstract Background Intensive maize production relies on mineral nitrogen (N), but reduced N availability and low N-use efficiency constrain productivity and profitability. Biofertilizers may enable partial substitution of mineral N; however, the comparative effects of microbial type and application method on soil N cycling, plant N acquisition and productivity remain insufficiently integrated. This study evaluated biofertilizer-based partial N substitution in maize under a rice–maize cropping system and tested the hypothesis that 80% recommended N (RDN) combined with an appropriate biofertilizer could maintain yield while improving N cycling and economic efficiency. Results A two-year field experiment compared 100% RDN without biofertilizer (T 1 ) with 80% RDN plus Azotobacter , Azospirillum , their combination or a bacterial consortium applied by seed or soil methods. The seed-applied bacterial consortium (T 5 ) produced the strongest integrated response ( P < 0.05), with grain yield 7.4% higher than T 1 and statistically comparable, while stover yield increased by 8.0%. Relative to T 1 , T 5 increased available N, P 2 O 5 and K 2 O by 12.2, 9.5 and 11.9%, respectively, and ammoniacal-N and nitrate-N by up to 39.2 and 30.5%. Microbial populations and urease, dehydrogenase and phosphatase activities were also enhanced. N uptake increased by up to 56.4%, while partial factor pr…
