title: Mechanical Tension Reduction Therapies for the Management of Keloids and Hypertrophic Scars: A Systematic Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanical tension reduction therapies have gained attention as potential treatments for keloids and hypertrophic scars. However, their efficacy and safety remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review evaluated the therapeutic outcomes of these modalities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two reviewers independently searched PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Embase for eligible clinical studies on March 17, 2024. Search terms included “keloid,” “hypertrophic scar,” “tension reduction,” “tension offloading,” “tension relief,” “super-tension relief,” and “ultra-reduced tension.” The inclusion criteria were predefined. Owing to study heterogeneity, a narrative analysis was conducted. RESULTS: Sixteen studies involving 790 cases were included. The interventions consisted of tension reduction suturing techniques (TRST) and tension offloading devices (TOD). Tension reduction suturing techniques showed significant improvements in scar scores, with over 70% improvement from baseline. Keloid recurrence rates ranged from 1.7% to 8.8%. The studies of tension offloading devices showed favorable outcomes, but evidence was limited by few studies and small sample sizes. Reported complications were infrequent, supporting a favorable safety profile. CONCLUSION TRST may benefit pathologic scar management, particularly as part of multimodal therapy, but current evidence remai…

title: Organic loading effects on physicochemical performance and metal attenuation in an integrated vertical flow constructed wetland–double filtration system
abstract: Abstract Vertical flow constructed wetlands coupled with filtration can provide compact post-treatment of anaerobic effluents, but their performance under variable organic loading remains insufficiently characterized. A pilot-scale vertical-flow constructed wetland followed by coagulant-free double filtration was evaluated using upflow anaerobic sludge blanket effluent fortified with cadmium, lead, chromium, nickel, and copper under organic loading rates of 25.0, 44.0, and 91.8 g COD/m 2 · d. Physicochemical variables and metal concentrations were monitored at the UASB, VFCW, and final double-filtration stages. Chemical oxygen demand and biochemical oxygen demand removal efficiencies remained at least 87.7% and 91.0%, respectively, whereas turbidity removal decreased descriptively from 94.3% to 63.1% across the sequential loading gradient. Metal removal efficiencies also declined descriptively from the lowest- to the highest-loading condition: Cd from 90.3% to 75.7%, Pb from 94.0% to 75.0%, Cr from 90.4% to 70.9%, Ni from 91.8% to 60.4%, and Cu from 92.5% to 74.4%. Friedman tests indicated significant treatment stage differences for all evaluated physicochemical variables except pH and for all five metals. An integrated block-balanced partial redundancy analysis (pRDA), conditioned on sampling event, revealed a strong treatment stage effect (partial R 2 = 0.898, pseudo- F = 70.…

title: Highly Selective Transfer Hydrogenation of Biomass-Derived Carbonyl Compounds in the Isopropanol-Based Endogenous Hydrogen System over a Zirconium-Hexamethylenetetramine Coordination Catalyst
abstract: Abstract Isopropanol-based endogenous hydrogen systems have been extensively employed for the catalytic transfer hydrogenation (CTH) of biomass-derived carbonyl compounds (BDCCs), in which constructing appropriate Lewis acid-base catalysts is the core task. At present, numerous studies are principally concentrated on zirconium-organic acid coordination catalysts. Still, most of them introduce a few Brønsted acid sites (BASs), which will inevitably influence the formation of target products. In this work, a novel zirconium-hexamethylenetetramine coordination catalyst (Zr-HMT) was designed and synthesized in ethanol at room temperature via a simple and green self-assembly process, in which HMT was used as a cheap organic base ligand. The systematic characterization results demonstrated that Zr-HMT contained abundant zirconium-nitrogen active species (Zr-Nx) with high Lewis acid-base strengths. Meanwhile, it lacked BASs, which could not only guarantee the smooth progression of CTH but also avert the occurrence of side reactions, such as acetalization and etherification. Thus, Zr-HMT showed wonderful catalytic performance. When it was used for the CTH of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) in isopropanol, the yield and selectivity of 2,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)furan (BHMF) could be achieved at 98.7% with an apparent turnover frequency of 6.98 h–1 at 140 °C for 2 h. title: Expectations versus reality: factors shaping retention intentions among higher-level apprentice consultants in Northern Ireland
abstract: Purpose This study examines how higher-level apprentice consultants at different stages describe the alignment between workplace expectations and experience, and how these accounts relate to stated intentions to remain with their employer post apprenticeship. Design/methodology/approach A cross-cohort, pseudo-longitudinal qualitative design was adopted. Separate semi-structured focus groups involved 19 apprentices at early (n = 4), middle (n = 7) and later (n = 8) stages. Microsoft Teams transcripts were checked against recordings and analysed manually using a hybrid thematic approach. Findings Five themes were identified: progression and future clarity; role misalignment; mentorship and development; organisational communication and work–life balance. Early-stage accounts emphasised support and belonging, mid-programme accounts emphasised role fit and development and final-year accounts emphasised credible progression outcomes. These are cross-cohort differences, not evidence of individual change or actual turnover. Research limitations/implications The single-organisation study has a small, uneven sample and examines retention intentions rather than behaviour. The findings and proposed framework are exploratory and require longitudinal, multi-organisation testing. title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine learning analyses identify DDX47 as a candidate diagnostic biomarker in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a highly heterogeneous hematological malignancy, and challenges remain in clinical diagnosis and the assessment of treatment response. This study aimed to identify candidate diagnostic biomarkers for AML and investigate their associations with the immune microenvironment and treatment response. Methods Transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) databases were integrated to identify candidate genes through differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and three machine learning algorithms. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with external validation performed using the independent GSE9476 cohort. Associations between the candidate gene and immune cell infiltration and predicted drug sensitivity were further investigated. Its clinical relevance and potential functional role were subsequently evaluated through expression analyses of bone marrow samples from patients with AML and experiments involving AML cell lines treated with venetoclax following DDX47 knockdown. Results DDX47 was consistently identified as a candidate feature gene by three machine learning algorithms. DDX47 expression was significantly elevated in AML samples, with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.824 in th…

title: Development and validation of machine learning models to predict mortality in elderly patients with chronic critical illness: a multi-cohort study using MIMIC, eICU, and a Chinese dataset
abstract: Background and objective Patients with chronic critical illness (CCI) often require prolonged mechanical ventilation and other ICU interventions. The significant morbidity and mortality linked to CCI make the early identification of risk factors an imperative clinical objective. Methods Data from elderly CCI patients were sourced from the MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and eICU databases. An independent external validation cohort of 308 patients was additionally collected from a Chinese hospital. PSM was applied to the eICU cohort to address class imbalance. Feature selection was conducted using LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm. Twelve machine learning models were developed and validated. To identify the optimal model, we evaluated AUC, accuracy, F1-score, sensitivity, and specificity. Calibration and clinical utility were further assessed using calibration plots and DCA, with SHAP employed for model interpretation. Results A total of 1,628 elderly CCI patients were included across three cohorts (MIMIC derivation: 928; eICU: 392; Chinese local: 308). Thirty variables with significant differences between survivors and non-survivors were identified in the derivation cohort. Eight key predictors were selected: age, AKI stage, hemoglobin, platelets, RDW, potassium, body temperature, and PaCO 2 , all measured on ICU day 14. title: Learning-based vision-guided precision landing for autonomous UAVs: comparative evaluation of reinforcement learning and evolutionary controller optimization
abstract: This paper presents a vision-guided framework for the terminal landing phase of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and compares two approaches to adaptive control: model-free policy learning with tabular Q-learning and genetic-algorithm optimization of a structured feedback controller (GA-PID), which in the investigated implementation operates in proportional–derivative form, which in the investigated implementation operates in proportional–derivative form. Both controllers share the same perception pipeline, in which a low-cost downward-facing camera detects an ArUco fiducial marker, and require neither GNSS nor external positioning during this phase. The controllers were trained and optimized in a ROS 2/Gazebo simulation and transferred to a physical multirotor UAV, so that both are evaluated with the same sensing, platform, landing task, and evaluation protocol. The results show that tabular Q-learning acquires a functional landing policy despite its compact state representation. In real-flight trials, the GA-PID controller landed significantly faster, whereas the differences in final accuracy and success rate were not statistically significant with ten trials per controller. In simulation, the GA-PID controller produced smoother trajectories, and its practical insensitivity to a change in illumination was confirmed by equivalence testing. The findings characterize the two spe…

title: Improving prostate cancer risk stratification using machine learning applied to routine PSA testing: a multicenter study
abstract: Background Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening reduces mortality but suffers from low specificity, leading to overdiagnosis and unnecessary biopsies. While specialized biomarkers exist, their high cost and limited availability hinder widespread implementation. Machine learning (ML) offers a scalable approach to enhance risk stratification using routinely collected clinical data. Methods We conducted a retrospective, large-scale multicenter study including 4,241 Brazilian men (709 prostate cancer cases; 3,532 controls) derived from a nationwide network spanning 421 clinical settings across 10 Brazilian states. Participants were men referred for prostate evaluation. Controls were defined by negative histopathology or PI-RADS 1–2 multiparametric MRI (diagnostic-evaluation cohort with a mixed reference standard). An interpretable machine learning model (PSA model) integrating total PSA, free-to-total PSA ratio, and age was evaluated on a held-out test set and, for robustness, by leave-one-group-out validation across four geographic groups. Incremental value from PSA density (PSAD), PSA kinetics, and complete blood count markers was also assessed. Results The PSA model significantly outperformed a fixed PSA threshold (≥4.0 ng/mL) on the test set (AUC of 0.73 vs. 0.63, p < 0.001). In the PSA gray zone (4–10 ng/mL), discrimination improved from 0.50 to 0.67. At the training-d…

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Phishing URL Detection: Integrating LSTM and CNN for Enhanced Cybersecurity
abstract: This manuscript presents a character-level deep learning model that integrates a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) layer to detect phishing URLs. The model is trained and evaluated using the PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset, a publicly available benchmark recently released through the UCI Machine Learning Repository. The dataset comprises 235,795 URLs, including 134,850 legitimate URLs and 100,945 phishing URLs. URLs are tokenized at the character level and padded to a fixed length of 200 characters before being mapped to a 128-dimensional embedding space. The resulting representations are then passed through a one-dimensional convolutional (Conv1D) layer to extract local patterns, followed by max pooling and a Bidirectional LSTM layer to capture long-range sequential dependencies. Finally, a dense layer with a sigmoid activation function performs binary classification. On a held-out test set, the model achieves an accuracy of 97.8%, precision of 97.2%, recall of 98.1%, an F1-score of 97.6%, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.987. Its performance is also compared with that of recent state-of-the-art phishing detection models reported in the literature from 2023 to 2026. Overall, this study contributes to the development of reliable and intelligent URL-based threat detection systems…

title: RELEVANSI FILSAFAT PENDIDIKAN R.A. KARTINI TERHADAP LITERASI MEMBACA DAN MENULIS DI SEKOLAH DASAR
abstract: ABSTRACT Reading and writing literacy in elementary education involves not only language proficiency but also the development of critical thinking, independence, and the ability to express ideas. This study aims to examine R.A. Kartini’s educational thought and its relevance to the development of reading and writing literacy through humanistic and emancipatory perspectives. The research employed a literature review with a historical-philosophical approach. The primary source consisted of Kartini’s letters in Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang, translated by Armijn Pane. The analysis involved examining the historical context, identifying educational ideas, and reflecting on their relevance to literacy practices in elementary schools. The findings reveal three interconnected ideas: reading as a means of broadening knowledge, writing as a medium for articulating experiences and thoughts, and education as a space for developing human potential with dignity. Kartini’s experience in organizing reading and writing activities for girls further demonstrates the relevance of her educational thought to literacy development. The Tuesday Reading and Thursday Writing activities at SD Muhammadiyah 4 Surabaya are presented as contextual illustrations rather than as objects of effectiveness evaluation. This study concludes that Kartini’s educational thought offers a reflective foundation for emancipa…

Classification of Smectite Content in Geological Materials Using Hyperspectral Imaging and Deep Learning
abstract: Abstract Smectite-bearing rocks may slake, swell, and weaken, posing risks in tunnel engineering. This study examined whether a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) could classify powdered rock specimens into X-ray diffraction (XRD)-estimated smectite-content classes (< 10 or ≥ 10 wt.%) using visible-to-near-infrared (VNIR; 450–950 nm) hyperspectral data. Specimens comprised hydrothermally altered andesite and tuff-siltstone mainly affected by diagenesis, and a separate model was developed for each domain. Three levels of evaluation are distinguished: (i) spectral-level five-fold cross-validation, with folds split by specimen and repeated with ten random seeds; (ii) within-domain tests; and (iii) cross-domain tests. Mean cross-validation accuracy and Macro-F1 (mean ± SD) were 74.45 ± 5.32% and 74.09 ± 5.75% for andesite, and 72.28 ± 2.93% and 71.44 ± 3.25% for tuff-siltstone. Within-domain test accuracy was 100% ( n = 8) and 88.89% ( n = 9), respectively, but fell to 53.33% and 57.58% in cross-domain tests. Occlusion analysis identified different wavelength regions; because lithology and geological history were confounded, these regions do not demonstrate direct detection of smectite. What factors predict the innovation of Chinese family firms: empirical evidence based on machine learning
abstract: Purpose Prior studies on family firm innovation have focused primarily on causal explanations and isolated variable significance, but lack a prediction-oriented approach that systematically compares the relative importance of multiple predictors. Drawing on the capability–willingness–pressure framework, this paper aims to identify the key predictors of innovation in Chinese family firms and to reconcile inconsistent findings in prior research. By integrating a prediction-oriented perspective to complement traditional causal inference, this study examines how the family, firm and environmental characteristics jointly predict innovation input and output. Design/methodology/approach Based on a systematic review of 102 empirical studies, this paper constructs a multidimensional framework encompassing 30 predictors across family, firm and external environmental factors. Using Chinese A-share listed family firms from 2010 to 2024, the final samples include 10,078 firm-year observations for R&D investment and 10,145 firm-year observations for R&D output. R&D investment is measured by R&D intensity, while R&D output is measured by patent applications. The study uses the gradient boosting regression tree algorithm. title: Differentiating vestibular migraine from posterior circulation ischemia initially presenting with dizziness/vertigo: a machine learning approach
abstract: Introduction Vestibular migraine (VM) and posterior circulation ischemia (PCI) share initial dizziness or vertigo as chief manifestations with substantial clinical overlap, and the limited diagnostic utility of available examinations complicates their differentiation, creating an urgent clinical demand for multidimensional assessment strategies to reduce misdiagnosis rates and improve diagnosis and treatment. Methods This retrospective study consecutively recruited 571 patients presenting with initial dizziness or vertigo, including 382 VM cases and 189 PCI cases. The dataset was randomly split into a 70% training set and a 30% test set. Optimal predictive features were screened by combining univariable area-under-the-curve analysis, LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm, and five machine-learning algorithms were further compared in terms of classification performance and clinical interpretability. Results Nine core predictive features were finally identified, and all five models achieved favorable discriminatory performance in validation. Among these models, XGBoost and Random Forest demonstrated strong and comparable diagnostic performance. Discussion This multidimensional machine-learning model can accurately distinguish VM from PCI in patients with new-onset dizziness or vertigo, and may serve as a potential auxiliary tool for differential diagnosis after initial clinic…

Occult odontogenic deep neck infection presenting as a reversible acute heart failure mimic: a multimodal diagnostic case report
abstract: Background Deep neck infections (DNIs) may rarely present with a cardiopulmonary collapse rather than classic orofacial symptoms. A concurrent diffuse goiter can further complicate causal interpretation. In this report, we present this case as a diagnostic synthesis of recognized complications and not as proof of a new pathophysiological mechanism. Case presentation A 52-year-old female with untreated hyperthyroidism presented with unexplained coma following a 2-month subclinical cough. Initial examinations revealed global left ventricular hypokinesis (an left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 25%), diffuse ST-segment depression, and bilateral pulmonary opacities, highly mimicking acute heart failure. Multiplanar CT imaging results revealed severe parapharyngeal inflammatory edema causing tracheal stenosis, while a multidisciplinary evaluation excluded goiter-induced compression. The results of comprehensive microbiological tests, including bronchoalveolar lavage fluid-mNGS, were negative. Following the failure of initial cephalosporin therapy, empiric escalation to meropenem rapidly normalized the organ function. Serial multimodal imaging confirmed complete resolution of parapharyngeal edema, pulmonary infiltrates, and myocardial stunning by day 9. A severe untreated dental caries was subsequently identified as the hidden infectious source. Conclusions In the case of our…

title: Further evidence supporting the in vitro biocompatibility of a fatty acid-based deep eutectic solvent as a potential carrier for cannabidiol
abstract: Introduction Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are increasingly explored as sustainable media for the extraction and formulation of plant-derived bioactives, yet their biological compatibility remains insufficiently characterized across human cell types. Here, we evaluated the cellular safety of a fatty acid-based DES and cannabidiol (CBD) prepared in this solvent using human keratinocyte (HaCaT) and hepatocyte-like (HepG2) models. Methods A two-phase approach combined MTS-based viability assessment and alkaline comet assay with measurements of reactive oxygen species (ROS), glutathione (GSH), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity following 24-h exposure. In Phase I, cells were exposed to the DES at 0.005–0.02% (v/v) and to the corresponding DES-based CBD formulations containing 0.24–0.98 μg/mL CBD. Results Both the DES and CBD formulation showed low cytotoxicity, with a significant viability reduction occurring only at the highest CBD concentration tested (0.98 μg/mL) in HepG2 cells. No evidence of treatment-induced DNA damage was observed in either cell line. In Phase II, CBD concentrations of 2.5, 5, and 10 μg/mL prepared in the DES were evaluated. Exposure at these concentrations did not significantly reduce HaCaT or HepG2 cell viability and no biologically relevant alterations in intracellular ROS, GSH levels, or SOD activity. title: Hobbesian libertarianism: Uncertainty, liability, and credible commitment
Too Committed to Fail? Credible Revisability and the Strategic Orchestration of Nusantara, New Capitals and Megaprojects under Radical Uncertainty
abstract: Between 2023 and 2026, several high-profile megaprojects underwent cancellation, scope reductions, funding withdrawals, or organizational restructuring. Existing theoretical perspectives explain why project sponsors escalate their commitments, why megaprojects experience cost overruns, how real options generate strategic value, and how orchestrators coordinate actors beyond their direct organizational control. However, these perspectives do not adequately explain how sponsors can maintain credible long-term commitments while preserving the legitimate capacity to revise strategic decisions under radical uncertainty. This article develops a theory of credible revisability by integrating insights from strategic commitment, escalation of commitment, megaproject governance, real options theory, ecosystem orchestration, public-sector dynamic capabilities, and mission-oriented innovation policy. The theoretical synthesis is supported by a comparative documentary analysis of twelve megaprojects and new capital city initiatives. The study identifies commitment displacement—the shift of commitment from enduring public functions toward specific implementation instruments—as a central mechanism through which strategic commitment can evolve into institutional entrenchment. Building on this mechanism, the article introduces Transformational Orchestration for Nexus Endurance (TONE), a governa…

title: The effect of corporate governance on dividend policy under conditions of economic uncertainty: evidence from Egypt
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effect of corporate governance on dividend policy under conditions of economic uncertainty for a sample of 60 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Exchange over the period 2016–2022. Design/methodology/approach Four logistic regression models are used to test the research hypotheses. Model 1 examines the effect of corporate governance on dividend policy. Model 2 assesses whether crisis periods related to the COVID-19 pandemic and the Egyptian currency devaluation moderate the relationship between corporate governance and dividend policy. Models 3 and 4 further explore these effects by examining the moderating roles of the pandemic and the currency devaluation separately. Findings The study finds that dividend payments in Egyptian firms are more likely when boards are smaller, managerial ownership is higher and boards are less independent. However, CEO duality is an insignificant determinant of dividend decisions, and macroeconomic shocks have no significant moderating effect. Practical implications This study presents important implications for regulators and policy makers. Regulators and policymakers may consider the role of macroeconomic conditions when designing governance frameworks, while investors and corporate decision-makers can use governance characteristics to better assess dividend sustainability during periods of heig…

title: Ordinal prototype learning with evidential uncertainty for uncertainty-aware diabetic retinopathy grading
abstract: Introduction Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading systems must recognize when their predictions are unreliable. Most deep learning approaches optimize solely for classification accuracy and produce overconfident predictions, limiting their safety in screening and referral workflows. Existing prototype-based methods do not model ordinal disease progression or calibrated confidence. Methods We propose EviProto-DR, a framework combining grade-supervised ordinal prototype learning with evidential deep learning for DR grading and predictive uncertainty estimation. The framework comprises three components: Grade-Supervised Ordinal Prototypes (GSOP), which produce class-anchored embeddings under a monotonicity constraint reflecting DR severity ordering an Evidential Prototype Classifier (EPC), which derives Dirichlet-based grade predictions and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass and a Prototype-Uncertainty Consistency Loss (PUCL), which aligns prototype geometry with predictive uncertainty. Results On APTOS 2019, EviProto-DR achieves a Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) of 0.918 and an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.061, while achieving a QWK of 0.897 on DDR. External evaluation on MESSIDOR-2 provides an initial assessment of cross-dataset performance without retraining. In a simulated referral setting, the model routes high-uncertainty cases to a specialist whil…

title: Diffusion-based constraint in topology optimization for additive manufacturing
abstract: Abstract This work presents an efficient method for identifying local and global overheating during additive manufacturing. The manufacturing process offers nearly complete design freedom without additional constraints. Regions prone to overheating must be integrated into the build platform using optimized support structures that enhance thermal conductivity during manufacturing. A single steady-state heat transfer analysis will be conducted instead of recreating the additive manufacturing process with its numerous layers. This greatly increases efficiency and reduces computational time. The information from this presented method can be used to optimize designs suited for additive manufacturing, thereby reducing overheating issues. As a result, geometries can be generated that do not require support structures, improving overall build quality. The current implementation is based on homogeneous, structured two-dimensional grids with potential extension to unstructured three-dimensional meshes. An extension to unstructured three-dimensional meshes is feasible, enabling application within widely used software solutions. The foundation of the code is provided by the open-source finite element solver CalculiX combined with a Python optimization module. The code is available at https://github.com/stoli89/topopt4ccx .

title: Trade Structure Optimization and Breakthrough Pathways for Chongqing–ASEAN Trade under the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor Initiative
abstract: In the context of the development of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, trade ties between Chongqing and ASEAN have continued to deepen. The corridor has created new opportunities for inland regions to open up further and participate in the regional division of labor, although trade structure upgrading continues to face several constraints. Focusing on trade between Chongqing and ASEAN, this paper examines trade structure optimization through product and market diversification, the upgrading of trade modes, and the extension of firms into higher-value-added segments of cross-border industrial chains. It then analyzes the mechanisms through which corridor development may promote such optimization. The analysis indicates that trade between Chongqing and ASEAN has expanded overall and industrial ties have strengthened. However, challenges remain, including insufficient upgrading toward higher-value-added products and activities, inadequate cross-border industrial coordination, and limited diversification into new markets. Accordingly, this paper proposes pathways for optimizing trade structure through industrial upgrading, cross-border industrial cooperation, the development of trade services, and improved corridor connectivity. These measures aim to translate the corridor’s advantages into stronger industrial capabilities and greater trade competitiveness.

title: Constrained route optimization on the Brenta mountain trail network
abstract: Routing over mountainous terrain is a challenging problem, as a practical route has to consider the horizontal distance as well as the extra cost incurred by elevation changes. This study investigates preference -based route optimization within a Digital Elevation Model (DEM)-integrated mountain trail network in the Brenta Dolomites, Trentino, northern Italy. A Digital Elevation Model (DEM) is a way of modeling terrain on a computer, taking a continuous landscape and turning it into a grid of discrete, connected points with different movement costs. Previous studies have shown that DEM-based least-cost path techniques and the Dijkstra's algorithm can effectively search for pathways in mountainous terrains. These methods, however, are typically based on a predefined cost function and have limited capability to incorporate explicit terrain constraints. For spatial planning problems, mathematical optimization methods have been applied to handle complex constraints and decision variables. This research extends these ideas by developing a constrained optimization framework for route selection in an integrated mountain trail system of a DEM. This study addresses that question by constructing a real, DEM-derived weighted graph for Brenta Dolomites, a mountain group in Trentino, northern Italy, near Madonna di Campiglio, in which nodes represent discrete terrain locations and edges rep…

Scoring-Driven Context Memory and Token Optimization for Rapid Prototyping of Scalable Multimodal Intelligent Agents: The MERIT Framework
abstract: Frameworks such as AutoGen and CrewAI make it fast to assemble multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs), yet as a prototype scales the binding constraint shifts from reasoning quality to how context is selected, retained, and emitted under a finite token budget. This article extends a prior conference study that compared two prototyping frameworks and catalogued the open challenges of LLM-based agents. The conference work observed that coarse controls such as fixed conversation rounds and agent iteration limits bound context quantity without judging its value. We turn that observation into a design. We introduce MERIT, a scoring-driven framework with four components: Multi-Signal Value Scoring (MSVS), which scores each context item from recency, relevance, task criticality, provenance, and redundancy; Budget-Aware Retention Optimization (BARO), which selects a high-value subset under a token budget through a value-density knapsack; Stable-Prefix Emission (SPE), which orders retained items so that low-churn content forms a cache-reusable prefix; and a Prototype Scoring Loop (PSL), which ranks candidate configurations on a joint quality, cost, and latency objective using a successive-halving schedule. We provide the scoring model, pseudocode, complexity bounds, an integration design for existing substrates, an evaluation protocol, and a controlled synthetic study…

DIANA-miTED v2: an expanded microRNA tissue expression database with an integrated healthy-tissue reference atlas
abstract: Abstract MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression that exhibit tissue- and condition-associated expression patterns. Interpreting their abundance in disease or experimental contexts requires a physiological reference. DIANA-miTED v2 expands its uniformly processed and manually curated collection from 15 183 to 49 630 human small RNA-sequencing profiles spanning healthy tissues, cell lines, and disease states. To our knowledge, this is the largest such collection of human miRNA expression profiles assembled to date. It adds 16 746 Genotype-Tissue Expression V10 profiles and expands the Sequence Read Archive collection from 4142 to 21 843, alongside the existing The Cancer Genome Atlas collection. Expression is quantified for 2656 mature miRNAs, with harmonized metadata covering 96 tissues or organs, 437 cell lines, and 503 diseases. Healthy-donor coverage increases from 709 to 23 281, with 1471 tumour-adjacent-normal profiles classified separately. The database distinguishes primary tissues and biofluids from cultured and derived preparations. A redesigned tissue-centric interface provides a body-map picker, sublocation refinement, multi-miRNA and multi-tissue querying, cohort summaries, and descriptive longitudinal browsing. Co-expression capabilities include pairwise Spearman correlation and precomputed WGCNA modules, with 263 overview and 105 …

Night shift work and subclinical cardiac remodelling: a multi-omic CMR study in 42 671 individuals
abstract: Abstract Aims Whether frequent night-shift work is associated with a distinct subclinical cardiac phenotype and accompanying molecular alterations remains uncertain. Methods and results We analysed 42 671 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Night-shift frequency was classified into four categories, and 15 CMR measures were assessed using multivariable regression. Compared with day workers, frequent night-shift workers showed greater left ventricular global wall thickness [standardized β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.050–0.135; false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.001] and left ventricular mass-to-volume ratio (β = 0.072, 95% CI 0.021–0.123; FDR = 0.019), with lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular stroke volume index, and maximal right atrial volume index (all FDR < 0.05). Left ventricular global circumferential strain was less favourable (β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.040–0.144; FDR = 0.002), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain were not significantly associated. Proteomic (n = 4889) and metabolomic (n = 42 671) analyses identified exploratory inflammatory, vascular, and lipid-related correlates. Mediation analyses identified FDR-significant indirect-effect estimates involving left ventricular end-diastolic volum…

title: Multi-Stakeholder Action Framework for Air Pollution Mitigation and Subjective Well-Being Enhancement in New Delhi: Lessons from Global Clean Air Transitions and a Low-Barrier Citizen Acceptance Model
abstract: Chronic ambient air pollution in New Delhi imposes severe biomedical and psychosocial penalties on urban residents, systematically eroding daily Subjective Well-Being (SWB) and life satisfaction. While complex atmospheric dispersion models and capital-intensive technological fixes dominate policy discourse, they frequently fail to gain traction among everyday citizens due to economic friction, behavioral disruption, and fragmented stakeholder accountability. Adopting an applied environmental urbanism perspective, this paper synthesizes empirical lessons from megacities that successfully reversed severe air quality crises specifically Beijing, London, Seoul, and Mexico City to establish a multi-stakeholder action framework and a low-calculation Citizen-Centric Clean Air & Happiness Model (3C-HAM) tailored for New Delhi. Through comparative policy synthesis and behavioral feasibility mapping, we formulate a minimal arithmetic 100-Point Neighborhood Happiness & Clean Air Score (NHCAS) alongside a friction- educed implementation matrix across five societal stakeholder groups: Municipal Governance, Households & Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), Private Industry & Construction, Educational/Medical Institutions, and Peri-Urban Agricultural Communities. Reversing New Delhi’s seasonal smog and restoring resident happiness does not depend solely on complex engineering; it requires al…

title: CoralDB: a comprehensive functional and evolutionary multi-omics database for stony corals
abstract: Abstract Stony corals are foundation species of coral reef ecosystems, yet their biology remains insufficiently explored from an integrative multi-omics perspective. Although the rapid accumulation of genomic and other omics resources offers opportunities to understand coral evolution, development, adaptation, and symbiosis, accessing and utilizing these resources remain challenging. Here, we present CoralDB (http://www.coraldb.net), a comprehensive, genome-centered multi-omics resource that systematically consolidates multi-omics, evolutionary, ecological, and phenotypic data for stony corals and their holobionts. CoralDB covers 414 species and integrates approximately 19 421 datasets, including 12 data dimensions. Moreover, CoralDB offers valuable customized datasets and analytical resources, including standardized functional annotations, gene-family and pan-genome profiles, macro- and microsynteny analyses, spatiotemporal expression patterns, cell-type markers, phylogenetic resources, and symbiont-associated data. An integrated genome browser and interactive modules support flexible data querying, filtering, analysis, visualization, and links to public databases. CoralDB provides an accessible and extensible platform that will help the coral research community manage expanding multi-omics resources, accelerate discoveries in coral biology, evolution, symbiosis, and conservat…

超越“黑箱”：审计大模型的因果可解释性框架
abstract: The “black box” nature of large models stands in fundamental tension with the rigid requirement that audit conclusions be traceable, verifiable and reviewable, and this tension has become a bottleneck constraining the large-scale application of audit large models. Drawing on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) and causal inference, this paper constructs a causal chain-based explainability framework for audit large models, which proceeds in three stages: in the first stage, a natural language processing model extracts voucher entities, and SHAP values quantify the contribution of each feature to the risk score; in the second stage, a causal graph depicts the causal paths among features and distinguishes direct causes from spurious correlations, while a large language model generates counterfactual explanations; in the third stage, the audit report presents the risk level, the confidence of key features and the complete causal chain. A comparison based on an accounts receivable audit scenario shows that this design can turn opaque scores into traceable and verifiable audit evidence chains. The paper further discusses hallucination risks and data governance costs, and proposes countermeasures such as human-in-the-loop review and “T-shaped” talent cultivation.

title: Circular economy trends in built environment towards enhancing sustainable practices
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to explore the trends in the implementation of circular economy (CE) by conducting a comprehensive literature review and bibliometric analysis. It examines impacts from the implementation of CE principles specifically within the built environment sector. This paper also examines the evolution, core concepts and applications of CE where it explores key themes, emerging trends and existing knowledge gaps by highlighting the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration within the built environment sector. This paper provides knowledge on sustainable design and practices, offering guidance for researchers, policymakers and practitioners aiming to enhance sustainability for the urban development. Design/methodology/approach This paper combines systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis to study the trends of circular economy (CE) in built environment. A total of 349 relevant English language articles ranging from 2010 to 2024 were identified with specific keywords from the Scopus database in order to conduct a valid bibliometric analysis. VOSviewer software was used to analyse publication patterns, key authors and thematic clusters. The process was followed with systematic literature review involving title, article analysis and thematic categorisation to identify the emerging trends and research gaps. title: FROM SCREEN TO STORE: EXPLORING OMNICHANNEL CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR
abstract: Online shopping has changed the way consumers search for and buy products. Today, many customers search for products online, compare prices and reviews, and then visit a physical store before making a final decision. This study, “From Screen to Store: Exploring Omnichannel Consumer Behaviour,” focuses on understanding how consumers move from online platforms to physical stores. The study aims to understand consumers’ online shopping behaviour, the reasons for visiting physical stores after online searches, and the factors that influence their purchase decisions. The study is based on primary data collected through a structured questionnaire from 161 respondents using convenience sampling. Percentage analysis, weighted average, Friedman’s Rank Test, One-Way ANOVA, Chi-Square Test and Factor Analysis were used for analysing the data. The findings show that most respondents search for products online before visiting a physical store. The main reasons for visiting a store are to check product quality and to see or try the product physically. Most respondents also prefer to compare both online and physical stores before buying. The study found that product quality, price and product availability are important factors in purchase decisions. It also found a significant relationship between age and the types of products purchased. Overall, the study shows that consumers use both online…

The Role of Droperidol in the Management of Acute Agitation
abstract: Background: Acute behavioral disturbance accounts for ~1.7 million emergency department visits in the USA annually, with 83% involving an underlying serious mental illness. A 2001 FDA black box warning regarding QT prolongation reduced use of droperidol, a butyrophenone antipsychotic, but recent data challenge these concerns. Methods: We reviewed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies from 2000 to 2025 assessing droperidol’s efficacy and safety. Results: Droperidol provides rapid, effective sedation, with onset within 3 to 10 minutes and median time to adequate sedation of 14 to 25 minutes. Sixty-four percent of patients achieved adequate sedation at 15 minutes with droperidol versus 25% to 35% with ziprasidone and 29% with lorazepam. QT prolongation occurred in 1.3% of 1009 patients, mostly those with pre-existing risk factors. Respiratory depression was less common with droperidol (12%) than with ziprasidone (36% to 39%) or lorazepam (48%). Droperidol-midazolam combinations achieved faster sedation and reduced need for rescue medications (41% vs. 62%). Droperidol-treated patients had shorter hospital stays. Large studies found negligible rates of torsades de pointes or extracardiac arrhythmias. Elderly and pediatric patients responded favorably to low-dose droperidol. The American College of Emergency Physicians now recommends droperidol a…

title: Indonesian Human Resource Management Challenges Amid Digital Transformation And Post-Pandemic Recovery
abstract: Digital transformation and post-pandemic recovery have made contemporary challenges in human resource management (HRM) concern not only technological adaptation but also the psychological meaning of organizational practices. This study explores contemporary HRM practices and the challenges of implementing them, as perceived by 243 human resources (HR) leaders across industries in Indonesia, using Perceived Organizational Support (POS) as an interpretive lens. A qualitative descriptive design was used; data were collected through an open-ended online questionnaire and analyzed with Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Seven interrelated themes emerged: leadership and top management support, talent acquisition and internal placement, employee well-being, compensation and benefits, generational differences, organizational culture, and knowledge management and adaptive learning. These themes reflect the perceptions of HR leaders. Rather than identifying entirely new HRM challenges, the findings illustrate how HR leaders perceive established HRM concerns as increasingly interconnected within the context of digital transformation and post-pandemic organizational adjustment. By employing POS as an interpretive lens, the study highlights the potential psychological significance of these organizational challenges without assuming that employees' perceptions of organizational support we…

title: Giant aneurysmal aorto-right atrial tunnel with anomalous right coronary origin: a case report
abstract: Background Aorto-right atrial tunnel (ARAT) is a rare vascular communication between an aortic sinus and the right atrium. Coronary takeoff from the proximal tunnel complicates its distinction from a coronary-cameral fistula and determines the safety of closure. Case presentation A 39-year-old woman presented with edema, rapid weight gain, exertional dyspnea, atrial fibrillation, and a continuous murmur. Multimodality imaging revealed right atrial volume loading and a large right coronary sinus–related vascular channel draining into the right atrium, with three aneurysmal dilatations measuring 64.0 × 53.5, 55.8 × 38.2, and 32.8 × 32.8 mm. Operative exploration confirmed that the right coronary artery (RCA) originated from the proximal tunnel. Complex angulation, extensive aneurysmal dilation, and the need to protect RCA inflow favored surgery over device closure. The tunnel was closed distal to the RCA takeoff, and the aneurysmal channel and atrial communication were surgically addressed. At approximately 3 months, the patient reported only occasional mild leg edema; NT-proBNP fell from 1,171 to 369 pg/mL, liver biochemical parameters had normalized, and electrocardiography showed sinus rhythm with premature atrial complexes. Echocardiography showed no residual shunt or evident aortic regurgitation and resolution of pericardial effusion. Postoperative CTA confirmed RCA patency …

abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the interplay between ownership structure (OS) mechanisms and earnings management (EM), with a specific focus on how board gender diversity (BGD) shapes and moderates these relationships within Egyptian listed companies. Design/methodology/approach By utilizing data from non-financial companies included in the Egyptian Stock Exchange (EGX100) index for the period 2020–2024, this study uses panel data analysis techniques such as random-effects (RE) regressions, supported by pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) and system generalized method of moments (System GMM) tests of robustness, to investigate the associations between OS, BGD and EM. Findings The results indicate that managerial, institutional and foreign ownership negatively relate to EM, whereas BGD is negatively associated with earnings management (EM). It has also been pointed out that BGD significantly affects the association between managerial ownership, foreign ownership and EM. It should be observed that the interaction effect between institutional ownership and BGD is sensitive to model specification (significant for the random-effects (RE) model but not significant for System GMM). title: Characteristics of HIV-1 molecular transmission networks among older men, their spouses, and female sex workers in Southwest China
abstract: Objective: The rising incidence of HIV-1 infection in older adults is a challenge in China. We have previously reported a close transmission connection between older men and female sex workers (FSWs). This study aimed to characterize the transmission network and explore the potential transmission directions among older men, their spouses, and FSWs. Methods: Participants with HIV-1, including older men, their female spouses, and FSWs, were recruited from Guigang City, Guangxi, China. Sanger-derived HIV-1 pol sequences were used for transmission network construction. Conjugal pairs within the largest cluster and the associated FSWs were subjected to next-generation sequencing (NGS) to infer transmission direction via Phyloscanner. Results: A total of 726 HIV pol sequences were obtained by Sanger sequencing, including 595 older men, 88 female spouses, and 43 FSWs. Seven HIV-1 subtypes were identified, with CRF01_AE being the predominant subtype (75.8%, 550/726). Overall, 70.5% (512/726) participants were clustered in transmission networks; 63.9% (327/512) of them belonged to clusters with older men, their spouses, and FSWs. NGS and transmission inference were performed for 30 individuals, revealing 12 source-recipient pairs: three from FSWs to older men, three from older men to spouses, three from spouses to older men, and the remaining three were same-sex pairs. Conclusion: This …

title: Yellow Finance: a solar-centric Islamic finance model for advancing SDG-7
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces Yellow Finance; a new Islamic finance model aimed at supporting solar energy access in developing countries. It addresses the financing gap in clean energy by aligning Islamic values, such as Maslahah (public benefit) and justice, with UN’s Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG-7). Yellow Finance builds on faith-based tools to create a thematic model focused on energy equity. The purpose of this paper is to explore how ethical Islamic financial instruments can be used to expand decentralized solar energy in ways that are both spiritually grounded and socially inclusive. Design/methodology/approach This paper uses a conceptual and policy-oriented approach, grounded in Islamic jurisprudence. It develops a multi-layered framework that connects Islamic principles, financial tools (such as Yellow Sukuk, solar Waqf and Zakat) and solar energy applications. The model is supported by case illustrations, including an adapted real-world example from Bangladesh and a hypothetical Yellow Sukuk for rural schools in Pakistan. These applications demonstrate how Islamic social and commercial finance can be used together. Stakeholder flow diagrams and a phased policy roadmap help visualize the model’s implementation potential. Findings Yellow Finance can fill a policy and funding gap in Islamic sustainable finance by offering a dedicated model for solar energy. It sh…

title: Islamic finance meets climate action: a conceptual exploration of challenges and solutions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the strategic alignment between Islamic financial principles and climate action, aiming to advance understanding of how Shariah-compliant instruments can contribute to sustainability goals. It highlights the pivotal role of corporate governance in mobilising Islamic finance for climate mitigation and adaptation, offering insights into the opportunities and challenges of integrating ethical finance with global environmental imperatives. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured literature review combined with expert interviews to explore the intersection of Islamic finance and climate action. The review systematically synthesises peer-reviewed academic research to identify conceptual linkages and thematic trends. In addition, semi-structured interviews with domain experts were conducted to complement the literature and provide practical insights, enhancing the findings’ theoretical grounding and real-world relevance. Findings This study reveals that Islamic finance offers distinct ethical and structural advantages for supporting climate action, particularly through instruments like green sukuk and social finance. While challenges exist – such as standardisation and governance alignment – Islamic finance demonstrates strong potential to drive sustainable development. Corporate governance emerges as a critical enabler in ensuring…

title: An explainable AI framework for integrated authentication, intrusion detection, and adaptive data transmission in IoMT networks
abstract: Abstract Real-time monitoring, remote diagnostics, and automated medical treatments are all made possible by the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), this has revolutionised healthcare. However, due of their improved connectivity, IoMT devices are more exposed to a range of cybersecurity attacks, such as malware insertion, spoofing, man-in-the-middle attacks, and distributed denial-of-service assaults. Traditional black-box AI models provide robust security mechanisms but lack transparency, making it difficult to identify and mitigate cyber threats effectively. This work introduces an explainable AI (XAI)-driven cybersecurity framework for IoMT applications to enhance trust, interpretability, and resilience against cyber threats. The proposed framework integrates deep learning networks with local model networks for authentication, employs a enhanced deep Q-Network for secure data transmission, and leverages XAI-based techniques for real-time attack detection and resistance. The model incorporates SHAP and LIME to provide interpretable security decisions, ensuring that IoMT stakeholders can understand and act on AI-generated security insights. In addition, this paper discusses a detailed attack resistance study using XAI, which shows the degree to which the proposed framework withstands various cyber threats.The paper evaluates security effectiveness metrics such as false positive…

title: PUBLIC FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND BUDGET ABSORPTION OF WAJIR COUNTY GOVERNMENT, KENYA
abstract: Purpose of Study The study examined the influence of public financial management practices on budget absorption in Wajir County Government, Kenya. Specifically, it evaluated the effects of budgeting credibility, financial reporting, internal control, and asset-liability management on budget absorption, addressing persistent challenges in development expenditure utilization and effective public resource management within the county. Methodology The study adopted a cross-sectional research design targeting 270 management-level employees of Wajir County Government. Stratified sampling yielded 161 respondents. Primary data were collected through semi-structured questionnaires, while secondary data covered budgeted and actual development expenditure. Data analysis employed descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression techniques. Findings The findings revealed that public financial management practices positively and significantly influenced budget absorption in Wajir County Government. The regression model explained 63.7% of variations in budget absorption (R²=0.637). Internal control demonstrated the strongest positive influence (β=0.312, p<0.001), followed by budgeting credibility (β=0.284, p<0.001), asset-liability management (β=0.219, p=0.002), and financial reporting (β=0.167, p=0.015). title: The role of librarians in promoting financial literacy (FL): a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose The study aimed to identify the practices adopted by librarians to promote financial literacy (FL) and to reveal the challenges associated with the adoption and sustainability of these practices. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) methodology was applied to address the study's objectives. A total of 47 seminal studies published in peer-reviewed journals across leading global databases were selected to conduct the SLR on the role of librarians in promoting financial literacy. Findings Findings of the study identified that instructional activities, resource provision, collaborations, online tools and community engagement are key practices applied by librarians to promote financial literacy. The results also revealed that resource constraints, lack of expertise, low patron awareness and relevance barriers cause challenges for librarians to promote financial literacy. Practical implications The study provides actionable insights for library managers and policymakers by emphasizing the need to adopt outcome-oriented performance measurement systems, strengthen librarians' financial literacy competencies and integrate structured evaluation mechanisms into library-led financial literacy initiatives. Social implications The findings highlight the broader societal value of library-led financial literacy initiatives in improving financial awareness, s…

title: Bifurcation and Optimal Control Analysis of a Tooth Cavity Transmission Model
abstract: This paper develops and examines a mathematical model that describes the dynamics of tooth cavity transmission with an ambient bacterial reservoir. In addition to a bacterial population that causes infection through a saturating incidence function, the model includes four human compartments that represent healthy teeth, early enamel lesions, cavitated caries and treated patients. We start by looking into the model’s qualitative characteristics. It is demonstrated that solutions stay confined and positive in a range that is biologically possible. The next-generation matrix method is used to derive the basic reproduction number [Formula: see text], which serves as the principal threshold parameter of the model. It is established that the disease-free equilibrium is locally and globally asymptotically stable when [Formula: see text], whereas it becomes unstable when [Formula: see text]. For [Formula: see text], a unique endemic equilibrium exists. Its local asymptotic stability is established under the corresponding Routh–Hurwitz conditions, while sufficient matrix conditions are derived for its global asymptotic stability in the infected feasible region. Center manifold analysis establishes a forward (transcritical) bifurcation at [Formula: see text], so that the endemic equilibrium emerges for [Formula: see text]. title: Association between right bronchial artery preservation and postoperative pneumonia after minimally invasive esophagectomy
An aerodynamic panel method and mesh generator for educational and research applications in aerodynamics of aircraft design
abstract: The open-source aerodynamic panel tool is a rapid and efficient tool for estimating aerodynamic characteristics, particularly during several phases of aircraft design; however, the accessibility of transparent, adaptable, user-friendly, and open-source aerodynamic tools suitable for educational and research environments remains challenging. This paper introduces Aircraft Panel Generation and Aerodynamic Analysis, an educational open-source software designed to provide easy access to aerodynamic analysis tools for aircraft studies. The software incorporates implementations of the Vortex Lattice Method and Doublet Lattice Method to compute steady and unsteady loads using the Aerodynamic Influence Coefficient matrices for compressible subsonic flows. The framework features advanced panel generation that discretizes lifting surface configurations into structured chordwise and spanwise trapezoidal elements. The accuracy of the code is demonstrated by validation against data from a published German Aerospace Center technical report across both steady and unsteady aerodynamic cases. The results show that the computed pressure coefficients are in good agreement with reference solutions. The example aircraft models are analyzed and visualized as illustrative examples. This software could serve as a valuable resource for academics and researchers, providing a foundation for further aeroe…

Design of an Earthquake Early Warning System Based on Vibration Sensors and IoT in Earthquake-Prone Areas of Bengkulu
abstract: Bengkulu Province is one of the regions in Indonesia with a relatively high level of earthquake vulnerability due to its location in a tectonic plate boundary zone. This condition highlights the importance of a system capable of providing early warnings so that people can increase their awareness when an earthquake occurs. This study aimed to design and develop an Internet of Things (IoT)- and vibration sensor-based earthquake early warning system using an MPU6050 sensor to detect vibrations and an Arduino Uno as the main system controller. The method used in this study was the Waterfall model, which consists of the stages of requirements analysis, system design, implementation, testing, and maintenance. The system was developed using an MPU6050 sensor, Arduino Uno, a 16 × 2 LCD, an LED, and a buzzer. Acceleration data along the X, Y, and Z axes were processed using resultant acceleration calculations to obtain the total acceleration value. The measurement results were then compared with a threshold value of 15 m/s². When the measured value exceeded the threshold, the system displayed the message "EARTHQUAKE!!!" on the LCD and activated the LED and buzzer as warning indicators. The test results showed that the system was able to detect changes in vibration effectively and distinguish between normal conditions and high-vibration conditions based on the predetermined threshold va…

title: Beyond Instrumental Design: Participation as Organizational Transformation in a Public Library Workplace
abstract: Abstract The article examines how participatory design methods can be applied to transform the working environment of public library employees, using the Municipal Library of Znojmo as a case study. Despite robust evidence linking workspace quality to employee satisfaction, performance, and professional identity, this dimension of library management remains largely neglected. Structured according to the Double Diamond model of design thinking, the research combined secondary analysis of annual employee interviews, participatory workshops, spatial prototyping, and user testing with a team of 26 employees across professional roles. The findings reveal five principal problems in the current working environment and demonstrate that participation functions not merely as a design instrument but as a transformative process that legitimizes employee needs, surfaces latent preferences, and strengthens professional identity. User testing of the spatial prototype identified a fundamental tension between the abstract preference for shared space and concrete concerns about privacy and acoustic comfort in open-plan configurations. The study offers a replicable methodological framework for participatory workspace design in public libraries and contributes to the broader discourse on employee wellbeing and organizational culture in library institutions.

title: Sensitivity analysis and physics-aware deep learning for aluminum mirror coatings: when network architecture outweighs loss-function design
abstract: Abstract Aluminum is the most prevalent material for broadband mirror coatings, yet the design parameters affecting its specular performance, such as film thickness and surface roughness, are not well quantified. Additionally, the pace of developing surrogate models for metallic reflectance has been slower than for dielectric models. This study addresses these gaps by implementing a numerically validated transfer-matrix framework for a single absorbing aluminum layer on a glass substrate, accompanied by an optical sensitivity analysis. The engine agrees with an independent transfer-matrix implementation to machine precision over 400–1200 nm, and its conclusions are robust to the choice among five aluminum optical-constant datasets. Results indicate reflectance saturates past an opaque thickness of approximately 40 nm, and the p -polarized response shows a pseudo-Brewster minimum that does not reach zero. Surface roughness decreases specular reflectance due to the Debye–Waller factor, with a characteristic $$1/\lambda ^{2}$$ scaling affecting the blue end of the spectrum. We then present a physics-informed deep-learning surrogate model that links thickness and roughness to the reflectance-deficit spectrum, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.9999 with held-out data. Our findings suggest that the architecture of the neural network is crucial for addressing metallic refl…

title: Teaching Reform of Civil Engineering Construction Course under the Background of AI
abstract: With the large-scale implementation of generative artificial intelligence, digital twin, BIM and other technologies in the construction industry, the construction industry is transforming from the traditional manual construction mode to the intelligent construction mode, and the demand for industry post ability has changed significantly. As a core compulsory course of civil engineering undergraduate major, civil engineering construction undertakes the task of imparting professional knowledge such as construction technology, construction organization and site management. The traditional classroom teaching mode has practical contradictions such as lack of practical scenes, lagging update of teaching content, insufficient individualized training of students, and single assessment method. The teaching practice shows that the reasonable introduction of AI auxiliary tools can make up for the shortcomings of traditional teaching field conditions, enrich classroom case resources, and strengthen students’ engineering practice thinking. However, it also faces practical challenges such as students’ excessive dependence on AI output content, professional information distortion, and teachers’ teaching ability can not keep up with technical iteration. This study can provide reference for the digital teaching reform of construction courses in similar engineering majors, and help to cultivate …

title: Effects of the new NCEE reform on talent competitions in “Double First-Class” universities
abstract: Significant changes to the new National College Entrance Examination (NCEE) reform and the implementation of the “Double First-Class” (DFC) initiative in China are coincidentally in the national spotlight and fall within the same policy window. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the new NCEE on talent competitions in DFC universities. By leveraging the 2018–2022 college admission data including 105 universities and 14,170 majors from Shandong Province, which first implemented the new NCEE in 2020, these effects are examined via the interrupted time-series technique. Weighted rankings for liberal arts and science disciplines and the admission ranking coefficient are adopted to ensure comparability before and after the reform. The findings reveal that after the reform, the quality of student application (QSA) in both world-class universities ( β = −0.069, p < 0.01) and first-class discipline universities ( β = −0.046, p < 0.001) improved. Focusing on urban differences, the QSA in DFC universities located in first-tier ( β = −0.086, p < 0.01), new first-tier cities ( β = −0.100, p < 0.001), and second-tier cities ( β = −0.174, p < 0.01) has also improved. In addition, the reform has had different estimated impacts on the QSA in different majors. Furthermore, the numerical magnitudes of these estimates suggest a potential pattern where high-scoring…

title: The Politics of Retirement Age Reform Under Xi Jinping
abstract: Abstract Raising the legal age for receiving pension benefits is a highly sensitive decision for any government, even for an authoritarian regime. This article addresses how the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) under Xi Jinping 习近平 proceeded cautiously for over a decade to raise China’s retirement ages, which had been established in the 1950s and, by the 2020s, ranked as the youngest retirement ages in the world. The CCP undertook strategies to make reforms possible and more palatable to the public, before a legal measure was finally enacted in 2024. Given the CCP’s ability to deter large-scale public protests, it did not expect anything like the fierce public opposition to recent retirement age increases seen in France (2023) and in Russia (2018). Why was retirement age reform in China deferred for so long? This article reviews policy documents and public messaging to understand Xi Jinping’s guarded approach to enacting retirement age increases, and the constraints that the CCP faced as it considered the timing and substance of the measure.

title: Linking gamification, environmental awareness, and purchasing decisions in sustainable retail within a higher-order S–O–R framework
abstract: Abstract Gamification is increasingly used to engage consumers with sustainability, yet how integrated gameful retail experiences are associated with sustainable purchasing decisions remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, this study examines Environmental Awareness as an intervening environmental orientation linking Gamification with self-reported Purchasing Decisions in sustainable retail. Data were collected from 310 consumers in Bangkok, Thailand, using 57 ordinal indicators and analyzed through higher-order structural equation modeling with diagonally weighted least squares. Gamification was strongly and positively associated with Environmental Awareness (β = 0.858, p < 0.001), and Environmental Awareness was strongly and positively associated with Purchasing Decisions (β = 0.910, p < 0.001). In contrast, the direct association between Gamification and Purchasing Decisions was small and statistically nonsignificant (β = −0.035, p = 0.532). The indirect association through Environmental Awareness was positive and statistically supported (B = 0.803, β = 0.780; Monte Carlo 95% CI [0.678, 0.936]), yielding a pattern consistent with indirect-only mediation. The model explained 73.6% of the variance in Environmental Awareness and 77.4% in Purchasing Decisions. The findings suggest that the relevance of gamification to repor…

title: Integrating Ecological Vulnerability, Actor-Level Mention Frequency, and Market Representation for Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plant Resources in the Peruvian Andes
abstract: Medicinal plant trade in Andean markets connects traditional knowledge, livelihoods, and biodiversity conservation, yet ecological vulnerability, actor-level recognition, and market representation are rarely examined together. This study assessed 81 ethnobotanical entries recorded across three traditional markets in Huanta, Peru, using an eight-criterion Rapid Vulnerability Assessment (RVA), a Relative Mention Index (RMI) derived from 23 purposively sampled market actors, and observed market occurrence. Complementary Smith’s Salience Index (S) values were calculated from 92 ordered plant mentions. Relationships among indicators were examined using rank correlations and multiple-testing correction, while conservation-screening rankings were evaluated through sensitivity analyses. RVA scores ranged from 15 to 28, with 10 entries classified as very highly vulnerable, 42 as highly vulnerable, and 29 as moderately vulnerable. Ecological vulnerability was not significantly associated with market representation (Spearman ρ = −0.226; FDR-adjusted p = 0.1285) or RMI (ρ = −0.053; FDR-adjusted p = 0.6377). Smith’s S identified Taraxacum officinale (S = 0.1261) and Borago officinalis (S = 0.1217) as the most salient provisional plant identifications within vendor free lists. RVA rankings remained highly stable under alternative criterion weights (median Spearman ρ = 0.996), although conser…

title: A DISCRIMINAÇÃO NO MERCADO DE TRABALHO: UMA ANÁLISE SOBRE A REALIDADE DAS MULHERES TRANS NO BRASIL
abstract: O presente trabalho tem como objetivo apresentar a influência do gênero na remuneração e no acesso ao mercado de trabalho, combatendo divergências salariais de mulheres cis e a exclusão estrutural de mulheres trans, e, através de pesquisas bibliográficas, artigos de lei e artigos publicados na rede mundial de computadores, apresentando o impacto social e jurídico do tema na área laboral, como forma de aplicação do direito (Constitucional, Trabalho) identificando o porquê de o setor empregatício brasileiro manter desigualdades, disparidades salariais, barreiras profundas de permanência e a persistente segregação no emprego formal, além de analisar os reflexos dessas barreiras na efetivação da dignidade da pessoa humana e na garantia da igualdade material dentro do cenário profissional do país.
