title: The Influence of Russia's Wheat Export Tax and the War in Ukraine on the Domestic Market: A Synthetic Control Method Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Russia, the world's leading wheat exporter, has implemented a wheat export tax since February 2021. This study examines the impact of the export tax and the war in Ukraine on the integration between Russia's domestic wheat market and the Black Sea export market, as well as its economic consequences for supply chain actors. Using a cointegration framework, results from the linear error correction model indicate a significant decline in market integration and an increase in domestic transaction costs following the introduction of the tax in 2021, particularly in major wheat‐producing and exporting regions. The outbreak of the war in 2022 further disrupted this relationship, leading to the complete decoupling of domestic prices from export price developments. Furthermore, using the synthetic control method, our results of counterfactual analysis indicate that the export tax significantly reduced domestic producer prices and, correspondingly, farmers’ export revenues, with reductions markedly larger during the war, reflecting the combined influence of the export tax and war‐related economic disruptions. Therefore, the export tax and Russia's war in Ukraine, which negatively affect market integration and producer revenues in Russia, hinder the long‐term development of Russia's wheat sector. To mitigate the adverse effects on global food security, import‐dependent countries …

title: HAMBATAN DINAS PERHUBUNGAN DALAM MENANGANI KASUS PEMASANGAN STIKER PERUSAHAN MAXIM YANG BERPOTENSI MENIMBULKAN BLIND SPOT PADA KENDARAAN RODA EMPAT DI KOTA KUPANG
abstract: This study analyzes the criminal law provisions, challenges, and efforts undertaken by the Kupang City Transportation Agency regarding the application of "Maxim" company stickers on four-wheeled vehicles, which may create blind spots. The research employs an empirical-juridical method, utilizing both a statutory approach and interviews with the Kupang City Transportation Agency, the Traffic Unit of the Kupang City Police, and Maxim drivers. The findings indicate that large stickers applied to vehicle windows can obstruct a driver's field of vision; however, there are currently no specific regulations governing the size, placement, or surface area of ​​such stickers. Challenges identified include limited personnel, a lack of detailed technical guidelines, driver non-compliance, and a low level of awareness regarding traffic safety. Measures taken by the authorities include public outreach, information dissemination, joint enforcement operations, the removal of stickers, and legal action in accordance with existing regulations. This study recommends the strengthening of technical guidelines, continuous oversight, and the promotion of traffic safety education.

title: AI-Based Analytics for Smart-Meter Electricity Data: A Review of Forecasting, Anomaly Detection, Explainability and Privacy, and the Research Gap in Session-Level Decision Intelligence
El Super Bowl como ritual mediático contemporáneo
abstract: The Super Bowl has consolidated itself as one of the most relevant media rituals in contemporary culture, articulating spectacle, market, and cultural identities on a global scale. Within this framework, the 2026 Halftime Show promotional spot, starring Bad Bunny and produced by Apple Music and the NFL, constitutes a privileged object for analyzing semiosis and sign mediation processes in media mega-events. This article proposes a Peircean semiotic analysis of the spot, understood not only as an advertising piece, but as a cultural mediation device operating at the frontier between the local and the global, Latin identity and the hegemony of American entertainment. From a qualitative and interpretive approach, Peircean phenomenological categories (Firstness, Secondness, Thirdness) and the sign action of audiovisual discourse are examined, showing how Bad Bunny's figure operates as a sign that generates interpretants and ritualizes the sports spectacle as a space of transcultural mediation. The analysis also shows the limits of this promise of universality, which received a divided response.

title: Market competition strategy optimization model based on the fusion of quantum game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning
Youth Employment Policy in Mobile Europe. How Regional Demographics Shape the Effectiveness of EU Social Investment
abstract: Abstract Youth job insecurity has been a persistent challenge across European regions, particularly since the financial crisis, and has gained significant attention in the public agenda. In 2013, the European Commission launched the Youth Employment Initiative (YEI) to support EU regions with high youth unemployment rates. The policy aims to ensure that, within 4 months of becoming unemployed or completing formal education, young people receive quality offers of employment, further education, apprenticeship or traineeship leading to a qualification. Using data from the EU Labour Force Survey (EU‐LFS) from 2015 to 2022, we employ a two‐step methodology to estimate the effects of YEI funding whilst accounting for the endogenous distribution of funds across regions, local variations in the composition of the youth workforce and the effects of population mobility. Whilst recent regional analyses demonstrate positive YEI effects across European territories, our findings reveal that the initiative is more effective in dynamic regions and has little impact in lagging regions.

A Social Signaling Function of Politicians on Boards: Evidence From an Emerging Market
abstract: ABSTRACT Politically connected directors in emerging market firms are largely assumed to serve a political function by providing political resources and regulatory advantage, but their effectiveness remains inconclusive. Our study draws on signaling theory to propose an alternative social function of the presence of politician directors. We theorize that the presence of politicians on boards of emerging‐market firms is associated with higher ESG ratings, which in turn result in higher firm value. Using 688 firm‐year observations in a sample of 234 Philippine publicly listed corporations for the period 2021–2024, we provide empirical evidence showing that ESG ratings fully mediate the positive relationship between the presence of politician directors and firm value. We also find that ownership structure moderates the link between politically connected directors and ESG ratings, where the signaling value is more pronounced in business group‐affiliated firms and those with dispersed ownership. Our research has important implications for the firms' political connections as a strategic tool for social signaling purposes to constantly communicate to stakeholders such as investors, rating agencies, regulators, and the general public about their orientation toward broader societal concerns beyond shareholder value.

title: Navigating Market Volatility: The Role of Investor Sentiment and Liquidity in Indonesia’s Capital Market, 2011–2025
abstract: Background: Stock market volatility reflects not only macroeconomic fundamentals but also investor sentiment and market liquidity. Although investor sentiment is widely recognized as a potential driver of volatility, its effects may depend on prevailing liquidity conditions. This interaction is particularly relevant in emerging markets, where investor behavior and trading activity may jointly shape price fluctuations.Purpose: This study examines the effects of positive and negative investor sentiment on Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) return volatility, with particular attention to the moderating role of market liquidity.Design/methodology/approach: The study uses monthly time-series data from January 2011 to December 2025. Investor sentiment indices are constructed using Google Search Trends, while the turnover ratio serves as a proxy for market liquidity and the moderating variable. An autoregressive distributed lag error correction model (ARDL-ECM) is employed to examine short-run and long-run relationships among investor sentiment, market liquidity, macroeconomic factors, and IHSG return volatility.Findings/Results: The findings indicate that both positive and negative investor sentiment significantly increase IHSG return volatility when modeled separately. However, when both sentiments are incorporated into a single model, only negative investor sentiment has a statisticall…

title: Көші-қон процестерін модельдеу мен болжауда кейс-талдау әдісін қолдану мүмкіндіктері: Қазақстан мысалында
abstract: Migration processes respond quickly to external shocks, policy changes and individual decisions, so forecasts based on time series alone may contain substantial errors. This article aims to substantiate the place and potential of the case method in the scientific modelling and forecasting of migration and to propose a case-based forecasting model. It traces how the case method moved from legal and business education into the social sciences as a research strategy. The scientific significance of the work lies in linking the case method with migration forecasting methodology and in justifying an approach that combines qualitative analysis with statistical models; its practical significance lies in offering an analytical tool for planning regional migration policy. The methodology comprises comparative case analysis, process tracing, case-based reasoning and scenario analysis. The empirical base consists of four Kazakhstani migration cases: internal migration to large agglomerations, the resettlement of kandas (ethnic Kazakh returnees) to northern regions, the autumn 2022 wave of relocants, and the shift of the external migration balance to positive values. Push, pull, institutional, network and shock factors were coded for each case and their possible social consequences compared. The result is a five-stage case-factor forecasting model that integrates a case base, a similarity m…

A Note on How Jevons and YBMD Indices Differ According to Price Relative Concentration
abstract: Most national statistical offices employ the Jevons index to measure the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at the elementary aggregation level. From an axiomatic perspective, it is also considered the most appropriate unweighted price index. The YBMD index has some attractive properties compared with the Jevons index. By exploiting a factorization of the YBMD index, this note demonstrates that the two indices differ according to the concentration of price relatives between the base and current periods.

title: An Autonomous, Observation-Based Short-Term Wind Forecasting Model Designed for Mobile Oceanography
abstract: This study developed an offline short-term sea surface wind forecasting model that produced 6 h forecasts at locations withheld from training, both inside and beyond the target domain, using only local real-time wind observations. The model was based on the Conditional Long Short-Term Memory (C-LSTM) algorithm and was pre-trained with long-term numerical simulations and sparse station observations to learn wind field variability and background knowledge, enabling forecasts at arbitrary locations. At the two test stations in the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea, the wind speed RMSE over the September verification period was 1.72 m/s and 1.02 m/s, respectively, averaged over the six forecast lead times. For extended 6–24 h lead times the forecast remained stable at the two in-domain stations, where the growth of the wind speed error was limited and remained below that of both comparison tests throughout the extended range; at the out-of-domain station the growth was considerably larger, so the extended-range skill was confined to the region covered by the pre-training. The model also exhibited some predictive capability for wind speed variability in adjacent areas outside the target domain, although errors increased. The developed model shows considerable application potential for ship navigation and operations under poor communication conditions in the open sea.

title: Transmission dynamics of pertussis in China (2015–2024): A SEIARV compartmental model with waning immunity, annual parameter fitting, and stochastic forecasting for 2025–2027
Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association
abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

title: Meteorological Models Evaluation for Optimized Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: Accurate meteorological forecasts are critical for optimizing photovoltaic (PV) power generation, yet the performance of numerical weather prediction (NWP) models at specific power plant sites remains underexplored. This study evaluates four meteorological models—a commercial model (named GD), the NUIST regional model, the European Centre for Medium-range Weather Forecasts-Integrated Forecast System (ECMWF-IFS), and the German Weather Service ICOsahedral Nonhydrostatic-seamless (DWD ICON-seamless) model—against 15-min observational data from three PV sites in China (coastal low-altitude ZJ, inland low-altitude JX, and high-altitude QH) over periods spanning 2023–2025. Standard error metrics (mean bias, mean absolute error or MAE, root-mean-square error or RMSE, index of agreement or IOA, and correlation) are applied to 10-day forecasts of surface pressure, temperature, humidity, wind, and 6-h forecasts of solar radiation components. The NUIST model substantially outperforms GD in 2-m temperature at QH (MAE reduction of ~52%) and in 10-m wind speed at ZJ (MAE reduction of ~16%), while GD shows slight advantages in wind speed at inland sites and in wind direction bias. For ultrashort-term solar radiation, the ICON model consistently achieves the lowest MAE for total shortwave radiation across all sites, with a 26.8% reduction at ZJ compared to GD. All models exhibit systematic te…

title: Analysis of the Mechanism of Void Formation in Vacuum-Bag-Only Process of High Areal Weight Carbon Fiber Unidirectional Prepregs
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for high-performance carbon fiber composites has driven interest in the vacuum-bag-only (VBO) process as a cost-effective alternative to autoclave curing. However, the VBO process typically relies on low areal weight (LAW) prepregs, which often suffer from low production efficiency and high porosity in the resulting laminates. In this study, high areal weight (HAW) unidirectional carbon fiber prepregs were processed using the VBO process. The porosity and void characteristics of the laminates were systematically investigated under different processing conditions. The VBO process yielded a maximum porosity of 6.32%, whereas the autoclave process reduced porosity to approximately 1.03%. The absence of roll-in pressing significantly increased porosity to 15.64%, indicating the critical role of inter- ply compaction in void reduction. To further improve void reduction, hybrid layups of HAW and LAW prepregs were designed. The ply count ratio LAW: HAW=3: 1 achieved a minimum porosity of 1.73% in the central region, and the interlaminar shear strength reached 75.26 MPa, which was comparable to that of autoclave-process laminates. These findings demonstrate that the VBO process, when combined with optimized layup design and roll-in pressing, can produce HAW prepreg laminates with porosity levels approaching those achieved by autoclave processing, offering…

title: آلية التناص وتوظيفه في النص الليبي عند بعض الشعراء الليبيين (دراسة وصفية تحليلية لتطبيق التناص)
abstract: إن دراسة آلية التناص تعدّ قضية نقدية حديثة، فضلاً عن أن جذورها التاريخية قديمة؛ لذلك نجد بعض النقاد قد وضعوها موضع الاهتمام الواسع، لارتباطها بشكل وثيق بالجانب الإبداعي، وتحديد مفهوم التناص موضوع اختلفت فيه كثير من الدراسات النقدية، ففي هذا البحث استكشاف لمعاني التناص الكثيرة، التي فتحت البحث فيه على مصرعيه في مضامينها العميقة، فعنونته تحت ( آلية التناص وتوظيفه في النص الليبي ) "نماذج تطبيقية للتناص عند بعض الشعراء الليبيين المعاصرين"، وقد تضمنت الدراسة موضوعات تتعلق مقاربات أولية لمفهوم مصطلح التناص لغةً واصطلاحاً، وأنواع التناص، وأهميته، فضلا عن آلية التناص في شعر بعض الشعراء الليبيين المعاصرين، واستراتيجية التناص، ومستوياته، ثم عرض بعض النماذج التطبيقية من التناص في الشعر الليبي المعاصر، ثم خاتمة مختصرة، ذكرتُ فيها ملخصاً للنتائج، وألحقتها بقائمة المصادر والمراجع، مستخدماً المنهج الوصفي والتحليلي والنقدي.

title: Gummy Candies Fortified with Propolis/Honey Microencapsulates and Goldenberry Juice: Bioactive Profile, Antioxidant Capacity, and Sensory Acceptance
abstract: Propolis and goldenberry (Physalis peruviana L.) provide bioactive compounds of interest for the development of food products enriched with natural bioactive ingredients. This study evaluated gummy candies fortified with propolis/honey microencapsulates produced by spray drying using maltodextrin and tara gum, together with goldenberry juice. Microencapsulates prepared with propolis from Colpa and Nueva Esperanza were characterized through bioactive and physicochemical analyses, SEM-EDS, FTIR, and TGA-DSC. Six gummy formulations were developed using a constrained mixture design, varying the microencapsulate (5, 6, and 7%), juice (25 and 30%), and water proportions, and their acceptance was evaluated by 120 consumers. The Colpa microencapsulate showed the most favorable bioactive profile and was selected for the formulations. The linear mixture models were significant (p < 0.001; R2 = 0.8240–0.9897). F6 showed the highest phenolic compound (1.22 mg GAE/g), flavonoid (0.90 mg QE/g), and total carotenoid contents (497.99 µg BCE/100 g), as well as the greatest antioxidant capacity (7.85 µmol TE/g). F5 achieved the highest sensory preference (33.33%) and contained 69.10 g/100 g of carbohydrates, 15.00 g/100 g of protein, 339.10 kcal/100 g, and a hardness of 2.46 N. The results showed that formulations with higher microencapsulate and juice contents exhibited greater bioactive respon…

title: Macro- and meso-scale study of the lateral bearing mechanism of a single pile with a cap under pure lateral loading
Mechanical response and fracture mechanism of granite with crossed fissures after thermal treatment
abstract: The safety of deep energy extraction is closely related to the distribution of fractures and the fracture behavior of rock masses. To clarify the thermal damage mechanism and deterioration characteristics of complex fissured rock masses, uniaxial tests on crossed-fissure granite considering fissure persistency were carried out using DIC to investigate the fracture mechanism. The results indicate that the granite specimens treated at 800°C exhibited significant changes in their apparent physical properties. The volumetric expansion rate ranged from 1.8% to 2.6%, and the elastic wave velocity dropped significantly. After thermal treatment, the compaction segment of the granite stress-strain curve was extended, but the brittle instability characteristics were still preserved. The observations suggest that pre-existing fissure geometry primarily guided macroscopic fracture development under the tested conditions. Thermal damage markedly influenced grain-scale crack propagation and weakened the mechanical properties. Thermally treated specimens also exhibited greater fragmentation than unheated specimens. However, the damage to the crystal structure significantly weakened the mechanical properties of the granite, resulting in a final failure mode that was more fragmented compared to granite under normal temperature conditions. The failure of the specimens exhibits a significant dama…

title: Molecular Mechanism of Salt-Induced Fibrinogen Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Fibrinogen nanofiber scaffolds, which closely mimic the fibrous architecture of the extracellular matrix, have emerged as promising biomaterials for wound healing and tissue engineering. Salt-induced, thrombin-free fibrinogen fiber assembly provides a versatile route for their fabrication, yet the molecular mechanism underlying its pronounced ion specificity has remained unresolved. Here, we combined complementary experimental analyses with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify the structural determinants governing phosphate-induced fibrillogenesis. MD simulations suggested that phosphate, but not chloride, preferentially stabilizes extended fibrinogen conformations through persistent interactions with the E domain and αC region, thereby increasing αC accessibility. Consistent with this mechanism, four complementary perturbation strategies, αC-domain truncation, antibody-mediated masking of the αC region, competitive inhibition by isolated αC fragments, and rescue experiments combining truncated fibrinogen with cognate αC fragments resulted in the absence of nanofiber assembly. Docking and MD simulations further demonstrated that preservation of the proposed β-hairpin-mediated αC dimer interface alone is insufficient to drive fibrillogenesis, highlighting the requirement for an intact αC region within native fibrinogen. Together, these findings support a mech…

title: Characterization of a novel disruption mechanism during plasma current ramp-down in the ADITYA-U tokamak
abstract: Abstract Safe termination of a tokamak plasma discharge remains a challenge due to the high risk of encountering a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD)-driven disruption during controlled ramp-down of the plasma current. During the current ramp-down phase of ADITYA-U discharges, the occurrence of MHD-driven disruptions cannot be described by the conventional locked-mode disruption (LMD) mechanism. Analysing hundreds of ADITYA-U discharges, it has been observed that when some specific plasma parameters exceeds a threshold rate, the disruption is always preceded by a steady rise in MHD mode-rotation frequency, followed by a sudden cessation of mode-rotation frequency before the current quench. Moreover, it has been found that the occurrence of this type of disruption depends mainly on the current decay rate and magnitude and the edge safety factor (qedge). Although the disruption seems to be predominantly governed only by the m/n=2/1 drift–tearing modes, the precursor phase in this kind of disruption survives for relatively much shorter times as compared to the conventional locked mode disruptions. Further investigation revealed that during the plasma current decay phase, the core radiation increases significantly, indicating a hollow temperature profile. This leads to destabilization of the MHD mode, which seems to be primarily responsible for the plasma disruption.

title: Mineralogical Characteristics and Coloration Mechanism of Blue-Toned Nephrite from Qiemo, Xinjiang, China
abstract: Newly discovered blue-toned nephrite (commonly called “Qiemo blue” in the market) from Qiemo County, Xinjiang Province, exhibits a unique soft blue hue and often has brown rinds. However, its mineralogical characteristics and coloration mechanism remain unclear. In this study, two typical Qiemo blue-toned nephrite samples were selected, and their mineral composition, structural characteristics, major and trace element contents, and spectroscopic properties are presented using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), polarized light microscopy, electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), ultraviolet-visible (UV–Vis) absorption spectroscopy, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry, and LA-ICP-MS. The analyses show that the major mineral of the samples is tremolite (>95%), which displays four types of textures: fine-grained, porphyroclastic, fibrous-oriented, and cluster-like. Minor minerals include titanite, apatite, REE-bearing epidote-group mineral and zircon. Colorimetric analysis confirms that the samples indeed exhibit a blue color, with local brown domains. In the UV–Vis absorption spectra, the blue regions exhibit absorptions at 312 nm, 445 nm, 472 nm, and 492 nm, along with a broad absorption band at 660–700 nm, while the brown regions exhibit absorptions at 312 nm, 472 nm, and 665 nm, along with a blue–violet region absorption band. Trace element analysis indicates that Ti…

title: Thermal Homogenization of Hot Mix Asphalt Agglomerates by Remixing in a Material Transfer Vehicle: A Transient Heat-Conduction Analysis
abstract: This study analyzes how remixing in a Material Transfer Vehicle (MTV) reduces thermal segregation of hot mix asphalt (HMA): after remixing, colder agglomerates surrounded by hotter HMA equalize by heat conduction. Transient conduction in cubic agglomerates of 2, 3, and 4 cm was modeled with a finite-conductivity model and a lumped-capacitance-type model, both at a Biot number of 0.5. The calculation was verified by oven-heating tests on two 4 cm cubic AC 8 S 50/70 specimens at the same Biot number: the finite-conductivity model reproduced the measured center temperature with a root-mean-square error of 2.0 °C, whereas the lumped model overpredicted it by 12.8 °C. The time to eliminate 90% of the initial temperature difference is 12, 28, and 50 min for 2, 3, and 4 cm agglomerates; a three-dimensional numerical analysis shows that perfect contact shortens these times by 1.5–2 times and that a cold-material fraction of 9–16% reduces the local temperature difference after 10–20 min by a further 10–50%. Equalization of 2 cm agglomerates within about 10 min is comparable with the estimated 5–20 min residence time in an MTV, whereas 4 cm agglomerates retain about 40% of it after 20 min. These conditional model results require field verification.

title: Excitonic order tuned by electric fields and driven by interorbital Coulomb interactions in twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Abstract Excitonic order, as a representative electronic instability in strongly correlated systems, has attracted significant attention in moiré systems. In this work, we investigate the emergence and tunability of excitonic order in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) within an effective two-orbital Hubbard model, using large-scale constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo simulations. We demonstrate that the excitonic correlations are significantly enhanced by the external electric field ε , the inter-orbital Coulomb interaction V ⊥ , and the inter-orbital hopping t ⊥ . By analyzing both short-range and long-range excitonic correlation functions across different lattice sizes, we find that long-range excitonic correlations are robust against finite-size effects and provide reliable evidence for excitonic condensation. Furthermore, we reveal a clear interplay between magnetic order and excitonic order. The spin structure factor shows that increasing ε , V ⊥ , and t ⊥ suppresses the antiferromagnetic order, indicating that excitonic order emerges as a competing instability with magnetism. Among these factors, the external electric field plays the dominant role in destabilizing antiferromagnetism and promoting excitonic correlations. Our results establish a unified physical picture in which excitonic order in TBG can be effectively controlled by tuning interlayer coupling and external fi…

title: A gestão de estoques e sua contribuição para a eficiência operacional de um comércio varejista em Parintins-AM
abstract: Inventory management in commercial establishments located in municipalities where supply depends on river transportation involves simultaneous decisions regarding product availability, record accuracy, and loss prevention, all of which influence operational continuity. This study aimed to understand how inventory management practices are related to the operational efficiency of a commercial company located in Parintins, Amazonas, Brazil. To this end, a qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive case study was conducted based on a 44-question semi-structured interview administered to the person responsible for inventory management. The results revealed procedures for checking incoming goods, categorizing products, using the LC Sistemas software, conducting inventories and physical stock checks, monitoring expiration dates on a weekly basis, and anticipating purchases during periods of increased demand. Discrepancies between physical stock quantities and system records were also identified, along with two stockout incidents in the previous six months, an average replenishment lead time of approximately seven days, and estimated financial losses of BRL 5,000.00 during the period, associated with expired, damaged, or missing products. The analysis highlighted the importance of keeping records up to date, organizing receiving and replenishment processes, and using control indicators …

title: Beyond Green Rhetoric: How Human Resource Management Bridges Strategy and Sustainability in Hotels
abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on the natural resource‐based view (NRBV) and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study examines the relationships among strategic green intentions, green human resource management (Green HRM) practices, sustainable business performance and employee outcomes in Ghana's hospitality industry. Two independent quantitative studies were conducted in star‐rated hotels. Study 1 surveyed 282 managers and supervisors to examine Green HRM practices as mediating mechanisms linking strategic green intentions to economic, social and environmental performance. Study 2 surveyed 302 frontline employees to investigate employee green commitment as a mediator of the relationships between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour and turnover intention. Data were analysed using a disjoint two‐stage PLS‐SEM approach. Study 1 revealed that strategic green intentions were directly associated with social performance but not with economic or environmental performance. Green HRM practices exhibited significant positive indirect effects across all three performance dimensions, with indirect‐only mediation for economic and environmental performance and complementary mediation for social performance. Study 2 demonstrated that employee green commitment significantly mediated the positive relationship between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour. However, neither Green HRM…

title: A Bioactive Lycopene-Coated Catheter Novel Strategy Against Multidrug-Resistant Proteus mirabilis Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections: Biofilm Disruption and rsbA-Mediated Mechanisms
abstract: Background: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Proteus mirabilis pose a formidable clinical challenge due to the pathogen’s exceptional capacity to form crystalline biofilms and exhibit hyper-swarming motility on indwelling medical devices, especially urinary catheters. Natural bioactive compounds, notably the carotenoid lycopene, have emerged as promising therapeutic candidates owing to their versatile anti-virulence properties. Consequently, this study aimed to develop and evaluate a bioactive lycopene-coated catheter strategy as a novel pharmaceutical intervention to combat strong biofilm-forming (SBF) MDR P. mirabilis-driven CAUTIs. Methods: The antibacterial activity of lycopene was determined using well diffusion and broth microdilution assays. In vitro antibiofilm efficacy was assessed via microtiter plate and medical-grade silicone catheter models. In situ structural changes within the biofilms were analyzed using light microscopy and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Anti-swarming activity was evaluated using a motility plate assay. Liquid Christensen’s medium was conducted to evaluate the effect on urease activity. Furthermore, the transcriptional impact of lycopene on the rsbA gene—a master regulator of swarming and biofilm formation—was investigated using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Results: A…

title: Adaptive Control-Oriented Energy Management Strategy for Enhanced Hybrid Vehicle Efficiency
From Retrospective Audit to Prospective Certainty: Domestic Advance Pricing Agreements, Shared Services and VAT Valuation in Kenya
abstract: Kenya's introduction of Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) under section 18G of the Income Tax Act, Cap. 470, represents an important move from retrospective tax controversy towards prospective tax certainty. The development is particularly significant because Kenya's domestic corporate environment increasingly contains related-party transactions involving preferential tax regimes, integrated corporate groups and centralized shared-service arrangements. The emerging framework, however, raises a broader policy question. While transfer-pricing rules seek to ensure that controlled transactions reflect the arm's-length principle, applying that principle in practice can be difficult where the transaction involves highly integrated group services for which no exact uncontrolled comparable exists. Recent Kenyan transfer-pricing disputes show disagreements over the functional characterization of intra-group services, benchmarking, allocation keys, and the choice between one-sided and two-sided transfer-pricing methodologies. The problem is compounded when the same economic transaction is subsequently examined under Value Added Tax (VAT). Section 13 of the VAT Act, 2013 provides that where a supplier and recipient are related, the taxable value is the open market value of the supply. The coexistence of an income-tax transfer-pricing analysis and a VAT open-market-value analysis creates a…

title: A ATUAÇÃO DO ENFERMEIRO NA ESTRATÉGIA DE SAÚDE DA FAMÍLIA NA PROMOÇÃO DA QUALIDADE DE VIDA DA POPULAÇÃO ADSCRITA
abstract: Introdução: A Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) constitui a principal porta de entrada do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), sendo a Estratégia Saúde da Família (ESF) fundamental para a promoção da saúde e da qualidade de vida da população. Nesse contexto, o enfermeiro exerce papel essencial na prevenção de agravos, no cuidado integral e na organização das ações de saúde. Objetivo: Analisou-se a atuação do enfermeiro na Estratégia Saúde da Família, com ênfase na promoção da qualidade de vida da população adscrita. Metodologia: Tratou-se de uma pesquisa descritiva, de abordagem qualitativa, baseada em revisão bibliográfica e documental. Foram consultados artigos científicos e documentos oficiais do Ministério da Saúde, publicados entre 2017 e 2026, nas bases SciELO, LILACS e BDENF. A seleção dos materiais ocorreu mediante critérios de inclusão e exclusão previamente definidos, seguida de leitura exploratória e analítica. Resultados: Os resultados demonstraram que o enfermeiro desempenha papel estratégico na promoção da saúde, na prevenção de agravos, na educação em saúde, no acompanhamento de grupos prioritários, nas visitas domiciliares e na organização do trabalho das equipes. Destacou-se, ainda, a importância dos indicadores de saúde no planejamento e na avaliação das ações, embora tenham sido identificados desafios relacionados à sobrecarga de trabalho, à insuficiência de recursos e…

title: Flexible strategy for purine supply in tumours
Meaning-making amid existential uncertainty: a hermeneutic phenomenological study of parents of children with trisomy 18
Escala de medición de capacidades dinámicas para hacer frente a la incertidumbre mediante la integración de prácticas de prospectiva estratégica y agilidad estratégica
abstract: The development of dynamic capabilities, strategic foresight, and strategic agility is fundamental to deal with uncertainty in the business environment, although their theoretical and empirical integration remains in its early stages. This study advances the construction and validation of a measurement scale that integrates these perspectives in order to address environmental uncertainty. Based on the study of 80 Argentine high-technology companies, a 16-item scale structured into four key dimensions is proposed: strategic foresight, customer-oriented seizing, systemic and functional reconfiguration, and agile reconfiguration. This work contributes to strategic management both theoretically, by enriching the dynamic capabilities framework, and methodologically, by proposing a rigorous and parsimonious scale. Furthermore, the identification of practices that enable firms to prepare to act proactively and respond quickly and effectively to uncertain contexts constitutes a contribution to managerial practice.

title: Price-Driven Optimization of Photovoltaic and Battery Storage Sizing in Energy Communities for Smart City Applications
abstract: Energy communities are increasingly viewed as a practical mechanism for accelerating decentralized renewable generation, improving local resilience, and supporting the transition to low-carbon electricity systems. This paper develops and verifies a genetic algorithm-based optimization framework for sizing photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) in a four-dwelling energy community across alternative electricity price scenarios. The model maximizes the net present value (NPV) of the investment over the project lifetime while accounting for grid imports and exports, internal community trading, and operation and maintenance costs. A high-resolution simulation of PV output, household demand, battery operation, and peer-to-peer exchanges is used to evaluate each candidate configuration. The framework is tested across a wide range of grid buy, grid sell, and community trading price scenarios representative of current European market conditions. The results show that profitability is strongly driven by the spread between import and export prices. Positive NPVs are obtained only under favorable price regimes, with annual profits reaching up to EUR 137,663 when grid buy prices exceed 0.30 EUR/kWh and sell prices exceed 0.15 EUR/kWh. In most scenarios, optimal PV capacities approach their upper bounds, whereas battery capacities remain very small, indicating that expor…

title: A risk-averse bidding and scheduling strategy for process industry VPPs in demand response markets based on thermodynamically-enhanced RTN
Enhancing uncertain demand prediction in hospitals using simple and advanced machine learning
abstract: Abstract Background Early and timely prediction of patient care demand not only affects effective resource allocation but also influences clinical decision-making as well as patient experience. Accurately predicting patient care demand, however, is a ubiquitous challenge for hospitals across the world due, in part, to the demand’s temporal uncertainty, and to the difficulty in modelling future trends. Methods We used data from the Rambam Medical Center in Israel between the years of 2004 and 2007. The dataset comprised aggregate hourly patient arrivals to the hospital, spanning emergency department attendances, direct ward admissions, and X-ray department arrivals. The time-varying linear approach predicted all patient arrivals to the hospital hourly over a week and over 3 days based on factors including day of the week and previous 7-day arrival patterns. The neural network method leveraged a long short-term memory (LSTM) model, capturing non-linear relationships between past data and forecasting windows of up to 7 days. We evaluated the predictive capabilities of the two proposed approaches compared to three existing approaches-a seasonal naive approach, a reduced-rank vector autoregressive (RVAR) model and the trigonometric seasonality, Box-Cox transformation, autoregressive moving average errors, trend, and seasonal components (TBATS) model. Forecasts were issued every day …

title: LcWRKY18 negatively regulates anthocyanin biosynthesis and is associated with high temperature-induced regreening in Loropetalum chinense var. rubrum
Integrated assessment of appliance life-cycle GHG emissions: a modeling framework applied to washing machines in Europe
abstract: Abstract Electrical appliances are essential to modern life, and their use is increasing with electrification and digitalization, driving substantial energy and material demand, emissions, and waste. Current assessments often lack life-cycle coverage and sufficient granularity to fully capture environmental impacts and evaluate mitigation options. Here we develop GLANCE–GAINS, a bottom-up integrated modeling framework combining a dynamic material flow analysis (dMFA) model with a waste and pollution model and prospective life-cycle inventory data, linked with the MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM integrated assessment model (IAM). Our objective is to provide a flexible framework for assessing appliance life cycles and environmental footprints across regions, device types, and future socioeconomic and climate pathways, and for evaluating mitigation strategies related to efficiency, circularity, and power-sector decarbonization. As a case study, we apply GLANCE–GAINS to washing machines in Europe through 2050 to assess future stocks, energy use, material flows, and life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions under alternative mitigation scenarios. A middle-of-the-road socioeconomic trajectory shows continued growth in stock, energy demand, material use, and emissions to 2050. Circularity strategies can cut embodied emissions by ~ 70% and total life-cycle emissions by ~ 25%, with demand-side measur…

title: The GAGE survey. I. Deep multi-band stellar variability characterisation and automated classification towards Baade's window
abstract: Long-term photometric surveys of the Galactic bulge are vital for characterising its complex stellar populations and structural components, and they provide an essential observational foundation and preparatory framework for next-generation facilities. We present the initial results of the GalActic bulGe with plEiadi (GAGE) project, focusing on the discovery and comprehensive characterisation of variable stars within a field in Baade's window. Utilising archival data from the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) on the Victor M. Blanco 4--m Telescope, we applied high-precision point-spread function (PSF) photometry to a multi-band (ugriz) dataset spanning six years. We developed a reproducible multi-step detection pipeline using a generalised Lomb--Scargle analysis to search for periodic signals combined with robust polynomial modelling of the phased light curves to derive accurate mean multi-band magnitudes and luminosity amplitudes. Our selective quality cuts yield a final catalogue made of high-confidence light curves for 6,304 sources. Of these sources, 4,568 are in common with the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE,IV) catalogue, for which we provide a comprehensive multi-band light curve expansion. Additionally, our method uncovered 1,736 (∼ 28%) variable candidates absent from the OGLE,IV catalogue. We categorised these sources using a supervised random forest classifi…

title: Building the relational bridge: how frontline social support fosters market inclusion for consumers with disabilities
abstract: Purpose Drawing on transformative service research and the social model of disability, this study aims to examine how social support from frontline employees influences relationship quality and behavioral outcomes among consumers with disabilities. Design/methodology/approach Data collected from 131 consumers with disabilities in Türkiye were analyzed using a two-stage hierarchical component model via partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4. Findings Social support exerts a strong positive effect on relationship quality but does not directly influence repurchase intention or word-of-mouth. Relationship quality fully mediates both pathways, indicating that supportive interactions must first accumulate into relational bonds before generating behavioral loyalty outcomes among consumers with disabilities. Research limitations/implications The convenience sample limits generalizability. Self-reported data may involve social desirability bias. The sample predominantly comprises consumers with visual and orthopedic impairments; future research should examine more diverse disability types and cultural contexts. Practical implications Retailers should invest in the relational competencies of frontline staff rather than expecting social support to produce direct loyalty returns. Since relationship quality is the necessary conversion mechanism, frontline training …

title: Evolving Trends in the Value-added Apple Product Market in India
abstract: Background: The Indian apple sector supports farm income and agro-processing employment in the major producing states and supplies a widely consumed source of dietary fibre and micronutrients, giving it direct economic and public-health relevance. Although apple production increased during last decade, India still imports apples due to supply-demand gaps and post-harvest losses. Methods: The study uses secondary sources of datasets, viz., Annual Survey of Industries dataset, Indiastat and FAOSTAT supplemented by a structured survey of apple juice products listed on the Amazon India e-commerce platform. Descriptive analysis to calculate the share, along with data visualization using line graphs, bar charts and box-and-whisker plots, is used for the study. Result: Most apples are produced in Jammu and Kashmir (79%), with lesser shares from Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, showing regional differences in productivity. Despite strong production potential, apple processing is limited in major producing states due to inadequate local processing infrastructure, while non-producing states lead in value-added products. An increase in consumer preference for convenient and healthy food choices has further boosted demand for processed apple juice. To encourage sustainable growth, the industry should improve post-harvest facilities, expand processing in local areas and adopt new technolog…

title: Self-pleasure vs conformity: understanding Chinese Gen Z consumption behaviors in the smart electronics market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain how Chinese Generation Z consumers construct preferences by moving between conformity and self-pleasure across a digitally mediated smart-appliance journey. Design/methodology/approach An abductive qualitative design combines 48 in-depth interviews (16 each for smart kitchen appliances, floor-mopping robots and smart toilets) with consumer journey mapping. Self-determination theory, conformity theory, social comparison theory and constructive consumer choice guide cross-case interpretation. Findings Retrospective accounts suggest a transition consistent with comparison-mediated internalization. Social cues first reduce uncertainty; social comparison can then convert visible choices into personally relevant benchmarks. Research and use build competence and perceived fit, allowing autonomy and experiential satisfaction to become more influential. Post-purchase sharing satisfies relatedness and renews social influence. Two category attributes shape the path: decision risk/technical complexity and social visibility/identity expressiveness. Practical implications Brands should use credible social proof for discovery, comparison support for evaluation, reliable experiences for use and context-appropriate advocacy mechanisms after purchase. Originality/value The study distinguishes the roles of conformity, social comparison and self-determination wit…

title: Post-market safety signals of the Yomi dental robotic system: an analysis of FDA MAUDE reports
Market conditions, temporal dynamics, and short-run forecasting of Thailand’s fattening hog prices: a dynamic regression approach
abstract: Abstract Fattening hog prices are important to livestock producers, food supply chains, and food-price monitoring, yet their short-run movements may reflect multiple market and temporal influences rather than contemporaneous changes in production inputs alone. This study develops an interpretable dynamic-regression framework for analyzing and forecasting Thailand’s fattening hog prices using monthly data from January 2001 to February 2026. The model incorporates upstream livestock-market and feed-related input conditions, seasonal and temporal components, dated level-shift controls, and an autoregressive disturbance process, with robust inference and recursive out-of-sample evaluation. The results show a positive and statistically significant association between piglet and fattening hog prices, while the included feed-related price variables provide limited incremental explanatory information either individually or jointly. Seasonal and temporal effects are also evident. The dated level-shift controls capture conditional price-level differences, although broader stability diagnostics do not provide sufficiently uniform evidence to interpret them as confirmed structural breaks. The significant AR(1) coefficient indicates serial dependence in unobserved influences rather than a direct lagged-price effect. Forecast performance is evaluated over March 2024–February 2026 under two i…

title: Two locked operators report mixed-spot TME composition on CosMx carcinomas
abstract: This study presents two locked operators around a training-free composition baseline in a standalone SPGD-TME Methods implementation so that, for the locked or explicitly eligible malignant–neighbor comparison, a per-spot malignant fraction is written only where the reference can separate the malignant program from its neighbor: a KEEP/ABSTAIN reportability gate that withholds the malignant coordinate once the malignant–neighbor cosine reaches a frozen cutoff c ⋆ = 0.80 and a Patient_ID donor split that builds mixed spots and reference from disjoint patients. On four-patient CosMx basal-cell carcinoma, the operators recover named tissue objects: ulcerated-nodular Patient B is tumor-rich relative to Patient A, the wound axis on D-from-C decreases tumor fraction from 0.8425 to 0.4665, while fibroblast and MoMacDC increase and directed transfer recovers composition most tightly on B from A (RMSE 0.0659, spot-level PCC 0.9528). The frozen cosine reports KEEP and, therefore, a tumor fraction, on CosMx BCC (cosine 0.6037), independent CosMx NSCLC (tumor versus fibroblast 0.6482; directed-transfer RMSE 0.1066, spot-level PCC 0.8415), CosMx colorectal carcinoma (0.5058), and CosMx HCC (0.6486). A Study on the Economic Aspects of Market Price, Crop Arrivals and Minimum Support Price for Wheat in Madhya Pradesh
abstract: Wheat marketing in Madhya Pradesh is characterised by concentrated seasonal arrivals and the coexistence of administered minimum support prices (MSPs) and wholesale market price observations. This descriptive study examines a compiled monthly wheat-market series for 2015–2024, with official MSPs matched to the relevant rabi marketing seasons. The analysis covers market arrivals, a source-reported indicator of arrivals classified below MSP, a monthly price series associated with that classification and percentage deviations of reported prices from the applicable MSP. Annual arrivals ranged from 7,006 thousand tonnes in 2021 to 10,835 thousand tonnes in 2022; 62.97% of total recorded arrivals occurred during March–May. Arrival-weighting the monthly classified shares yields an overall reported below-MSP indicator of 21.62%, with annual estimates from 11.60% in 2019 to 37.78% in 2016. The arithmetic mean of monthly reported prices increased from ₹1,379 per quintal in 2015 to ₹2,130 in 2024. However, seven monthly price entries exceed their contemporaneous official MSPs, demonstrating that the reported classification and aggregate price series cannot be interpreted as verified transaction-level below-MSP sales. The results document substantial seasonality and variation in reported market indicators but do not establish causal effects of MSP policy or farmers’ individual price realis…

title: A novel absolute distribution measurement method of beam spot on target surface in intense pulsed neutron generator
abstract: The typical characteristic of high current and narrow pulse neutron generator is to produce complex mixed ion beams, and the instantaneous beam intensity can reach the ampere level, which makes it difficult to diagnose the beam profile distribution and deuterium ion composition distribution. Especially, the spatial distribution of deuterium/titanium ion ratio on the target surface cannot be obtained, and there is no measurement method for the absolute beam cross section distribution on the target surface. In this paper, we propose that the single-crystal silicon [Formula: see text] secondary ion mass spectrometry method can obtain the relative distribution of various ion components on the target surface. Combined with the measurement of target current and neutron yield, the absolute cross-section distribution of multi-component high-current ion beams in complex mixed ion beams and the spatial distribution of deuterium ion ratio on the target surface can be obtained. This can guide the beam optical design of high-intensity and narrow-pulse neutron generators, and will be helpful to the physical design of targets and the study of beam-target interaction.

title: Managing healthcare capacity and demand, not just emissions: decarbonization as a purpose-preserving health system sustainability strategy—an Alberta policy case study
abstract: Introduction Healthcare decarbonization is increasingly important, yet strategies often focus on emissions from care delivery rather than the climate-related demand and disruption that health systems must absorb. Climate pressures can increase service use, workforce strain, infrastructure risk, and fiscal pressure at the same time, making healthcare capacity as much a concern as emissions. Methodology We use Alberta Health Services (AHS), 2013–2024, as a descriptive single case and interpret the evidence through Purpose-Preserving Resilience (PPR), distinguishing documented findings from conceptual interpretation. Conclusion Decarbonization can create a triple dividend—population health, workforce, and fiscal benefits—when mitigation and adaptation preserve essential health-system purpose without transferring unsustainable burden elsewhere. Climate action should be embedded in governance, capacity planning, workforce strategy, infrastructure and performance measurement, with system-wide measures of purpose outcomes.

title: Associations of intrinsic capacity and an age-friendly environment with healthy aging among community-dwelling older adults in Yanzhou District, eastern China: a cross-sectional study of the potential indirect role of health-promoting behavior
abstract: Background The Healthy Aging Framework recognizes that intrinsic capacity and a supportive age-friendly environment are important foundations for achieving healthy aging. However, the links between these two factors and healthy aging, especially the possible indirect role of health-promoting behavior, are still unclear. This study uses the data from older adults in the community to explore the relationships among these variables. Methods From September 2024 to January 2025, a community-based cross-sectional study was carried out in Yanzhou District, Jining City, Shandong Province, China. The research participants were older adults aged ≥60 years. The Healthy Aging Questionnaire, the reverse-scored 10-item Chinese Frailty Screening Scale, the Age-Friendly Cities and Communities Questionnaire, and the simplified Chinese version of the Health-Promoting Behavior Scale for Older Adultps were used to evaluate healthy aging, intrinsic capacity, the age-friendly environment, and health-promoting behavior, respectively. The Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated, and the unadjusted and covariate-adjusted structural equation models were used as co-primary analyses. Covariates included age, sex, type of residence, marital status, education level, personal monthly income and the number of chronic diseases. title: Thực trạng năng lực triển khai hoạt động phòng, chống tăng huyết áp tại các trạm y tế xã, phường của Thành phố Hà Nội năm 2025–2026
abstract: Tăng huyết áp là yếu tố nguy cơ quan trọng gây bệnh tim mạch và tử vong sớm. Trạm y tế xã, phường giữ vai trò quan trọng trong dự phòng, phát hiện, điều trị và quản lý người bệnh tăng huyết áp tại cộng đồng. Tuy nhiên, hiệu quả triển khai các hoạt động này phụ thuộc vào năng lực chuyên môn, trang thiết bị và khả năng cung ứng thuốc tại tuyến y tế cơ sở. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm mô tả thực trạng năng lực triển khai hoạt động phòng, chống tăng huyết áp tại các trạm y tế xã, phường của thành phố Hà Nội năm 2025-2026. Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang, điều tra toàn bộ 126 trạm y tế xã, phường từ tháng 2 đến tháng 5 năm 2026. Các nội dung đánh giá bao gồm trang thiết bị y tế, sự sẵn có của thuốc điều trị tăng huyết áp và việc triển khai các hoạt động tư vấn, đo huyết áp, điều trị và quản lý người bệnh. Kết quả cho thấy 97,6% trạm y tế có máy đo huyết áp và 96,0% có ống nghe, nhưng tỷ lệ đủ số lượng tương ứng chỉ đạt 62,7% và 65,9%. Tỷ lệ có máy điện tim là 61,9%, máy khử rung tim là 2,4%; chỉ 0,8% có đủ số lượng máy khử rung tim. Tỷ lệ sẵn có của các thuốc hạ áp chính dao động từ 62,7% đối với enalapril đến 83,3% đối với amlodipin; 72,2% trạm y tế có từ 3 nhóm thuốc hạ áp trở lên. Phần lớn trạm y tế triển khai các hoạt động tư vấn yếu tố nguy cơ, đo huyết áp, điều trị và quản lý người bệnh, trong khi thực hiện điện tâm đồ và đánh giá nguy cơ tim mạch còn hạn chế. title: Efecto de los ciclos de congelación-descongelación sobre la capacidad de retención de agua, textura y microestructura en carne bovina comercializada en Calceta, Ecuador
abstract: Objetivo: Se determinó el efecto de los ciclos de congelación-descongelación sobre la Capacidad de Retención de Agua (CRA), el perfil de textura y la microestructura de carne bovina comercializada en Calceta, Ecuador, debido a su importancia en la conservación de la calidad del producto. Metodología: Se seleccionaron intencionalmente cinco tercenas que declararon comercializar carne de bovinos con características similares de raza, sexo y edad. De cada establecimiento se obtuvo una muestra de 1 kg del músculo pulpa redonda, dividida en cuatro submuestras de 250 g, correspondientes a los tratamientos de 0, 10, 30 y 60 días de almacenamiento congelado acumulativo. Se determinaron la CRA, los parámetros de dureza, elasticidad, cohesividad y masticabilidad, y las características microscópicas mediante observación descriptiva. Los datos instrumentales se analizaron mediante estadística descriptiva y modelos lineales generalizados. Resultados: Se identificaron diferencias estadísticamente significativas en la CRA entre tercenas y tratamientos. También se observaron diferencias en los parámetros de textura, con variaciones según el establecimiento, el tiempo de almacenamiento y su interacción. title: Assessing the capacity of age-friendly communities to support older adults' digital inclusion: a probabilistic linguistic evaluation framework
abstract: Background Digital public services are expanding at the community level, yet older adults experience variation in digital inclusion. Research centers on individual digital divides or macro-level digital governance. How communities shape resource access, sustained use, and public participation remains underexamined. This capacity operates through digital infrastructure access, digital service support, support for digital capability development, and digital participation and sharing. Methods We develop a system of four primary dimensions and 16 indicators and assess eight age-friendly communities in Shijiazhuang. Standardized community evidence packages are used as the factual basis for structured expert assessment. The resulting linguistic judgments are aggregated using probabilistic linguistic term sets (PLTSs), weighted by entropy-derived discriminatory information, and ranked using TOPSIS, with weight-perturbation sensitivity analysis used to examine ranking stability. Results The communities differ descriptively in digital inclusion, but rankings show no fixed pattern by community type. Digital education activities, service terminals, volunteer services, support consultations, and online participation provide strong discriminating information. Conclusion The framework supports assessment of resource conditions, institutional support, capability support, and participation-cha…

title: Thực trạng năng lực triển khai hoạt động phòng, chống bệnh đái tháo đường tại các trạm y tế xã, phường của Thành phố Hà Nội, năm 2025 - 2026
abstract: Trong bối cảnh Hà Nội sắp xếp lại đơn vị hành chính và triển khai mô hình chính quyền địa phương hai cấp, việc đánh giá khả năng cung cấp các hoạt động phòng, chống và quản lý bệnh đái tháo đường (ĐTĐ) tại tuyến y tế cơ sở là cần thiết để định hướng phân bổ nguồn lực. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm mô tả thực trạng năng lực triển khai hoạt động phòng, chống bệnh đái tháo đường tại các trạm y tế xã, phường của thành phố Hà Nội năm 2026. Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang, điều tra toàn bộ 126 trạm y tế (TYT) thuộc khung khảo sát của thành phố Hà Nội, gồm 51 TYT phường và 75 TYT xã, từ tháng 2 đến tháng 5/2026. Số liệu được thu thập bằng bộ câu hỏi tự điền về nhân lực, trang thiết bị, thuốc và khả năng cung cấp dịch vụ; riêng số liệu sử dụng dịch vụ được hồi cứu cho giai đoạn 01/7/2025–31/3/2026. Tần số, tỷ lệ phần trăm được mô tả; so sánh giữa TYT phường (quy ước nhóm nội thành) và TYT xã (quy ước nhóm ngoại thành) bằng kiểm định χ² hoặc Fisher exact khi phù hợp, với α=0,05. Có 88,9% TYT triển khai dịch vụ quản lý/điều trị ĐTĐ thuộc phạm vi bảo hiểm y tế (BHYT). Thiết bị xét nghiệm đường huyết nhanh có tại 75,4% TYT; 41,3% TYT báo cáo thiết bị này đủ phục vụ hoạt động chuyên môn. Metformin và Gliclazid sẵn có lần lượt tại 71,4% và 69,8% TYT, trong khi Insulin chỉ có tại 16,7%; 25,4% TYT không có bất kỳ một trong ba nhóm thuốc khảo sát tại thời điểm thu thập số liệu. title: Literature review of wildlife disease surveillance capacity in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations region: status, gaps, and recommendations for national and regional strengthening
abstract: Southeast Asia is a globally recognized hotspot for emerging infectious diseases, yet wildlife disease surveillance (WDS) across the region remains fragmented, under-resourced, and poorly characterized. This review used domains adapted from a Needs Assessment Tool (NAT) for national wildlife health programs as an organizing framework to synthesize evidence from peer-reviewed literature, World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) country profiles and surveillance surveys, and regional network reports to analyze WDS capacity in the ASEAN region. Findings show predominant reliance on passive, outbreak-driven surveillance; fragmented legal and governance mandates; limited wildlife-specific laboratory capacity; non-interoperable digital data systems; and dependence on externally funded, time-limited projects for sustained surveillance activity, alongside promising innovations, including digital field data tools, ranger- and community-based networks, and multisectoral One Health platforms, in several countries. The review highlighted wide heterogeneity within the region, from highly institutionalized systems to near-absent or limited documented infrastructure. Regional mechanisms, including the ASEAN One Health Network, the South-East Asia Wildlife Health Network, and WildHealthNet, provide a foundation for coordination, but gaps in systematic surveillance, data sharing, and sustain…

Evaluation of antibacterial activity and the mechanism of naringenin against Mycoplasma synoviae
abstract: The global antibiotic resistance crisis has fueled a demand for promising novel alternatives. Naringenin, a type of traditional Chinese medicine, is known for its anti-tumor, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial activities. However, the inhibitory effect of naringenin on Mycoplasma has not yet been established. Herein, we reported that naringenin effectively inhibited various mycoplasmas. Using Mycoplasma synoviae ( M. synoviae ) as a model, naringenin inhibited cell growth, biofilm formation, cell division, and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of naringenin against M. synoviae was identified as 125 and 250 µg/mL, respectively. Dose-dependent inhibition effect of naringenin on the growth of M. synoviae . The anti-biofilm effect of naringenin was confirmed using crystal violet staining and laser confocal microscopy. Scanning electron microscopy showed that both cell length and width were significantly reduced, and the length/width ratio was significantly increased, indicating that cell morphology changed from spherical to rod-shaped upon treatment with naringenin. title: Study on the Uniaxial Compressive Mechanical Properties and Instability Mechanism of Fractured Coal–Rock Composite Bodies
abstract: Abstract In coal–rock systems, the weak interlayer zones between coal and rock strata are primary regions for fracture distribution, and the presence of fractures within the coal significantly influences the mechanical properties and engineering stability of coal–rock assemblages. Therefore, investigating the mechanical behavior and failure characteristics of coal–rock assemblages containing fractured coal is of great significance for controlling the stability of deep coal–rock engineering projects and preventing dynamic disasters. To investigate the impact of fractured coal on the mechanical characteristics of coal–rock systems, uniaxial compression experiments were conducted on coal–rock composite bodies with different fracture angles. The results indicate that as the fracture inclination angle increased from 0° to 90°, the average peak strength of the composites rose from 6.41 to 13.09 MPa; however, these values remained significantly lower than that of the intact composite (22.56 MPa), representing a reduction of 41.71% to 71.59%. During the uniaxial compression process, the internal energy of the samples is converted into the expansion of macroscopic cracks, and the failure modes are primarily tensile failure and shear failure. title: Deformation mechanism of a large-span small-clearance twin tunnel crossing a fault fracture zone
abstract: This study investigates the deformation behavior of large-span small-clearance twin tunnels crossing a fault fracture zone, using the Nanxiangling Tunnel as a case study. A closed-loop framework integrating numerical prediction, monitoring feedback, and model calibration is established. A three-dimensional FLAC3D model of sequential twin-tunnel excavation reproduces the spatial distribution of surrounding-rock displacement and support axial forces, while an integrated sensing–transmission distributed optical fiber monitoring system based on Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry (BOTDR) synchronously captures crown settlement and horizontal convergence at four typical sections. Taking the measured displacement at the fault-core section as the target, pattern-search back analysis inverts the elastic modulus, cohesion, and internal friction angle of the fault-zone surrounding rock, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0.94 between simulated and measured crown settlements. Crown settlement at the fault core is amplified to 11.39 and 12.90 mm in the left and right tunnels, 75% and 66% larger than at the normal section. The longitudinal disturbance zone spans 405–545 m, with a strong-influence range of about 60 m (3.3 times the fault width). Mechanism of shallow hard-shell-layer formation for newly-reclaimed dredged silt using vacuum dewatering combined with preloading
abstract: Newly-reclaimed dredged silt sites present a critical geotechnical challenge immediately after hydraulic filling. The ground surface remains as fluidized mud, preventing personnel and equipment access, yet conventional treatment methods assume the site is already accessible. This paper proposes a vacuum dewatering combined with preloading (VDCP) method for rapid formation of a shallow hard-shell layer without sand cushions or prolonged drying. A three-dimensional horizontal–vertical drainage network is established, coupling free-water extraction and negative-pressure consolidation. Physical model tests on Xiamen dredged silt (initial water content 281%) and Plaxis 2D numerical simulations are conducted to investigate the reinforcement mechanisms during the hard-shell formation stage. After 1,188 h of vacuum extraction, the average water content of the shallow soil decreases to 58%, the void ratio reduces from 7.53 to 1.49, and the ultimate bearing capacity increases from near zero to over 40 kPa, meeting the requirements for personnel and light machinery access. title: Nonlinear Resonance-Flattening Mechanism of an Internally Integrated TLCD for an Ultra-Large Floating Energy Island
abstract: Ultra-large floating energy islands are susceptible to pitch resonance, which can compromise operational stability and structural performance. This study investigates the potential of an internally integrated tuned liquid column damper (TLCD) to suppress pitch motion and reshape the resonance response. A mechanism-oriented framework combines case-specific analytical response reconstruction, a reduced-order pitch–liquid formulation, and supplementary nonlinear liquid-column analysis. Particular attention is given to liquid participation, the phase relationship between the control moment and platform motion, and amplitude-dependent hydraulic dissipation. The reconstructed response shows a decrease in the peak pitch response amplitude operator from 16.55 to 2.11 deg/m, corresponding to approximately 87% suppression, together with an approximately fourfold increase in the half-power bandwidth. These characteristics indicate a lower, broader resonance peak and reduced local sensitivity to excitation frequency. The supplementary liquid-column analysis independently demonstrates that quadratic hydraulic losses strengthen equivalent damping as liquid motion increases. How peer connection patterns shape mental health among university students: mechanism identification, pathway comparison, and contextual boundary conditions
abstract: University students show rising rates of psychological distress, yet research on how peer connection translates into mental health has been limited by single-dimension classifications, parallel mediator framings, and one-at-a-time moderator tests. Drawing on attachment, social support, and social identity traditions, this study modeled peer connection in terms of strength, breadth, quality, and reciprocity and combined latent profile analysis (LPA) with chained mediation and moderated mediation estimation in a stratified sample of 2,810 students from six Chinese universities. In total, four profiles were identified—high-quality high-frequency, moderate balanced, broad-but-shallow, and isolated–detached—which differed markedly in dual-factor mental health indicators. A sequenced self-efficacy → emotion regulation chain accounted for most of the connection benefit, but its share varied by profile contrast: The full chain was most prominent in comparisons involving isolation, while the first-stage self-efficacy pathway predominated in comparisons involving breadth without quality. The chained indirect effect was partially supported: It dominated in the high-quality versus isolated contrast but was exceeded by the self-efficacy-only pathway in the breadth-without-quality contrast, indicating profile-specific mechanism heterogeneity. title: Skew scattering induced contribution to orbital Hall response
abstract: Abstract Our study investigates the orbital Hall (OH) conductivity originating from the disorder induced mechanisms, namely side-jump and skew scattering. On treating the disorder potential within the first-order Born approximation and beyond and employing the quantum kinetic approach, the general scaling law for both mechanisms in terms of disorder potential is provided to signal out the process experimentally. The calculations have been processed for the three-dimensional Weyl semimetals under an oscillating electric field. We reveal that the higher order disorder contributions leading skew scattering process dominates the orbital Hall conductivity over the intrinsic and side-jump processes. In addition, we demonstrate the tunable nature of the extrinsic OH conductivity with the strength of the disorder potential and the external field. Finally, our findings highlights disorder scattering as a potential route for orbital transport.

title: Field phenotyping and targeted ILP marker screening of Indian mustard germplasm for white rust response
abstract: Abstract The present study was conducted during the Rabi season of 2023–24 to evaluate white rust response in Indian mustard germplasm and perform targeted intron-length polymorphism (ILP) marker screening of selected low-PDI entries. Agronomic traits were also recorded as secondary characterization of the germplasm panel. Sixty Indian mustard germplasm lines along with three checks were evaluated in augmented randomized complete block design (augmented RCBD) with a plot size of 2.4 m 2 and spacing of 30 × 10 cm. Augmented-design analysis indicated overall variation in the recorded agronomic traits; however, the unreplicated test-line design did not permit definitive identification of agronomically superior genotypes. Phenotypic screening under artificially created epiphytotic field conditions using standard scale for white rust revealed variation in disease response and twenty germplasm lines and two checks exhibited per cent disease index (PDI) values below 10%. Molecular screening using the ILP markers At5g41560 and At2g36360 detected the expected 430-bp and 750-bp marker-associated amplicons, respectively. Three entries—DRMRIJ-12-48, BIO-YSR, and PHR-2—produced the expected marker-associated amplicons for both markers. title: Durable response in a patient with HER2-positive esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and diffuse liver metastases treated with chemotherapy-free anti-HER2 therapy: a case report
abstract: Esophageal cancer (EC) is among the most prevalent and lethal malignancies worldwide, particularly in China where esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) represents the predominant histological subtype. Systemic chemotherapy plus immunotherapy remains the standard first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic ESCC; however, chemotherapy-associated toxicities frequently impair quality of life and limit treatment adherence. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a well-established therapeutic target in gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma, with multiple anti-HER2 agents approved globally. In contrast, HER2 overexpression is rare in ESCC, and its clinical significance and optimal treatment strategy remain poorly defined, especially in patients with extensive metastatic disease. Herein, we describe a 53-year-old male patient diagnosed with HER2-positive advanced ESCC complicated by diffuse liver metastases who achieved durable response following administration of a chemotherapy-free regimen combined with anti-HER2 therapy. Notably, the patient obtained durable disease control without traditional chemotherapy, supporting the feasibility and potential benefit of chemotherapy-free anti-HER2-based strategies in this rare molecular subset. This case provides valuable real-world evidence for the clinical utility of HER2-directed therapy in HER2-positive ESCC, ev…

title: Deep single-cell immune- and signaling profiles predict therapy response in chronic myeloid leukemia within hours
abstract: Abstract Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is effectively treated with small molecule BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) but as in all cancers, early identification of suboptimal responders and non-responders is a challenge. Through mass cytometry analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes collected on the first day of TKI treatment, we generated high-dimensional single-cell data from de novo chronic phase CML patients enrolled in two multicenter clinical trials (clinicaltrials.gov: NCT01725204 and NCT01061177). In leukocytes, dasatinib and nilotinib inhibited intracellular signaling within 1 or 3 h after first oral dose, respectively, and each TKI had a unique signaling signature reflecting its kinase specificity profile beyond BCR::ABL1. From these data, an immune and signaling profile was constructed for each patient that predicted the treatment response (BCR::ABL1 IS , %) during the first 12 months of treatment. The predictive features were drug specific: response to dasatinib was dominated by leukemic burden, neutrophil maturity (pSTAT3 Y705) and immune effector activity (pERK ½ in T- and NK cells), whereas response to nilotinib was driven by the intrinsic signaling states of CD34 + CD38 low CD25 + LSC-like cells (cleaved caspase-3, pCRKL Y207 and STAT3 [total and Y705]).
