title: Hypersomnia following COVID-19 infection or vaccination: a case series and response to low-dose aripiprazole
abstract: Sleep disturbances post-COVID-19 are increasingly recognized as one of the most common symptoms. While insomnia is the most frequently reported sleep disorder post-COVID-19, excessive sleep duration and central hypersomnias have also emerged as significant post-acute sequelae. Here, we present a clinical series of ten patients exhibiting sleep disturbances after COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Group A consists of seven adolescents who developed prolonged sleep duration (exceeding their baseline by at least 2 hours) following a COVID-19 infection. Group B includes three cases: one patient with exacerbated delayed sleep–wake phase disorder (DSWPD) post-infection, and two patients who developed central hypersomnias (idiopathic hypersomnia and Narcolepsy Type 1) subsequent to COVID-19 vaccination. For the seven patients with post-infectious prolonged sleep in Group A and for the DSWPD patient in Group B, pharmacological intervention with low-dose aripiprazole (mean final dose 1.4 mg) yielded robust clinical improvements. Recognizing these hypersomnia phenotypes and utilizing targeted therapies like low-dose aripiprazole is critical for restoring daily functioning and providing sustained support for individuals afflicted with Long COVID.

title: Đáp ứng kháng thể (IgM/IgG) theo thời gian và mối liên quan giữa tình trạng nhiễm với một số chỉ số huyết học và lâm sàng ở bệnh nhân sốt xuất huyết dengue nội trú tại Bệnh viện 199 Đà Nẵng, 2023–2024
abstract: Tại các khu vực lưu hành dịch sốt huyết Dengue (SXHD) cao như Đà Nẵng, sự biến đổi nhanh chóng của động học vi rút – kháng thể, và hiện tượng kháng thể IgG xuất hiện sớm ở bệnh nhân nhiễm thứ phát thường gây khó khăn trong chẩn đoán sớm cũng như tiên lượng bệnh. Nghiên cứu này nhằm mục tiêu là mô tả đáp ứng kháng thể (IgM/IgG) theo thời gian và phân tích mối liên quan giữa tình trạng nhiễm với một số chỉ số huyết học và lâm sàng ở người bệnh SXHD tại Bệnh viện 199, Đà Nẵng, giai đoạn 2023-2024. Nghiên cứu theo dõi dọc được thực hiện trên 128 người bệnh SXHD, gồm 42 trường hợp (32,8%) nhiễm tiên phát và 86 trường hợp (67,2%) nhiễm thứ phát. Mẫu huyết thanh giai đoạn cấp (M1) và giai đoạn hồi phục (M2, n=107) được xét nghiệm bằng Realtime RT-PCR (dương tính khi Ct ≤ 38), MAC-ELISA (IgM) và GAC-ELISA (IgG). Tình trạng nhiễm được phân loại theo tiêu chuẩn của WHO dựa trên mẫu M1: nhiễm thứ phát khi IgG dương tính, nhiễm tiên phát khi IgG âm tính. Kết quả cho thấy, trong 5 ngày đầu khởi phát (ngày 1–5), Realtime RT-PCR đạt tỷ lệ phát hiện 87,0% (94/108; 95% CI: 79,2–92,7), trong khi tỷ lệ dương tính với IgM chỉ đạt 22,6%. Tỷ lệ dương tính với IgM thấp ở giai đoạn cấp có thể liên quan đến đáp ứng IgG sớm (66,7% mẫu M1 dương tính với IgG) ở nhóm nhiễm thứ phát. title: “High demand, low training, moderate trust”: a needs assessment survey of AI integration in clinical medicine education among clinical medicine students
abstract: Objective As artificial intelligence increasingly permeates healthcare, it remains unclear whether clinical medicine students are adequately prepared for this transformation. This study aimed to investigate AI awareness, usage patterns, teaching needs, and curriculum expectations among clinical medicine students to inform evidence-based curricular reform. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was administered to 930 individuals affiliated with a medical and pharmaceutical college and its affiliated hospitals; 619 valid responses (94.18% current students/interns) were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results While 75.93% of respondents were aware of AI applications in healthcare, only 31.99% used AI tools frequently. Although 88.21% acknowledged the necessity of integrating AI into clinical medicine teaching, merely 48.47% reported that their institution offered relevant courses. Moderate trust in AI-assisted diagnosis was expressed by 70.76% of participants. The most desired teaching contents were case analysis and diagnostic simulation (75.61%), drug recommendation and dosage calculation (70.44%), and imaging/pathology recognition (65.91%). Conclusion These findings, derived from a predominantly student sample, highlight a pronounced ‘high demand, low training, moderate trust’ pattern in this vocational college context. A clinically grounded, progressively structured, …

title: Current status, associated factors, and demand priorities for health education among community priority populations in Nanjing, China
abstract: Objective To assess the current status, associated factors, and demand priorities for health education among community priority populations in Nanjing, China, and to provide evidence for the targeted delivery of primary health education services. Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted from April to May 2026 using a stratified multistage convenience sampling. Multiple-response analysis described access to health education content, formats, and channels. Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression were then performed to identify factors associated with the fulfillment of health education needs. The Kano model, Better-Worse coefficients, and average satisfaction coefficients were used to classify and prioritize health education needs across different population groups. Results Of 2,200 questionnaires, 1,844 valid responses were analyzed. Fulfillment rates for health education content, formats, and channels were 52.3%, 53.9%, and 55.8%, respectively. The most accessed content included chronic disease prevention and control (69.6%), commonly used medications (55.7%), and infectious disease prevention and control (51.8%). The main formats were videos (77.6%), text-based materials (70.6%), and images (68.5%), and the main channels were new media platforms (66.9%), community-based activities (64.1%), and television/radio (59.2%). Occupation, monthly per…

title: Influence of density-modulus relationships on the predicted biomechanical response of subject-specific mandibular finite element models: comparative analysis with experimental test data
abstract: Introduction Finite element (FE) analysis has become an essential tool for studying the biomechanical behavior of the mandible and predicting the mechanical performance of surgical and restorative interventions. The predictive accuracy of FE models, however, depends on underlying assumptions. Current models often rely on simplified homogeneous material assumptions and lack experimental comparison. Therefore, the present study aims to compare predictions from FE analyses with experimental test data to investigate the influence of heterogeneous density-modulus relationships on the biomechanical response of subject-specific FE models of the human mandible. Methods For this study, experimental testing with a universal testing machine and FE models of three human mandible specimens were developed in parallel. The experimental and computational boundary conditions included a 200 N load on the caudal side of the mandibular angle, embedding the condyles and fixing the incisor teeth or the left first molar for a central or unilateral load case, respectively. In the FE analysis, eight different density-modulus relationships were employed to represent the heterogeneous material of human bone. The global parameter stiffness and the local parameter surface strain were compared across different density-modulus relationships between predicted and experimental results. Results The experimental…

title: Orthodontic treatment need and perceived treatment demand among adolescents and their parents at a secondary school in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: alignment and associated factors
abstract: Objective To compare clinically assessed orthodontic treatment need defined by the Dental Health Component (DHC), aesthetic treatment need defined by the Aesthetic Component (AC), and perceived orthodontic treatment demand reported independently by adolescents and parents, and to examine need–demand alignment and factors associated with perceived treatment demand in a school-based sample. Methods This school-based analytical cross-sectional study included 581 adolescents aged 12–15 years and their parents at one secondary school in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Clinically assessed need was evaluated using the Dental Health Component (DHC), while aesthetic treatment need was evaluated using the Aesthetic Component (AC) of the Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN). Perceived treatment demand, dental satisfaction, and orthodontic information sources were measured independently using structured questionnaires. DHC–AC agreement was evaluated using Cohen's kappa. Factors associated with perceived treatment demand were examined using staged modified Poisson regression models with robust standard errors. Results Definite DHC-defined clinical treatment need was present in 27.2% of participants and definite AC-defined aesthetic treatment need in 8.6%. Binary DHC–AC agreement was 81.1% ( κ = 0.392), with marked asymmetry: 98.0% of AC-definite cases were also DHC-definite, whereas 31.0% …

title: Differentiated responses of ecosystem service supply and demand to urbanization across urban–rural gradients: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
First-line lorlatinib achieves durable systemic and intracranial response in EML4-ALK positive large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a case report with DNA/RNA fusion discordance
abstract: Background Lorlatinib, a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), is the current first-line standard of care for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring EML4-ALK rearrangement. However, ALK rearrangements are rarely identified in pulmonary large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC), and clinical evidence supporting ALK TKI directed therapy in this population remains limited. Case presentation We report a 35-year-old man diagnosed with advanced large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) carrying an EML4-ALK rearrangement. First-line lorlatinib resulted in rapid systemic tumor regression and complete intracranial response. At the data cutoff, the patient's progression-free survival had not been reached at 13.47 months with good tolerability. DNA-based next-generation sequencing identified two ALK rearrangements, whereas RNA-based sequencing detected only the canonical EML4-ALK rearrangement transcript. Testicular pain occurred during treatment and improved after dose modification; however, a definitive causal relationship could not be established. Conclusion This case report demonstrates the efficacy of lorlatinib as first-line therapy for large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma with ALK rearrangement. The observed DNA/RNA fusion discordance also illustrates the complementary roles of DNA- and RNA-based testing in interpreting…

title: Polystyrene nanoplastics exposure is associated with inflammatory and aging effects in aged mice via endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response and gut microbiome
abstract: Currently, it has been confirmed that polystyrene nano-plastics can damage the intestinal flora structure of young animals by inducing oxidative stress and inflammatory response. With the widespread use of plastic particles, the problem of plastic pollution has become increasingly serious. Although plastic products bring convenience to people’s lives, they simultaneously endanger the ecosystem and human health. Aging, as a natural process of physiological function decline is a significant feature of elderly individuals. We used naturally aged mice as a model and then fed them with polystyrene nanoparticles (PS-NPs) to explore their effects on the aging of mice and study the related molecular mechanisms. In this study, we observed that PS-NPs exposure was associated with reduced lifespan and with inflammatory and aging-related effects in naturally aged male and female mice. Furthermore, we found that PS-NPs inhibited endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response (UPR ER ) related proteins (p-IRE1, s-XBP1, PERK) and increased the expression of SASP and inflammatory genes in naturally aged male and female mouse tissues. Although α-diversity did not differ significantly between groups in either sex, PS-NPs induced compositional changes in the gut microbiota, decreasing the relative abundances of Actinobacteriota and Proteobacteria in aged female mice and those of Firmicutes and V…

title: Dynamic response and fatigue performance of wind turbine towers considering rotation-induced geometric stiffness and wind-sand erosion-corrosion damage
abstract: Wind turbine towers operating in wind-sand and saline-alkali environments are subjected to non-uniform coating erosion, which progressively exposes the local steel substrate and leads to cumulative corrosion during service. Because wind-sand-induced coating failure occurs non-uniformly, the steel substrate in different regions is exposed at different times, resulting in different corrosion ages and accumulated damage states. How to transfer the spatial distribution and temporal evolution of coating failure into a corrosion-damage model of the tower, and further quantify the effects of corrosion accumulation on structural dynamic response, fatigue life, and seismic fragility, remains a key issue in the life-cycle performance assessment of wind turbine towers exposed to wind-sand and saline-alkali environments. In this study, a 1.5 MW conical wind turbine tower is considered. Based on Bitter's erosion theory, rotor-wake characteristics, and regional wind-sand data, a coating damage assessment model is established, and a coating damage mass redistribution criterion is proposed to determine the location and time of first coating failure at the element level. The residual wall thickness and material properties of each element are then updated annually according to its corrosion age, thereby constructing an intact model and spatially non-uniform corrosion-accumulation models correspo…
venue: International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics

title: Expression of β-catenin, GLUT3, and HK1 in hepatoblastoma and their associations with cisplatin-based chemotherapy response and prognosis
abstract: Objective To examine the associations of β-catenin, GLUT3, and HK1 expression with response to cisplatin-based chemotherapy and event-free survival (EFS) in hepatoblastoma. Methods This retrospective study included 60 children. Pretreatment expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry, and regression models were used to examine associations with treatment response and EFS. Paired pre- and postchemotherapy specimens from 24 patients were compared, and transcript-level correlations were examined in 48 publicly available hepatoblastoma samples. Results Nineteen patients had a poor response, and 42 experienced an EFS event. Abnormal/high expression of the three markers and a high combined score were associated with lower objective response rates, but none of these associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for PRETEXT stage and distant metastasis. In sensitivity models adjusted for CHIC-HS risk, the associations for GLUT3 and the combined score were statistically significant. Abnormal β-catenin expression, high GLUT3 expression, and a high combined score were associated with shorter EFS in both adjusted models; hazard ratios in the primary models were 4.26, 2.41, and 2.37, respectively. HK1 was not significantly associated with EFS. In paired specimens, the proportion of cells with nuclear β-catenin positivity and the GLUT3 and HK1 H-scores increased after …

title: KerbTrack – A privacy-compliant modular AIoT solution for on-demand mapping of illegal kerbside bulk waste dumping
abstract: Purpose This study proposes an on-demand, privacy-compliant Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) framework for real-time detection and mapping of illegal kerbside household bulk waste dumping in urban environments. The system aims to support local councils with timely spatial intelligence for identifying unreported waste accumulation and recurring dumping hotspots. By integrating edge-based deep learning with waste collection vehicles, the proposed approach seeks to improve operational responsiveness, urban cleanliness, environmental sustainability, and evidence-based waste management decision-making while supporting broader smart city and sustainable development objectives. Design/methodology/approach An end-to-end AIoT system was developed using edge computing and deep learning-based object detection. A novel annotated dataset, KerbTrack, was curated to train and evaluate supervised object detection models, including YOLOv4 and DINO, for kerbside bulk waste detection. To assess scalability and generalisation, a large-scale synthetic benchmark, KerbTrack-Syn, comprising 5,114 images generated using a real-image-guided FLUX.1-dev and LoRA pipeline, was also developed. The detection pipeline was deployed on a NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge computer connected to an IMX335 USB camera mounted on waste collection trucks. Detection metadata and geospatial information were transmitte…

title: Motivation to mastery in knowledge management perspective: exploring how generative AI transforms student engagement and academic capability
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) competence and support on GenAI learning experience and absorptive capacity and, consequently, on GenAI performance from the integrated theoretical lens of digital and social capital theory. Design/methodology/approach This research adopted a quantitative, cross-sectional research design to collect data from 289 students and used covariance-based structural equation modelling for analysis. Findings The findings indicate that GenAI competence and support positively influence GenAI learning experience and absorptive capacity, which were subsequently found to be positively associated with student GenAI performance. Furthermore, GenAI learning experience and absorptive capacity positively mediate the relationships between GenAI competence, GenAI support and GenAI performance. Originality/value This study advances the intellectual capital research by extending the social-digital capital framework to student learning and knowledge assimilation processes. The study extends its framework from GenAI adoption research and offers a nuanced understanding of how GenAI resources get translated into performance outcomes in artificial intelligence-enabled learning ecosystems.

title: Case Report: Multidisciplinary management of toxic epidermal necrolysis in an elderly critically ill patient with multidrug exposure and concurrent MRSA pneumonia
abstract: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) is a life-threatening severe cutaneous adverse reaction whose management becomes particularly difficult in older critically ill patients with polypharmacy and active infection. We report a 74-year-old man with long-term ibuprofen exposure who was admitted for severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding and subsequently developed methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia requiring sequential antimicrobial therapy. During hospitalization, progressively confluent erythematous lesions evolved into bullae, erosions, and epidermal detachment, and TEN was diagnosed clinically after transfer to a specialized burn unit. Potentially causative medications were withdrawn or modified as clinically feasible. The patient underwent multidisciplinary management comprising supportive care, specialized wound management, susceptibility-guided anti-infective therapy, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) at 20 g/day for 5 days, and systemic methylprednisolone followed by tapering. Dongju lotion, a traditional Chinese medicine preparation used in the burn unit, was applied only as an adjunctive wound-bathing and cleansing measure. The cutaneous lesions subsequently ceased to progress, exudation decreased, and the erosive surfaces gradually re-epithelialized. Before discharge, most wounds had healed, with approximately 5% of the total body surface area remai…

title: Fear of aging, mental wellbeing, and ageist attitudes among young Lebanese adults: re-evaluating terror management and broaden-and-build theories
abstract: Introduction Ageist attitudes toward older adults remain understudied in Arab and Middle Eastern populations, particularly among young adults navigating economic and cultural pressures distinct from Western contexts where most theoretical models of ageism have been developed. This cross-sectional study examined whether fear of aging is associated with ageist attitudes among young Lebanese adults, and whether mental wellbeing moderates this relationship. Methods A convenience sample of 340 Lebanese adults aged 18 to 35, recruited online and in person, completed the Aging Anxiety Scale, the negative subscale of Kogan’s Attitudes Toward Old People Scale, and the WHO-5 Wellbeing Index. Results Contrary to Terror Management Theory (TMT)-informed expectations, fear of aging was negatively correlated with ageist attitudes at the bivariate level ( r = −0.135, p = 0.013), and this association was not significant after adjusting for sociodemographic and clinical covariates ( B = 0.04, 95% CI [−0.08, 0.16], p = 0.478). Mental wellbeing was also negatively correlated with ageist attitudes ( r = −0.179, p < 0.001) but was not significant after adjustment ( B = −0.11, 95% CI [−0.34, 0.12], p = 0.351), and it did not moderate the association between fear of aging and ageist attitudes ( B = 0.006, 95% CI [−0.018, 0.029], p = 0.644). Monthly income was the strongest correlate of ageist attit…

title: Successful blind bedside ileus tube placement supported by individualized nursing management in a patient at high risk of variceal bleeding: a case report
abstract: Background Blind bedside placement of an ileus tube in patients with decompensated cirrhosis and esophagogastric varices is exceptionally challenging because of the substantial risk of catastrophic variceal bleeding, particularly in the presence of portal hypertension, thrombocytopenia, and concurrent anticoagulation. Reports focusing on individualized nursing management in such high-risk situations remain scarce. Case presentation We describe a 74-year-old man with decompensated cirrhosis, portal hypertension, previous esophagogastric variceal bleeding, and superior mesenteric venous thrombosis who developed progressive incomplete intestinal obstruction complicated by sepsis without shock. Conservative medical treatment was initiated; however, worsening bowel obstruction led to blind bedside placement of a transnasal ileus tube. Given the patient's extremely high bleeding risk, an individualized nursing strategy was implemented throughout the peri-procedural period. Key nursing interventions included comprehensive bleeding-risk assessment, individualized peri-procedural management, dynamic tube monitoring, continuous surveillance for bleeding and sepsis, and multidisciplinary collaboration. In this case, the ileus tube was successfully advanced into the jejunum without procedure-related hemorrhage or other major complications. Progressive gastrointestinal decompression was ach…

title: Experimental research on characteristics of magnetic coupling resonance wireless power transfer system based on non-uniform low-frequency electromagnetic metamaterials
abstract: Abstract Low-frequency electromagnetic metamaterials (LFEMTM) can effectively improve the transfer efficiency of magnetic coupling resonance wireless power transfer (MCRWPT) systems. But it is difficult to accurately describe the electromagnetic characteristics of LFEMTM due to simulation and inversion errors encountered in practice. To address this issue, the paper proposes a 3 × 3 non-uniform LFEMTM array to enhance the transfer efficiency of a 6.78 MHz MCRWPT system. Differentiated electromagnetic response characteristics are constructed by adjusting the capacitance values of unit cells at different positions of the LFEMTM, and the optimal capacitance combination is obtained via experimental study. The experimental results demonstrate that the transfer efficiency of the system can be increased from 53.75% to 58.80% with the optimal non-uniform LFEMTM array, compared with the uniform array. Lateral offset experiments of the receiving coil reveal that the non-uniform array maintains a positive efficiency gain within the entire offset range. Its high-efficiency operating window (transfer efficiency >55%) spans −80 to +60 mm, outperforming the uniform array significantly. The research outcomes are conducive to further enhancing the transfer efficiency of MCRWPT systems.

title: Crowdedness in VR stores: effects on consumer responses
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework and integrating theories of inference, stress and social presence, this study examines how spatial and human crowdedness in virtual reality (VR) stores shape consumers' cognitive, affective and social responses. Design/methodology/approach Study 1 employed a 2 (spatial crowdedness: high vs. low) × 2 (shopping orientation: task-oriented vs. recreation-oriented) between-subjects experimental design with 171 valid responses. Study 2 employed a one-factor, three-level between-subjects design that manipulated human crowdedness (low, moderate, high), yielding 55 valid responses. Hypotheses were tested using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) and multiple regression analysis in SPSS. Findings Study 1 showed that high spatial crowdedness increased arousal but did not significantly affect store image. Shopping orientation moderated the effect of spatial density on store image evaluations, and both store image and emotional arousal predicted satisfaction. Study 2 showed that human crowdedness reduced store image evaluations and increased social presence primarily relative to the low-crowdedness condition, whereas arousal did not vary across density levels. Store image, emotional arousal and social presence all positively predicted satisfaction. Originality/value This study advance…

title: Perceived Emotional Invalidation and Employee Decision-Making: The Moderating role of sense of power
abstract: The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations among perceived emotional invalidation, sense of power and decision-making in employees of organizations. Additionally, the research aimed to examine the moderating role of sense of power in the relationship between perceived emotional invalidation and decision making of employees. A sample of 414 participants was selected from various public and private organizations using a convenient sampling technique. The study employed a cross-sectional research design and data analysis was conducted using SPSS version-23 and Jamovi (2.8.17). The findings showed that perceived emotional invalidation was positively related to overall decision-making and to sense of power. Sense of power was positively related to overall decision-making. Furthermore, the results showed a non-significant moderation of sense of power in this relationship. Similarly, the inclusion of employees from both private and public organizations made the findings relevant to a wider range of workplaces. The results could guide leadership development, the selection and training of supervisors, and employee support programs that promote respectful responses to emotions.

title: Successful hypofractionated whole-breast irradiation after breast-conserving surgery in a patient with a severe history of systemic lupus erythematosus: a case report on hypofractionation, prophylactic skin management, and DIBH
abstract: Background Historical concerns over radiation-induced toxicities frequently lead to the unwarranted omission of adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) in breast cancer patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, modern precision RT and assessments prioritizing concurrent disease activity challenge this perspective. Case presentation We present a 31-year-old woman with early-stage left-sided breast cancer (pTisN0M0) and a history of life-threatening SLE. Because her SLE was clinically confirmed to be in sustained unmedicated remission, she underwent breast-conserving surgery followed by hypofractionated whole-breast irradiation (HF-WBI). To strictly mitigate toxicity, we utilized volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) integrated with deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) for cardioprotection. Furthermore, stringent skin dosimetric constraints were applied alongside daily prophylactic topical superoxide dismutase (SOD) to potentially minimize radiofibrosis. The patient successfully completed RT, developing only Grade 1 acute radiodermatitis. Subsequent short-term follow-up at 10 months revealed excellent cosmetic outcomes and no early signs of late tissue toxicities. Conclusion A severe SLE history should not reflexively preclude modern breast-conserving therapy. For patients with clinically quiescent SLE, integrating VMAT-based hypofractionation, DIBH, stringent skin constrain…

title: Rethinking open government data utilization: the marvelous resonance between platform, task and data-using experiences
abstract: Purpose There remains a significant gap between the potential value of open government data (OGD) in strengthening governance and innovation and its actual utilization. How to provide actionable insights to promote the practical utilization of OGD warrants further investigation. Design/methodology/approach By conducting a user-centered randomized experiment and interviews, this study investigates the dual drivers (platform usability and task complexity) in users' data-using experiences (search behavior, satisfaction and intention to reuse) when utilizing three different OGD platforms for three types of data-seeking tasks. Self-feedback and behavioral data from 108 users were collected and analyzed on the OGD platforms. Findings The results indicated that platform usability and task complexity significantly influence users' OGD-using experiences. Research limitations/implications This study provides exploratory explanations for the dual driving pathways of user experiences with OGD use. It offers insights for designing data search tasks (in research) or test cases (in platform development) and constructing perceptual data provisioning platforms. Originality/value This study provides one of the first user-centered experimental investigations in the OGD field, directly addressing the scarcity of causal evidence on how platform design and task demands interact at a micro-behavioral…

title: Negotiated Religious Authority: A Knowledge-Power-Legitimacy Framework for Understanding Religious Influence in Contemporary Pakistan
abstract: Religious authority has become increasingly contested in contemporary Muslim societies as traditional religious institutions encounter challenges from emerging religious actors, expanding media platforms and changing forms of public engagement. In Pakistan, competing claims to religious legitimacy have intensified debates over who possesses the authority to speak for Islam and shape religious influence in the public sphere. Existing scholarship has examined the roles of religious scholars, institutions, Islamic movements and state actors; however, limited attention has been devoted to understanding how religious authority is produced through the interaction of Islamic knowledge, social power and legitimacy. This article addresses this gap by developing the concept of Negotiated Religious Authority and proposing a Knowledge, Power and Legitimacy Framework for analysing the production of religious influence in contemporary Pakistan. Drawing upon qualitative documentary analysis and a critical engagement with scholarship on religious authority, Public Islam and the sociology of religion, we argue that religious authority extends beyond scholarly credentials and emerges through ongoing processes of negotiation among religious actors, institutions and audiences. From this perspective, authority is neither an automatic consequence of formal religious training nor an exclusively insti…

title: Changes in apparent system performance after post hoc human review of a large language model-generated benchmark for hospital wayfinding search: a comparative methodological evaluation
abstract: Background We developed a hospital web application that searches 266 destinations and links results to indoor navigation. Its default retrieval tiers run locally; an optional cloud large language model (LLM) tier requires explicit invocation. Synthetic queries were used because default-tier searches are not server-logged. Objective We examined how post hoc review of an LLM-generated benchmark changed the apparent benefit of completed system updates. Methods Version v2 added pronunciation aliases to v1; v3 added colloquial knowledge, pronunciation forms, destination-level score combination, and false-match rules. Two v3 rules were informed by evaluation-query failures. A clinician and a medical administrative coauthor jointly reviewed 563 synthetic queries without blinding, excluding 129 and rewriting 289 under review-defined policies. The final data contained 401 answerable and 33 no-valid-destination queries. Archived versions were compared across sequential review stages and with lexical and embedding implementations. Results Among the same 192 answerable evaluation-query identifiers and final accepted destinations, rewriting increased top-1 accuracy from 43.8% to 62.0% for v1 and from 56.8% to 63.0% for v3. Their difference remained near 13 percentage points through earlier review stages and decreased to 1.0 point at rewriting. The tested multilingual-E5-small implementation…

title: Bridging the representation gap: the complementary efficacy of Perceptual Mapping in construction cost management
abstract: Purpose In the construction industry, cost information is critical for strategic decision-making, yet its representation remains complex due to a heavy reliance on Traditional Symbolic Representations like Bills of Quantities (BOQs) and Cost Plans. While Perceptual Mapping is a proven visual analytics technique for representing multi-dimensional trade-offs in other fields, it remains unexplored in construction. This study evaluates the efficacy of Perceptual Mapping versus Traditional Symbolic Representations in supporting multi-criteria cost decisions. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design surveyed 42 construction professionals comprising Quantity Surveyors, Architects and Engineers selected through purposive sampling. Respondents evaluated a Perceptual Map against a BOQ across five attributes: Visual Clarity, Grouping, Comparability, Complementarity and Decision-Making Efficiency. Data were analysed using one-sample t-tests, Kruskal–Wallis tests and post-hoc pairwise comparisons. Findings Results confirm that Perceptual Mapping significantly enhances decision-making across all attributes. The strongest consensus regarded Complementarity, positioning the technique as a Hybrid Information Model rather than a replacement for Traditional Symbolic Representations. A significant divergence in Visual Clarity was observed, with Quantity Surveyors perceiving the t…

title: Enhancing people–public–private partnerships in archaeological site management: a case study of the Santubong archaeological sites, Sarawak, Borneo
abstract: Purpose This study examines the application of the people–public–private partnership (P4) governance framework in managing the Santubong Archaeological Site with emphasis on stakeholder collaboration, governance effectiveness and sustainability. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a qualitative case study design integrating in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation and a supplementary stakeholder questionnaire. Qualitative evidence was analysed thematically, while questionnaire responses were summarised descriptively using the 19-response analytical dataset (n = 19). Findings The findings indicate that the P4 framework provides a useful collaborative governance structure, but its effectiveness is uneven and depends on institutional coordination, communication, stable resources, technical capacity and sustained community participation. Questionnaire frequencies are interpreted as descriptive stakeholder perceptions rather than statistical measures of governance performance. Research limitations/implications The study is a single-site qualitative case study. The supplementary questionnaire analysis is based on 19 responses and is weighted toward private-sector respondents; the percentages are therefore descriptive and not statistically representative of all P4 constituencies. The findings should be transferred to other heritage settings only…

title: Bilateral pleomorphic xanthoastrocytomas in a child: diagnostic challenges and single-stage surgical management - a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (PXA) is a rare circumscribed astrocytic tumor that typically presents as a solitary supratentorial lesion in children and young adults. Synchronous bilateral or multicentric presentations are exceptionally uncommon and may create diagnostic uncertainty and challenging surgical decision-making. Case presentation A 12-year-old girl presented after a first generalized tonic-clonic seizure following a two-month history of intermittent headaches. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated three cortical and cortico-subcortical frontal lesions involving both hemispheres. Whole-spine MRI and cerebrospinal fluid cytology showed no evidence of neuraxis dissemination. All visible lesions were resected during a single-stage bilateral frontal craniotomy using neuronavigation and intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. Histopathological and molecular analyses confirmed PXA, CNS WHO grade 2, with a BRAF V600E mutation. The patient developed a transient postoperative right-sided motor deficit clinically consistent with supplementary motor area syndrome, followed by complete neurological recovery. Serial follow-up MRI showed no residual or recurrent intracranial tumor, and there was no clinical or radiological evidence of dissemination during follow-up. At the latest follow-up, she was seizure-free and neurologically intact. Conclusio…

title: Occupational stress among education leaders in Uzbekistan: a cross-sectional survey of workload, failure appraisal, institutional sector and training
abstract: Purpose This study examines how often education leaders in Uzbekistan feel stressed at work, which demands, appraisals and institutional conditions accompany frequent stress and how far stress-resilience training reaches them. Design/methodology/approach A survey of 101 leaders of preschools, schools, vocational colleges and universities was analysed with exact tests, binary and ordinal logistic regression and content analysis of open responses. Findings A total of 38% reported frequent stress. It was more likely among leaders naming workload or time pressure (adjusted OR 7.90), seeing failure as stressful (adjusted OR 10.77) and leading non-state institutions (adjusted OR 4.20). Moreover, 76% had never received stress-resilience training. Research limitations/implications The design is cross-sectional and uses single self-report items from a convenience sample, so the associations are not causal. Practical implications Support could target workload and time, how leaders appraise setbacks and leaders of private institutions, with each measure evaluated before scale-up. Originality/value The study offers evidence on leader stress across all four levels of a Central Asian education system, identifies the private sector as a distinct site of leader stress and integrates appraisal and job demands-resources perspectives for educational management.

title: From clipboard to camera: an online video-based ergonomic assessment system for New Zealand workplaces
abstract: Background: Musculoskeletal disorders account for over 30% of work-related health harm in New Zealand (WorkSafe NZ). For forty years the response has rested on observational assessment (RULA, REBA, the NIOSH equation, and WorkSafe’s NZMAC, NZRAPP and NZART), applied with a clipboard, a printed score sheet and a trained assessor: expert-dependent, slow, and hard to repeat. Objective: To develop an online video-based ergonomic assessment system that analyses workplace tasks from a single standard video, and to establish how closely its outputs agree with laboratory reference methods.
venue: New Zealand Journal of Health and Safety Practice

title: The DARk side of aspartyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (DARS1): From tRNA aminoacylation to driver of liver cancer
Human bocavirus infection among hospitalized children in eastern China: epidemiology, co-infection, and time-series forecasting
abstract: Background Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) are the leading cause of pediatric hospitalization worldwide; data on human bocavirus (HBoV) epidemiology in eastern China remain scarce. Methods We enrolled 12,630 hospitalized children <18 years with ARTI from January 2025 to March 2026 across tertiary hospitals in eastern China. HBoV and other respiratory pathogens were detected using a commercial 13-target multiplex RT-PCR panel (SureX 13 Respiratory Pathogen Multiplex Kit; Ningbo Health Gene Technologies). A SARIMA model forecast HBoV positive rates for the next 30 weeks. Results Overall HBoV positive rate was 3.2%, with no sex difference ( p = 0.99) but peaking in children aged 1–<3 years (7.7%) and during June–October. Most common co-infections were human rhinovirus (Rhv), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human parainfluenza viruses (HPIV). Length of stay did not differ significantly across co-infection groups; the longest mean stay ( Mycoplasma pneumoniae , 8.3 days) was not significantly longer than the shortest (Chlamydia, 4.0 days; p = 0.279). By infection multiplicity, 230 children had mono-infection, 154 double infection, and 26 triple infection; mean length of stay was 5.9, 6.1, and 6.7 days, respectively (one-way ANOVA, F = 0.357, p = 0.700). Mean outcome score was lowest for triple infection (0.982) and highest for mono-infection (1.014). The SARI…

title: Physics-guided multi-scale temporal transformer with dynamic key variable selection for building energy consumption forecasting
abstract: Building energy consumption prediction plays a critical role in intelligent energy management, demand response, and low-carbon operation of smart buildings. This paper proposes a novel physics-guided multi-scale temporal Transformer (PMSTFormer) for building energy consumption forecasting. First, a dynamic key variable selection (DKVS) module is developed to adaptively estimate the contribution of heterogeneous input variables at each prediction horizon. Second, a multi-scale temporal fusion encoder (MTFE) is designed to capture temporal dependencies at multiple resolutions. Finally, a physics-guided thermal consistency learning (PTCL) strategy is proposed by embedding physical constraints into the optimization process. PTCL is implemented as a set of differentiable soft constraints that jointly optimize data fidelity and simplified thermal-response consistency. It does not require an explicit thermal model or solver in the loop, and is therefore complementary to methods that enforce physical consistency by construction. Extensive experiments are conducted on publicly available benchmark datasets Building Data Genome 2. Comparative studies demonstrate that the proposed PMSTFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting models. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies verify the effectiveness of each proposed module. The developed methodology not only improves f…

title: Effects of perceived justice and price fairness on passenger loyalty via satisfaction in Indian airlines: do gender and failure severity moderate such relationships?
abstract: Purpose This study examines how perceived justice in service recovery and price fairness influence passenger satisfaction and loyalty in the Indian airline industry. It further investigates whether gender and failure severity moderate these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 485 airline passengers in India who had experienced service failure and subsequent recovery efforts. Structural equation modeling was employed to test the hypothesized relationships. Findings The results indicate that perceived justice and price fairness significantly enhance passenger satisfaction and loyalty. Passenger satisfaction partially mediates these relationships. Multi-group analysis further shows that these relationships are stronger among female passengers and under low failure severity conditions. Research limitations/implications Future research could investigate the applicability of the conceptual framework across diverse service sectors by considering the variations in customer expectations and service delivery dynamics. Practical implications The findings suggest that airline managers should adopt severity-based recovery strategies, strengthen interpersonal recovery practices, and maintain transparent pricing policies to improve customer retention. Originality/value This study extends service-recovery literature by developing an integrated fairness–expectati…

title: Forecasting the future of postal services in Libya until 2030: a strategic analysis of the performance of Libya Post Company in the light of global Directions of the Universal Postal Union
abstract: يبحث هذا البحث مستقبل الخدمات البريدية في ليبيا حتى عام 2030 من خلال تحليل متطلبات الاتحاد البريدي العالمي وتوجهاته الاستراتيجية وتقييم آثارها على شركة بريد ليبيا. ويركز على التحول من المراسلات التقليدية إلى تسليم الطرود والخدمات اللوجستية والتجارة الإلكترونية والخدمات المتكاملة رقميا ، إلى جانب المتطلبات المتزايدة لجودة الخدمة والكفاءة التشغيلية والاستدامة وأمن المعلومات. يعتمد البحث نهجا وصفيا تحليليا يستند إلى المؤلفات العلمية الحديثة والتقارير الدولية والوثائق الاستراتيجية للاتحاد البريدي العالمي والمعلومات المتاحة عن شركة بريد ليبيا لتحديد مجالات التوافق الاستراتيجي والفجوات بين قدراتها المنشورة والمتطلبات القطاعية الناشئة. ويشير التحليل إلى أن تطوير الخدمات البريدية في ليبيا يعتمد على تنويع الأنشطة المدرة للدخل ، ودمج المنصات الرقمية مع عمليات الطرود والخدمات اللوجستية ، وتعزيز البنية التحتية التكنولوجية والقدرات البشرية. ويخلص التقرير أيضا إلى أن المواءمة مع متطلبات الاتحاد البريدي العالمي تتطلب ترجمة الالتزامات والتوجهات الاستراتيجية ذات الصلة إلى أهداف قابلة للقياس وبرامج تنفيذ ومؤشرات أداء. تم تحديد ثلاثة سيناريوهات مستقبلية: الاستمرارية المحدودة ، والتحول التدريجي ، والخدمات البريدية الذكية المتكاملة. وعلى الرغم من أن السيناريو الثالث يوفر أقوى مواءمة مع التطورات القطاعية الدولية ، فإن التحول التدريجي يمثل المسار الأكثر جدوى نحو تحقيقه. يوصي البحث باتباع نهج استراتيجي مرحلي لشركة بريد ليبيا ، مع إعطاء الأولوية للرقمنة والخدمات اللوجستية والطرود ، وتكامل التجارة الإلك…

title: How service quality drives purchase intention in cross-border livestreaming: trust and price sensitivity as mechanisms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how service quality dimensions in import cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) livestreaming influence consumer purchase intention, with customer trust as a mediating mechanism and price sensitivity as a moderating boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework and signaling theory, a four-dimensional service quality model – comprising information credibility, service responsiveness, streamer professionalism and cross-cultural appeal – was developed. The four dimensions were derived by decomposing the CBEC livestreaming encounter into its people, product and place elements and mapping them onto both the gap-based and Nordic service quality paradigms. These dimensions are conceptualized as quality signals that reduce information asymmetry inherent in cross-border livestreaming transactions. Survey data from 537 Chinese consumers with CBEC livestreaming purchase experience were analyzed using structural equation modeling (AMOS) and moderated mediation analysis (PROCESS). Common method bias was assessed through both Harman’s single-factor test and a common latent factor (CLF) approach. Findings All four service quality dimensions significantly enhance purchase intention. Customer trust partially mediates the effects of service responsiveness, streamer professionalism and cross-cultural appea…

title: A multi-strategy crested porcupine optimizer for air quality forecasting
abstract: Abstract Air quality prediction is critical for environmental governance and public health, but its accuracy depends heavily on model parameter configurations. Although the crested porcupine optimizer (CPO) has shown competitive performance, practical applications are often limited by low convergence accuracy and a tendency to become trapped in local optima. To address these limitations, an improved crested porcupine optimizer (ICPO) is proposed, which incorporates three targeted strategies to optimize search directions, step-size evolution, and population guidance. First, the guidance scheme of the fourth defense mechanism is reformulated using a dual-differential structure to enrich directional diversity within the optimal neighborhood, facilitating escape from local optima. Second, a nonlinear step-size evolution strategy is introduced to adapt search scales dynamically across different optimization stages, coordinating broad search with local refinement. Finally, a small-group guidance mechanism uses information from randomly sampled subsets of the population to diversify search directions. On the CEC2017 benchmarks, ICPO ranks second among nine algorithms and significantly outperforms six comparators, including CPO, under a common evaluation budget. In the reported air quality forecasting comparison, ICPO-optimized long short-term memory (ICPO-LSTM) achieves the lowest mea…

title: MFECL-DTI: Multiscale Feature Extraction and Cross-Branch Contrastive Learning for Drug–Target Interaction Prediction
abstract: Accurate drug–target interaction prediction plays an important role in drug discovery and repositioning. However, existing methods often struggle to fully exploit the complementary information between molecular structures and sequence representations. To address this issue, we propose MFECL-DTI, a dual-branch prediction framework integrating graph-based structural encoding, multiscale sequence feature extraction, cross-branch contrastive learning, and adaptive gated fusion. Specifically, the graph branch employs residual graph convolutional networks to extract structural features from drug molecular graphs and protein contact graphs, while the sequence branch combines multiscale convolutional neural networks with a Transformer to capture local patterns and contextual dependencies. Furthermore, a bidirectional contrastive learning mechanism is introduced to align the representations of the same drug–target pair across different branches. An adaptive gating mechanism then dynamically integrates complementary features for interaction prediction. Experiments on BioSNAP, DrugBank, and C.elegans achieve AUROC values of 0.925, 0.915, and 0.994, respectively, with corresponding AUPRC values of 0.927, 0.913, and 0.994. Comparative and ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving DTI prediction performance.

title: Multiple disease detection and prediction using advanced computing technologies: a comprehensive systematic review
abstract: Multimorbidity—the concurrent presence of two or more chronic long-term conditions—affects more than 37% of the global adult population and consumes 55%–80% of healthcare expenditure in high-income systems, yet artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic systems remain overwhelmingly disease-specific, creating a profound structural mismatch with the multi-disease complexity characterizing the majority of real-world clinical encounters across twelve review-defined disease groups mapped to World Health Organization (WHO) ICD-11 chapters. This systematic review, following PRISMA 2020 and registered with OSF.IO (Registration DOI number: 10.17605/OSF.IO/3HZ45; Date of Registration: 25 October 2026), evaluated advanced AI technologies for simultaneous multi-domain disease detection and prediction. Nine electronic databases, PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Springer Link, Wiley, MDPI, and Google Scholar, were searched for peer-reviewed literature published from January 2015 to 31 August 2026. Database-specific Boolean searches (full strings in Supplementary Table S1 ) combined AI terms with terms for the twelve review-defined disease groups. Quality appraisal was done using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST tools (Cohen's κ = 0.84 refers to study screening agreement). Of 4,215 records identified (3,368 after removing 847 duplicates; 612 full texts assessed; 332 exclu…

title: Mortality prediction at the tracheostomy decision point after liver transplantation: development and internal validation of a bedside risk score
abstract: Abstract Background Liver-transplant (LT) recipients requiring prolonged ventilation and considered for percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) have high short-term mortality, but LT-specific tools to support prognosis-aligned communication at this decision point are lacking. We developed and internally validated a simple PDT-day model and an integer Tracheostomy Decision-Point Risk Score (TRS) to estimate 90-day mortality from the PDT decision point in LT recipients undergoing PDT. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included 83 adult LT recipients undergoing PDT between December 2010 and June 2024. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 90 days from the PDT decision point, operationalized as the day of PDT. The model estimates risk after the PDT decision point and not the causal effect of PDT. Logistic regression used routinely available PDT-day variables; internal validation used bootstrap shrinkage. Discrimination and calibration were assessed by AUC, Brier score, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope. Coefficients were converted to an integer TRS. Results 90-day mortality was 62.7% (52/83). Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD; +5 points), age (+ 10 years), and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; +5 s) measured on the PDT day were independently associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratios 2.54 [95% confidence int…

title: First‐principles prediction of high solar‐to‐hydrogen efficiency in TaOX 2 and Janus TaOXY (X, Y = Cl, Br, I) monolayers
abstract: Abstract Many photocatalytic water splitting catalysts exhibit generally low energy conversion efficiencies due to insufficient sunlight absorption, stringent redox overpotential requirements, and rapid photogenerated carrier recombination. Based on first-principles calculations, this study systematically investigates the structural, optical, and electronic properties of two-dimensional (2D) TaOX 2 and its Janus TaOXY (X, Y=Cl, Br, I) monolayers. Our calculations reveal the band edges of these mechanically and optically anisotropic indirect-bandgap semiconductors (1.778–1.844 eV) span the redox potentials for water splitting, satisfying the requirements for photocatalytic water splitting. Importantly, the Janus structures generate an internal electric field due to the symmetry breaking of the top and bottom surfaces, which effectively suppresses the recombination of photogenerated carriers. Consequently, the carrier utilization efficiency of TaOIBr, which has the lowest utilization among the Janus structures (46.21%) is significantly higher than the maximum value (36.2%) observed for the TaOBr 2 at pH = 0. Except for TaOCl 2 , which does not satisfy the requirement for overall water splitting, and TaOI 2 , whose STH efficiency at pH = 0 is 9.12%, below the 10% commercial STH benchmark, the remaining TaOX 2 exceeds the benchmark within their applicable pH ranges. In particular, …

title: Time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired model for late dynamic PET frame prediction from early [ 11 C] raclopride
abstract: Abstract Objective . To reduce the burden of dynamic positron emission tomography (PET) acquisition while preserving quantitative analysis, we propose a time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired residual denoising framework for predicting late dynamic PET frames from a short early acquisition window (10 min in this study) of [ 11 C] raclopride. Approach . Irregular native dynamic frames were converted to a uniform 1 min indexing grid using overlap-weighted rebinning. The first 10 min were used as the early input and to derive the spatial and intensity preprocessing parameters. For each requested late time, a shared time-aware 3D U-Net predicted an anchor-relative residual with respect to the last available early frame. A training-only denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM)-inspired Gaussian perturbation and noise-prediction branch shared the prediction backbone and regularized residual learning, while temporal-consistency loss constrained predicted frame-to-frame changes. All learning-based methods used identical subject-wise five-fold cross-validation within the development cohort, followed by evaluation on a fixed internal test set; the external cohort was held out from model selection. Main results . The proposed approach achieved higher Peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index measure and lower mean absolute error than the comparison methods, whi…

title: Development of a Failure Prediction System for Industrial Laser Diodes Based on Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: Industrial laser diodes are essential devices used in semiconductor chip manufacturing, where the precision and stability of laser output strongly affect the process yield. However, under long-time operation and high thermal stress, these lasers tend to degrade slowly, sometimes leading to unexpected failure that causes production interruption and cost increasing. In this work, a data-driven fault prediction system is proposed for early detection of degradation behavior in industrial laser diodes. The experimental data were collected from a Monaco 517-40-30 femtosecond laser operating in an actual production environment. The proposed system monitors a set of electrical, thermal, and optical parameters that reflect the operational condition and degradation characteristics of the laser diode. After normalization, noise filtering and outlier removal, a feedforward neural network was trained using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm with Mean Squared Error (MSE) and regularization to reduce the overfitting problem. The model achieved above 98.9% for both training and testing accuracy, with minimum F1-score and Recall values of 0.9. This shows that the system can do early fault detection quite reliably even in industrial conditions. From these results, the system is considered a practical solution for predictive maintenance and can help improve uptime and reliability of laser equipmen…

title: Adaptive Semantic Prediction in Dynamic Linguistic Environments: Computational-Neural Insights From Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
abstract: Abstract Real-world language processing unfolds in environments of volatility and uncertainty, requiring comprehenders to continuously adapt semantic predictions as environmental statistics change. However, the fundamental computational-neural mechanisms supporting such hierarchical adaptive prediction remain incompletely understood. Critically, our goal was to examine how comprehenders update their beliefs about high-level environmental reliability as evidence accumulates across trials, and how this update modulates low-level semantic prediction. Here, we introduce a paradigm that extends traditional filler-based designs and allows for the examination of trial-by-trial adaptation and corresponding neural responses. We further implemented a computational neural analytical framework based on the Hierarchical Gaussian Filter to model the trial-by-trial hierarchical inference process. We showed that environmental statistical regularities systematically modulate multiple neural signatures, from the well-established N400 to later ERP components, such as late anterior positivity (LAP) and P600, as well as cortical oscillatory components in the theta and beta bands. Model-based analyses showed that distinct computational variables were reflected in dissociable neural signatures. At the ERP level, N400 activity was associated with both high-level belief states and precision-weighted pr…

title: Dynamic Graph Link Prediction by Integrating Historical Recurrence Signals and Time-Weighted Similarity Matching
abstract: Future link prediction on dynamic graphs must rank both recurring interactions and links between previously unconnected nodes. We extend the CRAFT-R candidate-aware cross-attention matcher with explicit historical recurrence statistics, time-weighted embedding similarity, and candidate-specific residual fusion. Under chronological splits and fixed 100-candidate queries on three competition datasets, we evaluate four retrained configurations alongside history-based ranking rules. The full model achieves test mean reciprocal ranks (MRRs) of 0.845, 0.296, and 0.576 on dataset1, dataset2, and dataset3, respectively, exceeding the backbone control by 0.033, 0.026, and 0.033. Removing the statistics branch reduces MRR by 0.020, 0.007, and 0.004; removing the similarity branch reduces it by 0.012, 0.021, and 0.012. Separate strict-past analyses show that direct recurrence is sensitive to historical coverage and to whether recent events remain visible at prediction time. The auxiliary signals therefore contribute differently across datasets, while the value of a longer or rolling history depends on the available evidence. The full model also leads seven evaluated baselines on AP, AUC, and MRR across the three datasets under the reported protocol.

title: Multimodal fusion of DCE-MRI habitat–peritumoral radiomics and mammographic deep learning features for early recurrence prediction and risk stratification in invasive breast cancer
abstract: Background Invasive breast cancer exhibits marked biological heterogeneity, resulting in variable postoperative recurrence risks among patients with similar clinicopathological characteristics. This study aimed to develop a multimodal combined model integrating DCE-MRI-derived habitat–peritumoral radiomics, mammographic deep learning features, and clinicoradiological variables for early recurrence prediction and risk stratification. Methods A total of 419 patients with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer who underwent surgery were retrospectively enrolled and randomly divided into training (n=293) and test (n=126) cohorts. Radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral habitat subregions and multi-scale peritumoral regions using preoperative DCE-MRI. Dual-view mammographic deep features were extracted using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 model. After feature selection, individual radiomics, deep learning, and clinicoradiological models were developed, followed by construction of a multimodal Combined model using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using ROC analysis, DeLong test, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and risk stratification analysis. Results The 3-mm peritumoral region showed the optimal predictive performance among different expansion scales. Age, PR status, N3 stage, adjacent vessel sign, and non-mass-like morphology w…

title: Turbulence-aware free-space optical communication system hybrid CNN–LSTM channel modeling, adaptive prediction, and real-time mitigation
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric optical turbulence severely degrades the performance of free-space optical communication. Mitigating these effects without costly additional hardware remains an open challenge. This paper presents a fully machine learning–driven adaptive modulation and coding architecture that combines a first-principles neural surrogate model with a hybrid deep learning predictor to optimize the modulation and coding scheme. A feed-forward neural network, trained on exact Kolmogorov phase-screen statistics, learns the differentiable mapping from the refractive-index structure parameter C n 2 ${C}_{n}^{2}$ to the gamma–gamma channel parameters α and β , bypassing the limitations of standard Rytov approximations. Turbulence forecasting, a systematic ablation study demonstrates that a hybrid convolutional-recurrent architecture with temporal attention achieves a near-perfect coefficient of determination ( R 2 = 0.9956) for log 10 C n 2 ${\mathrm{log}}_{10} {C}_{n}^{2}$ , dramatically outperforming standalone CNN ( R 2 = −104.42) and LSTM ( R 2 = −0.06) models. The predicted channel state drives a threshold-based MCS selector evaluated through exact analytic integrals for outage probability, average bit error rate (BER), and spectral efficiency. When benchmarked against adaptive optics, the predictive scheme achieves a 9.3 % lower average BER and a 10.5 % lower outage probabil…

title: Development and external validation of a prediction model for suboptimal orthokeratology control in adolescents
abstract: AIM: To develop and externally validate a risk prediction model for adolescents wearing orthokeratology (OK) lenses to predict the probability of suboptimal control effects. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of myopic children who used OK lenses consistently for at least 18mo between January 2021 and March 2023 were conducted. Various ophthalmic examinations and recorded baseline parameters were performed. A risk prediction model was developed using multifactorial logistic regression analysis, and the model’s discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Brier score. RESULTS: The modeling group included 228 eyes (mean age, 10.46±1.99y; 55.7% males), with 120 right eyes (52.6%) and 108 left eyes (47.4%), and the validation group included 100 eyes. Anisometropia was absent in 174 eyes (76.3%) and present in 54 eyes (23.7%). The risk prediction model identified age, anisometropia, and corneal diameter as independent predictors for the control effect of OK lenses. The model showed good discrimination [AUC 0.781, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.721–0.841] and acceptable calibration in derivation (Brier score 0.186) in the validation group. CONCLUSION: The study constructs a risk prediction model to forecast the likelihood that myopic adolescents will not achieve the ideal control effect after wearing OK lenses,…

title: Source composition and chemical representation in retrospective bioactivity prediction
A concept-guided multimodal mixture-of-experts framework for lung cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction
abstract: Accurate lung cancer assessment requires integrating histopathological morphology, molecular alterations, and prognostic risk. However, most computational pathology models are either task-specific or rely on high-dimensional multimodal fusion that provides limited insight into how image-derived and genomic evidence jointly supports a clinical decision. We propose CONCERTO, a concept-guided multimodal mixture-of-experts framework for multi-endpoint lung cancer analysis. The model integrates whole-slide images (WSIs) with genomics data, decomposes multimodal evidence into image-specific, omics-specific, redundant, and synergistic expert pathways, and maps expert representations to hierarchical morphology and molecular concepts. Across TCGA lung cancer tasks, CONCERTO demonstrates strong performance in subtype classification, molecular alteration prediction, and survival prediction. Ablation studies further support the contribution of concept bottlenecks, hierarchical concept organization, and interaction-aware expert specialization. These results suggest a scalable route toward multimodal lung cancer AI that is both predictive and interpretable.

title: Exploring the System Security Veil: Uncovering Domestic Motivation to Establish Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms (CRMs) (online first)
abstract: Nation states face critical trade-offs between energy security, efficiency, and climate goals when implementing Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms (CRMs). This study investigates factors influencing CRM adoption and design choices (targeted strategic reserves versus market-wide approaches) across EU member states from 2008–2021. Using logistic regression analysis on a new dataset, the research examines techno-economic, socio-technical, and political influences. Results show that while renewable integration creates legitimate security challenges, state responses reflect political preferences as much as technical necessities. Key adoption predictors include electricity heating dependence and gas energy share as well as intermittent energy, while interconnection capacity strongly predicts non-adoption — suggesting technical decisions often reflect deeper preferences about energy autonomy versus market integration. The choice between targeted and market-wide designs is influenced by party ideology, carbon intensity, and existing energy mix interests. This research reveals how functional pressures, generator interests, and politicization shape responses to system security concerns, which implies different decarbonization pathways.

title: Equilibrium models to analyse the impact of different coordination schemes between TSO and DSOs on market power in sequentially-cleared energy and ancillary services markets under load and renewable generation uncertainty
abstract: The current massive installation of distributed resources in electricity distribution systems is transforming these systems into active dispatching subjects. At the same time, the need to compensate for the intermittent generation of an increasing amount of renewable sources creates the need to acquire more ancillary services. Flexible resources in the distribution system could provide these services not only within the perimeter of the distribution network to which they are connected but also for the benefit of the transmission system. However, this requires Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to coordinate their dispatching actions effectively. One critical aspect of this coordination is establishing a market architecture that limits market power. This paper presents an innovative game-theoretic approach to compare different TSO-DSO coordination models for acquiring ancillary services from distribution resources. Several schemes are considered: some with coordinated market management by TSOs and DSOs, others with sequential or independent local markets. For each scheme, the dispatching problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic sequential game, where the first stage is the day-ahead market and the second stage is the balancing market. Nash equilibrium solutions are obtained by iteratively solving the profit maximization problem o…

title: A Risk-Based Probabilistic Transient Stability Approach for Ranking of Circuit Breakers in a Power System
abstract: Power systems are getting more complex than ever and are consequently operating close to their limit of stability. Moreover, with the increasing demand of renewable wind generation, and the requirement to maintain a secure power system, the importance of transient stability cannot be overestimated. Current deterministic industry practices of transient stability assessment ignore the probability of variables involved. With increasing system uncertainties and widespread electricity market deregulation, there is a strong inevitability to incorporate probabilistic transient stability analysis. Circuit breakers play a critical role in fault clearing and consequently in determining the system transient stability. It is important that they undergo timely and appropriate maintenance procedures based on some criterion. Considering the need of incorporating risk in modern power systems, this paper proposes a risk-based probabilistic transient stability approach for ranking of circuit breakers in a power system. A novel priority index was proposed to rank the circuit breakers based on the system transient stability risk. DIgSILENT PowerFactory software was used to conduct the required simulations on IEEE 14 bus system. The proposed risk-based framework was deemed to be efficient in identification of the circuit breakers based on their priority rank index which can aid in power system plan…

title: A Hybrid Strategy for Probabilistic Forecasting and Trading of Aggregated Wind-Solar Power: Design and Analysis in HEFTCom2024
abstract: Obtaining accurate probabilistic energy forecasts and making effective decisions amid diverse uncertainties are routine challenges in future energy systems. This paper presents the winning solution of team GEB, which ranked 3rd in trading, 4th in forecasting, and 1st among student teams in the IEEE Hybrid Energy Forecasting and Trading Competition 2024 (HEFTCom2024). The solution provides accurate probabilistic forecasts for a wind-solar hybrid system, and achieves substantial trading revenue in the day-ahead electricity market. Key components include: (1) a stacking-based approach combining sister forecasts from various Numerical Weather Predictions (NWPs) to provide wind power forecasts, (2) an online solar post-processing model to address the distribution shift in the online test set caused by increased solar capacity, (3) a probabilistic aggregation method for accurate quantile forecasts of hybrid generation, and (4) a stochastic trading strategy to maximize expected trading revenue considering uncertainties in electricity prices. This paper also explores the potential of end-to-end learning to further enhance the trading revenue by shifting the distribution of forecast errors. Detailed case studies are provided to validate the effectiveness of these proposed methods. Code for all mentioned methods is available for reproduction and further research in both industry and acad…

title: Economic evaluation and feasibility design of an electricity-hydrogen market with hydrogen-based system: Mathematical model and techno-economic analysis
Challenges and prospectives of energy storage integration in renewable energy systems for net zero transition
Congestion-Sensitive Grid Aggregation for DC Optimal Power Flow
abstract: The vast spatial dimension of modern interconnected electricity grids challenges the tractability of the DC optimal power flow problem. Grid aggregation methods try to overcome this challenge by reducing the number of network elements. Many existing methods use Locational Marginal Prices as a distance metric to cluster nodes. In this paper, we show that prevalent methods adopting this distance metric fail to adequately capture the impact of individual lines when there is more than one line congested. This leads to suboptimal outcomes for the optimization of the aggregated model. To overcome those issues, we propose two methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric, which preserves the impact of nodal power injections on individual line congestions. The proposed methods are compared to several existing aggregation methods based on Locational Marginal Prices. We demonstrate all methods on adapted versions of the IEEE RTS 24- and 300-Bus systems. We show that the proposed methods outperform existing approaches both in terms of objective function value error and maximum line limit violation, while exhibiting faster node clustering. We conclude that aggregation methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric are better at preserving the essential physical characteristics of the network topology in the grid aggregation process than methods based on Locational …

title: Integrated equilibrium model for electrified logistics and power systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated equilibrium model to characterize the complex interactions between electrified logistics systems and electric power delivery systems. The model consists of two major players: an electrified logistics operator (ELO) and a power system operator (PSO). The ELO aims to maximize its profit by strategically scheduling and routing its electric delivery vehicles (e-trucks) for deliveries and charging, in response to the locational marginal price (LMP) set by the PSO. The routing, delivery, and charging behaviors of e-trucks are modeled by a perturbed utility Markov decision process (PU-MDP) while their collective operations are optimized to achieve the ELO's objective by designing rewards in the PU-MDP. On the other hand, PSO optimizes the energy price by considering both the spatiotemporal e-truck charging demand and the base electricity load. The equilibrium of the integrated system is formulated as a fixed point, proved to exist under mild assumptions, and solved for a case study on the Hawaii network via Anderson's fixed-point acceleration algorithm. Along with these numerical results, this paper provides both theoretical insights and practical guidelines to achieve sustainable and efficient operations in modern electrified logistics and power systems.
